original_question: If global-in-time solutions of the evolutionary incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid problem can be constructed, can one then build generalized attractors and/or inertial manifolds for that problem?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the initial-boundary value problem for the evolutionary motion of an incompressible viscoelastic fluid of Jeffreys type in a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2,3$) with smooth boundary. The velocity field $v(t,x)$ and pressure $p(t,x)$ satisfy the system
$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} + (v\cdot\nabla)v - \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma + \nabla p = f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\, v = 0,$$
where the deviatoric stress tensor $\sigma$ obeys the Jeffreys constitutive relation
$$\sigma + \lambda_1 \frac{\mathcal{D}\sigma}{\mathcal{D}t} = 2\mu\!\left(\mathcal{E}(v) + \lambda_2 \frac{\mathcal{D}\mathcal{E}(v)}{\mathcal{D}t}\right),$$
with relaxation time $\lambda_1>0$, retardation time $\lambda_2\in(0,\lambda_1)$, viscosity $\mu>0$, rate-of-strain tensor $\mathcal{E}(v)=\tfrac{1}{2}(\nabla v + \nabla v^\top)$, and an objective (e.g. Jaumann or upper-convected) time derivative $\mathcal{D}/\mathcal{D}t$. The system is supplemented with no-slip boundary condition $v|_{\partial\Omega}=0$ and initial data $v(0,\cdot)=v_0$.

Assume that, for suitable classes of initial data and external force $f$, global-in-time (possibly weak or generalized) solutions of this problem have been constructed, giving rise to a (multivalued) dynamical system or a trajectory space on the phase space of divergence-free vector fields.

Question: Can one construct, for this dynamical system, a generalized global attractor (e.g. a trajectory attractor or a minimal attracting set in an appropriate weak topology) and/or an inertial manifold (a finite-dimensional, positively invariant Lipschitz manifold attracting all trajectories at an exponential rate)?
status_search_result: Existence of trajectory and global attractors for weak solutions of the autonomous motion equations of an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium has been established (e.g. Vorotnikov–Zvyagin and subsequent works in J. Math. Fluid Mech. and Lobachevskii J. Math.), and related results (global, exponential attractors, determining modes) are known for the closely related Navier–Stokes–Voight and Kelvin–Voigt fluids with memory. However, the construction of inertial manifolds for the Jeffreys-type viscoelastic fluid model does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem is only partially solved.

$$\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor 2 p^a/3 \rfloor} (21k+8)\binom{2k}{k}^{3} \equiv 8\,p^{a} \pmod{p^{\,a+5+(-1)^{p}}},$$

Let $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol and let $B_n$ denote the $n$-th Bernoulli number. Establish or refute the following three assertions.

(i) For each positive integer $n$, set
$$a_n \;=\; \frac{1}{n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(10k+3)\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\,8^{\,n-1-k}.$$

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}}{8^{k}}\;\equiv\;
\begin{cases}
4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}}, & \text{if }\left(\tfrac{-2}{p}\right)=1\text{ and }p=x^{2}+2y^{2}\text{ with }x,y\in\mathbb{Z},\\[4pt]
0\pmod{p^{2}}, & \text{if }\left(\tfrac{-2}{p}\right)=-1.
\end{cases}$$
Moreover, for every odd prime $p$ and every positive integer $a$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{10k+3}{8^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\;\equiv\;3+\frac{49}{8}p^{3}B_{p-3}\pmod{p^{4}}.$$

(iii) The infinite series identity
$$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(10k-3)\,8^{k}}{k^{3}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}}\;=\;\frac{\pi^{2}}{2}$$
holds.
status_search_result: The integrality assertion (part (i)) of this Z.-W. Sun conjecture was proved by V. J. W. Guo (arXiv:1601.04250, "Proof of Sun's conjectures on integer-valued polynomials," published in J. Math. Anal. Appl. 2016), as part of his confirmation of two of Sun's integer-valued conjectures. The supercongruence mod $p^4$ in (ii) involving $(10k+3)$ and $B_{p-3}$ has been addressed in subsequent work by Guo and Zudilin via $q$-analogues for primes $p>2$. The mod-$p^2$ supercongruence in (ii) involving the representation $p=x^2+2y^2$ and the closed-form Ramanujan-type series identity in (iii) do not appear to have a fully verified proof in the literature found, so those parts are best treated as not confirmed.

Let $p>3$ be a prime, and let $B_n$ and $E_n$ denote the Bernoulli and Euler numbers, respectively. Let $\left(\tfrac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Establish (or refute) all of the following congruences and integrality statement.

(i) If $p\equiv 1\pmod 6$, write $p=x^2+3y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 4x^2-2p\pmod{p^2},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p-4x^2}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(ii) If $p\equiv 5\pmod 6$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv 0\pmod{p^2},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv \frac{p}{3}\pmod{p^2}.$$

(iii) For every positive integer $a$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv p^a\Bigl(1+\tfrac{7}{6}\,p^3\,B_{p-3}\Bigr)\pmod{p^{a+3}}$$
(equivalently, $p^a\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\equiv 1+\tfrac{7}{6}p^3 B_{p-3}\pmod{p^4}$ in the appropriate normalization).

(iv) 
$$\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3}{16^k}\equiv p+2\Bigl(\tfrac{-1}{p}\Bigr)p^3 E_{p-3}\pmod{p^4}.$$

(v) For every integer $n\geq 2$,
$$2n\binom{2n}{n}\,\Bigl|\;\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3\,16^{n-1-k},$$
i.e. the quotient $\dfrac{1}{2n\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3 16^{n-1-k}$ is an integer.
status_search_result: Several pieces of this multi-part conjecture have been settled. The integrality statement (v) and related divisibility properties were proved by Guo and Zeng (arXiv:1511.05553) and by J.-C. Liu / Guo. The mod-$p^2$ congruences in case $p\equiv 1\pmod 6$ (with $p=x^2+3y^2$) have been established (in part by G.-S. Mao and collaborators), and the mod-$p^4$ congruence (iv) involving $E_{p-3}$ has been treated by WZ-type proofs (e.g., the Ramanujan Journal paper by Guillera and others). The full mod-$p^{a+3}$ statement (iii) for all $a\geq 1$ does not appear to be uniformly verified in the literature; thus the conjecture as a whole is partially solved but not fully closed.

so that $P_0=1,\ P_1=8,\ P_2=80,\ P_3=896,\dots$

Prove or disprove the following supercongruences for primes $p$.

(i) Suppose $p$ is a prime with $p\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$. Then $p$ can be written uniquely (up to signs) as $p=x^{2}+2y^{2}$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$; choose the sign of $x$ so that $x\equiv 1$ or $3\pmod 8$. Then

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{p-1}{k}\,\frac{P_{k}}{8^{k}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A62 ([S-4]). Let p > 3 be a prime. If p ≡ 7 (mod 12) and p = x2 + 3y2 with y ≡ 1 (mod 4) , then p−1∑ k=0 uk(4, 1) 64k (2k k ) 2 ≡ 2y − p 6y (mod p2) and p−1∑ k=0 kuk(4, 1) 64k (2k k ) 2 ≡ y (mod p2).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{u_k(4,1)\}_{k\ge 0}$ denote the Lucas sequence defined by $u_0=0$, $u_1=1$, and $u_{k+1}=4u_k-u_{k-1}$ for $k\ge 1$. For a prime $p>3$ with $p\equiv 7\pmod{12}$, it is known that $p$ can be uniquely written (up to signs) as $p=x^2+3y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$; fix the representation by requiring $y\equiv 1\pmod{4}$. Prove or disprove the following two congruences modulo $p^2$:
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{u_k(4,1)}{64^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\equiv \frac{2y-p}{6y}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\,u_k(4,1)}{64^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\equiv y\pmod{p^2}.$$
Here $\frac{1}{6y}$ denotes the inverse of $6y$ modulo $p^2$.

Many related Z.-W. Sun supercongruence conjectures have been resolved by various authors, but the status of this specific conjecture could not be confirmed from the available evidence.

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{v_k(4,1)}{4^k\binom{2k}{k}^{2}}\equiv (-1)^{(p-1)/4+(x-1)/2}\Bigl(4x-\frac{p}{x}\Bigr)\pmod{p^2},$$

self_contained_problem:
Define the Almkvist–Zudilin numbers $\{A_k\}_{k\geq 0}$ by
$$A_k=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor k/3\rfloor}(-1)^{k-3j}3^{k-3j}\binom{k}{3j}\binom{k+j}{j}\frac{(3j)!}{j!^3},$$
and for an indeterminate (or rational/integer parameter) $x$, set
$$A_k(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}^{2}\binom{2j}{j}\binom{2k-2j}{k-j}x^j.$$
Let $p$ denote a prime, and let $\bigl(\tfrac{\cdot}{p}\bigr)$ be the Legendre symbol. Prove or disprove the following three assertions.

(i) For every odd prime $p$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}A_k\equiv\begin{cases}4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}},&\text{if }p\equiv 1,3\pmod 8\text{ and }p=x^{2}+2y^{2},\ x,y\in\mathbb Z,\\ 0\pmod{p^{2}},&\text{if }p\equiv 5,7\pmod 8;\end{cases}$$
and
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{k}A_k\equiv\begin{cases}4x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}},&\text{if }p\equiv 1\pmod 3\text{ and }p=x^{2}+3y^{2},\ x,y\in\mathbb Z,\\ 0\pmod{p^{2}},&\text{if }p\equiv 2\pmod 3.\end{cases}$$

(ii) For every prime $p>3$:
- if $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{k}A_k\equiv\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{3}}{16^{k}}\pmod{p^{3}};$
- if $p\equiv 1,3\pmod 8$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}A_k\equiv\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{256^{k}}\pmod{p^{3}}.$

(iii) For every prime $p>3$, and every
$$x\in\{1,-4,9,-48,81,-324,2401,9801,-25920,-777924,96059601\}\cup\{\tfrac{81}{256},-\tfrac{9}{16},\tfrac{81}{32},-3969\}$$
with $x\not\equiv 0\pmod p$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}A_k(x)\equiv\Bigl(\tfrac{x}{p}\Bigr)\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}}{(256x)^{k}}\pmod{p^{2}}.$$
status_search_result: Several supercongruences of Z.-W. Sun and Z.-H. Sun involving Almkvist–Zudilin numbers have been proved in recent years (e.g. via q-supercongruences, WZ methods, and modular form techniques), and partial results on sums like $\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}A_k$ modulo $p^2$ have appeared in the literature. However, no source was located that simultaneously confirms all three parts (i)–(iii) of this conjectural cluster, including the mod $p^3$ identifications and the full list of parameter values in (iii). The status is therefore at best partially solved and overall unverified.

are all congruent modulo $p^2$ to
- $4x^2-2p$ if $p\equiv 1,7\pmod{24}$ and $p=x^2+6y^2$,
- $2p-8x^2$ if $p\equiv 5,11\pmod{24}$ and $p=2x^2+3y^2$,
- $0$ if $\left(\tfrac{-6}{p}\right)=-1$.

Moreover,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(3k+2)T_k(2,3)^3}{8^k}\equiv p\!\left(\Big(\tfrac{3}{p}\Big)-1\right)\!\!\pmod{p^2},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(3k+1)T_k(2,3)^3}{(-64)^k}\equiv p\Big(\tfrac{-2}{p}\Big)\!\!\pmod{p^3}.$$

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(72k+47)T_k(2,9)^3}{(-64)^k}\equiv 42p\pmod{p^2},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(72k+25)T_k(2,9)^3}{512^k}\equiv 12p\Big(\tfrac{3}{p}\Big)\!\!\pmod{p^2}.$$
Also, for every positive integer $n$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(3k+2)T_k(2,3)^3\,8^{n-1-k}\equiv 0\pmod{2n},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(3k+1)T_k(2,3)^3\,(-64)^{n-1-k}\equiv 0\pmod{n}.$$

(ii) The sums
$$\Big(\tfrac{2}{p}\Big)\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{T_k(18,49)^3}{8^{3k}}\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{T_k(18,49)^3}{16^{3k}}\pmod{p^2}$$
are congruent to $4x^2-2p$ if $p\equiv 1\pmod 4$ with $p=x^2+y^2$ ($2\nmid x$, $2\mid y$), and to $0$ if $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$.

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(7k+4)T_k(10,49)^3}{(-8)^{3k}}\equiv p\Big(\tfrac{2}{p}\Big)\!\Big(65-9\Big(\tfrac{-1}{p}\Big)\Big)\!\!\pmod{p^2},$$

Let $T_k$ denote the central trinomial coefficient, i.e., the coefficient of $x^k$ in $(1+x+x^2)^k$. Let $F_k$ and $L_k$ denote the Fibonacci and Lucas numbers, defined by $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, $F_{k+1}=F_k+F_{k-1}$ and $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$, $L_{k+1}=L_k+L_{k-1}$. Let $P_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}\binom{n+k}{k}\left(\frac{x-1}{2}\right)^k$ be the Legendre polynomial of degree $n$. For an odd prime $p$ and integer $a$ coprime to $p$, let $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. Prove or disprove the following.

(i) For every prime $p>3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^k \binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k \equiv \begin{cases} 4x^2-2p \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 1,4\pmod{15} \text{ and } p=x^2+15y^2,\\ 2p-12x^2 \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } p\equiv 2,8\pmod{15} \text{ and } p=3x^2+5y^2,\\ 0 \pmod{p^2}, & \text{if } \left(\frac{p}{15}\right)=-1.\end{cases}$$
Moreover,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(105k+44)(-1)^k \binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k \equiv p\left(20+24\left(\frac{p}{?}\right)(2-3^{p-1})\right) \pmod{p^3},$$
and for every positive integer $n$,
$$\frac{2n}{\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^{n-1-k}(105k+44)\binom{2k}{k}^2 T_k \in \mathbb{Z}^+.$$

(ii) If $p\equiv 1,4\pmod{15}$ is a prime and $p=x^2+15y^2$ with $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, then
$$P_{(p-1)/2}(7\sqrt{-15}\pm 16\sqrt{-3}) \equiv \left(\frac{-\sqrt{-15}}{p}\right)\left(\frac{x}{?}\right)\left(2x-\frac{p}{2x}\right) \pmod{p^2}.$$

(iii) Let $p>5$ be a prime. If $p\equiv 1,4\pmod{15}$, $p=x^2+15y^2$ with $x\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}F_k \equiv 2\left(\frac{p}{x}-2x\right)\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}L_k \equiv 4x-\frac{p}{x}\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{(3k+2)\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}L_k \equiv 4x \pmod{p^2}.$$
If $p\equiv 2,8\pmod{15}$ and $p=3x^2+5y^2$ with $y\equiv 1\pmod 3$, then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}F_k \equiv \frac{p}{5y}-4y\pmod{p^2},$$
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}F_k \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{k\binom{2k}{k}\binom{3k}{k}}{27^k}L_k \equiv \frac{4}{3y}\pmod{p^2}.$$

$$8(2n-1)\binom{3n}{n}\ \Bigg|\ \sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{6k}{3k}\binom{3k}{k}\binom{6(n-k)}{3(n-k)}\binom{3(n-k)}{n-k}.$$

is a (positive) integer for all $n\ge 1$. Here $\binom{a}{b}$ denotes the usual binomial coefficient.

original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A88 ([S11h]). Let k and l be positive integers. If (ln + 1) |(kn+ln kn ) for all suﬃciently large positive integers n, then each prime factor of k divides l. In other words, if k has a prime factor not dividing l then there are infinitely many positive integers n such that (ln + 1) ∤ (kn+ln kn ) .
self_contained_problem: Let $k$ and $\ell$ be positive integers. Prove or disprove the following: if $(\ell n + 1) \mid \binom{kn+\ell n}{kn}$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $n$, then every prime factor of $k$ divides $\ell$. Equivalently, show that if $k$ has a prime factor that does not divide $\ell$, then there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $(\ell n + 1) \nmid \binom{kn+\ell n}{kn}$.

For any n ∈ Z+ we have (−1)n−1 n2(n + 1) (2n n ) n−1∑ k=0 uk+1(4, 1) (2k k ) ≡      1 (mod 9) if n ≡ 0, 2 (mod 9) , 4 (mod 9) if n ≡ 5, 6 (mod 9) , −2 (mod 9) otherwise. Also, if a, b ∈ Z+ and a ⩾ b − 1 then the sum 32a 3a−1∑ k=0 uk+1(4, 1) (2k k ) modulo 3b only depends on b.
self_contained_problem:
Define the Lucas-type sequence $\{u_k(4,1)\}_{k\geq 0}$ by $u_0(4,1)=0$, $u_1(4,1)=1$, and $u_{k+1}(4,1)=4\,u_k(4,1)-u_{k-1}(4,1)$ for $k\geq 1$. For a positive integer $n$, define
$$S(n)\;=\;\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n^2(n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{u_{k+1}(4,1)}{\binom{2k}{k}}.$$
(Here it is understood that, although $S(n)$ is a priori a rational number, it is conjectured to be a $3$-adic integer, so the congruences below make sense.)

Prove or disprove the following two statements.

(1) For every positive integer $n$,
$$S(n)\;\equiv\;\begin{cases}1\pmod 9 & \text{if } n\equiv 0,2\pmod 9,\\[2pt] 4\pmod 9 & \text{if } n\equiv 5,6\pmod 9,\\[2pt] -2\pmod 9 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

(2) For all positive integers $a,b$ with $a\geq b-1$, the value
$$3^{2a}\sum_{k=0}^{3^a-1}\frac{u_{k+1}(4,1)}{\binom{2k}{k}}\pmod{3^b}$$
depends only on $b$ (and not on $a$).
status_search_result: This is one of Z.-W. Sun's open conjectures on congruences (Conjecture A93 in his list "Open Conjectures on Congruences"). No published resolution of this specific conjecture was located; it appears to remain open, but conclusive evidence is lacking.

If a ∈ Z+ and pa > 3, then pa−1∑ k=0 (hpa − 1 k )( 2k k )( −h ) k ≡ 0 (mod pa+1). Also, for any n ∈ Z+ we have νp (n−1∑ k=0 (hn − 1 k )( 2k k )( −h ) k ) ⩾ νp(n). 74 ZHI-WEI SUN

For a prime $p$ and a nonzero integer $m$, let $\nu_p(m)$ denote the $p$-adic valuation of $m$ (with $\nu_p(0)=+\infty$). Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $h\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $2h-1\equiv 0\pmod{p}$.

(i) Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $a$ with $p^a>3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p^a-1}\binom{hp^a-1}{k}\binom{2k}{k}(-h)^{-k}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{a+1}}.$$

$$\nu_p\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\binom{hn-1}{k}\binom{2k}{k}(-h)^{-k}\right)\geq \nu_p(n).$$

(Here $(-h)^{-k}$ is interpreted in the $p$-adic sense, which makes sense because $\gcd(h,p)=1$ since $2h\equiv 1\pmod p$.)

(i) If m > 2, m ̸≡r (mod 2) , and p ≡ r (mod m) with r ⩾ −m/ 2, then p−1∑ k=0 (−1)km (r/m k ) m ≡ 0 (mod p3). (ii) If p ≡ r (mod 2 m) with r ⩾ −m, then p−1∑ k=0 (−1)k (r/m k ) 2n+1 ≡ 0 (mod p2) for all n = 1 , . . . , m − 1. (iii) For any prime p and positive integer n, we have νp (n−1∑ k=0 (−1/ (p + 1) k ) p+1) ⩾ cp ⌊νp(n) + 1 ⌋ , where cp =      1 if p = 2 , 3 if p = 3 , 5 if p ⩾ 5.

Let $\binom{x}{k}=\frac{x(x-1)\cdots(x-k+1)}{k!}$ denote the generalized binomial coefficient, and let $\nu_p(\cdot)$ denote the $p$-adic valuation. Prove or disprove the following three statements.

(i) Let $m\ge 2$ be an integer with $m>2$, let $r$ be an integer with $r\ge -m/2$ such that $m\not\equiv r \pmod 2$, and let $p>r$ be an odd prime not dividing $m$ with $p\equiv r\pmod m$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{km}\binom{r/m}{k}^{m}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{3}}.$$

$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{k}\binom{r/m}{k}^{2n+1}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

$$\nu_p\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^{k}\binom{-1/(p+1)}{k}^{p+1}\right)\ge c_p\,\bigl\lfloor \nu_p(n)+1\bigr\rfloor,$$
where $c_p=1$ if $p=2$, $c_p=3$ if $p=3$, and $c_p=5$ if $p\ge 5$.

original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A100. (i) (raised on Nov. 2, 2009 via a message to Number Theory List) If n > 1 is an odd integer satisfying the Morley congruence ( n − 1 (n − 1)/ 2 ) ≡ (−1)(n−1)/ 24n−1 (mod n3), 76 ZHI-WEI SUN then n must be a prime. (ii) ([S10]) If an odd integer n > 1 satisfies the congruence n−1∑ k=0 (2k k ) 2k ≡ (−1)(n−1)/ 2 (mod n2), then n must be a prime. (iii) ([S11j]) Set an := ∑ n k=0 (n k ) 2 Ck for n = 0 , 1, 2, . . . . Any integer n > 1 satisfying a1 + · · · + an−1 ≡ 0 (mod n2) must be a prime.
self_contained_problem:
Let $C_k = \binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ denote the $k$-th Catalan number. Determine whether each of the following three primality criteria holds.

(i) If $n>1$ is an odd integer satisfying the Morley-type congruence
$$\binom{n-1}{(n-1)/2} \equiv (-1)^{(n-1)/2}\, 4^{n-1} \pmod{n^3},$$
must $n$ be prime?

(ii) If $n>1$ is an odd integer satisfying
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \binom{2k}{k}\, 2^k \equiv (-1)^{(n-1)/2} \pmod{n^2},$$
must $n$ be prime?

(iii) Define $a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}^2 C_k$ for $n=0,1,2,\dots$. If an integer $n>1$ satisfies
$$a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{n-1} \equiv 0 \pmod{n^2},$$
must $n$ be prime?

Related supercongruences for primes have been proved, but the converse (compositeness ruled out) appears not to be settled in the literature found.

context_brief: Linearity of prime-order actions on S^4 and CP^2
original_question: Let Z_p denote a cyclic group of prime order p. Is every Z_p-action on S^4 or on CP^2 conjugate to a linear action?
self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime and let Z_p denote the cyclic group of order p. Consider smooth (or, equivalently in this setting, locally linear) actions of Z_p on the 4-sphere S^4 and on the complex projective plane CP^2. A linear action on S^4 is one obtained by restricting an orthogonal representation of Z_p on R^5 to the unit sphere; a linear action on CP^2 is one induced by a linear representation of Z_p on C^3 via the natural projection C^3 \ {0} → CP^2. Two actions are conjugate if there is a homeomorphism (equivalently, a diffeomorphism) of the underlying manifold intertwining them.

Determine whether every Z_p-action on S^4 is conjugate to a linear action, and whether every Z_p-action on CP^2 is conjugate to a linear action.
status_search_result: The linearization question for prime-order cyclic actions on S^4 and CP^2 is a long-standing problem in 4-dimensional transformation group theory. Recent work (e.g., a 2025 preprint on involutions on S^4) continues to investigate special cases and partial results, indicating the general question remains open. No source found establishing a full positive or negative answer.

context_brief: Complexity of fixed-point and cohomological data for Z_p-actions
original_question: Fix a simply connected 4-manifold X and let a Z_p-action determine associated data Γ = (ρ, X_G, {ρ_x}), where ρ is the induced action on H^2(X) preserving cup product, X_G is the singular set of points with nontrivial isotropy, and ρ_x records the local linear isotropy representation near each singular point x. How complicated can the set of all such associated data Γ become when one ranges over all Z_p-actions on X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a closed, smooth, simply connected $4$-manifold, and let $p$ be a prime. Consider locally linear (smooth) actions of the cyclic group $G = \mathbb{Z}_p$ on $X$. To each such action assign the triple of data
\[
\Gamma \;=\; (\rho,\; X_G,\; \{\rho_x\}_{x \in X_G}),
\]
where:
- $\rho : G \to \mathrm{Aut}(H^2(X;\mathbb{Z}),\cup)$ is the induced action on second cohomology, preserving the cup-product intersection form;
- $X_G = \{x \in X : G_x \neq \{1\}\}$ is the fixed-point (singular) set of the action, where $G_x$ denotes the isotropy subgroup of $x$;
- for each $x \in X_G$, the map $\rho_x : G_x \to GL(4,\mathbb{R})$ is the linear isotropy representation modeling the action on a $G_x$-invariant neighborhood of $x$.

Let $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$ denote the set of all such triples $\Gamma$ realized by some $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action on $X$, considered up to the natural equivalence (conjugation of $\rho$ by automorphisms of the intersection form, equivariant identification of singular sets, and equivalence of local representations).

Problem: Describe and bound the complexity of the set $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$ as $X$ ranges over closed simply connected $4$-manifolds. In particular, determine which triples $\Gamma$ are realizable, and find effective constraints (in terms of the intersection form of $X$, the prime $p$, and the topology of $X_G$) that classify $\mathcal{D}(X,p)$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return conclusive evidence that this realization/classification question for the full data $\Gamma = (\rho, X_G, \{\rho_x\})$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions on a general simply connected $4$-manifold has been resolved. While partial constraints (G-signature, equivariant cohomology, and case studies for specific $X$ such as $S^4$, $\mathbb{CP}^2$, K3) are known in the literature, no general classification appears to be established.

context_brief: Smooth structure versus finite symmetry groups
original_question: Given a smooth 4-manifold, to what extent is its smooth structure reflected in its finite groups of smooth symmetries, and conversely to what extent do those finite smooth symmetry groups reflect the underlying smooth structure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a closed smooth 4-manifold. By a finite smooth symmetry group of $X$ we mean a finite group $G$ admitting a faithful, smooth, effective action $G \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Diff}(X)$. Let
$$\mathcal{S}(X) = \{G : G \text{ is a finite group acting smoothly and effectively on } X\},$$
considered together with the data of the conjugacy classes of such actions in $\mathrm{Diff}(X)$.

Investigate the following two-way relationship between the smooth structure on $X$ and the collection $\mathcal{S}(X)$:

(a) To what extent does the smooth structure of $X$ determine $\mathcal{S}(X)$? More precisely, can one exhibit pairs $(X_1, X_2)$ of closed 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic for which $\mathcal{S}(X_1) \neq \mathcal{S}(X_2)$, either as sets of finite groups or as sets of smooth conjugacy classes of actions? Identify invariants of the smooth structure (e.g. Seiberg–Witten or gauge-theoretic invariants) that obstruct or constrain which finite groups can act smoothly.

(b) Conversely, to what extent does the collection $\mathcal{S}(X)$, together with the conjugacy classes of smooth actions, determine the smooth structure on $X$? In particular, do there exist closed 4-manifolds $X_1$ and $X_2$ that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic and for which the sets $\mathcal{S}(X_1)$ and $\mathcal{S}(X_2)$ (with their action data) coincide?

Provide a systematic understanding of how finite smooth symmetry groups of closed 4-manifolds interact with their exotic smooth structures.

context_brief: Linearity of finite smooth actions on S^4 with isolated fixed point
original_question: Is every smooth action of a finite group on S^4 that has an isolated fixed point smoothly conjugate to a linear action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^4$ denote the standard 4-sphere, and let $G$ be a finite group acting smoothly on $S^4$. A fixed point $p \in S^4$ of the $G$-action is called isolated if $p$ is an isolated point of the fixed-point set $\mathrm{Fix}(G, S^4) = \{x \in S^4 : g\cdot x = x \text{ for all } g \in G\}$. The action is called linear if it is smoothly conjugate to the restriction of an orthogonal representation $G \to O(5)$ to the unit sphere $S^4 \subset \mathbb{R}^5$; equivalently, there exists a diffeomorphism $\varphi : S^4 \to S^4$ and a homomorphism $\rho : G \to O(5)$ such that $\varphi(g \cdot x) = \rho(g)\,\varphi(x)$ for all $g \in G$ and $x \in S^4$.

Question: Is it true that every smooth action of a finite group $G$ on $S^4$ which has at least one isolated fixed point is smoothly conjugate to a linear action?
status_search_result: The linearity question for smooth finite group actions on $S^4$ with an isolated fixed point is a long-standing open conjecture. Recent work (e.g., on involutions of $S^4$ and on equivariant trisections of 4-manifolds, 2025) treats only special cases such as involutions with fixed circles or 2-spheres, or imposes local linearity / homological triviality. No general resolution appears in the literature; the problem remains open.

original_question: Let (X, ω) be a minimal symplectic 4-manifold of Kodaira dimension 2, meaning that c1(K)·[ω] > 0 and c1(K)^2 > 0. Is there a universal constant c > 0 such that every finite group G of symplectomorphisms of (X, ω) satisfies |G| ≤ c · c1(K)^2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a closed minimal symplectic 4-manifold of Kodaira dimension 2; that is, $c_1(K)\cdot[\omega]>0$ and $c_1(K)^2>0$, where $K$ denotes the symplectic canonical class of $(X,\omega)$ (the first Chern class of the cotangent bundle with respect to any $\omega$-compatible almost complex structure). A symplectomorphism of $(X,\omega)$ is a diffeomorphism $\varphi:X\to X$ with $\varphi^*\omega=\omega$. 

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$, independent of $(X,\omega)$, such that for every finite group $G$ acting effectively on $(X,\omega)$ by symplectomorphisms one has
$$|G|\le c\cdot c_1(K)^2\,?$$
status_search_result: The question, attributed to W. Chen, asks for a universal linear bound in $c_1(K)^2$ on the orders of finite symplectomorphism groups of minimal symplectic 4-manifolds of Kodaira dimension 2. Related work by Chen and others (e.g., on symplectic Calabi-Yau 4-manifolds and symplectic symmetries) addresses neighboring cases (Kodaira dimension 0, cyclic actions, etc.), but no source found establishes a universal constant $c$ for the Kodaira dimension 2 case. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Describing bounds for smooth Z_p-actions via manifold invariants
original_question: For general smooth Z_p-actions, can the constant C from Question 4.1 be described in terms of invariants of the manifold? In particular, which invariants of the smooth structure, such as Seiberg-Witten basic classes or Seiberg-Witten invariants, enter that bound, and in what way do they enter it?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a closed smooth oriented $4$-manifold that does not admit any smooth (effective) action of the circle group $S^1$. It is conjectured (and known in special cases such as holomorphic or symplectic actions) that there exists a constant $C = C(X) > 0$ such that, for every prime $p > C$, the manifold $X$ admits no nontrivial smooth action of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of order $p$.

Recall that for a closed oriented smooth $4$-manifold $X$ with $b_2^+(X) \ge 2$, the Seiberg–Witten invariant is a function
\[ \mathrm{SW}_X : \mathrm{Spin}^c(X) \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}, \]
and a class $K \in H^2(X;\mathbb{Z})$ is called a Seiberg–Witten basic class if $K = c_1(\mathfrak{s})$ for some $\mathrm{Spin}^c$-structure $\mathfrak{s}$ on $X$ with $\mathrm{SW}_X(\mathfrak{s}) \ne 0$.

Question. For general smooth $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions on $X$, can the constant $C(X)$ above be expressed in terms of invariants of the smooth $4$-manifold $X$? In particular, determine which invariants of the smooth structure of $X$ (such as the set of Seiberg–Witten basic classes, the values of the Seiberg–Witten invariants, or related refinements) enter into an admissible bound $C(X)$, and give an explicit formula or recipe describing the way in which these invariants control $C(X)$.
status_search_result: The question, attributed to W. Chen, asks how a hypothetical bound on prime orders of smooth Z_p-actions on a 4-manifold (without smooth S^1-action) depends on smooth invariants such as Seiberg–Witten basic classes. Affirmative results exist for holomorphic and symplectic actions (with the symplectic constant involving the smooth structure), but for the general smooth case no description in terms of SW invariants is known; the question appears to remain open.

context_brief: Topological bounds on smoothable prime-order actions
original_question: Let X be a simply connected smoothable 4-manifold with even intersection form and nonzero signature. Does there exist a constant C > 0, depending only on the topological type of X, such that for every prime p > C there is no Z_p-action on X that is smooth with respect to any smooth structure on X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a closed, simply connected, smoothable topological 4-manifold whose intersection form $Q_X\colon H_2(X;\mathbb{Z})\times H_2(X;\mathbb{Z})\to \mathbb{Z}$ is even (i.e. $Q_X(\alpha,\alpha)\in 2\mathbb{Z}$ for every $\alpha\in H_2(X;\mathbb{Z})$) and whose signature $\sigma(X)$ is nonzero. For a prime $p$, let $\mathbb{Z}_p=\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, and call a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action on $X$ "smooth with respect to some smooth structure" if there exists a smooth structure on $X$ together with a smooth, effective $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action on the resulting smooth manifold inducing the given topological action.

Determine whether there exists a constant $C=C(X)>0$, depending only on the topological homeomorphism type of $X$, such that for every prime $p>C$ there is no $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action on $X$ which is smooth with respect to any smooth structure on $X$.
status_search_result: The question (attributed to Weimin Chen) asks for a topological-type-dependent prime bound above which no smooth Z/p-action exists on a simply connected smoothable 4-manifold with even form and nonzero signature. Recent work (e.g., Chen–Kwasik on exotic K3s, Montague's 2024 construction of non-smoothable Z/p-actions on Gompf nuclei for p≥5) provides families of non-smoothable prime-order actions, but no source found resolves the general existence of such a uniform bound C(X). The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Homologically trivial prime-order smooth actions on homotopy K3 surfaces
original_question: For any prime number p > 2, are there nontrivial smooth Z_p-actions on a homotopy K3 surface that act trivially on homology?
self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be a homotopy K3 surface, that is, a closed smooth 4-manifold homeomorphic to a (smooth) K3 surface. For a prime number $p > 2$, does there exist a nontrivial smooth action of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ on $X$ that acts trivially on the integral homology $H_*(X;\mathbb{Z})$? Determine, for each odd prime $p$, whether such a nontrivial homologically trivial smooth $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$-action on some homotopy K3 surface exists.
status_search_result: Web searches surface results for the involution case (p=2), where strong constraints on homologically trivial smooth involutions on K3 surfaces are known, but no source directly resolving the existence (or nonexistence) of nontrivial homologically trivial smooth $\mathbb{Z}/p$-actions on a homotopy K3 surface for odd primes p was found. The status appears unresolved in the available evidence.

context_brief: Open dominance question under general alpha-divergence
original_question: Consider the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance, under the special design assumption (AS1) used in the paper: m >= k >= 3, n = mN for a positive integer N, and the design matrix satisfies X = 1_N \otimes X~ = (X~', ..., X~')'. Under alpha-divergence loss D_alpha with -1 < alpha < 1, does the predictive density based on the same shrinkage prior pi_S,1(beta, sigma^2) = (beta' X~' X~ beta)^(1-k/2) (sigma^2)^(-2) improve on the best invariant predictive density, namely the generalized Bayes predictive density based on the right invariant prior pi_I,1(beta, sigma^2) = (sigma^2)^(-1)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a normal linear regression model with unknown variance:
  Y = X β + ε,    ε ~ N_n(0, σ² I_n),
where Y ∈ ℝ^n is the observed response, X is an n×k design matrix of full column rank k, β ∈ ℝ^k and σ² > 0 are unknown parameters. Let Ỹ ∈ ℝ^n be a future independent response satisfying Ỹ = X β + ε̃, ε̃ ~ N_n(0, σ² I_n), independently of Y.

Special design assumption (AS1). Assume m ≥ k ≥ 3 and that there exists a positive integer N and an m×k matrix X̃ of full column rank such that n = mN and
  X = 1_N ⊗ X̃,
so that X consists of N vertically stacked copies of X̃.

α-divergence loss. For −1 < α < 1, the α-divergence between a true predictive density p(ỹ | β, σ²) for Ỹ and a candidate predictive density q(ỹ) is
  D_α(p, q) = (4 / (1 − α²)) ∫ [ (1 − α)/2 · p(ỹ) + (1 + α)/2 · q(ỹ) − p(ỹ)^{(1−α)/2} q(ỹ)^{(1+α)/2} ] dỹ,
and the corresponding risk of a predictive density q(· | Y) is R_α(β, σ²; q) = E[ D_α(p(· | β, σ²), q(· | Y)) ].

Priors and predictive densities. Define
  π_{I,1}(β, σ²) = (σ²)^{−1}        (right-invariant prior),
  π_{S,1}(β, σ²) = (β' X̃' X̃ β)^{1 − k/2} · (σ²)^{−2}    (shrinkage prior).
Let q_{I,1}(ỹ | Y) and q_{S,1}(ỹ | Y) denote the (generalized) Bayes predictive densities of Ỹ given Y under the priors π_{I,1} and π_{S,1}, respectively. The predictive density q_{I,1} is the best invariant predictive density.

Question. Under assumption (AS1) and for every α with −1 < α < 1, does q_{S,1} dominate q_{I,1} under D_α-loss in the sense that
  R_α(β, σ²; q_{S,1}) ≤ R_α(β, σ²; q_{I,1})    for all (β, σ²) with β ≠ 0,
with strict inequality for at least one (β, σ²)?
category_tag: Bayesian predictive density estimation under alpha-divergence
status_search_result: The problem was explicitly posed as open. Subsequent work on predictive density estimation under α-divergence (e.g., a 2019 paper in Mathematical Methods of Statistics and a 2021 Bayesian Analysis article on "Optimal Shrinkage Estimation of Predictive Densities Under α-Divergences") addresses related multivariate-normal mean problems, but I could not verify from the searches whether the specific dominance question for the regression shrinkage prior π_{S,1} versus the right-invariant prior under (AS1) for −1 < α < 1 has been fully resolved.

original_question: Under D_1 loss for predictive density estimation in the normal linear regression model with unknown variance, and in the low-dimensional cases k = 1 or k = 2, can one construct Bayesian predictive densities that improve on the best invariant predictive density, even though improved non-Bayesian predictive densities are already known to exist in this setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the normal linear regression model with unknown variance. Let Y = Xβ + σε, where X is a known n×k design matrix of full column rank, β ∈ ℝ^k is an unknown regression coefficient vector, σ² > 0 is an unknown variance, and ε ~ N_n(0, I_n). One wishes to predict a future observation Ỹ = X̃β + σε̃, where X̃ is a known ñ×k design matrix and ε̃ ~ N_ñ(0, I_ñ) is independent of ε, by means of a predictive density p̂(ỹ | y) for Ỹ given Y = y.

The performance of a predictive density p̂(· | y) is measured under the D₁ loss
  D₁(β, σ²; p̂(· | y)) = ∫ {p(ỹ | β, σ²) − p̂(ỹ | y)} log{p(ỹ | β, σ²)/p̂(ỹ | y)} dỹ,
the symmetrized Kullback–Leibler divergence between the true density p(ỹ | β, σ²) and the predictive density p̂(· | y); the risk is the expectation of this loss over Y. The best invariant predictive density is the predictive density that minimizes the risk among all predictive densities equivariant under the natural group of location–scale transformations associated with (β, σ²).

A predictive density is called Bayesian if it is the posterior predictive density obtained from some (possibly improper) prior π(β, σ²): namely p̂_π(ỹ | y) = ∫ p(ỹ | β, σ²) π(β, σ² | y) dβ dσ².

Question: In the low-dimensional regimes k = 1 and k = 2, does there exist a (generalized) Bayesian predictive density p̂_π that strictly dominates the best invariant predictive density under D₁ risk, uniformly in (β, σ²)?
status_search_result: The problem is reported as solved: a class of improved hierarchical generalized Bayes predictive densities dominating the best invariant predictive density under D₁ loss has been constructed for k = 1 and k = 2 in the normal linear regression setting with unknown variance, extending the shrinkage-prior approach of Kobayashi–Komaki (2008) and George–Xu (2008).

original_question: For the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance, when the number of regression coefficients is k = 1 or k = 2 and the loss is alpha-divergence D_alpha with -1 <= alpha < 1, does the best invariant predictive density remain inadmissible? If it does, which Bayesian predictive density or class of Bayesian predictive densities improves upon it?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the normal linear regression prediction problem with unknown variance. Observe Y = Xβ + σε_Y ∈ R^n, where X is a known n×k design matrix of full column rank k, β ∈ R^k and σ^2 > 0 are unknown, and ε_Y ~ N_n(0, I_n). One wishes to predict a future independent observation Ỹ = X̃β + σε_{Ỹ} ∈ R^m, where X̃ is a known m×k design matrix of full column rank k and ε_{Ỹ} ~ N_m(0, I_m), independent of ε_Y.

A predictive density p̂(ỹ ; y) for Ỹ given Y is evaluated by the α-divergence loss
   D_α(p, p̂) = (4/(1−α^2)) ∫ [ 1 − (p̂(ỹ)/p(ỹ))^{(1−α)/2} ] p(ỹ) dỹ,    α ∈ (−1, 1),
with D_{−1} interpreted as the reverse Kullback–Leibler divergence (limit α → −1).

The model is invariant under the group of location–scale transformations (β, σ) ↦ (β + Xc/… , cσ) appropriate to this regression setting, and there is a unique best invariant predictive density p̂_I (the formal Bayes rule with respect to the right-invariant prior π(β, σ) ∝ 1/σ); p̂_I has constant frequentist risk under D_α.

Question. Suppose k ∈ {1, 2} and −1 ≤ α < 1.

(a) Is the best invariant predictive density p̂_I inadmissible under D_α loss; that is, does there exist a predictive density p̂ such that the risk R(β, σ; p̂) ≤ R(β, σ; p̂_I) for all (β, σ), with strict inequality for some (β, σ)?

(b) If so, exhibit a Bayesian predictive density (or a class of Bayesian predictive densities, e.g. arising from a hierarchical / shrinkage prior on β) that dominates p̂_I under D_α.
category_tag: Bayesian predictive density estimation under α-divergence
status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed Bayesian predictive density estimation under α-divergence loss for normal models, including harmonic-prior dominance results in dimensions ≥ 3 and hierarchical-prior constructions in linear regression. However, no source found explicitly resolves the low-dimensional cases k = 1, 2 for the full range −1 ≤ α < 1 in the unknown-variance regression setting; the status of this specific problem is not clearly established by available sources.

original_question: Find new examples of hyperkahler manifolds.
self_contained_problem:
A compact hyperkähler manifold is a compact, simply connected Kähler manifold $X$ of complex dimension $2n$ admitting a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic symplectic 2-form $\sigma \in H^0(X, \Omega^2_X)$ such that $H^0(X,\Omega^2_X) = \mathbb{C}\cdot\sigma$. Two hyperkähler manifolds are considered equivalent if they are deformation equivalent (i.e., they appear as fibers of a smooth proper holomorphic family with connected base in the category of complex manifolds). The currently known deformation classes of compact hyperkähler manifolds are: the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(S)$ of $n$ points on a K3 surface $S$ (for each $n\geq 1$); the generalized Kummer variety $K_n(A)$ associated to an abelian surface $A$ (for each $n\geq 1$); and the two sporadic examples $\mathrm{OG}_6$ and $\mathrm{OG}_{10}$ constructed by O'Grady in dimensions $6$ and $10$.

Problem: Construct a compact hyperkähler manifold that is not deformation equivalent to any of the four known families above, or prove that no other deformation classes exist.
status_search_result: The classification of compact hyperkähler manifolds remains a major open problem. As of 2026, only the four known deformation types are known: K3^[n], generalized Kummer K_n, OG6, and OG10. No new deformation classes have been constructed since O'Grady's examples (1999, 2003), and no classification result excluding new examples has been established. Recent surveys (e.g., by Debarre, Sawon, Beauville, Huybrechts) continue to list this as a central open question.

original_question: Let X and X' be hyperkahler manifolds of the same dimension. If there is a Hodge isometry lambda: H^2(X, Z) -> H^2(X', Z), determine what geometric relationship between X and X' follows, and whether one can force X and X' to be isomorphic by requiring lambda to preserve additional structure beyond the Hodge structure itself.
self_contained_problem:
A hyperkähler manifold is a simply connected compact Kähler manifold $X$ such that $H^0(X, \Omega_X^2)$ is generated by a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. The second integral cohomology $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ carries a pure weight-2 Hodge structure together with the integral Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki quadratic form, making it a lattice; an isomorphism of abelian groups $\lambda: H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \to H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$ is called a Hodge isometry if it preserves both the Hodge decomposition and the Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki form.

Let $X$ and $X'$ be hyperkähler manifolds of the same complex dimension and suppose there exists a Hodge isometry $\lambda: H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \to H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$.

(a) Determine what geometric relationship between $X$ and $X'$ must follow from the existence of such a $\lambda$ (e.g., deformation equivalence, bimeromorphic equivalence, or isomorphism).

(b) Identify additional structural conditions one may impose on $\lambda$ (beyond preservation of the Hodge structure and the Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki form) that force $X$ and $X'$ to be biholomorphic, and determine whether such conditions suffice in general.
status_search_result: Verbitsky's global Torelli theorem (2009, published in Duke Math. J. 2013, with an erratum) establishes that for hyperkähler manifolds of the same deformation type, the existence of a Hodge isometry $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \to H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$ that is a parallel transport operator is equivalent to $X$ and $X'$ being bimeromorphic, and that requiring the isometry to send a Kähler class to a Kähler class yields an isomorphism. However, in general a Hodge isometry alone need not even imply that $X$ and $X'$ are deformation equivalent: counterexamples to a naive Hodge-theoretic Torelli statement are known beyond the K3$^{[n]}$ case (e.g., for some OG-type or non-prime-power $n-1$ cases). So the question is partially solved: definitive in the deformation-equivalent / parallel-transport setting, but open/negative in full generality.

original_question: For a hyperkahler manifold X, determine which integral quadratic forms can occur as the Beauville-Bogomolov form q on H^2(X, Z), whether q must always be even, and which values can occur for the Fujiki constant f_X defined by the relation integral_X alpha^(2r) = f_X q(alpha)^r in dimension 2r.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a compact, simply connected, irreducible hyperkähler (holomorphic symplectic) manifold of complex dimension 2r, that is, X is Kähler, simply connected, and H^0(X, Ω_X^2) is generated by an everywhere non-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. There exists a canonical primitive integral quadratic form

   q : H^2(X, Z) → Z,

of signature (3, b_2(X) − 3), called the Beauville–Bogomolov form, together with a positive rational number f_X (the Fujiki constant) satisfying the Fujiki relation

   ∫_X α^{2r} = f_X · q(α)^r   for every α ∈ H^2(X, Z).

Both q and f_X depend only on the oriented topological type of X.

Address the following three questions.

(a) Is the integral quadratic form q necessarily even, i.e. does q(α) ∈ 2Z hold for every α ∈ H^2(X, Z)?

(b) More generally, classify which integral quadratic lattices of signature (3, b_2 − 3) can be realized as (H^2(X, Z), q) for some irreducible hyperkähler manifold X.

(c) Determine the set of possible values of the Fujiki constant f_X as X ranges over all irreducible hyperkähler manifolds.
status_search_result: All currently known deformation types of irreducible hyperkähler manifolds (K3^[n], generalized Kummer Kum_n, and O'Grady's OG6 and OG10) have even Beauville–Bogomolov form, and their Beauville lattices and Fujiki constants are explicitly tabulated in expository sources such as Debarre's lectures and the hyperkaehler.info reference site. However, no general proof that q must be even has been published, and the broader classification problem of which lattices and Fujiki constants occur is tied to the classification of hyperkähler deformation types, which remains a major open problem.

original_question: Determine whether there are only finitely many hyperkahler manifolds, up to deformation, in each dimension.
self_contained_problem:
A compact connected complex manifold $X$ of complex dimension $2n$ is called an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (hyperkähler) manifold if $X$ is simply connected, Kähler, and $H^0(X,\Omega_X^2)$ is spanned by an everywhere non-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. Two such manifolds $X_0$ and $X_1$ are said to be deformation equivalent if there exists a smooth proper holomorphic family $\mathcal{X} \to B$ over a connected base $B$ whose fibers are irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds and which contains both $X_0$ and $X_1$ as fibers.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, the set of deformation equivalence classes of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of complex dimension $2n$ is finite.
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. Only four deformation types are currently known in each even complex dimension ≥ 4 (the Hilbert schemes of K3 surfaces, generalized Kummer varieties, and the two O'Grady examples). Partial finiteness results are known under additional hypotheses: Huybrechts proved finiteness within each fixed Beauville–Bogomolov lattice type, and further finiteness theorems (due to Charles, Sawon, and others) hold for polarized families or under topological/lattice constraints, but unconditional finiteness in each dimension is unproven.

original_question: For a hyperkahler fourfold X, determine whether additional values of the second Betti number b2 can be excluded beyond the currently known cases, especially whether b2 = 3 can occur at all; and if b2 = 23, determine whether X must be deformation equivalent to the Hilbert square S^[2] of a K3 surface.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be an irreducible compact hyperkähler fourfold, i.e., a simply connected compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension 4 such that H^0(X, Ω_X^2) is generated by an everywhere non-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. Let b_2(X) denote the second Betti number of X. It is known (Guan) that either b_2(X) = 23, or 3 ≤ b_2(X) ≤ 8.

(a) Determine whether further values of b_2(X) in the range {3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8} can be excluded; in particular, decide whether b_2(X) = 3 can ever occur for an irreducible compact hyperkähler fourfold.

(b) Suppose b_2(X) = 23. Determine whether X must be deformation equivalent to the Hilbert square S^{[2]} of a K3 surface S (the Hilbert scheme of length-2 zero-dimensional subschemes of S).
status_search_result: Guan's bounds (b_2 ∈ {3,...,8} ∪ {23}) remain the state of the art for irreducible compact hyperkähler fourfolds. No example with b_2 = 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7 is known, but no further values have been excluded in general; the only known examples have b_2 = 7 (generalized Kummer K_2) or b_2 = 23 (Hilbert square of K3, OG6 in dim 4 doesn't apply). The deformation-uniqueness question for b_2 = 23 is also still open: it is not known whether a hyperkähler fourfold with b_2 = 23 must be deformation equivalent to S^{[2]}. Recent surveys (Debarre 2022; Sawon, Kim–Laza et al.) reiterate these as open problems.

original_question: Let X be a hyperkahler manifold of dimension 2r. If L is a nontrivial nef line bundle on X with Beauville-Bogomolov square q(L) = 0, determine whether there must exist a Lagrangian fibration f: X -> P^r such that L = f^* O_{P^r}(k) for some integer k >= 1. More generally, determine whether X is birational to a hyperkahler manifold X' admitting a Lagrangian fibration X' -> P^r exactly when X carries a nontrivial line bundle L with q(L) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a compact hyperkähler manifold of complex dimension 2r; that is, X is a simply connected compact Kähler manifold such that H^0(X, Ω^2_X) is generated by an everywhere non-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. Let q denote the Beauville–Bogomolov–Fujiki quadratic form on H^2(X, Z). A Lagrangian fibration on X is a surjective holomorphic map with connected fibers f: X → B onto a normal projective base B of dimension r, whose general fiber is a Lagrangian subvariety with respect to the holomorphic symplectic form; in this hyperkähler setting the base B is necessarily isomorphic to P^r whenever it is smooth.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(a) If L is a nontrivial nef line bundle on X with q(L) = 0, then there exists a Lagrangian fibration f: X → P^r and an integer k ≥ 1 such that L ≅ f^* O_{P^r}(k).

(b) There exists a hyperkähler manifold X' bimeromorphic to X admitting a Lagrangian fibration X' → P^r if and only if X carries a line bundle L ≇ O_X with q(L) = 0.
status_search_result: This is the hyperkähler SYZ conjecture. It is established for all currently known deformation types of compact hyperkähler manifolds (e.g. K3^[n], generalized Kummer, OG6, OG10) through work of Matsushita, Bayer–Macrì, Markman, and others, but it remains open as a general statement for arbitrary compact hyperkähler manifolds.

original_question: Does every hyperkahler manifold admit a deformation that carries a Lagrangian fibration?
self_contained_problem:
A compact hyperkähler manifold is a simply connected compact Kähler manifold $X$ such that $H^0(X, \Omega_X^2)$ is generated by a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic 2-form $\sigma$ (an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold). A holomorphic Lagrangian fibration on $X$ is a surjective holomorphic map $f : X \to B$ with connected fibers onto a normal Kähler base $B$ with $0 < \dim B < \dim X$, whose general fiber is a Lagrangian submanifold with respect to $\sigma$ (equivalently, $\sigma$ restricts to zero on the smooth fibers); by results of Matsushita such a fibration automatically has $\dim B = \tfrac{1}{2}\dim X$ and general fiber an abelian variety. A deformation of $X$ means a smooth proper family $\mathcal{X} \to \Delta$ of compact hyperkähler manifolds over a connected complex base $\Delta$ with a distinguished fiber isomorphic to $X$.

Question: Does every compact hyperkähler manifold $X$ admit a deformation $\mathcal{X} \to \Delta$ such that some fiber $\mathcal{X}_t$ carries a holomorphic Lagrangian fibration?
status_search_result: This is the (weak form of the) hyperkähler SYZ conjecture, also referred to as the Huybrechts–Sawon conjecture (with related earlier formulations by Hassett–Tschinkel). It is verified for the known deformation types in birational/partial forms (e.g., for K3^[n], generalized Kummer, OG6, OG10 types via Matsushita-type arguments and case studies), but the general statement remains open as of recent literature (2024–2025).

original_question: Let X be a hyperkahler manifold and let T subset X be a Lagrangian submanifold that is a complex torus. Must T occur as a fibre of a Lagrangian fibration X -> P^r, or at least of a birational model of such a fibration?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact hyperkähler manifold (i.e., a simply connected compact Kähler manifold admitting a holomorphic symplectic 2-form $\sigma$ that is everywhere non-degenerate and unique up to scalar). Let $T \subset X$ be a Lagrangian submanifold (so $\dim T = \tfrac{1}{2}\dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$ and $\sigma|_T \equiv 0$) that is biholomorphic to a complex torus.

(a) Does there necessarily exist a surjective holomorphic map with connected fibres $f : X \to \mathbb{P}^r$ (where $r = \tfrac{1}{2}\dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$) such that $T$ occurs as a fibre of $f$? (By results of Matsushita, any such non-trivial fibration is automatically a Lagrangian fibration with general fibre an abelian variety and base $\mathbb{P}^r$.)

(b) More weakly, must there exist a hyperkähler manifold $X'$ that is bimeromorphic to $X$ and a Lagrangian fibration $f' : X' \to \mathbb{P}^r$ such that the proper transform of $T$ in $X'$ is a fibre of $f'$?
status_search_result: The question has been resolved in significant cases but not fully in general. Greb–Lehn–Rollenske (2011) settled the non-projective case affirmatively. Hwang–Weiss and related work established that in the projective case, under additional topological/deformation hypotheses on (X,T), an almost holomorphic Lagrangian fibration exists, together with a smooth birational model on which the fibration becomes holomorphic; the bimeromorphic version is thereby known in many situations. For hyperkähler fourfolds, a holomorphic Lagrangian fibration with the given torus as a fibre always exists. The general projective case remains open.

original_question: For a polarized K3 surface S of genus g, describe the general projective deformation of S[2], for some choice of polarization on S[2], or at least find more examples of locally complete projective families. Ask the same question for S[r] with r >= 3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a smooth complex projective K3 surface, polarized by an ample line bundle $H$ with $H^2 = 2g-2$ (so $S$ has genus $g$). For an integer $r \geq 2$, let $S^{[r]}$ denote the Hilbert scheme of length-$r$ zero-dimensional subschemes of $S$; this is a smooth projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic variety of dimension $2r$ deforming as a hyperkähler manifold of $K3^{[r]}$-type. The polarization $H$ on $S$ together with a choice of additional class induces polarizations on $S^{[r]}$; deforming the pair $(S^{[r]}, L)$ in the moduli space of polarized hyperkähler varieties of $K3^{[r]}$-type yields a $20$-dimensional family inside the $21$-dimensional deformation space, and a "locally complete projective family" is a family of polarized hyperkähler varieties of $K3^{[r]}$-type whose image in moduli has full dimension $21$.

(a) For each genus $g \in \{2, 3, 4, \dots\}$ and for some choice of polarization on $S^{[2]}$, give an explicit projective-geometric description of the general projective deformation of $S^{[2]}$, or at least exhibit new examples of locally complete projective families of polarized hyperkähler fourfolds of $K3^{[2]}$-type beyond the previously known cases (Beauville–Donagi cubic fourfolds, varieties of sums of powers, Debarre–Voisin, and Iliev–Ranestad).

(b) Solve the analogous problem for $S^{[r]}$ with $r \geq 3$: produce locally complete projective families of polarized hyperkähler $2r$-folds of $K3^{[r]}$-type and describe the general projective deformation.
category_tag: Hyperkähler varieties and Hilbert schemes of K3 surfaces
status_search_result: The problem remains a guiding open question in hyperkähler geometry, but new examples and partial descriptions have appeared. Recent work on projective models for Hilbert squares of K3 surfaces (e.g., a 2025 preprint and earlier results on ⟨2⟩-polarized Hilbert squares of generic K3 surfaces, and Debarre–Voisin / Iliev–Ranestad type constructions) provides projective descriptions and additional locally complete families for $S^{[2]}$, particularly in low genus and for genera 7 and 8 via Mukai models. A complete classification, and the analogous problem for $S^{[r]}$ with $r \geq 3$, remains open.

original_question: Let X be a projective hyperkahler manifold. If z in CH(X) is a Chow class that is a polynomial in divisor classes D1, ..., Dk from Pic(X) and in the Chern classes c_i(X), and if the cohomology class of z vanishes in H^*(X, Z), must z already vanish in the Chow ring?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a projective hyperkähler manifold; that is, a simply connected smooth projective complex variety such that $H^0(X,\Omega_X^2)$ is spanned by a nowhere-degenerate holomorphic 2-form. Let $\mathrm{CH}(X)$ denote the Chow ring of $X$ with rational (or integral) coefficients, and let $\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ denote its Picard group. Let $c_i(X)\in\mathrm{CH}(X)$ denote the Chern classes of the tangent bundle of $X$, and let $\mathrm{cl}\colon \mathrm{CH}(X)\to H^*(X,\mathbb{Z})$ be the cycle class map.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every choice of divisor classes $D_1,\dots,D_k\in\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ and every class $z\in\mathrm{CH}(X)$ that can be written as a polynomial in $D_1,\dots,D_k$ and in the Chern classes $c_1(X),\dots,c_{\dim X}(X)$, the implication
$$\mathrm{cl}(z)=0\ \text{in}\ H^*(X,\mathbb{Z})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad z=0\ \text{in}\ \mathrm{CH}(X)$$
holds. Equivalently, show that the subring of $\mathrm{CH}(X)$ generated by $\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ and the Chern classes of $X$ injects into the cohomology ring of $X$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (Beauville–Voisin) remains open in general for arbitrary projective hyperkähler manifolds. It has been verified in several cases: Hilbert schemes of points on K3 surfaces (Voisin), generalized Kummer varieties, double EPW sextics (Laterveer, 2023), and partial results for LLSS eightfolds. No proof in full generality is known.

original_question: Let X be a Fano complex manifold with a holomorphic Poisson structure, and for even s let X_{<=s} be the union of the loci X_k where the Poisson structure has rank k for k <= s. Must X_{<=s} contain a component of dimension greater than s?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Fano complex manifold (i.e., a compact complex manifold whose anticanonical bundle $-K_X$ is ample) endowed with a holomorphic Poisson structure $\tau \in H^0(X, \wedge^2 T_X)$. The Poisson bivector induces a skew-symmetric bundle map $\tau^\sharp : \Omega^1_X \to T_X$, and at every point $x \in X$ the rank of $\tau$ at $x$ is defined as the rank of $\tau^\sharp(x)$ (which is necessarily an even integer). For each even integer $k \ge 0$, define
\[ X_k := \{ x \in X : \mathrm{rk}\, \tau(x) = k \}, \qquad X_{\le s} := \bigsqcup_{\substack{k \le s \\ k \text{ even}}} X_k. \]
Prove or disprove: for every even integer $s$ with $s < \dim_{\mathbb{C}} X$, the closed subset $X_{\le s}$ contains an irreducible component of dimension strictly greater than $s$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (Bondal's rank conjecture on degeneracy loci of holomorphic Poisson structures on Fano manifolds) appears to remain open in general. Polishchuk established a weaker bound, implying the conjecture for Poisson structures of generic rank ≤ 2 and for Fano varieties of dimension ≤ 3. Gualtieri–Pym and subsequent works (including a 2026 note by Aza) provide further partial evidence, including for Fano fourfolds, but the full conjecture is still cited as a conjecture in recent literature.

original_question: Let X be a compact complex manifold with a holomorphic Poisson structure. If X_s, the locus where the Poisson structure has rank s, is non-empty, must it contain a component of dimension greater than s?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold equipped with a holomorphic Poisson structure, i.e. a holomorphic bivector field $\tau \in H^0(X, \wedge^2 TX)$ satisfying $[\tau,\tau] = 0$ with respect to the Schouten bracket. At each point $x \in X$, the bivector $\tau(x)$ has an even rank, so $X$ admits the disjoint stratification
$$X = \bigsqcup_{s \text{ even}} X_s, \qquad X_s := \{x \in X : \mathrm{rk}\,\tau(x) = s\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every even integer $s \geq 0$ such that $X_s$ is non-empty, the stratum $X_s$ contains an irreducible component of complex dimension strictly greater than $s$.
status_search_result: This is known as Bondal's conjecture on Poisson degeneracy loci. It is established in several special cases (e.g., Fano varieties of dimension ≤3, Fano fourfolds, Poisson structures of generic rank ≤2, and the top non-trivial degeneracy stratum on projective space and on Poisson structures of maximal rank), and supporting partial results (such as the rank ≤2n−2 locus being a non-empty hypersurface in connected Fano Poisson 2n-folds) are established by Gualtieri–Pym and others. No general proof or counterexample appears to have been published, so the conjecture remains partially solved in general.

original_question: Classify projective contact manifolds: is every projective contact manifold either the projectivized cotangent bundle P(T^*M) of a compact complex manifold M or the closed contact Fano orbit X_g associated with a simple complex Lie algebra g?
self_contained_problem:
A compact complex manifold $Z$ of complex dimension $2n+1$ is called a holomorphic contact manifold if there exists a holomorphic line bundle $L \to Z$ together with a holomorphic 1-form $\theta \in H^0(Z, \Omega^1_Z \otimes L)$ such that $\theta \wedge (d\theta)^n$ is a nowhere-vanishing section of $K_Z \otimes L^{n+1}$; equivalently, the kernel $F \subset TZ$ of $\theta$ is a corank-one holomorphic distribution that is maximally non-integrable. A projective contact manifold is a holomorphic contact manifold whose underlying complex manifold is projective.

Two known families of projective contact manifolds are:

(a) For any compact complex manifold $M$, the projectivized cotangent bundle $\mathbb{P}(T^*M)$, equipped with its canonical contact structure coming from the Liouville form on $T^*M$.

(b) For any simple complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, let $G$ be the adjoint group of $\mathfrak{g}$ acting on the projective space $\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{g})$. Then this action admits a unique closed orbit $X_{\mathfrak{g}} \subset \mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{g})$ (every other orbit contains $X_{\mathfrak{g}}$ in its closure), and $X_{\mathfrak{g}}$ is a Fano manifold carrying a natural homogeneous holomorphic contact structure.

Question: Prove or disprove that every projective contact manifold is biholomorphic, as a contact manifold, to one of type (a) or type (b).
status_search_result: The classification (known as the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture) remains open in full generality as of 2024. Significant partial results exist: it is known in low dimensions (contact Fano manifolds of dimension ≤ 9 with a Kähler–Einstein metric, equivalently positive quaternion-Kähler manifolds of real dimension ≤ 16), for contact Fano manifolds with sufficiently large reductive automorphism group (rank ≥ max(2,(n-3)/2) on a (2n+1)-dimensional contact Fano), and in cases where the contact line bundle does not generate $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$.

original_question: Is every contact Fano manifold homogeneous?
self_contained_problem:
A complex contact manifold is a connected complex manifold $X$ of odd complex dimension $2n+1$ equipped with a holomorphic line bundle $L \to X$ and a holomorphic 1-form $\theta \in H^0(X, \Omega^1_X \otimes L)$ such that $\theta \wedge (d\theta)^n$ is a nowhere-vanishing section of $K_X \otimes L^{n+1}$ (equivalently, the kernel of $\theta$ defines a maximally non-integrable holomorphic distribution of corank one). A smooth complex projective variety $X$ is called Fano if its anticanonical line bundle $-K_X$ is ample. A contact Fano manifold is a smooth complex projective Fano variety carrying such a holomorphic contact structure. A complex manifold $X$ is called homogeneous if its biholomorphism group acts transitively on $X$.

Question: Is every contact Fano manifold homogeneous?
status_search_result: This is the well-known LeBrun–Salamon conjecture (in its complex-geometric formulation). It remains open in general. original_question: Are the only compact quaternion-Kahler manifolds with positive scalar curvature homogeneous?
self_contained_problem:
A Riemannian manifold $(M^{4n}, g)$ of real dimension $4n \geq 4$ is called quaternion-Kähler if its holonomy group is contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n)\cdot\mathrm{Sp}(1) \subset \mathrm{SO}(4n)$. Every such manifold is automatically Einstein, so its scalar curvature is constant. The known compact examples with positive scalar curvature are the so-called Wolf spaces, which are symmetric spaces of compact type associated to compact simple Lie groups (e.g. $\mathbb{HP}^n$, $\mathrm{Gr}_2(\mathbb{C}^{n+2})$, $\widetilde{\mathrm{Gr}}_4(\mathbb{R}^{n+4})$, and five exceptional examples), and these are homogeneous.

Prove or disprove: every compact quaternion-Kähler manifold of positive scalar curvature is homogeneous (equivalently, isometric to a Wolf space).
status_search_result: This is the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. It remains open in general. It is known to hold in real dimensions 4 (Hitchin), 8 (Poon–Salamon, LeBrun–Salamon), and 12 and 16 (following work of Buczyński–Wiśniewski and others). The conjecture is unresolved for real dimension ≥ 20, and continues to be the subject of active research as of 2024–2025.

original_question: Let a polygon with at least four sides be circumscribed to a circle, and let D consist of its diagonals together with the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides. The paper proves that D contains at least three concurrent lines. Determine conditions under which more than three of these lines are concurrent.
self_contained_problem:
Let $P = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_n$ be a convex polygon with $n \ge 4$ sides that is circumscribed to a circle $\omega$ (i.e., every side of $P$ is tangent to $\omega$). For each side $A_i A_{i+1}$ let $T_i$ denote its point of tangency with $\omega$. Define the family of lines
$$\mathcal{D} = \{A_i A_j : 1 \le i < j \le n,\ j - i 
ot\equiv \pm 1 \pmod{n}\} \;\cup\; \{T_i T_j : 1 \le i < j \le n,\ j - i 
ot\equiv \pm 1 \pmod{n}\},$$
that is, the set consisting of all diagonals of $P$ together with all lines joining the tangency points of pairs of non-adjacent sides.

It is known that $\mathcal{D}$ always contains at least three concurrent lines. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $P$ (and on $n$) under which more than three lines of $\mathcal{D}$ pass through a single point, and describe explicitly the families of circumscribed polygons for which such higher-order concurrences occur.
status_search_result: No specific source addressing this exact higher-order concurrency question for tangential $n$-gons (combining all diagonals together with all chords of non-adjacent contact points) was located. Related classical results — Newton's theorem for tangential quadrilaterals (the two diagonals and the two contact chords concur) and Brianchon's theorem for tangential hexagons (the three main diagonals concur) — give baseline cases of three concurrent lines, but a general characterization of when strictly more than three lines from this family concur does not appear in standard references found.

original_question: For a polygon circumscribed to a circle, with D defined as the set of diagonals and the lines joining the points of contact of two non-adjacent sides, determine the maximum possible number of concurrent lines in D and characterize the configurations in which this maximum is attained.

(b) all "contact chords", i.e., lines joining the points of tangency of any two non-adjacent sides of P with ω.

original_question: Replace the circle in the circumscribed-polygon concurrency problem by an ellipse, and consider a polygon all of whose sides are tangent to that ellipse. Let $E \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be an ellipse, and let $P = A_1 A_2 \cdots A_n$ ($n \geq 4$) be a polygon, called "ellipso-scribed" about $E$, all of whose sides are tangent to $E$, with $E$ contained in the interior of $P$. (i) all diagonals of $P$ (i.e., lines $A_i A_j$ with $|i-j| \not\equiv 0,1 \pmod{n}$), and

Determine, as a function of $n$ (and the combinatorial type of $P$), the maximum possible number of concurrencies among the lines in $\mathcal{L}(P)$, where a concurrency means a point through which at least three of these lines pass; equivalently, characterize all triples (or larger subfamilies) of lines in $\mathcal{L}(P)$ that must, or may, meet at a single point for an arbitrary ellipso-scribed polygon.

context_brief: Polygon generalization of a cevian product identity
original_question: Generalize the following triangle identity from cevians to polygons: if cevians AA1, BB1, and CC1 in triangle ABC intersect at P, then (|PA|/|PA1|) (|PB|/|PB1|) (|PC|/|PC1|) = (|AB| |BC| |CA|) / (|A1B| |B1C| |C1A|). Find the corresponding polygon statement and prove it.
self_contained_problem:
In a triangle $ABC$, let three cevians $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ (with $A_1\in BC$, $B_1\in CA$, $C_1\in AB$) be concurrent at a point $P$. Then the following identity holds:
$$\frac{|PA|}{|PA_1|}\cdot\frac{|PB|}{|PB_1|}\cdot\frac{|PC|}{|PC_1|} \;=\; \frac{|AB|\cdot|BC|\cdot|CA|}{|A_1B|\cdot|B_1C|\cdot|C_1A|}.$$

Formulate and prove the analogous statement for an arbitrary (convex) polygon. More precisely: let $A_1A_2\cdots A_n$ be a convex polygon ($n\ge 3$) in the Euclidean plane, and for each vertex $A_i$ let $B_i$ be a point on a designated side (or diagonal) of the polygon such that the $n$ cevian-like segments $A_iB_i$ are all concurrent at a common point $P$. Determine an identity, generalizing the triangle identity above, that relates the ratios $|PA_i|/|PB_i|$ to ratios of side lengths (or diagonal lengths) of the polygon, and give a complete proof of this identity.

original_question: Let A1A2...Am be a polygon and let P be a point inside it. Drop perpendiculars from P to each side AiAi+1, and let Ai' be the foot of the perpendicular on AiAi+1. The polygon A1'A2'...Am' is the pedal polygon of P. Determine what properties this pedal polygon must satisfy.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A_1 A_2 \dots A_m$ be a polygon in the Euclidean plane (with $m \ge 3$), and let $P$ be a point in its interior. For each side $A_i A_{i+1}$ (indices taken modulo $m$), let $A_i'$ denote the foot of the perpendicular dropped from $P$ to the line containing $A_i A_{i+1}$. The polygon $A_1' A_2' \dots A_m'$ is called the pedal polygon of $P$ with respect to $A_1 A_2 \dots A_m$, generalizing the classical notion of the pedal triangle.

Investigate and determine the geometric properties of this pedal polygon. In particular:
(a) Derive formulas or relations for the side lengths $A_i' A_{i+1}'$ in terms of the original polygon, the distances $P A_i$, and the angles at $P$.
(b) Determine conditions on the polygon $A_1 \dots A_m$ and on the pedal point $P$ under which the pedal polygon is convex, simple (non-self-intersecting), cyclic, similar to the original polygon, or degenerates onto a line (a generalized Simson-line condition).
(c) Establish a generalization of Simson's theorem characterizing those points $P$ for which $A_1', A_2', \dots, A_m'$ are collinear, if any such points exist for $m \ge 4$.
(d) Express the area of the pedal polygon in terms of $P$ and the original polygon, and identify the location of $P$ that extremizes this area.
status_search_result: The question as posed is an open-ended request to generalize properties of the pedal triangle to pedal polygons; it is not a single sharply formulated conjecture with a definite yes/no answer. While many partial results exist for pedal triangles and for cyclic polygons, no comprehensive resolution of the general pedal-polygon properties question has been verified, so the status is recorded as unknown.

original_question: Let A1A2...An be a polyhedron and let P be a point inside it. From P draw perpendiculars to each edge AiAj, and let Aij' be the foot of the perpendicular on the edge AiAj. Study the resulting edge pedal polyhedron and determine its geometric properties.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a (convex) polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with vertices $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ and edge set $E(\mathcal{P}) = \{A_iA_j : (i,j) \in I\}$, and let $P$ be a point in the interior of $\mathcal{P}$. For each edge $A_iA_j \in E(\mathcal{P})$, let $A'_{ij}$ denote the foot of the perpendicular dropped from $P$ onto the line containing $A_iA_j$ (assume $P$ is chosen so that each $A'_{ij}$ lies on the corresponding edge). Define the \emph{edge pedal polyhedron} of $\mathcal{P}$ with respect to $P$ to be the polyhedron whose vertices are the points $\{A'_{ij}\}_{(i,j)\in I}$, with combinatorial structure inherited from $\mathcal{P}$ in a natural way (e.g., $A'_{ij}$ and $A'_{ik}$ are joined when edges $A_iA_j$ and $A_iA_k$ share the vertex $A_i$, and faces are formed from the feet of perpendiculars to edges bounding each face of $\mathcal{P}$).

Investigate and determine the geometric properties of this edge pedal polyhedron. In particular:
(a) For which polyhedra $\mathcal{P}$ and points $P$ is the construction well-defined (each foot lies in the relative interior of its edge)?
(b) Express the edge lengths, face areas, dihedral angles, and volume of the edge pedal polyhedron in terms of the geometry of $\mathcal{P}$ and the position of $P$.
(c) Identify points $P$ for which the edge pedal polyhedron has distinguished properties (e.g., maximum/minimum volume, regularity, inscribability in a sphere, similarity to $\mathcal{P}$).
(d) State and prove a three-dimensional analogue of the classical pedal-triangle relations (such as Simson's theorem or Euler's pedal-triangle area formula) for this construction.
status_search_result: No published results addressing the geometric properties of the "edge pedal polyhedron" defined by feet of perpendiculars from an interior point onto all edges were located. The problem is posed as an open generalization of the planar pedal-triangle construction and its current status appears unresolved in the literature.

original_question: Let A1A2...An be a polyhedron and let P be a point inside it. From P draw perpendiculars to each face Fi, and let Ai' be the foot of the perpendicular on Fi. The resulting polyhedron A1'A2'...Ap', where p is the number of faces, is a face pedal polyhedron. Determine what properties this face pedal polyhedron has.

Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with faces $F_1, F_2, \ldots, F_p$, and let $P$ be a point in the interior of $\mathcal{P}$. For each $i \in \{1, \ldots, p\}$, let $A_i'$ denote the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to the plane containing the face $F_i$. The convex hull (or polyhedron) determined by the points $A_1', A_2', \ldots, A_p'$ is called the face pedal polyhedron of $\mathcal{P}$ with respect to $P$.

Determine the geometric properties of this face pedal polyhedron: in particular, characterize its combinatorial structure, its volume, its surface area, and its shape, in terms of the polyhedron $\mathcal{P}$ and the position of the point $P$. Establish three-dimensional analogues (if any) of the classical pedal-triangle theorems (such as Simson's line condition, the volume formula, and the iterated pedal property) for this construction.

original_question: Generalize the circle-locus theorem of Problem 9 to 3D. Let two spheres intersect in a circle C, let a line through a point of C meet the two sphere surfaces again at M1 and M2, and let M divide M1M2 in the ratio k. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be two spheres in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with centers $O_1, O_2$ and radii $r_1, r_2$, intersecting in a circle $C$ (so $|O_1 O_2| < r_1 + r_2$ and the spheres are not tangent). context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for left D-Chebyshev convexity
original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The Bregman distance induced by f is D(x, y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x - y> for y in U. The set C is called left D-Chebyshev when, for every y in U, the left nearest-points map P_left,C(y) = {x in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(z, y)} is a singleton. It is known that if f is supercoercive and C is left D-Chebyshev, then C is convex. Is the supercoercivity assumption actually necessary for that convexity conclusion?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f : X \to [-\infty, +\infty]$ be a convex Legendre function in the sense of Bauschke–Borwein–Combettes; that is, $f$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex. Set $U = \operatorname{int}\,\operatorname{dom} f$, which is a nonempty open convex set on which $f$ is differentiable. The Bregman distance induced by $f$ is
$$D(x,y) = f(x) - f(y) - \langle \nabla f(y), x - y\rangle, \qquad y \in U,\ x \in X,$$
with the convention $D(x,y) = +\infty$ when $f(x) = +\infty$. Recall that $f$ is called supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty} f(x)/\|x\| = +\infty$.

Let $C$ be a nonempty closed subset of $U$. For $y \in U$ define the left Bregman nearest-point map
$$\overleftarrow{P}_C(y) = \{x \in C : D(x,y) = \inf_{z \in C} D(z,y)\}.$$
The set $C$ is called left $D$-Chebyshev if $\overleftarrow{P}_C(y)$ is a singleton for every $y \in U$.

It is known that if $f$ is supercoercive and $C \subseteq U$ is closed and left $D$-Chebyshev, then $C$ is convex.

Question: Is the supercoercivity hypothesis on $f$ essential? Equivalently, does there exist a convex Legendre function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is not supercoercive together with a nonempty closed left $D$-Chebyshev subset $C \subseteq U$ that fails to be convex? Or, can the implication "left $D$-Chebyshev $\Rightarrow$ convex" be proved without assuming supercoercivity?
status_search_result: A subsequent survey on Chebyshev/Klee sets with respect to Bregman distances explicitly lists the necessity of the supercoercivity hypothesis as an open problem, and no later resolution appears in the literature reachable via search. Therefore the problem appears to remain open.
