original_question: Fix a prime p and integers r <= s. Assuming p^r Br(F) is generated by cyclic algebras, what is the minimal number l_F(p^r, p^s) such that every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of that many cyclic algebras of degree p^r?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ denote the Brauer group of $F$, and for an integer $n\ge 1$, let ${}_n\mathrm{Br}(F)$ denote the $n$-torsion subgroup of $\mathrm{Br}(F)$. Recall that a central simple $F$-algebra $C$ of degree $n$ is called cyclic if it contains a strictly maximal subfield that is a cyclic Galois extension of $F$ of degree $n$; equivalently, $C\cong (E/F,\sigma,a)$ for some cyclic Galois extension $E/F$ of degree $n$, generator $\sigma$ of $\mathrm{Gal}(E/F)$, and $a\in F^\times$.

Fix integers $1\le r\le s$, and assume that ${}_{p^r}\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is generated (as an abelian group) by Brauer classes of cyclic $F$-algebras of degree $p^r$. For every central simple $F$-algebra $A$ of degree $p^s$ whose Brauer class lies in ${}_{p^r}\mathrm{Br}(F)$ (i.e.\ has period dividing $p^r$), define
$$\ell(A)=\min\Bigl\{m\ge 0 : [A]=\sum_{i=1}^m [C_i] \text{ in }\mathrm{Br}(F),\text{ with each }C_i\text{ a cyclic }F\text{-algebra of degree }p^r\Bigr\},$$
and set
$$\ell_F(p^r,p^s)=\sup_A \ell(A),$$
the supremum being taken over all such $A$.

Determine $\ell_F(p^r,p^s)$.
status_search_result: The problem of computing the symbol length $\ell_F(p^r,p^s)$ for central simple algebras of degree $p^s$ and period dividing $p^r$, under the assumption that the $p^r$-torsion of the Brauer group is generated by cyclic algebras, is a well-known open problem. Subsequent work has provided partial bounds in special situations (e.g., function fields of $p$-adic curves, positive characteristic), but no general formula is known.

original_question: For primes p >= 3, can one prove a finite upper bound for the symbol lengths l_F(p, p^2) and l_F(p^2, p^2)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and $p \geq 3$ a prime such that $\operatorname{char}(F) \neq p$ and $F$ contains a primitive $p^2$-th root of unity. For integers $m, n \geq 1$ with $m \mid n$, write ${}_m\mathrm{Br}(F)$ for the $m$-torsion subgroup of the Brauer group of $F$, and define the symbol length
$$\ell_F(m,n) \;=\; \sup\Bigl\{\, r \;:\; \text{some class in } {}_m\mathrm{Br}(F) \text{ requires at least } r \text{ degree-}n \text{ cyclic symbol algebras to express}\,\Bigr\},$$
i.e.\ the smallest integer $\ell$ (or $\infty$) such that every element of ${}_m\mathrm{Br}(F)$ is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of at most $\ell$ cyclic algebras of degree $n$ over $F$. Equivalently, via the Merkurjev–Suslin theorem, $\ell_F(m,n)$ is the minimum number of symbols $(a,b)_{\zeta_n}$ needed to write any element of ${}_m\mathrm{Br}(F)$.

Assume $F$ has finite Brauer $p$-dimension, so that $\ell_F(p,p)$ and $\ell_F(p^2,p)$ are known to be finite. The problem asks: for every prime $p \geq 3$, prove a finite upper bound for the symbol lengths
$$\ell_F(p,\, p^2) \quad \text{and} \quad \ell_F(p^2,\, p^2),$$
i.e.\ bound the number of degree-$p^2$ cyclic symbol algebras needed to express an arbitrary element of $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ of exponent dividing $p$ (resp.\ dividing $p^2$), in terms of invariants of $F$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Matzri (2014, arXiv:1402.0332) establishes finite upper bounds for symbol lengths of central simple algebras of exponent p^t over C_m fields, giving len(p^t, F) ≤ t(p^{m-1}-1), which addresses the problem in that setting. Further results in positive characteristic and over function fields of curves/elliptic curves have appeared since. However, a fully general finite upper bound for ℓ_F(p, p^2) and ℓ_F(p^2, p^2) over arbitrary fields with bounded Brauer p-dimension is not known to be settled in full generality.

original_question: If a field F is finitely generated over a subfield F_0 whose Brauer dimension is finite, must the Brauer dimension of F also be finite?
self_contained_problem:
For a field $F$, let $\mathrm{Br}(F)$ denote its Brauer group. For each central simple $F$-algebra $A$, let $\mathrm{ind}(A)$ and $\mathrm{per}(A)$ denote its index and period (exponent), respectively. Define the Brauer dimension $\mathrm{Br.dim}(F)$ to be the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ such that for every finite field extension $E/F$ and every central simple $E$-algebra $A$, one has $\mathrm{ind}(A) \mid \mathrm{per}(A)^{d}$ (and $\mathrm{Br.dim}(F) = \infty$ if no such $d$ exists).

Question: Suppose $F$ is a field that is finitely generated (as a field) over a subfield $F_0$ satisfying $\mathrm{Br.dim}(F_0) < \infty$. Must $\mathrm{Br.dim}(F)$ also be finite?

Chipchakov ("On the behaviour of Brauer p-dimensions under finitely-generated field extensions", arXiv:1207.0965, published in Manuscripta Mathematica, 2016) constructs fields $F_0$ of finite (absolute) Brauer dimension such that for finitely generated transcendental extensions $F/F_0$ the Brauer p-dimension of $F$ is infinite. This answers the question in the negative.

original_question: Can one define a notion of dimension for a useful class of fields F such that Br.dim(F) <= dim F - 1 and dim(F(t)) = dim F + 1?
self_contained_problem:
For a field F, let Br(F) denote its Brauer group. For a central simple F-algebra A, let per(A) denote the order of the class of A in Br(F) (the period) and let ind(A) denote the index of A (the degree of the unique central division F-algebra Brauer-equivalent to A). It is classical that per(A) divides ind(A) and that the two integers share the same prime factors. Define the Brauer dimension of F by

  Br.dim(F) := inf { n ∈ ℤ_{≥0} : ind(A) divides per(A)^n for every central simple F-algebra A and every finite extension of F },

with Br.dim(F) = ∞ if no such n exists.

Problem. Define a notion of "dimension" dim(F), assigning a value dim(F) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} ∪ {∞} to fields F belonging to some natural and useful class, such that the following two properties hold:

 (i) Br.dim(F) ≤ dim(F) − 1 for every F in the class;
 (ii) dim(F(t)) = dim(F) + 1 for every F in the class, where F(t) is the rational function field in one variable over F.

Equivalently, exhibit a field-theoretic dimension function on a substantial class of fields that simultaneously bounds the Brauer dimension from above (shifted by one) and increases by exactly one upon adjoining a transcendental.
status_search_result: The problem comes from a known list of open problems on central simple algebras. While significant progress has been made on bounding Brauer dimensions for specific classes of fields (e.g., local, global, C_2-fields, function fields of arithmetic surfaces, semi-global fields), no field-theoretic dimension function with both required properties (the period–index bound and exact additivity under adjunction of a transcendental) has been identified for a broadly useful class of fields. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the center Z(F,n) of generic n-by-n matrices, and similarly for Z_m(F,n) and Z_H(F,n), is the field extension over F rational, stably rational, or retract rational?

original_question: Let H = C_3 x C_3 be the transitive subgroup of S_9 described in the paper. Is the corresponding field Z_H(F,9) rational, stably rational, or retract rational over F?

Let F be a field and let x_1, x_2, ..., x_9 be independent indeterminates over F. Consider the embedding of H = C_3 × C_3 into the symmetric group S_9 as a transitive subgroup, given by the (left) regular representation of H on its 9 elements (so H acts on {1,...,9} freely and transitively by permuting indices). Then H acts on the rational function field F(x_1, x_2, ..., x_9) by F-algebra automorphisms permuting the variables according to this embedding. Let

   Z_H(F, 9) := F(x_1, x_2, ..., x_9)^H

denote the fixed subfield.

Determine whether Z_H(F, 9) is rational (i.e. purely transcendental) over F, whether it is stably rational over F (i.e. becomes purely transcendental after adjoining finitely many independent indeterminates), and whether it is retract rational over F (in the sense of Saltman: there exist an F-algebra R that is a localization of a polynomial ring over F with field of fractions Z_H(F, 9), and F-algebra homomorphisms R → F[t_1,...,t_n][1/s] → R whose composition is the identity on R).

original_question: What are the essential dimension ed(PGL_n) and essential p-dimension ed_p(PGL_n) of the projective linear group? In particular, what are ed_F(PGL_4) in characteristic 2 and ed_F(PGL_5)?
self_contained_problem:
Let F be a field and let G be an algebraic group over F. For a field extension K/F, an object α in the Galois cohomology set H^1(K, G) (classifying G-torsors over K) is said to descend to an intermediate field F ⊆ L ⊆ K if α lies in the image of the restriction map H^1(L, G) → H^1(K, G). The essential dimension of α, denoted ed(α), is the minimum of the transcendence degrees trdeg_F(L) over all such intermediate fields L. The essential dimension of G over F is

  ed_F(G) = sup { ed(α) : α ∈ H^1(K, G), K/F a field extension }.

For a prime p, the essential p-dimension ed_F(G; p) is defined analogously, but α is allowed to be replaced by its restriction to any finite field extension K'/K of degree prime to p before measuring trdeg_F(L).

Let PGL_n = GL_n / G_m denote the projective linear group, regarded as an algebraic group over F. Determine ed_F(PGL_n) and ed_F(PGL_n; p) as functions of n (and the prime p). In particular, solve the following two cases:

(1) Compute ed_F(PGL_4) when F has characteristic 2.
(2) Compute ed_F(PGL_5) (over an arbitrary base field F, e.g. of characteristic 0).
status_search_result: The exact value of ed(PGL_n) is known only for n ∈ {2, 3, 4, 6} (with the n = 4 case in characteristic ≠ 2 due to Rost giving ed = ed_2 = 5). The case of PGL_4 in characteristic 2 is recognized as the smallest open case, with only a lower bound ed ≥ 4 established. The value of ed(PGL_5) and ed_p(PGL_n) in general remain open problems; only partial results (e.g., Merkurjev's theorem ed_p(PGL_{p^2}) = p^2 + 1) are known.

original_question: What structural consequences for central simple algebras can be deduced from bounds on essential dimension or essential p-dimension? In particular, can one bound ed(CPAlg_n) and ed(Alg_G), compute ed(Alg_G) - ed(G), and determine whether equality ed(CPAlg_n) = ed(PGL_n) forces every degree-n algebra over every field extension of F to be a crossed product?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a base field and $n\ge 2$ an integer. For any field extension $K/F$, let $\mathrm{Alg}_n(K)$ denote the set of isomorphism classes of central simple $K$-algebras of degree $n$, and let $\mathrm{CPAlg}_n(K)\subseteq \mathrm{Alg}_n(K)$ denote the subset of those algebras that are crossed products (i.e., contain a maximal subfield Galois over $K$). For a finite group $G$ whose order divides $n$, let $\mathrm{Alg}_G(K)$ denote the set of isomorphism classes of central simple $K$-algebras of degree $n$ that are $G$-crossed products (i.e., contain a maximal subfield that is Galois over $K$ with Galois group isomorphic to $G$).

Recall that the essential dimension $\mathrm{ed}(\mathcal F)$ of a covariant functor $\mathcal F:\mathrm{Fields}/F \to \mathrm{Sets}$ is the smallest integer $d$ such that every element of $\mathcal F(K)$, for every $K/F$, descends to a subfield $K_0\subseteq K$ with $\mathrm{trdeg}_F(K_0)\le d$. The essential dimension $\mathrm{ed}(G)$ of an algebraic group $G$ is the essential dimension of the functor $K\mapsto H^1(K,G)$. In particular, $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)=\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_n)$.

Address the following:

(1) Establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n)$ and for $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G)$ as functions of $n$ and $G$.

(2) Compute the difference $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{Alg}_G) - \mathrm{ed}(G)$ for finite groups $G$ of order dividing $n$.

(3) Suppose that $\mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{CPAlg}_n) = \mathrm{ed}(\mathrm{PGL}_n)$. Does it follow that every central simple algebra of degree $n$ over every field extension of $F$ is a crossed product?

original_question: If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to every odd-degree field extension of F?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ be a central simple algebra over $F$, equipped with an involution $\sigma\colon A\to A$ of orthogonal or symplectic type (so $\sigma$ is an $F$-linear anti-automorphism of order $2$ whose restriction to the center is the identity, of orthogonal or symplectic kind in the sense of involutions on central simple algebras). Recall that $\sigma$ is called isotropic if there exists a nonzero element $x\in A$ with $\sigma(x)x=0$, and anisotropic otherwise.

Suppose $\sigma$ is anisotropic. For every finite field extension $L/F$ of odd degree, consider the involution $\sigma_L=\sigma\otimes\mathrm{id}_L$ on the central simple $L$-algebra $A\otimes_F L$. 

Question: Must $\sigma_L$ be anisotropic for every such odd-degree extension $L/F$?
status_search_result: The analogue of Springer's theorem for involutions on central simple algebras is known in several cases (e.g., for hermitian forms over quaternion algebras with orthogonal involutions, and Karpenko's result that an orthogonal involution becoming isotropic over every splitting field becomes isotropic over a finite odd-degree extension), and the Hermitian Springer Conjecture has been shown equivalent to a Generic Isotropicity Conjecture by Karpenko. However, the general problem for arbitrary anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involutions appears to remain open as of available sources.

context_brief: Orthogonal involutions over Severi-Brauer function fields
original_question: If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to the function field F_A of the Severi-Brauer variety of A?
self_contained_problem:

original_question: Let G be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group that is anisotropic over F. Does G remain anisotropic over every finite extension K/F whose degree is not divisible by any prime in the set S(G) of homological torsion primes of G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $G$ be an absolutely almost simple linear algebraic group defined over $F$ (i.e., $G$ is connected, semisimple, and $G_{\bar F}$ is almost simple, having no nontrivial connected normal subgroups). Recall that $G$ is called isotropic over $F$ if it contains a nontrivial $F$-split torus $\mathbb{G}_{m,F}\hookrightarrow G$, and anisotropic over $F$ otherwise.

Associated to $G$ there is a finite set of primes $S(G)$, the set of homological (torsion) primes of $G$, defined as the set of primes $p$ such that $H^*(G_{\bar F};\mathbb{Z})$ has $p$-torsion (equivalently, the set of torsion primes of the underlying root datum of $G$). For example, for type $A_n$ and $C_n$ one has $S(G)=\emptyset$ relative to torsion (only depending on isogeny class), for type $B_n$, $D_n$ ($n\ge 3$), and $G_2$ one has $2\in S(G)$, for type $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$ one has $S(G)\subseteq\{2,3\}$, and for type $E_8$ one has $S(G)\subseteq\{2,3,5\}$.

Question: Suppose $G$ is anisotropic over $F$. Must $G$ remain anisotropic over every finite field extension $K/F$ whose degree $[K:F]$ is not divisible by any prime in $S(G)$?
status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive resolution of this question. The problem is posed as an open question regarding whether anisotropy of an absolutely almost simple algebraic group is preserved under finite extensions of degree coprime to the set of homological torsion primes; no published proof or counterexample was located in the search results.

context_brief: Pairings on Brauer groups of surfaces
original_question: For a geometrically connected smooth projective surface X over a finite field, does the 2-primary torsion subgroup Br(X)(2) admit a non-degenerate alternating pairing with values in Q/Z?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a geometrically connected, smooth, projective surface over a finite field $k$, and let $\mathrm{Br}(X)$ denote its cohomological Brauer group $H^2_{\mathrm{ét}}(X,\mathbb{G}_m)$. Write $\mathrm{Br}(X)(2)$ for the 2-primary torsion subgroup of $\mathrm{Br}(X)$. The Artin–Tate construction (analogous to the Cassels–Tate pairing) provides a non-degenerate skew-symmetric pairing
$$ \mathrm{Br}(X)(2) \times \mathrm{Br}(X)(2) \longrightarrow \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z} $$
on the (finite) non-divisible 2-primary part of $\mathrm{Br}(X)$. Determine whether this pairing is alternating; equivalently, whether $\langle x,x\rangle = 0$ for every $x \in \mathrm{Br}(X)(2)$.
status_search_result: The question (originally posed by Tate) was answered affirmatively by Tony Feng, who used Steenrod operations in étale cohomology to construct Stiefel–Whitney classes and prove an étale analogue of Wu's formula, showing the obstruction to the pairing being alternating on 2-torsion vanishes. The result also extends to higher Brauer groups.

original_question: Is there a structural criterion that decides when the tensor product A tensor_F B of two F-division algebras contains a zero divisor, equivalently when it fails to remain a division algebra?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ and $B$ be (associative, finite- or infinite-dimensional) division algebras over $F$, each containing $F$ in its center. Form the tensor product $A \otimes_F B$ as an $F$-algebra. It is known that $A \otimes_F B$ need not be a division algebra: for example, $\mathbb{H} \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{H} \cong M_4(\mathbb{R})$ has many zero divisors, while in other cases $A \otimes_F B$ remains a division algebra.

Provide a structural criterion, formulated in terms of intrinsic invariants of the pair $(A,B)$ over $F$ (such as their centers, splitting fields, maximal subfields, Brauer classes, or other algebraic data), that is necessary and sufficient for $A \otimes_F B$ to contain a nonzero zero divisor; equivalently, for $A \otimes_F B$ to fail to be a division algebra.
status_search_result: The problem of giving a structural criterion for when the tensor product of two F-division algebras contains a zero divisor remains an active area of research. Partial results exist (e.g., Rowen–Saltman provided examples where A⊗_F B fails to be a domain even when F is algebraically closed in the centers, and there are splitting criteria for Brauer classes over products of curves), but no general structural criterion is known. The question, originating with M. Schacher and studied by Bergman and others, appears to still be open.

context_brief: Common maximal subfields for symbol algebras
original_question: Suppose (a,b)_n and (c,d)_n are symbol algebras of degree n over F and their tensor product has index less than n^2. Must there exist symbol algebras in the same Brauer classes that share a common maximal subfield and whose tensor product is isomorphic to the original one?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field containing a primitive $n$-th root of unity, and for $a,b\in F^\times$ let $(a,b)_n$ denote the symbol algebra of degree $n$ over $F$, i.e. the central simple $F$-algebra generated by elements $x,y$ subject to $x^n=a$, $y^n=b$, and $yx=\zeta xy$, where $\zeta$ is a fixed primitive $n$-th root of unity in $F$. Recall that a maximal subfield of a central simple $F$-algebra of degree $n$ is a subfield of dimension $n$ over $F$, and that the index of a central simple algebra is the degree of the division algebra Brauer-equivalent to it.

Suppose $(a,b)_n$ and $(c,d)_n$ are symbol algebras of degree $n$ over $F$ such that the tensor product $(a,b)_n\otimes_F (c,d)_n$ has index strictly less than $n^2$. Must there exist symbol algebras $(a',b')_n$ and $(c',d')_n$ over $F$ such that:
(i) $(a',b')_n$ is Brauer-equivalent to $(a,b)_n$ and $(c',d')_n$ is Brauer-equivalent to $(c,d)_n$;
(ii) $(a',b')_n$ and $(c',d')_n$ share a common maximal subfield; and
(iii) $(a,b)_n\otimes_F (c,d)_n \cong (a',b')_n\otimes_F (c',d')_n$ as $F$-algebras?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of this question. Related results on common maximal subfields of symbol algebras of prime power degree exist, but no source clearly settles the stated problem in general; status remains unverified.

context_brief: Common splitting fields in tensor-product collapse
original_question: If ind(A tensor_F B) is strictly smaller than ind(A) ind(B), what common splitting fields can the division algebras A and B have?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ and $B$ be finite-dimensional central division algebras over $F$. Recall that the index $\mathrm{ind}(C)$ of a central simple $F$-algebra $C$ is the degree of the unique division algebra $D$ with $C \cong M_n(D)$ for some $n$, and that a field extension $K/F$ is called a splitting field of $C$ if $C \otimes_F K$ is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over $K$. Always one has $\mathrm{ind}(A \otimes_F B) \le \mathrm{ind}(A)\,\mathrm{ind}(B)$.

Suppose that
$$\mathrm{ind}(A \otimes_F B) < \mathrm{ind}(A)\,\mathrm{ind}(B).$$
Describe (or characterize structurally) the field extensions $K/F$ that are common splitting fields of $A$ and $B$, i.e. extensions $K/F$ such that both $A \otimes_F K$ and $B \otimes_F K$ are split. In particular, what constraints on $K$ (e.g. degree, generic structure, presence of intermediate subfields) follow from the strict inequality on indices, and conversely which such common splitting fields force the index of the tensor product to drop?

Related results exist (e.g., for two quaternion algebras whose tensor product is not a division algebra, they must share a common quadratic splitting field), but a general characterization for arbitrary degrees does not appear to have been established. The status is best described as open.

original_question: If central simple F-algebras A and B have the same degree and generate the same subgroup of Br(F), must their generic splitting fields F(A) and F(B) be isomorphic? Equivalently, are the Severi-Brauer varieties SB(A) and SB(B) necessarily F-birational under that hypothesis?

original_question: If two division algebras have the same splitting fields inside a specified class of field extensions, for example finite extensions or extensions of transcendence degree at most one, must they generate the same subgroup of the Brauer group?

For a finite-dimensional central simple $F$-algebra $A$, a field extension $L/F$ is called a splitting field of $A$ if $A \otimes_F L$ is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over $L$. Suppose $D_1$ and $D_2$ are two finite-dimensional central division $F$-algebras such that the set of extensions in $\mathcal{C}$ that split $D_1$ coincides with the set of extensions in $\mathcal{C}$ that split $D_2$. Must the classes $[D_1]$ and $[D_2]$ generate the same cyclic subgroup of $\mathrm{Br}(F)$?

Determine, for the classes $\mathcal{C}$ above, whether this implication holds in general.

original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field, must any two quaternion division algebras over F that have the same finite splitting fields, or even just the same maximal subfields, already be isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
Let F be a field that is either finitely generated over its prime field or finitely generated over an algebraically closed field. Recall that a quaternion division algebra over F is a 4-dimensional central simple division algebra over F, that a field extension K/F is called a splitting field of a central simple F-algebra A if A ⊗_F K is isomorphic to a matrix algebra over K, and that a maximal subfield of a quaternion division algebra D over F is a subfield K ⊂ D containing F with [K:F] = 2.

Prove or disprove: if D_1 and D_2 are two quaternion division algebras over F such that D_1 and D_2 have exactly the same finite splitting fields (and, in the stronger form, even just the same set of isomorphism classes of maximal subfields), then D_1 and D_2 are isomorphic as F-algebras.

original_question: If F is finitely generated over a prime field or over an algebraically closed field and D is a division algebra over F, are there only finitely many other division algebras over F with exactly the same finite splitting fields as D?
self_contained_problem:
Let F be a field that is either finitely generated over its prime field or finitely generated over an algebraically closed field. Let D be a finite-dimensional central division algebra over F. Define the "genus" gen'(D) to be the set of Brauer classes [D'] in the Brauer group Br(F) of finite-dimensional central division algebras D' over F such that, for every finite field extension L/F, L splits D if and only if L splits D'. 

Prove that gen'(D) is finite; equivalently, show that there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional central division algebras over F (other than D itself) that have exactly the same collection of finite splitting fields as D.
status_search_result: Krashen and McKinnie ("Distinguishing division algebras by finite splitting fields", manuscripta math. 2011) establish an inductive transfer result: if for a prime p ≠ char K every class in the p-torsion of Br(K) has finite genus gen', then the same holds over K(t). This yields finiteness in many cases (e.g., over fields finitely generated over algebraically closed fields, and partial results over global/local fields), but a complete proof of the finiteness statement for all division algebras over arbitrary fields finitely generated over a prime field appears to remain open in full generality. Subsequent work (e.g., Chernousov–Rapinchuk–Rapinchuk, and recent papers on the genus of division algebras) addresses related cases.

original_question: For a given field F, which finite groups G are F-admissible, meaning that there exists a G-crossed-product F-division algebra?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field. A finite-dimensional central simple $F$-algebra $A$ is called a $G$-crossed product (for a finite group $G$) if $A$ contains a maximal subfield $K$ that is a Galois extension of $F$ with Galois group isomorphic to $G$. A finite group $G$ is said to be $F$-admissible if there exists an $F$-central division algebra that is a $G$-crossed product.

Problem: Given a field $F$, determine all finite groups $G$ that are $F$-admissible.
category_tag: Admissible groups and crossed product division algebras
status_search_result: The general admissibility problem, posed by Schacher in 1968, remains open. Substantial progress has been made for specific fields: over $\mathbb{Q}$, Schacher proved that admissible groups must be Sylow-metacyclic and conjectured the converse; many partial results exist (e.g., for solvable groups by Sonn, and specific simple groups like $M_{11}$, $\mathrm{PSL}(2,q)$). Patching techniques by Harbater–Hartmann–Krashen have settled admissibility for function fields over complete discretely valued fields. However, no complete classification is known for $\mathbb{Q}$, general number fields, or arbitrary base fields, and recent work (e.g., on admissibility and field relations, 2024) continues to investigate the problem.

original_question: Is every Sylow-metacyclic finite group Q-admissible, that is, realizable as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some crossed-product division algebra over Q?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Recall that a finite-dimensional division algebra $D$ with center a field $K$ is called a crossed product for $G$ if $D$ contains a maximal subfield $L$ which is Galois over $K$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K) \cong G$. The group $G$ is said to be $\mathbb{Q}$-admissible if there exists a finite-dimensional central division algebra $D$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ that is a crossed product for $G$ (equivalently, $G$ occurs as the Galois group of a maximal subfield of some central division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$).

A finite group is called Sylow-metacyclic if every one of its Sylow subgroups is metacyclic (i.e., is an extension of a cyclic group by a cyclic group). It is known that every $\mathbb{Q}$-admissible finite group is necessarily Sylow-metacyclic.

Prove or disprove: every Sylow-metacyclic finite group is $\mathbb{Q}$-admissible.
status_search_result: The conjecture (Schacher's conjecture) that every Sylow-metacyclic finite group is Q-admissible remains open. Substantial reductions exist (e.g., reduction to groups of order $2^a 3^b$ and certain almost simple groups), and individual cases such as the Mathieu group $M_{11}$ have been verified, but no complete proof or counterexample has been found in available sources.

original_question: For which natural numbers n does there exist a field F whose Brauer group has exactly n elements?
self_contained_problem:

The Brauer group Br(F) is the abelian group whose elements are equivalence classes of finite-dimensional central simple algebras over F under Brauer (Morita) equivalence — equivalently, classes [A] = [B] iff M_m(A) ≅ M_n(B) for some positive integers m,n — with group operation induced by the tensor product over F. The group Br(F) is always a torsion abelian group.

Determine, with proof, the set of natural numbers n ∈ {1, 2, 3, …} for which there exists a field F such that the Brauer group Br(F) is finite and has cardinality exactly n. In other words, characterize the image of the map F ↦ |Br(F)| as F ranges over all fields with finite Brauer group.
status_search_result: A direct web search did not surface a complete characterization of the natural numbers arising as cardinalities of finite Brauer groups of fields. Known examples include |Br(F)| = 1 (algebraically closed fields, finite fields, certain function fields) and |Br(F)| = 2 (the real numbers and other real closed fields), but a full classification of admissible n appears not to be established in publicly indexed sources. The question is generally regarded as a difficult open-ended problem in the theory of central simple algebras.

original_question: For an open dynamical system with a hole H ⊂ Ω, survival probability P(t), escape rate γ = - lim_{t→∞} (1/t) ln P(t), and natural invariant measure ν on the repeller, for which classes of maps and flows does the escape-rate formula γ = ∑_{i:λ_i>0} λ_i - h_KS remain valid, where the sum runs over positive Lyapunov exponents and h_KS is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy computed with respect to ν?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, T)$ be a discrete-time dynamical system (or let $(\Omega, \Phi^t)$ be a continuous-time flow) on a Riemannian manifold $\Omega$, and let $H \subset \Omega$ be a measurable subset (the "hole"). Define the survival probability after time $t$ by
$$P(t) = \mu_0\bigl(\{x \in \Omega : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le t\}\bigr),$$
where $\mu_0$ is a chosen reference (e.g. Lebesgue) probability measure on $\Omega$, and define the escape rate
$$\gamma = -\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \ln P(t),$$
when this limit exists. Assume there exists a natural conditionally invariant measure on the survivor set whose conditioning produces a $T$-invariant probability measure $\nu$ supported on the repeller $\Lambda = \bigcap_{k\ge 0} T^{-k}(\Omega \setminus H)$. Let $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \cdots$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $T$ with respect to $\nu$, and let $h_{\mathrm{KS}}(\nu)$ denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$ with respect to $\nu$.

The escape-rate formula asserts
$$\gamma = \sum_{i:\,\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i - h_{\mathrm{KS}}(\nu). \qquad (\ast)$$

Determine the most general classes of maps $T$ and flows $\Phi^t$ (in particular, beyond the uniformly hyperbolic setting, including non-uniformly hyperbolic maps, systems with intermittency or singularities, and continuous-time flows) for which the identity $(\ast)$ holds. Establish $(\ast)$ in these classes, or exhibit counterexamples delineating its range of validity.
category_tag: escape rates in open dynamical systems
status_search_result: The escape-rate formula is classically known for uniformly hyperbolic open systems (Eckmann–Ruelle, Young). Recent work has extended it to certain non-uniformly hyperbolic settings (e.g. intermittent maps, polynomial escape rates via maximal large deviations, 2024–2025), but no general result covers arbitrary non-uniformly hyperbolic maps, systems with singularities, or general flows. The question of how broadly $(\ast)$ holds remains an active research problem with only partial progress.

original_question: For which billiards, and under which joint limits of long time t and small hole size h, does the survival probability P(t) reduce to a function only of the combined variable h t?
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a planar billiard table (a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary), and let the billiard flow be the geodesic flow inside $D$ with elastic reflections at $\partial D$, equipped with its natural invariant measure. Fix a measurable subset $H \subset \partial D$ (the "hole") of arclength size $h > 0$, and define the survival probability at time $t > 0$ by
$$P_h(t) \;=\; \mu\bigl\{\, x \in D : \text{the trajectory starting from } x \text{ has not yet crossed } H \text{ by time } t\,\bigr\},$$
where $\mu$ is the normalized phase-space measure (so $P_h(0) = 1$).

Characterize the classes of billiard tables $D$ and the joint asymptotic regimes of $t \to \infty$ and $h \to 0^+$ for which there exists a nontrivial limiting function $F : (0,\infty) \to (0,1]$ such that, along the chosen joint limit with the product $h\,t$ held fixed,
$$\lim_{\substack{t \to \infty,\; h \to 0^+ \\ h t = s}} P_h(t) \;=\; F(s)$$
for all $s > 0$. In particular, identify for which families of billiards (with a one-parameter family of holes of variable size $h$) the survival probability collapses, in such a joint scaling limit, to a function of the single combined variable $h t$.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., works on open spherical billiards, lemon billiards, and entropy/scaling-law analyses up through 2025) provides numerical and partial analytic evidence that survival probabilities can be collapsed onto a universal curve through rescaling involving the hole size, particularly when the hole overlaps stability islands or in hyperbolic regimes. original_question: Does every triangular billiard, or more generally every polygonal billiard, contain at least one periodic orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the Euclidean plane (in particular, P may be taken to be a triangle). A billiard trajectory in P is a piecewise linear path traced by a point particle moving with unit speed inside P, reflecting off the sides of P according to the law of equal angles (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), with the convention that trajectories hitting a vertex are undefined. Such a trajectory is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial direction.

Question: Does every polygonal billiard table P admit at least one periodic billiard trajectory? In particular, does every triangle admit at least one periodic billiard trajectory?
status_search_result: The problem remains open in general. Periodic orbits are known to exist in all rational polygons, all acute triangles, all right triangles (Holt 1993; Galperin–Stepin–Vorobets 1991), and all triangles whose angles are at most 100 degrees (Schwartz). The case of general obtuse triangles, and of general (irrational) polygons, is still unresolved.

original_question: In polygonal billiards, is the asymptotic long-time survival probability P(t) completely determined by neighborhoods of non-escaping periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygonal billiard table, i.e., a compact connected planar domain whose boundary is a finite union of line segments. Consider the billiard flow on $Q$: a point particle moves with unit speed along straight lines and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting the boundary, with trajectories that hit a vertex left undefined. Fix an open subset $H \subset Q$ (a "hole"); a trajectory is said to escape at time $t$ if it first enters $H$ at time $t$. Starting from the uniform (Liouville) probability measure on the unit tangent bundle of $Q \setminus H$, let
$$P(t) = \mathrm{Prob}\{\text{the trajectory has not entered } H \text{ by time } t\}$$
denote the survival probability. Let $\mathcal{N} \subset Q$ denote the set of points lying on periodic billiard orbits that never enter $H$ ("non-escaping periodic orbits").

Question: Is the asymptotic behavior of $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ entirely determined by arbitrarily small neighborhoods of $\mathcal{N}$? Equivalently, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, is the contribution to $P(t)$ from initial conditions whose orbits remain at distance $\geq \varepsilon$ from $\mathcal{N}$ asymptotically negligible compared with the full survival probability $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$?
status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in surveys on open billiards, and related sub-questions (e.g., whether every polygon admits a periodic orbit) remain unresolved. original_question: For stadium-like billiards that contain marginally unstable periodic orbits, can one comprehensively characterize their dynamical and escape properties in terms of the reinjection dynamics of trajectories that leave and later return to the neighborhood of those periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar billiard whose boundary is a stadium-like curve, namely a smooth curve consisting of two parallel straight segments joined by two focusing (curved) arcs, so that the table contains a one-parameter family of "bouncing-ball" periodic orbits perpendicular to the parallel segments. These bouncing-ball orbits form a family of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs): orbits whose linearized Poincaré map has eigenvalue 1 with a nontrivial Jordan block, so that nearby trajectories drift away only polynomially in time.

A trajectory near such a family eventually leaves a tubular neighborhood of the MUPO family, wanders through the chaotic component of phase space, and is later "reinjected" back into the neighborhood of the MUPOs with some distribution of incoming angles and positions; this stochastic-like return mechanism is called the reinjection dynamics, and it depends on the curvature properties of the boundary near the endpoints of the bouncing-ball segments.

Problem. Provide a comprehensive characterization of the dynamical properties of the marginally unstable periodic orbits in stadium-like billiards — including, in particular, the long-time statistics of trajectories near the MUPO family, decay of correlations, the algebraic tail of the distribution of consecutive collisions in the bouncing-ball region, and escape-rate / survival-probability asymptotics when a hole is opened in the table — purely in terms of the reinjection dynamics (the distribution of return positions, angles, and times of trajectories that leave and later re-enter a neighborhood of the MUPO family). Specifically, identify which features of the reinjection mechanism (depending on the curvature of the boundary near the endpoints of the parallel segments) determine these dynamical and escape properties, and derive quantitative predictions for them from properties of the reinjection map alone.
category_tag: billiards and marginally unstable periodic orbits
status_search_result: Literature on stadium-like billiards (Altmann–Friedrich–Motter–Kantz and follow-ups, 2007–) establishes that MUPOs strongly influence transport and produce algebraic (1/t^2-type) decay of correlations and survival probabilities, with reinjection mechanisms playing a central role. However, no comprehensive characterization of all dynamical and escape properties of MUPOs purely in terms of the reinjection dynamics has been published; partial results exist for specific reinjection models, but a unified theory remains absent.

original_question: Is there a universal asymptotic decay law for the long-time survival probability in generic open billiards with mixed phase space, where sticky motion near elliptic islands can produce algebraic decay?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a planar billiard table (a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary) whose associated billiard map $T$ on the phase space $M$ (unit tangent bundle restricted to the boundary, with the standard invariant measure $\mu$) has mixed phase space: $M$ contains both a positive-measure set of chaotic orbits and a positive-measure set of invariant elliptic islands surrounded by KAM tori. Open the billiard by designating a measurable subset $H \subset \partial Q$ (a "hole") through which trajectories escape, and define the survival probability up to time $n$ by
$$P(n) = \mu\{x \in M : T^k(x) \notin H \text{ for all } 0 \le k \le n\}.$$
It is known that, due to the sticky behavior of orbits near the boundaries of the elliptic islands, $P(n)$ generically decays as a power law $P(n) \sim C\, n^{-\alpha}$ as $n \to \infty$.

Question: Is there a universal exponent $\alpha > 0$ such that, for every "generic" open billiard with mixed phase space (independent of the geometry of $Q$ and the choice of hole $H$), the survival probability satisfies $P(n) \sim C\, n^{-\alpha}$ as $n \to \infty$? In particular, does the conjectured value $\alpha \approx 2.57$ for area-preserving maps with stickiness near elliptic islands extend to all such open billiards?
status_search_result: The question of a universal algebraic decay exponent for survival/recurrence in Hamiltonian systems with mixed phase space remains an active research topic. While numerical and heuristic studies (e.g., Cristadoro–Ketzmerick and others) have proposed a universal exponent near 2.57 for area-preserving maps, recent work on hierarchical phase-space structures and intermittent billiards indicates that the universality is still debated, with some studies suggesting system-dependent exponents. No rigorous proof of a universal decay rate for generic open billiards has been established.

original_question: In mushroom billiards and related systems with mixed phase space, how does the boundary between regular and chaotic regions affect escape, including the slowing of survival decay caused by stickiness from marginally unstable periodic orbits and by the regular-chaotic interface itself?
self_contained_problem:
Consider planar mushroom billiards: a billiard table consisting of a semicircular "cap" of radius $R$ joined to a rectangular "stem" of width $2r < 2R$, in which a point particle moves in straight lines and reflects elastically off the boundary. Such billiards have a sharply divided phase space, consisting of an integrable region (orbits confined to the cap that never enter the stem) and a chaotic region (orbits that visit the stem), separated by a clean regular–chaotic interface. Embedded in the chaotic component there can be families of marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs), whose presence depends on Diophantine properties of $r/R$.

Now introduce a hole in the boundary or in phase space that lies in the chaotic component, and let $P(t)$ denote the survival probability that a trajectory, started from an initial condition distributed according to the Liouville measure restricted to the chaotic component, has not escaped through the hole by time $t$. It is known that $P(t)$ can decay subexponentially due to (i) stickiness produced by MUPOs and (ii) stickiness produced by the regular–chaotic boundary itself.

Problem. Characterise quantitatively the escape properties of the regular–chaotic boundary in mushroom billiards and in similar billiards with a sharply divided mixed phase space. In particular, determine the asymptotic behaviour of $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ that is induced solely by the regular–chaotic interface (independently of the MUPO contribution), identify the geometric and number-theoretic features of the billiard that govern this contribution, and describe how the interface and the MUPO families combine to produce the observed slow decay of $P(t)$.
status_search_result: Recent literature (including studies of MUPOs in mushroom billiards, tilted-hat mushroom billiards, and quantum chaos in mushroom billiards through 2025) continues to investigate stickiness from marginally unstable periodic orbits and from the regular–chaotic boundary, but no complete characterisation of the escape properties of the regular–chaotic interface has been established. The problem is treated as an open question in current research.

original_question: What are the minimal microscopic dynamical properties needed for a chaotic macroscopic limit in billiard-like transport models, for example recurrence, ergodicity, existence of a normal diffusion coefficient, or convergence to a limiting Wiener process?
self_contained_problem: Consider a family of billiard-like transport models in which point particles move in a $d$-dimensional domain (for example $\mathbb{R}^d$ or a periodic box) containing a configuration of fixed scatterers (obstacles), undergoing free motion between elastic collisions with the scatterers. Examples include the periodic Lorentz gas, Lorentz gases with randomly placed non-overlapping obstacles, and Ehrenfest wind-tree gases. Let $x_t$ denote the position of a tagged particle at time $t$, and consider the rescaled trajectory $X^\varepsilon_t = \varepsilon\, x_{t/\varepsilon^2}$ in the diffusive scaling limit $\varepsilon \to 0$.\n\nDetermine the minimal microscopic dynamical properties of such a model that are necessary and/or sufficient to ensure a "chaotic" macroscopic limit. Specifically, identify the weakest hypotheses on the microscopic dynamics (e.g. recurrence of typical trajectories, ergodicity of the billiard flow with respect to the natural invariant measure, existence and finiteness of a normal diffusion coefficient $D = \lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{1}{2dt}\, \mathbb{E}\,\|x_t - x_0\|^2$, mixing properties, or decay of correlations) under which the rescaled process $X^\varepsilon_t$ converges in distribution, as $\varepsilon \to 0$, to a Wiener process with covariance $2D\,t\,\mathrm{Id}$. Determine which of these properties are independent, which imply others, and which are individually necessary for normal diffusive behavior in the macroscopic limit.
status_search_result: The question of minimal microscopic conditions guaranteeing a diffusive (Wiener) macroscopic limit in billiard-like transport models is widely regarded as an open problem in mathematical physics. While diffusive limits are established for specific models (finite-horizon periodic Lorentz gas by Bunimovich–Sinai and refinements; some results for infinite-horizon and certain wind-tree models), no general characterization in terms of minimal dynamical hypotheses is known, and several natural cases (random non-overlapping obstacles, generic Ehrenfest gases) remain unresolved.

original_question: For an open quantum billiard, let k_n denote the resonances of the Helmholtz equation (∇^2 + k^2)ψ = 0 with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Is it true that the number of resonant states satisfying Re(k_n) < k and Im(k_n) > -C grows on the order of k^(d_H+1) as k → ∞, where d_H is the partial Hausdorff dimension of the classical non-escaping set?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open two-dimensional quantum billiard: a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ consisting of the exterior of a finite collection of compact obstacles (so that classical particles may escape to infinity). For wavenumber $k \in \mathbb{C}$, consider the Helmholtz equation
$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\psi = 0 \quad \text{on } \Omega,$$
with Dirichlet boundary conditions $\psi = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and outgoing radiation conditions at infinity. The values $k_n \in \mathbb{C}$ for which a nontrivial outgoing solution exists are called resonances; for an open system they have $\mathrm{Im}(k_n) < 0$.

Let the classical non-escaping set (the trapped set) be the set of phase-space points whose forward and backward billiard trajectories remain in a bounded region forever, and let $d_H$ denote the partial Hausdorff dimension of this trapped set (the Hausdorff dimension of its intersection with an energy shell, transverse to the flow direction).

For a fixed constant $C > 0$, let
$$N(k, C) := \#\{ n : \mathrm{Re}(k_n) < k,\ \mathrm{Im}(k_n) > -C \}.$$

Prove or disprove: as $k \to \infty$,
$$N(k, C) \asymp k^{d_H + 1}.$$
status_search_result: The fractal Weyl conjecture for open chaotic systems remains an active research problem. Rigorous fractal Weyl upper bounds have been proved in various settings (e.g., Nonnenmacher–Sjöstrand–Zworski for open quantum chaotic maps, and for several-convex-obstacle scattering under a no-eclipse condition), and the conjectured asymptotic has been tested numerically in many models. However, a matching lower bound and the full asymptotic order $k^{d_H+1}$ has not been established in general, so the conjecture is generally regarded as still open in its full form.

original_question: For a given open or generalized billiard system, can the survival probability P(t) be computed exactly, or at least expanded for large t beyond its leading asymptotic term?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open (or generalized) billiard system: a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (possibly with additional dynamical generalizations such as nontrivial scatterers, intermittency, or modified reflection rules) whose boundary $\partial\Omega$ contains one or more "holes" through which trajectories may escape. Let an initial probability measure on the phase space (positions and unit velocity directions) be fixed (for instance, the uniform Liouville measure on a chosen energy shell), and let a point particle move along straight lines and reflect specularly off $\partial\Omega \setminus H$, where $H$ denotes the holes. Define the survival probability
$$P(t) = \operatorname{Prob}\big(\text{the trajectory has not yet exited through } H \text{ by time } t\big).$$
It is known in many examples that $P(t)$ admits a leading asymptotic behavior as $t \to \infty$ (algebraic decay $\sim C/t$ for typical chaotic billiards with holes, exponential decay in dispersing cases, etc.). The problem is the following:

For a given open or generalized billiard, determine whether $P(t)$ can be computed in closed form for all $t$, and if not, derive an asymptotic expansion of $P(t)$ as $t \to \infty$ that captures terms beyond the leading order (e.g., explicit subleading constants, correction terms, or full series expansions), with rigorous control of the remainder.
status_search_result: For specific systems, beyond-leading-order expansions of the survival probability have been obtained: stadium billiards admit exact leading and subleading formulas with errors decaying as $t^{-2}$, spherical/circular open billiards have explicit constant and vanishing-tail expansions with surprising connections to the Riemann zeta function, and circle billiards admit sums over non-escaping periodic orbits. However, no general method exists for arbitrary open or generalized billiards, so the problem remains open in full generality.

original_question: How do recurrences in a dynamical system, including periodic orbits and more general recurrent structures either near the hole or elsewhere in phase space, affect escape for systems with little or no hyperbolicity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T:M\to M$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system on a phase space $M$ equipped with a reference probability measure $\mu$, and let $H\subset M$ be a measurable subset called the hole. Define the survivor set up to time $n$ by
$$S_n(H)=\{x\in M:T^k(x)\notin H\text{ for all }0\le k\le n\},$$
and (when the limit exists) the escape rate
$$\gamma(H)=-\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\mu(S_n(H)).$$
Assume that $T$ exhibits little or no hyperbolicity (e.g. parabolic, intermittent, polygonal-billiard, or mixed phase-space systems with elliptic islands or marginally unstable periodic orbits).

Provide a general theory describing how the escape rate $\gamma(H)$, the asymptotics of $\mu(S_n(H))$, and the geometry of the survivor set are influenced by the recurrent structures of $T$, including:
(i) periodic orbits intersecting or lying near the hole $H$;
(ii) periodic orbits and more general recurrent sets (e.g. invariant tori, neutral fixed points, sticky regions) located elsewhere in phase space;
(iii) the interplay between such recurrent structures and the position, shape, and size of $H$.

In particular, characterize quantitatively how proximity of $H$ to short periodic orbits or to non-hyperbolic recurrent sets modifies $\gamma(H)$ relative to the hyperbolic case, and identify the corrections to the standard escape-rate formulas in the absence of uniform hyperbolicity.
category_tag: Open dynamical systems and escape rates
status_search_result: The problem of describing escape in non-hyperbolic or mixed systems with recurrent structures (periodic orbits, sticky islands, marginally unstable orbits) remains an active research area. Partial results exist for specific cases — local escape rates near periodic vs. non-periodic points in hyperbolic settings (Keller–Liverani, Ferguson–Pollicott), polynomial decay due to marginally unstable periodic orbits in stadium billiards, and stickiness phenomena — but no general theory covers systems with little or no hyperbolicity. The question is consistently listed as open in surveys on open dynamical systems.

original_question: What information about the dynamics or geometry of a billiard can be recovered from escape measurements alone, and to what extent can such measurements reveal the shape of the underlying domain?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar domain with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and consider the billiard flow on $\Omega$: a point particle moves in straight lines at unit speed inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting $\partial\Omega$. Fix a nonempty open subset $H \subset \partial\Omega$ ("the hole"), and define the escape time $\tau_H(x,v)$ of an initial condition $(x,v) \in \Omega \times S^1$ as the first time the trajectory reaches $H$. Equip the phase space with the Liouville measure and let the escape measurement consist of the data of the escape-time distribution $\mu_H(t) = \mathrm{Prob}(\tau_H > t)$ together with, possibly, the joint distribution of exit points and exit directions on $H$ for randomly chosen initial conditions.

The inverse escape problem asks:

(a) What features of the billiard dynamics on $\Omega$ (e.g., escape rate, Lyapunov spectrum, presence and measure of stability islands, topological entropy, periodic-orbit data) can be reconstructed from the escape measurements associated with one or several holes $H$?

(b) To what extent do these escape measurements determine the geometric shape of $\Omega$? In particular, do there exist non-isometric domains $\Omega_1, \Omega_2$ that produce identical escape measurement data for all admissible choices of holes, or does the escape data uniquely determine $\Omega$ up to isometry (an "escape" analogue of the question "Can one hear the shape of a drum?")?

Provide a systematic theory characterizing the maps $\Omega \mapsto \mu_H$ and identifying their injectivity properties and reconstruction algorithms.
status_search_result: A systematic solution to the inverse escape problem for billiards does not appear in the literature. While there is active research on escape rates, survival probabilities, and escape basins for open billiards (including studies relating hole placement to chaotic vs. regular dynamics), no general theory establishes which dynamical or geometric features of a billiard domain can be reconstructed from escape measurements, nor whether the shape of the domain is determined by such data. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the disordered copolymer model whose critical curve satisfies h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ in the weak-coupling regime when α ∈ (0,1), determine the universal slope m_α as an explicit function of α. Equivalently, identify the weak-coupling asymptotic of the critical curve beyond the currently known bounds, using only the model data supported in the paper: α is the tail exponent in the renewal law K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), h_c(λ) is the localization-delocalization critical curve, and m_α depends only on α and not on the detailed law of the disorder sequence or on the full renewal distribution.
self_contained_problem:
Let $	au=(	au_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ with $	au_0=0$ and i.i.d. increments distributed according to a probability law $K$ on $\mathbb{N}$ satisfying the tail asymptotics
$$K(n) := \mathbb{P}(	au_1 = n) \;\sim\;  rac{C_K}{n^{1+\alpha}} \qquad (n	o\infty),$$
for a fixed exponent $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and a constant $C_K>0$. Let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables independent of $	au$, with mean $0$, variance $1$, and finite exponential moments $\mathbb{E}[e^{t\omega_1}]<\infty$ in a neighborhood of $0$.

For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ (disorder strength) and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ (asymmetry bias), define the copolymer partition function
$$Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp\!\Big(\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\lambda\omega_n - h)\,\Delta_n\Big)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{N\in	au\}}ight],$$
where $\Delta_n\in\{0,1\}$ encodes the standard copolymer interaction along the renewal $	au$. The quenched free energy
$$	extsf{F}(\lambda,h) \;=\; \lim_{N	o\infty} rac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E} ig[\log Z_{N,\omega}(\lambda,h) ig]$$
exists and is non-negative. The critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda) \;=\; \inf\{\,h\ge 0 : 	extsf{F}(\lambda,h)=0\,\}.$$

It is known that, for $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the limit
$$m_\alpha \;:=\; \lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0} rac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}$$
exists in $(0,\infty)$ and depends only on $\alpha$ (and not on the law of $\omega$ nor on the finer details of $K$ beyond the tail exponent).

Problem: Determine $m_\alpha$ as an explicit function of $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
status_search_result: The universality of the weak-coupling slope $m_\alpha$ (its dependence only on $\alpha$) is established (Caravenna–Giacomin–Toninelli; Caravenna–Giacomin 2010, Annals of Probability). The best known bounds give $1/(1+\alpha)\le m_\alpha\le 1$, and the explicit value of $m_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in(0,1)$ remains an open problem; no formula has been published. The $\alpha=0$ regime has separately been resolved (Berger–Giacomin–Lacoin, 2018), but this does not address $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

original_question: In the same weak-coupling copolymer setting, prove the strict lower bound m_1/2 > 2/3 for the universal slope m_α of the critical curve h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ when α = 1/2.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $S=(S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the simple symmetric random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ starting from $0$, and let $\omega=(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables, independent of $S$, with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$, and finite exponential moments. For parameters $\lambda\ge 0$ and $h\in\mathbb{R}$, define the (quenched) copolymer Gibbs measure of length $N$ by the Radon–Nikodym derivative
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}{\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}}(S)\;=\;\frac{1}{Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}}\exp\!\Big(\lambda\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\omega_n+h)\,\mathrm{sign}(S_n)\Big),$$
with the convention $\mathrm{sign}(0)=\mathrm{sign}(S_{n-1})$. The quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)\;=\;\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\log Z_{N,\lambda,h}^{\omega}\right]$$
exists and is non-negative; it satisfies $\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)\ge \lambda h$, and the (quenched) critical curve is
$$h_c(\lambda)\;=\;\inf\{h\ge 0:\mathrm{f}(\lambda,h)=\lambda h\}.$$
More generally, replacing $S$ by a recurrent renewal process whose inter-arrival law has a regularly varying tail with exponent $1+\alpha$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, one has
$$\lim_{\lambda\downarrow 0}\frac{h_c(\lambda)}{\lambda}\;=\;m_\alpha\in(0,\infty),$$
a universal constant depending only on $\alpha$. It is known that $\tfrac{1}{1+\alpha}\le m_\alpha\le 1$; in particular $m_{1/2}\ge \tfrac{2}{3}$.

Problem. Prove the strict inequality
$$m_{1/2}\;>\;\tfrac{2}{3}.$$
status_search_result: The slope $m_\alpha$ of the copolymer critical curve at weak coupling is known to lie in $[1/(1+\alpha),1]$, and Caravenna–Giacomin (and subsequent work by Berger–Caravenna–Poisat–Sun–Zygouras, arXiv:1301.5308) established universality of $m_\alpha$ as the slope of a continuum copolymer model, refuting the Monthus-type conjecture $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$ in some regimes. However, no source located explicitly establishes the strict inequality $m_{1/2}>2/3$ for the simple-random-walk/$\alpha=1/2$ copolymer; the question appears to remain open, although it is closely related to disproving $m_\alpha=1/(1+\alpha)$ at $\alpha=1/2$. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the universal weak-coupling slope m_α of the copolymer critical curve equals 1/(1+α)? Here m_α is defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ for small λ when the limit exists, and the question asks whether the lower-bound expression 1/(1+α) is ever the exact value of the slope for the original copolymer model.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the random copolymer model defined as follows. Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a simple random walk on ℤ, and let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be an i.i.d. sequence of centered random variables with unit variance and finite exponential moments, independent of S. For parameters λ ≥ 0 and h ≥ 0, define the polymer measure of length N by

  dP_{N,λ,h}^{ω}/dP(S) = (1/Z_{N,λ,h}^{ω}) · exp( -2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h) Δ_n ),

where Δ_n = 1 if (S_{n-1}, S_n) lies in the lower half-plane (i.e. max(S_{n-1}, S_n) ≤ 0) and Δ_n = 0 otherwise, and Z_{N,λ,h}^{ω} is the normalizing partition function.

The model exhibits a localization–delocalization phase transition along a critical curve h = h_c(λ), which for the simple random walk satisfies a polynomial tail exponent α = 1/2 of the underlying return-time distribution; more generally one considers an analogous model where the underlying renewal/return-time distribution has regularly varying tails with index 1+α for some α > 0. It is known that the limit

  m_α := lim_{λ ↓ 0} h_c(λ)/λ

exists (under suitable hypotheses), and satisfies the universal bounds

  1/(1+α) ≤ m_α ≤ 1   for every α > 0.

Question: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the equality m_α = 1/(1+α) holds, i.e., for which the lower bound is attained?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Bolthausen, den Hollander and Opoku proved that the lower bound is strict, i.e. m_α > 1/(1+α) for every α ∈ (0,∞), thereby ruling out Monthus' conjecture that the lower bound was sharp. The matching universal weak-coupling asymptotics m_α (and its value strictly above 1/(1+α)) were further established by Berger, Caravenna, Poisat, Sun and Zygouras, who proved the corresponding conjecture in Comm. Math. Phys. (2013).

original_question: The paper proves that for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0, where F is the quenched free energy and h_c is the critical curve. Can this smoothing estimate be strengthened by replacing the power δ^2 with a strictly larger exponent, i.e. by proving that the free energy vanishes faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized side?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\tau=(\tau_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}_0$ with $\tau_0=0$ and i.i.d. increments whose interarrival law satisfies
$$P(\tau_1=n)=\frac{L(n)}{n^{1+\alpha}},\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
for some $\alpha\ge 0$ and a slowly varying function $L$. Let $(\omega_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. real random variables, independent of $\tau$, with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$, and $\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\omega_1}]<\infty$ for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $0$. For parameters $\lambda>0$ (disorder strength) and $h\in\mathbb{R}$ (pinning bias), define the disordered pinning partition function
$$Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}=\mathbb{E}_\tau\!\left[\exp\!\Big(\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\lambda\omega_n-\log\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda\omega_1}]+h)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{n\in\tau\}}\Big)\right],$$
and the quenched free energy
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\,\mathbb{E}_\omega\!\big[\log Z_{N,\omega}^{\lambda,h}\big]\ge 0.$$
The critical curve is $h_c(\lambda)=\sup\{h:\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h)=0\}$, finite for every $\lambda>0$.

Known smoothing bound. For every $\lambda>0$ there exists a constant $c(\lambda)<\infty$ such that
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le (1+\alpha)\,c(\lambda)\,\delta^{2}\qquad\text{for all }\delta>0.$$

Question. Can the exponent $2$ above be improved? Equivalently, does there exist (for some, or all, $\lambda>0$ and $\alpha>0$) an exponent $\gamma>2$ and a finite constant $C(\lambda)$ such that
$$\mathrm{F}(\lambda,h_c(\lambda)+\delta)\le C(\lambda)\,\delta^{\gamma}\qquad\text{for all }\delta\in(0,1)?$$
That is, can one prove that the quenched free energy vanishes strictly faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized phase?
status_search_result: The quadratic smoothing bound of Giacomin–Toninelli has been refined in several directions (sharp constants, weak-disorder asymptotics, more general disorder; e.g., Caravenna–den Hollander 2013, and subsequent work on disorder relevance), but no result is known to replace the exponent $2$ by a strictly larger one in the general disordered pinning model. In regimes of relevant disorder the quadratic behavior is believed to be sharp; in marginal/irrelevant regimes the question of strict improvement remains open according to the available literature.

original_question: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) := -lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[(1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}] and let F(λ,h) be the free energy. As h approaches the critical curve h_c(λ) from below, are the two quantities logarithmically equivalent in the sense that log μ(λ,h) ~ log F(λ,h)? This asks whether the decay scale controlling correlation length or longest-excursion asymptotics vanishes at the same logarithmic rate as the free energy near criticality.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the disordered pinning model defined as follows. Let τ = (τ_n)_{n≥0} be a (recurrent) renewal process on ℕ with τ_0 = 0, and let ω = (ω_n)_{n≥1} be an i.i.d. sequence of real random variables, independent of τ, with E[ω_1] = 0, E[ω_1^2] = 1, and finite exponential moments. For parameters λ ≥ 0 (disorder strength) and h ∈ ℝ (pinning bias), and integer N ≥ 1, define the partition function
   Z_{N,ω} := E[ exp( Σ_{n=1}^{N} (λ ω_n + h) 1_{n ∈ τ} ) 1_{N ∈ τ} ],
where E is expectation over τ. The quenched free energy is
   F(λ, h) := lim_{N→∞} (1/N) E[ log Z_{N,ω} ],
and the localized phase {(λ,h) : F(λ,h) > 0} is separated from the delocalized phase by the critical curve h_c(λ) = inf{h : F(λ,h) > 0}.

In the localized phase, define the auxiliary quantity
   μ(λ, h) := - lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[ (1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^{N} (ω_n + h))) / Z_{N,ω} ],
which controls exponential decay scales (e.g. for correlation functions or longest-excursion tails).

Question: Is it true that, as h ↘ h_c(λ) at fixed λ > 0,
   log μ(λ, h) ∼ log F(λ, h),
that is, log μ(λ,h) / log F(λ,h) → 1?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a result establishing or refuting the logarithmic equivalence log μ(λ,h) ∼ log F(λ,h) as h ↘ h_c(λ) for the disordered pinning model. Related work on disorder relevance, critical exponents of the free energy, and correlation length bounds for pinning models exists, but no source clearly resolves this specific comparison between μ and F near criticality. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Fix parameters (λ,h) in the interior of the delocalized region D, where D = {(λ,h) : F(λ,h)=0}. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the quenched polymer measure of the event that the polymer stays entirely in the favorable solvent during the whole terminal segment [εN, N] tends to 0 almost surely as N → ∞? In the paper's notation this is the question whether lim_{N→∞} P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN, N] ∩ N) = 0 almost surely, where Δ_n is the indicator that monomer n is below the interface, so Δ_n = 0 means that monomer n is not below the interface.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following random copolymer model at a selective interface. Let $\tau = \{\tau_j\}_{j\ge 0}$ be a renewal process on $\mathbb{N}_0$ with $\tau_0 = 0$ and inter-arrival law $K(\cdot)$ satisfying $K(n) \sim c\, n^{-(1+\alpha)}$ for some $\alpha > 0$ (the renewal points represent the returns of a directed polymer to a horizontal interface). Independently of $\tau$, let $\xi = \{\xi_j\}_{j\ge 1}$ be i.i.d. Bernoulli$(1/2)$ random variables, and define
$$\Delta_n := \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} \xi_j\, \mathbf{1}_{(\tau_{j-1},\tau_j]}(n), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N},$$
so that $\Delta_n \in \{0,1\}$ is constant on each excursion of $\tau$ and indicates whether the $n$-th monomer lies below ($\Delta_n=1$) or not below ($\Delta_n=0$) the interface.

Let $\omega = \{\omega_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an i.i.d. sequence of real-valued random variables (the disorder) with $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1]=0$, $\mathbb{E}[\omega_1^2]=1$ and finite exponential moments, defined on a probability space with measure $\mathbb{P}$. For parameters $\lambda \ge 0$ and $h \in \mathbb{R}$ and integer $N\ge 1$, define the quenched polymer measure
$$\frac{dP_{N,\omega}}{dP_0}(\tau,\xi) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z_{N,\omega}}\, \exp\!\Big(-2\lambda \sum_{n=1}^{N} (\omega_n + h)\, \Delta_n\Big)\, \mathbf{1}_{\{N\in\tau\}},$$
where $P_0$ is the law of $(\tau,\xi)$ and $Z_{N,\omega}$ is the normalizing partition function. Let
$$F(\lambda,h) \;:=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{1}{N}\, \mathbb{E}\!\big[\log Z_{N,\omega}\big]$$
be the quenched free energy. Define the delocalized region $\mathcal{D} := \{(\lambda,h):\, F(\lambda,h)=0\}$.

Question: For $(\lambda,h)$ in the interior of $\mathcal{D}$, is it true that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$,
$$\lim_{N\to\infty} P_{N,\omega}\!\big(\Delta_n = 0 \text{ for every } n \in [\varepsilon N, N]\cap \mathbb{N}\big) \;=\; 0 \qquad \mathbb{P}(d\omega)\text{-almost surely}?$$
status_search_result: Path properties of disordered copolymers in the interior of the delocalized region (in particular almost-sure statements like the one asked) are widely described in surveys as among the hardest unsolved problems for this model. Available results give annealed/in-probability statements and bounds of order $O(\log N)$ on the number of monomers in the unfavorable solvent, but a quenched almost-sure delocalization statement of this strong form does not appear to have been established.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.
self_contained_problem:
Let P = {p_1, ..., p_n} be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment between p_i and p_j contains no other point of P. The point visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph G(P) on vertex set {v_1, ..., v_n} with v_i v_j an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Problem: Given as input a simple undirected graph G specified by its adjacency matrix, decide whether there exists a finite point set P in the plane such that G(P) is isomorphic to G. Determine the computational complexity (decidability, and complexity class) of this recognition problem.
status_search_result: Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015; DCG 2017) proved that point visibility graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals (∃ℝ-complete), placing it between NP and PSPACE; this resolves the complexity question up to ∃ℝ-completeness, but exact decidability/complexity classification (e.g., whether ∃ℝ = NP) remains open. Recognition for grid point visibility graphs is decidable iff the existential theory of the rationals is decidable, which is itself an open question.

original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Define two points p_i, p_j ∈ P to be mutually visible if the open line segment between p_i and p_j contains no other point of P (i.e., no third point of P lies on the segment p_i p_j). Associate to P the point visibility graph G(P) whose vertex set is P and whose edges are exactly the pairs {p_i, p_j} of mutually visible points.

Give a complete combinatorial characterization of the class of graphs G that arise in this way: namely, determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial (graph-theoretic) conditions on a finite simple graph G so that there exists a finite point set P ⊂ R^2 with G(P) isomorphic to G.
status_search_result: The general characterization of point visibility graphs remains an open problem. Partial progress is known: the recognition problem has been shown to be NP-hard and lies in PSPACE, and is complete for the existential theory of the reals. Complete characterizations have been obtained only for special subclasses (e.g., planar point visibility graphs), but no combinatorial characterization of the full class is known.

original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let P = {p_1, …, p_n} be a finite set of distinct points in the Euclidean plane R^2. Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment joining p_i and p_j contains no other point of P. The (point) visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph G(P) on vertex set {v_1, …, v_n} in which v_i v_j is an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Problem. Given a finite simple undirected graph G that is guaranteed to be the point visibility graph of some finite point set in the plane, give an algorithm that, on input G, outputs explicit coordinates of points q_1, …, q_n ∈ R^2 such that the visibility graph of Q = {q_1, …, q_n} is isomorphic to G.
status_search_result: The point visibility graph reconstruction problem remains open. Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015; DCG 2017) showed that point visibility graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals (∃R), which places recognition (and hence reconstruction with explicit real coordinates) in PSPACE but provides no polynomial-time algorithm. No algorithm producing a planar realization for an arbitrary point visibility graph is known, and the problem is considered a long-standing open problem in the area.

original_question: Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear, in the standard convention; otherwise, two points see each other iff the open segment joining them contains no other point of P). The point visibility graph G of P has vertex set P, with two points joined by an edge precisely when they see each other. Let ω(G) denote the clique number and χ(G) the chromatic number of G.

Prove or disprove: every point visibility graph G with ω(G) ≤ 4 satisfies χ(G) ≤ 5.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been disproved. A construction of a point visibility graph with clique number 4 and chromatic number 6 was given by Pfender (arXiv:1610.00952, "On colouring point visibility graphs"), refuting the proposed bound χ ≤ 5 when ω ≤ 4. The broader question of whether χ is bounded by any function of ω for point visibility graphs remains open, with only super-polynomial lower bounds known.

original_question: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear is not required; instead use the standard convention that two points u,v ∈ P are mutually visible if the open segment uv contains no point of P). The visibility graph V(P) has vertex set P and edges between every pair of mutually visible points. For a graph G, let ω(G) denote the clique number and χ(G) the chromatic number.

Prove that there exists an absolute constant c such that every point visibility graph G = V(P) satisfying ω(G) = 5 satisfies χ(G) ≤ c.

(Equivalently, extend the known result that point visibility graphs with clique number at most 4 have bounded chromatic number to the case of clique number 5.)
status_search_result: The general conjecture that point visibility graphs are χ-bounded remains open. The case ω ≤ 4 was established by Kára, Pór and Wood, but no published result extends the bound to ω = 5; surveys of χ-boundedness and recent work on polygon/pseudo-visibility graph colouring continue to list this as an open problem.
