original_question: For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. Two points x, y in P are said to be mutually visible (with respect to P) if the open line segment between x and y contains no point of P. A subset S ⊆ P is called a visible clique if every pair of distinct points in S is mutually visible. A subset of P is called collinear if all its points lie on a single line.

The big-line-big-clique conjecture asserts: for all integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, there exists an integer h(k, ℓ) such that every set P of at least h(k, ℓ) points in the plane contains either ℓ collinear points or a visible clique of size k.

It is known that the conjecture holds whenever ℓ ≤ 3 (since in this case general-position point sets are forced) and whenever k ≤ 5 (using the existence of an empty convex pentagon in any sufficiently large planar point set with no ℓ collinear points).

Prove the conjecture in either of the following remaining cases:
(a) k = 6 (with ℓ ≥ 2 arbitrary), or
(b) ℓ = 4 (with k ≥ 2 arbitrary).

That is, show that there is an integer h such that any planar point set of at least h points contains 6 mutually visible points or ℓ collinear points (case a), respectively contains k mutually visible points or 4 collinear points (case b).
category_tag: discrete geometry / visibility in point sets
status_search_result: The big-line-big-clique conjecture of Kára, Pór, and Wood remains open for finite planar point sets. The case k ≤ 5 was settled by the empty-pentagon theorem, and ℓ ≤ 3 is trivial; the next cases k = 6 and ℓ = 4 are still listed as unsolved on the Open Problem Garden and on the Wikipedia page for the conjecture, with no resolution found in subsequent literature.

original_question: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. A finite set P of points is said to be in general position if no three points of P are collinear. Given such a set P, a blocking set for P is a finite set Q of points in the plane, disjoint from P, such that for every pair of distinct points p, p' in P the open segment pp' contains at least one point of Q. Let b(P) denote the minimum cardinality of a blocking set for P, and define
   b(n) = min { b(P) : P is a set of n points in the plane in general position }.

Prove that b(n)/n → ∞ as n → ∞.
status_search_result: Available references on blocking visibility for points in general position establish only b(n) ≥ (1+ε)n type bounds in general (with Ω(n log n) known when P is in convex position). No source found that proves b(n)/n → ∞ for arbitrary n-point sets in general position; the question is repeatedly listed as an open problem in surveys on general-position problems.

original_question: Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?
self_contained_problem:
An obstacle representation of a simple graph G = (V, E) consists of an injective placement P : V → ℝ² of the vertices as points in the plane together with a finite collection Q of pairwise disjoint connected polygonal regions in the plane (the obstacles), disjoint from P(V), such that for any two distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, the open straight-line segment connecting P(u) and P(v) is disjoint from every obstacle in Q if and only if uv ∈ E. The obstacle number obs(G) of G is the minimum cardinality of Q over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every graph G on n vertices satisfies obs(G) ≤ C·n? Equivalently, is the obstacle number of an n-vertex graph bounded above by a linear function of n?
status_search_result: The question of whether every n-vertex graph has obstacle number O(n) appears to remain open. The best known general upper bound is O(n log n) (Balko, Cibulka, Valtr). On the lower-bound side, there are n-vertex graphs with obstacle number Ω(n/log log n), and a linear lower bound Ω(n) is known when obstacles are restricted to be convex (Balko et al., 2022). No linear upper bound for general (polygonal) obstacles has been established.

original_question: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. An obstacle representation of $G$ consists of a set $P$ of $|V|$ points in general position in the plane (one for each vertex) together with a finite collection $Q$ of pairwise disjoint closed connected subsets of the plane (called obstacles), each disjoint from $P$, such that for any two distinct vertices $u,v\in V$ the open straight-line segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle in $Q$ if and only if $\{u,v\}\in E$. The obstacle number $\mathrm{obs}(G)$ of $G$ is the minimum cardinality of $Q$ over all obstacle representations $(P,Q)$ of $G$.

Define $f(n)=\max\{\mathrm{obs}(G): G \text{ is a graph on } n \text{ vertices}\}$. It is known that $f(n)=\Omega(n/\log^2 n)$. Improve this lower bound; that is, determine an asymptotically larger lower bound for $f(n)$, ideally matching (up to logarithmic factors) the known upper bound $f(n)=O(n\log n)$.
status_search_result: The lower bound has been improved several times since the original O(n/log² n) bound. Mukkamala, Pach, and Pálvölgyi (2012) improved it to Ω(n/log n); Dujmović and Morin (2015) gave Ω(n/(log log n)²); and Balko, Ganian, Hliněný, Pach, and Valtr (2022) further improved bounds in restricted settings (Ω(n/log log n) for simple-polygon obstacles, Ω(n) for convex obstacles). Thus the problem has been partially solved—improvements exist—but a tight bound matching the O(n log n) upper bound is still not established.

original_question: For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with vertex set V(G). An obstacle representation of G consists of a set P of |V(G)| distinct points in the plane, in bijection with V(G), together with a finite set Q of pairwise disjoint simply connected closed regions (obstacles) in the plane whose interiors are disjoint from P, such that for any two vertices u, v of G, the open straight-line segment between the points representing u and v avoids every obstacle in Q if and only if uv is an edge of G. The obstacle number obs(G) of G is the minimum cardinality of Q over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

For each integer h > 1, determine

   f(h) := min { |V(G)| : G is a finite simple graph with obs(G) = h }.

That is, find the smallest number of vertices of any graph whose obstacle number equals exactly h.
status_search_result: The problem is widely cited as open. Subsequent research has obtained partial results: small graphs requiring 2 obstacles have been identified (e.g., a 10-vertex graph K*_{5,5} and an 8-vertex example needing two obstacles), and lower/upper bounds on obstacle numbers in general have been studied (Mukkamala et al.; Alpert–Koch–Laison; Balko et al.). However, no closed-form expression for the minimum vertex count f(h) for general h > 1 appears to have been established.

original_question: Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a simple graph. An obstacle representation of G consists of:
(i) an injection P: V → ℝ² mapping the vertices of G to distinct points in the plane in general position, and
(ii) a finite set Q of pairwise-disjoint closed polygonal regions ("obstacles") in the plane, disjoint from P(V),
such that for any two distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, the open straight-line segment between P(u) and P(v) avoids every obstacle in Q if and only if {u, v} ∈ E. The obstacle number of G, denoted obs(G), is the minimum cardinality |Q| over all obstacle representations (P, Q) of G.

Question: Does every planar graph G satisfy obs(G) ≤ 1?
status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Smaller examples (such as the gyroelongated 4-bipyramid, on 10 vertices) have since been found. A related question — whether the obstacle number of planar graphs is bounded by an absolute constant — remains open.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \{s_1, s_2, \dots, s_n\}$ be a finite set of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and let $P = \{p_1, p_2, \dots, p_{2n}\}$ be the set of their endpoints. Two points $p_i, p_j \in P$ are said to be mutually visible if the open line segment joining $p_i$ and $p_j$ does not intersect any segment in $S$. The segment (endpoint) visibility graph of $S$ is the graph $G(S)$ on vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_{2n}\}$ (with $v_i$ corresponding to $p_i$) in which $v_i v_j$ is an edge if and only if either $p_i$ and $p_j$ are mutually visible, or $p_i$ and $p_j$ are the two endpoints of a common segment of $S$.

Problem: Design an algorithm that, given the adjacency matrix of an arbitrary finite simple graph $G$, decides whether there exists a set $S$ of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane such that $G \cong G(S)$. Equivalently, characterize the class of graphs that arise as segment endpoint visibility graphs of finite sets of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.
status_search_result: The recognition, characterization, and reconstruction problems for segment (endpoint) visibility graphs of disjoint line segments in the plane are reported as open in the computational-geometry literature. Only partial progress is known: a characterization exists for the subclass of segment visibility graphs without $K_5$ as a minor (Everett et al.), and it has been proven that every segment endpoint visibility graph is Hamiltonian (Hoffmann–Tóth). No general recognition algorithm or full characterization is known.

context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles in segment visibility graphs
original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a finite set of pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane in general position (no three endpoints collinear), and let V be the set of the 2|S| endpoints of segments in S. The segment (endpoint) visibility graph G = (V, E) has an edge between two endpoints u, v ∈ V whenever the open segment uv does not properly intersect the relative interior of any segment in S; in particular, the two endpoints of each segment in S are adjacent in G. It is known that G always contains a Hamiltonian cycle whenever the segments are not all collinear.

Problem: Design an algorithm that, given only the adjacency matrix of such a segment visibility graph G (without the underlying geometric realization), outputs a Hamiltonian cycle of G, and runs in time polynomial in |V|.
status_search_result: While Hoffmann and Tóth proved that every segment endpoint visibility graph (of non-collinear disjoint segments) admits a Hamiltonian cycle, their proof relies on the geometric realization. The algorithmic problem of finding such a Hamiltonian cycle in polynomial time given only the adjacency matrix appears to remain open; recognition and reconstruction of visibility graphs more generally are noted as widely open in subsequent literature.

- The vertex set of $G$ consists of the $2n$ endpoints of the segments in $S$.
- Two vertices $u, v$ are joined by an edge of $G$ if and only if either (i) $u$ and $v$ are the two endpoints of a common segment $s_i \in S$, or (ii) the open segment $uv$ does not properly intersect any segment of $S$ (i.e., $u$ is visible from $v$ with respect to the obstacle set $S$).

original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs admit a unit bar visibility representation, meaning a bar visibility representation in which all horizontal bars have the same length.
self_contained_problem:
A bar visibility representation of a graph $G=(V,E)$ assigns to each vertex $v\in V$ a closed horizontal line segment ("bar") $B_v$ in the plane, where the bars have pairwise disjoint interiors and lie on distinct horizontal lines, in such a way that two vertices $u,v\in V$ are adjacent in $G$ if and only if there exists a non-degenerate vertical open rectangle (a "band of visibility") whose top edge lies in $B_u$, whose bottom edge lies in $B_v$, and whose interior is disjoint from every other bar $B_w$. A graph is called a unit bar visibility graph if it admits such a bar visibility representation in which all bars have the same (unit) length.

original_question: For k >= 5, determine whether there exist (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs.

A bar k-visibility representation consists of a finite collection of pairwise disjoint, horizontal, closed line segments ("bars") in the plane, no two of which share a y-coordinate. The associated bar k-visibility graph G has the bars as its vertices, and two bars b and b' are adjacent in G if and only if there is a vertical (closed) line segment whose endpoints lie on b and b' and whose interior intersects at most k other bars (and no endpoint of any other bar). self_contained_problem:

original_question: Design a constant-factor approximation algorithm for the minimum dominating set problem on visibility graphs of simple polygons.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with vertex set V(P). Two vertices u, v ∈ V(P) are said to see each other if the open line segment uv lies entirely in the interior of P (equivalently, the closed segment is contained in the closure of P and does not exit through the boundary). The visibility graph G(P) of P has vertex set V(P), with an edge {u,v} whenever u and v see each other. A dominating set of a graph G = (V, E) is a subset D ⊆ V such that every vertex in V \ D has at least one neighbor in D; the minimum dominating set problem asks for a dominating set of smallest cardinality.

Design a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an arbitrary simple polygon P, computes a dominating set of G(P) whose size is at most c · γ(G(P)), where γ(G(P)) denotes the minimum dominating set size of G(P) and c is an absolute constant independent of P. Equivalently, prove that the minimum dominating set problem on visibility graphs of simple polygons admits a constant-factor approximation algorithm.
status_search_result: For general simple polygons, the question (closely tied to Ghosh's conjecture on vertex guarding) remains unresolved. Constant-factor and PTAS results are known for restricted classes: a PTAS exists for terrain-like graphs and weakly-visible polygons (Ashur et al.), and constant-factor approximations are known for vertex guarding weakly-visible polygons. No constant-factor approximation for the minimum dominating set on visibility graphs of arbitrary simple polygons has been established as of recent literature.

context_brief: Maximum hidden sets with boundary order
original_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with vertex set V. The visibility graph G = (V, E) of P is the graph in which two vertices u, v ∈ V are adjacent if and only if the closed segment uv lies in the closure of P (so, in particular, all edges of the boundary of P are edges of G, and the boundary forms a Hamiltonian cycle of G). A hidden set (independent set) in G is a subset S ⊆ V such that no two vertices of S are adjacent in G; equivalently, no two vertices of S see each other inside P. 

Devise an algorithm that, given as input the visibility graph G together with the distinguished Hamiltonian cycle of G that corresponds to the boundary of P, computes a hidden set of G of maximum cardinality. In particular, determine the computational complexity of this problem and, if possible, give a polynomial-time exact algorithm or prove hardness.
status_search_result: The maximum hidden set problem in visibility graphs of simple polygons is known to be NP-hard and APX-hard. Whether it admits a polynomial-time exact algorithm given the boundary Hamiltonian cycle is open; even membership in NP is unresolved (it might be ∃ℝ-hard). Recent work (2024+) gives approximation algorithms (e.g., a 1/2-approximation for simple polygons; exact polynomial-time algorithms only for restricted classes such as funnel polygons and monotone mountains). The problem as posed remains open.

original_question: Design an approximation algorithm for computing a maximum hidden set in a visibility graph.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon (possibly with holes) in the plane with vertex set V(P). Two points x, y ∈ P are mutually visible if the closed segment xy is contained in P. The visibility graph G(P) has vertex set V(P), with an edge between u and v whenever u and v are mutually visible in P. A hidden set in G(P) is a subset H ⊆ V(P) such that no two vertices of H are mutually visible (equivalently, an independent set of G(P)). The maximum hidden set problem asks for a hidden set of maximum cardinality.

Design a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the maximum hidden set problem on visibility graphs of polygons, and analyze its approximation ratio. Specifically, determine the best achievable approximation factor for this problem (for the general class of polygons, and/or for natural subclasses such as simple polygons without holes).
status_search_result: The problem is known to be NP-hard and APX-hard, and for polygons with holes is inapproximable within n^ε unless P=NP. Recent work (Browne, Kasthurirangan, Mitchell, Polishchuk; 2024) provides a 1/2-approximation for the maximum hidden set in polygons weakly visible from a convex edge, and further hardness/approximability results for visibility graph problems appear in 2024 surveys. No constant-factor approximation is known for general simple polygons, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G, compute a maximum clique of G.
self_contained_problem: A simple polygon P in the plane is a closed region whose boundary is a simple polygonal curve with vertex set V(P). The visibility graph G(P) of P has vertex set V(P), and two vertices u, v are adjacent in G(P) if and only if the open line segment uv lies entirely inside the closed region P (equivalently, u and v see each other in P). A graph G is called a visibility graph if there exists a simple polygon P (possibly with polygonal holes) such that G is isomorphic to G(P). A clique in a graph is a set of pairwise adjacent vertices, and a maximum clique is a clique of largest possible size.\n\nProblem. Design an algorithm that, given as input the adjacency matrix of an n-vertex graph G that is guaranteed to be a visibility graph, computes a maximum clique of G. In particular, determine whether such a maximum clique can be computed in time polynomial in n when only the abstract adjacency matrix of G is provided (no embedding or polygon realization is given).
status_search_result: Polynomial-time algorithms (e.g., O(n^3)) are known for finding a maximum clique in the visibility graph of a simple polygon without holes when a polygon realization is given, while the problem is hard to approximate for visibility graphs of polygons with holes. However, when only the abstract adjacency matrix of an (unknown) visibility graph is supplied, the problem appears to remain open, as visibility graph recognition itself is a long-standing open problem and no general polynomial-time algorithm for maximum clique is known in this setting.

original_question: Improve the current lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons with n vertices.
self_contained_problem:
A simple polygon P in the plane is a closed region bounded by a simple polygonal curve with n vertices v_1, ..., v_n. The visibility graph G(P) of P is the graph on vertex set {v_1, ..., v_n} in which two vertices v_i and v_j are adjacent if and only if the open line segment v_i v_j lies entirely inside the closed region P (i.e., they "see" each other through P; equivalently, the segment does not cross the exterior of P). Two visibility graphs are considered the same if they are isomorphic as abstract graphs.

Let f(n) denote the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs that arise from simple polygons with exactly n vertices. It is known that
    2^{n-4} ≤ f(n) ≤ 2^{O(n log n)}.

Improve these bounds: establish either a lower bound on f(n) that grows asymptotically faster than 2^{n-4}, or an upper bound on f(n) that grows asymptotically slower than 2^{O(n log n)} (ideally determining the correct asymptotic order of log f(n)).

original_question: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple undirected graph. A point-visibility realization of G in the plane is an injective map f : V → R^2 such that for any two distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, the open straight-line segment between f(u) and f(v) contains no point f(w) with w ∈ V \ {u, v}, and {u, v} ∈ E if and only if no such collinear blocker exists. (Equivalently, edges of G correspond exactly to mutually visible pairs of points among the placed points, where visibility is blocked only by other points of the realization.) Such a graph G is called a (point) visibility graph.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial p(n) such that every point visibility graph G on n vertices admits a point-visibility realization f : V → Z^2 in which every coordinate of every point f(v) is an integer whose binary representation uses at most p(n) bits?

Equivalently: can every realizable visibility graph on n vertices be drawn with integer coordinates of bit-length polynomial in n?
status_search_result: Recent work (Cardinal–Hoffmann, SoCG 2015 / DCG 2017) shows point visibility graph recognition is ∃R-complete and NP-hard, and exhibits visibility graphs of grid points requiring doubly exponential grid size. Whether every visibility graph admits an integer-coordinate realization with only polynomially many bits per coordinate (which would put recognition in NP) remains open as of the most recent results found.

original_question: Determine the correct asymptotic order of the minimum number of bits needed by an optimal covering-set representation of a visibility graph, where a covering set is a family of cliques and complete bipartite graphs whose members are subgraphs of the visibility graph and whose union covers every edge.
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be the visibility graph of a set of n non-crossing line segments in the plane (vertices are segment endpoints, with edges joining two endpoints if the open segment between them does not cross any input segment). A covering set of G is a family F = {H_1, H_2, ..., H_k} of subgraphs of G such that each H_i is either a clique or a complete bipartite graph, and every edge of G belongs to at least one H_i. The bit-size of such a covering set is the total number of bits required to encode F by listing, for each H_i, its vertex set (or, for bicliques, its two parts), using ceil(log_2 n) bits per vertex reference.

Let B(G) denote the minimum bit-size over all covering sets of G, and let B(n) = max_G B(G), where the maximum is taken over all visibility graphs G on n vertices arising from n non-crossing segments. It is known that B(n) = O(n log^4 n) and B(n) = Ω(n log^2 n).

Determine the correct asymptotic order of B(n).

No source was found closing the asymptotic gap on the bit-size of an optimal covering-set representation, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.
self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon with n vertices, and let G = (V,E) be its visibility graph: V is the vertex set of P, and {u,v} ∈ E if and only if the open line segment uv lies in the closure of the interior of P (so u and v see each other). 

A covering set for G is a family F = {H_1, …, H_k} of subgraphs of G such that:
(i) each H_i is either a clique of G or a complete bipartite subgraph of G (with both sides being independent in H_i, but the bipartition need not be induced in G);
(ii) every edge of G is contained in at least one H_i.

The size (or bit complexity) of F is the total number of vertices listed across the H_i, i.e. Σ_i |V(H_i)|; this is the natural bit-cost of representing G via F.

It is known that every visibility graph of a simple n-gon admits a covering set of size O(n log³ n), and there exist n-vertex simple polygons whose visibility graphs require any such covering to have size Ω(n log n).

Problem. Design an algorithm which, given a simple polygon P with n vertices, runs in time polynomial in n and outputs a covering set F of its visibility graph G whose size matches the asymptotic upper bound O(n log³ n) (more generally, matching the best known asymptotic upper bound on the minimum covering-set size).
status_search_result: Existence results give a covering of size O(n log³ n) for visibility graphs of simple polygons, with a lower bound of Ω(n log n). A web search did not surface a published polynomial-time construction algorithm matching the upper bound, nor a definitive resolution of the constructive question; current status appears unverified.

context_brief: Bounded size of k-blocked point sets
original_question: For each integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points? Here a k-blocked point set is a set of planar points colored with k colors so that mutually visible points receive different colors and points that are not visible because of collinear blockers receive the same color.
self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. For a finite set P of points in the plane, say two distinct points v, w ∈ P are visible in P if no point of P \ {v, w} lies on the open line segment vw; otherwise v and w are blocked (by some collinear point of P between them).

Fix an integer k ≥ 2. A finite planar point set P is called k-blocked if there is a coloring of P with exactly k colors such that:
(i) any two points of P that are visible in P receive different colors, and
(ii) any two points of P that are blocked (by a point of P on the open segment between them) receive the same color.

Question: For every integer k ≥ 2, does there exist an integer n = n(k) such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points? Equivalently, is the maximum cardinality of a k-blocked point set finite for each fixed k?

context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets
original_question: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Two distinct points $v,w \in P$ are said to be visible in $P$ if the open line segment between $v$ and $w$ contains no point of $P$; otherwise they are blocked. For an integer $k \geq 2$, the set $P$ is called k-blocked if there exists a coloring $c : P \to \{1,2,\dots,k\}$ using exactly $k$ colors such that:

(i) for every pair of distinct points $v,w \in P$ that are visible in $P$, $c(v) \neq c(w)$;
(ii) for every pair of distinct points $v,w \in P$ that are blocked in $P$ (i.e., some point of $P$ lies strictly between them on the segment $vw$), $c(v) = c(w)$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $k \geq 2$, every $k$-blocked point set $P$ satisfies $|P| \leq C k^2$.

Recent papers (e.g., on visibility cliques and cubic containers, 2026) continue to address related questions without resolving this conjecture, indicating it remains open.

context_brief: Color-class size in k-blocked point sets
original_question: In every k-blocked point set, must each color class contain at most k points?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane. Say that two distinct points $v, w \in P$ are mutually visible in $P$ if no other point of $P$ lies on the open line segment $vw$. For a fixed integer $k \geq 2$, a $k$-coloring of $P$ is an assignment of one of $k$ colors to each point of $P$ such that:
(i) if $v, w \in P$ are mutually visible, then $v$ and $w$ receive different colors, and
(ii) if $v, w \in P$ are not mutually visible (i.e., some point of $P$ lies on the open segment $vw$), then $v$ and $w$ receive the same color.
A finite point set $P$ is called a $k$-blocked point set if it admits such a $k$-coloring. The color classes of any such coloring partition $P$ into "monochromatic" subsets (which must be collinear-blocked independent sets in the visibility graph).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $k \geq 2$ and every $k$-blocked point set $P$, each color class of any valid $k$-coloring of $P$ contains at most $k$ points.
status_search_result: Web search returned the work on blocking colored point sets where small cases are settled (every 2-blocked set has at most 3 points, every 3-blocked set has at most 6 points, and every 4-blocked set has at most 12 points), and constructions of k-blocked sets with about k^{1.79} points are known. However, no source explicitly confirms or refutes the specific conjecture that every color class in a k-blocked point set has at most k points. Status appears unresolved in the indexed literature.

original_question: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?

Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane, no three of which are required to be in any particular position. The visibility graph $G = G(P)$ has vertex set $P$, and two distinct points $u, v \in P$ are joined by an edge if and only if the open line segment $uv$ contains no point of $P$. For a graph $H$, let $\delta(H)$ denote its minimum degree and $\kappa(H)$ denote its vertex-connectivity (the minimum number of vertices whose removal disconnects $H$ or reduces it to a single vertex).

$$\kappa(G) \;\geq\; \frac{2\,\delta(G) + 1}{3}.$$

$$L(d,m) = dH - m(E_1 + \cdots + E_r) \quad \text{on } X,$$
and set
$$a(S,m) := \min\{ d \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} : h^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(L(d,m))) > 0 \}.$$
Equivalently, $a(S,m)$ is the least degree of a nonzero homogeneous polynomial in $\mathbb{K}[x_0, \ldots, x_N]$ that vanishes to order at least $m$ at every point of $S$. The Waldschmidt constant of $S$ is defined as
$$\widehat{\alpha}(S) := \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{a(S,m)}{m},$$
and one has $m \cdot \widehat{\alpha}(S) \le a(S,m)$ for every $m \ge 1$.

Develop computational or conceptual methods for evaluating, estimating, or bounding $\widehat{\alpha}(S)$ for arbitrary finite sets $S \subset \mathbb{P}^N$.
status_search_result: The general problem of evaluating, estimating, or bounding the Waldschmidt constant $\widehat{\alpha}(S)$ for arbitrary point configurations remains an active open research area. Partial results exist (e.g., exact values for star configurations, standard k-configurations, and recursive lower bounds for very general points connected to Demailly's conjecture, with recent progress in 2024–2025), but no general method is known. The problem continues to motivate substantial recent literature.

original_question: Let S be a finite subset of P^N, let a(S,1) be the least degree of a hypersurface containing S, and let e(S) be the Waldschmidt constant lim_{m->infinity} a(S,m)/m. Is it always true that (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N <= e(S)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N \geq 2$ and let $S \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ (over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero) be a finite set of points. For each positive integer $m$, define
$$a(S,m) = \min\{\, d \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} : \text{there exists a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree } d \text{ vanishing to order at least } m \text{ at every point of } S\,\}.$$
Equivalently, if $I(S) \subset k[x_0,\dots,x_N]$ is the homogeneous radical ideal of $S$ and $I(S)^{(m)}$ is its $m$-th symbolic power, then $a(S,m)$ is the least degree of a nonzero element of $I(S)^{(m)}$. The Waldschmidt constant of $S$ is
$$\widehat{\alpha}(S) := \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{a(S,m)}{m} = \inf_{m \geq 1} \frac{a(S,m)}{m}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every finite set $S \subset \mathbb{P}^N$,
$$\frac{a(S,1) + N - 1}{N} \;\leq\; \widehat{\alpha}(S).$$
status_search_result: This is Chudnovsky's conjecture. It is known unconditionally for $N=2$ (Chudnovsky), for very general/general configurations of points in $\mathbb{P}^N$ (Dumnicki–Tutaj-Gasińska, Fouli–Mantero–Xie, Bisui–Hà–Nguyen–Trung and others), and in various special cases (e.g., points on rational normal curves, star configurations). The general case for arbitrary finite sets of points in $\mathbb{P}^N$ with $N\geq 3$ remains open.

original_question: Suppose S is a finite subset of P^N and a(S,m) is the least degree d such that h^0(X, L(d,m)) > 0 on the blow-up of P^N at S. If for some m one has a(S,m)/m = (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N, must S either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration? Likewise, if e(S) = (a(S,1) + N - 1)/N, must S either lie in a hyperplane or be a star configuration?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 2$ and let $S=\{P_1,\dots,P_s\}$ be a finite set of distinct points in projective space $\mathbb{P}^N$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. Let $\pi: X\to \mathbb{P}^N$ be the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^N$ at the points of $S$, with exceptional divisors $E_1,\dots,E_s$, and let $H$ denote the pullback of the hyperplane class. For positive integers $d,m$, define the line bundle
$$L(d,m) := dH - m(E_1+\cdots+E_s),$$
and define
$$\alpha(S,m) := \min\{\,d\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0} : h^0(X, L(d,m))>0\,\},$$
i.e. the least degree of a hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^N$ passing through every point of $S$ with multiplicity at least $m$. The Waldschmidt constant of $S$ is
$$\widehat{\alpha}(S) := \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m} = \inf_{m\geq 1}\frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m}.$$
A star configuration of points in $\mathbb{P}^N$ is the set of all pairwise intersection points of $N$ general hyperplanes among a collection of $\geq N$ general hyperplanes (equivalently, the points obtained as transverse intersections of every $N$-tuple from a generic family of hyperplanes).

It is known that for any finite set $S\subset\mathbb{P}^N$ not contained in a hyperplane, one has the inequality
$$\frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m}\;\geq\;\frac{\alpha(S,1)+N-1}{N}\qquad\text{for all }m\geq 1,$$
and consequently $\widehat{\alpha}(S)\geq \frac{\alpha(S,1)+N-1}{N}$.

Questions:
(a) Suppose there exists some $m\geq 1$ with
$$\frac{\alpha(S,m)}{m} = \frac{\alpha(S,1)+N-1}{N}.$$
Must $S$ either be contained in a hyperplane, or be a star configuration?

(b) Suppose
$$\widehat{\alpha}(S) = \frac{\alpha(S,1)+N-1}{N}.$$
Must $S$ either be contained in a hyperplane, or be a star configuration?
status_search_result: Web searches turn up active research on Waldschmidt constants of star configurations and related point configurations (e.g. matroid/k-configurations, icosahedral configurations, fat flat subschemes), but no source clearly resolves the characterization question of whether equality in the bound $\alpha(S,m)/m=(\alpha(S,1)+N-1)/N$ (or the analogous Waldschmidt-constant equality) forces $S$ to be contained in a hyperplane or to be a star configuration. The status appears to remain unresolved in general.

original_question: Let f : X -> P^N be the blow-up of distinct points p_1, ..., p_r with exceptional divisors E_1, ..., E_r, and let D = dH - m_1 E_1 - ... - m_r E_r where H is the pullback of a hyperplane. Is there a general way to determine whether the divisor D is semi-effective, meaning that h^0(X, nD) > 0 for some integer n > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be distinct points in the complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^N$ (with $N\geq 2$), and let $f:X\to\mathbb{P}^N$ be the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^N$ at these points, with exceptional divisors $E_1,\dots,E_r$. Let $H$ denote the pullback to $X$ of the hyperplane class on $\mathbb{P}^N$. For integers $d,m_1,\dots,m_r$, consider the divisor
$$D = dH - m_1 E_1 - \cdots - m_r E_r$$
on $X$. Call a line bundle (or divisor) $L$ on $X$ semi-effective if there exists an integer $n>0$ such that $h^0(X, nL) > 0$.

Provide a general criterion, in terms of the data $(N, r, d, m_1,\dots,m_r)$ and the position of the points $p_1,\dots,p_r$, that determines whether $D$ is semi-effective.
category_tag: Linear systems on blow-ups of projective space
status_search_result: No general criterion is known. Determining effectivity of such divisors generalizes long-standing open conjectures (Nagata, SHGH/Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz) on linear systems through general points of projective space, and recent work shows that for sufficiently many very general points, blow-ups of projective space need not be Mori Dream Spaces and may have infinitely many extremal effective divisors. Thus the problem of giving a general semi-effectivity criterion for $D=dH-\sum m_iE_i$ remains open.

original_question: For a finite-length monomial subscheme type Z = Spec k[x,y]/I on a smooth projective surface S, let Hilb_I S denote the constructible locus in the Hilbert scheme whose closed points are subschemes Y subset S isomorphic to Z. Describe Hilb_I S: is this locus locally closed, and what adjacency relations occur between such loci inside the Hilbert scheme?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $S$ be a smooth irreducible projective surface over $k$. Fix a monomial ideal $I \subset k[x,y]$ such that $Z := \mathrm{Spec}\, k[x,y]/I$ has finite length $n$, and let $\mathrm{Hilb}^n S$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing length-$n$ closed subschemes of $S$. Define
$$\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S \;:=\; \{\, [Y] \in \mathrm{Hilb}^n S \;:\; Y \text{ is a closed subscheme of } S \text{ isomorphic (as a } k\text{-scheme) to } Z\,\},$$
which is an irreducible constructible subset of $\mathrm{Hilb}^n S$.

(a) Describe $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ explicitly. In particular, determine whether $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ is locally closed in $\mathrm{Hilb}^n S$.

(b) For monomial ideals $I, I' \subset k[x,y]$ with $\dim_k k[x,y]/I = \dim_k k[x,y]/I' = n$, determine the adjacency relations between the loci $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ and $\mathrm{Hilb}_{I'}\, S$, i.e., describe when $\mathrm{Hilb}_{I'}\, S$ meets the closure of $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ inside $\mathrm{Hilb}^n S$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of the described stratification problem (whether the isomorphism-type loci $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\,S$ are locally closed and what their adjacency pattern is). General references on Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces discuss related stratifications by partition/monomial type and their closure relations combinatorially, but no source explicitly confirms a complete answer to the question as stated. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: Let Y be a general subscheme of a smooth projective surface S lying in the monomial Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to a finite-length monomial ideal I, and let D be a divisor on S. What can be said about the cohomology of I_Y tensor O_S(D)? In particular, what conditions on S, I, and D force h^0(I_Y tensor O_S(D)) = max{0, h^0(O_S(D)) - n}, where n is the length of the monomial scheme?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, and let $I \subset \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^2}$ (equivalently, a monomial ideal in the local ring at a chosen point of $S$) be a finite-colength monomial ideal, defining a zero-dimensional monomial subscheme $Z \subset S$ of length $n$. Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ denote the locally closed locus inside the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(S)$ parametrizing subschemes of $S$ that are locally isomorphic to $Z$ at one point and reduced elsewhere; this locus is irreducible, so one may speak of a general (very general, generic) subscheme $Y \in \mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$. Let $D$ be a divisor on $S$, and let $\mathcal{I}_Y \subset \mathcal{O}_S$ denote the ideal sheaf of $Y$.

Determine geometric/numerical conditions on the triple $(S, I, D)$ which guarantee that for a general $Y \in \mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$,
$$h^0\bigl(S, \mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_S(D)\bigr) \;=\; \max\bigl\{0,\; h^0(S, \mathcal{O}_S(D)) - n\bigr\}.$$
That is, characterize when imposing the monomial scheme $Y$ of length $n$ as base conditions on the linear system $|D|$ imposes the maximal number of independent conditions.
category_tag: Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question generalizing classical interpolation/SHGH-type problems for fat points to arbitrary monomial zero-dimensional schemes on surfaces. A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution; results in the literature on Hilbert schemes of points and monomial ideals do not appear to address this specific cohomological conditions question in full generality.

original_question: Let S = P^2 and let I = (y, x^r)^m with integers r > 9 and m >= 1. If Y is a general element of the Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to this monomial ideal, is it true that for every degree d > 0 one has dim H^0(I_Y tensor O_{P^2}(d)) = max{0, binom(d+2,2) - r binom(m+1,2)}?

Let $S=\mathbb{P}^2$ be the projective plane over an algebraically closed field, with homogeneous coordinates such that $x,y$ denote local affine coordinates on a chosen open subset. Fix integers $r>9$ and $m\geq 1$, and consider the monomial ideal
$$I=(y,x^{r})^{m}\subset k[x,y].$$
Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_{I}\,S$ denote the locus in the Hilbert scheme of $S$ parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes of $S$ that are locally (at a single distinguished point) isomorphic to the subscheme defined by $I$ (equivalently, the closure of the orbit, under the group of automorphisms of $S$ acting on a marked point, of the subscheme cut out by $I$ at that point). For a closed subscheme $Y\subset S$ let $\mathcal{I}_{Y}\subset\mathcal{O}_{S}$ be its ideal sheaf.

original_question: Let S = P^2 and let I = (y, x^r)^m with integers r > 9 and m >= 1. If Y is a general element of the Hilbert-scheme locus Hilb_I S associated to this monomial ideal, is it true that H^0(I_Y tensor O_{P^2}(d)) = 0 for every degree d satisfying d <= m sqrt(r)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \mathbb{P}^2$ over an algebraically closed field, and fix integers $r > 9$ and $m \geq 1$. Consider the monomial ideal
$$I = (y, x^r)^m \subset k[x,y,z]$$
(viewed as a homogeneous ideal in suitable coordinates on $\mathbb{P}^2$, with the corresponding zero-dimensional subscheme supported at the point $[0:0:1]$). Let $\mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ denote the locally closed locus in the Hilbert scheme of $\mathbb{P}^2$ parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes whose ideal has the same equivariant Hilbert function (i.e., the same monomial-ideal type) as $I$, and let $Y \in \mathrm{Hilb}_I\, S$ be a general element. Let $\mathcal{I}_Y$ denote the ideal sheaf of $Y$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $d$ with $d \leq m\sqrt{r}$,
$$H^0\!\left(\mathbb{P}^2,\ \mathcal{I}_Y \otimes \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(d)\right) = 0.$$

original_question: Let X -> P^2 be the blow-up of generic points p_1, ..., p_s. If C subset X is a prime divisor, must h^1(X, O_X(C)) vanish?

Let $p_1, \ldots, p_s$ be generic points of the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\pi : X \to \mathbb{P}^2$ denote the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at these points. Let $C \subset X$ be a prime (i.e. integral) divisor on $X$, and let $\mathcal{O}_X(C)$ denote the associated invertible sheaf. Prove or disprove: the first sheaf cohomology group always vanishes, i.e.
$$h^1\bigl(X,\, \mathcal{O}_X(C)\bigr) = 0.$$

original_question: Can the SHGH vanishing statement for blow-ups of P^2 be extended beyond the case of generic blown-up points? More concretely, how can one remove the assumption that the points are generic in the SHGH conjecture?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p_1,\dots,p_n$ be distinct points in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$, and let $m_1,\dots,m_n$ be positive integers. Let $\pi: X \to \mathbb{P}^2$ denote the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$, with exceptional divisors $E_1,\dots,E_n$, and let $H$ denote the pullback of the hyperplane class. For an integer $d \ge 0$, consider the linear system
$$\mathcal{L}(d; m_1,\dots,m_n) := \big| dH - \textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n m_i E_i \big|$$
on $X$, equivalently the linear system of plane curves of degree $d$ with multiplicity at least $m_i$ at $p_i$. Its virtual dimension is
$$v(d;m_1,\dots,m_n) := \binom{d+2}{2} - 1 - \sum_{i=1}^n \binom{m_i+1}{2},$$
its expected dimension is $\max(v,-1)$, and the system is called special if its actual dimension exceeds the expected dimension.

The Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz (SHGH) conjecture asserts that when the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ are very general, $\mathcal{L}(d;m_1,\dots,m_n)$ is special if and only if it has a multiple $(-1)$-curve in its base locus (equivalently, there exists a $(-1)$-curve $C$ on $X$ such that $\mathcal{L}\cdot C \le -2$).

Problem. Formulate and prove a version of the SHGH statement that does not require the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ to be in very general position: identify explicit geometric conditions on a configuration of (possibly special) points $p_1,\dots,p_n \in \mathbb{P}^2$ under which the speciality of every linear system $\mathcal{L}(d;m_1,\dots,m_n)$ can be characterized in terms of curves in its base locus, thereby removing the genericity hypothesis from the SHGH conjecture.
category_tag: Linear systems on blow-ups of projective plane
status_search_result: The SHGH conjecture itself remains open in general, and the question of removing the genericity hypothesis is an active area with only partial progress. Recent work (e.g., on Seshadri constants via Okounkov functions and on Nagata-type statements) addresses related variants and special configurations, but no full non-generic version of SHGH has been established.

original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface, either rational or in characteristic 0. Does there exist a constant c_X such that for every prime divisor C on X one has h^1(X, C) <= c_X h^0(X, C)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, and assume that either $X$ is rational or the base field has characteristic $0$. For a divisor $D$ on $X$, write $h^i(X,D) := \dim_k H^i(X, \mathcal{O}_X(D))$. A prime divisor on $X$ is an integral curve $C \subset X$, identified with its associated Weil/Cartier divisor.

Question: Does there exist a constant $c_X > 0$, depending only on $X$, such that
$$h^1(X, C) \;\leq\; c_X \, h^0(X, C)$$
holds for every prime divisor $C$ on $X$?
category_tag: Bounded cohomology of divisors on surfaces
status_search_result: The "bounded cohomology property" conjecture is known to remain open in general. Partial results are available: it has been verified in several cases for smooth projective surfaces of Picard number 2 (e.g., when the Kodaira dimension is at most 1 with a negative curve, or when X has two negative curves, and certain Kodaira-dimension-2 cases with irregularity 0 and Iitaka dimension 1). No general proof for all rational surfaces or all characteristic-0 smooth projective surfaces appears in the literature.

original_question: Let X be a projective manifold with large algebraic fundamental group, and let L be an ample line bundle on X. Given a positive number N, does there exist a finite etale cover p : X' -> X such that either (1) the Seshadri number of p^*L at every point of X' is greater than N, or (2) the Seshadri number along the diagonal D' subset X' x X' of p_e^*(p_1^*L tensor p_2^*L) is greater than N? If neither statement is always true, what condition on the fundamental group of X guarantees a positive answer?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety, and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Recall the following definitions.

(a) The Seshadri constant of $L$ at a point $x \in X$ is
$$\varepsilon(L;x) \;=\; \inf_{C \ni x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\operatorname{mult}_x C},$$
where the infimum is over all irreducible curves $C \subset X$ passing through $x$. More generally, for a closed subscheme $Z \subset Y$ on a projective variety $Y$, the Seshadri constant of an ample line bundle $M$ along $Z$ is
$$\varepsilon(M;Z) \;=\; \sup\{\, t \ge 0 : \mu^* M - t E \text{ is nef}\,\},$$
where $\mu : \widetilde{Y} \to Y$ is the blow-up of $Y$ along $Z$ with exceptional divisor $E$.

(b) The algebraic fundamental group $\pi_1^{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ is called large if for every positive-dimensional irreducible subvariety $Z \subset X$ with normalization $\widetilde Z \to Z$, the image of $\pi_1^{\mathrm{alg}}(\widetilde Z) \to \pi_1^{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ is infinite.

For a finite étale cover $p : X' \to X$, write $p_e : X' \times X' \to X \times X$ for the induced cover, $p_1, p_2 : X \times X \to X$ for the two projections, and $D' \subset X' \times X'$ for the diagonal.

Question. Suppose $X$ has large algebraic fundamental group and $L$ is ample on $X$. For every $N > 0$:

(1) Does there exist a finite étale cover $p : X' \to X$ such that $\varepsilon(p^*L;x') > N$ for every $x' \in X'$?

(2) Does there exist a finite étale cover $p : X' \to X$ such that the Seshadri constant of $p_e^*(p_1^*L \otimes p_2^*L)$ along the diagonal $D' \subset X' \times X'$ is greater than $N$?

If either statement fails in general, determine a condition on the fundamental group of $X$ that ensures a positive answer.
status_search_result: A 2014 preprint by G. and L. F. Di Cerbo ("On Seshadri constants of varieties with large fundamental group", arXiv:1411.1033) affirmatively resolves part (1) of this problem: when $X$ has large algebraic fundamental group and $L$ is ample, the Seshadri constant $\varepsilon(p^*L)$ can be made arbitrarily large by passing to a suitable finite étale cover $p : X' \to X$. They also prove the analogous statement when $\pi_1(X)$ is large and residually finite, and extend to big and nef line bundles outside the augmented base locus, answering Hwang's conjecture.

original_question: Do the known results for line arrangements in P^2 extend to arrangements in higher-dimensional projective space? In particular, if A is a hyperplane arrangement in P^n, can one give an explicit description of the graded Betti numbers of the Orlik-Terao algebra C(A) in terms of the geometry of A?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{A} = \{H_1, \dots, H_d\}$ be an essential hyperplane arrangement in complex projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$, where each hyperplane $H_i$ is the zero locus of a linear form $\ell_i \in S = \mathbb{C}[x_0, \dots, x_n]$. The Orlik–Terao algebra of $\mathcal{A}$ is defined as
$$ C(\mathcal{A}) \;=\; \mathbb{C}\!\left[\tfrac{1}{\ell_1}, \dots, \tfrac{1}{\ell_d}\right] \;\subset\; \mathbb{C}(x_0,\dots,x_n), $$
graded so that each generator $1/\ell_i$ has degree $1$. Equivalently, $C(\mathcal{A}) \cong \mathbb{C}[y_1,\dots,y_d]/I(\mathcal{A})$, where $I(\mathcal{A})$ is the Orlik–Terao ideal generated by the homogenizations of the linear dependencies among the forms $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_d$.

It is known that the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $C(\mathcal{A})$ as a graded module over $\mathbb{C}[y_1,\dots,y_d]$ is bounded above by $n$.

Problem. For an arbitrary hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ with $n \geq 2$, give an explicit formula for the graded Betti numbers
$$ \beta_{i,j}(C(\mathcal{A})) \;=\; \dim_{\mathbb{C}} \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathbb{C}[y_1,\dots,y_d]}\!\bigl(C(\mathcal{A}), \mathbb{C}\bigr)_j $$
in terms of the combinatorics and geometry of $\mathcal{A}$ (e.g., its intersection lattice and the dimensions and incidences of the flats). In particular, do explicit descriptions known for line arrangements in $\mathbb{P}^2$ extend to higher-dimensional arrangements?
status_search_result: Web searches reveal substantial work on Orlik–Terao algebras (e.g., results on regularity, modular decompositions, and resolutions for special classes such as generic or graphic arrangements), but no general explicit formula for the graded Betti numbers of $C(\mathcal{A})$ for arbitrary hyperplane arrangements in $\mathbb{P}^n$ in terms of the geometry/combinatorics of $\mathcal{A}$ appears in the located sources. The status of the general problem is therefore not conclusively determined from available evidence.

original_question: Let I be a radical ideal of big height e. Must the symbolic power containment I^(m) subset I^r hold whenever m >= re - (e - 1)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R = k[x_1,\dots,x_N]$ be a polynomial ring (or more generally a regular ring). For an ideal $I \subseteq R$, the $m$-th symbolic power of $I$ is
$$I^{(m)} = \bigcap_{P \in \mathrm{Ass}(R/I)} (I^m R_P \cap R).$$
For a radical ideal $I$, this equals the intersection of the $m$-th ordinary powers of the minimal primes localized appropriately. The big height of $I$, denoted $\mathrm{bight}(I)$, is the maximum of the heights of the associated (equivalently, minimal) primes of $I$.

Question: Let $I \subseteq R$ be a radical ideal with big height $e = \mathrm{bight}(I)$. Is it true that for all positive integers $r$ and $m$ satisfying
$$m \;\ge\; r\,e - (e-1),$$
the symbolic power containment
$$I^{(m)} \;\subseteq\; I^r$$
holds?
category_tag: Symbolic powers of ideals / Harbourne–Huneke containment
status_search_result: This is the Harbourne–Huneke containment conjecture. The original (uniform) form is known to fail in general: explicit counterexamples exist (e.g., Dumnicki–Szemberg–Tutaj-Gasińska and subsequent work), so the answer to "must it hold for all r,m as stated" is no. However, the conjecture is known to hold in many important cases (monomial ideals, generic points, etc.) and a "stable" version (containment for r sufficiently large) has been established under various hypotheses, e.g. by Grifo and collaborators in connection with Chudnovsky's conjecture.

original_question: Suppose (R, m) is a regular local ring of dimension n and I subset R is an ideal with big height e. Do the following containments hold: (1) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r) I^r for m >= rn; (2) I^(m) subset m^(rn-r-(n-1)) I^r for m >= rn - (n - 1); (3) I^(m) subset m^(re-r) I^r for m >= re; and (4) I^(m) subset m^(re-r-(e-1)) I^r for m >= re - (e - 1)?
status_search_result: These are refined versions of the Harbourne–Huneke containment conjectures relating symbolic and ordinary powers of ideals in regular local rings, sharpened by an extra factor of a power of the maximal ideal. The base containments $I^{(rn-r+1)}\subseteq I^r$ and $I^{(re-e+1)}\subseteq I^r$ (with big height $e$) are known to fail in general (counterexamples by Dumnicki–Szemberg–Tutaj-Gasińska and others), but partial positive results are known (e.g. for monomial ideals, F-pure rings, and stable/asymptotic versions). The refined $\mathfrak{m}$-power versions stated here remain open in general; recent work establishes them in special cases (e.g., stable Harbourne–Huneke containment for general points, F-pure cases) but no general proof or disproof is known.

original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r distinct points in arbitrary position, and let L be an effective nef divisor on X. Must one of the following hold: (a) there exists m >= 1 such that h^1(mL) = 0, with m = 1 expected when the points are in general position; or (b) there exists a curve C on X, not necessarily irreducible, such that |L - C| is nonempty, the arithmetic genus p_a(C) is positive, and L.C = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the blow-up of the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $r$ distinct points, where $r \geq 1$ is arbitrary and the points are in arbitrary (not necessarily general) position, subject only to being distinct. Let $L$ be an effective nef divisor on $X$. Decide whether at least one of the following two statements must hold:

(a) There exists an integer $m \geq 1$ such that $h^1(X, \mathcal{O}_X(mL)) = 0$. Moreover, when the points are in general position, one expects that $m = 1$ suffices.

(b) There exists a curve $C$ on $X$ (not required to be irreducible) such that the linear system $|L - C|$ is nonempty, the arithmetic genus satisfies $p_a(C) > 0$, and the intersection number $L \cdot C = 0$.

Either prove that for every such $X$ and every effective nef divisor $L$ on $X$ at least one of (a), (b) holds, or exhibit a counterexample.
category_tag: Linear systems on blow-ups of P^2
status_search_result: The question is closely related to the well-known SHGH (Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz) conjecture and its variants concerning speciality of linear systems on blow-ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. The SHGH conjecture remains open in general (proved only in low cases such as $r \leq 9$ points in general position), and the proposed dichotomy here, allowing arbitrary configurations of distinct points, has not been established. Recent work continues to formulate equivalent conjectures, suggesting the problem is still open.

original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b(X) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X satisfies C^2 >= -b(X)?
self_contained_problem:
Bounded Negativity Conjecture. Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Does there exist a constant $b(X) \geq 0$ such that for every reduced, irreducible curve $C \subset X$ one has
$$C^2 \geq -b(X)?$$
Equivalently, is the set $\{C^2 : C \subset X \text{ reduced and irreducible}\}$ bounded below?
status_search_result: The Bounded Negativity Conjecture remains open in characteristic zero. It is known to hold in some special cases (e.g., surfaces with anticanonical assumptions or specific geometric structure) but is unresolved even for blow-ups of the projective plane at 10 or more general points. Recent works study weighted, weak, and linear weighted variants, all still active and partially open as of 2024–2025.

original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero and fix an integer g >= 0. Does there exist a positive constant b(X,g) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X whose normalization has genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(X,g)?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and fix a non-negative integer g. Does there exist a positive constant b(X, g), depending only on X and g, such that every reduced irreducible curve C ⊂ X whose normalization has genus equal to g satisfies the self-intersection bound

  C² ≥ -b(X, g)?

Equivalently, prove or disprove that on any such surface X, the self-intersection numbers of reduced irreducible curves of fixed geometric genus g are bounded below by a constant depending only on X and g.
status_search_result: The Weak Bounded Negativity Conjecture, asserting a lower bound on C² in terms of X and the geometric genus g, was proved by Feng Hao (arXiv:1708.09463, 2017) for complex smooth projective surfaces. Subsequent work (e.g., variations and weighted versions) has built on this result. The full Bounded Negativity Conjecture (without genus dependence) remains open.

self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and fix an integer $g \geq 0$. Does there exist a positive constant $b_s(X,g)$, depending only on $X$ and $g$, such that every smooth irreducible curve $C \subset X$ of geometric genus $g$ satisfies
$$C^2 \geq -b_s(X,g),$$
where $C^2$ denotes the self-intersection number of $C$ on $X$?

original_question: Let f : Y -> B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. For a fixed geometric genus g, does there exist a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C subset Y of geometric genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(Y,g), where the self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Y$ be a smooth complex projective threefold, let $B$ be a smooth complex projective curve, and let $f : Y \to B$ be a surjective morphism whose general fiber is a smooth projective surface. By a vertical curve in $Y$ we mean an irreducible curve $C \subset Y$ such that $f(C)$ is a single point $b \in B$; let $Y_b = f^{-1}(b)$ denote the (scheme-theoretic) fiber containing $C$, and define the self-intersection $C^2$ to be computed inside $Y_b$ (using the intersection theory on the surface $Y_b$ when $b$ is a regular value, or the appropriate intersection product on the fiber in general).

Fix a non-negative integer $g$. Question: does there exist a constant $b(Y,g)$, depending only on $Y$ and $g$, such that
$$ C^2 \;\geq\; -\,b(Y,g) $$
for every vertical curve $C \subset Y$ whose geometric genus equals $g$?

original_question: Is the global Seshadri constant epsilon(X) = inf{epsilon(L) : L in Pic(X) is ample} positive for every smooth projective surface X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective surface and let $\mathrm{Pic}(X)$ denote its Picard group. For an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$ and a point $x \in X$, define the local Seshadri constant of $L$ at $x$ by
$$\varepsilon(L,x) \;=\; \inf_{C \ni x} \frac{L \cdot C}{\mathrm{mult}_x(C)},$$
where the infimum runs over all irreducible curves $C \subset X$ passing through $x$, and $\mathrm{mult}_x(C)$ is the multiplicity of $C$ at $x$. Define the Seshadri constant of $L$ by
$$\varepsilon(L) \;=\; \inf_{x \in X} \varepsilon(L,x),$$
and the global Seshadri constant of $X$ by
$$\varepsilon(X) \;=\; \inf\{\varepsilon(L) : L \in \mathrm{Pic}(X) \text{ is ample}\}.$$
Determine whether $\varepsilon(X) > 0$ for every smooth projective surface $X$.
status_search_result: The positivity of the global Seshadri constant for arbitrary smooth projective surfaces is widely cited as an open problem, closely tied to the Bounded Negativity Conjecture: an affirmative answer to BNC would imply $\varepsilon(X) > 0$. Recent work (e.g., on weighted bounded negativity for rational surfaces, 2024) treats it as still unresolved in general.

original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b_w(X) such that for every irreducible curve C subset X and every big and nef line bundle H with H.C > 0, one has C^2 >= -b_w(X) (H.C)^2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over a field of characteristic zero. The Weighted Bounded Negativity question asks: does there exist a positive constant $b_w(X)$, depending only on $X$, such that
$$C^2 \;\geq\; -\,b_w(X)\,(H\cdot C)^2$$
holds for every irreducible curve $C \subset X$ and every big and nef line bundle $H$ on $X$ satisfying $H\cdot C > 0$?

Here $C^2$ denotes the self-intersection number of $C$, and $H\cdot C$ denotes the intersection number of $H$ with $C$. A line bundle $H$ on $X$ is called nef if $H\cdot D \geq 0$ for every irreducible curve $D \subset X$, and big if its top self-intersection $H^2 > 0$ together with nefness (equivalently, if $h^0(X, H^{\otimes m})$ grows like $m^2$).

Prove or disprove the existence of such a constant $b_w(X)$ for every smooth projective surface $X$ in characteristic zero.
status_search_result: The Weighted Bounded Negativity Conjecture remains open in general. Subsequent works (e.g., a 2017 paper "Towards the weighted Bounded Negativity Conjecture for blow-ups of algebraic surfaces" published in Manuscripta Mathematica, a 2024 paper on weighted bounded negativity for rational surfaces, and a 2025 paper "Linear weighted bounded negativity") establish only partial results in special cases (blow-ups, rational surfaces, linear variants). It is known to imply positivity of global Seshadri constants and remains an active research topic.

original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b'(X) such that every reduced curve C subset X, without assuming irreducibility, satisfies C^2 >= -b'(X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface over a field of characteristic zero. A reduced curve $C \subset X$ is an effective divisor whose underlying scheme has no embedded components and whose local rings at generic points are reduced; $C$ is not assumed to be irreducible. Let $C^2$ denote the self-intersection number of $C$ as a divisor on $X$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $b'(X) > 0$, depending only on $X$, such that
$$C^2 \geq -b'(X)$$
for every reduced curve $C \subset X$.
status_search_result: The Bounded Negativity Conjecture (including its formulation for reduced—not necessarily irreducible—curves, which is equivalent to the standard form) remains open in characteristic zero. It is known to fail in positive characteristic. Active recent research (2024–2025) addresses weighted and linear weighted versions and special cases such as blow-ups of specific surfaces, but the general conjecture is unresolved.

original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map rho : |D| -> |D|_E, is it true that (1) every base point in the image of rho comes from a base curve in |D|, and (2) if |D| has no fixed component, then rho has maximal rank?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the blow-up of the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $r$ points in very general position, let $D$ be an effective divisor on $X$, and let $E \subset X$ be a $(-1)$-curve (a smooth rational curve with $E^2 = -1$). Consider the complete linear system $|D|$ and the restriction map
$$\rho : |D| \longrightarrow |D|_E := |\mathcal{O}_E(D\cdot E)|,$$
obtained by restricting sections of $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ to $E \cong \mathbb{P}^1$. Decide whether both of the following statements hold:

(1) Every base point of the image linear system $\rho(|D|) \subset |D|_E$ on $E$ arises as the intersection of $E$ with a fixed component (base curve) of $|D|$.

(2) If $|D|$ has no fixed component, then the linear map $\rho$ has maximal rank, i.e. it is either injective or surjective.

original_question: Let L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) denote the linear system of plane curves of degree d passing through n points with multiplicities at least m_1, ..., m_n, and let L(d; m_1, ..., m_r, m_{r+1}, ..., m_n) denote the analogous system where the first r points are constrained to be collinear but are otherwise general. If d >= m_1 + ... + m_r, is it true that L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) is nonempty if and only if the corresponding system with the first r points collinear is nonempty?
self_contained_problem:
Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero (e.g., the complex numbers). For a positive integer $d$ and nonnegative integers $m_1,\dots,m_n$, and for points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ in the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$, let $L(d; m_1,\dots,m_n; p_1,\dots,p_n)$ denote the linear system of plane curves of degree $d$ that have multiplicity at least $m_i$ at $p_i$ for every $i=1,\dots,n$. 

Write $L(d; m_1,\dots,m_n)$ for this linear system when the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ are chosen general in $\mathbb{P}^2$, and write $L(d; \overline{m_1,\dots,m_r}, m_{r+1},\dots,m_n)$ for this linear system when the points $p_1,\dots,p_r$ are constrained to lie on a common line but are otherwise general (and $p_{r+1},\dots,p_n$ are general).

$$L(d; m_1,\dots,m_n) \neq \emptyset \iff L(d; \overline{m_1,\dots,m_r}, m_{r+1},\dots,m_n) \neq \emptyset\,?$$

original_question: Give a mathematical proof for the page-5 observation that, in the three displayed examples of bimagic squares of orders 256x256, 625x625, and 2401x2401, the first listed subgroup orders 64x64, 125x125, and 343x343 respectively have a common bimagic sum S2 within each case. Here S2 denotes the common sum of the squares of the entries in each row, each column, and the two principal diagonals of a bimagic square.
self_contained_problem:
A magic square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array of distinct positive integers such that the sum of the entries in each row, each column, and each of the two principal diagonals equals a common value $S_1$. A bimagic square is a magic square that, in addition, satisfies the property that the sum of the squares of the entries in each row, each column, and each of the two principal diagonals equals a common value $S_2$ (called the bimagic sum of squares).

For an integer $k\ge 2$, consider a bimagic square $B$ of order $k^4\times k^4$ whose entries are the integers $1,2,\dots,k^8$. Suppose $B$ admits a hierarchical block decomposition: $B$ is partitioned into a $k\times k$ array of blocks of size $k^3\times k^3$; each $k^3\times k^3$ block is in turn partitioned into a $k\times k$ array of blocks of size $k^2\times k^2$; and each $k^2\times k^2$ block is partitioned into a $k\times k$ array of blocks of size $k\times k$. Assume further that, at every level of this decomposition, the corresponding blocks (of sizes $k^3\times k^3$, $k^2\times k^2$, and $k\times k$) are themselves bimagic squares (with respect to their own entries), so that one obtains, in particular, a distinguished "first" sub-block at each scale.

Prove that for $k=4,5,7$ (i.e. for the bimagic squares of orders $256\times 256$, $625\times 625$, and $2401\times 2401$ constructed in this hierarchical fashion), the bimagic sum of squares $S_2$ of the first sub-block of order $k^3\times k^3$, of the first sub-sub-block of order $k^2\times k^2$, and of the first sub-sub-sub-block of order $k\times k$ are all equal to one another within each case. More generally, identify and prove the precise condition under which the bimagic sums $S_2$ of the nested first sub-blocks at scales $k^3,k^2,k$ coincide.

context_brief: Nevanlinna four shared values without multiplicity agreement
original_question: Suppose f and g are distinct non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values a1, a2, a3, and a4 in the sense that, for each shared value a_nu, the set of points where f = a_nu is the same as the set of points where g = a_nu, but no agreement of multiplicities is assumed. Must Nevanlinna's Four-Value conclusion still hold: after relabelling the shared values, must the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equal -1, so that a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?
self_contained_problem:
Let f and g be two distinct non-constant meromorphic functions on the complex plane. We say that f and g share a value a in C ∪ {∞} ignoring multiplicity (IM) if {z ∈ C : f(z) = a} = {z ∈ C : g(z) = a} as sets, with no condition that the multiplicities of the a-points of f and g agree.

Suppose that f and g share four pairwise distinct values a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 ∈ C ∪ {∞} in this IM sense. Must it follow that, after a suitable relabelling of the values, the cross-ratio satisfies (a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4) = -1, that a_1 and a_2 are Picard exceptional values of both f and g, and that g is a Möbius transformation of f fixing a_3 and a_4 and interchanging a_1 and a_2?

In other words, does Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem (originally proved under the assumption that the four values are shared counting multiplicities) remain valid when multiplicities are not taken into account?
status_search_result: The problem (attributed to L. Rubel) is solved in the negative: G. Gundersen constructed an explicit counterexample of two distinct non-constant meromorphic functions sharing four values IM but not satisfying the conclusion of Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem, showing that the "counting multiplicities" hypothesis cannot simply be removed.

original_question: Suppose f and g are non-constant meromorphic functions that share four distinct values, and one of those four shared values is shared by counting multiplicities, meaning that for that one value the two functions take the value at exactly the same points with the same multiplicities, while for the other three values only the sets of shared points are assumed to coincide. Must the conclusion of Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem still follow, namely that after relabelling the values the cross-ratio (a1, a2, a3, a4) equals -1, a1 and a2 are Picard values of both functions, and g is a Mobius transformation of f that fixes a3 and a4 and permutes a1 and a2?
self_contained_problem:
Let f and g be non-constant meromorphic functions on the complex plane. Recall that f and g share a value a ∈ ℂ ∪ {∞} ignoring multiplicities (IM) if {z : f(z) = a} = {z : g(z) = a} as sets, and they share a counting multiplicities (CM) if in addition the multiplicities of f and g at every such point coincide. Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem asserts that if f and g share four distinct values a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ all CM, then (after relabelling) the cross-ratio (a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄) equals −1, the values a₁ and a₂ are Picard exceptional values of both f and g, and g is a Möbius transformation of f that fixes a₃ and a₄ and interchanges a₁ and a₂.

Question: Suppose f and g are non-constant meromorphic functions sharing four distinct values a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ ∈ ℂ ∪ {∞}, where exactly one of the four values is shared CM and the remaining three are shared only IM. Must the same conclusion as in Nevanlinna's Four-Value Theorem necessarily hold? That is, after relabelling, must (a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄) = −1, must a₁ and a₂ be Picard values of both f and g, and must g be a Möbius transformation of f fixing a₃, a₄ and permuting a₁, a₂?
status_search_result: The (1+3) four-value problem (sharing one value CM and three values IM) is a long-standing open problem in Nevanlinna value-distribution theory. Survey discussions and problem lists in complex analysis from 2011 onward continue to list it as an unresolved gap between the classical 4CM theorem and the known failure under 4IM (Gundersen's counterexample). Partial results exist (e.g., 2CM+2IM ⇒ 4CM, and 3IM+1CM has been settled in certain restricted settings such as difference operators or angular domains), but the general (1+3) statement does not appear to have been proven or disproven.

context_brief: Open rescaling reduction for the (1+3) problem
original_question: Can the general problem of two meromorphic functions sharing four values be reduced by Zalcman rescaling to a limit pair with bounded spherical derivative without losing the essential shared-value data? More precisely, after passing to rescaled limits, can one rule out the possibilities that a value shared by the original pair becomes only a Picard value of the limit pair, that a value not originally shared by counting multiplicities becomes shared by counting multiplicities in the limit, or that the two limit functions collapse to the identical function, so that a proof of the (1+3) conjecture in the bounded-spherical-derivative setting would imply the general case?
self_contained_problem:
Let f and g be two non-constant meromorphic functions on the complex plane, and let a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 be four distinct values in the Riemann sphere. Say that f and g share the value a "ignoring multiplicities" (IM) if f^{-1}(a) = g^{-1}(a) as sets, and "counting multiplicities" (CM) if in addition the multiplicities of the corresponding a-points coincide. Recall Zalcman's lemma: if a family F of meromorphic functions on a domain D is not normal at a point z_0, then there exist sequences f_n in F, z_n → z_0, and ρ_n → 0+ such that f_n(z_n + ρ_n ζ) converges locally uniformly on C to a non-constant meromorphic function F̂ on C with bounded spherical derivative.

The (1+3) conjecture asserts: if f and g are non-constant meromorphic functions on C sharing four distinct values a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 such that one of them is shared CM and the other three are shared IM, then f ≡ g (equivalently the cross ratio (a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4) takes a prescribed value, e.g. equals −1, in degenerate situations).

Question. Suppose the (1+3) conjecture is established for all pairs (f,g) of non-constant meromorphic functions on C with bounded spherical derivative. By applying a Zalcman rescaling to a hypothetical counterexample (f,g) of arbitrary order of growth, one obtains rescaled limits (f̂, ĝ) on C with bounded spherical derivative. Can one in general rule out each of the following three "loss of information" phenomena under such rescaling:

(a) some value a_ν shared (IM or CM) by f and g becomes only a Picard exceptional value of f̂ and ĝ (i.e., is omitted by both limit functions, so the sharing condition becomes vacuous);

(b) some value a_ν that is shared by f and g only IM, not CM, is shared CM by f̂ and ĝ (so the (1+3) hypothesis on the limit pair is strictly stronger than on the original);

(c) f̂ ≡ ĝ?

Equivalently: can the general (1+3) conjecture for meromorphic functions of arbitrary order be reduced via Zalcman rescaling to the bounded-spherical-derivative case without loss of the essential shared-value data?

status_search_result: Web searches on the (1+3)/(3+1) shared-values conjecture and Zalcman-rescaling reduction did not return any source that confirms either a successful reduction of the general case to the bounded-spherical-derivative case or a definitive obstruction. The (3+1) conjecture itself appears to remain open in the literature on Nevanlinna theory and shared values, and no clear resolution of the rescaling obstacles (a)–(c) was found.
