original_question: For each positive integer n, determine C(n), the number of Costas arrays of order n. In particular, do Costas arrays exist for every order n > 0, and if not, which positive integers n satisfy C(n) = 0?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array containing exactly n marks, with one mark in each row and one mark in each column (i.e., the array is the permutation matrix of some permutation of {1,2,…,n}), such that all (n choose 2) displacement vectors between distinct pairs of marks are distinct. Equivalently, a permutation f:{1,…,n}→{1,…,n} is Costas if for every integers i,j,k with 1≤i<i+k≤n and 1≤j<j+k≤n, we have f(i+k)−f(i) ≠ f(j+k)−f(j) whenever i ≠ j. Let C(n) denote the number of Costas arrays of order n.

Determine C(n) as a function of the positive integer n. In particular, decide whether C(n) > 0 for every positive integer n, and if not, determine the set X = { n ∈ ℤ_{>0} : C(n) = 0 }.
status_search_result: The problem remains open. No general formula for C(n) is known; values are known only by exhaustive enumeration up to roughly n ≈ 29. The smallest orders for which the existence of a Costas array is unresolved are n = 32 and n = 33 (also n = 43), and no n with C(n) = 0 has been proved. Known algebraic constructions (Welch and Lempel–Golomb, based on primes and prime powers) do not cover these cases.

original_question: Let E(n) be the decision problem that asks whether at least one Costas array of order n exists, equivalently whether C(n) > 0. What is the computational complexity of E(n) as a function of n, and in particular is this decision problem NP-complete?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and each column (equivalently, the graph of a permutation π:{1,...,n}→{1,...,n}) such that all the n(n−1)/2 displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are pairwise distinct; equivalently, for every triple of integers i, j, k with 1 ≤ i, i+k ≤ n and k ≠ 0, the difference π(i+k) − π(i) determines (i,k) uniquely among all such pairs sharing the same k. Let C(n) denote the number of Costas arrays of order n, and define the decision problem E(n): given a positive integer n (encoded in binary), decide whether C(n) > 0, i.e., whether at least one Costas array of order n exists.

Determine the computational complexity of E as a function of n. In particular, decide whether E is NP-complete. (Note that verification of the Costas property of a candidate permutation can be performed in time polynomial in n, so E lies in NP under the standard encoding.)
status_search_result: The complexity of the Costas array existence decision problem remains open. While verifying the Costas property of a candidate permutation is polynomial-time (placing E in NP), no proof of NP-completeness or of a polynomial-time algorithm is known. The existence and counting problems for Costas arrays are still listed among the major unresolved questions in the area.

original_question: Define the degrees of freedom of a Costas array of order n as the smallest k <= n for which there exist indices i1 < i2 < ... < ik in [n] such that, for any prescribed values f1, ..., fk in [n], there is at most one Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] with f(ij)=fj for all j. Determine this quantity for Costas arrays of order n, and if possible improve the definition so it captures the phenomenon more effectively.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas permutation of order $n$ is a bijection $f:[n]\to[n]$ (where $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$) such that all the vectors $(j-i,\,f(j)-f(i))$ with $1\le i<j\le n$ are distinct; equivalently, the displacement vectors between distinct points of the graph $\{(i,f(i)):i\in[n]\}$ are pairwise distinct. Define the degrees of freedom of Costas arrays of order $n$, denoted $d(n)$, to be the smallest integer $k\le n$ for which there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k$ in $[n]$ with the following property: for every choice of values $f_1,\dots,f_k\in[n]$, there is at most one Costas permutation $f:[n]\to[n]$ satisfying $f(i_j)=f_j$ for all $j=1,\dots,k$.

(a) Determine $d(n)$, or provide nontrivial upper and lower bounds on $d(n)$ as a function of $n$.

(b) If possible, propose an improved definition of "degrees of freedom" that more effectively captures the rigidity phenomenon (namely, that a Costas permutation is determined by very few of its values).

original_question: Find an upper or asymptotic bound for C(n), the number of Costas arrays of order n, that matches the empirically observed decay of C(n)/n! more closely than the currently known O((n-1)!) bound. Also prove or disprove whether the ratio C(n)/n! decreases monotonically to 0.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix (equivalently, a permutation f:{1,…,n}→{1,…,n}) with the property that all displacement vectors between distinct pairs of its 1-entries are distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer h with |h|<n, the function i↦f(i+h)−f(i) is injective on its domain {1,…,n−h} (or {1−h,…,n}). Let C(n) denote the number of Costas arrays of order n.

It is known that C(n) ≤ (n−1)·(n−1)! (so C(n)/n! = O(1)), but empirical data for small n suggest that the ratio C(n)/n! decreases much faster than this trivial bound and appears to tend to 0 monotonically.

(a) Prove an upper bound on C(n) (equivalently on C(n)/n!) that more closely reflects the empirically observed rate of decay of C(n)/n!, improving substantially on C(n) = O((n−1)·(n−1)!).

(b) Prove or disprove that the sequence C(n)/n! is monotonically decreasing in n and converges to 0 monotonically.

Part (b), the question of whether C(n)/n! is monotonically decreasing to 0, remains open as of available sources; the monotonicity has only been verified empirically for small n.

original_question: Determine whether sporadic Costas arrays form only a finite set, or whether they instead arise from one or more still-unknown generally applicable construction techniques.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix (equivalently a permutation f of {1,2,…,n}) with the property that the (n choose 2) displacement vectors between distinct pairs of marked cells are all distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer h, the differences f(i+h) − f(i) (taken over all valid i) are pairwise distinct. The principal known infinite families of Costas arrays come from the Welch and Lempel–Golomb algebraic constructions (and their variants/transformations) based on primitive roots in finite fields; arrays produced by these constructions are called "generated." Arrays obtained from generated arrays by adding or removing a corner row/column or by other simple combinatorial operations are called "emergent." A Costas array is called "sporadic" if it is neither generated nor emergent. Computer enumeration has produced sporadic Costas arrays at various small orders.

Settle the following questions about the family of all sporadic Costas arrays (taken across all orders n):
(a) Is the set of sporadic Costas arrays finite? Equivalently, is there an order N₀ such that for every n ≥ N₀ no sporadic Costas array of order n exists?
(b) If the set is infinite, exhibit one or more generally applicable construction techniques (analogous in spirit to, but distinct from, the Welch and Lempel–Golomb constructions) that produce infinitely many sporadic Costas arrays.
status_search_result: The status of sporadic Costas arrays remains open. The largest known sporadic Costas array has order 27, and existence of Costas arrays of all orders is unknown. No general construction technique producing sporadic arrays has been found, and no proof of finiteness exists; the problem continues to be listed among the central open problems on Costas arrays.

original_question: A pair of Costas permutations g1,g2:[n]->[n] is called twin when both are obtained from a Costas permutation f:[n]->[n] by shifting the graph of f one step and adding opposite corner points exactly as specified in Definition 7.   $g_j(i) = f(i-1)+1$ for $i=2,\dots,n+1$ and $j\in\{1,2\}$,
  $g_1(1)=1$,  $g_2(n+2)=1$,
  $g_2(1)=n+2$,  $g_1(n+2)=n+2$.

original_question: Do there exist finite-order sporadic Costas arrays of order n > 1 whose dots also form a configuration of non-attacking queens on an n x n chessboard? If such arrays exist, how many are there, and can they be constructed systematically?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array with exactly one dot in each row and each column (equivalently, the graph of a permutation of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$) such that all $\binom{n}{2}$ displacement vectors between pairs of dots are distinct. Two known infinite families produce Costas arrays for infinitely many orders: the Welch construction and the Lempel–Golomb (and its variants) construction; these together with arrays obtained from them by elementary symmetries (transpose, reflections, rotations) and certain operations (such as adding/removing a corner dot) are called generated or emergent. A Costas array that is neither generated nor emergent is called sporadic.

A configuration of non-attacking queens on an $n\times n$ chessboard is a placement of $n$ queens, one in each row and one in each column, such that no two queens lie on a common diagonal (neither slope $+1$ nor slope $-1$); equivalently, the corresponding permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfies $\pi(i)-\pi(j)\neq \pm(i-j)$ for all $i\neq j$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n>1$ and a sporadic Costas array of order $n$ whose dots simultaneously form a non-attacking queens configuration on the $n\times n$ board? If such arrays exist, determine how many there are (for each such $n$, or in total) and give a systematic construction.
status_search_result: The problem of whether sporadic Costas arrays that simultaneously yield non-attacking queens configurations exist is reported as an open problem. It is known that any Costas array (of order n>1) which also forms a non-attacking queens configuration must be sporadic, since the standard generated/emergent constructions (Welch, Lempel–Golomb and their variants) always place dots that share a diagonal. There is a conjecture that no such arrays exist, but no proof or counterexample has been published, and existing literature continues to list the question as unresolved.

original_question: Let g:[l]->[l] be a Costas permutation. Does there always exist a larger Costas permutation f having an arithmetic-progression substructure S1,S2 as in Definition 8 such that g(i) = (f(a1 + b1 i) - a2)/b2 on those progressions, so that g is a sub-permutation of f? A Costas permutation of order n is a bijection f:[n]→[n] (where [n]={1,2,…,n}) such that the displacement vectors {(j−i, f(j)−f(i)) : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n} are all distinct; equivalently, no two of the vectors connecting distinct points of the graph {(i,f(i))} are equal.

Define a sub-permutation as follows. Let f:[n]→[n] be a permutation. Suppose there exist nonnegative integers a₁, a₂ and positive integers b₁, b₂, l such that the arithmetic progressions
  S_j = {a_j + b_j · i : i ∈ [l]},  j = 1, 2,
are both contained in [n] and satisfy f(S₁) = S₂. Then the map g:[l]→[l] defined by
  g(i) = (f(a₁ + b₁ i) − a₂) / b₂
is called a sub-permutation of f.

original_question: Describe the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. In particular, for a specific Costas permutation or a specific family, determine the full cycle decomposition, whether cycles of a given length can occur, the longest cycle length, and the smallest positive integer k for which the k-fold iterate equals the identity permutation.
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and write [n] = {1,2,…,n}. A Costas permutation of order n is a bijection f : [n] → [n] whose graph {(i, f(i)) : i ∈ [n]} ⊂ [n]×[n] forms a Costas array, i.e. all of the n(n−1)/2 displacement vectors (i₂ − i₁, f(i₂) − f(i₁)) with 1 ≤ i₁ < i₂ ≤ n are distinct.

For a permutation f : [n] → [n], let I denote the identity (I(i) = i), set f^{(0)} = I, and define f^{(k+1)}(i) = f(f^{(k)}(i)) for all k ∈ ℕ and i ∈ [n]. The cycle of i ∈ [n] under f is the finite set {f^{(k)}(i) : k ∈ ℕ} ⊆ [n], and the disjoint union of the distinct cycles gives the cycle decomposition of f.

Investigate the cycle structure of Costas permutations under iteration. Specifically:
1. For a given Costas permutation (or for explicit infinite families of Costas permutations, such as those arising from the Welch and Lempel constructions over finite fields), determine the full cycle decomposition.
2. For a given length ℓ, decide whether a cycle of length ℓ can occur in a specified Costas permutation or family.
3. Determine the longest cycle length appearing in a specified Costas permutation or family.
4. Determine the smallest positive integer k such that f^{(k)} = I, i.e. the order of f in the symmetric group S_n, for a specified Costas permutation f or family.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems concerning Costas arrays. No subsequent work providing a general description of the cycle structure of Costas permutations (including for the standard Welch/Lempel families) has been located; surveys and follow-up papers continue to treat structural and enumerative questions about Costas arrays as open.

original_question: Consider the algebraic Costas-array construction families listed in Section 3.2, including the Welch- and Golomb-type families W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5*. Is it true that for every order n > 5 these construction methods are pairwise disjoint, so that no Costas array of that order can be produced by two different methods?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix such that the n(n−1) displacement vectors between pairs of its 1-entries are all distinct. Several classical algebraic constructions produce Costas arrays from primitive roots of finite fields:

- Welch construction W1: For an odd prime p and a primitive root α of GF(p), define the (p−1)×(p−1) Costas array with a 1 in row i, column j iff α^{i} ≡ j (mod p) (and its transpose / shifted variants).
- Exponential Welch W2(p,α): variant of W1 obtained by exponential indexing.
- Welch W3: a further variant from W1 by removing/altering rows-columns.
- Golomb construction G2(p,m,α,β): For primitive elements α, β of GF(p^m), the (p^m−2)×(p^m−2) array with a 1 at (i,j) iff α^{i} + β^{j} = 1.
- Golomb G3, G4, G4*, G4**, G5*: standard sub-/super-cases of G2 obtained, e.g., when α=β (Lempel construction), when α + β = 1, or by adjoining additional rows/columns when characteristic conditions hold.

Each method M produces a finite set S_M(n) of Costas arrays of order n (counting equivalence under reflection/transposition as separate arrays, in accordance with the standard listing of these algebraic families).

Question: Is it true that for every integer n > 5, the families
W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, G5*
are pairwise disjoint, i.e., for any two distinct families M ≠ M′ from this list, S_M(n) ∩ S_{M′}(n) = ∅?
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in the Costas array literature. Partial results are known: the exponential and logarithmic Welch families are disjoint for p > 5, and enumeration studies (e.g., for order 28) confirm overlaps only in small cases. No general proof of pairwise disjointness for all n > 5 across all listed Welch/Golomb families has been published.

original_question: For each unpredictably emergent Costas-array construction method obtained by adding one or more dots to an existing Costas array, determine whether there is a finite threshold N beyond which that method never produces a Costas array of order n > N.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ permutation matrix (equivalently, a permutation $f:\{1,\dots,n\}\to\{1,\dots,n\}$) with the distinct-difference property: for every integers $i,j,k$ with $1\le i,j,j+k\le n$ and $k\ne 0$, one has $f(j+k)-f(j)\ne f(i+k)-f(i)$ whenever $i\ne j$. Equivalently, all the displacement vectors between distinct dots of the array are pairwise distinct.

A "dot-addition" construction is a deterministic procedure that takes as input a Costas array $A$ of some order $m$ and outputs a candidate array of order $m+r$ (for some fixed $r\ge 1$ depending on the procedure) by inserting $r$ new dots in prescribed positions (typically corner positions) and possibly shifting some existing dots; the output is accepted only if it satisfies the Costas property. Several such heuristic procedures are known (e.g. variants denoted $G_0$, $G_1$, $W_0$, the Welch–Rickard and Golomb–Rickard extensions), each producing only sporadic Costas arrays whose appearance cannot be predicted from the input.

Question: For each such dot-addition construction method $M$, decide whether there exists a finite threshold $N_M\in\mathbb{N}$ with the property that $M$ produces no Costas array of order $n>N_M$. In other words, determine whether each unpredictably emergent dot-addition construction has finite scope, and if so, identify the largest order at which it succeeds.
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Numerical searches have extended verification of the unpredictably emergent dot-addition methods to order 300, with the last $G_1$ and $W_0$ Costas arrays found at orders 52 and 53 respectively, and Rickard-type constructions producing nothing new past order 100. While the empirical evidence strongly suggests these methods "die out," no proof of a finite threshold $N_M$ has been established for any of the methods.

original_question: Do any two sufficiently large Costas arrays necessarily share a common distance vector? More specifically, is it enough for the smaller array to have size at least 3 x 3 and the larger to have size at least 5 x 5 for a common distance vector to be forced?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array with exactly one dot in each row and each column (so it represents a permutation of $\{1,\dots,n\}$) such that all $\binom{n}{2}$ vectors joining pairs of distinct dots are distinct. Equivalently, if $f:\{1,\dots,n\}\to\{1,\dots,n\}$ is the corresponding permutation, then for every triple of integers $(i,j,k)$ with $1\le i,i+k\le n$, $1\le j,j+k\le n$, and $k\ne 0$, the equality $f(i+k)-f(i)=f(j+k)-f(j)$ implies $i=j$.

A distance vector of a Costas array $f$ of order $n$ is any vector of the form $(k,\,f(i+k)-f(i))\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ for some $1\le i<i+k\le n$. Two Costas arrays (possibly of different orders) are said to share a common distance vector if their respective sets of distance vectors have nonempty intersection.

Question: Is it true that any two sufficiently large Costas arrays must share a common distance vector? More precisely, is it the case that whenever $A$ is a Costas array of order at least $3$ and $B$ is a Costas array of order at least $5$, the arrays $A$ and $B$ necessarily have a common distance vector?
status_search_result: The question is listed among open problems on Costas arrays. Work on common distance vectors between Costas arrays (e.g., Drakakis et al.) provides partial results for algebraically constructed families but does not resolve the general conjecture that any two sufficiently large Costas arrays (smallest order ≥ 3, largest order ≥ 5) share a common distance vector. No source confirming a full resolution was found.

original_question: A Costas array is called singly periodic when cyclic shifts of the columns of a W1 array again produce W1 arrays, and more generally the paper asks whether any singly periodic Costas array must belong to the W1 family. Is every singly periodic Costas array necessarily a W1 array?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n permutation matrix (equivalently, a permutation f:{1,…,n}→{1,…,n}) such that all the displacement vectors (i−j, f(i)−f(j)), with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, are distinct.

The Welch construction W₁ produces a Costas permutation of order p−1, where p is an odd prime, as follows: fix a primitive root g modulo p; then define f(i) ≡ g^{i−1} (mod p) for i = 1,…,p−1, viewed as a permutation of {1,…,p−1}. A Costas array obtained by this construction (possibly after the standard rotations/reflections that are conventionally included in the W₁ family, i.e. the orbit under the natural symmetries) is called a W₁ array.

A Costas array of order n is said to be singly periodic if every cyclic shift of its columns (regarded as a permutation array on the n×n torus, shifting columns cyclically and translating the row indices accordingly) again yields a Costas array. It is known that every W₁ array is singly periodic.

Question: Is every singly periodic Costas array necessarily a W₁ array? That is, does the singly periodic property characterize the W₁ family?
status_search_result: The problem appears still open. No singly periodic Costas array other than a W₁ array is known, and partial results have been obtained (e.g., Costas arrays of odd order cannot be singly periodic; the related notion of "circular Costas" arrays has been introduced and shown to require n+1 prime, with every W₁ array being circular Costas). However, the converse characterization—that every singly periodic Costas array is a W₁ array—remains unresolved in the available literature, including more recent surveys and dissertations on Costas arrays.

original_question: Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top, every cyclic shift of the rows still yields a non-square array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be an exponential Welch W1 array?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order $n$ is an $n \times n$ array with exactly one dot in each row and each column such that all $\binom{n}{2}$ vectors joining pairs of dots are distinct (equivalently, the permutation $f:\{1,\dots,n\}\to\{1,\dots,n\}$ marking the dot positions satisfies $f(i+k)-f(i) = f(j+k)-f(j)$ with $1\le i<j$ and $1\le k\le n-j$ implies no repetition).

The exponential Welch construction $W_1$ produces, for an odd prime $p$ and a primitive root $\alpha$ modulo $p$, a $(p-1)\times(p-1)$ Costas array given by the permutation $f(i) \equiv \alpha^{i} \pmod{p}$ for $i=1,\dots,p-1$.

Let $A$ be a Costas array of order $n$. Form the $(n+1)\times n$ array $A^{+}$ obtained from $A$ by prepending a blank row at the top (so the new top row contains no dot). For each integer $k$ with $0 \le k \le n$, let $A^{+}_k$ denote the $(n+1)\times n$ array obtained from $A^{+}$ by cyclically shifting its rows by $k$ positions. (The arrays $A^{+}_k$ are non-square.) Say that $A$ has the cyclic-blank-row Costas property if every $A^{+}_k$ (for $k=0,1,\dots,n$) has the Costas property, i.e., all vectors between pairs of dots are distinct.

Question: Must every Costas array $A$ with the cyclic-blank-row Costas property be an exponential Welch $W_1$ array?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in the literature on Costas arrays. Recent surveys and a 2023 dissertation on Costas arrays do not record a resolution of this inverse characterization of the exponential Welch $W_1$ family via the cyclic-blank-row property.

original_question: Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top and one blank column at the side, every cyclic shift of rows and columns still yields a square non-permutation array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be a G2 array?
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ permutation matrix (exactly one dot in each row and each column, all other entries blank) such that all $\binom{n}{2}$ vectors joining pairs of dots are distinct (no two are equal as vectors). 

Given an $n\times n$ Costas array $A$, form the $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ array $A^{+}$ by prepending one blank row at the top and one blank column on the left (so $A^{+}$ contains the $n$ dots of $A$ in its lower-right $n\times n$ block, and is no longer a permutation array since one row and one column are empty). For integers $i,j$, let $\sigma_{i,j}(A^{+})$ denote the $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ array obtained from $A^{+}$ by cyclically shifting all rows down by $i$ and all columns right by $j$ (indices mod $n+1$). Say that $A^{+}$ has the Costas property if all vectors joining distinct pairs of dots in it are distinct.

A Costas array $A$ is called a $G_2$ array if it arises from a known algebraic construction (the Golomb $G_2$ construction) producing arrays for which every cyclic shift $\sigma_{i,j}(A^{+})$ retains the Costas property.

Question: Suppose $A$ is an $n\times n$ Costas array such that for every $(i,j) \in \{0,1,\dots,n\}^{2}$, the cyclically shifted array $\sigma_{i,j}(A^{+})$ still satisfies the Costas property (although it is square and not a permutation array). Must $A$ necessarily be a $G_2$ array?
status_search_result: The problem appears in standard lists of open problems on Costas arrays and has not been resolved. Subsequent surveys and theses on structural properties of Costas arrays (e.g., Jedwab–Wodlinger 2014 and Ardalani 2023) treat the inverse characterization of G2 arrays via the cyclic-shift Costas property as still open.

original_question: For G2 Costas arrays constructed over finite fields of characteristic 2, determine the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo, namely the numbers of dots whose coordinates are respectively even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and each column (equivalently, a permutation f:{1,…,n}→{1,…,n}, where the dot in column i is placed in row f(i)) such that all the (n choose 2) displacement vectors between pairs of dots are distinct; equivalently, for every nonzero integer h and every i with 1≤i, i+h≤n, the difference f(i+h)−f(i) is unique as a function of i.

Golomb (G2) construction in a finite field of order q. Let q be a prime power and let F_q be the finite field with q elements. Choose two primitive elements α, β of F_q (i.e. generators of the multiplicative group F_q^*, which has order q−1). Define a permutation f of {1,2,…,q−2} by the rule
   f(i) = j   if and only if   α^i + β^j = 1.
The resulting (q−2)×(q−2) permutation array is the G2 (Golomb) Costas array associated with the pair (α,β); it is known to be a Costas array.

Parity populations. For any permutation array A on {1,…,n}, classify its n dots according to the parities of their (column,row) coordinates and define
   ee(A) = #{ i : i even and f(i) even },
   eo(A) = #{ i : i even and f(i) odd },
   oe(A) = #{ i : i odd  and f(i) even },
   oo(A) = #{ i : i odd  and f(i) odd }.
These four nonnegative integers are called the parity populations of A and satisfy ee+eo+oe+oo = n.

It is known that, for G2 arrays constructed in fields F_q of odd characteristic, the four parity populations depend only on q (not on the chosen primitives α, β) and are explicitly:
 • if q ≡ 1 (mod 4): ee = (q−5)/4 and eo = oe = oo = (q−1)/4;
 • if q ≡ 3 (mod 4): oo = (q+1)/4 and ee = eo = oe = (q−3)/4.

Problem. Determine the parity populations ee, eo, oe, oo of the G2 Costas arrays constructed in finite fields F_q of characteristic 2 (i.e. q = 2^m, m ≥ 2), as functions of q and possibly of the chosen pair of primitive elements (α, β).
status_search_result: Web sources on Costas arrays indicate that, while parity populations of G2 arrays in odd characteristic are explicitly known and depend only on q, the analogous determination for G2 arrays in characteristic 2 has been highlighted as one of the open challenges in the field, with no closed-form determination reported.

original_question: Fix a prime power q and an integer r relatively prime to q-1. Determine how many elements x of the finite field F(q) satisfy the equation x^r + x = 1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $\mathbb{F}_q$ denote the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $r$ be a positive integer such that $\gcd(r,\,q-1)=1$. Determine, as an explicit function of $q$ and $r$, the number of elements $x\in\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfying
$$x^{r}+x=1.$$
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a closed-form count for the number of solutions of $x^r+x=1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$ under the assumption $\gcd(r,q-1)=1$. The condition $\gcd(r,q-1)=1$ implies $x\mapsto x^r$ is a bijection on $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, but determining the exact number of solutions in general is not addressed by any authoritative source found, so the status of an explicit general formula remains unclear.

original_question: Let p be a prime, let C be a nonzero element of the finite field F(p), and let alpha be a primitive root modulo p. Determine the number of integers i in [p-1] that satisfy the congruence i ≡ C alpha^i (mod p).
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ denote the finite field with $p$ elements, and let $\mathbb{F}_p^* = \mathbb{F}_p \setminus \{0\}$. Fix an element $C \in \mathbb{F}_p^*$ and a primitive root $\alpha$ modulo $p$ (i.e., an element of $\mathbb{F}_p^*$ whose multiplicative order equals $p-1$). Let $[p-1] = \{1, 2, \ldots, p-1\}$. Determine, as a function of $p$, $C$, and $\alpha$, the number of integers $i \in [p-1]$ that satisfy the congruence
$$i \equiv C\,\alpha^{i} \pmod{p}.$$
Equivalently, give a closed-form expression (or an asymptotic/exact count) for $\#\{i \in [p-1] : i \equiv C\alpha^i \pmod p\}$.
status_search_result: The problem of counting fixed points of maps of the form $i \mapsto C\alpha^i \pmod p$ (sometimes called self-power or exponential fixed-point congruences) is a known difficult problem in elementary number theory; partial results and heuristics exist (e.g., for the case $C=1$, work by Holden, Moree, and others gives heuristic averages and bounds), but no general closed-form count is known. The general problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For a fixed order n, determine the forbidden positions of Costas arrays: grid locations in the n x n board that are not occupied by a dot in any Costas array of that order. Solve this without relying on exhaustive enumeration.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n × n arrangement of dots and blanks such that each row and each column contains exactly one dot (i.e., the dots form the graph of a permutation of {1,...,n}), with the additional property that all the displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are distinct. Equivalently, a permutation f : {1,...,n} → {1,...,n} is Costas if for every choice of integers i, j, k with 1 ≤ i, i+k, j, j+k ≤ n and i ≠ j, one has f(i+k) − f(i) ≠ f(j+k) − f(j).

A grid cell (i, j) ∈ {1,...,n} × {1,...,n} is called a forbidden position for order n if no Costas array of order n has a dot at (i, j); equivalently, no Costas permutation f of {1,...,n} satisfies f(i) = j.

Problem: For a given order n, determine, by means other than exhaustive enumeration of Costas arrays, the complete set of forbidden positions in the n × n grid. Provide a method (e.g., structural, algebraic, or combinatorial criteria) which, taking n as input, identifies which cells (i, j) are forbidden without needing to generate or check all Costas arrays of order n.
status_search_result: Determining forbidden positions of Costas arrays of a given order without exhaustive enumeration is listed as an open problem in the Costas arrays literature. Forbidden positions are currently known only through enumeration results (e.g., none for n = 1, 2, 4–24; specific positions for n = 3 and for orders 25–27 obtained computationally). No non-enumerative characterization appears to have been published.

original_question: For the families of Welch W1 and Golomb G2 Costas arrays, determine the maximal pairwise cross-correlation quantities defined by the paper as Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(q), classify primes and prime powers into the cases stated in Problem 21, prove the listed formulas and exceptional cases, derive formulas for the local minima, and show where the maxima are attained in the non-safe cases described there.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A Costas array of order n is a permutation f: {1,...,n} → {1,...,n} whose difference vectors (i₂−i₁, f(i₂)−f(i₁)) for distinct i₁,i₂ are all distinct. Two standard algebraic constructions are:

• Welch construction W₁: For a prime p and a primitive root g of ℤ/pℤ, define f_g: {1,...,p−1}→{1,...,p−1} by f_g(i) = g^{i−1} mod p. The set of all such f_g, as g ranges over primitive roots, is the W₁ family of order p−1.

• Golomb construction G₂: For a prime power q and a pair (α,β) of primitive elements of 𝔽_q, define f_{α,β}: {1,...,q−2}→{1,...,q−2} by the relation α^{f_{α,β}(i)} + β^i = 1 (whenever a solution exists). The set of all such f_{α,β}, as (α,β) ranges over ordered pairs of primitive elements, is the G₂ family of order q−2.

Cross-correlation. For two permutations f₁,f₂ of the same domain {1,...,N} and shifts (u,v) ∈ ℤ², define
   Ψ_{f₁,f₂}(u,v) = #{ i : f₁(i+u) = f₂(i) + v },
where the equality is taken with the convention that i and i+u must lie in {1,...,N}.

Define
   Ψ_{W₁}(p) = max_{(u,v)} max_{f₁ ≠ f₂ ∈ W₁, produced by different primitive roots} Ψ_{f₁,f₂}(u,v),
   Ψ_{G₂}(q) = max_{(u,v)} max_{f'₁ ≠ f'₂ ∈ G₂} Ψ_{f'₁,f'₂}(u,v).

A prime p is called safe if (p−1)/2 is prime; a prime power q is called safe if (q−1)/2 is prime.

Problem. Establish the following.

(a) Prove that primes p split, with respect to Ψ_{W₁}(p) and Ψ_{G₂}(p), into three classes (safe primes; non-safe primes; and a finite list of exceptional primes), and determine the corresponding closed-form value of Ψ_{W₁}(p) (respectively Ψ_{G₂}(p)) in each class, including the listed exceptional cases.

(b) Prove the analogous classification of prime powers q into three classes with respect to Ψ_{G₂}(q), giving the closed-form value of Ψ_{G₂}(q) in each class.

(c) For p a non-safe prime, prove that
   Ψ_{W₁}(p) = max_{f₁ ≠ f₂} Ψ_{f₁,f₂}(0,0).
For q a non-safe prime power with q ≠ 16, 19 such that q−1 is not prime, prove that
   Ψ_{G₂}(q) = max_{f'₁ ≠ f'₂} Ψ_{f'₁,f'₂}(0,0).

(d) Derive closed-form formulas for the local minima of p ↦ Ψ_{W₁}(p) and q ↦ Ψ_{G₂}(q), and identify the shifts (u,v) at which the maxima are attained in the non-safe cases.
status_search_result: Subsequent work (Moon Ho Lee–Müller-type results, 2020) settles some of the conjectured cross-correlation formulas: for primes p ≥ 5 the maximal cross-correlation of the W₁ family is shown to be (p−1)/t (with t the smallest prime divisor of (p−1)/2) when p is not safe, and bounded by 1+√p in the safe case. Analogous bounds are proven for a subfamily of Golomb permutations of size φ(q−1), but the full G₂ family of size φ(q−1)² is observed to have larger maximal cross-correlation than that bound for some q, so the Golomb conjecture in its full strength, the prime-power classification, and the precise formulas/local-minima/attainment claims are not completely resolved.

original_question: For G2 arrays generated over finite fields of characteristic 2, find an intrinsic necessary structural property analogous to the anti-reflective symmetry known for W1 arrays and analogous to the congruence f(mu + i) - f(mu - i) ≡ i [f(mu + 1) - f(mu - 1)] mod (q - 1), where mu = (q - 1)/2, which is known for G2 arrays over odd characteristic.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A Costas array of order n is a permutation matrix corresponding to a bijection f:{1,...,n}→{1,...,n} with the property that all vectors (i−j, f(i)−f(j)) with i≠j are distinct.

Two standard finite-field constructions are recalled below.

(W1, Welch construction.) Let p be an odd prime and let α be a primitive root of the field F_p. The W1 permutation f:{1,...,p−1}→{1,...,p−1} is defined by f(i) ≡ α^i (mod p), with values taken in {1,...,p−1}. It is known that every W1 permutation satisfies the "anti-reflective symmetry"
   f(i) + f(i + (p−1)/2) = p,   for all i ∈ {1,...,(p−1)/2}.

(G2, Golomb construction.) Let q = p^k be a prime power and let α, β be (not necessarily distinct) primitive elements of the field F_q. The G2 permutation f:{1,...,q−2}→{1,...,q−2} is defined by the relation
   α^i + β^{f(i)} = 1,   for i ∈ {1,...,q−2}.
When q is odd, set μ = (q−1)/2. Then every G2 permutation f is known to satisfy the congruence
   f(μ + i) − f(μ − i) ≡ i · [f(μ + 1) − f(μ − 1)]   (mod q − 1),
for every admissible i.

Problem. For q = 2^k a power of 2, identify and prove an intrinsic necessary structural property of the G2 permutations f:{1,...,q−2}→{1,...,q−2} obtained from the Golomb construction over F_q, analogous in nature to the anti-reflective symmetry of W1 permutations and to the displayed congruence valid for G2 permutations in odd characteristic.
status_search_result: Searches for structural/necessary properties of G2 (Golomb) Costas arrays in characteristic 2 returned related work by Jedwab–Wodlinger and Drakakis on structural properties of Costas arrays and on parity populations of Golomb arrays in characteristic 2, but no source clearly states a necessary structural property analogous to anti-reflective symmetry specifically for G2 arrays in characteristic 2. The status could not be conclusively verified.

original_question: Let C(m,n,N) denote the number of m x n Golomb rectangles containing N dots, where a Golomb rectangle is a rectangular dot pattern whose autocorrelation takes exactly the three values {N, 1, 0}. Determine C(m,n,N). In particular, for fixed m and n find the largest N with C(m,n,N) > 0, and for fixed N find the smallest m and n with C(m,n,N) > 0.
self_contained_problem:
A rectangular dot pattern is an m×n array whose entries lie in {0,1}, where 1 represents a dot and 0 a blank. For such a pattern A=(a_{i,j}), define its (two-dimensional) autocorrelation at shift (s,t)∈ℤ² by
   R_A(s,t) = Σ_{i,j} a_{i,j} · a_{i+s, j+t},
where a_{i,j} = 0 outside the m×n grid. Let N = R_A(0,0) denote the number of dots in A. The pattern A is called an m×n Golomb rectangle with N dots if N>2 and the set of values
   { R_A(s,t) : (s,t) ∈ ℤ² }
equals exactly {0, 1, N}.

Let C(m,n,N) denote the number of m×n Golomb rectangles containing exactly N dots (counted as distinct binary arrays).

(a) Determine C(m,n,N) as an explicit function of m, n, and N.
(b) For fixed positive integers m and n, determine the largest N for which C(m,n,N) > 0.
(c) For a given integer N>2, determine the smallest values of m and n for which C(m,n,N) > 0.
status_search_result: No general formula for C(m,n,N) appears in the literature. Existing work (e.g., Robinson's 1985 study of Golomb rectangles and subsequent bounds and computational results) provides partial enumerations, bounds, and tables for small cases, but the general enumeration problem and the extremal questions for arbitrary m, n, N remain unresolved.

original_question: Enumerate all honeycomb arrays, where a honeycomb array is equivalently a Costas array with exactly one dot on every bottom-left to top-right diagonal.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array of cells, with exactly one dot placed in each row and each column (i.e., the placement of dots corresponds to a permutation of {1,...,n}), such that all of the n(n−1)/2 displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are pairwise distinct.

Index the cells of such an array by (column, row) with both coordinates ranging over {1,...,n}. The "bottom-left to top-right diagonals" are the sets of cells {(i,j) : i − j = c} for each integer c with −(n−1) ≤ c ≤ n−1.

A honeycomb array is a Costas array with the additional property that every bottom-left to top-right diagonal contains exactly one dot. (Equivalently, the map i ↦ π(i) − i is a bijection, where π is the underlying permutation; arrays satisfying these properties can be visualized as point configurations on a hexagonal lattice.)

Problem: Determine, with proof, the complete list of all honeycomb arrays (up to the natural symmetries). In particular, decide whether the currently known finite collection of honeycomb arrays — those of sizes corresponding to n ∈ {1, 3, 7, 9, 15, 21, 27, 45} — exhausts all honeycomb arrays.
status_search_result: The complete enumeration of honeycomb arrays remains open. It is known that only finitely many exist (no honeycomb array with 2r+1 ≥ 1289 dots exists), and 12 honeycomb arrays (up to symmetry) are currently known, occurring at sizes n ∈ {1, 3, 7, 9, 15, 21, 27, 45}; this list is conjectured but not proven to be complete.

original_question: Find exact formulas for the two fundamental extremal functions for Golomb rulers: the minimum possible length n of a Golomb ruler with a given number m of points, and the maximum possible number of points m in a Golomb ruler of a given length n.
self_contained_problem:
A Golomb ruler with $m$ marks is a set $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_m\}$ of nonnegative integers with $a_1=0$ such that all pairwise differences $a_j-a_i$ (for $i<j$) are distinct; its length is $a_m$. Define the two extremal functions:

(a) $L(m) = \min\{a_m : A 	ext{ is a Golomb ruler with } m 	ext{ marks}\}$, the minimum possible length of a Golomb ruler with exactly $m$ marks;

(b) $M(n) = \max\{m : 	ext{there exists a Golomb ruler with } m 	ext{ marks of length } n\}$, the maximum possible number of marks in a Golomb ruler of length $n$.

Provide closed-form exact formulas, as functions of $m$ and $n$ respectively, for $L(m)$ and $M(n)$.
status_search_result: Determining exact formulas for the optimal length of Golomb rulers with a given number of marks (and the dual problem) is a long-standing open problem. Optimal rulers have been verified computationally only up to a small number of marks (e.g., via the OGR distributed projects, currently around 28–29 marks), and only asymptotic bounds (e.g., $L(m)=m^2(1+o(1))$, with conjectures of Erdős–Turán type) are known. No closed-form expression is known.

original_question: Give an efficient conversion in both directions between Costas arrays (or more generally Golomb rectangles) and Golomb rulers. In particular, for a given Costas array or family of Costas arrays, determine the minimum number of blank rows that must be added at the bottom so that stacking the columns in order produces a Golomb ruler.
self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and each column such that all the vector displacements between distinct pairs of dots are distinct. More generally, a Golomb rectangle is an m×n array with at most one dot in each row and column whose pairwise displacement vectors between dots are all distinct. A Golomb ruler is a finite set of nonnegative integers all of whose pairwise differences are distinct.

Given an m×n Golomb rectangle (in particular a Costas array, where m=n), label the rows from top to bottom as 0,1,...,m-1 and the columns from left to right as 0,1,...,n-1. The "column-stacking" map sends a dot in row i and column j to the integer i + jm; this produces a set S of n integers in {0,1,...,mn-1}. Adding extra blank rows at the bottom of the array corresponds to replacing m by some m' ≥ m and using the map (i,j) ↦ i + jm'.

Problem:
(a) Provide an efficient algorithm that, given a Costas array (or more generally a Golomb rectangle), produces a Golomb ruler, and conversely an efficient algorithm that, given a Golomb ruler, produces (when possible) a Costas array or Golomb rectangle that maps to it under the column-stacking construction.
(b) For a given Costas array (or family of Costas arrays) of order n, determine the minimum number k ≥ 0 of blank rows that must be appended at the bottom (so that m' = n + k) such that the column-stacking construction with parameter m' yields a Golomb ruler. Equivalently, characterize the set of valid m' ≥ n for which the resulting set S ⊂ {0,1,...,m'n-1} is a Golomb ruler, and determine the smallest such m'.
status_search_result: Several works (e.g., Drakakis et al.) provide explicit conditions and computational methods for determining how many blank rows must be appended to a Costas array so that column stacking yields a Golomb ruler, with known upper bounds and simulation results for small orders. However, no closed-form characterization of the minimum number of blank rows for a general Costas array (or family) is known, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T1, ..., Tℓ) be a measure preserving system and define the multiple correlation sequence by C(n1, ..., nℓ) := ∫ f0 · T1^n1 f1 · ... · Tℓ^nℓ fℓ dµ. Is every such sequence an approximate integral combination of generalized ℓ-step nilsequences in ℓ variables?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\ge 1$ be an integer and let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ be a measure preserving system, meaning that $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T_1,\dots,T_\ell:X\to X$ are (not necessarily commuting) invertible measurable maps each preserving $\mu$. For bounded measurable functions $f_0,f_1,\dots,f_\ell:X\to\mathbb{C}$, define the multiple correlation sequence $C:\mathbb{Z}^\ell\to\mathbb{C}$ by
$$C(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)\;:=\;\int_X f_0\cdot (T_1^{n_1}f_1)\cdots(T_\ell^{n_\ell}f_\ell)\,d\mu,\qquad (n_1,\dots,n_\ell)\in\mathbb{Z}^\ell.$$

Recall that an $\ell$-step nilsequence in $\ell$ variables is a sequence of the form $(F(g_1^{n_1}\cdots g_\ell^{n_\ell}\Gamma))_{(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)\in\mathbb{Z}^\ell}$, where $G/\Gamma$ is an $\ell$-step nilmanifold, $g_1,\dots,g_\ell\in G$, and $F:G/\Gamma\to\mathbb{C}$ is continuous; a generalized $\ell$-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of such nilsequences. Say that a sequence $C:\mathbb{Z}^\ell\to\mathbb{C}$ is an approximate integral combination of generalized $\ell$-step nilsequences if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist generalized $\ell$-step nilsequences $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_k:\mathbb{Z}^\ell\to\mathbb{C}$ and integers $a_1,\dots,a_k\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
$$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N^\ell}\sum_{(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)\in[1,N]^\ell}\Bigl|C(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)-\sum_{j=1}^k a_j\,\psi_j(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)\Bigr|\;<\;\varepsilon.$$

Determine whether every multiple correlation sequence $C$ arising as above is an approximate integral combination of generalized $\ell$-step nilsequences in $\ell$ variables.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. For a single transformation ($\ell$ commuting iterates of one $T$) with polynomial iterates, Frantzikinakis (Inventiones, 2015/16, arXiv:1407.0631) decomposed the correlation as a nilsequence plus an error small in uniform density. More recent work proved that every multi-correlation sequence (for commuting transformations) is the sum of a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence, resolving a related conjecture of Frantzikinakis; see "Nilsequences, null-sequences, and multiple correlation sequences" and the 2025 preprint "Structured extensions and multi-correlation sequences" (arXiv:2504.07038). The full original question in the form stated (approximate integral combination of generalized $\ell$-step nilsequences in $\ell$ variables, for $\ell$ general commuting/non-commuting transformations) is therefore partially solved.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g, h ∈ L∞(µ). If C(n) := ∫ f · T^n g · T^(2n) h dµ, is the sequence (C(n)) an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving system on a standard probability space, and let $f,g,h \in L^\infty(\mu)$. Define the 3-term correlation sequence
$$C(n) := \int_X f \cdot (T^n g) \cdot (T^{2n} h)\, d\mu, \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Recall that a basic 2-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $(F(a^n \cdot e\Gamma))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $G$ is a 2-step nilpotent Lie group, $\Gamma \le G$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup, $a\in G$, and $F: G/\Gamma \to \mathbb{C}$ is continuous; a generalized 2-step nilsequence is defined analogously but allowing $F$ to be Riemann integrable on $G/\Gamma$. An "(approximate) integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences" means a sequence that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, can be approximated in uniform density (i.e.\ in the seminorm $\limsup_{N-M\to\infty}\frac{1}{N-M}\sum_{n=M}^{N-1}|\cdot|$) up to error $\varepsilon$ by a finite integral combination $\int \psi_t(n)\,d\nu(t)$ of generalized 2-step nilsequences $\psi_t$ indexed measurably by a parameter $t$ on a probability space $(Y,\nu)$.

Question: Is the sequence $(C(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ always such an approximate integral combination of generalized 2-step nilsequences?
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Frantzikinakis (Inventiones, 2016, arXiv:1407.0631) showed that 3-term correlation sequences decompose as a uniform-density approximation by a nilsequence plus a null-sequence under certain hypotheses, and further work by Le, and by Frantzikinakis–Host on structured extensions (arXiv:2504.07038) extends and refines such decompositions. However, the general conjecture that every multi-correlation sequence is an (approximate) integral combination of generalized nilsequences remains open in full generality.

original_question: Let CT,S be the set of sequences of the form (∫ f · T^n g · S^n h dµ) as (X, X, µ, T, S) ranges over systems and f, g, h range over L∞(µ), and let CT be the subclass where T and S are powers of a single transformation. Must CT,S and CT actually coincide?
self_contained_problem:
Let a measure-preserving system be a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a standard probability space and $T,S\colon X\to X$ are commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. For such a system and for $f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)$, consider the bounded sequence
$$a_n = \int_X f\cdot (T^n g)\cdot (S^n h)\,d\mu, \qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
Define
$$\mathcal{C}_{T,S} = \big\{(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} : (X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)\text{ a system}, \ f,g,h\in L^\infty(\mu)\big\},$$
and let $\mathcal{C}_T\subseteq \mathcal{C}_{T,S}$ be the subclass obtained by additionally requiring that $T$ and $S$ are powers of a single measure-preserving transformation $R$ (i.e., $T=R^a$, $S=R^b$ for some integers $a,b$, on the same system).

Determine whether $\mathcal{C}_{T,S} = \mathcal{C}_T$. That is, is every triple correlation sequence arising from two commuting measure-preserving transformations equal to a triple correlation sequence arising from powers of a single measure-preserving transformation?
category_tag: multiple correlation sequences in ergodic theory
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Frantzikinakis (Inventiones 2016, "Multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences") and a 2020 paper by Frantzikinakis–Host show that such commuting correlation sequences decompose as a nilsequence plus an error term small in uniform density, paralleling the single-transformation case. However, the exact equality $\mathcal{C}_{T,S}=\mathcal{C}_T$ does not appear to have been established; the decomposition results are weaker than the asked equality and we found no source claiming the problem is resolved. We therefore record it as still open.

original_question: For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), are the following conditions equivalent: (i) the sequences are good for ℓ-convergence of commuting transformations; (ii) they are good for ℓ-convergence on ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\ge 1$ be an integer. A bounded sequence $\psi\colon\mathbb{Z}^\ell\to\mathbb{C}$ is called a **basic generalized $\ell$-step nilsequence in $\ell$ variables** if there exist an $\ell$-step nilmanifold $X=G/\Gamma$ (i.e., $G$ is an $\ell$-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma\le G$ a cocompact discrete subgroup), commuting elements $b_1,\dots,b_\ell\in G$, a point $x\in X$, and a continuous function $F\colon X\to\mathbb{C}$ such that
$$\psi(n_1,\dots,n_\ell)=F(b_1^{n_1}\cdots b_\ell^{n_\ell}\,x)\qquad(n_1,\dots,n_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}).$$

Let $a_1,\dots,a_\ell\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be integer sequences. Consider the following three properties.

(i) **Good for $\ell$-convergence of commuting transformations.** For every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every $\ell$-tuple of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ of $(X,\mu)$, and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^{a_1(n)}f_1\cdot T_2^{a_2(n)}f_2\cdots T_\ell^{a_\ell(n)}f_\ell$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

(ii) **Good for $\ell$-convergence on $\ell$-step nilsystems.** The same convergence holds whenever $(X,\mu)$ is an $\ell$-step nilsystem and $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ are commuting nilrotations.

(iii) **Nilsequence convergence.** For every basic generalized $\ell$-step nilsequence $\psi$ in $\ell$ variables, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N \psi(a_1(n),\dots,a_\ell(n))$$
converge as $N\to\infty$.

**Question.** Are conditions (i), (ii), and (iii) equivalent?
status_search_result: The equivalence is posed as an open problem in Frantzikinakis's lists of open problems on multiple ergodic averages, and subsequent works (e.g., on multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences, and joint ergodicity for commuting transformations) treat related decomposition and convergence questions but do not establish the full equivalence. No source found claiming a complete proof of (i)⇔(ii)⇔(iii) in general.

original_question: Let a(n) be an integer sequence such that the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a(n)) converge for every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ. Must it follow that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and f, g ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a(n)} f · S^{a(n)} g converge weakly in L2(µ)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. By a measure-preserving system we mean a quadruple $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a standard probability space and $T\colon X\to X$ is an invertible measurable map preserving $\mu$. Given two commuting measure-preserving transformations $T,S$ of $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$, we call $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ a system.

A 2-step nilmanifold is a quotient $X=G/\Gamma$ where $G$ is a 2-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma$ a discrete cocompact subgroup. A basic 2-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $n\mapsto F(b^{n}\Gamma)$ where $b\in G$, $F\in C(G/\Gamma)$. A basic generalized 2-step nilsequence is a uniform limit of basic 2-step nilsequences (equivalently, sequences of the form $F(b^n\Gamma)$ where $F$ is bounded Borel and Riemann-integrable on $G/\Gamma$ with respect to Haar measure, suitably formulated).

Question. Suppose $a\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is a sequence of integers with the following property: for every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence $\psi\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\psi(a(n))$$
converge as $N\to\infty$. Does it follow that for every system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T,S)$ (with $T,S$ commuting measure-preserving transformations) and every pair of functions $f,g\in L^{\infty}(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T^{a(n)} f)\cdot (S^{a(n)} g)$$
converge weakly in $L^{2}(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$?
status_search_result: The question is a special case of a general convergence-criterion problem on multiple ergodic averages along non-conventional sequences. Subsequent work on multi-correlation sequences and nilsequence decompositions (e.g., Frantzikinakis's "Multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences" and later works on joint ergodicity and structured extensions) has clarified parts of the broader program, but no source found explicitly resolves this two-transformation special case under the stated 2-step nilsequence convergence hypothesis. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: Suppose an integer sequence a(n) has the property that for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b on X, the sequence (b^{a(n)} Γ) is equidistributed in X, and for every r ∈ N the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Must a(n) then be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$. A connected $\ell$-step nilmanifold is a quotient $X=G/\Gamma$, where $G$ is a connected $\ell$-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma$ is a discrete cocompact subgroup; $X$ is endowed with its (unique) $G$-invariant Haar probability measure $\mu_X$. For $b\in G$, the (left) nilrotation $T_b\colon X\to X$ is $T_b(g\Gamma)=bg\Gamma$. The nilrotation $b$ is called irrational if the induced rotation on the maximal factor torus of $X$ is ergodic (equivalently, has dense orbit). A sequence $(x_n)\subset X$ is equidistributed in $X$ if $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N f(x_n)\to \int_X f\,d\mu_X$ for every $f\in C(X)$.

A set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density if $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|A\cap\{1,\dots,N\}|}{N}>0$.

A sequence $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of integers is called good for $\ell$-recurrence of commuting transformations if, for every probability space $(Y,\mathcal{B},\nu)$, every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$ of $(Y,\mathcal{B},\nu)$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\nu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with
$$\nu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-a(n)}A\cap T_2^{-a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_\ell^{-a(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

Prove or disprove: Suppose $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of integers such that
(i) for every connected $\ell$-step nilmanifold $X=G/\Gamma$ and every irrational nilrotation $b\in G$, the sequence $(b^{a(n)}\Gamma)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is equidistributed in $X$, and
(ii) for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the set $\{n\in\mathbb{N}:r\mid a(n)\}$ has positive upper density.
Then $(a(n))$ is good for $\ell$-recurrence of commuting transformations.
status_search_result: Web search surfaces a problem list by Frantzikinakis on multiple ergodic averages and related work on commuting transformations and equidistribution on nilmanifolds, but no result was found that explicitly resolves the stated implication for general ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations under these two hypotheses. Closely related advances exist (joint ergodicity for commuting transformations, structure of multiple correlation sequences via nilsequences), but a definitive solution to this specific question could not be confirmed.

original_question: If an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, must each power sequence a(n)^k be good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, ..., ℓ?
self_contained_problem:
Let (a(n))_{n∈N} be a sequence of integers. Recall:

• (a(n)) is good for 1-recurrence if for every invertible measure-preserving system (X, B, μ, T) and every A ∈ B with μ(A) > 0, there exists n ∈ N such that
  μ(A ∩ T^{-a(n)} A) > 0.

• For an integer ℓ ≥ 1, the sequence (a(n)) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers if for every invertible measure-preserving system (X, B, μ, T) and every A ∈ B with μ(A) > 0, there exists n ∈ N such that
  μ(A ∩ T^{-a(n)} A ∩ T^{-a(n)^2} A ∩ ⋯ ∩ T^{-a(n)^ℓ} A) > 0.

Question: Suppose (a(n)) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers. Must the sequence (a(n)^k)_{n∈N} be good for 1-recurrence for every k = 1, 2, …, ℓ?
status_search_result: The question appears in a survey of open problems on multiple ergodic averages by Frantzikinakis and is connected to the program of Frantzikinakis–Lesigne–Wierdl on powers of sequences and recurrence. Related results show that for k = 2 the analogous statement about sets of recurrence can fail, while the case k ≥ 3 and the precise formulation here for sequences remain open. No subsequent resolution was found.

original_question: If an integer sequence is good for 2-convergence of powers of a single transformation, must it also be good for 2-convergence of commuting transformations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of integers. Say that $(a_n)$ is good for $2$-convergence of powers if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ and every pair of functions $f_1,f_2\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$ rac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{a_n}x)\, f_2(T^{2a_n}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N	o\infty$.

Say that $(a_n)$ is good for $2$-convergence of commuting transformations if for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every pair of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,T_2$ of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, and every $f_1,f_2\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$ rac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T_1^{a_n}x)\, f_2(T_2^{a_n}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N	o\infty$.

Prove or disprove: every integer sequence $(a_n)$ that is good for $2$-convergence of powers is also good for $2$-convergence of commuting transformations.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific implication. Related results show that sequences good for one ergodic-averaging problem need not be good for another (e.g., $(a_n)$ good for the mean ergodic theorem but $(a_n^2)$ not), and norm convergence for commuting transformations along certain sequences is established only in special cases. The status of this particular problem appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

original_question: Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ denote a probability space. A measure-preserving transformation of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ is a measurable map $T:X\to X$ with $\mu(T^{-1}A)=\mu(A)$ for all $A\in\mathcal{B}$.

Call a sequence of integers $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$:

(i) good for $2$-recurrence of powers (of a single transformation) if for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every measure-preserving transformation $T:X\to X$, and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-a_n}A\cap T^{-2 a_n}A\right)>0;$$

(ii) good for $2$-recurrence of commuting transformations if for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every pair of commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1,T_2:X\to X$ (i.e.\ $T_1T_2=T_2T_1$), and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\!\left(A\cap T_1^{-a_n}A\cap T_2^{-a_n}A\right)>0.$$

Question: Does there exist an integer sequence $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ that is good for $2$-recurrence of powers but is not good for $2$-recurrence of commuting transformations?
status_search_result: The problem appears in Frantzikinakis's list of open problems on multiple ergodic averages. Subsequent literature on recurrence sequences for commuting transformations (e.g., works by Chu, Frantzikinakis, and others, including the 2023 paper on multiple recurrence without commutativity) does not appear to report a resolution distinguishing 2-recurrence of powers from 2-recurrence of commuting transformations at the level of integer sequences. No source confirming a solution was found, so the status is treated as unverified.

original_question: Can one give an explicit fast growing sequence of positive integers, meaning a(n) grows faster than every power of n, that is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence both for powers of a single transformation and for commuting transformations?
self_contained_problem:
A sequence $(a(n))_{n\ge 1}$ of positive integers is called fast growing if 
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log a(n)}{\log n}=\infty,$$
equivalently if it can be written in the form $a(n)=n^{b(n)}$ with $b(n)\to\infty$.

A sequence $(a(n))$ of positive integers is said to be good for multiple recurrence of powers of a single transformation if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every integer $k\ge 1$, and every set $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\ge 1$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T^{-a(n)}A\cap T^{-2a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-k\,a(n)}A\bigr)>0.$$

It is said to be good for multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation if for every such system, every $k\ge 1$, and all $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{a(n)}x)\,f_2(T^{2a(n)}x)\cdots f_k(T^{k\,a(n)}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

It is said to be good for multiple recurrence of commuting transformations if for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, every $k\ge 1$, every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_k$ of $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, there exists $n\ge 1$ with
$$\mu\bigl(A\cap T_1^{-a(n)}A\cap T_2^{-a(n)}A\cap\cdots\cap T_k^{-a(n)}A\bigr)>0,$$
and good for multiple convergence of commuting transformations if for every such configuration and all $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T_1^{a(n)}x)\,f_2(T_2^{a(n)}x)\cdots f_k(T_k^{a(n)}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

Problem: Exhibit an explicit fast growing sequence $(a(n))$ of positive integers that is simultaneously good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence both for powers of a single transformation and for commuting transformations.
status_search_result: No explicit construction of such a fast growing sequence (good simultaneously for multiple recurrence and convergence under both powers of a single transformation and commuting transformations) appears in the literature. Related work establishes good universal weights for multiple recurrence with commuting transformations and quantitative growth bounds, but the explicit construction problem remains open as of 2026.

original_question: Let P be a family of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let dmin(P) be the least d such that the Host–Kra factor Zd,T is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ T^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)} fℓ. Must one always have dmin(P) ≤ |P| - 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space. For each non-negative integer $d$, let $\mathcal{Z}_{d,T}$ denote the $d$-th Host–Kra factor of the system (so $\mathcal{Z}_{0,T}$ is the trivial factor, $\mathcal{Z}_{1,T}$ is the Kronecker factor, and in general $\mathcal{Z}_{d,T}$ is the maximal factor that is an inverse limit of $d$-step nilsystems).

Given integer-valued polynomials $p_1,\dots,p_\ell\in\mathbb{Z}[n]$, the family $\mathcal{P}=\{p_1,\dots,p_\ell\}$ is called essentially distinct if the differences $p_i-p_j$ are non-constant for all $i
eq j$. We say a factor $\mathcal{Y}$ of $(X,T)$ is characteristic for the averages
$$ rac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T^{p_1(n)}f_1)\cdots (T^{p_\ell(n)}f_\ell)$$
if, for all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the difference between the above average and the corresponding average obtained by replacing each $f_i$ with its conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}(f_i\mid\mathcal{Y})$ converges to $0$ in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N	o\infty$.

It is known that for any essentially distinct family $\mathcal{P}$ there exists a finite $d$ such that $\mathcal{Z}_{d,T}$ is characteristic for the above averages, in every measure-preserving system. Define $d_{\min}(\mathcal{P})$ to be the smallest such $d$.

Problem: Prove that for every family $\mathcal{P}$ of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, $d_{\min}(\mathcal{P})\le |\mathcal{P}|-1$, where $|\mathcal{P}|$ denotes the number of polynomials in the family.

context_brief: optimal characteristic factor on Weyl systems
original_question: For the same polynomial family P, let dW_min(P) be the least d for which Zd,T is characteristic for the corresponding averages on every Weyl system, that is, every system (T^d, X_{T^d}, m_{T^d}, T) with T a unipotent affine transformation. Must one always have dW_min(P) ≤ |P| - 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P=\{p_1,\dots,p_k\}$ be a finite family of integer-valued polynomials in one variable with $|P|=k\ge 2$. A Weyl system is a measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal B,m,T)$ in which $X=T^d$ is a finite-dimensional torus, $m$ is normalized Haar measure, and $T:X\to X$ is a unipotent affine transformation, i.e., $Tx=Ax+b$ for some unipotent matrix $A\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb Z)$ and $b\in T^d$.

For each $d\ge 0$ and each measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal B,m,T)$, let $\mathcal Z_{d,T}\subseteq \mathcal B$ denote the $d$-th Host–Kra characteristic factor of $T$. The factor $\mathcal Z_{d,T}$ is said to be characteristic for the multiple polynomial averages associated with $P$ if, for all $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(m)$,
$$\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N \prod_{i=1}^k T^{p_i(n)}f_i \;-\; \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^k T^{p_i(n)}\mathbb E(f_i\mid \mathcal Z_{d,T})\longrightarrow 0$$
in $L^2(m)$ as $N\to\infty$.

Define
$$d^{W}_{\min}(P)=\min\{d\ge 0 : \mathcal Z_{d,T}\text{ is characteristic for the }P\text{-averages on every Weyl system }(X,\mathcal B,m,T)\}.$$

Question: Must one always have $d^{W}_{\min}(P)\le |P|-1$?

Hernández studies Weyl complexity for polynomial families on Weyl systems and is closely related, but the available abstract does not explicitly confirm or refute the bound $d^W_{\min}(P)\le|P|-1$. No clear resolution of this specific bound was found in the search results.

original_question: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials, meaning every nontrivial linear combination of the sequences p1,N, ..., pℓ,N is good in the sense that its exponential sums against every nonzero frequency tend to zero. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ T^[p1,N(n)] f1 · ... · T^[pℓ,N(n)] fℓ converge in L2(µ) to ∫f1 dµ · ... · ∫fℓ dµ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and for each $N\in\mathbb{N}$ let $p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N}\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be real polynomials. Call the sequence of $\ell$-tuples $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ "good" if for every nonzero $(c_1,\dots,c_\ell)\in\mathbb{R}^\ell$, the linear combination $q_N := c_1 p_{1,N}+\cdots+c_\ell p_{\ell,N}$ satisfies
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} e^{2\pi i\,\beta\, q_N(n)} \;=\; 0$$
for every $\beta\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$.

For an integer $m$, let $[m]$ denote the integer part (the floor of $m$ when $m\ge 0$, extended in the usual way for $m\in\mathbb{R}$). Given an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T$ on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$, write $T^{[r]}$ for the $[r]$-th iterate.

Question: Is it true that whenever $(p_{1,N},\dots,p_{\ell,N})_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good, then for every ergodic measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ and every $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, one has
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\,\Bigl\| \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \bigl(T^{[p_{1,N}(n)]}f_1\bigr)\cdots\bigl(T^{[p_{\ell,N}(n)]}f_\ell\bigr) \;-\; \prod_{j=1}^{\ell}\int f_j\,d\mu \Bigr\|_{L^2(\mu)} \;=\; 0\,?$$

original_question: For every system (X, X, µ, T) and bounded functions f, g, h, do the polynomial multiple ergodic averages (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) and (1/N) Σ f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a probability space and $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measurable map preserving $\mu$. For functions $f,g,h\in L^{\infty}(\mu)$, consider the multiple ergodic averages
$$A_N(f,g,h)(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^{n}x)\,g(T^{2n}x)\,h(T^{3n}x)$$
and, for $f,g\in L^{\infty}(\mu)$, the bilinear polynomial averages
$$B_N(f,g)(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^{n}x)\,g(T^{n^{2}}x).$$
Show that for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$, both $A_N(f,g,h)(x)$ and $B_N(f,g)(x)$ converge as $N\to\infty$.
status_search_result: The bilinear case $\frac{1}{N}\sum f(T^n x)g(T^{n^2}x)$ was resolved affirmatively by Krause, Mirek, and Tao (Annals of Math., 2022), who established pointwise a.e. convergence for non-conventional bilinear averages with a polynomial of degree $\ge 2$. The triple linear average $\frac{1}{N}\sum f(T^n x)g(T^{2n}x)h(T^{3n}x)$ remains open in general; pointwise a.e. convergence for such conventional triple averages is a notorious open problem, subsumed under the Furstenberg–Bergelson–Leibman conjecture.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ). If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function with values in the closed unit disk that has convergent means, do the weighted averages (1/N) Σ Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$. Let $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$.

Let $\Lambda$ denote the von Mangoldt function, defined by $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^k$ for some prime $p$ and integer $k\ge 1$, and $\Lambda(n)=0$ otherwise.

Let $\varphi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a multiplicative function (i.e. $\varphi(mn)=\varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ whenever $\gcd(m,n)=1$) with $|\varphi(n)|\le 1$ for all $n$, and assume that $\varphi$ has convergent mean, i.e. the limit
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)$$
exists in $\mathbb{C}$.

Prove or disprove: for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$, both of the weighted bilinear ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Lambda(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)\qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)$$
converge as $N\to\infty$.
status_search_result: Recent work has resolved this problem. A 2026 preprint on bilinear ergodic averages with arithmetic weights explicitly states it resolves Problem 12 of Frantzikinakis' survey, proving almost sure convergence of $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\le N} w(n) T^{an}f\cdot T^{bn}g$ for $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ where $w$ is the von Mangoldt function. A 2024 preprint also established pointwise a.e. convergence for Möbius-weighted (and more general multiplicative) bilinear averages with $P_1(n)=n$, $P_2(n)=2n$, again citing the resolution of Frantzikinakis' problem.

original_question: Let a(n) be one of the sequences p_n (the nth prime), [n^c] with c > 0, or 2^n. For every ergodic system (X, X, µ, T) and f0, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(µ), does the correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T^{a(n)} f1 · ... · T^{ℓ a(n)} fℓ dµ always admit a decomposition ψ(a(n)) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro average of |e(n)| tends to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be an ergodic invertible measure-preserving system on a probability space, and let $\ell\geq 1$ be an integer. For $f_0,f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, define the multicorrelation sequence
$$C(n)=\int_X f_0\cdot (T^{a(n)}f_1)\cdot (T^{2a(n)}f_2)\cdots (T^{\ell a(n)}f_\ell)\,d\mu,\qquad n\in\mathbb{N},$$
where $(a(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is one of the following sequences:
(i) $a(n)=p_n$, the $n$-th prime;
(ii) $a(n)=\lfloor n^c\rfloor$ for some fixed real $c>0$;
(iii) $a(n)=2^n$.

Recall that an $\ell$-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $(F(g^n\Gamma))_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$, where $G/\Gamma$ is an $\ell$-step nilmanifold, $g\in G$, and $F\colon G/\Gamma\to\mathbb{C}$ is continuous; uniform limits of such sequences are also called $\ell$-step nilsequences.

Question: For every choice of ergodic system $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$, integer $\ell\geq 1$, and functions $f_0,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, does there exist an $\ell$-step nilsequence $(\psi(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and a sequence $(e(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with
$$C(n)=\psi(a(n))+e(n)\quad\text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N},\qquad \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N |e(n)|=0\,?$$
status_search_result: The case of primes a(n)=p_n has been addressed by Koutsogiannis–Le–Moreira–Richter (2020, Discrete Analysis), who established a decomposition of multicorrelation sequences along primes (in fact for commuting transformations), settling the prime variant of this question. The cases a(n)=⌊n^c⌋ and a(n)=2^n appear to remain open in this generality, though related decomposition results along subsequences (Frantzikinakis and others) have been obtained.

original_question: If p1, ..., pℓ are integer-valued generalized polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure preserving transformations on a common system, must the averages (1/N) Σ T1^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)} fℓ always converge in L2?
self_contained_problem:
A generalized polynomial is a function p: ℤ → ℤ obtained from ordinary polynomials with real coefficients by finitely many applications of addition, multiplication, and the floor function ⌊·⌋, restricted to integer arguments. Let (X, 𝓑, μ) be a probability measure space and let T₁, …, T_ℓ : X → X be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. Let p₁, …, p_ℓ be integer-valued generalized polynomials, and let f₁, …, f_ℓ ∈ L^∞(X, μ).

Determine whether the averages
   (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^{N} (T₁^{p₁(n)} f₁)(x) · (T₂^{p₂(n)} f₂)(x) · … · (T_ℓ^{p_ℓ(n)} f_ℓ)(x)
necessarily converge in L²(X, μ) as N → ∞, for every such system, every choice of commuting transformations, every tuple of integer-valued generalized polynomials, and every tuple of bounded measurable functions.
category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along generalized polynomials
status_search_result: L²-convergence of multiple ergodic averages for commuting transformations along ordinary integer polynomials was established by Walsh (2012). Extensions to generalized-polynomial iterates (involving floor functions) are known in restricted settings (e.g., a single transformation or totally ergodic / Hardy-field-type hypotheses, via work of Bergelson–Leibman, Frantzikinakis, and others), but the general case for arbitrary commuting transformations and arbitrary integer-valued generalized polynomials does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.
