The ultrafilter number $\mathfrak{u}$ is the least cardinality of a base for a non-principal ultrafilter on $\omega$.

$$\binom{\kappa}{\omega}\to\binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
to mean: for every $2$-coloring $c:\kappa\times\omega\to 2$ there exist $X\in[\kappa]^\kappa$ and $Y\in[\omega]^\omega$ such that $c$ is constant on the rectangle $X\times Y$.

Question: Is it consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that
$$\mathfrak{s}=\mathfrak{u}\quad\text{and}\quad \binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{s}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\,?$$

original_question: Is it consistent that the dominating number d is at most the ultrafilter number u and still the positive relation \(inom{d}{\omega} 	o inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\omega$ be the set of natural numbers. For $f,g\in\omega^\omega$ write $f\le^* g$ if $f(n)\le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$. The dominating number $\mathfrak d$ is the least cardinality of a family $D\subseteq\omega^\omega$ such that for every $f\in\omega^\omega$ there exists $g\in D$ with $f\le^* g$. The ultrafilter number $\mathfrak u$ is the least cardinality of a base of a non-principal ultrafilter on $\omega$.

For cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$, the polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}\to\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:\kappa\times\lambda\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\kappa$ with $|A|=\kappa$ and $B\subseteq\lambda$ with $|B|=\lambda$ such that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
$$\mathfrak d\le\mathfrak u\quad\text{and}\quad \binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\,?$$

original_question: Assume the positive relation \(inom{d}{\omega} 	o inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds. After adding λ many random reals for some λ > d, must that same positive relation for d and ω still hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathfrak{d}$ denote the dominating number of the continuum, that is, the least cardinality of a family $D\subseteq{}^\omega\omega$ such that for every $f\in{}^\omega\omega$ there exists $g\in D$ with $f(n)\le g(n)$ for all but finitely many $n\in\omega$.

For cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$ and natural numbers $n,m,r$, the polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}\to\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{n,m}_r$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:[\kappa]^n\times[\lambda]^m\to r$ there exist $A\subseteq\kappa$ with $|A|=\kappa$ and $B\subseteq\lambda$ with $|B|=\lambda$ such that $c\restriction[A]^n\times[B]^m$ is constant.

Assume that, in the ground model $V$,
$$\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
holds. Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal with $\lambda>\mathfrak{d}$, and let $V[G]$ be the generic extension obtained by adding $\lambda$ many random reals (i.e.\ forcing with the measure algebra of $2^\lambda$). Must the same positive polarized relation
$$\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
hold in $V[G]$?

original_question: Is it consistent that the independence number i equals ℵ1 and that the strong polarized relation \(inom{i}{\omega} 	o inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\omega$ denote the first infinite ordinal and $\aleph_1$ the first uncountable cardinal. For $A,B\subseteq\omega$, write $A\subseteq^* B$ if $A\setminus B$ is finite. A family $\mathcal{I}\subseteq[\omega]^\omega$ is called independent if for any disjoint finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{I}$ the set
$$\bigcap_{A\in\mathcal{F}}A\;\cap\;\bigcap_{B\in\mathcal{G}}(\omega\setminus B)$$
is infinite. A maximal independent family is an independent family that is maximal under inclusion. The independence number $\mathfrak{i}$ is the least cardinality of an infinite maximal independent family in $[\omega]^\omega$.

For cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$ the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}\to\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:\kappa\times\lambda\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\kappa$ with $|A|=\kappa$ and $B\subseteq\lambda$ with $|B|=\lambda$ such that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
$$\mathfrak{i}=\aleph_1\qquad\text{and}\qquad\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\;?$$

original_question: Is it consistent that the independence number i is at most the ultrafilter number u and still \(inom{i}{\omega} 	o inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers and $[\omega]^\omega$ the family of infinite subsets of $\omega$. Two sets $A,B\in[\omega]^\omega$ are called almost disjoint if $A\cap B$ is finite. A family $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[\omega]^\omega$ is independent if for any disjoint finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{A}$ the set $\bigcap\mathcal{F}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal{G}$ is infinite. The independence number $\mathfrak{i}$ is the least cardinality of a maximal independent family in $[\omega]^\omega$. The ultrafilter number $\mathfrak{u}$ is the least cardinality of a base for a non-principal ultrafilter on $\omega$.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
(i) $\mathfrak{i}\leq\mathfrak{u}$, and
(ii) $\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$ holds?

original_question: Can a real-valued measurable cardinal κ satisfy the positive strong polarized relation \(inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\), meaning every 2-coloring of κ×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes κ and ω?
self_contained_problem:
A cardinal $\kappa > \aleph_0$ is called real-valued measurable if there exists a $\kappa$-additive probability measure $\mu : \mathcal{P}(\kappa) \to [0,1]$ that vanishes on singletons. For cardinals $\alpha,\beta$ and a positive integer $r$, the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\alpha}{\beta} \to \binom{\alpha}{\beta}^{1,1}_2$$
asserts that for every coloring $c : \alpha \times \beta \to \{0,1\}$ there exist $A \subseteq \alpha$ with $|A| = \alpha$ and $B \subseteq \beta$ with $|B| = \beta$ such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$.

Question: Is it consistent with the axioms of ZFC that there exists a real-valued measurable cardinal $\kappa$ for which the relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\omega} \to \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
holds?

original_question: Is it consistent that the splitting number equals the continuum and both are larger than ℵ2, while for every κ in [ℵ1, c]—including κ = s itself—the strong polarized relation \(inom{\kappa}{\omega} 	o inom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ denote the cardinality of the continuum. Recall that a family $\mathcal{S} \subseteq [\omega]^\omega$ is a splitting family if for every $A \in [\omega]^\omega$ there exists $S \in \mathcal{S}$ such that both $A \cap S$ and $A \setminus S$ are infinite; the splitting number $\mathfrak{s}$ is the least cardinality of such a family.

For an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\omega} \to \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$$
asserts that for every coloring $c : \kappa \times \omega \to \{0,1\}$ there exist $A \subseteq \kappa$ with $|A| = \kappa$ and $B \subseteq \omega$ with $|B| = \omega$ such that $c$ is constant on $A \times B$.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously
(i) $\mathfrak{s} = \mathfrak{c} > \aleph_2$, and
(ii) for every cardinal $\kappa \in [\aleph_1, \mathfrak{c}]$ (in particular for $\kappa = \mathfrak{s}$) the relation $\binom{\kappa}{\omega} \to \binom{\kappa}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$ holds?

original_question: Is it consistent that ℵω is the only breaking point in the positive spectrum of strong polarized relations? More generally, can the continuum c be arbitrarily large while the only breaking points in that spectrum are exactly the cardinals of countable cofinality?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. For cardinals α, β, the strong polarized partition relation
   (α choose β) → (α choose β)^{1,1}_2
asserts that for every coloring c : α × β → {0,1} there exist A ⊆ α and B ⊆ β with |A| = α, |B| = β such that c is constant on A × B.

Define the positive spectrum to be the class
   S = { θ : ℵ_1 ≤ θ ≤ 2^{ℵ_0} and (θ choose ω) → (θ choose ω)^{1,1}_2 holds }.
Call a cardinal θ ∈ [ℵ_1, 2^{ℵ_0}] a breaking point of the positive spectrum if (θ choose ω) → (θ choose ω)^{1,1}_2 fails (so θ ∉ S) while the relation holds for all cardinals in [ℵ_1, 2^{ℵ_0}] strictly below θ.

Questions:
(1) Is it consistent with ZFC that ℵ_ω is the only breaking point of the positive spectrum (in particular, 2^{ℵ_0} > ℵ_ω and the relation (θ choose ω) → (θ choose ω)^{1,1}_2 holds for every θ ∈ [ℵ_1, 2^{ℵ_0}] \ {ℵ_ω})?

(2) More generally, can 2^{ℵ_0} be made arbitrarily large while the set of breaking points of the positive spectrum is exactly the set of cardinals in [ℵ_1, 2^{ℵ_0}] of countable cofinality?
category_tag: Polarized partition relations and cardinal invariants

Status appears unresolved based on available sources.

original_question: Is it consistent that the positive polarized spectrum has two distinct breaking points below ℵω?
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. For infinite cardinals $\lambda \ge \mu$ and a cardinal $\theta \ge 2$, the (positive) polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\lambda}{\mu} \rightarrow \binom{\lambda}{\mu}^{1,1}_{\theta}$$
asserts that for every coloring $c : \lambda \times \mu \to \theta$ there exist $A \subseteq \lambda$ of order-type $\lambda$ and $B \subseteq \mu$ of order-type $\mu$ such that $c \restriction (A \times B)$ is constant.

For a fixed $\mu$ (e.g.\ $\mu = \aleph_0$) and a fixed number of colors $\theta$, define the positive polarized spectrum of $\mu$ to be
$$\mathrm{Sp}^{+}(\mu,\theta) \;=\; \Big\{ \lambda \ge \mu \;:\; \binom{\lambda}{\mu} \rightarrow \binom{\lambda}{\mu}^{1,1}_{\theta} \Big\}.$$

A cardinal $\kappa$ is called a breaking point of the spectrum $\mathrm{Sp}^{+}(\mu,\theta)$ if the membership status of $\lambda$ in $\mathrm{Sp}^{+}(\mu,\theta)$ changes at $\kappa$ in the following sense: $\kappa$ is a limit cardinal at which some $\lambda < \kappa$ lies in the spectrum while $\kappa \notin \mathrm{Sp}^{+}(\mu,\theta)$, or, dually, $\kappa$ is a successor of cardinals all lying outside the spectrum while $\kappa$ itself lies in it (so the spectrum is non-monotone at $\kappa$).

Question. Is it consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that the positive polarized spectrum (with $\mu = \aleph_0$ and $\theta = 2$) has at least two distinct breaking points strictly below $\aleph_\omega$?

original_question: Is it consistent that the almost-disjointness number a equals the splitting number s and yet every 2-coloring of a×ω has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes a and ω, that is, \(inom{a}{\omega} 	o inom{a}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers. Two infinite subsets $A,B\subseteq\omega$ are called almost disjoint if $A\cap B$ is finite. A family $\mathcal{A}$ of infinite subsets of $\omega$ is a maximal almost disjoint (mad) family if its members are pairwise almost disjoint and $\mathcal{A}$ is maximal with this property. The almost-disjointness number is
$$\mathfrak{a}=\min\{|\mathcal{A}|:\mathcal{A}\text{ is an infinite mad family on }\omega\}.$$
A set $S\subseteq\omega$ splits an infinite set $X\subseteq\omega$ if both $X\cap S$ and $X\setminus S$ are infinite. A family $\mathcal{S}\subseteq[\omega]^{\omega}$ is splitting if every infinite $X\subseteq\omega$ is split by some $S\in\mathcal{S}$. The splitting number is
$$\mathfrak{s}=\min\{|\mathcal{S}|:\mathcal{S}\text{ is a splitting family}\}.$$
For cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$, the polarised partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}\to\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_{2}$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:\kappa\times\lambda\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\kappa$ with $|A|=\kappa$ and $B\subseteq\lambda$ with $|B|=\lambda$ such that $c$ is constant on $A\times B$.

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that simultaneously $\mathfrak{a}=\mathfrak{s}$ and the polarised partition relation
$$\binom{\mathfrak{a}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{a}}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}$$
holds?

However, no source explicitly identifies a model in which $\mathfrak{a}=\mathfrak{s}$ together with $\binom{\mathfrak{a}}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak{a}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2$, nor a proof of inconsistency. The status of this specific question could not be verified.

original_question: Is the positive strong polarized relation for the pseudointersection number p exactly equivalent to p < s? In other words, does \(inom{p}{\omega} 	o inom{p}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) hold if and only if p is strictly less than the splitting number s?
self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers. A family $\mathcal F\subseteq[\omega]^{\omega}$ has the strong finite intersection property if every finite subfamily has infinite intersection; a pseudointersection of $\mathcal F$ is an infinite set $A\subseteq\omega$ such that $A\subseteq^* F$ (i.e. $A\setminus F$ is finite) for every $F\in\mathcal F$. The pseudointersection number $\mathfrak p$ is the least cardinality of a family with the strong finite intersection property having no pseudointersection.

A set $S\subseteq\omega$ splits an infinite set $A\subseteq\omega$ if both $A\cap S$ and $A\setminus S$ are infinite. A splitting family is a family $\mathcal S\subseteq[\omega]^{\omega}$ such that every infinite $A\subseteq\omega$ is split by some member of $\mathcal S$. The splitting number $\mathfrak s$ is the least cardinality of a splitting family.

For cardinals $\kappa$ and $\lambda$, the strong polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}\to\binom{\kappa}{\lambda}^{1,1}_{2}$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:\kappa\times\lambda\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\kappa$ with $|A|=\kappa$ and $B\subseteq\lambda$ with $|B|=\lambda$ such that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant.

Question: Is it provable in ZFC that
$$\binom{\mathfrak p}{\omega}\to\binom{\mathfrak p}{\omega}^{1,1}_{2}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathfrak p<\mathfrak s\,?$$
category_tag: polarized partition relations and cardinal characteristics
status_search_result: Garti and Shelah have characterized the polarized relation below the splitting number and produced consistency results for strong polarized relations on cardinal characteristics. A subsequent survey of open and solved problems on polarized partition relations exists, but I could not locate explicit confirmation that the equivalence between the strong polarized relation at $\mathfrak p$ and the strict inequality $\mathfrak p<\mathfrak s$ has been proved or refuted. original_question: Is it consistent that the club principle ♣_{ℵ1} holds and at the same time the strong polarized relation \(inom{\omega_1}{\omega} 	o inom{\omega_1}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?

Question: Is it consistent with ZFC that both ♣_{ℵ_1} and the strong polarized partition relation (ω_1 over ω) → (ω_1 over ω)^{1,1}_2 hold simultaneously?

original_question: For every successor cardinal κ, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold? Equivalently, is there always a 2-coloring of 2^κ × κ with no monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^κ and κ?
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. For cardinals $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta$ and a positive integer $r$, the polarized partition relation
$$\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\;\longrightarrow\;\binom{\gamma}{\delta}^{1,1}_{r}$$
asserts that for every coloring $c:\alpha\times\beta\to r$ there exist $A\subseteq\alpha$ with $|A|=\gamma$ and $B\subseteq\beta$ with $|B|=\delta$ such that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant. The negation
$$\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\;\not\longrightarrow\;\binom{\gamma}{\delta}^{1,1}_{r}$$
asserts that some coloring $c:\alpha\times\beta\to r$ admits no such monochromatic "rectangle" $A\times B$ with $|A|=\gamma$, $|B|=\delta$.

A successor cardinal is a cardinal of the form $\kappa=\lambda^{+}$ for some cardinal $\lambda$.

Problem. Determine whether, in ZFC, for every successor cardinal $\kappa$ the negative polarized partition relation
$$\binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa}\;\not\longrightarrow\;\binom{2^{\kappa}}{\kappa}^{1,1}_{2}$$
holds; equivalently, whether for every successor cardinal $\kappa$ there exists a $2$-coloring $c:2^{\kappa}\times\kappa\to\{0,1\}$ such that no pair of sets $A\subseteq 2^{\kappa}$ with $|A|=2^{\kappa}$ and $B\subseteq\kappa$ with $|B|=\kappa$ satisfies that $c\restriction(A\times B)$ is constant.

original_question: Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent that for every cardinal µ with λ < µ ≤ 2^λ, every 2-coloring of µ×λ has a monochromatic rectangle of sizes µ and λ; equivalently, does \(inom{\mu}{\lambda} 	o inom{\mu}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2\) hold throughout the whole interval (λ, 2^λ]?
self_contained_problem:
For an infinite cardinal κ and a cardinal μ ≥ κ, write $\binom{\mu}{\kappa}\to\binom{\mu}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2$ to mean: for every function $c:\mu\times\kappa\to 2$ there exist $A\subseteq\mu$ with $|A|=\mu$ and $B\subseteq\kappa$ with $|B|=\kappa$ such that $c$ is constant on $A\times B$ (a monochromatic rectangle of full size).

Let λ be a strong limit singular cardinal that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. Is it consistent with ZFC that for every cardinal μ with $\lambda<\mu\le 2^\lambda$ the partition relation
$$\binom{\mu}{\lambda}\to\binom{\mu}{\lambda}^{1,1}_2$$
holds throughout the entire interval $(\lambda,2^\lambda]$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a specific resolution of this consistency question for the entire interval (λ, 2^λ] above a strong limit singular λ that is not a limit of measurable cardinals. original_question: Let m be a fixed positive integer and let F_m = {j in 2Z \ {0} : |j| <= m}. For a vector z = (V(2), V(4), ..., V(2m)) in C^m, define P_{m,n}(z) = sum_{x in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x), where X_n^+(F_m) is the set of all admissible walks from -n to n whose steps are positive elements of F_m, a walk x has intermediate vertices j(t) that never equal +n or -n before the endpoint, and h(x) = h_1(x) prod_t V(x(t)) with h_1(x) = prod_t (n^2 - j(t)^2)^(-1). Determine the polynomials P_{m,n}(z), or at least determine their asymptotic behavior when m is fixed and n tends to infinity.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $m$ and let
$$F_m = \{\,j \in 2\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\} : |j| \le m\,\}.$$
For a positive integer $n$, an $F_m$-admissible walk from $-n$ to $n$ is a finite sequence of integers $j(0), j(1), \dots, j(\nu+1)$ together with steps $x(1), \dots, x(\nu+1)$ such that:
- $j(0) = -n$ and $j(\nu+1) = n$;
- each step $x(t) = j(t) - j(t-1)$ belongs to $F_m$ and is positive (i.e. $x(t) \in F_m \cap \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$);
- the intermediate vertices $j(1), \dots, j(\nu)$ all lie strictly between $-n$ and $n$, i.e. $j(t) \notin \{-n, n\}$ for $1 \le t \le \nu$.

Let $X_n^+(F_m)$ denote the set of all such walks. For each walk $x \in X_n^+(F_m)$ with $\nu$ intermediate vertices, define
$$h_1(x) = \prod_{t=1}^{\nu} \frac{1}{n^2 - j(t)^2}, \qquad h(x) = h_1(x) \prod_{t=1}^{\nu+1} V(x(t)),$$
where $V : F_m \cap \mathbb{Z}_{>0} \to \mathbb{C}$ is given by a vector $z = (V(2), V(4), \dots, V(2m)) \in \mathbb{C}^m$.

Define the polynomial
$$P_{m,n}(z) = \sum_{x \in X_n^+(F_m)} h(x) \in \mathbb{C}[V(2), V(4), \dots, V(2m)].$$

Determine the polynomials $P_{m,n}(z)$ explicitly, or, failing that, determine their asymptotic behavior as $m$ is held fixed and $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any follow-up work explicitly resolving the explicit form or large-$n$ asymptotics of the walk-sum polynomials $P_{m,n}(z)$ posed in this question. No published solution or partial result could be confirmed from the available sources, so the status is recorded as unknown.

context_brief: Generic validity of the comparison bound
original_question: Let F_m be a finite set of permitted steps and define β_n^+ = sum_{x in X_n(F_m)} h(x), where X_n(F_m) is the set of admissible walks from -n to n with steps in F_m and h(x) is the walk weight used earlier in the paper. Proposition 4 states that β_n^+ = (sum_{x in X_n^+} h(x)) [1 + O(log n / n)] provided the inequality sum_{x in X_n^+} |h(x)| <= C(V) |sum_{x in X_n^+} h(x)| holds. Is this inequality true for almost every parameter vector z = {V} in C^m, and what is the structure of the exceptional set W = { z : C(z) = infinity } for which such a bound fails?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer m ≥ 1 and a finite set F_m ⊂ ℤ of permitted steps. For each integer n ≥ 1, let X_n^+ denote the set of finite sequences x = (x_0, x_1, …, x_L) with x_0 = -n, x_L = n, and consecutive differences x_{i+1} - x_i ∈ F_m for all i (admissible walks from -n to n with steps in F_m). Assign to each step s ∈ F_m a complex weight V_s, collected into a parameter vector z = (V_s)_{s ∈ F_m} ∈ ℂ^m, and define the walk weight
   h(x) = ∏_{i=0}^{L-1} V_{x_{i+1}-x_i}.
For z ∈ ℂ^m, let
   C(z) = sup_{n ≥ 1} ( Σ_{x ∈ X_n^+} |h(x)| ) / | Σ_{x ∈ X_n^+} h(x) |,
with the convention C(z) = ∞ if the denominator vanishes for some n or the supremum diverges, and define the exceptional set
   W = { z ∈ ℂ^m : C(z) = ∞ }.

Question: Is C(z) < ∞ for Lebesgue-almost every z ∈ ℂ^m (equivalently, does W have Lebesgue measure zero)? Describe the structure of the exceptional set W (for instance, whether it is a countable union of proper analytic subvarieties of ℂ^m, or admits some other explicit characterization).
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any work explicitly resolving this comparison-bound question for weighted admissible walks with steps in a finite set F_m, nor any characterization of the exceptional set W = {z : C(z) = ∞}. No follow-up paper claiming to settle the almost-everywhere validity of the bound or to describe the structure of W was located, so the current status is not verifiable from available sources.

context_brief: Lower bound or asymptotics for B_3(2m+1)
original_question: Take the permitted step set F = {-2, +4}, equivalently R = 1 and S = 2, and let n = 2m + 1 be odd. For κ negative steps, let X_n(κ) be the set of admissible walks from -n to n having exactly κ steps equal to -2R, and define P_κ(a,b) = sum_{x in X_n(κ)} h(x) = a^κ b^q B_κ(n), where q is determined by Sq = n + Rκ and B_κ(n) = sum_{x in X_n(κ)} h_1(x). In the case κ = 3, determine an asymptotic formula for B_3(2m+1), or at least prove that there exists an absolute constant C such that |B_3(2m+1)| >= C^m / m!.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers R = 1 and S = 2 with permitted step set F = {-2R, +2S} = {-2, +4}. For an integer n ≥ 1, an admissible walk from -n to n is a finite sequence x = (x(0), x(1), …, x(L)) of integers with x(0) = -n, x(L) = n, and each step x(t+1) - x(t) ∈ F.

For a nonnegative integer κ, let X_n(κ) denote the set of admissible walks from -n to n having exactly κ steps equal to -2R (i.e. #{t : x(t+1) - x(t) = -2R} = κ). For such a walk, if q denotes the number of positive steps (steps equal to +2S), the endpoint condition gives Sq - Rκ = n, equivalently 2q - κ = n.

To each admissible walk x ∈ X_n(κ) associate a weight h_1(x) defined by
   h_1(x) = ∏_{t=0}^{L-1} 1/(x(t+1)^2 - x(t)^2) · (combinatorial product determined by the walk),
more precisely the walk-weight that arises in the eigenfunction expansion for the Hill operator with potential a e^{-2ix} + b e^{4ix}, so that the polynomial
   P_κ(a, b) := Σ_{x ∈ X_n(κ)} h(x) = a^κ b^q · B_κ(n),
where
   B_κ(n) := Σ_{x ∈ X_n(κ)} h_1(x).

Specialize to n = 2m + 1 (so 2q = 2m + 1 + κ) and κ = 3, giving q = m + 2. Determine the asymptotic behavior, as m → ∞, of the sequence
   B_3(2m + 1).
At the very least, prove that there exists an absolute constant C > 0 such that
   |B_3(2m + 1)| ≥ C^m / m!  for all sufficiently large m.

original_question: For the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB, which gradings by small finite abelian groups preserve the algebraic or coalgebraic structure? More concretely, for groups such as Z2, Z3, Z4, and Z2 × Z2, classify the group actions or coactions that turn these paraparticle algebras into graded module algebras or graded module coalgebras.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}\langle b_i^+, b_i^-, f_j^+, f_j^- angle$ denote the free associative unital $\mathbb{C}$-algebra on parabosonic generators $\{b_i^\pm : i \in I\}$ and parafermionic generators $\{f_j^\pm : j \in J\}$. The Relative Parabose-Fermi algebra $P_{BF}$ is the quotient of this free algebra by the trilinear (Green-Greenberg-Messiah) relations

$[\{b_i^\xi, b_k^\eta\}, b_l^\epsilon] = (\epsilon - \eta)\delta_{kl}\, b_i^\xi - (\epsilon - \xi)\delta_{il}\, b_k^\eta,$
$[[f_j^\xi, f_m^\eta], f_n^\epsilon] = 2\delta_{mn}\delta_{\eta,-\epsilon}\, f_j^\xi - 2\delta_{jn}\delta_{\xi,-\epsilon}\, f_m^\eta,$
$[\{b_i^\xi, b_k^\eta\}, f_j^\epsilon] = 0, \quad [[f_j^\xi, f_m^\eta], b_i^\epsilon] = 0, \quad [\{b_i^\xi, f_j^\eta\}, b_k^\epsilon] = 0, \quad [\{b_i^\xi, f_j^\eta\}, f_m^\epsilon] = 0,$

for all admissible indices and signs $\xi,\eta,\epsilon \in \{+,-\}$, where mixed brackets are taken as anticommutators between paraboson-parafermion pairs. The Relative Fermi-Bose algebra $P_{FB}$ is defined analogously, with the roles of commutator/anticommutator interchanged on the mixed relations (so that the bose and fermi sectors are swapped in their statistics with respect to each other). Both $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$ carry compatible coalgebra (Hopf-like) structures making them graded (co)module (co)algebras over suitable group algebras.

Let $G$ be one of the finite abelian groups $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2 	imes \mathbb{Z}_2$, and let $\mathbb{C}G$ be its group algebra. Classify, up to equivalence of gradings, all $G$-gradings on $P_{BF}$ and on $P_{FB}$ that make them $\mathbb{C}G$-module algebras (equivalently $\mathbb{C}G$-comodule algebras) and, dually, all $G$-actions/coactions that turn them into $\mathbb{C}G$-(co)module coalgebras. That is, determine all group (co)actions of $G$ on $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$ that preserve their (co)algebra structures, and produce a complete classification list for each of these four groups.
status_search_result: The problem appears to be stated as an open research objective in a problems-survey-style article on paraparticle algebras. No publication has been located that provides a full classification of $\mathbb{Z}_2$-, $\mathbb{Z}_3$-, $\mathbb{Z}_4$-, or $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$-gradings preserving the (co)algebra structure of $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$. Status appears open.

original_question: For each grading of the paraparticle algebras under consideration, what braided group structures are possible? Equivalently, determine the compatible bicharacters, universal R-matrices of the corresponding group Hopf algebras, and braidings on the associated module or comodule categories, and decide which of these choices support compatible graded algebra and coalgebra structures that actually produce a braided group.
self_contained_problem:
Let A be a paraparticle algebra (for instance the parabosonic algebra PB, the parafermionic algebra PF, or a mixed parabose–parafermi algebra PBF defined by Green's relations on generators), and let G be an abelian group equipped with a chosen G-grading A = ⊕_{g∈G} A_g compatible with the defining relations of A.

(a) Determine all bicharacters β: G × G → k^× (where k is the ground field, typically ℂ), equivalently all universal R-matrices of the group Hopf algebra k[G], equivalently all braidings of the symmetric/braided monoidal category ^G_k M (resp. M^G_k) of G-graded vector spaces (G-modules of k[G], resp. G-comodules), that are compatible with the given grading on A.

(b) For each such bicharacter/braiding β, decide whether A admits graded algebra and coalgebra structures (a coproduct Δ: A → A ⊗_β A, counit ε, antipode S, and unit/multiplication) that are morphisms in the braided category determined by β, so that (A, m, η, Δ, ε, S) becomes a braided group (Hopf algebra in the braided category) in the sense of Majid.

Provide a complete classification of admissible bicharacters for each natural grading of PB, PF, and PBF, and specify which of these braidings support a compatible braided group structure on the corresponding paraparticle algebra.

The status is best described as open.

original_question: Can one apply or develop bosonization, or bosonization-like constructions, that convert the graded and braided paraparticle Hopf structures into ordinary Hopf structures with trivial braiding while preserving equivalent representation theory?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a paraparticle algebra (for instance the parabosonic algebra $P_B$, the parafermionic algebra $P_F$, or a Relative Paraparticle Set $P_{BF}$ combining both), equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$- (or more general group-) grading and a braided Hopf algebra structure in a suitable braided monoidal category $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., a Hopf algebra object with respect to a non-trivial braiding $\Psi$ that encodes the para-statistics).

Develop, or show the (non)existence of, a bosonization-type construction $A \rightsquigarrow \widehat{A}$ producing an ordinary Hopf algebra $\widehat{A}$ (i.e., a Hopf algebra in the symmetric category of vector spaces with trivial flip braiding and no nontrivial grading) such that:

(a) $\widehat{A}$ is built functorially from $A$ together with auxiliary data (e.g. a smash/biproduct with a Hopf algebra $H$ encoding the grading and the braiding, in the spirit of the Radford–Majid biproduct/bosonization);

(b) the categories of (suitable) representations of $A$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and of $\widehat{A}$ in the category of vector spaces are equivalent as monoidal categories, so that all Fock-like and other physically relevant representations of the paraparticle algebra are recovered as ordinary modules over $\widehat{A}$.

Specifically: exhibit such a construction for the parabosonic, parafermionic, and relative paraparticle algebras, or determine the obstructions to its existence.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as a research objective in works on paraparticle algebras and their braided/graded Hopf structures. While the general Radford–Majid bosonization theory is well established, no published results were found that fully carry out an equivalence-of-representations bosonization for all paraparticle algebras (parabosonic, parafermionic, relative paraparticle set). The most recent surveys list it among open problems.

original_question: Can the braided-tensor-product method be completed to give explicit Fock-like representations of the infinite-degree-of-freedom parabosonic algebra PB? In particular, can one develop the needed multinomial theorem for the anticommuting creation operators that arise in the graded tensor-product realization, so that the action of PB generators and the corresponding matrix elements can be computed explicitly?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a complex vector space with countably infinite basis $\{x_i\}_{i\in I}$, and let $PB$ denote the infinite-degree-of-freedom parabosonic algebra, namely the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by symbols $\{b_i^{+},\,b_i^{-} : i\in I\}$ subject to the Green (trilinear) parabosonic relations
$$[\,\{b_i^{\xi},b_j^{\eta}\},\,b_k^{\varepsilon}\,] = (\varepsilon-\eta)\,\delta_{jk}\,b_i^{\xi} - (\varepsilon-\xi)\,\delta_{ik}\,b_j^{\eta},$$
for all $i,j,k\in I$ and $\xi,\eta,\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}$. The algebra $PB$ carries a natural $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading with $b_i^{\pm}$ odd, and admits a graded (braided) Hopf-algebraic structure whose comultiplication, applied to a single mode algebra $PB^{(1)}$, yields a braided tensor product realization $PB^{(1)}\,\underline{\otimes}\,PB^{(1)}\,\underline{\otimes}\,\cdots$ in which creation operators $b_i^{(k)+}$ corresponding to different tensor factors $k$ anticommute up to suitable signs.

(a) Construct, explicitly and in closed form, Fock-like (vacuum) representations of $PB$ via the braided tensor product method: starting from a one-mode Fock representation of $PB^{(1)}$ on a graded module $F^{(1)}$ with vacuum $|0\rangle$ annihilated by $b^{-}$, build a representation of $PB$ on a braided tensor product $F = \bigotimes_{k} F^{(k)}$ in such a way that the action of every generator $b_i^{\pm}$ on every basis vector, and all matrix elements $\langle v\,|\,b_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots b_{i_n}^{\varepsilon_n}\,|w\rangle$, can be written down explicitly.

(b) As the principal combinatorial step required by (a), establish a multinomial theorem for the anticommuting (graded) creation variables $\{b_i^{(k)+}\}$ arising in the braided tensor product: derive a closed-form expansion of $\big(\sum_{k} b_i^{(k)+}\big)^{N}$ (and more generally of products $\prod_i (\sum_k b_i^{(k)+})^{N_i}$) as a sum over multi-indices, with explicit sign coefficients determined by the braided grading, suitable for computing the action of $PB$-generators on Fock states.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open program in a survey on gradings, braidings and paraparticles. Subsequent work on the Relative Parabose Set algebra constructs explicit Fock-like representations and ladder-operator actions for related (mixed/relative) parabose algebras, but a complete explicit braided-tensor-product Fock construction for the infinite-degree-of-freedom $PB$, together with the required multinomial theorem in anticommuting creation variables, does not appear to have been carried out in the literature located. Status appears still open.

original_question: When one decomposes the graded tensor-product representations built for PB and PF, do irreducible components appear beyond the known p-Fock-like modules? In other words, can these decompositions produce direct summands or more general submodules that are not equivalent to the standard p-Fock-like representations?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P_B$ denote the parabosonic algebra and $P_F$ denote the parafermionic algebra. Recall that $P_F$ is isomorphic to the universal enveloping algebra of the orthogonal Lie algebra $so(2n+1)$ (or its infinite-rank limit $so(\infty)$), and $P_B$ is isomorphic to the universal enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $osp(1|2n)$ (or $osp(1|\infty)$). For each positive integer $p$, the so-called $p$-Fock-like (parastatistics) module $F(p)$ is the unitary irreducible lowest-weight module of order $p$: for $P_F$ it is the unique irreducible quotient of the Fock-type module generated by a vacuum vector $|0\rangle$ subject to $f_j^- |0\rangle = 0$ and $f_j^- f_k^+ |0\rangle = p\,\delta_{jk}|0\rangle$, and similarly (with anticommutators) for $P_B$.

Consider graded tensor-product representations of $P_B$ (respectively $P_F$) of the form $F(p_1)\otimes F(p_2)\otimes\cdots\otimes F(p_k)$, where the tensor product is taken in the appropriate $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded (super) sense for $P_B$ and in the ordinary sense for $P_F$. It is known that every $p$-Fock-like module appears as an irreducible factor in some such graded tensor-product decomposition.

Question: In the decomposition of these graded tensor-product representations into irreducible (or indecomposable) constituents, do there exist direct summands, or more generally submodules, that are not isomorphic to any of the standard $p$-Fock-like modules $F(p)$? Equivalently, is the class of $p$-Fock-like modules closed under taking irreducible constituents of graded tensor products, or do genuinely new (inequivalent) irreducible representations of $P_B$ or $P_F$ arise this way?
status_search_result: A web search located related work by Stoilova and Van der Jeugt on parafermion/paraboson Fock spaces and representations of $so(\infty)$ and $osp(1|\infty)$, showing that $p$-Fock-like modules appear as irreducible factors in graded tensor products. No source was found that fully classifies all irreducible constituents of such tensor products or proves/disproves the existence of non-$p$-Fock-like summands, so the question appears to remain open.

original_question: Can the same braided-representation strategy be extended from PB and PF to the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB by viewing Ws and Was as suitable graded quotient algebras? To make that extension work, can one develop the required multinomial theorem that handles expressions mixing commuting and anticommuting variables?
self_contained_problem:
Let $W_s$ denote the Weyl algebra (the unital associative algebra generated by elements $x_1,\dots,x_n$ and $\partial_1,\dots,\partial_n$ with relations $[\partial_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij}$, $[x_i,x_j]=[\partial_i,\partial_j]=0$), and let $W_{as}$ denote its $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded (Clifford-like) analogue generated by anticommuting variables $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_m$ and derivations $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_m$ with $\{\eta_i,\xi_j\}=\delta_{ij}$, $\{\xi_i,\xi_j\}=\{\eta_i,\eta_j\}=0$. Let $P_B$ and $P_F$ denote the parabose and parafermi algebras (defined by Green's trilinear commutation relations), and let $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$ denote the two mixed paraparticle algebras (relative parabose set and relative parafermi set), generated by parabosonic and parafermionic creation/annihilation operators interrelated by either relative commutation or relative anticommutation trilinear relations.

Suppose one has a braided-representation construction realizing the Fock-like representations of $P_B$ and $P_F$ as irreducible submodules of suitable graded tensor product representations of $W_s$ and $W_{as}$ respectively, after viewing them as graded quotient algebras.

(a) Can this braided-representation strategy be extended to produce the Fock-like representations of the mixed paraparticle algebras $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$ as irreducible submodules of the graded tensor product representations of $W_s$ and $W_{as}$, viewed as appropriate graded quotient algebras?

(b) Formulate and prove a multinomial expansion theorem for monomials in a finite collection of variables some of which mutually commute and some of which mutually anticommute (with mixed cross-relations), of the form needed to carry out the combinatorial computations underlying (a).

original_question: Do the proposed paraparticle Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p + 1)-level system yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model? If so, can one compute their energy levels, eigenfunctions, and transition rates and compare those predictions directly with theoretical and experimental results?
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a positive integer, and let $b^\pm$ denote parabosonic creation/annihilation operators satisfying the order-$p$ relations
$$[\{b^-, b^+\}, b^\pm] = \pm 2 b^\pm, \qquad [\{b^+, b^+\}, b^-] = -4 b^+, \qquad [\{b^-, b^-\}, b^+] = 4 b^-,$$
acting on the Fock-like parabosonic module $V(p)$ with vacuum $|0\rangle$ satisfying $b^- |0\rangle = 0$ and $b^- b^+ |0\rangle = p\,|0\rangle$. Let $\mathcal{H}_A$ be the Hilbert space of a $(p+1)$-level atomic system, with orthonormal levels $|j\rangle$, $j = 0,1,\dots,p$, and ladder operators $E_{jk} = |j\rangle\langle k|$.

Consider on $V(p) \otimes \mathcal{H}_A$ a "paraparticle Jaynes–Cummings" Hamiltonian of generalized rotating-wave form
$$H = \omega_F\, \tfrac{1}{2}\{b^+, b^-\} + \sum_{j=0}^{p} \varepsilon_j\, E_{jj} + \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} g_j\,\bigl( b^+ E_{j,j+1} + b^- E_{j+1,j} \bigr),$$
with real parameters $\omega_F$, $\{\varepsilon_j\}$, $\{g_j\}$.

(a) Determine, for each fixed $p$, whether $H$ is exactly diagonalizable on $V(p)\otimes \mathcal{H}_A$ in the sense that all eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be written in closed form via finite-dimensional invariant subspaces analogous to the Jaynes–Cummings doublets at $p=1$.

(b) Compute explicitly the energy levels and eigenstates, and derive closed-form expressions for the transition rates between dressed states under a dipole-type perturbation $V = \mu(b^+ + b^-)\sum_j (E_{j,j+1}+E_{j+1,j})$.
status_search_result: The case $p=1$ (two-level atom in a single-mode para-Bose cavity field) has been treated with exact energy spectrum and eigenstates obtained, and various deformed/parity-deformed Jaynes–Cummings extensions are known to be (quasi-)exactly solvable. The general $(p+1)$-level paraparticle formulation with arbitrary couplings does not appear to have a complete published solution, so the broader question is at most partially solved.

original_question: Determine the exact enumeration and asymptotic growth of permutations that avoid the classical pattern 1324. In particular, determine the Stanley-Wilf limit for 1324-avoiding permutations and, if possible, an exact formula or asymptotic description for the number of 1324-avoiders of length n.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation π = π(1)π(2)…π(n) of {1,2,…,n} is said to contain the classical pattern 1324 if there exist indices i₁ < i₂ < i₃ < i₄ such that π(i₁) < π(i₃) < π(i₂) < π(i₄); otherwise π is said to avoid 1324. Let S_n(1324) denote the set of permutations of {1,…,n} that avoid 1324, and let a_n = |S_n(1324)|.

By the Marcus–Tardos theorem (formerly the Stanley–Wilf conjecture), the limit
  L(1324) := lim_{n→∞} a_n^{1/n}
exists and is finite.

(a) Determine the exact value of the Stanley–Wilf limit L(1324).

(b) Determine an exact enumeration formula for a_n, or otherwise a precise asymptotic description (including any subexponential correction factors) for a_n as n → ∞.
status_search_result: The exact enumeration of 1324-avoiding permutations and the value of the Stanley–Wilf limit L(1324) remain open. Current rigorous bounds place L(1324) between roughly 10.271 and 13.5, with numerical/series evidence suggesting a value near 11.6. Recent work (e.g., December 2025 preprints on encoding pattern-avoiding permutations as walks) continues to improve lower bounds (a conditional bound of about 10.418), but no exact value or closed-form enumeration is known. 1324 remains the only length-4 classical pattern (up to Wilf equivalence) whose Stanley–Wilf limit is unknown.

original_question: Prove or refute the conjectured upper bound SW(1324) < e*pi*sqrt(2/3) for the Stanley-Wilf limit of the classical pattern 1324.
self_contained_problem:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,2,\dots,k\}$, a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ is said to contain the pattern $\sigma$ if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the values $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \dots, \pi(i_k)$ appear in the same relative order as $\sigma(1), \sigma(2), \dots, \sigma(k)$; otherwise $\pi$ avoids $\sigma$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_n(\sigma)$ denote the number of permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ that avoid $\sigma$. By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, the limit
$$ \mathrm{SW}(\sigma) := \lim_{n\to\infty} \mathrm{Av}_n(\sigma)^{1/n} $$
exists and is finite for every pattern $\sigma$. Consider the pattern $\sigma = 1324$. Determine whether
$$ \mathrm{SW}(1324) < e^{\,\pi\sqrt{2/3}} \approx 13.001954, $$
proving the inequality or producing a refutation.
status_search_result: The conjectured bound $\mathrm{SW}(1324) < e^{\pi\sqrt{2/3}} \approx 13.002$ originates from work of Bóna and would follow from a still-unproven monotonicity conjecture on inversion-graded counts of 1324-avoiders. The current best unconditional upper bound is approximately 13.5 (Bevan, Brignall, Elvey Price, Pantone, 2020), and the best lower bound is around 10.27, leaving the conjectured bound unproven. The problem is open.

original_question: Prove or refute that for every fixed inversion count k, the number of 1324-avoiding permutations of length n having exactly k inversions is an increasing function of n.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation π of {1,2,...,n} is said to avoid the pattern 1324 if there do not exist indices i₁ < i₂ < i₃ < i₄ such that π(i₁) < π(i₃) < π(i₂) < π(i₄). An inversion of a permutation π of length n is a pair (i,j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n and π(i) > π(j); the inversion count of π is the total number of such pairs.

For nonnegative integers n and k, let a(n,k) denote the number of 1324-avoiding permutations of {1,2,...,n} that have exactly k inversions.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed nonnegative integer k, the sequence n ↦ a(n,k) is (weakly) increasing in n; that is, a(n,k) ≤ a(n+1,k) for all n ≥ 1.
status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, 2012) that the number of 1324-avoiding permutations of length n with exactly k inversions is weakly increasing in n appears to remain open in full generality. A 2025 paper by Linusson and Verkama, "Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions," verifies the monotonicity for all k ≤ 2n − 7, providing partial progress but not a complete resolution.

original_question: For each pattern length k, determine whether the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among all classical patterns of length k is always attained by a layered pattern.
self_contained_problem:
For a permutation σ of {1,…,n} and a permutation τ of {1,…,k} (a classical pattern), say that σ contains τ if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ⋯ < i_k ≤ n such that σ(i_a) < σ(i_b) if and only if τ(a) < τ(b). Otherwise σ avoids τ. Let S_n(τ) denote the number of permutations of {1,…,n} that avoid τ. By the Marcus–Tardos theorem, the limit

  L(τ) = lim_{n→∞} S_n(τ)^{1/n}

exists and is finite for every classical pattern τ.

A permutation τ of length k is called layered if it is a concatenation of consecutive decreasing blocks whose values, taken block by block, increase; equivalently, τ is the direct sum of decreasing permutations.

Question: Is it true that for every integer k ≥ 1,

  max{ L(τ) : τ a permutation of length k } = max{ L(τ) : τ a layered permutation of length k } ?

That is, for every pattern length k, is the maximum Stanley–Wilf limit over all classical patterns of length k always attained by some layered pattern?
status_search_result: The conjecture that the largest Stanley–Wilf limit among classical patterns of a given length is attained by a layered pattern is widely cited as an open conjecture, supported by computer enumeration up to length eight. Recent work (e.g., on bounds for L(1324) and on blockable permutations, 2025) still treats it as conjectural and uses it to derive conditional upper bounds such as 4k².

original_question: For each positive integer k, determine the form of the layered permutation pattern of length k that is avoided by the largest number of permutations, equivalently the layered pattern of length k that is most easily avoided.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation of length n is a bijection from {1,2,...,n} to itself, written in one-line notation. A permutation σ of length n is said to contain a permutation π of length k as a pattern if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k ≤ n such that σ(i_1), σ(i_2), ..., σ(i_k) appear in the same relative order as π(1), π(2), ..., π(k); otherwise σ avoids π. For a pattern π, let Av_n(π) denote the number of permutations of length n that avoid π.

A layered permutation is a permutation that can be written as a concatenation of consecutive decreasing runs ("layers") whose minima are increasing; equivalently, π is layered if it is a concatenation of blocks B_1, B_2, ..., B_r, where each B_i consists of consecutive integers written in decreasing order, and each entry of B_i is less than every entry of B_{i+1}. Such a layered pattern is determined by the composition (ℓ_1, ℓ_2, ..., ℓ_r) of k giving the layer lengths.

Problem: For each positive integer k, determine the layered permutation pattern π of length k that is most easily avoided, in the sense that

    Av_n(π) = max { Av_n(τ) : τ is a layered permutation of length k }

for all sufficiently large n (or, equivalently, that maximizes the Stanley–Wilf limit lim_{n→∞} Av_n(τ)^{1/n} over layered patterns τ of length k). Describe the composition (ℓ_1, ..., ℓ_r) of the optimal pattern as an explicit function of k.
status_search_result: The problem of identifying the most avoided layered pattern of each length k appears to remain open. While the Stanley–Wilf conjecture (proved by Marcus–Tardos) and various bounds for layered patterns are known, the exact form of the extremal layered pattern of length k has not been determined; published conjectures for specific families exist, and several have been disproved.

original_question: For every even integer k, prove or refute that the layered pattern of length k with layers (1, 2, 2, ..., 2, 2, 1) is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length k.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $S_n$ denote the set of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For permutations $\pi\in S_n$ and $\tau\in S_k$ with $k\le n$, we say that $\pi$ contains $\tau$ as a pattern if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k\le n$ such that $\pi(i_a)<\pi(i_b)$ if and only if $\tau(a)<\tau(b)$ for all $a,b$. Otherwise $\pi$ is said to avoid $\tau$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)$ denote the number of permutations in $S_n$ that avoid $\tau$.

A permutation $\tau\in S_k$ is called layered with layer sequence $(\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_r)$, where $\ell_1+\ell_2+\dots+\ell_r=k$, if it is the concatenation of $r$ blocks of consecutive entries such that the $j$-th block consists of $\ell_j$ entries that form a decreasing sequence, and the entries of the $j$-th block are all smaller than the entries of the $(j+1)$-th block. Equivalently, a layered permutation is a direct sum of decreasing permutations.

Problem. For every even integer $k\ge 2$, let $\tau_k\in S_k$ denote the layered permutation with layer sequence $(1,2,2,\dots,2,2,1)$ (that is, the first and last layers have size $1$ and the $k/2-1$ intermediate layers each have size $2$). Prove or refute the following statement: for every even integer $k\ge 2$ and every sufficiently large $n$,
$$\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau_k)\ge \mathrm{Av}_n(\sigma)\qquad\text{for all }\sigma\in S_k,$$
i.e., $\tau_k$ is the most avoided pattern among all patterns of length $k$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Kézdy and Snevily, recorded as Conjecture 9.10 in Bóna's "Combinatorics of Permutations") asserts that for even $k$ the layered pattern with layers $(1,2,\dots,2,1)$ is the most avoided pattern of length $k$. Web searches do not turn up a proof or refutation; the conjecture is referred to as still not refuted in subsequent literature on permutation pattern avoidance, suggesting it remains open.

original_question: For every integer k congruent to 1 modulo 4, prove or refute that the most avoided pattern of length k is the layered pattern with symmetric layer sizes (1, 2, ..., 2, 3, 2, ..., 2, 1).
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For a positive integer n, let S_n denote the symmetric group of permutations of {1,2,…,n}, written in one-line notation. A permutation σ ∈ S_n is said to contain a pattern τ ∈ S_k (with k ≤ n) if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ⋯ < i_k ≤ n such that the subsequence σ(i_1) σ(i_2) ⋯ σ(i_k) is order-isomorphic to τ; otherwise, σ avoids τ. Let Av_n(τ) denote the set of permutations in S_n that avoid τ, and let s_n(τ) = |Av_n(τ)|.

A layered permutation with composition (a_1, a_2, …, a_r) of k (so each a_i ≥ 1 and a_1 + a_2 + ⋯ + a_r = k) is the permutation in S_k obtained by concatenating decreasing blocks of sizes a_1, a_2, …, a_r in such a way that the first block consists of the integers {1,…,a_1} written in decreasing order, the second block consists of {a_1+1, …, a_1+a_2} in decreasing order, and so on. Equivalently, the permutation is a concatenation of decreasing runs whose minima are increasing.

For fixed k, call a pattern τ ∈ S_k a most avoided pattern of length k if s_n(τ) ≥ s_n(π) for every π ∈ S_k and for all sufficiently large n; equivalently (using the existence of the Stanley–Wilf limit L(π) = lim_{n→∞} s_n(π)^{1/n}), τ achieves the maximum of L(π) over π ∈ S_k.

Problem. Let k be a positive integer with k ≡ 1 (mod 4), and write k = 4m + 1 with m ≥ 1. Consider the symmetric layered pattern of length k with composition

(1, 2, 2, …, 2, 3, 2, …, 2, 2, 1),

where the central block has size 3, this 3 is flanked on each side by exactly (m − 1) blocks of size 2, and the outermost blocks on each side have size 1 (so the composition has 2m − 1 entries total, with sum 4m + 1 = k). Prove or disprove the following statement:

For every k ≡ 1 (mod 4) with k ≥ 5, the symmetric layered pattern with the above composition is a most avoided pattern of length k; that is, it maximizes the Stanley–Wilf limit L(π) over all π ∈ S_k.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a proof or refutation of Burstein's conjecture on the most avoided length-k pattern (for k ≡ 1 mod 4) being the symmetric layered pattern (1,2,…,2,3,2,…,2,1). Surveys on pattern avoidance still list this as an open conjecture, and no recent paper appears to settle it.

original_question: Determine whether there exist two permutation patterns whose avoidance counts switch relative order more than once, and in particular whether two patterns can switch places infinitely often as n grows.
self_contained_problem:
For a permutation pattern σ (a permutation of {1,2,…,k}), let Av_σ(n) denote the number of permutations of {1,2,…,n} that avoid σ, where a permutation π avoids σ if there is no subsequence of π whose entries appear in the same relative order as the entries of σ. Given two patterns σ and τ, say that the pair (σ, τ) "switches" at n if the strict inequality between Av_σ(n) and Av_τ(n) reverses direction between n and n+1 (i.e., (Av_σ(n) − Av_τ(n)) and (Av_σ(n+1) − Av_τ(n+1)) have opposite nonzero signs).

(a) Determine whether there exist two patterns σ and τ such that the pair (σ, τ) switches at more than one value of n.

(b) In particular, determine whether there exist two patterns σ and τ such that the pair (σ, τ) switches at infinitely many values of n as n → ∞.

(c) (Weak form) Determine whether for every pair of patterns σ and τ there exists an integer N such that either Av_σ(n) < Av_τ(n) for all n > N, or Av_σ(n) > Av_τ(n) for all n > N.
status_search_result: The conjectures of Stankova and West that no two permutation patterns can have their avoidance counts switch relative order more than once (and the weaker eventual-monotonicity conjecture) appear to remain open. Web searches surface the conjecture and related work in permutation pattern enumeration, but no announcement of a proof or counterexample was found.

original_question: Determine whether the bound 2.25*k^2 is the best possible general upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical permutation pattern of length k.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For permutations $\pi\in S_n$ and $\tau\in S_k$, we say $\pi$ contains the (classical) pattern $\tau$ if there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ such that $\pi(i_1),\pi(i_2),\dots,\pi(i_k)$ are in the same relative order as $\tau(1),\tau(2),\dots,\tau(k)$; otherwise $\pi$ avoids $\tau$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)=\{\pi\in S_n:\pi\text{ avoids }\tau\}$. The Marcus–Tardos theorem (formerly the Stanley–Wilf conjecture) implies the existence of the limit
$$L(\tau)=\lim_{n\to\infty}|\mathrm{Av}_n(\tau)|^{1/n},$$
called the Stanley–Wilf limit of $\tau$.

A permutation $\tau\in S_k$ is called layered if it is a concatenation of consecutive decreasing runs whose values form increasing blocks (e.g.\ $321\,54\,876$). Assume the conjecture that, among all patterns of length $k$, the maximum value of $L(\tau)$ is attained by some layered pattern; this conjecture together with known bounds yields the upper bound
$$L(\tau)\le 2.25\,k^2\qquad\text{for every }\tau\in S_k.$$

Determine whether the constant $2.25$ in the bound $L(\tau)\le 2.25\,k^2$ is best possible as a general upper bound for the Stanley–Wilf limit over all classical permutation patterns of length $k$; that is, decide whether the bound $2.25\,k^2$ can be replaced by $c\,k^2$ for some smaller constant $c<2.25$ holding for all $k$ and all $\tau\in S_k$.

original_question: Characterize completely the intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function satisfies μ(σ, τ) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \bigcup_{n\geq 1} S_n$ be the set of all finite permutations. For $\sigma \in S_k$ and $\tau \in S_n$ with $k \le n$, say that $\sigma$ is a pattern of $\tau$, written $\sigma \le \tau$, if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the subsequence $\tau(i_1)\tau(i_2)\cdots\tau(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\sigma(1)\sigma(2)\cdots\sigma(k)$ (i.e., $\tau(i_a) < \tau(i_b)$ if and only if $\sigma(a) < \sigma(b)$). With this relation, $S$ becomes a poset, the permutation pattern poset.

For any pair $\sigma \le \tau$ in $S$, let $[\sigma,\tau] = \{\pi \in S : \sigma \le \pi \le \tau\}$ and let $\mu$ denote the Möbius function of this poset, defined recursively by $\mu(\sigma,\sigma) = 1$ and $\mu(\sigma,\tau) = -\sum_{\sigma \le \pi < \tau} \mu(\sigma,\pi)$ for $\sigma < \tau$.

Problem: Give a complete combinatorial characterization of all pairs $(\sigma,\tau)$ with $\sigma \le \tau$ for which $\mu(\sigma,\tau) = 0$.
category_tag: Möbius function of permutation pattern poset
status_search_result: The problem of completely characterizing intervals with zero Möbius function in the permutation pattern poset remains open. Several partial results identify large families of such intervals (e.g., intervals [1,π] where π contains two non-isomorphic length-2 intervals, or a triple of consecutive letters with consecutive monotone values), and recent asymptotic work shows that at least a (1−1/e)² ≈ 0.3995 fraction of principal intervals have zero Möbius function, but no complete characterization has been published.

original_question: Characterize the intervals [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset for which the absolute value |μ(σ, π)| of the Möbius function equals the number of occurrences of σ in π.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the permutation pattern poset: its elements are all finite permutations (one from each $S_n$, $n\geq 1$), and the partial order is defined by $\sigma \leq \pi$ if and only if $\pi$ contains $\sigma$ as a pattern, i.e., there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ (where $k = |\sigma|$ and $n = |\pi|$) such that the subsequence $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \ldots, \pi(i_k)$ has the same relative order as $\sigma(1), \sigma(2), \ldots, \sigma(k)$. Such an index tuple is called an occurrence of $\sigma$ in $\pi$, and the number of occurrences is denoted $\mathrm{occ}(\sigma, \pi)$.

For $\sigma \le \pi$ in $\mathcal{P}$, let $\mu(\sigma, \pi)$ denote the Möbius function of the interval $[\sigma, \pi]$, defined recursively by $\mu(\pi, \pi) = 1$ and $\mu(\sigma, \pi) = -\sum_{\sigma \le \tau < \pi} \mu(\sigma, \tau)$ for $\sigma < \pi$.

Give a complete characterization of those intervals $[\sigma, \pi]$ in $\mathcal{P}$ for which
$$|\mu(\sigma, \pi)| = \mathrm{occ}(\sigma, \pi).$$
category_tag: Möbius function of permutation pattern poset
status_search_result: The general characterization appears to remain open. Subsequent work has established the equality |μ(σ,π)| = (number of normal occurrences) for various subclasses (e.g., intervals of permutations with a fixed number of descents, separable permutations, certain 132-avoiding cases), and conjectures bound |μ| by the number of occurrences in particular families, but no complete characterization of the intervals where |μ(σ,π)| equals the total number of occurrences of σ in π has been published.

original_question: Find a bound for |μ(σ, τ)| in the permutation pattern poset that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ, without requiring additional structure such as separability.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the permutation pattern poset: the elements of $\mathcal{P}$ are all finite permutations (one from each $S_n$, $n\ge 1$), and $\sigma\le\tau$ iff $\tau$ contains $\sigma$ as a pattern, i.e. there exist indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k\le n$ (where $k=|\sigma|$ and $n=|\tau|$) such that $\tau(i_1),\tau(i_2),\dots,\tau(i_k)$ are in the same relative order as $\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\dots,\sigma(k)$. For $\sigma\le\tau$ in $\mathcal{P}$, let $\mu(\sigma,\tau)$ denote the Möbius function of the interval $[\sigma,\tau]$ in $\mathcal{P}$, defined recursively by $\mu(\tau,\tau)=1$ and $\mu(\sigma,\tau)=-\sum_{\sigma\le\rho<\tau}\mu(\sigma,\rho)$. Let $\operatorname{occ}(\sigma,\tau)$ denote the number of occurrences of $\sigma$ as a pattern in $\tau$, i.e. the number of index sequences $i_1<\cdots<i_k$ as above.

Problem: Find a function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ such that
$$|\mu(\sigma,\tau)|\le f(\operatorname{occ}(\sigma,\tau))$$
for all pairs $\sigma\le\tau$ in $\mathcal{P}$, with no further structural restriction (such as separability, or pattern-avoidance) on $\sigma$ or $\tau$. Equivalently, decide whether $\sup\{|\mu(\sigma,\tau)| : \operatorname{occ}(\sigma,\tau)=N\}$ is finite for each fixed $N$, and if so, give an explicit bound.
category_tag: Möbius function of permutation pattern poset
status_search_result: The question of bounding |μ(σ,τ)| in the permutation pattern poset purely in terms of the number of occurrences of σ in τ remains open in general. Bounds of this form are known only under additional hypotheses—most notably for separable permutations and for certain pattern-avoiding subclasses (e.g. avoiding 132)—and recent constructions exhibit polynomial growth of |μ(1,π)| in |π|, but no general bound depending only on the number of occurrences has been established.

original_question: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) of the interior of the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \bigcup_{n \geq 1} S_n$ denote the set of all finite permutations. For $\sigma \in S_k$ and $\pi \in S_n$ with $k \leq n$, say that $\sigma$ is a pattern of $\pi$, written $\sigma \leq \pi$, if there exist indices $1 \leq i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \leq n$ such that the sequence $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \ldots, \pi(i_k)$ has the same relative order as $\sigma(1), \sigma(2), \ldots, \sigma(k)$. Under this relation $S$ becomes a poset, the permutation pattern poset.

For $\sigma \leq \pi$, let $(\sigma, \pi) = \{\tau \in S : \sigma < \tau < \pi\}$ denote the open interval, and let $\Delta(\sigma, \pi)$ be its order complex, i.e., the abstract simplicial complex whose faces are the chains of $(\sigma, \pi)$.

Characterize precisely the pairs $(\sigma, \pi)$ for which $\Delta(\sigma, \pi)$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres (of possibly varying dimensions).
status_search_result: A general characterization remains open. Partial results are known: for instance, intervals of layered permutations with no disconnected subinterval of rank ≥ 3 have the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres, and shellability (which implies the wedge-of-spheres property) has been established or conjectured for further families such as separable permutations. Subsequent work by Smith and others has extended Möbius/topology results, but no full characterization has been published.

original_question: Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those permutations τ in the interval [σ, π] with μ(σ, τ) not equal to 0. Determine whether Γ must always be pure, meaning that all of its maximal simplices have the same dimension.
self_contained_problem: Order the symmetric groups by pattern containment: for permutations σ and π, write σ ≤ π if there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ⋯ < i_k ≤ n (where k = |σ| and n = |π|) such that the values π(i_1), π(i_2), …, π(i_k) appear in the same relative order as σ(1), σ(2), …, σ(k). With this partial order on the set of all finite permutations, fix σ ≤ π and consider the closed interval [σ, π] = { τ : σ ≤ τ ≤ π }. Let μ denote the Möbius function of this poset. Define the order complex Δ(σ, π) to be the abstract simplicial complex whose simplices are the chains of the open interval (σ, π) = [σ, π] ∖ {σ, π}. Let Γ be the subcomplex of Δ(σ, π) induced by those τ ∈ (σ, π) for which μ(σ, τ) ≠ 0; that is, Γ consists of all chains of (σ, π) all of whose elements τ satisfy μ(σ, τ) ≠ 0. The complex Γ is called pure if all of its maximal simplices (with respect to inclusion) have the same dimension. Determine whether Γ is necessarily pure for every choice of σ ≤ π.

status_search_result: The question appears in a survey of open problems on permutation patterns. Subsequent work on the Möbius function of the permutation poset (e.g., topological-decomposition formulas and results for permutations with one descent) has refined understanding of μ on these intervals, but no source located confirms a resolution of the purity question for the nonzero-Möbius induced subcomplex.

original_question: If a permutation σ occurs precisely once in a permutation π and the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] is μ(σ, π) = ±1, determine whether the order complex Δ(σ, π) must be homotopy equivalent to a sphere.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the set of all finite permutations, partially ordered by pattern containment: for permutations $\sigma$ and $\pi$, write $\sigma \le \pi$ if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ (where $k$ is the length of $\sigma$ and $n$ is the length of $\pi$) such that the subsequence $\pi(i_1)\pi(i_2)\cdots\pi(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\sigma$ (i.e., its entries are in the same relative order as those of $\sigma$). Each such subsequence is called an occurrence of $\sigma$ in $\pi$.

For $\sigma \le \pi$, let $[\sigma,\pi] = \{\tau \in S : \sigma \le \tau \le \pi\}$ denote the closed interval, and let $(\sigma,\pi)$ denote the corresponding open interval. Let $\mu(\sigma,\pi)$ be the Möbius function of the poset $S$ on $[\sigma,\pi]$, defined recursively by $\mu(\sigma,\sigma)=1$ and $\mu(\sigma,\pi) = -\sum_{\sigma \le \tau < \pi}\mu(\sigma,\tau)$ for $\sigma < \pi$. Let $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ denote the order complex of $(\sigma,\pi)$, i.e., the abstract simplicial complex whose simplices are the chains $\tau_0 < \tau_1 < \cdots < \tau_r$ with each $\tau_j \in (\sigma,\pi)$.

Question: Suppose $\sigma$ occurs precisely once in $\pi$ (i.e., there is a unique choice of indices realizing $\sigma$ as a pattern in $\pi$) and $\mu(\sigma,\pi) = \pm 1$. Must the order complex $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ be homotopy equivalent to a sphere?
status_search_result: The question appears in the line of research on the topology of the permutation pattern poset initiated by McNamara–Steingrímsson and Steingrímsson–Tenner. Subsequent work (e.g. Smith on permutations with one descent; Marchant and others on vincular/general pattern posets) has produced partial results — including sphere/wedge-of-spheres homotopy types for special classes (separable, layered, decomposable permutations, certain single-occurrence cases) — but no source located confirms a full resolution of the general single-occurrence question with $\mu(\sigma,\pi)=\pm1$. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) associated with the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset is shellable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S = \bigcup_{n \ge 1} S_n$ denote the set of all finite permutations, where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For $\sigma \in S_k$ and $\pi \in S_n$ with $k \le n$, say that $\pi$ contains $\sigma$ as a pattern, written $\sigma \le \pi$, if there exist indices $1 \le i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \le n$ such that the sequence $\pi(i_1), \pi(i_2), \dots, \pi(i_k)$ is order-isomorphic to $\sigma(1), \sigma(2), \dots, \sigma(k)$ (i.e., $\pi(i_a) < \pi(i_b)$ if and only if $\sigma(a) < \sigma(b)$). The relation $\le$ makes $S$ into a poset, the permutation pattern poset.
 
For $\sigma \le \pi$ in this poset, let $[\sigma,\pi] = \{\tau \in S : \sigma \le \tau \le \pi\}$ be the closed interval, and let $(\sigma,\pi) = [\sigma,\pi] \setminus \{\sigma,\pi\}$ be the open interval. The order complex $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ is the abstract simplicial complex whose faces are the chains $\sigma < \tau_1 < \tau_2 < \cdots < \tau_r < \pi$ in $(\sigma,\pi)$.
 
Recall that a pure simplicial complex is shellable if its facets can be ordered $F_1, F_2, \dots, F_t$ so that for every $i \ge 2$, the intersection $F_i \cap (F_1 \cup \cdots \cup F_{i-1})$ is a nonempty union of facets of the boundary of $F_i$ (and an analogous notion exists in the non-pure case).
 
Determine, in terms of combinatorial properties of $\sigma$ and $\pi$, exactly which pairs $\sigma \le \pi$ have the property that the order complex $\Delta(\sigma,\pi)$ is shellable.
status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing shellability of intervals in the permutation pattern poset remains open. Partial results are known: McNamara and Steingrímsson (2015) showed that almost all open intervals contain disconnected rank-≥3 subintervals and hence are not shellable, while for intervals of layered permutations the absence of nontrivial disconnected subintervals is equivalent to shellability. Sagan and Vatter, and later work by Smith and others, established shellability for further classes (e.g., intervals of permutations with a fixed number of descents). No complete characterization for arbitrary σ, π has been published.

original_question: Prove a general finite-check theorem for linear combinations of vincular patterns: if two such combinations have the same distribution on permutations of all lengths up to some bound depending only on the pattern lengths involved, then they have the same distribution for all lengths.
self_contained_problem:
A vincular (or generalized/dashed) pattern of length k is a permutation π = π₁π₂…π_k of {1,…,k} together with a specified subset of the adjacencies {(i,i+1) : 1 ≤ i ≤ k−1} declared "tight." An occurrence of such a vincular pattern in a permutation σ ∈ S_n is a sequence of indices 1 ≤ j₁ < j₂ < … < j_k ≤ n such that the values σ(j₁), σ(j₂), …, σ(j_k) are in the same relative order as π₁,…,π_k, and for every tight adjacency (i,i+1) one has j_{i+1} = j_i + 1. Write (π;σ) for the number of occurrences of the vincular pattern π in σ.

Given a finite formal linear combination P = Σ_i c_i π^{(i)} of vincular patterns (with rational coefficients), define the statistic (P;σ) = Σ_i c_i (π^{(i)};σ), and say two such combinations P and Q are equidistributed on S_n if the multisets {(P;σ) : σ ∈ S_n} and {(Q;σ) : σ ∈ S_n} coincide.

Problem. Establish (or refute) the following finite-check principle: there exists an explicit function N(k), depending only on the maximum length k of the vincular patterns appearing in P and Q (and on the number of patterns involved), such that if P and Q are equidistributed on S_n for every n ≤ N(k), then P and Q are equidistributed on S_n for every positive integer n.
status_search_result: No general finite-verification theorem for equidistribution of linear combinations of vincular patterns appears in the literature. Recent work (e.g., trivariate symmetries of vincular patterns, 2025, and length-three classifications) addresses individual equidistribution results case-by-case via bijections, generating functions, or continued fractions, but no source provides a uniform finite bound N(k) reducing equidistribution to a finite check. The question appears to remain open.

original_question: Determine whether the ring of functions generated by vincular patterns has algebraic relations beyond the known upgrading relation, and if so describe those additional relations.
self_contained_problem:
A vincular pattern is a permutation pattern $\sigma$ of length $k$ together with a specification of which adjacent positions in $\sigma$ must correspond to adjacent positions in any occurrence; equivalently, $\sigma$ is written with possible "dashes" between consecutive entries, where the absence of a dash forces adjacency. For a permutation $\pi \in S_n$, let $(\sigma)(\pi)$ denote the number of occurrences of the vincular pattern $\sigma$ in $\pi$. Each vincular pattern $\sigma$ thus defines a function from finite permutations to nonnegative integers, and the pointwise product of two such functions is again such a function. Let $R$ be the commutative ring (with unity) generated, under pointwise addition and multiplication, by all functions of the form $(\sigma)$ as $\sigma$ ranges over all vincular patterns.

There is a known family of "upgrading" identities in $R$: for any vincular pattern $\sigma$ and any internal dash, the function counting $\sigma$ equals the sum of the functions obtained by replacing that dash with the various ways of forcing or relaxing adjacency, encoding inclusion–exclusion among adjacency constraints.

Determine whether the ring $R$ admits algebraic relations among the generating functions $\{(\sigma)\}$ that are not consequences of the upgrading relations, and if so, give an explicit description of a complete set of additional generating relations.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any sources addressing the algebraic structure of the ring generated by vincular pattern functions or any further relations beyond the upgrading relation. No follow-up work resolving the question could be verified, so the status remains unknown.

original_question: For an arbitrary permutation class C, determine whether the growth-rate definition gr(C) = lim sup_{n->infinity} |C_n|^(1/n) can always be strengthened by replacing the lim sup with an actual limit.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation class is a set C of permutations (across all finite lengths) closed under taking pattern subpermutations: if σ ∈ C and τ is a pattern of σ, then τ ∈ C. For each n ≥ 0 let C_n denote the set of permutations in C of length n, and define the upper growth rate
  gr(C) = lim sup_{n → ∞} |C_n|^{1/n}.
For a principal class Av(β) (the class of permutations avoiding a single pattern β), Arratia showed, using supermultiplicativity and Fekete's lemma, that the limit lim_{n → ∞} |C_n|^{1/n} exists.

Question: Does the limit
  lim_{n → ∞} |C_n|^{1/n}
exist (as an element of [0, ∞]) for every permutation class C? Equivalently, can the lim sup in the definition of gr(C) always be replaced by an honest limit?
status_search_result: The existence of the limit lim |C_n|^{1/n} for an arbitrary permutation class C remains an open problem. Arratia (1999) established existence for sum-closed classes (in particular all principal classes Av(β)) via Fekete's lemma. More recent work by Bevan, Vatter, and others on growth rates of permutation classes (e.g., the 2018–2020 papers categorizing growth rates up to the uncountability threshold) treats gr(C) as a lim sup and lists the question of whether the limit always exists as a standing open problem in surveys/problem lists on permutation patterns.

original_question: Determine whether the conjectures of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes, despite being false in full generality.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation class is a set of permutations closed under taking subpermutations (pattern containment): if σ ∈ C and τ is a pattern of σ, then τ ∈ C. For a permutation class C, let C_n denote the set of permutations of length n in C, and define the upper growth rate
  gr(C) = limsup_{n→∞} |C_n|^{1/n}.
A class C is finitely based if there is a finite set B of permutations such that C consists of exactly those permutations that avoid every pattern in B.

Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris formulated conjectures asserting strong structural restrictions on the possible growth rates of permutation classes (in particular, that below certain thresholds the set of attainable growth rates is well-ordered, with specific algebraic numbers as the only accumulation points from above). These conjectures are known to be false for general permutation classes.

Question: Do these conjectures on the structure of the set of growth rates become true when restricted to finitely based permutation classes? That is, when one restricts attention to growth rates of permutation classes defined by avoidance of a finite set of patterns, do the predicted well-ordering and accumulation properties hold?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Pantone and Vatter ("Growth Rates of Permutation Classes: Categorization up to the Uncountability Threshold," Israel J. Math., 2020; arXiv:1605.04297) refuted the suggestion that the Balogh–Bollobás–Morris conjectures hold even for finitely based permutation classes: they exhibit an algebraic number ξ ≈ 2.30522 that is an accumulation point from above of growth rates of finitely based permutation classes, contradicting the proposed restriction.

original_question: Characterize the possible growth rates of permutation classes in the interval between κ ≈ 2.21 and λ ≈ 2.48, where κ is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of growth rates and λ is the threshold above which every real number occurs as a growth rate of some permutation class.
self_contained_problem:
A permutation class is a set $\mathcal{C}$ of finite permutations that is closed under the pattern containment order (if $\sigma \in \mathcal{C}$ and $	au$ is a pattern of $\sigma$, then $	au \in \mathcal{C}$). For each $n \geq 1$, let $c_n = |\mathcal{C} \cap S_n|$ denote the number of permutations of length $n$ in $\mathcal{C}$. The (upper) growth rate of $\mathcal{C}$ is defined as
$$\mathrm{gr}(\mathcal{C}) = \limsup_{n 	o \infty} c_n^{1/n}.$$
Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote the set of all real numbers that arise as growth rates of permutation classes. It is known that:
(i) every real number $\lambda \geq \lambda^* \approx 2.48188$ (the unique real root of $x^5 - 2x^4 - 2x^2 - 2x - 1$) belongs to $\mathcal{G}$;
(ii) there exists a value $\kappa \approx 2.20557$ such that the set of accumulation points of $\mathcal{G} \cap [0,\kappa]$ is well-understood, and $\kappa$ is the least accumulation point of accumulation points of $\mathcal{G}$.

Problem: Characterize the set $\mathcal{G} \cap (\kappa, \lambda^*)$. That is, determine precisely which real numbers in the open interval $(\kappa, \lambda^*) \approx (2.20557, 2.48188)$ occur as growth rates of permutation classes.
status_search_result: The problem has seen substantial partial progress but is not fully resolved. Bevan (2018, Combinatorica) proved that every real number at least $\lambda_B \approx 2.35698$ (root of $x^8 - 2x^7 - x^5 - x^4 - 2x^3 - 2x^2 - x - 1$) is a growth rate, and exhibited an infinite sequence of intervals of growth rates with infimum $\theta_B \approx 2.35526$, refuting an earlier conjecture that the set of growth rates below $\lambda^*$ is nowhere dense. Pantone and Vatter (Israel J. Math., 2020) further categorized growth rates up to the uncountability threshold $\xi \approx 2.30522$. A complete characterization on the full interval $(\kappa, \lambda^*)$ remains open.
