original_question:
Fix d in {2, 3}, let v_0 in H^1(R^d) be initial data for the cubic focusing NLS that produce a finite-time blow-up solution v at time T > 0, and let v_epsilon be the solution of the regularized equation

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + f(epsilon^r |v|^2)) |v|^2 v = 0

with the same initial data. What is the limiting behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon tends to 0 for times t > T, that is, after the blow-up time of the unregularized cubic NLS has already passed?
self_contained_problem:
Fix the spatial dimension $d \in \{2,3\}$. Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\partial_t v + \Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0, \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R}^d, \tag{1}$$
with initial datum $v_0 \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ chosen so that the resulting solution $v$ blows up in finite time $T>0$ in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Let $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a fixed smooth saturating function with $f(0)=0$, $f(s)\to -1$ as $s\to\infty$ (so that $1+f(\varepsilon^r|v|^2)\to 1$ pointwise as $\varepsilon\to 0$ for each fixed $v$, and $1+f(\varepsilon^r|v|^2)$ remains bounded for all $v$), and let $r>0$ be a fixed exponent. For each $\varepsilon>0$ let $v_\varepsilon$ be the global-in-time solution of the regularized equation
$$ i\partial_t v_\varepsilon + \Delta v_\varepsilon + \bigl(1 + f(\varepsilon^r |v_\varepsilon|^2)\bigr)|v_\varepsilon|^2 v_\varepsilon = 0, \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R}^d, \tag{2}$$
with the same initial datum $v_\varepsilon(0,\cdot)=v_0$. (When $d=2$ this corresponds to the no-GVD setting; when $d=3$ to the anomalous-GVD setting.)

Determine the limiting behavior of $v_\varepsilon(t,\cdot)$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$ for times $t>T$, i.e., describe in what sense (and to what limit, if any) $v_\varepsilon(t)$ converges after the blow-up time $T$ of the unregularized cubic NLS (1).
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work that resolves the post-blow-up ($t>T$) behavior of the saturation-regularized focusing cubic NLS solutions $v_\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ in dimensions $d=2,3$. Related work treats blow-up itself or cubic-quintic/saturated NLS approximations up to and near the blow-up time, but the post-blow-up limit appears not to have been characterized. Status thus appears open.

original_question:
Consider the ionization-coupled variants of the focusing cubic NLS used for laser filamentation, namely the fixed-frame system

 i(partial_t + c_g partial_z)u + epsilon(Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)u + epsilon(|u|^2 - rho)u = -i epsilon c(alpha_4 |u|^{2K-2}u + alpha_5 rho u),
 partial_t rho = epsilon alpha_4 |u|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho |u|^2,

and the moving-frame version

 i partial_tau v + (Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)v + (|v|^2 - rho_tilde)v = -i c(alpha_4 |v|^{2K-2}v + alpha_5 rho_tilde v),
 -c_g partial_z rho_tilde = epsilon alpha_4 |v|^{2K} + epsilon alpha_5 rho_tilde |v|^2,

where the paper prescribes the boundary condition lim_{z -> +infinity} (nabla_perp)^l rho_tilde(tau, X_perp, z) = 0 for all l >= 0. Can one prove that solutions of these ionization models are global in dimensions 2 and 3, so that ionization really prevents finite-time collapse?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and write the spatial variable as $(X_\perp,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{d-1}\times\mathbb{R}$, where $\nabla_\perp$ and $\Delta_\perp$ denote the gradient and Laplacian in the transverse variable $X_\perp$. Fix real parameters $\varepsilon>0$, $c_g\in\mathbb{R}$, $c>0$, $\alpha_1\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha_4\ge 0$, $\alpha_5\ge 0$ and an integer $K\ge 2$. Consider the following two coupled systems for a complex-valued envelope and a nonnegative scalar density.

Fixed-frame system, for $u=u(t,X_\perp,z)\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\rho=\rho(t,X_\perp,z)\ge 0$:
$$ i(\partial_t + c_g\partial_z)u + \varepsilon(\Delta_\perp + \alpha_1\partial_z^2)u + \varepsilon(|u|^2-\rho)u = -i\varepsilon c\bigl(\alpha_4|u|^{2K-2}u + \alpha_5\rho u\bigr), $$
$$ \partial_t\rho = \varepsilon\alpha_4|u|^{2K} + \varepsilon\alpha_5\rho|u|^2, $$
with initial data $u|_{t=0}=u_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $s$ large enough and $\rho|_{t=0}=0$.

Moving-frame system, for $v=v(\tau,X_\perp,z)\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\tilde\rho=\tilde\rho(\tau,X_\perp,z)\ge 0$:
$$ i\partial_\tau v + (\Delta_\perp+\alpha_1\partial_z^2)v + (|v|^2-\tilde\rho)v = -ic\bigl(\alpha_4|v|^{2K-2}v + \alpha_5\tilde\rho v\bigr), $$
$$ -c_g\partial_z\tilde\rho = \varepsilon\alpha_4|v|^{2K} + \varepsilon\alpha_5\tilde\rho|v|^2, $$
together with the boundary condition
$$ \lim_{z\to+\infty}(\nabla_\perp)^l\tilde\rho(\tau,X_\perp,z)=0,\qquad\forall l\ge 0. $$

Prove or disprove: for every sufficiently smooth, decaying initial datum, the Cauchy problem for each of the two systems above admits a unique global-in-time solution (i.e., no finite-time blow-up of $\|u(t)\|_{H^1}$ or of $\|v(\tau)\|_{H^1}$ occurs) in spatial dimensions $d=2$ and $d=3$. original_question:
For the modified focusing cubic NLS

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_t v + Delta v + |v|^2 v = 0,

assume that the positive self-adjoint operator P_2(epsilon nabla) gives only partial off-axis regularization, meaning it controls derivatives only in some distinguished directions rather than the full H^1 norm. Can one develop both the local and the global well-posedness theory in that partial off-axis case, and in particular decide whether this partial off-axis dependence is enough to prevent finite-time breakdown of solutions that would blow up for the standard focusing cubic NLS?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the modified focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
   i P(ε∇) ∂_t v + Δ v + |v|^2 v = 0,    v: ℝ_t × ℝ^d → ℂ,
where d = 2 or d = 3, ε > 0 is a fixed parameter, and P(ε∇) is a positive self-adjoint Fourier multiplier with symbol P(εξ) (ξ ∈ ℝ^d) satisfying the partial off-axis coercivity estimate
   (P(ε∇) v, v)_{L^2} ≳ ‖v‖_{L^2}^2 + ε^2 Σ_{k=1}^{j} ‖ v_k · ∇ v ‖_{L^2}^2,
for fixed unit vectors v_1, …, v_j ∈ ℝ^d, with j = 1 when d = 2, and j ∈ {1, 2} when d = 3, so that the right-hand side does not control the full H^1 norm of v (i.e. derivatives are controlled only along a proper subset of directions). The equation possesses formally conserved mass and a modified energy
   E(v) = ½ ‖∇ v‖_{L^2}^2 − ¼ ‖v‖_{L^4}^4.

(a) Develop a local well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem associated with this equation in a natural function space adapted to the partial off-axis regularization provided by P(ε∇).

(b) Develop a global well-posedness theory using the available conserved quantities.

(c) Decide whether the partial off-axis dependence is sufficient to prevent finite-time blow-up of solutions; that is, determine whether all (or a large class of) sufficiently regular solutions extend globally in time, in contrast to the standard focusing cubic NLS (P ≡ 1), for which finite-time blow-up occurs for a large class of initial data in dimensions d = 2, 3.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed the partial off-axis case: a SIAM J. Math. Anal. paper "Regularizing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations Through Partial Off-axis Variations" establishes local and global well-posedness for cubic-type focusing NLS with only partial off-axis regularization, showing that the partial off-axis dependence yields a regularizing mechanism preventing the standard focusing-NLS finite-time blow-up in supercritical regimes. This indicates the open problem has been resolved affirmatively.

original_question:
For the self-steepening model

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon alpha_3 . nabla)(|v|^2 v) = 0

in dimension 2 for no group velocity dispersion or dimension 3 for anomalous group velocity dispersion, how can the finite-time blow-up solutions behave? In particular, can one rigorously describe the blow-up scenarios, including whether solutions can develop the shock-like profiles that the paper associates with optical self-steepening?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the self-steepening modification of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$i\,\partial_t v + \Delta v + (1 + i\varepsilon\, \alpha_3 \cdot \nabla)\bigl(|v|^2 v\bigr) = 0,$$
where $v : [0,T) \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$, $\varepsilon > 0$ is a small parameter, $\alpha_3 \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a fixed nonzero vector (a distinguished "propagation" direction), and the spatial dimension is either $d = 2$ (the case modeling absence of group velocity dispersion) or $d = 3$ (the case of anomalous group velocity dispersion). The Laplacian and gradient act on the spatial variables $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.

Provide a rigorous description of the possible finite-time blow-up scenarios for solutions of this equation. In particular:

1. Classify the dynamical behaviors (e.g.\ blow-up rates, concentration profiles, stability, universality classes) of solutions $v(t,x)$ that develop a singularity at some finite time $T^* < \infty$, in the sense that $\limsup_{t \to T^*} \|v(t,\cdot)\|_{H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} = \infty$.

2. Determine whether there exist initial data leading to solutions whose corresponding profile develops a shock-like singularity (i.e.\ the gradient of an appropriately rescaled amplitude/phase profile blows up while the amplitude remains bounded, mimicking optical self-steepening shock formation), and if so, construct such solutions and describe the associated shock formation mechanism.
status_search_result: A web search did not return any rigorous results describing blow-up scenarios or shock formation for this self-steepening NLS model. Available literature on self-steepening solitons and supercritical NLS blow-up (Merle–Raphaël–Rodnianski–Szeftel and related works) addresses different equations, and no construction of shock-developing blow-up solutions for this specific equation was located. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question:
For the hyperbolic or non-elliptic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0

in dimensions 2 and 3, can one prove that every H^1 solution is global, despite the lack of the standard elliptic structure of the usual focusing cubic NLS?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the hyperbolic (non-elliptic) cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
  i ∂_t v + (Δ_⊥ − ∂_z^2) v + |v|^2 v = 0,
where v = v(t, x_⊥, z) is a complex-valued function with (x_⊥, z) ∈ R^{d−1} × R and d ∈ {2, 3}. Here Δ_⊥ denotes the Laplacian in the transverse variables x_⊥ (in dimension d = 2, x_⊥ ∈ R and Δ_⊥ = ∂_{x}^2; in dimension d = 3, x_⊥ ∈ R^2 and Δ_⊥ = ∂_{x_1}^2 + ∂_{x_2}^2), so that the spatial operator Δ_⊥ − ∂_z^2 is of mixed (indefinite, hyperbolic) signature rather than elliptic. The equation is locally well-posed in H^1(R^d) and conserves the mass ∫|v|^2 dx and the (indefinite) energy
  E(v) = (1/2) ∫(|∇_⊥ v|^2 − |∂_z v|^2) dx − (1/4) ∫|v|^4 dx.
Because of the indefinite sign of the quadratic part of the energy, the standard variational/coercivity argument that yields global existence for the elliptic defocusing cubic NLS, and the Glassey-type virial obstruction for the elliptic focusing cubic NLS, do not apply directly.

Problem: Prove that for every initial datum v(0, ·) ∈ H^1(R^d) (with d = 2 or d = 3), the corresponding solution v of the above hyperbolic cubic NLS exists globally in time in H^1, i.e. no finite-time blow-up (whether by pulse splitting or any other mechanism) occurs.
status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on the hyperbolic (non-elliptic) cubic NLS in two and three dimensions, including recent well-posedness results on T^2 and analyses of radial standing/self-similar waves, but no source establishes global existence in H^1 on R^2 or R^3 for the hyperbolic cubic NLS. The problem of ruling out finite-time blow-up in this setting appears to remain open.

original_question:
For the hyperbolic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0,

can one rigorously prove and describe the pulse-splitting phenomenon seen in simulations, where a concentrating pulse reaches a threshold and then separates into lower-amplitude pulses moving apart instead of forming a singularity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the hyperbolic cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in dimension d = d_⊥ + 1, for a complex-valued function v(t, x_⊥, z) with t ∈ ℝ, x_⊥ ∈ ℝ^{d_⊥}, z ∈ ℝ:

   i ∂_t v + (Δ_⊥ − ∂_z^2) v + |v|^2 v = 0,

where Δ_⊥ = Σ_{j=1}^{d_⊥} ∂_{x_j}^2 denotes the Laplacian in the transverse variables x_⊥, and the dispersive operator Δ_⊥ − ∂_z^2 has indefinite (hyperbolic) signature.

Numerical simulations of this equation reveal a "pulse-splitting" phenomenon: starting from suitable focusing initial data, the solution concentrates and its amplitude grows until it reaches a certain threshold, after which, instead of forming a finite-time singularity, the pulse splits into two pulses of smaller amplitude that move away from each other.

Provide a rigorous mathematical description and proof of this pulse-splitting phenomenon. Specifically:
(a) Identify a class of initial data v(0, ·) for which the solution exhibits pulse splitting.
(b) Define rigorously what is meant by pulse splitting (e.g., describe the asymptotic profile, the threshold amplitude, the locations and velocities of the emerging pulses, and the regime of validity).
(c) Prove that for such initial data the solution is global in time and decomposes asymptotically (in a suitable norm) into at least two separating localized pulses, ruling out finite-time blow-up in this regime.
status_search_result: Available literature indicates that pulse splitting in the hyperbolic cubic NLS is observed in numerical simulations, but no rigorous proof or description of the phenomenon (including global existence vs. blow-up for large data in the relevant regime) is known. Recent surveys and works on hyperbolic NLS confirm that questions about large-data dynamics in this equation remain open.

original_question:
When partial off-axis variation of the group velocity and longitudinal self-steepening are both present in the same direction, namely for

 i(1 - epsilon^2 partial_z^2) partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + i epsilon partial_z)(|v|^2 v) = 0,

do solutions still exhibit self-steepening, or does the off-axis regularization suppress or qualitatively change that shock-like steepening effect?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\varepsilon>0$ be a small parameter, and consider a complex-valued function $v=v(t,z,x_\perp)$ with $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $z\in\mathbb{R}$, and $x_\perp\in\mathbb{R}^{d-1}$ (with $d\in\{2,3\}$ the physically relevant cases). Let $\Delta=\partial_z^2+\Delta_{x_\perp}$ denote the full spatial Laplacian (or, in the partial off-axis context, write $\Delta v$ for the standard Laplacian acting on $v$). Consider the modified focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation combining a partial off-axis regularization of the group velocity with a longitudinal self-steepening term, both acting along the propagation direction $z$:
$$ i\bigl(1-\varepsilon^2\partial_z^2\bigr)\partial_t v \;+\; \Delta v \;+\; \bigl(1+i\varepsilon\partial_z\bigr)\bigl(|v|^2 v\bigr) \;=\; 0. $$
The classical NLS with self-steepening term $i\varepsilon\partial_z(|v|^2 v)$ is known to produce a shock-like steepening of the pulse profile in $z$ (formation of large gradients in finite time). The off-axis operator $1-\varepsilon^2\partial_z^2$ on the left-hand side acts as a regularization of the time derivative.

Question: Do solutions of the above equation still exhibit self-steepening (the formation of shock-like longitudinal gradients), or does the partial off-axis regularization of the group velocity suppress or qualitatively alter this steepening phenomenon? Specifically, determine whether there exist smooth, suitably localized initial data $v(0,\cdot)$ for which $\|\partial_z v(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty}$ becomes arbitrarily large in finite time, or prove that the off-axis term enforces a uniform bound preventing such steepening.
status_search_result: The equation appears as an open problem in a survey on variants of the focusing NLS equation related to laser filamentation. No subsequent work directly resolving whether solutions to this combined off-axis/self-steepening NLS variant exhibit self-steepening was located; related works treat self-steepening or off-axis regularization separately rather than the combined equation.

original_question: The paper rigorously derives several NLS-type asymptotic models from Maxwell's equations and justifies them on times of order T/epsilon only while the approximating NLS-type solution stays bounded, which in the standard focusing case means times strictly before the focusing time T_foc. Can one rigorously justify at least one of these derived NLS-type models on a time interval [0, T/epsilon] with T greater than or equal to the focusing time T_foc, so that the approximation remains valid in the regime where the different models begin to differ in a physically meaningful way?
self_contained_problem:
Consider Maxwell's equations in a nonlinear isotropic dielectric medium in $\mathbb{R}^3$,
$$\partial_t D = \nabla \times H, \qquad \partial_t B = -\nabla \times E, \qquad \nabla\cdot B = 0,\ \nabla\cdot D = 0,$$
with constitutive laws $B = \mu_0 H$ and $D = \varepsilon_0 E + P(E)$, where the polarization $P(E)$ has a linear part with susceptibility kernel giving rise to a smooth dispersion relation $\omega = \omega(k)$ and a cubic instantaneous nonlinear part of Kerr type. Let $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$ be a small parameter measuring the ratio of the wavelength to the typical longitudinal scale of the envelope, and let
$$E_{\mathrm{NLS}}^\varepsilon(t,x) = \varepsilon\, A(\varepsilon t,\varepsilon(x_\parallel - v_g t),\varepsilon^{1/2} x_\perp)\, e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega(k)t)/\varepsilon} + \mathrm{c.c.}$$
denote a quasi-monochromatic wave packet ansatz, where the slowly varying complex envelope $A(\tau,X)$ satisfies a focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (or one of its standard variants: full-dispersion NLS, NLS with self-steepening, NLS with mean-field coupling, off-axis NLS, etc.) of the form
$$i\partial_\tau A + \alpha\, \partial_{X_\parallel}^2 A + \beta\, \Delta_{X_\perp} A + \gamma\, |A|^2 A + (\text{lower-order corrections}) = 0,$$
with coefficients computed from $\omega$ and the cubic susceptibility, and prescribed initial data $A|_{\tau=0}=A_0\in H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for $s$ sufficiently large.

In the focusing regime, the envelope solution $A$ blows up at a finite focusing time $T_{\mathrm{foc}}\in(0,\infty)$, in the sense that $\|A(\tau)\|_{H^s}\to\infty$ as $\tau\to T_{\mathrm{foc}}^-$. Standard rigorous justification yields, for any $T<T_{\mathrm{foc}}$, an exact Maxwell solution $E^\varepsilon$ with the same initial data such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T/\varepsilon} \|E^\varepsilon(t,\cdot) - E_{\mathrm{NLS}}^\varepsilon(t,\cdot)\|_{L^\infty} \le C(T)\, \varepsilon^\theta$$
for some $\theta>0$.

Problem. For at least one such NLS-type envelope model (chosen among the variants derivable from the above Maxwell system at the relevant order), prove a rigorous justification estimate of the above type on a time interval $[0,T/\varepsilon]$ with $T\ge T_{\mathrm{foc}}$; equivalently, establish that the Maxwell solution $E^\varepsilon$ remains $o(1)$-close in a suitable norm to the chosen NLS-type envelope solution on a time scale reaching or surpassing the envelope focusing time, where the various derived variants begin to differ in a physically meaningful way.
status_search_result: A subsequent 2018 exposition by the same line of work restates the question as an open problem related to filamentation, and no later paper appears to give a rigorous justification of any NLS-type model derived from Maxwell's equations on a time interval reaching or exceeding the focusing time. Standard justification results in the literature remain confined to times strictly before envelope blow-up.

original_question: In bootstrap algebraic multigrid, how should one define a form of compatible relaxation together with a convergence-rate estimate derived from the compatible-relaxation factor rho_cr so that, for a chosen interpolation strategy, the estimate accurately predicts the performance of the resulting two-grid method?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix and consider the linear system $A\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{f}$. A two-grid algebraic multigrid method is defined by:
(i) a splitting of the index set $\{1,\dots,n\} = C \cup F$ (with $|C| = n_c$);
(ii) a smoother $M$ (with error-propagation $E_s = I - M^{-1}A$);
(iii) an interpolation operator $P \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n_c}$ with $P|_C = I$, giving the coarse-grid correction $E_c = I - P(P^T A P)^{-1} P^T A$. The two-grid error-propagation operator is $E_{TG} = E_s\, E_c\, E_s$, and its convergence rate is $\rho_{TG} := \|E_{TG}\|_A$.

Compatible relaxation (CR), as introduced by Brandt, is a relaxation scheme on the $F$-variables only, with error-propagation $E_F = I_F - M_{FF}^{-1} A_{FF}$ (or a more general $F$-restricted iteration). Its asymptotic convergence factor is
$$\rho_{cr} := \lim_{k\to\infty} \|E_F^k\|^{1/k}_{A_{FF}}.$$
It is known that a small $\rho_{cr}$ is necessary for the existence of a sparse interpolation $P$ yielding a uniformly convergent two-grid method.

Problem. Construct a definition of compatible relaxation and an associated convergence-rate estimate $\Phi(\rho_{cr})$ (possibly involving auxiliary quantities determined by the smoother and the $C/F$ splitting) such that, for a prescribed interpolation strategy $\mathcal{I}$ that produces $P$ from $(A,C,F)$, the estimate sharply predicts the actual two-grid convergence rate; that is, exhibit functions $\Phi$ and a CR formulation for which
$$\rho_{TG}(A,C,F,\mathcal{I}) \approx \Phi(\rho_{cr})$$
holds with provable two-sided bounds, uniformly over a specified class of SPD matrices $A$ and admissible splittings.
status_search_result: Compatible relaxation provides necessary conditions and lower bounds for two-grid convergence, and recent work (e.g., Brannick–Cao–Kahl–Falgout–Zikatanov, 2017–2025) has produced sharper CR-type estimates and optimal-interpolation frameworks. However, deriving a CR-based estimate that sharply predicts (with matching upper and lower bounds) the two-grid convergence rate for a given practical interpolation strategy across general SPD problems remains an active research question without a definitive resolution.

original_question: How can least-squares interpolation and the bootstrap setup used to compute test vectors be combined in a way that is simultaneously optimal and robust for defining algebraic multigrid interpolation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an algebraic multigrid (AMG) framework for solving linear systems $A x = b$ with $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ a large sparse matrix (e.g., arising from a discretized PDE). In AMG one selects a set of coarse-grid degrees of freedom $\mathcal{C} \subset \{1,\dots,n\}$ together with a prolongation (interpolation) operator $P \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times |\mathcal{C}|}$ that maps coarse-grid vectors to fine-grid vectors and is used recursively to define a multilevel solver.

In the bootstrap algebraic multigrid (BAMG) approach, the rows of $P$ are determined by a weighted least-squares fit. Concretely, given a set of test vectors $\{v^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ together with positive weights $\{\omega_k\}_{k=1}^K$, the interpolation weights $(p_{ij})_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i}$ for each fine-grid point $i \notin \mathcal{C}$ (with neighboring coarse set $\mathcal{C}_i$) are defined by
$$
\min_{(p_{ij})_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i}} \sum_{k=1}^{K} \omega_k \Big( v^{(k)}_i - \sum_{j \in \mathcal{C}_i} p_{ij}\, v^{(k)}_j \Big)^2 .
$$
The test vectors $\{v^{(k)}\}$ are themselves computed by a "bootstrap" setup procedure: starting from random initial vectors, one applies relaxation to the homogeneous equation $A x = 0$, then iteratively improves the test vectors via a multilevel eigensolver applied to the current multigrid hierarchy, possibly combined with adaptive residual-based relaxation.

Problem. Devise and analyze a procedure that combines the least-squares definition of the prolongation $P$ with the bootstrap setup for generating test vectors so that the resulting interpolation operator is simultaneously:

(i) Optimal, in the sense that for an appropriate quantitative measure of two-grid (or multigrid) convergence — for example, the asymptotic convergence factor of the resulting V-cycle, or the constant in the weak approximation property
$$
\inf_{x_c} \| x - P x_c \|_{D}^2 \le C\, \langle A x, x \rangle \qquad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}^n,
$$
where $D$ is a suitable diagonal scaling — the constructed $P$ achieves (or provably approaches) the best possible value of that measure over the class of interpolation operators with the given sparsity pattern.

(ii) Robust, in the sense that the construction yields uniformly bounded multigrid convergence factors across a broad class of problems (including, e.g., scalar elliptic problems with strongly varying or anisotropic coefficients, indefinite systems, and systems of PDEs) without requiring problem-specific parameter tuning, and is stable with respect to the number, accuracy, and choice of test vectors produced by the bootstrap cycle (avoiding overfitting and degenerate least-squares systems).

Specify (a) how the test-vector set, weights, and least-squares regularization should be chosen as functions of the bootstrap iterates, (b) the precise sense in which the resulting $P$ is optimal, and (c) prove a robustness theorem giving an a priori bound on the multigrid convergence factor that depends only on natural properties of $A$ and not on problem-specific parameters.
status_search_result: The combination of least-squares interpolation with bootstrap test-vector setup remains an active area of research in algebraic multigrid. Status reports and recent works (e.g., on bootstrap AMG with operator-based interpolation, least-angle-regression coarsening, and learning-based weighted least-squares variants) continue to propose and refine such combinations, indicating the question of a simultaneously optimal and robust integration is still open and being explored, rather than definitively resolved.

original_question: For Hermitian positive definite problems, how should the compatible relaxation, algebraic distance, least-squares interpolation, test-vector generation, and related bootstrap algebraic multigrid components be integrated into a practical overall algorithm, validated on a carefully chosen and diverse collection of test problems including systems of partial differential equations, so that the method becomes a fast solver usable in practice?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the class of Hermitian positive definite (HPD) linear systems $A x = b$, where $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n	imes n}$ satisfies $A = A^*$ and $x^* A x > 0$ for all nonzero $x \in \mathbb{C}^n$. A bootstrap algebraic multigrid (BAMG) solver for such systems is built from the following components:

1. Compatible relaxation: an iterative relaxation scheme restricted to a candidate set of fine-grid variables, used to assess the quality of a coarse-variable set $C \subset \{1,\dots,n\}$ via its convergence rate.
2. Algebraic distance: a notion of strength of connection between variables derived from the smoothed behavior of test vectors, used to guide coarsening and sparsity patterns of interpolation.
3. Least-squares interpolation: for each fine variable $i 
otin C$, an interpolation operator row obtained by solving a weighted least-squares problem that fits a collection of test vectors $\{v^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K}$ on a chosen neighborhood in $C$.
4. Test-vector generation: a bootstrap process in which test vectors are produced and iteratively improved by applying the current multigrid hierarchy (e.g. via multigrid eigensolver / setup cycles) to expose algebraically smooth error.
5. Auxiliary BAMG ingredients: coarse-grid construction, choice of smoother, cycling strategy, and adaptive updating of the hierarchy.

Problem. Design a complete, practical BAMG algorithm for general HPD problems that specifies precisely how components (1)–(5) are combined, including all algorithmic parameters and stopping criteria, and prove or empirically demonstrate, on a carefully chosen and diverse collection of HPD test problems (including discretizations of scalar PDEs, anisotropic and jump-coefficient diffusion, and systems of PDEs such as elasticity and Stokes-type saddle-free reductions), that the resulting solver achieves grid-independent or nearly grid-independent convergence with optimal or near-optimal computational complexity, qualifying it as a fast solver usable in practice.
status_search_result: This is a broad research program rather than a single sharply-posed conjecture. While many BAMG components and integrated algorithms have been proposed and tested for various HPD problems, no universally validated, practical BAMG fast solver covering the full range of HPD systems (including general systems of PDEs) has been established. The problem is best classified as open / ongoing research.

original_question: For non-Hermitian problems treated with Galerkin-based algebraic multigrid, how can one correctly characterize the algebraically smooth error, or near-kernel components, that restriction and interpolation must approximate on coarse levels when small-singular-vector information can fail to describe that near kernel unless the matrix is normal?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a (possibly non-normal, non-Hermitian) invertible matrix arising from the discretization of a linear problem $Ax = b$, and consider a two-level Galerkin algebraic multigrid scheme: choose a relaxation (smoothing) iteration with error-propagation matrix $S$, and choose interpolation $P \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times m}$ and restriction $R \in \mathbb{C}^{m\times n}$ with coarse operator $A_c = R A P$, so that the coarse-grid correction operator is $T = I - P A_c^{-1} R A$ and the two-level error propagation is $E = S^{\nu_2} T S^{\nu_1}$.

Call an error vector $e$ "algebraically smooth" if relaxation reduces it slowly, i.e., $\|S e\| \approx \|e\|$. For Hermitian positive-definite $A$, algebraically smooth errors coincide with the near-kernel of $A$, namely vectors $v$ with $\|Av\|/\|v\|$ small, equivalently right singular vectors associated with small singular values; this is also equivalent for normal $A$. For general non-normal $A$, however, vectors $v$ with $\|Av\|$ small need not be slow to be reduced by typical relaxation schemes, so the small-singular-vector subspace need not describe the components that $P$ and $R$ must capture.

Problem. Provide a precise, computable characterization of the subspaces of slow-to-reduce errors of $A$ and $A^*$ under a given relaxation $S$ when $A$ is non-Hermitian and non-normal, such that:

(i) the characterization reduces to the near-kernel / small-singular-vector description in the normal case;

(ii) it identifies the right and left subspaces that the columns of $P$ and the rows of $R$ must respectively approximate in order to guarantee uniform two-level convergence, i.e., a bound $\|E\| \le \rho < 1$ independent of $n$;

(iii) it can be used as the target subspace in an adaptive/bootstrap AMG setup procedure.

Equivalently: identify the correct analogue of the "algebraically smooth error" / near-kernel for non-normal $A$ that restriction and interpolation must approximate on coarse levels in Galerkin-based AMG.
status_search_result: Several lines of work address this question. Energy-minimization interpolation strategies and generalized smoothed-aggregation setups have been extended to non-Hermitian/indefinite problems by targeting the right and left near-null-spaces of $A$ separately (so $P$ approximates right near-kernel, $R$ approximates left near-kernel). Adaptive/bootstrap AMG and reduction-based multigrid for nearly singular non-symmetric operators address the characterization in practice, and recent (2025) work explicitly studies "characterization of the near-null error components utilized in composite adaptive AMG solvers." A fully general, theoretically tight characterization that guarantees uniform convergence for arbitrary non-normal $A$ remains incomplete, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

original_question: For indefinite, non-elliptic problems such as Helmholtz and Schroedinger operators in higher dimensions, how can bootstrap algebraic multigrid be developed so that several locally orthogonal prolongation operators and the resulting multiple Galerkin coarse-grid operators are constructed efficiently, and to what extent can those techniques be extended into fast solvers for general sparse matrix equations?
self_contained_problem:
Consider linear systems Au = f arising from discretizations of indefinite, non-elliptic operators in dimension d ≥ 2, in particular the Helmholtz operator -Δ - k^2 with wavenumber k > 0 and the (real or complex) Schrödinger operator -Δ + V(x) with sign-changing or oscillatory potentials. The bootstrap algebraic multigrid (BAMG) framework constructs a hierarchy of coarse spaces by:
  (i) generating a set of test vectors that approximate the algebraically smooth (near-null-space) components of A,
  (ii) defining one or more prolongation operators P_1, …, P_m: ℝ^{n_c} → ℝ^{n_f} of small caliber (each fine point interpolated from a uniformly bounded number of coarse points),
  (iii) forming Galerkin coarse-grid operators A_c^{(j)} = P_j^T A P_j (or their complex/non-symmetric analogues), and
  (iv) recursively repeating the construction on each coarse level.

For indefinite non-elliptic problems, the algebraically smooth (near-kernel) modes are highly oscillatory plane-wave-like functions whose direction depends on local geometry, and they cannot be accurately captured by a single small-caliber prolongation on sufficiently fine scales; multiple prolongations are therefore required. To preserve optimal O(n) complexity per V-cycle, the multiple prolongations P_1, …, P_m must be locally orthogonal in the sense that, for each fine degree of freedom, the rows of the P_j associated with that point are mutually orthogonal (so that the resulting hierarchy of coarse operators stays sparse and the work per level decays geometrically).

Problem. 
(a) Devise a constructive BAMG algorithm for indefinite, non-elliptic problems (Helmholtz and Schrödinger in d ≥ 2) that produces several locally orthogonal small-caliber prolongation operators P_1, …, P_m together with their Galerkin coarse-grid operators A_c^{(j)}, with total setup and per-cycle cost that is provably linear (or quasi-linear) in the number of unknowns, and prove that the resulting multilevel iteration converges with a contraction factor bounded independently of the mesh size h and (ideally) the wavenumber k or potential V.
(b) Determine to what extent such a multiple-prolongation, locally orthogonal BAMG construction can be developed into a fast (linear or quasi-linear complexity) solver for general sparse matrix equations Au = f, identifying structural conditions on A under which uniform convergence and optimal complexity hold.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2024–2025 SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing paper "Toward an Algebraic Multigrid Method for the Indefinite Helmholtz Equation" and the 2023 preprint "Stand-alone multigrid for Helmholtz revisited") explicitly states that designing a robust, optimal-complexity AMG (including bootstrap-style approaches with multiple coarse spaces) for indefinite Helmholtz/Schrödinger problems remains an open challenge, and that extending such ideas to general sparse systems is not yet achieved. The problem is therefore still open, with active partial progress.

original_question: Determine the exact asymptotic growth of D(n), where D(n) is the minimum number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by an n-point set in the plane.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of $P$, i.e.,
$$D(P) = \bigl|\{\,\|p-q\| : p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}\bigr|.$$
Define
$$D(n) = \min_{\substack{P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\\ |P|=n}} D(P),$$
the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an $n$-point planar set. Determine the exact asymptotic growth rate of $D(n)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, close the gap between the known lower bound $D(n)=\Omega(n/\log n)$ and the known upper bound $D(n)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ achieved by a $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ section of the integer lattice.
status_search_result: The Erdős distinct distances problem in the plane remains open. Guth and Katz (2015) established the lower bound $D(n)=\Omega(n/\log n)$, while Erdős's $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ lattice gives $D(n)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$. The exact asymptotic (in particular, whether the upper bound is tight) is still unresolved.

original_question: Characterize the planar n-point sets P with D(P) = O(n/sqrt(log n)), meaning sets that span a near-optimal number of distinct distances up to the currently best known order of magnitude.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let
$$D(P)=|\{\,\|p-q\|:p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}|$$
denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by $P$. It is known (Guth–Katz) that every $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfies $D(P)=\Omega(n/\log n)$, and the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ integer grid shows $D(P)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ is achievable. Call an $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ near-optimal if
$$D(P)=O\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}\right).$$
Give a structural characterization of all near-optimal planar point sets: describe the geometric and combinatorial properties (e.g., distribution along lines, circles, lattice-like structure) that an $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ must possess in order to satisfy $D(P)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$.
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing near-optimal planar point sets (those with D(P)=O(n/√log n)) remains open. Partial structural results are known: Sheffer, Zahl, and de Zeeuw and subsequent works show that in any near-optimal set, no line contains more than O(n^{43/52}) points and no circle contains more than O(n^{5/6}) points. Recent work (e.g., on forbidden 4-point patterns) continues to investigate constraints on such sets, but no full characterization has been obtained.

original_question: Prove or disprove that, for some sufficiently small epsilon > 0, every near-optimal planar n-point set contains at least Omega(n^epsilon) points on a single line.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of $n$ points in the plane, let $d(P)$ denote the number of distinct distances determined by $P$, i.e. the cardinality of $\{\,\|p-q\|:p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}$. It is known (Guth–Katz) that $\min_{|P|=n} d(P)=\Theta(n/\sqrt{\log n})$. Call a sequence of planar point sets $(P_n)_{n\ge 1}$ with $|P_n|=n$ near-optimal if $d(P_n)=O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, i.e. the number of distinct distances is within a constant factor of the minimum possible.

Prove or disprove the following: there exists a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every near-optimal sequence $(P_n)$ has the property that, for all sufficiently large $n$, the set $P_n$ contains $\Omega(n^{\varepsilon})$ points lying on a single line.
status_search_result: This is a well-known open question of Erdős concerning the structure of near-optimal sets for the distinct distances problem. Even after the Guth–Katz resolution of the main distinct-distances bound in the plane, this structural weakening — whether near-optimal sets must contain Ω(n^ε) collinear points for some fixed ε>0 — remains unresolved according to surveys on the Erdős distance problem.

original_question: Prove or disprove that for every near-optimal planar n-point set P and every epsilon > 0, every constant-degree algebraic curve contains at most O(n^(0.5+epsilon)) points of P.
self_contained_problem: For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of $n$ points, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of $P$. Call a sequence of planar point sets $\{P_n\}$ with $|P_n|=n$ near-optimal if $D(P_n) = O\!\left(n/\sqrt{\log n}\right)$, i.e., it matches (up to constants) the lower bound of Guth–Katz on the minimum number of distinct distances determined by $n$ points in the plane.\n\nProve or disprove the following: for every near-optimal planar $n$-point set $P$, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every algebraic curve $\gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of degree at most a fixed constant $c$ (independent of $n$), the number of points of $P$ lying on $\gamma$ is at most $O_{c,\varepsilon}\!\left(n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\right)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the distinct-distances literature. The best published bound for points of a near-optimal set on a constant-degree algebraic curve is $O(n^{43/52})$, far from the conjectured $O(n^{1/2+\varepsilon})$. Web searches reveal no announcement of a resolution; subsequent work refines special cases (lines, circles) but does not settle the general constant-degree curve case.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dcurve(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by n points lying on a constant-degree algebraic curve in the plane when the curve contains neither a line nor a circle.
self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $D_{\mathrm{curve}}(n)$ denote the minimum, over all irreducible algebraic curves $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of degree at most some fixed constant and all sets $P$ of $n$ distinct points lying on $\gamma$, of the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\|_2 : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\,\}$, taken under the restriction that $\gamma$ contains no straight line and no circle. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $D_{\mathrm{curve}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: A lower bound of $\Omega(n^{4/3})$ was established by Pach and de Zeeuw for points on a constant-degree planar algebraic curve that contains neither a line nor a circle. original_question: Find the exact value of Dno3l(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set with no three collinear points.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, let $D(P) = |\{\,\|p-q\| : p,q \in P,\; p\neq q\,\}|$ denote the number of distinct pairwise distances determined by $P$. Define
$$D_{\mathrm{no3\ell}}(n) = \min\{\,D(P) : P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ \text{no three points of }P\text{ are collinear}\,\}.$$
Determine the exact value of $D_{\mathrm{no3\ell}}(n)$ for every integer $n\geq 3$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact value, or even the asymptotic order, of the minimum number of distinct distances among n planar points with no three collinear is listed as an open problem in surveys of the Erdős-style distinct distances literature. No matching exact formula has been established; only partial bounds are known.

original_question: Find the exact value of Dhat_conv(n), where Dhat_conv(n) is the largest number such that every set of n points in strict convex position contains a point whose distances to the other n-1 points realize at least Dhat_conv(n) distinct values.
self_contained_problem:
A finite set $P$ of $n\ge 3$ points in the Euclidean plane is said to be in strict convex position if the points are the vertices of a convex polygon (no three collinear). For such a set $P$ and a point $p\in P$, let $d(p,P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\|:q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}$. Define
$$\widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n)=\min_{P}\;\max_{p\in P} d(p,P),$$
where the minimum is over all $n$-point sets $P$ in strict convex position in the plane. Equivalently, $\widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n)$ is the largest integer $k$ such that every $n$-point set in strict convex position contains a point that determines at least $k$ distinct distances to the remaining $n-1$ points.

Determine the exact value of $\widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n)$ for every $n$.
status_search_result: The problem is a classical Erdős-type question (Erdős conjectured in 1946 that the value is at least ⌊n/2⌋). The best known lower bound is approximately (13/36 + 1/22701)n + O(1) due to Nivasch–Pach–Pinchasi–Zerbib, improving Dumitrescu's ⌈(13n−6)/36⌉ bound (2006). The exact value remains undetermined, so the problem is open.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dgen(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in general position, meaning no three points are collinear and no four points are cocircular.
self_contained_problem:
A finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is said to be in general position if no three points of $P$ are collinear and no four points of $P$ lie on a common circle. For a finite point set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let
$$D(P)=\bigl|\{\,\|p-q\|:p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}\bigr|$$
denote the number of distinct pairwise Euclidean distances determined by $P$. Define
$$D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)=\min\bigl\{D(P):P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ P\text{ in general position}\bigr\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $D_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. The general Erdős distinct-distances problem was settled asymptotically by Guth and Katz with a lower bound of order $n/\log n$, which also applies to general-position sets. Known constructions for sets in general position (e.g., parabola-mod-p and projection-from-hypersphere constructions) yield only upper bounds of the form $n\cdot 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$, leaving a gap. original_question: Derive non-trivial lower or upper bounds for distinct distances determined by points constrained to algebraic varieties in R^d for dimensions d >= 3.
self_contained_problem:

  D(P) = |{ ‖p − q‖ : p, q ∈ P, p ≠ q }|

denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by P. Define

  f_V(n) = min { D(P) : P ⊂ V, |P| = n }.

The problem is to establish non-trivial lower bounds (and matching or near-matching upper bounds) on f_V(n) as n → ∞ that exploit the fact that the points are constrained to lie on V. More precisely: prove bounds of the form f_V(n) = Ω(n^{α(d,V)}) with exponent α(d,V) strictly larger than the trivial exponent obtained from the ambient-space distinct distances bound for ℝ^D, valid for all (or for a natural class of) d-dimensional constant-degree irreducible varieties V ⊂ ℝ^D with d ≥ 3, and complement these by constructions giving upper bounds on f_V(n).

context_brief: Largest distinct-distance subset in the plane
original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset(n), the largest number such that every n-point set in the plane contains a subset of that size in which no positive distance occurs more than once.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $\mathrm{subset}(P)$ denote the largest cardinality of a subset $Q\subseteq P$ such that all pairwise Euclidean distances $\{\,\|x-y\|:x,y\in Q,\,x\ne y\,\}$ are distinct (equivalently, no positive distance is realized by more than one unordered pair of points of $Q$). Define
$$\mathrm{subset}(n)=\min_{\substack{P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\\ |P|=n}}\mathrm{subset}(P),$$
so that $\mathrm{subset}(n)$ is the largest integer with the property that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $\mathrm{subset}(n)$ points spanning all distinct pairwise distances. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\mathrm{subset}(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. The best known lower bound is $\mathrm{subset}(n) = \Omega((n/\log n)^{1/3})$ due to Charalambides (2013), improving earlier $\Omega(n^{1/3})$ bounds of Lefmann–Thiele and others. The best known upper bound is roughly $O(n^{c})$ derived from configurations like the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ grid, giving $\mathrm{subset}(n)=O(n^{?})$ much larger than the lower bound. No matching asymptotic is known.

context_brief: Distinct-distance subset in the planar lattice
original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset(L) when L is a sqrt(n) by sqrt(n) integer lattice, where subset(L) is the size of the largest subset of lattice points that spans each positive distance at most once.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer such that $\sqrt{n}$ is an integer, and let $L = \{0,1,\dots,\sqrt{n}-1\}^2 \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ be the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ integer lattice (so $|L|=n$). Define $\mathrm{subset}(L)$ to be the maximum size of a subset $S\subseteq L$ such that all pairwise Euclidean distances between distinct points of $S$ are distinct; equivalently, every positive real number occurs as the distance between at most one (unordered) pair of points of $S$.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\mathrm{subset}(L)$ as $n\to\infty$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the asymptotics of the largest subset of a $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ integer lattice with all pairwise distances distinct, posed by Erdős and Guy, appears to remain open. Known bounds give roughly $n^{1/3}$ from below and $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ from above (via the Erdős distinct-distances bound on the grid), but no matching asymptotic is established. It is listed among the unresolved Erdős distance-type problems.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset(L_d) when L_d is the d-dimensional integer lattice n^(1/d) x ... x n^(1/d), where subset(L_d) is the size of the largest subset whose positive distances are all unique.

$$L_d=\{1,2,\ldots,\lceil n^{1/d}\rceil\}^d\subset\mathbb{Z}^d,$$
so that $|L_d|=\Theta(n)$. Define $\operatorname{subset}(L_d)$ to be the largest cardinality of a subset $S\subseteq L_d$ such that all positive Euclidean distances $\|x-y\|$ between distinct points $x,y\in S$ are pairwise distinct (a "Sidon set" with respect to Euclidean distance). 

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\operatorname{subset}(L_d)$ as $n\to\infty$. The known bounds are
$$\Omega\!\left(n^{2/(3d)}\right)\le \operatorname{subset}(L_d)\le O\!\left(n^{1/d}\right);$$

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of subset_d(n) for d >= 3, where subset_d(n) is the largest number such that every n-point set in R^d contains a subset of that size in which each positive distance occurs at most once.
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d \geq 2$ and a finite set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, say that a subset $S \subseteq P$ has all distinct distances if for every positive real $r$, the number of unordered pairs $\{x,y\} \subseteq S$ with Euclidean distance $\|x-y\| = r$ is at most one. Define
$$\mathrm{subset}_d(n) = \min_{\substack{P \subset \mathbb{R}^d \\ |P|=n}} \; \max\{\, |S| : S \subseteq P \text{ has all distinct distances} \,\}.$$
Equivalently, $\mathrm{subset}_d(n)$ is the largest integer $k$ such that every $n$-point set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a $k$-point subset in which each positive distance occurs at most once.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\mathrm{subset}_d(n)$ as $n \to \infty$ for each fixed $d \geq 3$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the asymptotics of the largest distinct-distance subset guaranteed in every n-point set of R^d remains open for d >= 3. Known results give only partial lower bounds (e.g., Charalambides-type bounds of order n^{c/d} up to logs, and improvements via algebraic-variety arguments by Raz, Sharir, and others), with no matching upper bound. No source found resolving the asymptotic value.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,3,3), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every three points determine three distinct distances, equivalently a set with no isosceles triangles, including degenerate collinear ones.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, let $D(P) = \{\,\|p-q\| : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\,\}$ denote the set of distinct pairwise distances. Say that $P$ "spans no isosceles triangle" if every three points of $P$ determine three pairwise distinct distances; here triples of collinear points are also required to satisfy this condition (so no three points $a,b,c \in P$ may satisfy $\|a-b\|=\|a-c\|$, even when $a,b,c$ are collinear). Define
$$\varphi(n,3,3) \;=\; \min\bigl\{\,|D(P)| : P \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ P\text{ spans no isosceles triangle}\,\bigr\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\varphi(n,3,3)$ as $n \to \infty$. In particular, is there a function $f(n) \to \infty$ such that $\varphi(n,3,3) \geq f(n)\cdot n$?
status_search_result: The problem is open. The trivial lower bound is $\varphi(n,3,3) = \Omega(n)$ (since every point has $n-1$ distinct distances to the others), and Erdős noted upper bounds, but the asymptotic value is unknown. It is not even known whether $\varphi(n,3,3)/n \to \infty$, even in the analogous problem on the line $\mathbb{R}$.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,4,3), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every four points determine at least three distinct distances, equivalently a set with no squares.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of points in the plane, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\|:p,q\in P,\,p\neq q\,\}$. Say that $P$ "spans a square" if there exist four points of $P$ forming the vertices of a (non-degenerate) square. Define
$$\varphi(n,4,3) \;=\; \min\bigl\{\,D(P)\,:\,P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ \text{every 4 points of } P \text{ determine at least 3 distinct distances}\bigr\}.$$
Equivalently (since a 4-point set determining only 2 distances must be one of a finite list of configurations, and among them the square is the relevant case here), this is the minimum of $D(P)$ over all $n$-point planar sets that span no square.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\varphi(n,4,3)$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, find matching upper and lower bounds (up to constants or logarithmic factors) for $\varphi(n,4,3)$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the asymptotics of the minimum number of distinct distances over n-point planar sets containing no square (the (4,3) local condition) is part of a family of Erdős-style problems on local-versus-global distinct distances. Recent work, including a 2024 blog post by T. Tao on planar point sets with forbidden four-point patterns and related results on Erdős Problem #135, addresses neighboring questions but does not establish matching asymptotic bounds for φ(n,4,3); the problem appears to remain open, with the standard Guth–Katz bound Ω(n/log n) and the √n × √n grid upper bound O(n/√log n) being the best general bounds available.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,4,4), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every four-point subset determines at least four distinct distances; equivalently, the set contains no rhombus, no rectangle, and no deltoid with one vertex equidistant from the other three.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct distances determined by pairs of points of $P$. Say that $P$ satisfies the local condition $(4,4)$ if every 4-point subset of $P$ determines at least 4 distinct pairwise distances; equivalently, $P$ contains no four points forming a rhombus, no four points forming a rectangle, and no four points forming a "deltoid" configuration in which one point is equidistant from the other three (so the three pairwise distances from that point are equal).

Define
$$\varphi(n,4,4) = \min\{\,D(P) : P \subset \mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ P \text{ satisfies the local condition }(4,4)\,\}.$$

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\varphi(n,4,4)$ as $n \to \infty$.

original_question: Prove or disprove that if a planar n-point set P spans only O(n/sqrt(log n)) distinct distances, then the additive energy E(P) = |{(a,b,c,d) in P^4 : a+b = c+d}| must be large.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ of $n$ points, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\|p-q\| : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\}$, and define the additive energy of $P$ by
$$E(P) = \big|\{(a,b,c,d) \in P^4 : a+b = c+d\}\big|,$$
where addition is the usual vector addition in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ with $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every planar point set $P$ with $|P|=n$ satisfying $D(P) = O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, one has
$$E(P) \;\geq\; f(n) \cdot n^{2}.$$

In other words, must any $n$-point planar set realizing the conjecturally extremal number of distinct distances necessarily have large additive energy?
status_search_result: The problem links the Erdős distinct distances extremal regime (where the conjectured lower bound is $\Omega(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, while Guth–Katz proved $\Omega(n/\log n)$) with additive energy. Subsequent work (e.g., Lund–Sheffer–de Zeeuw on bisector energy, 2014) gives partial structural results for sets achieving few distinct distances, but no proof or disproof that such sets must have large additive energy is known. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For a finite set A in R, determine the asymptotic size of the difference set A-A under the assumption that the Cartesian product A x A spans few distinct distances in the plane.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a finite set, and consider the Cartesian product $A \times A \subset \mathbb{R}^2$. For a planar point set $P$, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of $P$. The difference set of $A$ is $A - A = \{a - a' : a, a' \in A\}$.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $|A - A|$ as $|A| \to \infty$ under the hypothesis that $A \times A$ determines few distinct distances, i.e. $D(A \times A) = O(|A|/\sqrt{\log |A|})$ (the Guth–Katz lower-bound order for distinct distances of an $|A|^2$-point set). More precisely, find the smallest exponent $\alpha$ and the correct logarithmic factor such that the implication
$$D(A \times A) \ll \frac{|A|}{\sqrt{\log |A|}} \implies |A - A| \ll |A|^{\alpha}\,(\log |A|)^{O(1)}$$
holds for every finite $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, and decide whether $|A - A|$ must in fact be linear (up to logarithmic factors) under this hypothesis.
category_tag: Discrete geometry: distinct distances and sumsets
status_search_result: The best known bound, due to Pohoata (Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, 2019), shows that if $A\times A$ spans few distinct distances then $|A-A| \ll |A|^{2-2/7}(\log|A|)^{1/7}$, improving earlier results of Hanson and Roche-Newton. The exact asymptotic value of $|A-A|$ under this hypothesis is not determined; the problem of pinning down the correct exponent (and whether $|A-A|$ must be near-linear) remains open.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dhat(n), the largest function such that every n-point planar set contains a point incident to at least Dhat(n) distinct distances to the other points.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $p \in P$, let $D(p, P\setminus\{p\}) = |\{\,\|p-q\| : q \in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}|$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances from $p$ to the other points of $P$. For each integer $n \ge 2$, define
$$\widehat{D}(n) \;=\; \min_{\substack{P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \\ |P|=n}} \; \max_{p \in P} \; D(p,\, P\setminus\{p\}).$$
Thus $\widehat{D}(n)$ is the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains at least one point whose distances to the remaining $n-1$ points take at least $\widehat{D}(n)$ distinct values. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\widehat{D}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: The problem is a well-known open question in combinatorial geometry. The best known upper bound is $\widehat{D}(n) = O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, achieved by the integer lattice (Erdős), while the best lower bound is roughly $\widehat{D}(n) = \Omega(n^{c})$ for some $c<1$ (Katz–Tardos, building on Solymosi–Tóth and Guth–Katz). No matching bounds are known; the asymptotic value remains undetermined.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of DhatSigma(n), where DhatSigma(n) is the minimum, over all planar n-point sets P, of the sum over p in P of the number of distinct distances from p to the rest of P.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite planar point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $p \in P$, let $\hat{D}_p(P)$ denote the number of distinct values in the multiset $\{\,\|p-q\| : q \in P \setminus \{p\}\,\}$ (i.e., the number of distinct distances from $p$ to the other points of $P$). Define
$$\hat{D}_\Sigma(P) = \sum_{p \in P} \hat{D}_p(P), \qquad \hat{D}_\Sigma(n) = \min_{\substack{P \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \\ |P|=n}} \hat{D}_\Sigma(P).$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\hat{D}_\Sigma(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a survey of open problems on distinct distances and is listed there as an open problem. A web search did not surface any later work resolving the asymptotic value of this sum-of-one-point distinct-distance counts quantity; related results focus on the original Erdős distinct-distances problem (resolved up to logarithmic factors by Guth–Katz) rather than this variant.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of L(m,n), the minimum number of distinct point-to-line distances determined by a set of m points and a set of n lines in the plane.
self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $P$ be a set of $m$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a set of $n$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a point $p\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and a line $\ell\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let $d(p,\ell)$ denote the usual Euclidean distance from $p$ to $\ell$ (the infimum of $\|p-q\|$ over $q\in\ell$). Define
$$D(P,\mathcal{L}) = |\{\, d(p,\ell) : p\in P,\ \ell\in\mathcal{L}\,\}|,$$
the number of distinct point-to-line distances determined by $P$ and $\mathcal{L}$, and set
$$L(m,n) = \min\{\, D(P,\mathcal{L}) : |P|=m,\ |\mathcal{L}|=n\,\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $L(m,n)$ as $m,n\to\infty$; that is, find matching (up to constants and lower-order factors) lower and upper bounds for $L(m,n)$ in terms of $m$ and $n$.
status_search_result: Sharir and Smorodinsky studied distinct distances between points and lines and obtained near-tight bounds: a lower bound roughly of the form $\Omega(\min(m^{2/3}n^{2/3}, m^2, n^2))$ matched (up to lower-order factors) by constructions, but a complete asymptotic determination of $L(m,n)$ across all ranges of $m,n$ does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

original_question: Find the asymptotic value of vgen(n), the minimum number of distinct vectors spanned by an n-point planar set in general position, meaning no three points are collinear and no four are cocircular.
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, let
$$v(P)=\bigl|\{\,p-q:\ p,q\in P\,\}\bigr|$$
be the number of distinct vectors (translation-equivalence classes of ordered pairs) determined by $P$. A set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is said to be in general position if no three points of $P$ are collinear and no four points of $P$ lie on a common circle. Define
$$v_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)=\min\{\,v(P):\ P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n,\ P\text{ in general position}\,\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $v_{\mathrm{gen}}(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work establishing the asymptotic value of v_gen(n). The closely related problem of distinct distances in general position (studied by Erdős, Füredi, Pach, and Ruzsa) is itself still open, and the distinct-vectors variant in general position appears to remain unresolved.

original_question: Let X be a separated locally convex space, and let C and D be convex subsets of X. For a convex set E, define its quasi relative interior by qri E := {x in E | cone(E - x) is a linear space}. Is it possible that the Minkowski sum of the quasi relative interiors, qri C + qri D, is a proper subset of the quasi relative interior of the Minkowski sum, qri(C + D)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a convex subset $E \subseteq X$, define the quasi relative interior of $E$ by
$$\operatorname{qri} E := \{x \in E \mid \operatorname{cone}(E - x) \text{ is a linear subspace of } X\},$$
where $\operatorname{cone}(A) := \{\lambda a \mid \lambda \ge 0,\ a \in A\}$ denotes the cone generated by $A$. For convex subsets $C, D \subseteq X$, the Minkowski sum is $C + D := \{c + d \mid c \in C,\ d \in D\}$, and one always has the inclusion $\operatorname{qri} C + \operatorname{qri} D \subseteq \operatorname{qri}(C + D)$.

Question: Do there exist a separated locally convex space $X$ and convex subsets $C, D \subseteq X$ such that the inclusion is strict, i.e.
$$\operatorname{qri} C + \operatorname{qri} D \subsetneq \operatorname{qri}(C + D)?$$
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Borwein and Goebel (2003), is answered affirmatively by an explicit example constructed in a 2014 work that resolves both Borwein–Goebel questions and a related Grad–Pop conjecture about calculus rules for the quasi relative interior.

original_question: Let X be a separated locally convex space, and let A and B be convex subsets of X. For a convex set E, define its quasi interior by qi E := {x in E | cone(E - x) = X}. Assuming qi B is nonempty, must the equality A + qi B = qi(A + B) always hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a convex subset $E \subseteq X$, define the quasi interior of $E$ by
$$\operatorname{qi} E := \{x \in E \mid \overline{\operatorname{cone}(E - x)} = X\},$$
where $\operatorname{cone}(S) = \{\lambda s : \lambda \geq 0,\ s \in S\}$ and the closure is taken in $X$. Let $A, B \subseteq X$ be convex subsets with $\operatorname{qi} B \neq \emptyset$. Decide whether the equality
$$A + \operatorname{qi} B \;=\; \operatorname{qi}(A + B)$$
must always hold, or exhibit convex sets $A, B$ in some separated locally convex space $X$ for which it fails.
status_search_result: The conjecture (formulated by Grad and Pop in 2014) is resolved negatively: a counterexample exists showing that $A + \operatorname{qi} B = \operatorname{qi}(A+B)$ can fail even when $\operatorname{qi} B \neq \emptyset$. The resolution is given in a 2014 note that addresses this conjecture together with related questions of Borwein and Goebel on quasi-relative interior calculus.

original_question: Let X be a separated locally convex space, and let C and D be nonempty convex subsets of X. For a convex set E, define its quasi relative interior by qri E := {x in E | cone(E - x) is a linear space}. If qri C intersect qri D is nonempty, can the inclusion qri(C intersect D) subset qri C intersect qri D fail?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separated locally convex topological vector space. For a nonempty convex subset $E\subseteq X$, define the quasi relative interior of $E$ by
$$\operatorname{qri} E := \{x\in E \mid \operatorname{cone}(E-x)\text{ is a linear subspace of }X\},$$
where $\operatorname{cone}(A) = \{\lambda a : \lambda \ge 0,\ a\in A\}$.

Let $C, D\subseteq X$ be nonempty convex sets such that $\operatorname{qri} C \cap \operatorname{qri} D \ne \emptyset$. Decide whether the inclusion
$$\operatorname{qri}(C\cap D) \subseteq \operatorname{qri} C \cap \operatorname{qri} D$$
can fail; that is, can there exist $x\in \operatorname{qri}(C\cap D)$ with $x\notin \operatorname{qri} C \cap \operatorname{qri} D$?
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Borwein and Goebel, has been answered in the negative: under the hypothesis that qri C ∩ qri D is nonempty, one always has qri(C ∩ D) ⊆ qri C ∩ qri D, so the inclusion cannot fail. This follows from established calculus rules for the quasi relative interior in separated locally convex spaces.

original_question: For subsets A of {0,1,...,r} that are more-sums-than-differences (MSTD), explicit infinite constructions were known with density about C/r^4 among all subsets of [0,r]. Can one construct a substantially denser explicit family of MSTD sets, and in particular can one obtain an explicit family that occupies a positive proportion of all subsets of [0,r]?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$, define the sumset $A+A = \{a+b : a,b \in A\}$ and the difference set $A-A = \{a-b : a,b \in A\}$. The set $A$ is called a more-sums-than-differences (MSTD) set if $|A+A| > |A-A|$.

For an integer $r \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{M}(r)$ denote the collection of MSTD subsets of $\{0,1,\ldots,r\}$. There exist explicit infinite families $\mathcal{F}_r \subset \mathcal{M}(r)$ that achieve $|\mathcal{F}_r| \geq C \cdot 2^{r+1}/r^4$ for some absolute constant $C > 0$, and (using bidirectional ballot sequences) explicit families of size $\Theta(2^r/r)$.

Question: Construct an explicit infinite family $\{\mathcal{F}_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ with $\mathcal{F}_r \subset \mathcal{M}(r)$ whose density among all subsets of $\{0,1,\ldots,r\}$ is substantially larger than $1/r$. In particular, give an explicit construction such that
$$\liminf_{r \to \infty} \frac{|\mathcal{F}_r|}{2^{r+1}} > 0,$$
i.e., an explicit family that occupies a positive proportion of all subsets of $\{0,1,\ldots,r\}$.
status_search_result: The best previously known explicit family had density $\Theta(1/r^4)$ (Miller–Orosz–Scheinerman). Y. Zhao improved this to $\Theta(2^r/r)$ via bidirectional ballot sequences, an improvement over the $1/r^4$ bound but still not a positive proportion. It is known by probabilistic arguments (Martin–O'Bryant) that a positive proportion of all subsets of $\{0,\dots,r\}$ are MSTD, but no explicit construction achieving positive proportion appears to be known, so the explicit positive-proportion question remains open.

original_question: An MSTD subset of the integers has more pairwise sums than pairwise differences. Starting from the minimal 8-element integer example, one can build an MSTD subset of Z^2 by taking its product with a 2-point set. Can one instead construct an MSTD subset of Z^2 directly, without obtaining it from an MSTD subset of Z by such a lifting procedure?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $A$ in an abelian group, define the sumset $A+A=\{a+b:a,b\in A\}$ and difference set $A-A=\{a-b:a,b\in A\}$. The set $A$ is called an MSTD (more sums than differences) set if $|A+A|>|A-A|$.

It is known that MSTD subsets of $\mathbb{Z}$ exist (the smallest has $8$ elements). Given any MSTD set $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$ and any $2$-element set $B\subset\mathbb{Z}$, the product $A\times B\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$ is an MSTD subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

Construct an MSTD subset $S\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$ that does not arise from such a lifting procedure; that is, $S$ should not be expressible (up to affine equivalence in $\mathbb{Z}^2$) as a Cartesian product $A\times B$ where $A$ is an MSTD subset of $\mathbb{Z}$ and $B\subset\mathbb{Z}$ has two elements, nor obtained from a one-dimensional MSTD set by an embedding $\mathbb{Z}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{Z}^2$ followed by a product with a $2$-element set.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Iyer, Lazarev, Miller, and Zhang on generalized MSTD sets establishes that a positive proportion of subsets of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (for $d\ge 2$) are MSTD, which in particular yields direct MSTD constructions in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that are not products of a one-dimensional MSTD set with a 2-element set. Thus the question of constructing MSTD sets in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ directly has been answered affirmatively.

original_question: Let A be a subset of Z_n. The order of A is the least h such that hA = Z_n but (h-1)A != Z_n. Which integers can occur as orders of bases in Z_n, especially in the regime where the order grows linearly with n?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $\mathbb{Z}_n = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. For a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n$ containing $0$ (or, more generally, such that the iterated sumsets eventually cover $\mathbb{Z}_n$), define the sumset $hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_i \in A\}$ for each positive integer $h$. Call $A$ a basis of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ if $hA = \mathbb{Z}_n$ for some $h$, and define the order of $A$ to be the least such $h$, i.e. the unique $h$ with $hA = \mathbb{Z}_n$ and $(h-1)A \neq \mathbb{Z}_n$.

Determine which integers can occur as the order of a basis of $\mathbb{Z}_n$. In particular, characterize the set of attainable orders in the regime where the order grows linearly with $n$: prove that for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k > 0$ such that, for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every basis $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_n$ whose order exceeds $n/k$ has order within $c_k$ of $n/\ell$ for some integer $\ell \in [1,k]$, and conversely show that every such value (up to the appropriate error) is realized.
status_search_result: The problem was resolved by Peter Hegarty (arXiv:0906.5484), who proved the Dukes–Herke conjecture: for each k there is a constant c_k such that any basis A ⊆ Z_n of order greater than n/k has order within c_k of n/ℓ for some integer ℓ ∈ [1,k]. This characterizes the possible orders of bases in the linear-in-n regime.

original_question: Define g_0 = 0 and, greedily, let g_i be the least positive integer such that {g_0,...,g_i} has no solutions to 5w + 2x = 5y + 2z. Define a_0 = 0, define a_i by the recurrence given in the paper, and let A be the set of sums of distinct a_i. Is the greedy set G exactly {5x + y : x in A and 0 <= y <= 4}?
self_contained_problem:
Construct a set $G \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ greedily as follows. Set $g_0 = 0$, and for each $i \ge 1$ let $g_i$ be the least positive integer strictly greater than $g_{i-1}$ such that the set $\{g_0, g_1, \ldots, g_i\}$ contains no four (not necessarily distinct) elements $w, x, y, z$ with $(w,x) \ne (y,z)$ satisfying
$$5w + 2x \;=\; 5y + 2z.$$
Let $G = \{g_0, g_1, g_2, \ldots\}$.

Separately, define a sequence $(a_i)_{i \ge 0}$ by
$$a_0 = 0,\qquad a_1 = 3,\qquad a_i = 5\,a_{i-1} \text{ for } i \ge 2,$$
so that $a_i = 3 \cdot 5^{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$. Let
$$A \;=\; \Big\{\, \sum_{i \in S} a_i \;:\; S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \text{ finite} \Big\}$$
be the set of all sums of finitely many distinct terms of $(a_i)$.

Decide whether
$$G \;=\; \{\, 5x + y \;:\; x \in A,\; 0 \le y \le 4 \,\}.$$

Yin Choi Cheng's work "Greedy Sidon sets for linear forms" (Journal of Number Theory, 2024; CUNY thesis 2023) gives an explicit description of the greedy Sidon set for binary linear forms with coefficients $(c_1,c_2)=(2,c_2)$ when $c_2 \ge 4$ (the "structured" domain), which covers the case $c_2 = 5$. Thus the conjectured explicit form is established.

original_question: Suppose the first N terms of an increasing sequence already form an initial segment of a basis of order 2 for the nonnegative integers, meaning every sufficiently small nonnegative integer is a sum of two elements of the full basis. Must every such initial segment be extendable to a minimal basis, that is, a basis from which removing any one element destroys the basis property?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A set $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$ is called a basis of order $2$ for $\mathbb{N}_0$ if every sufficiently large nonnegative integer can be written as a sum $b_1+b_2$ with $b_1,b_2\in B$. Such a basis $B$ is called minimal if for every $b\in B$ the set $B\setminus\{b\}$ fails to be a basis of order $2$ (i.e., removing any single element destroys the property that all sufficiently large integers are sums of two elements).

Suppose $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_N\}\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ is a finite increasing initial segment that is "extendable to a basis of order $2$" in the following sense: there exists a set $B\supseteq A$ such that $B$ is a basis of order $2$ for $\mathbb{N}_0$ and $A=B\cap[0,a_N]$ (so $A$ consists exactly of the elements of $B$ up to its $N$-th term).

Question: Does every such finite initial segment $A$ admit an extension to a minimal basis of order $2$? Equivalently, given any finite $A$ that begins some basis of order $2$, must there exist a minimal basis $B$ of order $2$ whose first $N$ elements are exactly $a_1,\dots,a_N$?
status_search_result: The question originates from a CANT conference problem session compilation. Web searches return general literature on minimal asymptotic bases (Nathanson, Erdős and successors), but no source explicitly resolves the specific question of whether any finite initial segment of a basis of order 2 can be completed to a minimal basis of order 2. Status could not be verified.

original_question: For the unrestricted partition generating function product over m >= 1 of (1 + x^m + x^(2m) + ...), can one choose signs in some of the factors so that, after expansion, every coefficient belongs to {0, -1, 1}?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the formal power series identity
$$\prod_{m\ge 1}\bigl(1+x^m+x^{2m}+x^{3m}+\cdots\bigr)=\sum_{n\ge 0}p(n)x^n,$$
where $p(n)$ denotes the number of unrestricted partitions of $n$. For each $m\ge 1$ and each $k\ge 1$, let $\varepsilon_{m,k}\in\{+1,-1\}$ be a choice of sign, and define
$$F(x)=\prod_{m\ge 1}\Bigl(1+\sum_{k\ge 1}\varepsilon_{m,k}\,x^{km}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge 0}b_n x^n.$$
Question: does there exist a choice of signs $\{\varepsilon_{m,k}\}$ such that $b_n\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for every $n\ge 0$?

A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution or partial result specifically addressing whether signs in the factors of the unrestricted partition product can be chosen to force all coefficients into {-1,0,1}. Status appears unresolved in the literature accessible via search.
