original_question: For a finite abelian group G, let L(G) denote the collection of all sets of factorization lengths arising from G. Can one determine a function f: N -> N such that, whenever |G| >= f(M), the system L(G) contains every finite set L subset N_{>=2} whose width max L - min L is at most M?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written additively. Consider the monoid $\mathcal{B}(G)$ of zero-sum sequences over $G$, i.e. finite sequences $S = g_1 \cdots g_\ell$ of elements of $G$ (multiplicities allowed, order irrelevant) with $g_1 + \cdots + g_\ell = 0$, under concatenation. The atoms of $\mathcal{B}(G)$ are the minimal zero-sum sequences (those with no proper zero-sum subsequence). For a zero-sum sequence $a \in \mathcal{B}(G)$, define its set of lengths
$$\mathsf{L}(a) = \{\, k \in \mathbb{N} : a = u_1 \cdots u_k \text{ for some atoms } u_1,\ldots,u_k \,\},$$
and define the system of sets of lengths of $G$ by
$$\mathcal{L}(G) = \{\, \mathsf{L}(a) : a \in \mathcal{B}(G) \,\}.$$
For a finite nonempty set $L \subset \mathbb{N}$, call $\max L - \min L$ the width of $L$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $M \in \mathbb{N}$ and every finite abelian group $G$ with $|G| \geq f(M)$, the system $\mathcal{L}(G)$ contains every finite set $L \subset \mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$ with $\max L - \min L \leq M$?
category_tag: Sets of lengths in factorization theory
status_search_result: Related realization results for sets of lengths exist (e.g., Geroldinger–Schmid for numerical monoids, and a realization result for systems of sets of lengths in Dedekind domains by Geroldinger–Zhong, arXiv:2008.08820), but none of the readily accessible sources explicitly state that the specific question—existence of a uniform threshold function $f(M)$ for finite abelian groups guaranteeing realization of all length sets of width at most $M$—has been resolved. Status could not be definitively verified.

context_brief: When the minimal-distance set is an interval
original_question: Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which the set Delta*(G) = {min Delta(G0) : G0 subset G and Delta(G0) is nonempty} is an interval and, at the same time, the exponent of G is at least 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|\ge 3$. By the structure theorem there are uniquely determined integers $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ such that $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$; one calls $r(G)=r$ the rank of $G$ and $\exp(G)=n_r$ the exponent of $G$.

For a subset $G_0\subseteq G$, a sequence over $G_0$ is a finite unordered tuple of elements of $G_0$ (formally, an element of the free abelian monoid $\mathcal F(G_0)$ on $G_0$). A sequence $S=g_1\cdots g_\ell$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $g_1+\cdots+g_\ell=0$, and it is called a minimal zero-sum sequence if it is a zero-sum sequence and no proper nonempty subsequence of it is a zero-sum sequence. Let $\mathcal A(G_0)$ denote the set of minimal zero-sum sequences over $G_0$. For a zero-sum sequence $S$ over $G_0$, the set of lengths of $S$ is
$$\mathsf L(S)=\{k\in\mathbb N : S=U_1\cdots U_k \text{ with } U_1,\dots,U_k\in\mathcal A(G_0)\}.$$
Let $\mathcal L(G_0)=\{\mathsf L(S): S \text{ a zero-sum sequence over }G_0\}$. For a finite set $L=\{l_1<l_2<\cdots<l_k\}\subseteq\mathbb N$ define $\Delta(L)=\{l_{i+1}-l_i : 1\le i\le k-1\}$, and put
$$\Delta(G_0)=\bigcup_{L\in\mathcal L(G_0),\,|L|\ge 2}\Delta(L).$$
Define
$$\Delta^*(G)=\{\min\Delta(G_0) : G_0\subseteq G,\ \Delta(G_0)\neq\varnothing\}\subseteq\mathbb N.$$

Question: Does there exist a finite abelian group $G$ such that $\Delta^*(G)$ is an interval of $\mathbb N$ (i.e. $\Delta^*(G)=[\min\Delta^*(G),\max\Delta^*(G)]\cap\mathbb N$) and at the same time $\exp(G)\ge 2r(G)+2$?
category_tag: zero-sum sequences and sets of lengths
status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of this specific question about whether some finite abelian group has $\Delta^*(G)$ an interval together with $\exp(G)\ge 2r(G)+2$. Related work on $\Delta^*(G)$ and sets of minimal distances exists, but no source clearly confirms or refutes the existence of such a group.

context_brief: Growth rate of the STSL bound
original_question: For a Krull monoid with finite class group, the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths says that there exist a nonnegative integer M and a finite nonempty set Delta* such that every set of lengths L(a) is an almost arithmetic multiprogression with bound M and difference d in Delta*. For the systems L(G) attached to finite abelian groups G, what is the rough order of magnitude of the smallest such bound as a function of the Davenport constant D(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with finite class group $G$. For an element $a \in H$, write $a = u_1 \cdots u_k$ as a product of atoms (irreducibles); the set of lengths of $a$ is
$$L(a) = \{ k \in \mathbb{N} : a = u_1 \cdots u_k \text{ with each } u_i \text{ an atom of } H \},$$
and the system of sets of lengths of $H$ is $\mathcal{L}(H) = \{ L(a) : a \in H \}$.

A non-empty subset $L \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ is called an almost arithmetic multiprogression (AAMP) with bound $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$, difference $d \in \mathbb{N}$, and period $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \{0, d, 2d, \dots\}$ with $0, d \in \mathcal{D}$, if there exist integers $y, \ell$ with
$$L = y + (L' \cup L^* \cup L'') \subseteq y + \mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z},$$
where $L^* = (\mathcal{D} + d\mathbb{Z}) \cap [0, \ell d]$ is the central part, and $L' \subseteq [-M, -1]$, $L'' \subseteq \ell d + [1, M]$ are bounded "end" perturbations.

The Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths asserts: for every Krull monoid $H$ with finite class group there exist $M \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a finite non-empty set $\Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that every $L \in \mathcal{L}(H)$ is an AAMP with bound $M$ and difference $d \in \Delta^*$.

For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\mathcal{B}(G)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G$, and write $\mathcal{L}(G) = \mathcal{L}(\mathcal{B}(G))$. Let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of $G$, i.e.\ the smallest $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ has a non-empty zero-sum subsequence. Let
$$M^*(G) = \min\{M \in \mathbb{N}_0 : \exists \text{ finite } \Delta^* \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ with every } L \in \mathcal{L}(G) \text{ an AAMP with bound } M \text{ and difference } d \in \Delta^*\}.$$

Determine the rough order of magnitude of $M^*(G)$ as a function of $\mathsf{D}(G)$, as $G$ ranges over finite abelian groups.
category_tag: Krull monoids and sets of lengths
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published determination of the order of magnitude of the optimal bound in the Structure Theorem for Sets of Lengths in terms of the Davenport constant. Surveys of factorization theory in Krull monoids continue to list quantitative refinements of the STSL bound as an open direction, and no source identified gives an asymptotic answer. Status appears to remain open.

context_brief: Isomorphism between A_q, q-Onsager, and a coideal subalgebra
original_question: Let q be a non-root of unity. The q-Onsager algebra is the algebra generated by W_0 and W_1 subject to the pair of q-Dolan-Grady type relations written in the paper, namely [W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_0,W_1] and [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=ρ[W_1,W_0], where [X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX and ρ is a scalar. The algebra A_q is an infinite-dimensional current algebra introduced in terms of generators {W_{-k}, W_{k+1}, G_{k+1}, G̃_{k+1} | k ∈ ℤ_+} whose first modes satisfy the same pair of relations. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending W_0 to k_+e_1 + k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1} + ε_+q^{h_1}, W_1 to k_-e_0 + k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0} + ε_-q^{h_0}, and ρ to (q+q^{-1})^2k_+k_-. Show that these three infinite-dimensional algebras — A_q, the q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) — are isomorphic.
self_contained_problem:
Fix a field $\mathbb{K}$ and a nonzero scalar $q\in\mathbb{K}$ that is not a root of unity. For $X,Y$ in an associative algebra set $[X,Y]_q=qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

(1) The q-Onsager algebra $O_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra with two generators $W_0,W_1$ and the q-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=\rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $\rho\in\mathbb{K}$ is a fixed scalar.

(2) The current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebra generated by an infinite family of generators $\{W_{-k},\,W_{k+1},\,G_{k+1},\,\tilde G_{k+1}\mid k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\}$ subject to the standard list of defining relations under which the first modes $W_0,W_1$ satisfy the q-Dolan–Grady relations above with the same parameter $\rho$.

(3) Let $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ be the quantum affine algebra with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$). Fix scalars $k_\pm,\varepsilon_\pm\in\mathbb{K}$ with $\rho=(q+q^{-1})^2 k_+k_-$, and let $B$ be the left coideal subalgebra of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ generated by
$$\mathcal{W}_0=k_+e_1+k_-q^{-1}f_1q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\qquad \mathcal{W}_1=k_-e_0+k_+q^{-1}f_0q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_- q^{h_0}.$$

Prove or disprove: the three algebras $\mathcal{A}_q$, $O_q$, and $B$ are mutually isomorphic as associative $\mathbb{K}$-algebras.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Terwilliger and collaborators (notably "The alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra", arXiv:2103.03028, and "The q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension", arXiv:2106.14041, Comm. Math. Phys. 2021) clarified the relation: the current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q$ is the alternating central extension of $O_q$, with an algebra isomorphism $\langle W_0,W_1\rangle\subset\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ and a tensor-product factorization $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q\otimes Z$ where $Z$ is a polynomial center. Thus $O_q$ embeds in $\mathcal{A}_q$ but the two are not isomorphic; $\mathcal{A}_q$ is strictly larger. The isomorphism of $O_q$ with the coideal subalgebra image is established in Baseilhac–Belliard and related work. Hence the conjecture as stated is partially resolved (with a negative answer for $\mathcal{A}_q\cong O_q$ in the strict sense).

context_brief: Isomorphism for the augmented q-Onsager setting
original_question: Let A_q^{diag} denote the current algebra obtained from the quotient of the reflection equation algebra discussed in the paper, with current modes K_k, K_{k+1}, Z_{k+1}, and Z̃_{k+1}. Let the augmented q-Onsager algebra be the algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and Z̃_1 subject to the displayed commutation and higher q-commutator relations in the paper. There is also an explicit homomorphism from the augmented q-Onsager algebra to a coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) sending K_0 to ε_+q^{h_1}, K_1 to ε_-q^{h_0}, Z_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_+q^{-1}e_0q^{h_1}+ε_-f_1q^{h_1+h_0}), and Z̃_1 to (q^2-q^{-2})(ε_-q^{-1}e_1q^{h_0}+ε_+f_0q^{h_1+h_0}). Show that the infinite-dimensional algebra A_q^{diag}, the augmented q-Onsager algebra, and that coideal subalgebra of U_q(\hat{sl}_2) are isomorphic.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $q$ be a generic nonzero complex parameter and let $\varepsilon_+,\varepsilon_-$ be fixed nonzero scalars. Consider the quantum affine algebra $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ with Chevalley generators $e_i,f_i,q^{\pm h_i}$ ($i=0,1$) and standard relations.

(i) Augmented $q$-Onsager algebra $\mathcal{O}_q$. Define $\mathcal{O}_q$ as the unital associative algebra with generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ satisfying
- $[K_0,K_1]=0$,
- $K_0 Z_1 K_0^{-1}=q^{2}Z_1$, $K_0\widetilde Z_1K_0^{-1}=q^{-2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- $K_1 Z_1 K_1^{-1}=q^{-2}Z_1$, $K_1\widetilde Z_1K_1^{-1}=q^{2}\widetilde Z_1$,
- the higher $q$-Serre / $q$-commutator relations
$$[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,\qquad [\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[\widetilde Z_1,K_0K_1]\,K_0K_1,$$
with $\rho=-(q^2-q^{-2})^2$ and $[X,Y]_p:=XY-pYX$.

(ii) Coideal subalgebra $\mathcal{B}\subset U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be the subalgebra generated by
$$\varepsilon_+ q^{h_1},\quad \varepsilon_- q^{h_0},\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_+ q^{-1}e_0 q^{h_1}+\varepsilon_- f_1 q^{h_1+h_0}),\quad (q^2-q^{-2})(\varepsilon_- q^{-1}e_1 q^{h_0}+\varepsilon_+ f_0 q^{h_1+h_0}).$$

(iii) Current algebra $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$. Let $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ be the algebra obtained as the quotient of the reflection equation algebra for the $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ $R$-matrix by the diagonal/scalar reduction giving currents with modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ ($k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$), subject to the relations induced by the reflection equation.

Problem. Prove that there are algebra isomorphisms
$$\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}} \;\cong\; \mathcal{O}_q \;\cong\; \mathcal{B},$$
where the second isomorphism is induced by the assignment in (ii). Furthermore, find explicit polynomial formulas expressing the higher current modes $K_k,K_{k+1},Z_{k+1},\widetilde Z_{k+1}$ of $\mathcal{A}_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ as noncommutative polynomials in the generators $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ of $\mathcal{O}_q$.
category_tag: Quantum affine algebras and coideal subalgebras
status_search_result: The augmented q-Onsager algebra is widely recognized as a coideal subalgebra of U_q(ŝl_2) (Ito–Terwilliger, Baseilhac–Belliard), and an isomorphism between a quantum reflection algebra and a new current algebra of q-Onsager type has been established in related work. However, no source clearly verifies the full triple isomorphism together with the explicit polynomial formulas relating higher current modes to the augmented q-Onsager generators in the diagonal case, so the status is inconclusive.

context_brief: Polynomial formulae relating A_q^{diag} and augmented q-Onsager
original_question: For the current algebra A_q^{diag} arising from a quotient of the reflection equation algebra, and the augmented q-Onsager algebra generated by K_0, K_1, Z_1, and Z̃_1 with the displayed defining relations, determine explicit polynomial formulae expressing the generators or current modes of A_q^{diag} in terms of the augmented q-Onsager algebra, so that the precise algebraic relationship between A_q^{diag} and the augmented q-Onsager algebra is made explicit.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a nonzero complex number that is not a root of unity. The augmented $q$-Onsager algebra is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by elements $K_0,K_1,Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$ subject to the relations
$$K_0K_1=K_1K_0,\qquad K_0K_0^{-1}=K_1K_1^{-1}=1,$$
$$K_iZ_1K_i^{-1}=q^{a_i}Z_1,\qquad K_i\widetilde Z_1K_i^{-1}=q^{-a_i}\widetilde Z_1\quad(i=0,1),$$
with $a_0=2$, $a_1=-2$, together with the cubic $q$-Serre type relations
$$[Z_1,[Z_1,[Z_1,\widetilde Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=-q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 Z_1(K_0K_1)Z_1,$$
$$[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,[\widetilde Z_1,Z_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}]=-q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})^2 \widetilde Z_1(K_0K_1)^{-1}\widetilde Z_1,$$
where $[X,Y]_p:=XY-pYX$.

Let $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ denote the current algebra obtained as the quotient of the reflection equation algebra associated with $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ at a diagonal $K$-matrix, with its standard system of mode generators (Cartan-type modes and root-type current modes indexed by nonnegative integers).

Problem. Provide explicit polynomial formulae that express each generator (equivalently, each current mode) of $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ as a noncommutative polynomial in $K_0^{\pm 1},K_1^{\pm 1},Z_1,\widetilde Z_1$, thereby exhibiting an explicit algebra homomorphism (and, in particular, an isomorphism) between $\mathcal A_q^{\mathrm{diag}}$ and the augmented $q$-Onsager algebra.
status_search_result: The web search shows extensive subsequent work by Baseilhac, Terwilliger, and others on current algebras for the q-Onsager algebra and its alternating central extension, together with PBW-basis isomorphisms. However, even for the (non-augmented) q-Onsager algebra it is reported that closed-form polynomial expressions for the alternating/current generators in terms of the standard generators are not known. No source found explicitly states that the analogous problem for A_q^diag and the augmented q-Onsager algebra has been completely solved with explicit polynomial formulae, so the status appears to be unknown / at most partially addressed.

original_question: For finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q, q-analogs of Davies' relations are described as polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on the module, and A_q^{[2N+1]} is defined to be the quotient of A_q by these relations. When N=1 this quotient is isomorphic to the Askey-Wilson algebra AW(3), and there is a known homomorphism from AW(3) to the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨. Is there a homomorphism from A_q^{[2N+1]} to an algebra that generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type C_1,C_1^∨?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A_q$ denote the $q$-Onsager algebra, defined as the unital associative algebra over $\mathbb{C}(q)$ generated by two elements $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho [W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho \in \mathbb{C}(q)$ is fixed.

For each integer $N \geq 1$, on every finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q$-module of "type 1" with diameter $N$, there exist $q$-analogues of Davies' relations: certain explicit polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ act as zero on the module. Let $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ be the quotient of $A_q$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these universal polynomial relations.

For $N=1$, $A_q^{[3]}$ is isomorphic to the Askey–Wilson algebra $AW(3)$ of Zhedanov, and there is a known algebra homomorphism from $AW(3)$ into the double affine Hecke algebra (DAHA) of type $(C_1^\vee,C_1)$.

Question: For general $N \geq 2$, does there exist an algebra homomorphism from $A_q^{[2N+1]}$ into an algebra that naturally generalizes the double affine Hecke algebra of type $(C_1^\vee, C_1)$?

context_brief: Classification of finite-dimensional irreducibles of A_q^{[2N+1]}
original_question: Let A_q^{[2N+1]} be the quotient of A_q obtained by imposing the polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 in W_0 and W_1 that vanish on finite-dimensional modules. Classify the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of A_q^{[2N+1]}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field and $q\in\mathbb{F}^\times$ a nonzero scalar that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the associative $\mathbb{F}$-algebra with generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1],\qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY-q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q^2-q^{-2})^2$.

For a fixed positive integer $N$, on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module certain polynomials of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0$ and $W_1$ are known to act as zero. Let $I_{2N+1}\subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all such polynomial relations of total degree $2N+1$ in $W_0,W_1$ that vanish on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module, and define
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem. Classify, up to isomorphism, all finite-dimensional irreducible $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules.
status_search_result: While the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of the full q-Onsager algebra A_q are known to correspond to tridiagonal pairs of q-Racah type, no source found explicitly establishes a complete classification for the truncated quotient A_q^{[2N+1]} defined by the degree-(2N+1) relations. The status of this specific classification problem appears to be unresolved in the readily accessible literature.

original_question: The paper states that some multivariable polynomials introduced by Gasper and Rahman in 2006 provide an infinite-dimensional basis of the q-Onsager algebra. Study in detail the finite-dimensional modules associated with these Gasper-Rahman multivariable polynomials, in the setting of the quotient algebra A_q^{[2N+1]} built from the polynomial relations of total degree 2N+1 that vanish on finite-dimensional A_q-modules.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $q$ be a nonzero complex parameter that is not a root of unity. The $q$-Onsager algebra $A_q$ is the unital associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with two generators $W_0, W_1$ subject to the $q$-Dolan–Grady relations
$$[W_0,[W_0,[W_0,W_1]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_0,W_1], \qquad [W_1,[W_1,[W_1,W_0]_q]_{q^{-1}}] = \rho\,[W_1,W_0],$$
where $[X,Y]_q = qXY - q^{-1}YX$ and $\rho = -(q-q^{-1})^2$.

Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials. Let $\{P_{n_1,\dots,n_k}(x_1,\dots,x_k)\}$ denote the family of multivariable orthogonal $q$-Racah polynomials of Gasper and Rahman (a multivariable extension of the Askey–Wilson/$q$-Racah scheme). Suppose that, viewed as elements built from $W_0, W_1$ via a fixed substitution, these polynomials yield a linear basis of $A_q$.

Quotient. For an integer $N \ge 1$, let $I_{2N+1} \subset A_q$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all polynomial relations in $W_0, W_1$ of total degree $2N+1$ that act as zero on every finite-dimensional $A_q$-module of "level" $2N+1$, and set
$$A_q^{[2N+1]} := A_q / I_{2N+1}.$$

Problem. 
(a) Classify, up to isomorphism, the finite-dimensional irreducible modules of $A_q^{[2N+1]}$.
(b) Carry out a detailed study of the finite-dimensional $A_q^{[2N+1]}$-modules naturally associated with the Gasper–Rahman multivariable polynomials: describe their structure, weights/eigenvalues of natural commuting subalgebras, decomposition into irreducibles, and the role played by the Gasper–Rahman polynomials as overlap coefficients between distinguished eigenbases.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., work on the q-Onsager algebra and the universal Askey–Wilson algebra, and on higher-rank q-Bannai–Ito algebras with Gasper–Rahman multivariate (−q)-Racah polynomials as connection coefficients) develops related structure but does not provide a complete classification of finite-dimensional irreducible modules of the truncated quotient $A_q^{[2N+1]}$, nor a full study of the finite-dimensional modules attached to Gasper–Rahman polynomials. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Direct problem for ordinary h-fold sumsets
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let A be an m-element subset of G with m <= p < hm - h + 1. Is it true that the minimum possible size of the h-fold sumset hA is p, and that equality |hA| = p holds if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a positive integer $h$ and a finite subset $A\subseteq G$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA=\{a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h\in A\}\,. $$
For positive integers $m,h$, let
$$\rho(G,m,h)=\min\{|hA| : A\subseteq G,\ |A|=m\}\,. $$
Assume that $m\le p<hm-h+1$. Prove or disprove the following statement: under these hypotheses one has $\rho(G,m,h)=p$, and for every $m$-element subset $A\subseteq G$ the equality $|hA|=p$ holds if and only if $A$ is contained in a coset of some subgroup $H\le G$ of order $p$.
status_search_result: The conjecture appears in Bajnok's compendium of open problems on sumsets in finite abelian groups. Subsequent surveys (including recent ones in 2023–2025) continue to discuss direct and inverse problems for $\rho(G,m,h)$, but no source found in the search definitively establishes a full proof or disproof of the inverse characterization stated above. The status is therefore reported as unknown based on the available evidence.

original_question: In the boundary case where p is the smallest prime divisor of n and p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of a finite abelian group G for which the h-fold sumset hA has minimum possible size. In particular, beyond arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p, determine all subsets that can occur in this extremal case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A\}.$$
For positive integers $m, h$ with $1 \le m \le |G|$, let
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Consider the boundary case in which $p = hm - h + 1$. In this regime two known families of $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ achieve the minimum value of $|hA|$:
(i) arithmetic progressions of length $m$ in $G$ (i.e., subsets of the form $\{a, a+d, a+2d, \ldots, a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$);
(ii) $m$-element subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of order $p$.

Problem: Classify completely all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ for which $|hA|$ equals the minimum value $\rho(G, m, h)$ when $p = hm - h + 1$. In particular, determine all extremal configurations beyond the two families (i) and (ii).
category_tag: Additive combinatorics / sumsets in finite abelian groups

Related work by Bajnok and others studies ρ(G,m,h) and inverse problems, but no explicit classification of all extremal m-subsets in this boundary case was located. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

context_brief: Restricted sumset formula when m <= p
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume h < m <= p. Is the minimum size of the h-fold restricted sumset of an m-element subset always min{p, hm - h^2 + 1}? In other words, does rho_hat(G, m, h) = min{p, hm - h^2 + 1} hold throughout this range?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For an integer $h \ge 1$ and a subset $A \subseteq G$, define the $h$-fold restricted sumset of $A$ by
$$h^{\wedge} A = \{\, a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1,\dots,a_h \in A,\ a_i \neq a_j \text{ for } i \neq j\,\}.$$
For integers $m, h$ with $1 \le h \le m \le |G|$, define
$$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, |h^{\wedge} A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\,\}.$$
Assume $h < m \le p$. Prove or disprove:
$$\hat{\rho}(G, m, h) = \min\{\, p,\ hm - h^2 + 1\,\}.$$
status_search_result: For cyclic groups of prime order, the formula follows from the Dias da Silva–Hamidoune theorem (1994). For general finite abelian groups with $h<m\le p$ (smallest prime divisor of $|G|$), the equality is stated as a conjecture in Bajnok's work on restricted sumsets, and recent literature on critical numbers and restricted sumsets does not report a full proof for arbitrary finite abelian groups; only partial/related results and tight upper bounds are available. Status appears to remain open in general.

context_brief: Inverse problem for restricted sumsets above the prime threshold
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume 2 <= h <= m - 2 and p > hm - h^2 + 1. Classify the m-element subsets A of G whose h-fold restricted sumset has the minimum size hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that equality |h_hat A| = hm - h^2 + 1 occurs only in the exceptional case h = 2, m = 4 with A = {a, a + g1, a + g2, a + g1 + g2}, or when A is an arithmetic progression in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $p$ denote the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and an integer $h$ with $1 \le h \le |A|$, define the $h$-fold restricted sumset by
$$h^{\wedge} A \;=\; \{\, a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_1, \ldots, a_h \in A \text{ are pairwise distinct}\,\}.$$
Fix integers $m \ge 4$ and $h$ with $2 \le h \le m-2$, and assume that $p > hm - h^2 + 1$. It is known that under these hypotheses every $m$-element subset $A \subseteq G$ satisfies $|h^{\wedge} A| \ge hm - h^2 + 1$. Classify all $m$-element subsets $A \subseteq G$ for which equality $|h^{\wedge} A| = hm - h^2 + 1$ holds. Specifically, prove or disprove: equality holds if and only if either
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h = 2$, $m = 4$, and $A = \{a,\; a+g_1,\; a+g_2,\; a+g_1+g_2\}$ for some $a, g_1, g_2 \in G$, or
\item $A$ is an arithmetic progression in $G$, i.e., $A = \{a,\; a+d,\; a+2d,\; \ldots,\; a+(m-1)d\}$ for some $a, d \in G$.
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: For finite sets of integers, the analogous inverse result (equality forcing an arithmetic progression for $m \ge 5$) is established. For general finite abelian groups under the prime threshold $p > hm - h^2 + 1$, the classification appears to be stated as a conjecture; recent works on Kneser-type theorems and inverse Erdős–Heilbronn problems address related cases but no source verifying a complete proof of this exact classification in arbitrary finite abelian groups was found.

original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and assume m <= p < hm - h^2 + 1. Is it true that an m-element subset A satisfies |h_hat A| = p if and only if A is contained in a coset of some subgroup H of G of order p?

context_brief: Frequency of disagreement for two-fold signed sumsets
original_question: For an abelian group G of order n, compare the minimum size of a 2-fold signed sumset with the minimum size of the ordinary 2-fold sumset. Is it true that the values rho_plusminus(G, m, 2) and rho(G, m, 2) differ for fewer than n/4 choices of m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, written additively. For a subset $A \subseteq G$ and a positive integer $h$, define the $h$-fold sumset
$$hA = \{a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_h : a_i \in A\}$$
and the $h$-fold signed sumset
$$h_{\pm}A = \{\varepsilon_1 a_1 + \varepsilon_2 a_2 + \cdots + \varepsilon_h a_h : a_i \in A,\ \varepsilon_i \in \{+1,-1\}\}.$$
For integers $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ and $h \ge 1$, set
$$\rho(G, m, h) = \min\{|hA| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\},$$
$$\rho_{\pm}(G, m, h) = \min\{|h_{\pm}A| : A \subseteq G,\ |A| = m\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every finite abelian group $G$ of order $n$, the number of integers $m \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ for which
$$\rho_{\pm}(G, m, 2) \ne \rho(G, m, 2)$$
is strictly less than $n/4$.
status_search_result: A web search reveals active research on $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,h)$ vs $\rho(G,m,h)$, including results showing equality when $G$ is cyclic and resolution of related conjectures (e.g., for elementary abelian $p$-groups). However, no source directly confirming or refuting the specific quantitative claim that $\rho_{\pm}(G,m,2)$ and $\rho(G,m,2)$ disagree on fewer than $n/4$ values of $m$ for all finite abelian groups $G$ of order $n$ was found.

context_brief: Sharpness of lower bounds for chi_hat(Z_n,3)
original_question: For cyclic groups Z_n, determine whether the known lower bounds for the three-term restricted critical number chi_hat(Z_n, 3) are always sharp. More precisely, if n has a prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3 and p is the smallest such divisor, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 3 when n = p, (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 2 when n = 3p, and (1 + 1/p)n/3 + 1 otherwise? If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 mod 3, does chi_hat(Z_n, 3) always equal floor(n/3) + 4 when 9 divides n and floor(n/3) + 3 otherwise?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite abelian group G and a positive integer h, define the restricted h-fold sumset of a subset A ⊆ G by
  h^∧ A = { a_1 + a_2 + ⋯ + a_h : a_1, …, a_h ∈ A, a_i ≠ a_j for i ≠ j },
and define the restricted h-critical number χ̂(G, h) to be the smallest positive integer m such that h^∧ A = G for every subset A ⊆ G with |A| = m (when such an m exists).

Take G = Z_n, the cyclic group of order n, and h = 3. Determine whether the following equalities hold for all n ≥ 16:

(1) If n has at least one prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), and p denotes the smallest such prime divisor, then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 3   if n = p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 2   if n = 3p,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = (1 + 1/p) · n/3 + 1   otherwise.

(2) If n has no prime divisor congruent to 2 (mod 3), then
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 4   if 9 | n,
    χ̂(Z_n, 3) = ⌊n/3⌋ + 3   otherwise.

The corresponding inequalities "≥" are known to hold; the question is whether equality always holds.
status_search_result: The conjectured equality is a known generalization of a Gallardo–Grekos-type conjecture; the lower bound is proved, and equality is verified for n even, n prime, and (by computer) small n. No general proof for all n appears in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: embedding problem for H^p Dirichlet series
original_question: Let H^p denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}, with norm induced by vertical translation and equivalently by the Hardy space on the infinite-dimensional torus under the Bohr correspondence. Is there a constant C_p,L depending only on p and the fixed segment length L, but not on the coefficients or on N, such that every Dirichlet polynomial satisfies an inequality of the form \int_I |\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-1/2-it}|^p \, dt \le C_{p,L} \|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}\|_{H^p}^p for every interval I of length L on the vertical line Re s = 1/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet polynomials, i.e., finite sums $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ with complex coefficients $a_n$. For $1\le p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal H^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of $\mathscr{D}$ with respect to the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p \;=\; \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt,$$
which, via the Bohr lift $n^{-s}\mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional torus.

Fix a real number $L>0$. The question is the following:

For which $p\in[1,\infty)$ does there exist a constant $C_{p,L}>0$, depending only on $p$ and $L$, such that the inequality
$$\int_I \Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-1/2 - it}\Big|^p\,dt \;\le\; C_{p,L}\,\|F\|_{\mathcal H^p}^p$$
holds for every Dirichlet polynomial $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ (with $N\ge 1$ arbitrary and coefficients arbitrary) and for every interval $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ of length $L$ on the critical line $\operatorname{Re} s=1/2$?

For $p<2$ in particular and for non-even $p$ in general, the inequality remains an open problem; surveys on the analysis of Dirichlet series continue to list it as a central open question.

original_question: For the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series on the half-plane Re s > 1/2, characterize the Carleson measures when p<2; that is, characterize the positive measures μ on {Re s > 1/2} for which there is a constant C such that \int_{Re s>1/2} |F(s)|^p \, dμ(s) \le C \|F\|_{H^p}^p for all F in H^p.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the space of Dirichlet series $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$. For $0<p<\infty$, define the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series as the completion of the set of Dirichlet polynomials $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
$$\|P\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Bigl|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Bigr|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p}.$$
Every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

A positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ is called a Carleson measure for $\mathcal{H}^p$ if there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb{C}_{1/2}} |F(s)|^p\,d\mu(s) \;\le\; C\,\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p \qquad \text{for every } F\in\mathcal{H}^p.$$

Problem: For $0<p<2$, give an intrinsic geometric or capacitary characterization of all positive Borel measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ that are Carleson measures for $\mathcal{H}^p$.
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Carleson measures for Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series on the half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$ for $p<2$ is repeatedly stated as open in surveys and recent work on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., the 2019 survey on Hardy spaces of general Dirichlet series and subsequent work on Volterra/multiplier operators, which use partial Carleson-type embeddings without obtaining a full characterization). Even the case $p=2$ — known as the embedding problem — remains only partially understood, so the case $p<2$ is a fortiori open.

original_question: If F belongs to H^p for some p<2, must the zero set of F in the half-plane Re s > 1/2 satisfy the Blaschke condition for that half-plane, i.e. the natural summability condition on the zeros analogous to the classical Hardy-space Blaschke condition?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}^p$ (for $0<p<\infty$) denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series defined as follows. For a Dirichlet polynomial $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, set
$$\|P\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}:=\left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|P(it)|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},$$
and define $\mathcal{H}^p$ as the completion of the Dirichlet polynomials in this norm. Equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n=\mathfrak{p}^{\alpha}$ identifying $n^{-s}$ with the monomial $z^{\alpha}$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus $\mathbb{T}^{\infty}$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometric to $H^p(\mathbb{T}^{\infty})$. Every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ has an analytic extension to the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

A sequence $\{s_k\}\subset\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ is said to satisfy the Blaschke condition for $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ if
$$\sum_{k}\frac{\operatorname{Re}(s_k)-\tfrac12}{1+|s_k|^2}<\infty,$$
equivalently $\sum_k(\operatorname{Re}(s_k)-\tfrac12)/|s_k+\tfrac12|^2<\infty$ once one accounts for the conformal map onto the unit disk.

Question: Suppose $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ for some $0<p<2$ and $F\not\equiv 0$. Must the zero set of $F$ in the half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$, counted with multiplicities, satisfy the Blaschke condition for that half-plane?
status_search_result: Web searches surface surveys on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., a 2019 survey on $\mathcal{H}_p$-theory of general Dirichlet series listing open problems), but no source explicitly resolves whether zeros of $\mathcal{H}^p$ functions with $p<2$ must satisfy the Blaschke condition in $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$. No solution has been verifiably located, and the problem appears to remain open, but available evidence is inconclusive.

original_question: If F belongs to H^p for some p<2, is F locally in the Nevanlinna class in the half-plane Re s > 1/2; in other words, on every bounded subregion of that half-plane, does F have the local logarithmic-integrability property characteristic of Nevanlinna-class functions?
self_contained_problem:
For $0<p<\infty$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
$$\|F\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} |F(it)|^p \, dt\right)^{1/p}.$$
Equivalently, via Bohr's correspondence $n^{-s} \mapsto z^{\kappa(n)}$ (where $\kappa(n)$ is the multi-index of prime exponents of $n$), $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically identified with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional polytorus. Each $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$ defines a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}:=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>1/2\}$.

Recall that a holomorphic function $f$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ is said to belong locally to the Nevanlinna class if for every relatively compact subdomain $U\Subset\Omega$ with smooth boundary,
$$\sup_{r}\int_{\partial U_r} \log^+ |f(z)|\, |dz| < \infty,$$
where $\{U_r\}$ is an exhaustion of $U$; equivalently, $\log^+|f|$ has a positive harmonic majorant on every relatively compact subdomain of $\Omega$.

Question: For every $p<2$ and every $F\in\mathcal{H}^p$, does $F$ belong locally to the Nevanlinna class on the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question on whether $\mathcal{H}^p$ functions ($p<2$) of Dirichlet series are locally in the Nevanlinna class on $\operatorname{Re} s>1/2$. Related work on Nevanlinna-class Dirichlet series and a mean counting function for $\mathcal{H}^p$ exists, but no source explicitly settles this problem. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

original_question: For exponents p in (1,\infty) with p\neq 2, does the Hardy space H^p of Dirichlet series admit an unconditional basis; that is, does it have a basis for which convergence is stable under arbitrary sign changes or bounded coefficient multipliers in the usual Banach-space sense?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $p\in[1,\infty)$, let $\mathcal{H}^p$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series defined as follows. For a Dirichlet polynomial $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$, set
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \lim_{T\to\infty}\Big(\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt\Big)^{1/p},$$
and define $\mathcal{H}^p$ as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials in this norm. Equivalently, via the Bohr lift $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}p_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots\mapsto z_1^{\alpha_1}z_2^{\alpha_2}\cdots$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus equipped with normalized Haar measure.

A Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of a Banach space $X$ is called unconditional if for every $x\in X$ with expansion $x=\sum_n c_n e_n$, the series converges unconditionally (equivalently, $\sum_n \varepsilon_n c_n e_n$ converges in $X$ for every choice of signs $\varepsilon_n\in\{-1,+1\}$).

Question: For every $p\in(1,\infty)$ with $p\neq 2$, does the Banach space $\mathcal{H}^p$ admit an unconditional Schauder basis?
status_search_result: The question of whether the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series admits an unconditional basis for $p\in(1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$ appears to remain open. It is known that the canonical Dirichlet monomial basis $\{n^{-s}\}$ is unconditional in $\mathcal{H}^p$ only for $p=2$, but the existence of some other unconditional basis is unresolved. Recent literature on linear-space properties of $\mathcal{H}^p$ and on related dilation/translation systems continues to treat this as an outstanding question.

original_question: Does the Hardy space H^1 of Dirichlet series admit a Schauder basis at all, and if it does, can such a basis be chosen to be unconditional?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{D}$ denote the set of formal Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$. For a Dirichlet polynomial $P(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, define
$$\|P\|_{H^1} := \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Bigl|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Bigr|\,dt.$$
Equivalently, via the Bohr lift identifying $n^{-s}$ with the monomial $z^{\kappa(n)}$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ (where $\kappa(n)=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\dots)$ is the exponent vector in the prime factorization $n=\prod_j p_j^{\kappa_j}$), the norm equals $\|P\|_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^\infty)}$. The Hardy space $H^1$ of Dirichlet series is the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials under this norm.

Recall that a sequence $(e_k)_{k\geq 1}$ in a Banach space $X$ is a Schauder basis if every $x\in X$ has a unique norm-convergent expansion $x=\sum_k c_k(x)e_k$, and it is unconditional if this convergence is unconditional for every $x\in X$.

(a) Does $H^1$ admit a Schauder basis?

(b) If so, can such a basis be chosen to be unconditional?
status_search_result: The canonical system $\{n^{-s}\}$ is known to be a Schauder basis of $H^p$ for $1<p<\infty$ and only a Markushevich basis (not Schauder) for $H^1$; it is unconditional only when $p=2$. Whether $H^1$ of Dirichlet series admits any Schauder basis, and whether it admits an unconditional one, appears to remain open in the literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series; recent works (e.g., on translated Hardy spaces and Fourier multipliers) treat related but distinct questions without resolving these.

original_question: Let H^p(T^\infty) be the Hardy space on the infinite-dimensional torus, viewed as boundary values of analytic functions on the infinite polydisc D^\infty. What general conditions on a radial or non-tangential approach to a boundary point of T^\infty guarantee that a Fatou-type theorem holds, meaning that functions in H^p(T^\infty) have almost-everywhere boundary limits along that approach?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}^\infty = \{ z = (z_1, z_2, \ldots) : z_j \in \mathbb{C},\ |z_j| < 1 \text{ for all } j,\ \sup_j |z_j| < 1 \}$ be the infinite polydisc, and let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{j=1}^\infty \{ |w_j| = 1 \}$ be the infinite-dimensional torus, equipped with the product Haar (Lebesgue) measure $m_\infty$. For $1 \le p \le \infty$, let $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ denote the Hardy space defined as the closure in $L^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty, m_\infty)$ of the analytic trigonometric polynomials (those whose Fourier coefficients are supported on multi-indices $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ with $\alpha_j \ge 0$ for all $j$). Each $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ corresponds to an analytic function $\widetilde{f}$ on $\mathbb{D}^\infty$ (defined for instance on $\bigcup_{0<r<1} r\,\mathbb{D}^\infty$ via its monomial expansion), and $f$ is recovered as a boundary value of $\widetilde{f}$.

For a point $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, an "approach family" to $w$ is a family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ of subsets $A_w \subset \mathbb{D}^\infty$ accumulating at $w$ (e.g., the radial approach $\{rw : 0 < r < 1\}$, or some non-tangential analogue).

Problem. Determine general conditions on such an approach family $\{A_w\}_{w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty}$ — radial or non-tangential — under which a Fatou-type theorem holds: namely, for every $f \in H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ and for $m_\infty$-almost every $w \in \mathbb{T}^\infty$, the limit
$$\lim_{\substack{z \to w \\ z \in A_w}} \widetilde{f}(z)$$
exists and equals $f(w)$.
category_tag: Hardy spaces on the infinite polydisc
status_search_result: The problem of identifying general radial or non-tangential approach regions yielding a.e. boundary limits for $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ functions remains a delicate one. Aleman, Olsen, and Saksman (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique, 2019) established several Fatou-type theorems for restricted modes of radial convergence and showed that the pointwise Fatou theorem fails in infinite dimensions without such restrictions even for bounded analytic functions. No comprehensive characterization of admissible radial/non-tangential approaches has been found in subsequent literature, so the problem appears to remain open in its general form, with only partial results.

original_question: For the Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series, especially in the non-locally-convex range 0<p<1 highlighted just before the question, describe their dual spaces; equivalently, determine the continuous linear functionals on H^p and represent them in an explicit usable form.
self_contained_problem:
For a Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$, recall the following construction. By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, each integer $n\ge 1$ factors uniquely as $n=p_1^{\kappa_1}p_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$ where $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ are the primes. The Bohr correspondence assigns to $f$ the formal power series $\mathcal{B}f(z)=\sum_n a_n z^{\kappa(n)}$ in infinitely many variables $z=(z_1,z_2,\dots)$, where $z^{\kappa(n)}=z_1^{\kappa_1}z_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$. For $0<p<\infty$, the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm (quasi-norm when $0<p<1$)
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} := \left(\int_{\mathbb{T}^\infty} |\mathcal{B}f(z)|^p\, dm_\infty(z)\right)^{1/p},$$
where $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ is the infinite-dimensional torus and $m_\infty$ is its normalized Haar measure. Equivalently (by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem), $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p}^p = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T |f(it)|^p\,dt$ for Dirichlet polynomials.

For $1<p<\infty$, $\mathcal{H}^p$ is a reflexive Banach space, but for $0<p\le 1$ — and especially in the non-locally-convex range $0<p<1$ — the structure of the topological dual is far less understood.

Problem. Describe the dual space $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$. That is, characterize all continuous linear functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ and provide an explicit, usable concrete representation of them (for instance, as a space of Dirichlet series or via pairings with such, together with a norm or quasi-norm equivalent to the dual norm).
status_search_result: Subsequent literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g., works on linear space properties of $\mathcal{H}^p$, multipliers, and Volterra operators) continues to investigate functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$ for $0<p\le 1$ — for instance establishing that $\varphi_\beta(s)=\sum n^{-\beta-s}$ defines a bounded functional on $\mathcal{H}^p$ when $\beta>1/p$ and not when $\beta<1/p$, and conjecturing the boundary case. However, no full description of $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ for $0<p<1$ appears in the literature; the problem is referenced as still open in recent surveys and papers.

original_question: On the infinite-dimensional torus T^\infty, what should replace Nehari’s theorem for Hankel forms or small Hankel operators? In particular, how should one characterize the Riesz projection of L^\infty(T^\infty) and the corresponding bounded-mean-oscillation-type spaces on T^\infty?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^\infty = \prod_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{T}$ denote the infinite-dimensional torus equipped with its normalized Haar measure. For a multi-index $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ (finitely supported integer sequences), let $z^\alpha = \prod_n z_n^{\alpha_n}$ denote the corresponding character. Define the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ as the closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ spanned by $\{z^\alpha : \alpha \ge 0\}$ (i.e., $\alpha_n \ge 0$ for all $n$), and let $P_+ : L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty) \to H^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ be the orthogonal Riesz projection. For an analytic symbol $\psi = \sum_{\alpha \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha) z^\alpha$, the (small) Hankel form is defined on finite analytic polynomials by
$$H_\psi(f,g) = \sum_{\alpha,\beta \ge 0} \hat\psi(\alpha+\beta)\, \hat f(\alpha)\, \hat g(\beta),$$
with norm $\|H_\psi\|$ as a bilinear form on $H^2 \times H^2$.

Nehari's classical theorem on $\mathbb{T}$ states that $H_\psi$ is bounded if and only if $\psi = P_+\varphi$ for some $\varphi \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T})$, with $\|H_\psi\| \asymp \inf\{\|\varphi\|_\infty : P_+\varphi = \psi\}$.

Problem: Formulate and establish the appropriate counterpart of Nehari's theorem on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. Specifically, characterize intrinsically the space $P_+(L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty))$ — the Riesz projection of $L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ — and identify natural BMO-type spaces on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ that govern the boundedness of Hankel forms / small Hankel operators in this infinite-dimensional setting.
category_tag: Hankel forms and BMO on the infinite torus
status_search_result: Searches indicate this remains an open problem. The classical Nehari theorem holds on finite polydisks $\mathbb{T}^d$ (Ferguson–Lacey for $d=2$, Lacey–Terwilleger for $d>2$), but the constants grow at least exponentially in the dimension (work building on Helson), which precludes a direct passage to $\mathbb{T}^\infty$. No intrinsic characterization of $P_+(L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty))$ or of a corresponding BMO space adequate to characterize bounded Hankel forms on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ has been established.

original_question: Consider the Dirichlet-series symbol \u03d5_0(s)=1+\sum_{n=2}^\infty (\log n)^{-1} n^{-1/2-s}, which arises as the analytic symbol of the multiplicative Hilbert matrix. Is \u03d5_0 the Riesz projection of some essentially bounded function on the infinite-dimensional torus T^\infty?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ denote the infinite-dimensional torus, equipped with its normalized Haar measure. For $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ with Fourier expansion $f(z) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}} \hat{f}(\alpha) z^\alpha$ (where $\mathbb{Z}^{(\infty)}$ denotes finitely supported integer multi-indices), the Riesz projection $P_+ f$ is defined by
$$P_+ f(z) = \sum_{\alpha \geq 0} \hat{f}(\alpha) z^\alpha,$$
the sum being taken over multi-indices with all nonnegative entries. Via the Bohr correspondence $z_j \leftrightarrow p_j^{-s}$ (where $p_j$ is the $j$-th prime), an analytic function on $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ corresponds to a Dirichlet series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$.

Consider the Dirichlet series
$$\phi_0(s) = 1 + \sum_{n=2}^\infty \frac{1}{\log n}\, n^{-1/2 - s},$$
which is the analytic symbol of the multiplicative Hilbert matrix $\bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{mn}\,\log(mn)}\bigr)_{m,n\geq 2}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $F \in L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ such that, under the Bohr correspondence, $\phi_0$ corresponds to the analytic projection $P_+ F$?
status_search_result: The problem was posed in connection with the multiplicative Hilbert matrix and its analytic symbol. Subsequent literature on Riesz projection for Dirichlet series and on critical exponents of the Riesz projection (through 2024) discusses the question and related embedding problems but does not appear to resolve it. No source located indicates that $\phi_0$ has been shown to be (or fail to be) the Riesz projection of an $L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ function, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Characterize the compact composition operators on H^2, the Hilbert space of Dirichlet series with square-summable coefficients. Equivalently, determine exactly which analytic self-maps that induce composition on Dirichlet series act compactly on H^2.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{H}^2$ denote the Hilbert space of Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n n^{-s}$ with square-summable coefficients, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_{\mathscr{H}^2}^2=\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2$. By a theorem of Gordon and Hedenmalm, an analytic function $\varphi:\mathbb{C}_{1/2}\to\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$ (where $\mathbb{C}_\theta=\{s\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re} s>\theta\}$) induces a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi f = f\circ\varphi$ on $\mathscr{H}^2$ if and only if $\varphi$ admits a representation
$$\varphi(s) = c_0 s + \sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n n^{-s},$$
with $c_0\in\mathbb{N}_0$ a non-negative integer, the Dirichlet series $\sum_n c_n n^{-s}$ converges uniformly in $\mathbb{C}_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and either (a) $c_0\geq 1$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_0$, or (b) $c_0=0$ and $\varphi$ maps $\mathbb{C}_0$ into $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$.

Problem: Give a complete characterization of those symbols $\varphi$ in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class for which the composition operator $C_\varphi:\mathscr{H}^2\to\mathscr{H}^2$ is compact.
category_tag: Composition operators on Dirichlet series spaces
status_search_result: Brevig and Perfekt (Advances in Mathematics 385 (2021), 107775; arXiv:2005.05094) introduced a mean counting function for Dirichlet series and characterized the compact composition operators with Dirichlet series symbols on $\mathscr{H}^2$: $C_\varphi$ is compact iff the mean counting function of $\varphi$ satisfies a specified decay condition at the boundary of the half-plane $\mathbb{C}_{1/2}$. This resolves the characterization problem in the Gordon–Hedenmalm class.

original_question: For the partial sums of the ordinary Dirichlet series with all coefficients equal to 1, is the H^1 norm strictly smaller than the square-root scale in the sense that \|\sum_{n=1}^N n^{-s}\|_{H^1}=o(\sqrt{N}) as N\to\infty?
self_contained_problem:
For a complex variable $s$, consider the ordinary Dirichlet polynomial
$$D_N(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{N} n^{-s}.$$
Let $H^1$ denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials with respect to the norm
$$\Big\|\sum_{n} a_n n^{-s}\Big\|_{H^1} = \lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\Big|\sum_{n} a_n n^{-it}\Big|\,dt,$$
or equivalently, via the Bohr lift, as the $L^1$-norm on the infinite-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^\infty$ of the corresponding multiplicative Fourier series. Equivalently, via Bohr's correspondence,
$$\|D_N\|_{H^1} \;=\; \mathbb{E}\Big|\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(n)\Big|,$$
where $f$ is the Steinhaus random multiplicative function (i.e., $f(p)$ for primes $p$ are independent random variables uniformly distributed on the unit circle, extended completely multiplicatively).

Determine whether
$$\|D_N\|_{H^1} \;=\; o(\sqrt{N})\qquad \text{as } N\to\infty.$$
status_search_result: Helson's problem was resolved affirmatively by A. J. Harper, who proved that $\mathbb{E}|\sum_{n\le N} f(n)| \asymp \sqrt{N}/(\log\log N)^{1/4}$ for the Steinhaus random multiplicative function $f$, which is equivalent (via Bohr lift) to $\|\sum_{n=1}^N n^{-s}\|_{H^1} \asymp \sqrt{N}/(\log\log N)^{1/4} = o(\sqrt{N})$. A short alternative proof was given by Gorodetsky (2024/2025).

context_brief: higher moments of homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials
original_question: Fix an integer k>1. For which values of m=m(N) are the L^{2k} norms of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials of length N comparable to their L^2 norms, where m-homogeneous means that the summation is restricted to integers n with exactly m prime factors counted with multiplicity, i.e. \Omega(n)=m?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer N≥1 and integer m≥1, an m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomial of length N is a finite Dirichlet series of the form
   P(s) = Σ_{n≤N, Ω(n)=m} a_n n^{-s},
where Ω(n) denotes the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity, and (a_n) are complex coefficients. For q≥1, define the L^q norm by
   ‖P‖_q = ( lim_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T |P(it)|^q dt )^{1/q}.
By orthogonality, ‖P‖_2^2 = Σ |a_n|^2.

Fix an integer k>1. Determine the range of m = m(N) (as N→∞) for which there exists a constant C = C(k) (independent of N and of the coefficients) such that
   ‖P‖_{2k} ≤ C ‖P‖_2
holds for every m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomial P of length N. Equivalently, characterize those m=m(N) for which the L^{2k} and L^2 norms are comparable on the space of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials of length N.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this comparability question for higher moments of m-homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials. Related work (Bohnenblust–Hille type and hypercontractive estimates for homogeneous Dirichlet polynomials) addresses sup-norm vs. coefficient norms, but the precise threshold m=m(N) for which ‖·‖_{2k} ≍ ‖·‖_2 (k≥2 integer) does not appear to have been established. Status appears open.

original_question: Determine the asymptotic behavior, as N\to\infty, of the H^p norm of the critically weighted Dirichlet polynomial \sum_{n=1}^N n^{-1/2-s} for every exponent 0<p\le 1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{P}$ denote the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$, where $s$ is a complex variable. For $0<p<\infty$, define the Hardy space norm
$$\|f\|_{H^p} \;=\; \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T\Big|\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-it}\Big|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},$$
which makes $\mathscr{P}$ into a normed space whose completion is the Hardy space $H^p$ of Dirichlet series.

For each integer $N\ge 1$, consider the critically weighted Dirichlet polynomial
$$Z_N(s) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^N \frac{1}{n^{1/2+s}}.$$

Determine, for every exponent $0<p\le 1$, the precise asymptotic behavior of $\|Z_N\|_{H^p}$ as $N\to\infty$.
status_search_result: A search of the recent literature on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (work of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman, Seip and collaborators, including subsequent papers on linear-space properties of $H^p$, contractive inequalities, and almost-periodic Hardy–Stein identities) does not turn up a determination of the asymptotics of $\|\sum_{n\le N} n^{-1/2-s}\|_{H^p}$ for $0<p\le 1$. The question is closely related to Helson-type problems on $H^1$ norms of partial sums of $\zeta$ on the critical line, which remain unresolved. No source surveyed reports a solution, so the problem appears to be still open.

original_question: Fix a real parameter \gamma. Determine the precise asymptotic growth, as N\to\infty, of the H^p norm of the weighted Dirichlet polynomial \sum_{n=1}^N [d(n)]^\gamma n^{-1/2-s}, where d(n) is the divisor function, in the range p\le 1.
self_contained_problem:
For $0<p<\infty$, the Hardy space $H^p$ of Dirichlet series is defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s)=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}$ under the norm
\[
\|f\|_{H^p} := \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt\right)^{1/p},
\]
equivalently realized via the Bohr correspondence as the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ on the infinite-dimensional polytorus.

Let $d(n)=\sum_{k\mid n}1$ denote the classical divisor function, and fix a real parameter $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$. For each integer $N\ge 1$, consider the weighted Dirichlet polynomial
\[
F_{N,\gamma}(s) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{N} \bigl[d(n)\bigr]^{\gamma}\, n^{-1/2-s}.
\]

Determine, for every $0<p\le 1$, the precise asymptotic growth of $\|F_{N,\gamma}\|_{H^p}$ as $N\to\infty$, as a function of $N$, $\gamma$, and $p$.
status_search_result: Searches on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series, weighted critical Dirichlet polynomials and the divisor function did not surface a published proof of the precise asymptotics in the regime $0<p\le 1$. Related work by Bondarenko–Brevig–Saksman–Seip and follow-ups treats the case $p\ge 1$ and partial estimates for $p<1$, but the sharp asymptotic for $p\le 1$ does not appear to be established. Status remains unverified.

original_question: Let S_N act on a Dirichlet series \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s} by truncation to its first N terms, S_N(\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s})=\sum_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}. What is the precise asymptotic growth, as N\to\infty, of the operator norm of S_N on H^1? More generally, what is the corresponding asymptotic for H^p when p\le 1 and for p=\infty?
self_contained_problem:
For 0 < p ≤ ∞, let H^p denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, defined as the completion of the space of Dirichlet polynomials f(s) = Σ_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s} under the norm

  ‖f‖_{H^p} = lim_{T→∞} ( (1/T) ∫_0^T |f(it)|^p dt )^{1/p}        (with the usual modification for p = ∞, taking the supremum on the imaginary axis),

equivalently realized via the Bohr lift as H^p of the infinite-dimensional polytorus. For each positive integer N, let S_N be the partial sum operator

  S_N : Σ_{n=1}^∞ a_n n^{-s}  ↦  Σ_{n=1}^N a_n n^{-s}.

Determine the precise asymptotic growth, as N → ∞, of the operator norm ‖S_N‖_{H^p → H^p} in the following cases:
(i) p = 1;
(ii) 0 < p < 1;
(iii) p = ∞.
status_search_result: For 1 < p < ∞, Helson's classical theorem gives boundedness of S_N on H^p. For p ∈ (0,1] and p = ∞, only upper and lower bounds are known (e.g. work of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman, Seip and others, supplementing Helson's result), with no matching precise asymptotic. Recent literature continues to refer to the exact asymptotic growth as an open problem.

original_question: Let \chi(p) be independent identically distributed random variables, uniformly distributed on the unit circle T for primes p, and extend multiplicatively by \chi(n)=\prod_{j=1}^\ell \chi(p_j)^{k_j} when n=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_\ell^{k_\ell}. Determine the almost sure growth rate, as N increases, of the random character sum \sum_{n=1}^N \chi(n).
self_contained_problem: Let $\{\chi(p)\}_{p\text{ prime}}$ be a family of independent and identically distributed random variables, each uniformly distributed on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|=1\}$. Extend $\chi$ to a completely multiplicative function on the positive integers by setting $\chi(1)=1$ and, for $n=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_\ell^{k_\ell}$ with distinct primes $p_j$, $\chi(n)=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}\chi(p_j)^{k_j}$. (This is the Steinhaus random multiplicative function.) Define the partial sums $S_N=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\chi(n)$. Determine the almost sure growth rate of $|S_N|$ as $N\to\infty$; that is, find a deterministic function $\psi(N)$ such that $|S_N|/\psi(N)$ has a finite, nonzero (almost sure) limsup behavior, and quantify both the almost sure upper and lower asymptotic envelopes of $S_N$.
status_search_result: The exact almost sure growth rate remains undetermined. Harper (2020, IMRN 2023) proved that almost surely there exist arbitrarily large $x$ with $|\sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)|\ge \sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+o(1)}$, the first lower bound exceeding $\sqrt{x}$, and conjectured the exponent $1/4$ is sharp. Subsequent work (Caich 2023, and others on related models) has narrowed upper bounds toward $\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{C}$ but a matching tight almost sure asymptotic has not been established, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Current sharp estimates for greatest-common-divisor sums \sum_{k,\ell\le N} ((\gcd(n_k,n_\ell))^{2\alpha})/(n_k n_\ell)^\alpha and their optimized variants can be interpreted through Poisson integrals on infinite polydiscs. Can these estimates be systematically linked to the function theory and operator theory of the Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series, for example through analogues of Poisson-kernel or bounded-mean-oscillation phenomena?
self_contained_problem:
For a real parameter $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and a finite set of distinct positive integers $n_1,\dots,n_N$, consider the GCD sum
$$S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N)=\sum_{k,\ell=1}^{N}\frac{(\gcd(n_k,n_\ell))^{2\alpha}}{(n_k n_\ell)^{\alpha}},$$
together with its optimized (weighted) variants. Such sums admit a representation as Poisson-type integrals on the infinite-dimensional polydisc $\mathbb{T}^\infty$, via Bohr's correspondence between Dirichlet series and power series in infinitely many variables. Let $\mathscr{H}^p$ ($1\le p\le\infty$) denote the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $f(s)=\sum_{n\ge 1} a_n n^{-s}$, defined as the closure of Dirichlet polynomials under the norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathscr{H}^p}=\Bigl(\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(it)|^p\,dt\Bigr)^{1/p}\qquad(1\le p<\infty),$$
which by Bohr's lift coincides with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite polydisc.

Establish a systematic correspondence between the sharp upper bounds (and lower bounds) for $S_\alpha$ and its optimized variants on the one hand, and the function-theoretic and operator-theoretic structure of the spaces $\mathscr{H}^p$ on the other. Concretely, develop analogues for $\mathscr{H}^p$ of classical phenomena such as:
(i) Poisson kernel representations and boundary behaviour,
(ii) bounded mean oscillation (BMO) and its duality with $\mathscr{H}^1$,
that recover, refine, or interpret the known GCD-sum estimates as quantitative statements about norms, embeddings, multipliers, or operators acting on $\mathscr{H}^p$.
category_tag: Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series and GCD sums
status_search_result: The problem is a programmatic research direction asking to systematically tie GCD sum estimates to the function/operator theory of Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. While individual results connecting GCD sums to Poisson integrals on polydiscs exist (e.g., Aistleitner–Berkes–Seip), and ongoing work develops Poisson semigroups, multipliers, BMO-type results and translated Hardy spaces for Dirichlet series, no comprehensive linkage of the full GCD-sum estimate framework to $\mathscr{H}^p$ theory has been completed; the problem remains open as an active research program.

original_question: Develop further applications of the recent GCD-sum and Dirichlet-series methods to the Riemann zeta function, and clarify new structural links between those estimates and the behavior of \zeta(s), especially on or near the critical line.
self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n_1,\dots,n_N$, define the GCD sum
$$S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N) \;=\; \sum_{j,k=1}^{N} \frac{(\gcd(n_j,n_k))^{2\alpha}}{(n_j n_k)^{\alpha}}, \qquad 0<\alpha\le 1,$$
and let
$$\Gamma_\alpha(N) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{ S_\alpha(n_1,\dots,n_N) : 1\le n_1<\dots<n_N \bigr\}.$$
Recent work has shown, via the resonance method of Soundararajan together with sharp estimates for $\Gamma_{1/2}(N)$, that
$$\max_{T^{1/2}\le t\le T} \bigl|\zeta\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}+it\bigr)\bigr| \;\ge\; \exp\!\left(\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{\sqrt 2}+o(1)\Bigr)\sqrt{\frac{\log T\,\log\log\log T}{\log\log T}}\right).$$
The problem is to develop further applications of GCD-sum estimates and the associated Dirichlet-series techniques to the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$, and to establish new structural links between such estimates and the behavior of $\zeta(s)$ on or near the critical line $\Re s = 1/2$. Concretely, one seeks:
(i) improved unconditional lower bounds for $\max_{t\in[T^\theta,T]} |\zeta(1/2+it)|$ for various $\theta\in[0,1)$, derived from refined bounds on $\Gamma_\alpha(N)$ or related multiplicative quadratic forms;
(ii) corresponding bounds for the imaginary part $\arg\zeta(1/2+it)$ and for $1/\zeta(1/2+it)$;
(iii) analogous applications to moments $\int_0^T |\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2k}\,dt$ and to the value distribution of $\zeta$ inside the critical strip;
(iv) a clarification of the precise relationship between the asymptotic order of $\Gamma_\alpha(N)$ as $N\to\infty$ and the maximal growth of $|\zeta(1/2+it)|$, including whether the constant $1/\sqrt 2$ above is optimal for the resonance-based approach.
category_tag: GCD sums and the Riemann zeta function
status_search_result: The problem is a broad research direction asking for further applications of GCD-sum/Dirichlet-series methods to ζ(s). Subsequent works (e.g., refinements of the resonance method, lower bounds for max|ζ(1/2+it)|, and applications to 1/|ζ| and large values in short intervals) have produced partial advances, but the program as a whole remains active and open with no definitive resolution.

context_brief: maxima of zeta on short intervals
original_question: Let \omega be uniformly distributed on [0,T], and consider the random field h \mapsto \log|\zeta(1/2+i h+i\omega)| on h\in[0,1]. Is it true that, as T\to\infty, the maximum over h\in[0,1] satisfies max_{h\in[0,1]} \log|\zeta(1/2+i h+i\omega)| = \log\log T - (3/4)\log\log\log T + E, where the error term E stays bounded in probability?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta$ denote the Riemann zeta function. Let $T>0$ and let $\omega$ be a random variable uniformly distributed on $[0,T]$ (so that $[0,T]$ is regarded as a probability space with normalized Lebesgue measure). Define the random variable
$$M(\omega,T) := \max_{h\in[0,1]} \log\bigl|\zeta\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}+i h + i\omega\bigr)\bigr|.$$
Prove or disprove: as $T\to\infty$,
$$M(\omega,T) = \log\log T - \tfrac{3}{4}\log\log\log T + E(\omega,T),$$
where the error term $E(\omega,T)$ is bounded in probability as $T\to\infty$ (i.e., for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C_\varepsilon>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(|E(\omega,T)|>C_\varepsilon)<\varepsilon$ for all sufficiently large $T$).
status_search_result: This is the Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating conjecture for the maximum of |ζ(1/2+it)| on a typical short interval. Arguello-Bourgade and collaborators have established it in successive works ("The Fyodorov–Hiary–Keating Conjecture I" (2020) proving the tightness of the centered maximum, "II" (2023) proving the conjectured limiting law of the recentered maximum), and a 2024 preprint extends it to mesoscopic intervals. The leading two-term asymptotic with tightness of the error has been established, so the precise statement asked here (boundedness in probability of E) is essentially proved in the literature, although the original conjecture also predicts a specific limiting distribution which has been settled more recently.

context_brief: non-Gaussian chaos from random Dirichlet series
original_question: Let X(x)=\sum_p p^{-1/2}(\cos(x\log p)\cos \theta_p + \sin(x\log p)\sin \theta_p), where the sum runs over primes and the random phases \theta_p are independent and uniformly distributed on [0,2\pi]. Study the properties of the non-Gaussian multiplicative-chaos-type field formally written as exp(\beta X(x)).
self_contained_problem:
For each prime $p$, let $\theta_p$ be independent random variables uniformly distributed on $[0,2\pi]$. Define the random field
$$X(x) \;=\; \sum_{p \text{ prime}} p^{-1/2}\bigl(\cos(x\log p)\cos\theta_p + \sin(x\log p)\sin\theta_p\bigr), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
For a parameter $\beta>0$, consider the formal exponential $e^{\beta X(x)}$. Since the series defining $X$ does not converge pointwise, one must regularize it (for instance by truncating the sum to primes $p\le N$, obtaining $X_N$, and considering $e^{\beta X_N(x)}/\mathbb{E}[e^{\beta X_N(x)}]\,dx$) and study the resulting non-Gaussian multiplicative-chaos-type random measure as $N\to\infty$.

Investigate the properties of this non-Gaussian multiplicative chaos $\text{``}e^{\beta X(x)}\text{''}$: in particular, for which values of $\beta$ does the regularized measure converge to a nontrivial limit (subcritical phase), determine the critical value $\beta_c$, establish existence and uniqueness of the limiting measure independently of the regularization scheme, characterize the support and multifractal structure of the limit, and analyze the moments and the freezing/critical behavior at $\beta=\beta_c$.
status_search_result: Recent work has constructed non-Gaussian multiplicative chaos measures from random Dirichlet series of this type and established universality (independence of approximation scheme) in the subcritical regime, including a non-Gaussian analogue of Shamov's characterization. The L^1-regime and phase transitions for related holomorphic multiplicative chaos have also been studied. However, a complete description (e.g., the critical and supercritical regimes, full multifractal analysis) is still an active research area, so the problem is partially solved.

context_brief: Schur positivity for normalized Schur-seed outputs
original_question: Fix a partition μ of d and coprime integers a,b ≥ 1. Let Θ_{a,b} be the paper’s elliptic-Hall-algebra operator embedding, and for any seed f_d define f_d^(a,b)(x;q,t) := Θ_{a,b}(f_d)(1). The question is whether the normalized Schur-seed output (-qt)^(-ι(μ)) s_μ^(a,b)(x;q,t) is always Schur-positive, meaning that its expansion in the Schur basis has coefficients in N[q,t], for every partition μ of d and every coprime pair (a,b). The paper also asks for a representation-theoretic explanation of this positivity in terms of bigraded subrepresentations of the S_n-module of generalized diagonal harmonics.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Lambda_{q,t} = \mathbb{Q}(q,t)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\Lambda$ denote the algebra of symmetric functions in variables $x = (x_1,x_2,\dots)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(q,t)$, with Schur basis $\{s_\lambda\}$. Recall the elliptic Hall algebra $\mathcal{E}_{q,t}$ of Burban–Schiffmann and its standard action on $\Lambda_{q,t}$: for each pair of coprime integers $(a,b)$ with $a,b\ge 1$, there is an embedding 
$$\Theta_{a,b}\colon \Lambda_{q,t}\longrightarrow \mathrm{End}\bigl(\Lambda_{q,t}\bigr),$$
sending a symmetric function $f_d$ of degree $d$ to an operator $\Theta_{a,b}(f_d)$ on $\Lambda_{q,t}$, in such a way that $\Theta_{1,0}$ recovers multiplication operators, $\Theta_{0,1}$ recovers the Macdonald eigenoperators (so that $\Theta_{0,1}(e_n)$ is, up to normalization, the operator $\nabla$ on the modified Macdonald basis), and $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ acts by automorphisms cycling these slopes.

For every symmetric function $f_d$ of degree $d$ define
$$f_d^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) \;:=\; \Theta_{a,b}(f_d)(1) \;\in\; \Lambda_{q,t}.$$

For a partition $\mu$ of $d$ let $\iota(\mu) := \sum_i \binom{\mu_i}{2}$ (or, equivalently, $n(\mu')$ in the standard notation), and consider the normalized Schur image
$$\widetilde{s}_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t) \;:=\; (-qt)^{-\iota(\mu)}\, s_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t).$$

Prove or disprove: for every $d\ge 1$, every partition $\mu \vdash d$, and every coprime pair of integers $a,b\ge 1$, the symmetric function $\widetilde{s}_\mu^{(a,b)}(x;q,t)$ is Schur-positive, i.e. its expansion in the Schur basis has all coefficients in $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$. Furthermore, give a representation-theoretic interpretation of this positivity in terms of bigraded $S_n$-subrepresentations of the module of generalized diagonal harmonics.
category_tag: Elliptic Hall algebra and Schur positivity
status_search_result: The conjectural Schur positivity of the normalized images of Schur functions under the elliptic-Hall-algebra slope-$(a,b)$ operators (a rational/(a,b)-generalization of the classical $\nabla s_\mu$ Schur-positivity conjecture of Bergeron–Garsia–Haiman–Tesler) appears to remain open in general. Recent work (e.g., Blasiak–Haiman–Morse–Pun–Seelinger on Catalanimals and LLT positivity, and Negut/Mellit-style results) has established related positivity statements and the shuffle/rational shuffle theorem at the level of $\Theta_{a,b}(p_n)$ and $\Theta_{a,b}(e_n)$, but a general proof for arbitrary Schur seeds $s_\mu$ and arbitrary coprime $(a,b)$, together with the representation-theoretic interpretation via bigraded subrepresentations of generalized diagonal harmonics, has not been reported.
