context_brief: Two-sided Hölder Green function on R
original_question: Find a compact set K contained in the real line for which the Green function g_{C\K} has two-sided Hölder behavior near K. That is, determine whether there exists α>0 and constants C1,C2>0 such that, for all z with sufficiently small δ=dist(z,K), one has C1·δ^α ≤ g_{C\K}(z) ≤ C2·δ^α.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a compact subset of the real line such that the unbounded connected component $\Omega = \mathbb{C} \setminus K$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem, and let $g_{\Omega}: \mathbb{C}\setminus K \to [0,\infty)$ denote the Green function of $\Omega$ with logarithmic pole at infinity (so $g_{\Omega}$ is harmonic on $\Omega$, vanishes quasi-everywhere on $K$, and satisfies $g_{\Omega}(z) = \log|z| + O(1)$ as $|z|\to\infty$). For $z \in \mathbb{C}\setminus K$, set $\delta(z) = \operatorname{dist}(z,K)$.

Construct (or prove the existence of) a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ together with a number $\alpha>0$ and constants $C_1, C_2 > 0$ such that, for every $z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with $\delta(z)$ sufficiently small,
$$ C_1\,\delta(z)^{\alpha} \;\le\; g_{\Omega}(z) \;\le\; C_2\,\delta(z)^{\alpha}. $$
That is, exhibit a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ for which the Green function of its complement satisfies a two-sided Hölder estimate near $K$ with the same exponent $\alpha$ on both sides.
status_search_result: The problem is attributed to A. Volberg and appears in a list of open problems concerning orthogonal polynomials on fractals. Related work establishes upper Hölder bounds (Hölder continuity) for Green functions of Cantor-type sets and Wiener-type characterizations, but I could not find published evidence settling the existence of a compact subset of the real line with matching two-sided Hölder behavior of the same exponent. Status appears unresolved based on available sources.

original_question: Characterize the growth rates of the Markov factors M_n(K), where M_n(K) is the operator norm of differentiation on holomorphic polynomials of degree at most n with the uniform norm on an infinite compact set K, that determine the boundary of the 'zone of uncertainty' for the extension property. Here the extension property means the existence of a continuous linear extension operator from the Whitney function space E(K) to the space of infinitely differentiable functions on R^d.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an infinite compact set. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, denote by $\mathcal{P}_n$ the space of (holomorphic) polynomials of degree at most $n$, equipped with the uniform norm $\|p\|_K = \sup_{x \in K} |p(x)|$, and define the $n$-th Markov factor of $K$ by
$$M_n(K) = \sup\{\|p'\|_K : p \in \mathcal{P}_n, \ \|p\|_K \le 1\}.$$
Let $\mathcal{E}(K)$ denote the Whitney space of jets on $K$ that extend to $C^\infty$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$. The set $K$ is said to have the extension property (EP) if there exists a continuous linear operator $L : \mathcal{E}(K) \to C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that $L$ is a right inverse of the natural restriction map.

It is known that:
(a) if $(M_n(K))_n$ grows at most polynomially in $n$ (i.e., $K$ is a Markov set), then $K$ has EP;
(b) there exist compact sets $K$ with arbitrarily fast growth of $(M_n(K))_n$ that fail to have EP, as well as compact sets with fast growth of $(M_n(K))_n$ that do have EP.
Hence there is a "zone of uncertainty": growth rates of $(M_n(K))_n$ that are compatible with both presence and absence of EP.

Problem. Characterize precisely those growth rates $\varphi(n)$ of the Markov factors $M_n(K)$ that lie on the boundary of this zone of uncertainty for the extension property; that is, identify the threshold growth rates separating those for which $M_n(K) \le \varphi(n)$ forces $K$ to have EP, from those compatible with the failure of EP.
category_tag: Markov factors and Whitney extension property
status_search_result: The problem appears to be a well-known open problem posed by Goncharov in connection with Mityagin's extension problem. Existing results show the extension property cannot be fully characterized purely by Markov-factor growth (examples exist where slower Markov growth fails EP while faster growth has it), but the precise boundary of the "zone of uncertainty" remains unresolved in the literature available, and recent surveys still list it as open.

original_question: Let (f_n) be a regular polynomial sequence, meaning f_n(z)=Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j with d_n≥2 for every n and with positive constants A1,A2,A3 such that |a_{n,d_n}|≥A1, |a_{n,j}|≤A2|a_{n,d_n}| for 0≤j<d_n, and log|a_{n,d_n}|≤A3 d_n. Assume the generalized Julia set J(f_n) is a Cantor-type subset of the real line. Prove that the recurrence coefficients in the three-term recurrence for the equilibrium measure μ_{J(f_n)} are asymptotically almost periodic, in the sense that they converge to an almost periodic sequence up to an error tending to zero.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. For each n ∈ ℕ, let f_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d_n} a_{n,j} z^j be a polynomial with complex coefficients of degree d_n ≥ 2. Call the sequence (f_n) a regular polynomial sequence if there exist positive constants A_1, A_2, A_3 (independent of n) such that for every n ∈ ℕ:
  (i) |a_{n,d_n}| ≥ A_1;
  (ii) |a_{n,j}| ≤ A_2 |a_{n,d_n}| for 0 ≤ j ≤ d_n − 1;
  (iii) log |a_{n,d_n}| ≤ A_3 · d_n.

For such a sequence, define the generalized (filled) Julia set by
  J(f_n) = { z ∈ ℂ : the sequence (F_n(z))_{n≥1} is bounded }, where F_n = f_n ∘ f_{n−1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1.

Assume J(f_n) ⊂ ℝ is a Cantor-type set (compact, perfect, totally disconnected). Let μ_{J(f_n)} be its logarithmic equilibrium measure, and let (a_k, b_k)_{k≥0} be the coefficients in the three-term recurrence
  x p_k(x) = a_{k+1} p_{k+1}(x) + b_k p_k(x) + a_k p_{k−1}(x)
satisfied by the orthonormal polynomials (p_k) associated with μ_{J(f_n)}.

A bounded sequence (c_k)_{k≥0} of real numbers is called almost periodic if for every ε > 0 the set { m ∈ ℕ : sup_k |c_{k+m} − c_k| < ε } is relatively dense in ℕ.

Problem. Prove that the recurrence coefficient sequences (a_k) and (b_k) are asymptotically almost periodic; that is, there exist almost periodic sequences (a_k^*) and (b_k^*) such that
  |a_k − a_k^*| → 0  and  |b_k − b_k^*| → 0  as  k → ∞.
status_search_result: The problem is a generalization of Bellissard's long-standing conjecture on limit periodicity of Jacobi matrices associated with the balanced measure on Julia sets of hyperbolic polynomials. Only partial results are known: limit periodicity is established for scaled Chebyshev iterates and certain weakly equilibrium Cantor-type sets, but the asymptotic almost periodicity for general regular polynomial sequences with Cantor-type real Julia sets has not been established. No published resolution was found.

context_brief: Zero spacing, Green function, Markov factors
original_question: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R, let μ_K be its equilibrium measure, and let P_n(x;μ_K) be the n-th monic orthogonal polynomial with zero set Z_n(μ_K)={x:P_n(x;μ_K)=0}. If U_n(μ_K)=inf{|x-x'|: x,x'∈Z_n(μ_K), x≠x'} denotes the minimal spacing between distinct zeros, determine whether there is a general relationship between this zero spacing and the smoothness of the Green function g_{C\K}; also determine whether there is a general relationship between that zero spacing and the Markov factors of K.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a non-polar compact set, and let $\mu_K$ denote its (logarithmic) equilibrium measure. For each integer $n \ge 1$, let $P_n(\cdot;\mu_K)$ be the $n$-th monic orthogonal polynomial with respect to $\mu_K$, and set
$$Z_n(\mu_K) := \{x \in \mathbb{R} : P_n(x;\mu_K) = 0\}, \qquad U_n(\mu_K) := \inf\{|x-x'| : x,x' \in Z_n(\mu_K),\ x \ne x'\}.$$
Let $g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}$ denote the Green function of the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. For each $n$, define the $n$-th Markov factor of $K$ by
$$M_n(K) := \sup\Bigl\{\frac{\|Q'\|_{L^\infty(K)}}{\|Q\|_{L^\infty(K)}} : Q \in \mathbb{R}[x],\ \deg Q \le n,\ Q\not\equiv 0\Bigr\}.$$

(a) Establish (or disprove) a general quantitative relationship between the zero-spacing sequence $\{U_n(\mu_K)\}_{n\ge 1}$ and the smoothness (modulus of continuity) of $g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}$ on $\mathbb{C}$.

(b) Establish (or disprove) a general quantitative relationship between $\{U_n(\mu_K)\}_{n\ge 1}$ and the Markov factors $\{M_n(K)\}_{n\ge 1}$.
status_search_result: The problem of relating the minimal spacing of zeros of orthogonal polynomials for the equilibrium measure of a non-polar compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ to the smoothness of the Green function of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ and to the Markov factors of $K$ appears to remain open in general. Recent work on weakly equilibrium Cantor sets and on Markov-type inequalities versus extreme zeros of orthogonal polynomials addresses partial cases (e.g. specific Cantor-type families and one-sided implications), but no general equivalence has been established.

original_question: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem, and let μ be a measure with essential support ess supp(μ)=K whose isolated support points {x_n} satisfy Σ_n g_{C\K}(x_n)<∞. Suppose the logarithmic integrability condition ∫_K log(dμ/dμ_K) dμ_K(x) > -∞ holds, where μ_K is the equilibrium measure on K. Must μ then satisfy either the Widom condition limsup_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0 or the Widom condition 2 liminf_{n→∞} W_n^2(μ)>0? Conversely, if μ satisfies a Widom condition, must the logarithmic integrability condition hold?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a non-polar compact set that is regular with respect to the Dirichlet problem. Let $\mu_K$ denote the logarithmic equilibrium measure of $K$, and let $g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(\,\cdot\,)$ denote the Green function of the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity (extended by $0$ on $K$). For a finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\operatorname{ess\,supp}(\mu)=K$, let $\{P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the monic orthogonal polynomials with respect to $\mu$, and define the Widom factors
$$W_n(\mu)\;=\;\frac{\|P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu)\|_{L^2(\mu)}}{\operatorname{cap}(K)^{\,n}},$$
where $\operatorname{cap}(K)$ is the logarithmic capacity of $K$.

Assumption. Suppose the isolated points $\{x_n\}$ of $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ satisfy
$$\sum_{n} g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(x_n)\;<\;\infty.$$

Question. 
(a) If the Szegő-type condition
$$\int_K \log\!\Bigl(\frac{d\mu}{d\mu_K}\Bigr)\,d\mu_K(x)\;>\;-\infty \tag{$\ast$}$$
holds (where $d\mu/d\mu_K$ is the Radon–Nikodym derivative of the absolutely continuous part of $\mu$ with respect to $\mu_K$), does it follow that at least one of the following Widom conditions must hold?
$$\text{(W1)}\quad \limsup_{n\to\infty} W_n^{\,2}(\mu)>0,\qquad \text{(W2)}\quad \liminf_{n\to\infty} W_n^{\,2}(\mu)>0.$$
(b) Conversely, if (W1) (or equivalently (W2)) holds for $\mu$, must the Szegő-type condition $(\ast)$ hold?
status_search_result: Closely related results are known for Parreau–Widom sets (e.g. Christiansen's work extending Szegő's theorem, and reviews of Widom factors and Szegő–Widom asymptotics), where partial equivalences between the Szegő condition and Widom-type boundedness have been established. However, no source found in this search explicitly resolves both directions of the stated equivalence for general non-polar regular compact sets in $\mathbb{R}$ under the isolated-points assumption $\sum_n g_{\mathbb{C}\setminus K}(x_n)<\infty$. The problem appears to remain open in this generality.

original_question: Does there exist a regular non-polar compact subset K of R that is not a Parreau-Widom set but whose Widom factors W_n(K)=||T_{n,K}||_{L^∞(K)}/Cap(K)^n remain bounded? More specifically, if K has zero Lebesgue measure, must the sequence (W_n(K)) be unbounded? The same questions are asked for the Widom-Hilbert factors (W_n^2(μ_K)) associated with the equilibrium measure μ_K.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a compact set. Denote by $\operatorname{Cap}(K)$ its logarithmic capacity, and assume $K$ is non-polar (i.e., $\operatorname{Cap}(K) > 0$) and regular for the Dirichlet problem. Let $\mu_K$ be the equilibrium measure of $K$.

For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $T_{n,K}$ be the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $n$ for $K$ — the unique monic polynomial of degree $n$ minimizing $\|P\|_{L^\infty(K)}$ among all monic degree-$n$ polynomials. Define the $n$-th Widom factor of $K$ by
$$W_n(K) \;=\; \frac{\|T_{n,K}\|_{L^\infty(K)}}{\operatorname{Cap}(K)^n}.$$
Let $P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu_K)$ denote the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$ associated with $\mu_K$, and define the $n$-th Widom–Hilbert factor by
$$W_n^2(\mu_K) \;=\; \frac{\|P_n(\,\cdot\,;\mu_K)\|_{L^2(\mu_K)}}{\operatorname{Cap}(K)^n}.$$

A non-polar compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ is called Parreau–Widom if $\sum_{j} G_{\Omega}(c_j) < \infty$, where $\Omega$ is the unbounded component of $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$, $G_\Omega$ is its Green function with pole at infinity, and $\{c_j\}$ are the critical points of $G_\Omega$.

Answer the following:

(a) Does there exist a regular non-polar compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ that is not Parreau–Widom but for which the sequence $(W_n(K))_{n=1}^\infty$ is bounded?

(b) If $K$ is a regular non-polar compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ with Lebesgue measure zero, must the sequence $(W_n(K))_{n=1}^\infty$ be unbounded?

(c) The same two questions as (a) and (b), but with the sequence of Widom–Hilbert factors $(W_n^2(\mu_K))_{n=1}^\infty$ in place of $(W_n(K))_{n=1}^\infty$.
status_search_result: Recent work (including a 2025 preprint extending earlier Goncharov–Hatinoğlu type constructions) has produced explicit non-polar Cantor sets of Lebesgue measure zero with unbounded Widom factors and unbounded Widom–Hilbert factors, providing further families of examples on the "unbounded" side. However, the general questions—whether every zero-Lebesgue-measure regular non-polar compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ has unbounded Widom (or Widom–Hilbert) factors, and whether some non-Parreau–Widom regular non-polar compact set in $\mathbb{R}$ can have bounded Widom (or Widom–Hilbert) factors—do not appear to be resolved in the literature.

context_brief: Rational equilibrium masses and generalized Julia sets
original_question: Let K be a regular non-polar compact subset of R with leftmost endpoint α, and let μ_K be its equilibrium measure. Assume that μ_K([α,c]) is rational for every c∈R\K. Characterize such sets K. In particular, must every such K be a polynomial generalized Julia set, or equivalently must there exist a sequence (f_n) of admissible polynomials such that, with F_n=f_n∘f_{n-1}∘···∘f_1, the inverse-image sets F_n^{-1}([-1,1]) form a decreasing sequence and K=⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([-1,1])?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) For a non-polar compact subset K of the real line, let cap(K) denote its logarithmic capacity and let μ_K denote its equilibrium measure, i.e. the unique Borel probability measure on K minimizing the logarithmic energy
  I(μ) = ∬ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x)dμ(y).
Recall that K is called regular if its complement (in C) is regular for the Dirichlet problem, equivalently if the Green function with pole at infinity of C\K is continuous up to K.

(b) A real polynomial T of degree N ≥ 2 is called admissible if it has N real simple zeros x_1 < x_2 < ⋯ < x_N and N−1 critical points y_1 < y_2 < ⋯ < y_{N−1} satisfying |T(y_i)| ≥ 1 for every i ∈ {1,…,N−1}.

(c) Given a sequence (f_n)_{n≥1} of admissible polynomials, set F_n = f_n ∘ f_{n−1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1. Then the sets F_n^{-1}([−1,1]) form a decreasing sequence of compact subsets of R, and the corresponding polynomial generalized Julia set is defined by
  J_{(f_n)} := ⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([−1,1]).

Problem. Let K ⊂ R be a regular non-polar compact set, let α := min K be its leftmost endpoint, and assume that the equilibrium-measure value
  μ_K([α, c])
is a rational number for every c ∈ R \ K. Characterize all such sets K. In particular, decide whether every such K must be a polynomial generalized Julia set: is there necessarily a sequence (f_n)_{n≥1} of admissible polynomials such that, with F_n = f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1, the sets F_n^{-1}([−1,1]) are decreasing in n and
  K = ⋂_{n=1}^∞ F_n^{-1}([−1,1]) ?
category_tag: potential theory and generalized Julia sets
status_search_result: A web search for follow-up work on the characterization of regular non-polar compact subsets of R whose equilibrium measure assigns rational mass to every initial segment determined by a gap endpoint did not turn up a published resolution. Related work by Alpan and Goncharov on generalized Julia sets (e.g. orthogonal polynomials on generalized Julia sets, arXiv:1503.07098) develops the surrounding framework but does not appear to settle this characterization, so the status is best recorded as unknown.

context_brief: When equilibrium measure is Hausdorff measure
original_question: Let K be a non-polar compact subset of R such that the equilibrium measure μ_K coincides with a Hausdorff measure restricted to K. Must the Hausdorff dimension of K be equal to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}$ be a non-polar compact set, i.e. a compact subset of the real line whose logarithmic capacity is positive, and let $\mu_K$ denote its (logarithmic) equilibrium measure — the unique Borel probability measure supported on $K$ that minimizes the logarithmic energy $I(\mu) = \iint \log\frac{1}{|x-y|}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)$ among all Borel probability measures on $K$. Recall that for a non-decreasing continuous function $h:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $h(0)=0$, the $h$-Hausdorff measure $\Lambda_h$ is defined by $\Lambda_h(E) = \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}\inf\{\sum_i h(\operatorname{diam} U_i): E\subset \bigcup_i U_i,\ \operatorname{diam} U_i\le\delta\}$, and when $h(t)=t^s$ this gives the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

Suppose that there exists a Hausdorff measure $\Lambda_h$ (for some such gauge $h$, possibly $h(t)=t^s$) such that 
$$\mu_K = \Lambda_h\!\restriction_K,$$
that is, the equilibrium measure of $K$ equals the restriction of $\Lambda_h$ to $K$ (in particular $0<\Lambda_h(K)<\infty$ and the equality holds as Borel measures on $K$).

Must the Hausdorff dimension of $K$ be equal to $0$?
status_search_result: The question concerns whether non-polar compact subsets of the real line whose logarithmic equilibrium measure coincides with a Hausdorff measure restricted to the set must have Hausdorff dimension zero. Known constructions (Goncharov's weakly equilibrium Cantor-type sets) yield examples where the equilibrium measure and a generalized Hausdorff measure are mutually absolutely continuous, and the only known examples of literal equality occur on sets of Hausdorff dimension zero. Web searches did not surface a published resolution of the problem in either direction, so its current status appears unresolved.

context_brief: Dimension formulas for Julia-set equilibrium measures
original_question: For a regular polynomial sequence (f_n), find simple formulas for the Hausdorff dimension of the measure μ_{J(f_n)} supported on the generalized Julia set J(f_n). Here the Hausdorff dimension of a unit Borel measure μ is defined by dim(μ)=inf{HD(K): μ(K)=1}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a regular polynomial sequence on $\mathbb{C}$, that is, a sequence of polynomials $f_n(z) = a_{n,d_n} z^{d_n} + \cdots + a_{n,0}$ with $\deg f_n = d_n \ge 2$ such that the associated generalized Julia set
$$J(f_n) := \partial\{z \in \mathbb{C} : (F_n(z))_{n\ge 1}\ \text{is bounded}\},\qquad F_n := f_n\circ f_{n-1}\circ\cdots\circ f_1,$$
is well-defined, and such that the corresponding pluripotential-theoretic equilibrium measure $\mu_{J(f_n)}$ (the weak-$*$ limit of normalized pull-backs of a probability measure on a large disc, or equivalently the Brolin-type measure associated with the sequence) exists as a Borel probability measure supported on $J(f_n)$.

For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$, define its Hausdorff dimension by
$$\dim(\mu) := \inf\{\mathrm{HD}(K) : K\ \text{Borel},\ \mu(K) = 1\},$$
where $\mathrm{HD}(K)$ denotes the Hausdorff dimension of $K$.

Problem. Find a simple closed-form expression for $\dim\!\big(\mu_{J(f_n)}\big)$ in terms of the data of the regular polynomial sequence $(f_n)$ (e.g.\ in terms of the degrees $d_n$, the leading and lower-order coefficients of the $f_n$, or Lyapunov exponents of the sequence).
status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published result giving simple closed-form formulas for the Hausdorff dimension of the equilibrium measure on a generalized Julia set of an arbitrary regular polynomial sequence. Related work exists for autonomous polynomials and for random/quadratic sequences, but no general resolution for regular polynomial sequences was found, so the status is taken as unknown.

original_question: Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Here an R-derivation is an R-linear map D: A -> A satisfying D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b), and an R-E-derivation is an R-linear map delta: A -> A satisfying delta(ab) = delta(a)b + adelta(b) - delta(a)delta(b), equivalently delta = I - phi for some R-algebra endomorphism phi. For every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, what is the radical r(delta(I)), where r(V) denotes the set of all a in A such that a^m belongs to V for all sufficiently large m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring (with identity), and let $A$ be an associative $R$-algebra. 

(i) An $R$-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map $D: A \to A$ satisfying the Leibniz rule
$$D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b) \quad \text{for all } a, b \in A.$$

(ii) An $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map $\delta: A \to A$ satisfying
$$\delta(ab) = \delta(a)b + a\delta(b) - \delta(a)\delta(b) \quad \text{for all } a, b \in A,$$
equivalently, $\delta = I - \phi$ for some $R$-algebra endomorphism $\phi$ of $A$ (where $I$ is the identity map).

For an $R$-subspace $V \subseteq A$, define the radical of $V$ to be
$$r(V) := \{ a \in A : a^m \in V \text{ for all sufficiently large } m \}.$$

Problem. Let $\delta$ be either an $R$-derivation or an $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$. For every left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal $I$ of $A$, determine the radical $r(\delta(I))$.
status_search_result: The problem is part of a program (the LFED/LNED conjectures and the broader "radical question" for derivations and E-derivations) initiated by Wenhua Zhao around 2017. Various special cases have been established—e.g., for polynomial algebras $K[x]$, Laurent polynomial algebras, and algebraic algebras under additional hypotheses—but no complete answer in the general setting of arbitrary $R$-algebras and arbitrary one- or two-sided ideals appears in the literature, so the general problem remains open.

original_question: Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Which such maps have the property that their image Im delta = delta(A) is a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and let $A$ be an associative (not necessarily commutative) $R$-algebra. 

(a) An $R$-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map $D : A \to A$ satisfying the Leibniz rule
$$D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b)\qquad\text{for all } a,b\in A.$$

(b) An $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$ is an $R$-linear map $\delta : A \to A$ satisfying
$$\delta(ab) = \delta(a)b + a\delta(b) - \delta(a)\delta(b)\qquad\text{for all } a,b\in A.$$
(Equivalently, $\delta = \mathrm{id}_A - \varphi$ for some $R$-algebra endomorphism $\varphi$ of $A$.)

For $\theta\in\{\text{left, right, two-sided}\}$, an $R$-subspace $V\subseteq A$ is called a $\theta$-Mathieu subspace ($\theta$-MS) of $A$ if, for every $a\in A$ with $a^m\in V$ for all $m\ge 1$, and for every $b,c\in A$, the following holds for all sufficiently large $m$:
- $ba^m\in V$, when $\theta=\text{left}$;
- $a^m c\in V$, when $\theta=\text{right}$;
- $ba^m c\in V$, when $\theta=\text{two-sided}$.

Problem. Characterize all $R$-derivations $D$ and all $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivations $\delta$ of $A$ such that the image $\mathrm{Im}\,D = D(A)$, respectively $\mathrm{Im}\,\delta = \delta(A)$, is a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A$.
category_tag: Mathieu-Zhao subspaces and images of derivations
status_search_result: The problem (often called the LFNED / image problem for Mathieu-Zhao subspaces) is open in general. It is connected to the Jacobian and Mathieu conjectures. Partial results exist: e.g., the image of a locally finite K-E-derivation of K[x,y] over a field of characteristic zero is known to be a Mathieu subspace, and various special cases (univariate polynomial algebras, linear derivations of K[x_1,x_2,x_3], divergence-zero cases, monomial-preserving derivations) have been resolved, but no complete characterization is known.

original_question: Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Which such maps send every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A to a corresponding left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace delta(I) of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring (with unity), let $A$ be an associative $R$-algebra, and fix one of the words $\theta\in\{\text{left, right, two-sided}\}$.

Definitions.
1. An $R$-linear map $\delta:A\to A$ is called an $R$-derivation if $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+a\delta(b)$ for all $a,b\in A$. It is called an $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation if there exists an $R$-algebra endomorphism $\varepsilon:A\to A$ such that $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+\varepsilon(a)\delta(b)$ for all $a,b\in A$ (equivalently, $\delta=\mathrm{id}_A-\varepsilon$).
2. An $R$-submodule $V\subseteq A$ is called a $\theta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$ if, whenever $a\in A$ satisfies $a^m\in V$ for every integer $m\ge 1$, then for every $b,c\in A$:
   - (left) $ba^m\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, if $\theta=\text{left}$;
   - (right) $a^m c\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, if $\theta=\text{right}$;
   - (two-sided) $ba^m c\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, if $\theta=\text{two-sided}$.
3. A $\theta$-ideal of $A$ means a left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal according to the value of $\theta$.

Problem. Determine (characterize) all $R$-derivations and all $R$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivations $\delta$ of $A$ with the property that for every $\theta$-ideal $I$ of $A$, the image $\delta(I)$ is a $\theta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$.
status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing which derivations and $\mathcal{E}$-derivations of an arbitrary $R$-algebra send every (one-sided or two-sided) ideal to a Mathieu subspace appears to remain open in full generality. Partial results have been obtained in special settings, e.g. for univariate polynomial algebras $K[x]$ over a field of characteristic zero, for bivariate polynomial algebras, and for linear (locally finite) derivations and $\mathcal{E}$-derivations of $K[x_1,x_2,x_3]$, where the related LFED/LNED conjectures have been verified.

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be either a locally finite K-derivation or a locally finite K-E-derivation. Here locally finite means that for each a in A, the K-submodule spanned by delta^i(a) for i >= 0 is finitely generated. Is the image Im delta = delta(A) always a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A, meaning that if a^m belongs to Im delta for every m >= 1, then ba^m c also belongs to Im delta for all sufficiently large m and all b, c in A?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be an associative $K$-algebra. A $K$-linear map $\delta : A \to A$ is called a $K$-derivation if $\delta(ab) = \delta(a)b + a\delta(b)$ for all $a,b \in A$, and is called a $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation if there exists a $K$-algebra endomorphism $\phi : A \to A$ such that $\delta = I - \phi$, where $I$ denotes the identity map. A $K$-linear endomorphism $\eta$ of $A$ is said to be locally finite if, for every $a \in A$, the $K$-subspace of $A$ spanned by $\{\eta^{i}(a) : i \ge 0\}$ is finite-dimensional. A $K$-subspace $V \subseteq A$ is called a two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A$ if, whenever $a \in A$ satisfies $a^{m} \in V$ for all $m \ge 1$, then for every $b, c \in A$ there exists $N = N(a,b,c) \ge 1$ such that $b\,a^{m}\,c \in V$ for all $m \ge N$.

Question: Is it true that for every locally finite $K$-derivation or locally finite $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation $\delta$ of $A$, the image $\operatorname{Im}\delta = \delta(A)$ is a two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A$?

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be either a locally nilpotent K-derivation or a locally nilpotent K-E-derivation. Here locally nilpotent means that for each a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. For every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, must the image delta(I) be a corresponding left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a left, right, or two-sided Mathieu subspace V of A means that whenever a^m lies in V for every m >= 1, the products ba^m, a^m c, or ba^m c eventually lie in V in the corresponding left, right, or two-sided case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be an associative $K$-algebra. A $K$-linear endomorphism $\eta$ of $A$ is called locally nilpotent if for every $a\in A$ there exists an integer $m\geq 1$ with $\eta^m(a)=0$. A $K$-derivation of $A$ is a $K$-linear map $D:A\to A$ satisfying $D(ab)=D(a)b+aD(b)$ for all $a,b\in A$. A $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$ is a $K$-linear map of the form $\delta=\mathrm{id}_A-\phi$, where $\phi$ is a $K$-algebra endomorphism of $A$.

Let $\theta$ stand for one of the words "left", "right", or "two-sided". A $K$-subspace $V\subseteq A$ is called a $\theta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$ if for every $a\in A$ such that $a^m\in V$ for all $m\geq 1$, and for all $b,c\in A$, one has:
- $ba^m\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, when $\theta=$ left;
- $a^m c\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, when $\theta=$ right;
- $ba^m c\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$, when $\theta=$ two-sided.

A $\theta$-ideal of $A$ means a left, right, or two-sided ideal according to the value of $\theta$.

Question: Let $\delta$ be either a locally nilpotent $K$-derivation or a locally nilpotent $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$. For every $\theta$-ideal $I$ of $A$, must $\delta(I)$ be a $\theta$-Mathieu subspace of $A$?
category_tag: Mathieu-Zhao subspaces and locally nilpotent derivations
status_search_result: The LNED conjecture has been confirmed in several special settings (for example, for Laurent polynomial algebras, for various classes of algebraic algebras, and for principal ideals under rank-one locally nilpotent derivations of polynomial algebras in three variables), but no general proof or counterexample is known. Hence the conjecture is partially solved and remains open in full generality.

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally finite K-derivation or K-E-derivation. Here locally finite means that for each a in A, the K-submodule spanned by delta^i(a) for i >= 0 is finitely generated. If e is an idempotent element of Im delta, meaning e^2 = e, must the principal ideal (e) generated by e be contained in Im delta?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be a $K$-algebra (associative, not necessarily commutative). A $K$-linear map $\delta:A\to A$ is called a $K$-derivation if $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+a\delta(b)$ for all $a,b\in A$, and is called a $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation if there exists a $K$-algebra endomorphism $\phi:A\to A$ such that $\delta=\mathrm{id}_A-\phi$ (equivalently, $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+a\delta(b)-\delta(a)\delta(b)$). A $K$-linear endomorphism $\eta$ of $A$ is called locally finite (LF) if for every $a\in A$, the $K$-submodule of $A$ spanned by $\{\eta^i(a):i\geq 0\}$ is finitely generated.

For $e\in A$, let $(e)$ denote the two-sided ideal of $A$ generated by $e$.

Question: Suppose $\delta$ is a $K$-derivation or a $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation of $A$ that is locally finite, and let $e\in\mathrm{Im}\,\delta$ be an idempotent (i.e., $e^2=e$). Must the principal ideal $(e)$ be contained in $\mathrm{Im}\,\delta$?
category_tag: Idempotent conjecture for locally finite derivations
status_search_result: The Idempotent Conjecture for locally finite K-derivations and K-E-derivations is generally still open. Partial results exist: it has been verified when the idempotent additionally lies in the kernel of δ, and various special cases (e.g., polynomial algebras in two variables, formal power series algebras) have been treated, but the full conjecture in arbitrary K-algebras is not established.

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let delta be a locally nilpotent K-derivation or K-E-derivation. Here locally nilpotent means that for each a in A there exists m >= 1 such that delta^m(a) = 0. For every choice of left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A and every idempotent e in delta(I), meaning e^2 = e, must the corresponding left, right, or two-sided ideal generated by e be contained in delta(I)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be a (not necessarily commutative) associative $K$-algebra. A $K$-linear map $\delta\colon A\to A$ is called a $K$-derivation if $\delta(ab)=\delta(a)b+a\delta(b)$ for all $a,b\in A$, and a $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation if $\delta=\mathrm{Id}_A-\phi$ for some $K$-algebra endomorphism $\phi$ of $A$. Such a map $\delta$ is locally nilpotent if for every $a\in A$ there exists an integer $m\ge 1$ with $\delta^m(a)=0$.

Fix a choice of "$\theta$-ideal" meaning either left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal (the same choice throughout). For an ideal $I\subseteq A$ of the chosen type, let $\delta(I)=\{\delta(x):x\in I\}$, and for $e\in A$ let $(e)_\theta$ denote the left, right, or two-sided ideal of $A$ generated by $e$.

Prove or disprove: for every locally nilpotent $K$-derivation or $K$-$\mathcal{E}$-derivation $\delta$ of $A$, every $\theta$-ideal $I$ of $A$, and every idempotent $e\in\delta(I)$ (i.e., $e^2=e$), one has $(e)_\theta\subseteq \delta(I)$.
category_tag: Idempotent conjecture for locally nilpotent derivations
status_search_result: The Idempotent Conjecture of Zhao has been verified in several cases: it holds for all locally finite K-derivations and all locally nilpotent K-E-derivations of A, with results on principal ideals generated by idempotents in the image being contained in the image. The general statement for arbitrary K-algebras and all locally nilpotent K-derivations or K-E-derivations with arbitrary one-/two-sided ideals appears not to have a fully resolved status; partial results exist.

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let (Lambda, *) be a monoid with unit e such that A has a K-algebra grading A = direct sum of A_lambda over lambda in Lambda, with each A_lambda a K-subspace and A_lambda A_mu contained in A_{lambda*mu} for all lambda and mu. Must the direct sum of all homogeneous components of degree different from e, namely the sum of A_lambda over all lambda != e, be a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A? Here a two-sided Mathieu subspace V means that if a^m belongs to V for every m >= 1, then ba^m c belongs to V for all sufficiently large m and all b, c in A.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero. For a (not necessarily commutative, not necessarily unital) $K$-algebra $A$, a $K$-subspace $V \subseteq A$ is called a two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A$ if, whenever $a \in A$ satisfies $a^m \in V$ for every integer $m \geq 1$, then for all $b, c \in A$ one has $b\, a^m\, c \in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$.

Let $(\Lambda, *)$ be a monoid with identity element $e$, and assume $A$ is $\Lambda$-graded as a $K$-algebra; that is, there is a direct sum decomposition
$$A = \bigoplus_{\lambda \in \Lambda} A_\lambda,$$
where each $A_\lambda$ is a $K$-subspace of $A$ and $A_\lambda \cdot A_\mu \subseteq A_{\lambda * \mu}$ for all $\lambda, \mu \in \Lambda$.

Prove or disprove: the $K$-subspace
$$V := \bigoplus_{\lambda \neq e} A_\lambda$$
consisting of all elements with zero homogeneous component of degree $e$ is necessarily a two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A$.
status_search_result: The Grading Conjecture for Mathieu-Zhao subspaces of graded algebras over fields of characteristic zero is part of a research program initiated by Zhao on Mathieu(-Zhao) subspaces. Web searches surface related work on Mathieu-Zhao subspaces of polynomial rings, vertex algebras, and derivation images, but no source verifying a full proof or disproof of this specific Grading Conjecture in general was found. Status appears to remain open, but this could not be confirmed from authoritative sources.

original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, let A be a K-algebra, and let z = (z1, z2, ..., zn) be commutative or noncommutative free variables. In the Laurent polynomial algebra A[z^{-1}, z], let M be the K-subspace consisting of all Laurent polynomials with no constant term. Is M always a two-sided Mathieu subspace of A[z^{-1}, z]? Here a two-sided Mathieu subspace V means that if f^m belongs to V for every m >= 1, then g f^m h belongs to V for all sufficiently large m and all g, h in the algebra.
self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $A$ be an associative $K$-algebra. Fix $n\ge 1$ and let $z=(z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n)$ be either $n$ commuting or $n$ noncommuting free variables, and form the Laurent polynomial algebra $A[z^{-1},z]$ (in the commuting case this is $A\otimes_K K[z_1^{\pm 1},\dots,z_n^{\pm 1}]$; in the noncommuting case the free Laurent algebra in $z_1,\dots,z_n$ over $A$). Denote by $M\subseteq A[z^{-1},z]$ the $K$-subspace of all Laurent polynomials with zero constant term (i.e. whose coefficient of the empty monomial is $0$).

A $K$-subspace $V$ of a $K$-algebra $B$ is called a two-sided Mathieu subspace (two-sided Mathieu–Zhao space) of $B$ if, for every $a\in B$ such that $a^m\in V$ for all $m\ge 1$, and for all $b,c\in B$, one has $b\,a^m\,c\in V$ for all sufficiently large $m$.

Prove or disprove: $M$ is a two-sided Mathieu subspace of $A[z^{-1},z]$, for every such $K$ and $A$ and for both the commutative and noncommutative cases.
status_search_result: The conjecture generalizes the Duistermaat–van der Kallen theorem (the case $A=K$, commuting variables, where $M$ is known to be a Mathieu subspace) to arbitrary $K$-algebras $A$ and to the noncommutative free-variable setting. Web search returns the surrounding literature on Mathieu–Zhao spaces and the image conjecture, but no result establishing the full conjecture for general $A$ or in the noncommutative case; it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
context_brief: negative chordless circle through an edge
original_question: For a signed graph Σ, where each edge has sign + or − and a circle is negative when the product of its edge signs is negative, determine whether a specified edge e belongs to at least one negative chordless circle.
self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G, \sigma)$ where $G = (V, E)$ is a finite undirected graph (possibly with multiple edges) and $\sigma : E \to \{+1, -1\}$ is a sign function on the edges. A circle (cycle) in $G$ is a connected 2-regular subgraph. The sign of a circle $C$ is the product $\prod_{e \in C} \sigma(e)$; the circle is called negative if this product equals $-1$ and positive otherwise. A circle $C$ in $G$ is called chordless (induced) if no edge of $G$ outside $C$ has both endpoints in $V(C)$.

Problem. Provide an algorithm (and determine its computational complexity), or otherwise characterize, the following decision problem: given a signed graph $\Sigma$ and a distinguished edge $e \in E$, decide whether $e$ lies on at least one negative chordless circle of $\Sigma$.
status_search_result: The question appears in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative and positive circles in signed graphs, where the answer is listed as unknown. Recent related work (e.g., heuristics for maximum balanced induced subgraphs via negative chordless cycles, 2024 work on weakly negative circles) addresses related computational problems but does not resolve this specific edge-membership question. No published resolution was located.

context_brief: complexity of excluding negative induced circles
original_question: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether the decision problem “e does not belong to any negative induced circle” lies in the complexity class NP.
self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (G, σ) consisting of a finite undirected graph G = (V, E) together with a sign function σ : E → {+1, −1}. The sign of a circle (simple cycle) C in Σ is the product of the signs of its edges; C is called negative if this product equals −1, and positive otherwise. A circle C in Σ is called induced if the subgraph it spans has no chord, i.e. C is an induced subgraph of G.

Consider the following decision problem (NIC̄): given a signed graph Σ and a designated edge e of Σ, decide whether e does NOT belong to any negative induced circle of Σ.

Determine whether NIC̄ lies in the complexity class NP; that is, decide whether there exists a polynomial-size certificate, verifiable in deterministic polynomial time, witnessing that no negative induced circle of Σ contains the edge e.
status_search_result: The problem appears as an explicit open question in Zaslavsky's problem collection on negative and positive circles in signed graphs. Available sources (the problem collection itself and related surveys) restate the question without resolving it; while the complementary problem ("does e belong to some negative induced circle") is clearly in NP, a polynomial-time-verifiable certificate for the non-existence variant has not been exhibited in the located sources. No subsequent paper resolving this complexity-class question was found.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
original_question: Characterize the signed graphs in which every pair of negative circles has at least two vertices in common; the paper calls such signed graphs quasibalanced.
self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a graph (possibly with multiple edges and loops) and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ assigns a sign to each edge. The sign of a circle (simple closed walk) $C$ in $(G,\sigma)$ is the product $\prod_{e\in C}\sigma(e)$; the circle is called negative if this product equals $-1$ and positive otherwise. Call a signed graph quasibalanced if any two negative circles in it share at least two vertices in common (in particular, a signed graph with at most one negative circle, including a balanced signed graph having no negative circles, is quasibalanced).

Give a structural characterization of all quasibalanced signed graphs.
status_search_result: Zaslavsky's problem-collection paper (AKCE Int. J. Graphs Combin., 2018) reports that a signed graph is quasibalanced if and only if it has at most one unbalanced block and that block is itself quasibalanced; this reduces the problem to characterizing 2-connected quasibalanced signed graphs, which is the property motivating the matroid-circuit description of frame/lift matroids. A complete non-recursive structural characterization does not appear in the located sources, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

original_question: Characterize signed simple graphs that have no chordless negative circles, or equivalently no negative holes other than possibly triangles.
self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a function called a signature. The sign of a cycle (called a circle) in $(G,\sigma)$ is the product of the signs of its edges; a circle is negative if this product is $-1$ and positive otherwise. A circle $C$ in $G$ is chordless if no edge of $G$ joins two non-consecutive vertices of $C$; chordless circles of length at least four are called holes.

Problem: Give a structural characterization of those signed simple graphs $(G,\sigma)$ that contain no chordless negative circle. Equivalently (in the second formulation), characterize the signed simple graphs $(G,\sigma)$ in which every negative chordless circle is a triangle, i.e., $(G,\sigma)$ contains no negative hole.

original_question: Generalize the spectral existence results for odd and even cycles to signed graphs: determine for which signed simple graphs Nikiforov-type eigenvalue conditions force the existence of negative or positive circles, and determine whether the Yuan and Nikiforov–Yuan upper-bound theorems for forbidden odd or even cycle lengths extend to signed simple graphs with negative or positive circles of prescribed lengths.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a simple graph and $\sigma: E \to \{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function. The sign of a circle (cycle) $C$ in $\Sigma$ is the product of the signs of its edges; the circle is called positive if its sign is $+1$ and negative if its sign is $-1$. A signed graph is balanced if every circle is positive, and unbalanced otherwise. The adjacency matrix $A(\Sigma)$ is the $|V|\times|V|$ matrix with $A_{uv} = \sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise; let $\lambda_1(\Sigma) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(\Sigma)$ be its eigenvalues. For an unsigned graph $G$, write $\lambda_1(G)$ for the spectral radius of its (ordinary) adjacency matrix.

The following classical spectral existence theorems for unsigned simple graphs are taken as given:

(N) Nikiforov's theorem on non-bipartiteness: there exists an explicit eigenvalue condition on $\lambda_1(G)$ (and on $G$'s edge count or order) which forces $G$ to be non-bipartite, equivalently to contain an odd circle.

(Y) Yuan's theorem and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorem: if a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices contains no circle of a prescribed odd length (resp. no circle of a prescribed even length) $\ell$, then $\lambda_1(G)$ satisfies an explicit upper bound depending on $n$ and $\ell$, with the extremal graphs characterized.

Problems.

(1) Determine the class of signed simple graphs $\Sigma$ for which the analogue of (N), with "non-bipartite" replaced by "unbalanced" (i.e., containing a negative circle), holds. Specifically, identify a sharp spectral condition on $\lambda_1(\Sigma)$ (or on a suitable spectral invariant of $\Sigma$) that forces $\Sigma$ to contain a negative circle, and characterize precisely the signed simple graphs satisfying the hypotheses of (N) for which this implication is valid.

(2) Determine whether Yuan's theorem and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorem extend to signed simple graphs in the following form: for prescribed $\ell$, give a sharp upper bound on $\lambda_1(\Sigma)$ for signed simple graphs $\Sigma$ on $n$ vertices that contain no negative circle of length $\ell$ (when one seeks an analogue of the odd-cycle case) and, separately, no positive circle of length $\ell$ (when one seeks an analogue of the even-cycle case). In each case, characterize the extremal signed graphs.
status_search_result: Several recent works (2022–2025) have addressed signed-graph analogues of Nikiforov-type spectral Turán theorems. Results include spectral conditions forcing negative 3-cycles in unbalanced signed graphs, the maximum spectral radius among negative-$C_4$-free unbalanced signed graphs, extremal results for $C_3^-$-free signed graphs, and spectral Turán problems for $C_k^-$-free, $K_4^-$-free, $K_{3,3}^-$-free, and $K_5^-$-free signed graphs. Thus the program has been carried out for specific small/short forbidden circles, but a complete generalization of Nikiforov's, Yuan's, and the Nikiforov–Yuan theorems to arbitrary negative or positive circle lengths in signed simple graphs has not been fully established.

Let $D = (V, A)$ be a directed graph (digraph), and let $\sigma : A \to \{+1, -1\}$ be a signing of its arcs; the pair $(D, \sigma)$ is called a signed digraph. The sign of a directed cycle in $D$ is the product of the signs of its arcs. The signed digraph $(D, \sigma)$ is said to be cycle balanced if every directed cycle of $D$ has positive sign. Define the directed frustration index $\ell(D, \sigma)$ to be the minimum number of arcs whose deletion from $D$ yields a cycle balanced signed digraph.

Let $\Gamma$ denote the underlying undirected multigraph of $D$, with each arc replaced by an edge keeping the same sign, giving a signed graph $(\Gamma, \sigma)$. A signed undirected graph is balanced if every cycle has positive sign, and its (undirected) frustration index $\ell(\Gamma, \sigma)$ is the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $(\Gamma, \sigma)$ balanced. One always has
$$\ell(D, \sigma) \le \ell(\Gamma, \sigma).$$

Problem. Characterize the signed digraphs $(D, \sigma)$ for which equality $\ell(D, \sigma) = \ell(\Gamma, \sigma)$ holds; that is, give necessary and sufficient structural conditions on $(D, \sigma)$ under which the directed frustration index coincides with the frustration index of the underlying undirected signed graph.

Define the directed frustration number $l_0(D,\sigma)$ to be the minimum number of vertices whose deletion makes the resulting signed digraph cycle balanced.

Since balance of $(\Gamma,\sigma)$ implies cycle balance of $(D,\sigma)$, one always has 
$$l_0(D,\sigma)\le l_0(\Gamma,\sigma).$$

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
context_brief: edge cover for positive directed cycles
original_question: For a signed digraph, determine the smallest number of edges that meet every positive directed cycle.
self_contained_problem:
Let $D=(V,E,\sigma)$ be a finite signed digraph: a directed graph with arc set $E$ together with a sign function $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$. The sign of a directed cycle (a closed directed walk with no repeated vertices) is the product of the signs of its arcs. A directed cycle is called positive if its sign is $+1$.

An arc set $F\subseteq E$ is said to cover all positive directed cycles if every positive directed cycle of $D$ contains at least one arc of $F$. Define
$$\tau^+(D)=\min\{|F|:F\subseteq E\text{ and }F\text{ meets every positive directed cycle of }D\}.$$

Determine $\tau^+(D)$: give a combinatorial formula, structural characterization, or efficient algorithm to compute the minimum number of arcs needed to cover every positive directed cycle of an arbitrary signed digraph $D$.
status_search_result: The corresponding decision problem (covering all positive, resp. negative, directed cycles by a minimum set of arcs in a signed digraph) is known to be NP-complete via reductions to covering even/odd directed cycles in unsigned digraphs. No closed-form combinatorial formula or efficient algorithm for the minimum cover number is known, and the problem is listed among open questions in the signed-graphs problem literature.

paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
context_brief: vertex cover for positive directed cycles
original_question: For a signed digraph, determine the smallest number of vertices that meet every positive directed cycle.
self_contained_problem:
A signed digraph is a pair $(D,\sigma)$ where $D=(V,E)$ is a finite directed graph (loops and multiple arcs allowed if desired) and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on the arcs. The sign of a directed cycle $C$ in $D$ is the product $\sigma(C)=\prod_{e\in C}\sigma(e)$; the cycle is called positive if $\sigma(C)=+1$ and negative otherwise. A vertex set $S\subseteq V$ is said to cover the positive directed cycles of $(D,\sigma)$ if every positive directed cycle of $D$ contains at least one vertex of $S$.

Define
$$\tau^{+}(D,\sigma) \;=\; \min\bigl\{\,|S| \;:\; S\subseteq V \text{ covers every positive directed cycle of } (D,\sigma)\,\bigr\}.$$

Problem: Determine $\tau^{+}(D,\sigma)$. More precisely, give a combinatorial formula, a min–max characterization, or sharp bounds (in terms of natural parameters of $(D,\sigma)$) for the smallest number of vertices needed to meet every positive directed cycle of an arbitrary signed digraph, and analyze the computational complexity of computing this minimum.
status_search_result: No specific resolution of the minimum positive-directed-cycle vertex cover problem for signed digraphs was located. The question appears in a problem collection on signed graphs and remains, to the best of available evidence, open. Related undirected versions (covering negative/positive cycles in signed graphs) are known to be NP-hard via connections with odd-cycle transversal and even-cycle problems, but a definitive solution for the directed positive-cycle case was not found.

original_question: For suitable perturbations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line and suitable almost periodic initial data u_0(x), does the Cauchy problem have a unique global solution u(x,t) that evolves almost periodically in time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider perturbations of the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation
    u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = F(u, u_x, u_{xx}, ...),  x ∈ ℝ, t ∈ ℝ,
where F denotes a (suitably regular and small) perturbation term that breaks the complete integrability of KdV. A function v: ℝ → ℝ is called almost periodic (in the sense of Bohr) if for every ε > 0 the set of ε-almost periods {τ ∈ ℝ : sup_{x∈ℝ} |v(x+τ) − v(x)| < ε} is relatively dense in ℝ; equivalently, v lies in the closure (in the uniform norm) of the trigonometric polynomials. A solution u(x,t) is said to evolve almost periodically in time if, for each fixed x ∈ ℝ, the map t ↦ u(x,t) is almost periodic, and more strongly if the orbit {u(·,t) : t ∈ ℝ} is precompact in the uniform topology.

Question: Identify a natural class of perturbations F and a natural class of almost periodic initial data u_0(x) on ℝ such that the Cauchy problem
    u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = F(u, u_x, ...),    u(x,0) = u_0(x)
admits a unique global-in-time solution u(x,t) which is almost periodic in x for every t and evolves almost periodically in time. Prove or disprove the conjecture that, for suitable choices of F and u_0, this global existence, uniqueness, and almost periodicity holds.
status_search_result: For the unperturbed (integrable) KdV equation with almost periodic initial data, work by Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic (Duke Math J., 2018) established almost periodicity in time for suitable classes of initial data, addressing a conjecture of Deift. However, for non-integrable perturbations of KdV the question remains open: no general results establishing global existence, uniqueness, and almost periodicity in time on almost periodic backgrounds for perturbed KdV are known. Recent work (Damanik–Lukić–Volberg–Yuditskii and follow-ups, 2021–2024) has produced counterexamples in related settings, indicating the problem is delicate, but the perturbed-KdV conjecture itself is still considered open.

original_question: For random n x n band matrices H with bandwidth w <= n and independent entries H_ij inside the band, can one prove the Fyodorov-Mirlin conjecture that the local eigenvalue statistics are in the GUE universality class when w is much larger than sqrt(n), but become Poisson when w is much smaller than sqrt(n), in both the real symmetric and complex Hermitian settings?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and $1 \leq w \leq n$ be integers. Consider an $n \times n$ random band matrix $H = (H_{ij})$ defined as follows:

- $H$ is either real symmetric or complex Hermitian;
- $H_{ij} = 0$ whenever $|i-j| \geq w$ (with indices viewed either on the line or on the cycle $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$);
- the entries $\{H_{ij} : i \leq j,\ |i-j| < w\}$ are independent (subject to the symmetry/Hermitian constraint), centered, and have variance proportional to $1/w$, so that the empirical spectral distribution converges to the semicircle law.

For an energy $E$ in the bulk of the semicircle, study the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ near $E$ on the natural microscopic scale $1/(n\rho_{sc}(E))$. Prove the following dichotomy:

(i) If $w/\sqrt{n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ converge to those of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (in the Hermitian case) or Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (in the real symmetric case); equivalently, the appropriately rescaled $k$-point correlation functions converge to the sine-kernel determinantal/Pfaffian limits.

(ii) If $w/\sqrt{n} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, then the local eigenvalue statistics of $H$ near $E$ converge to those of a Poisson point process with intensity $n\rho_{sc}(E)$.

Establish (i) and (ii) in both the real symmetric and the complex Hermitian settings.
status_search_result: The Fyodorov–Mirlin conjecture remains open in its full form. Significant partial progress exists: GUE/GOE bulk universality has been established for bandwidths well above $\sqrt{n}$ (e.g., $w \gg n^{3/4}$ and subsequent improvements by Bourgade–Erdős–Yau–Yin and others), and the conjecture has been fully proved for special chiral band-matrix models at zero energy (Letters in Mathematical Physics, 2024). Recent 2025 works combine localization results with Yau–Yin/Erdős–Riabov delocalization to obtain a localization–delocalization transition for a wide class of 1D band matrices, but proving Poisson statistics in the regime $w \ll \sqrt{n}$ for general band matrices is still not completed.

original_question: For random Schrodinger operators H = -Delta + V with random potential V, can one rigorously analyze the bulk spectral regime where eigenfunctions are expected to delocalize and eigenvalues are expected to follow random-matrix statistics, and can one construct and analyze models that exhibit the conjectured transition from Poisson statistics to random-matrix statistics at a mobility edge?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H = -\Delta + V$ act on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ (or on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$), where $\Delta$ is the discrete (resp. continuum) Laplacian and $V$ is a random potential (for example, $V(x) = \omega_x$ with i.i.d. random variables $\{\omega_x\}_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ having a bounded density). For finite-volume restrictions $H_L$ to a box of side $L$, denote the eigenvalues by $E_1(L) \le E_2(L) \le \cdots$ and consider, for an energy $E$ in the spectrum, the rescaled local eigenvalue point process
$$\xi_L^E := \sum_i \delta_{L^d (E_i(L) - E)}.$$

The mobility edge conjecture asserts the existence of a threshold $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ such that:
(i) for energies $E$ in the localization regime (e.g. $E < \mu$ in $d \ge 3$, or throughout the spectrum in $d = 1, 2$), $H$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions and $\xi_L^E$ converges to a Poisson point process;
(ii) for energies $E$ in the delocalized (bulk) regime ($E > \mu$, $d \ge 3$, weak disorder), $H$ has absolutely continuous spectrum with extended eigenfunctions and $\xi_L^E$ converges to the local eigenvalue statistics of a random matrix ensemble (e.g. the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble $\operatorname{Sine}_1$ process).

Problem: Rigorously establish, for a non-trivial random Schrödinger operator $H = -\Delta + V$, the existence of the delocalized regime with random-matrix-type local eigenvalue statistics and absolutely continuous spectrum, and prove the existence of a mobility edge $\mu$ separating the Poisson and random-matrix statistical regimes. Equivalently, construct and rigorously analyze a concrete model in which the transition from Poisson to random-matrix local eigenvalue statistics at a mobility edge is proved.
category_tag: Random Schrödinger operators and mobility edge
status_search_result: The mobility edge conjecture for random Schrödinger operators in dimension d ≥ 3 — including the existence of absolutely continuous spectrum/extended states and a Poisson-to-random-matrix transition — remains widely regarded as open. Poisson statistics in the localized regime are known (Minami and successors, including results on regular graphs and continuum operators), but the delocalized regime with GOE/Sine_1 statistics has not been established for any standard Anderson-type model. Partial results exist for related toy models (e.g. random band matrices, regular graphs/trees), but the full conjecture is unresolved.

original_question: For Wigner ensembles whose equilibrium measure is supported on more than one interval, can one prove universality in the bulk and at all spectral edges, and can one also analyze parameter regimes in which intervals in the support of the equilibrium measure open and close?
self_contained_problem:
Let $W_N=(w_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le N}$ be an $N\times N$ Hermitian (or real symmetric) Wigner-type random matrix whose entries $\{w_{ij}:i\le j\}$ are independent with mean zero and a (possibly site-dependent) variance profile $S=(s_{ij})$, $s_{ij}=\mathbb{E}|w_{ij}|^2$. Assume the variance profile is chosen so that, as $N\to\infty$, the empirical spectral measure $\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\delta_{\lambda_k(W_N)}$ converges weakly to a deterministic equilibrium (self-consistent) probability measure $\rho$ on $\mathbb{R}$ whose support $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)=\bigcup_{r=1}^{p}[a_r,b_r]$ consists of $p\ge 2$ disjoint compact intervals.

(i) Prove bulk universality: for every fixed energy $E$ in the interior of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)$ with $\rho(E)>0$, the local correlation functions of the eigenvalues of $W_N$, rescaled by $1/(N\rho(E))$, converge to the sine-kernel correlation functions of the GUE (resp. GOE).

(ii) Prove edge universality at every spectral edge: for each endpoint $a_r$ and $b_r$ of every connected component of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho)$, the suitably rescaled extremal eigenvalues near that edge converge to the Tracy–Widom $\beta=2$ (resp. $\beta=1$) distribution.

(iii) Consider one-parameter families $W_N=W_N(t)$ of such ensembles in which the variance profile (or an external deformation) depends continuously on a parameter $t$, and in which two adjacent intervals of $\mathrm{supp}(\rho_t)$ merge (closing a gap) or a single interval splits (opening a gap) as $t$ crosses a critical value $t_*$. Establish the corresponding local eigenvalue statistics at the critical parameter $t_*$, in particular at the cusp/critical points where intervals meet or separate, and describe the universal limiting process governing the transition.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since 2017. For Wigner-type matrices with multi-interval (multi-cut) self-consistent density, bulk universality (Ajanki–Erdős–Krüger), edge universality with Tracy–Widom statistics in both single- and multi-cut cases, and cusp universality with the Pearcey process at points where intervals meet or split (Erdős–Krüger–Schröder; Cipolloni–Erdős–Krüger–Schröder) have been established for complex Hermitian and real symmetric symmetry classes, completing the Wigner–Dyson–Mehta program for these singularity types. Full quantitative control of arbitrary one-parameter families through gap-opening/closing transitions in the most general Wigner setting still receives ongoing refinements, so the broader program is best described as partially solved.

original_question: For random-matrix models that depend on external parameters p and undergo critical changes in the support of the equilibrium measure at values p_c, can one rigorously analyze the corresponding double-scaling and more general multi-scaling limits in which p approaches p_c while the matrix size n tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a family of unitary-invariant Hermitian random matrix ensembles on the space of n×n Hermitian matrices M, with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

   (1/Z_{n,p}) · ∏_{i<j}(x_i − x_j)^2 · ∏_i exp(−n V(x_i; p)),

where V(·; p): ℝ → ℝ is a real-analytic confining potential depending smoothly on an external parameter p ∈ I ⊂ ℝ, and Z_{n,p} is the normalization constant. As n → ∞ with p fixed, the empirical eigenvalue measure (1/n)∑_i δ_{x_i} converges weakly to a deterministic equilibrium measure μ_p, defined as the unique minimizer of the weighted logarithmic energy functional

   E_p(μ) = ∬ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x; p) dμ(x)

over Borel probability measures μ on ℝ.

Assume there exists a critical value p_c ∈ I at which the topology or regularity of the support of μ_p changes (for example, the number of connected components of supp(μ_p) jumps, or the equilibrium density develops a higher-order vanishing point or merges into a singular endpoint).

Develop a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the local eigenvalue statistics, partition function Z_{n,p}, and correlation kernels in the double-scaling limit

   n → ∞,   p = p_c + c · n^{−α},   c ∈ ℝ fixed,

for the appropriate critical exponent α > 0, and more generally in multi-scaling regimes where several parameters approach their critical values simultaneously at coordinated rates. Identify the limiting kernels (expressible via solutions to Painlevé-type equations or Riemann–Hilbert problems associated with the type of critical transition) and establish universality of these limits within natural classes of potentials V(·; p) producing the same critical behavior.
status_search_result: The general program of rigorously analyzing double-scaling and multi-scaling limits at critical transitions of equilibrium measures in random matrix theory remains broadly open. Several specific cases (e.g., Painlevé II at the soft edge / one-cut-to-two-cut transitions, Painlevé I/II hierarchies at singular interior points, certain birth-of-a-cut transitions) have been resolved via Riemann–Hilbert steepest-descent methods by Bleher–Its, Claeys, Kuijlaars, Vanlessen and others, but a comprehensive theory covering arbitrary critical transitions and multi-parameter scaling limits has not been completed.

original_question: Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?
self_contained_problem:
For each $\beta>0$, consider the soft-edge scaling limit of the largest eigenvalue of the $\beta$-ensemble on $\mathbb{R}$ with joint density proportional to
$$\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}|x_i-x_j|^{\beta}\,\prod_{i=1}^{N} e^{-\beta N V(x_i)/2},$$
and let $F_\beta(s)$ denote the corresponding Tracy–Widom$_\beta$ distribution function (the limiting distribution of the appropriately centered and scaled largest eigenvalue, which is known to exist and to be universal in $V$).

For $\beta\in\{1,2,4\}$, classical results of Tracy and Widom express $F_\beta$ in closed form via the Hastings–McLeod solution of the Painlevé II equation $q''(s)=sq(s)+2q(s)^3$.

(a) For every even integer $\beta>0$, give a fully rigorous derivation of an explicit Painlevé/Lax-pair representation of $F_\beta(s)$ extending the formulas obtained for $\beta=6$ via the Bloemendal–Virág PDE and a corresponding Lax pair (the "Rumanov-type" approach), including a complete justification of the integrability of the associated auxiliary ordinary differential equation and of the asymptotic analysis of the resulting Riemann–Hilbert / isomonodromic system.

(b) For general real $\beta>0$, rigorously establish the asymptotic expansions of $F_\beta(s)$ as $s\to\pm\infty$ that have been proposed for the right and left tails, of the schematic form
$$\log F_\beta(s) \sim -\tfrac{2\beta}{24}|s|^3 + \cdots \quad (s\to-\infty), \qquad 1-F_\beta(s) \sim e^{-\tfrac{2\beta}{3}s^{3/2}+\cdots}\quad (s\to+\infty),$$
together with all subleading coefficients (including the nonperturbative constants).

State and prove such explicit formulas and rigorous asymptotic expansions, or prove that no such closed-form Painlevé representation exists.
status_search_result: The β=6 case has seen significant progress: Rumanov (2014) derived a Painlevé-type representation, and subsequent work by Grava–Its–Kapaev–Mezzadri (2016) and Bertola–Cafasso–Rubtsov (2017–2020) connected it to the second Calogero–Painlevé system and proved Lax integrability, bringing the analysis closer to rigor. However, the rigorous integrability and asymptotic analysis of the auxiliary ODE in Rumanov's β=6 formula remains incomplete, no analogous explicit formulas have been rigorously established for even β>6, and the conjectured tail asymptotics of Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal for general β>0 have not been fully rigorously verified. Thus the problem is partially solved.

original_question: For the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with general initial data, can one prove full 3:2:1 KPZ universality in the strong sense proposed by Corwin, Quastel, and Remenik for solutions of the Cauchy problem, and can one identify the limiting process that arises in that scaling limit?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic PDE on the real line,
  ∂_t h(t,x) = (1/2) ∂_x^2 h(t,x) + (1/2) (∂_x h(t,x))^2 + ξ(t,x),  t > 0, x ∈ ℝ,
where ξ is a space–time Gaussian white noise, interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transform h = log Z, with Z solving the multiplicative stochastic heat equation ∂_t Z = (1/2) ∂_x^2 Z + Z ξ.

For ε > 0, define the 3:2:1 (equivalently 1:2:3) rescaled height process
  h_ε(t,x) := ε^{1/2} ( h(ε^{-3/2} t, ε^{-1} x) + (1/24) ε^{-3/2} t ),
with initial profile h_ε(0,·) prescribed from a class of admissible initial data (e.g. functions of at most linear growth, possibly plus narrow wedges, sampled from a broad subclass of continuous functions).

Strong KPZ universality problem (Cauchy problem, full form):
(a) Prove that, as ε → 0, the random space–time field (t,x) ↦ h_ε(t,x) converges in distribution (with respect to a suitable topology, e.g. uniform on compacts in (t,x), with t > 0) to a universal random field H(t,x) — the so-called KPZ fixed point — for the widest possible class of initial data h_ε(0,·) → 𝔥(·).
(b) Identify the limiting space–time process H explicitly: describe its finite-dimensional distributions, its Markov property in t, its dependence on the initial datum 𝔥, and its joint law as a space–time random field (i.e. as the directed landscape composed with the initial datum).

Goal: establish 3:2:1 universality in this strong (process-level, general-initial-data) sense for solutions of the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation, and explicitly characterize the limit.
status_search_result: The KPZ fixed point was constructed by Matetski–Quastel–Remenik (2017, published 2021). Convergence of the KPZ equation to the KPZ fixed point under the 1:2:3 scaling was subsequently established by Quastel–Sarkar (arXiv:2008.06584) for a class of initial data (continuous functions of at most linear growth plus finitely many narrow wedges), and independently/related results by Virág and by Wu use the directed landscape. Thus the strong universality problem for the Cauchy problem of the KPZ equation has been substantially solved for broad classes of initial data, with the limit identified as the KPZ fixed point / directed landscape; full universality for the most general initial data and complete process-level statements remain an active area, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

original_question: Can one analyze solutions of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation simultaneously at more than one space-time point, rather than only through one-point statistics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) stochastic partial differential equation
$$\partial_t h(t,x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 h(t,x) + \tfrac{1}{2}(\partial_x h(t,x))^2 + \xi(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\xi$ is a space-time white noise on $\mathbb{R}_{>0}\times\mathbb{R}$, and the nonlinearity is interpreted via the Cole–Hopf transform $h = \log Z$, with $Z$ solving the multiplicative stochastic heat equation $\partial_t Z = \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_x^2 Z + Z\,\xi$.

For a fixed admissible initial condition (e.g. narrow wedge $h(0,\cdot) = -\tfrac{x^2}{2\varepsilon}$ in the $\varepsilon\to 0$ limit, flat, or stationary), and for any finite collection of distinct space-time points $(t_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_n,x_n)$ with $t_i>0$, develop an exact and tractable description of the joint probability distribution of the random vector
$$\bigl(h(t_1,x_1),\,h(t_2,x_2),\,\ldots,\,h(t_n,x_n)\bigr).$$

Specifically, obtain explicit formulas (for example, Fredholm determinant or contour-integral representations) for the multi-point joint distribution function
$$F_n(s_1,\ldots,s_n) = \mathbb{P}\bigl(h(t_1,x_1)\le s_1,\ldots,h(t_n,x_n)\le s_n\bigr),$$
suitable for asymptotic analysis as the points are scaled into the KPZ scaling limit, and use them to study the resulting multi-point correlation structure (in space, in time, and in space-time jointly), going beyond the previously known one-point statistics.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since 2017. The KPZ fixed point (Matetski–Quastel–Remenik) gives multi-point spatial distributions, and the directed landscape (Dauvergne–Ortmann–Virág) provides a full space-time scaling limit. Convergence of the narrow-wedge KPZ equation to the directed landscape has recently been established (Wu and others, 2023+), and explicit multi-time/multipoint Fredholm-determinant formulas for the KPZ fixed point with various initial conditions (including compactly supported ones) have been obtained as recently as 2024–2025. Multi-point analysis of the positive-temperature KPZ equation itself (not just the fixed point) is now accessible but a complete tractable theory at the level of one-point Tracy–Widom asymptotics remains under active development.

original_question: For last-passage percolation with general weights, can one prove the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling law, meaning time scale 3, spatial-correlation scale 2, and fluctuation scale 1 in the KPZ normalization?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\omega(i,j) : (i,j) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge 0}\}$ be a family of i.i.d. real-valued random variables (the "weights") with a common distribution $F$ satisfying mild moment/regularity conditions (for instance, finite exponential moments and a non-degenerate continuous distribution). For $(m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\ge 0}$ define the last-passage time
$$T(m,n) \;=\; \max_{\pi : (0,0) \to (m,n)} \sum_{(i,j) \in \pi} \omega(i,j),$$
where the maximum runs over all up-right lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(m,n)$. By Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem there exists a deterministic shape function $g$ with $T(\lfloor xN \rfloor, \lfloor yN \rfloor)/N \to g(x,y)$ a.s.

The conjectural Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) $3{:}2{:}1$ scaling law for this model asserts that, along a fixed direction $(x,y)$ with $x,y>0$:

(i) (fluctuation exponent $1/3$) There exist constants $c_1>0$ and a non-degenerate distribution $\mathcal{L}$ such that
$$\frac{T(\lfloor xN \rfloor,\lfloor yN \rfloor) - N\, g(x,y)}{c_1 N^{1/3}} \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathcal{L} \quad\text{as } N\to\infty;$$

(ii) (transversal exponent $2/3$) The maximizing path (geodesic) from $(0,0)$ to $(\lfloor xN \rfloor,\lfloor yN \rfloor)$ has typical transversal fluctuations of order $N^{2/3}$ around the straight line joining its endpoints;

(iii) (time exponent $1$) The time scale is linear, so that exponents $(1, 2/3, 1/3)$ — i.e. the $3{:}2{:}1$ ratio between time, space, and fluctuation scales — appear in the natural KPZ normalization.

Prove that this $3{:}2{:}1$ KPZ scaling holds for last-passage percolation with general weight distribution $F$ (subject only to mild non-degeneracy/moment assumptions), without using exact-solvability features specific to particular weight distributions such as the exponential or geometric ones.
status_search_result: Establishing the full 3:2:1 KPZ scaling for last-passage percolation with general (non-integrable) weight distributions is widely regarded as a major open problem. Rigorous proofs of the 1/3 fluctuation and 2/3 transversal exponents currently exist only for exactly solvable models (e.g., exponential or geometric weights) via integrable-probability methods. Recent works (e.g., Ganguly–Hegde 2020 and follow-ups) obtain optimal tail exponents in general LPP under curvature/tail assumptions on the shape function, but the full scaling-limit statement for general weights remains unresolved.
