original_question: For the longest increasing subsequence problem, can one prove KPZ-class fluctuation results when the permutation is sampled from distributions more general than the uniform distribution?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and for a permutation $\pi\in S_n$ let $L(\pi)$ be the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $\pi$, i.e. the largest $k$ such that there exist indices $i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k$ with $\pi(i_1)<\pi(i_2)<\dots<\pi(i_k)$.

When $\pi$ is sampled from the uniform distribution on $S_n$, it is known (Baik–Deift–Johansson) that
$$\frac{L(\pi)-2\sqrt{n}}{n^{1/6}}\;\xrightarrow{d}\;F_{\mathrm{TW}_2},$$
where $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$ is the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution, placing the model in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class with characteristic fluctuation exponent $1/3$ (here $n^{1/6}=(\sqrt n)^{1/3}$) and limit law $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$.

Problem. Identify natural families of non-uniform probability distributions $\{\mu_n\}$ on $S_n$ (for instance Mallows measures with parameters $q=q_n$ in suitable regimes, or other inversion-weighted, descent-weighted, or pattern-restricted ensembles) for which the centered and rescaled longest increasing subsequence
$$\frac{L(\pi)-a_n}{b_n},\qquad \pi\sim\mu_n,$$
admits, with appropriate centering $a_n$ and scaling $b_n$ of order $n^{1/3}$ (up to slowly varying factors), a limiting distribution belonging to the KPZ universality class (e.g. the Tracy–Widom $F_{\mathrm{TW}_2}$ law). Prove a KPZ-class fluctuation theorem in such a setting, or characterize the regimes in which KPZ-type behavior holds versus crosses over to Gaussian or other limits.
category_tag: KPZ universality and longest increasing subsequences
status_search_result: For Mallows-distributed permutations, limit theorems for the longest increasing/decreasing subsequence have been established (Bhatnagar–Peled and others), but the limit is Gaussian rather than Tracy–Widom in the regime $0<q<1$ with $n(1-q)\to\infty$. KPZ-class (Tracy–Widom) fluctuations for the LIS have been rigorously established essentially only for the uniform distribution and a few closely related Schur-measure-type models; obtaining KPZ fluctuations for genuinely different non-uniform permutation ensembles remains largely open, though scaling-limit results (Dauvergne) further confirm KPZ behavior in the uniform case.

original_question: Can one explain the mechanism behind Tracy and Widom's solution of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with step initial data, and extend that method to more general initial data sets?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$: particles occupy sites of $\mathbb{Z}$ subject to the exclusion rule (at most one particle per site), and each particle independently attempts to jump one step to the right at rate $p$ and one step to the left at rate $q = 1 - p$, with $p \neq q$, executing a jump only if the target site is empty. For step initial data (sites $\{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ initially occupied and all other sites empty), Tracy and Widom derived exact contour-integral formulas for the distribution of the position of the $m$-th leftmost particle at time $t$ via a coordinate Bethe ansatz, leading after asymptotic analysis to Tracy–Widom GUE fluctuation limits for the current.

(a) Provide a conceptual explanation of why the Tracy–Widom method works: identify the structural mechanism (algebraic, combinatorial, or analytic) responsible for reducing the Bethe-ansatz sum over the symmetric group, applied to step initial data, to a Fredholm determinant amenable to asymptotic analysis.

(b) Using this mechanism, extend the Tracy–Widom solution method to a broader class of deterministic or random initial configurations on $\mathbb{Z}$ (beyond step and step-Bernoulli initial data) so as to obtain explicit, asymptotically tractable formulas for the distribution of particle positions and current fluctuations.
status_search_result: The Tracy–Widom coordinate Bethe ansatz approach to ASEP has, to date, produced asymptotic current fluctuation results only for step and step-Bernoulli initial data. A recognized limitation of the method is that it requires combinatorial guesswork to match a sum identity to the initial configuration, and no general mechanism extending the method to broader initial data has been established. The conceptual question of why the method "works" and how to extend it remains open.

original_question: Can one develop a perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-type interacting-particle models that plays a role analogous to KAM theory in integrable dynamical systems, so that persistence of integrability-like structure and robustness of asymptotic scaling phenomena can be studied beyond exactly solvable models?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a general perturbation theory for KPZ-type interacting-particle systems and stochastic growth models that plays, for the integrable/exactly solvable models in the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class, a role analogous to that of Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser (KAM) theory for integrable Hamiltonian dynamical systems.

Concretely, the KPZ universality class consists of (1+1)-dimensional random growth processes (e.g. the asymmetric simple exclusion process, last-passage percolation with exponential or geometric weights, the q-TASEP, the log-gamma polymer, the KPZ equation itself, etc.) whose height function h(t,x) is conjectured to satisfy, in suitable scaling, h(t,x) ≈ v∞ t + t^{1/3} ξ(x t^{-2/3}), where ξ is a universal limiting field (e.g. the Airy_2 process). For a small but distinguished family of "exactly solvable" models, this scaling and the limiting distributions (Tracy–Widom GUE/GOE, Baik–Rains, etc.) have been rigorously established by means of exact algebraic identities (determinantal/Pfaffian structure, Bethe ansatz, Macdonald processes, stochastic vertex models, etc.).

The problem is the following. Construct a robust mathematical framework in which:

(a) one defines a notion of "integrability" for a stochastic interacting-particle / growth model that captures the algebraic structure used to obtain exact one-point and multi-point asymptotics in the solvable cases;

(b) given an exactly solvable model M_0 and a perturbation M_ε within a suitable class of local stochastic perturbations of its dynamics (with ε a small parameter), one proves that, for ε in some non-trivial set (possibly of positive measure, in analogy with the Cantor-like sets of KAM tori), the perturbed model M_ε retains enough of the integrable structure of M_0 to deduce KPZ-class scaling exponents (1/3, 2/3) and the same universal limiting distributions for its height function;

(c) the framework yields quantitative stability statements: explicit (and sharp in ε) bounds on the deformation of the integrable structure and on the convergence to the universal limit.

Equivalently, give a perturbative scheme that proves persistence of the KPZ scaling limit and of the asymptotic distributional invariants under small non-integrable perturbations of integrable stochastic growth models, in the same way that KAM theory proves persistence of invariant tori under small non-integrable perturbations of integrable Hamiltonian systems.
status_search_result: No general "KAM-type" perturbation theory for non-solvable KPZ-class models is known. Surveys and lecture notes on KPZ universality and integrable probability continue to describe universality beyond exactly solvable models as a major open conceptual challenge, with progress confined to specific solvable models and limited robustness results (e.g., comparison/coupling techniques, slow-decorrelation, and recent invariance results), but no systematic perturbative framework analogous to KAM has been established.

original_question: For the Toda algorithm applied to random Hermitian matrices, where the stopping time T^(1)(H) is used to compute the largest eigenvalue, can one prove universality for the centered and scaled stopping-time variable in the cases of beta = 1 invariant ensembles and beta = 1 or 2 Wigner ensembles?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $H$ be an $n\times n$ random Hermitian (or real symmetric) matrix. Recall that the Toda flow on Hermitian matrices is the isospectral evolution
$$ \frac{dH}{dt} = [B(H),H], \qquad B(H) = H_{+} - H_{-}, $$
where $H_{+}$ (resp. $H_{-}$) is the strictly upper (resp. lower) triangular part of $H$. Under this flow, $H(t)$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to a diagonal matrix whose entries are the eigenvalues of $H$, ordered so that $H_{11}(t)\to\lambda_{\max}(H)$, the largest eigenvalue.

For a tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, define the stopping time
$$ T^{(1)}_{\varepsilon}(H) = \inf\Bigl\{ t\ge 0 : \sum_{j>1} |H_{1j}(t)|^{2} < \varepsilon \Bigr\}, $$
i.e.\ the first time the first row/column of $H(t)$ is essentially diagonal, so that $H_{11}(t)$ approximates $\lambda_{\max}(H)$ to accuracy $\varepsilon$. Write $\langle T^{(1)}\rangle = \mathbb{E}[T^{(1)}_{\varepsilon}(H)]$ and $\sigma_{T^{(1)}} = \operatorname{Var}(T^{(1)}_{\varepsilon}(H))^{1/2}$, and consider the centered and scaled variable
$$ \tau_{\varepsilon,n}(H) = \frac{T^{(1)}_{\varepsilon}(H) - \langle T^{(1)}\rangle}{\sigma_{T^{(1)}}}. $$

The relevant ensembles are: (a) the $\beta=1$ invariant ensembles, with density on $n\times n$ real symmetric matrices proportional to $\exp(-n\,\mathrm{Tr}\,V(H))$ for a suitable potential $V$; (b) the $\beta=1$ Wigner ensemble (real symmetric matrices with i.i.d.\ entries above the diagonal, satisfying standard moment conditions); and (c) the $\beta=2$ Wigner ensemble (Hermitian matrices with i.i.d.\ complex entries above the diagonal). For each of these, the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_j\}$ and the squared first-eigenvector components $\{\beta_k\}$ (the weights $|\langle e_1, v_k\rangle|^{2}$ in the spectral decomposition of $H$) determine $T^{(1)}_{\varepsilon}(H)$ via an explicit formula; controlling their joint statistics as $n\to\infty$ is what is required.

Problem. For each of the three classes of ensembles above — namely $\beta=1$ invariant ensembles, $\beta=1$ Wigner ensembles, and $\beta=2$ Wigner ensembles — prove a universality theorem for the centered and scaled Toda stopping-time variable $\tau_{\varepsilon,n}$: identify a deterministic regime of parameters $(\varepsilon,n)$ in which the distribution of $\tau_{\varepsilon,n}$ converges, as $n\to\infty$, to a limiting distribution that depends only on the symmetry class and not on the further details of the ensemble (such as the potential $V$ in the invariant case or the entry distribution in the Wigner case).
status_search_result: Universality for the centered and scaled Toda halting time was proven for $\beta=2$ invariant ensembles using Riemann–Hilbert techniques. Subsequent work by Deift and Trogdon (arXiv:1604.07384, "Universality for the Toda algorithm to compute the largest eigenvalue of a random matrix") established universality of the halting-time fluctuations for real symmetric and complex Hermitian Wigner-type matrices, using rigidity, delocalization and edge universality for the eigenvalue/eigenvector statistics. A subsequent extension treats sample covariance matrices. The full joint control of eigenvalues and first-eigenvector weights for $\beta=1$ invariant ensembles needed to obtain universality of $\tau$ in that case appears to remain open in the literature surveyed.

original_question: For the QR algorithm applied to random matrices, can one control, as n tends to infinity, the bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j| and |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| near the eigenvalue lambda_j closest to zero, together with the associated normalized eigenvectors, so as to prove the analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for QR?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix drawn from a suitable ensemble (e.g., a Wigner matrix or a sample covariance matrix), and consider the QR algorithm applied to $X_n$: starting from $A_0 = X_n$, recursively compute $A_k = Q_k R_k$ (the QR factorization with $Q_k$ unitary and $R_k$ upper triangular with nonnegative diagonal) and set $A_{k+1} = R_k Q_k$. The diagonal entries of $A_k$ converge to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$ of $X_n$, and the off-diagonal entries decay at a rate governed by neighboring eigenvalue ratios.

Index the eigenvalues so that $|\lambda_1| \ge |\lambda_2| \ge \cdots \ge |\lambda_n|$, and let $j = j(n)$ be such that $\lambda_j$ lies deep in the bulk of the limiting spectrum and is closest to $0$. 

(a) Establish, as $n \to \infty$, the limiting joint distribution (after appropriate normalization) of the bulk eigenvalue ratios
$$\left|\frac{\lambda_{j+1}}{\lambda_j}\right|, \qquad \left|\frac{\lambda_{j-1}}{\lambda_j}\right|,$$
together with the corresponding normalized eigenvectors of $X_n$ associated with $\lambda_{j-1},\lambda_j,\lambda_{j+1}$, and show that this joint limit is universal, i.e., depends on the ensemble only through symmetry class.

(b) Use (a) to prove a universality theorem for the QR algorithm asserting that, with appropriate centering and scaling, the number of QR iterations required to compute the eigenvalue closest to zero to a prescribed accuracy $\varepsilon$ converges in distribution, as $n\to\infty$, to a universal limiting law independent of the underlying matrix distribution (the QR analogue of the known Toda-algorithm universality theorem).
status_search_result: Universality results have been established for the Toda algorithm and for power/inverse-power and QR halting times on sample covariance matrices (Deift–Trogdon, Paquette–Trogdon), but control of bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics $|\lambda_{j\pm1}/\lambda_j|$ near $\lambda_j\approx 0$ together with the associated eigenvectors, and the corresponding full QR-algorithm universality theorem analogous to the Toda case, do not appear to have been proved as of 2026.

original_question: For some eigenvalue algorithm A, can one prove a universality theorem for the deflation time T_{epsilon,n,A,E}, where T_{epsilon,n,A,E} is the smallest time at which the evolving matrix becomes approximately block diagonal to accuracy epsilon and the problem depends on statistics of both eigenvalues and eigenvectors?
self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be an invariant ensemble of $n\times n$ real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) random matrices, and let $A$ be an eigenvalue algorithm that, given an initial matrix $X(0)$ drawn from $E$, produces a sequence (or continuous flow) of isospectral matrices $\{X(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ (for example, the Toda flow, the QR algorithm, or the Jacobi algorithm). For a fixed accuracy parameter $\varepsilon>0$, define the deflation time
$$T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E} \;=\; \inf\Bigl\{t\ge 0 : X(t) \text{ admits a block decomposition } \begin{pmatrix}A & B\\ B^* & C\end{pmatrix} \text{ with } A\in\mathbb{C}^{j\times j},\ C\in\mathbb{C}^{(n-j)\times(n-j)},$$
$$\ 1\le j\le n-1,\ \text{and } \|B\|=\|B^*\|\le \varepsilon\Bigr\}.$$
Let $\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E} = (T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E} - \mathbb{E}[T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}])/\mathrm{sd}(T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E})$ denote the normalized deflation time.

Prove (or disprove) the following universality statement: there exists an algorithm $A$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$ in a suitable range and every fixed $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\bigl(\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}\le x\bigr)$$
exists and is independent of the choice of ensemble $E$ within a wide class (e.g., Wigner ensembles with sub-Gaussian entries having matching first two moments). The deflation time depends on joint statistics of both eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $X(0)$, so a proof must handle both rigidity/edge-universality of the spectrum and delocalization/universality of the eigenvectors.

status_search_result: Universality for the related "halting time" has been established in several specific settings: Deift–Trogdon proved universality for the Toda algorithm computing the largest eigenvalue of Wigner matrices (arXiv:1604.07384) and for the power/inverse power and QR algorithms on sample covariance matrices (arXiv:1701.01896). However, a full universality theorem for the general deflation time T_{ε,n,A,E} (which requires controlling all off-diagonal blocks and thus eigenvector statistics globally) does not yet appear to have been proved for any standard algorithm in full generality, and this remains identified as a challenging problem.

original_question: Can one rigorously prove universality for one of the other numerical algorithms with random data discussed in the paper, especially the conjugate-gradient algorithm for solving a random linear system A x = b with both A and b random?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$ be a symmetric positive-definite random matrix drawn from a suitable ensemble (for example, a sample covariance / Wishart-type ensemble whose entries satisfy standard moment conditions, or a Wigner-type ensemble shifted to be positive definite), and let $b \in \mathbb{R}^N$ be an independent random vector with i.i.d. coordinates having mean $0$, variance $1$, and finite higher moments. Apply the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm to the linear system $A x = b$, producing iterates $x_0=0, x_1, x_2, \ldots$ with residuals $r_k = b - A x_k$, and define the halting time
$$T_N(\varepsilon) = \min\{ k \ge 0 : \|r_k\|_2 / \|b\|_2 \le \varepsilon \}.$$

Prove a universality theorem for the CG algorithm in this setting: namely, show that the fluctuations and/or limiting distribution of $T_N(\varepsilon)$ (and of related quantities such as the residual norms $\|r_k\|_2$ and the Lanczos tridiagonalization data generated by CG on $(A,b)$), suitably normalized as $N \to \infty$, depend only on a small number of moments of the entry distributions of $A$ and $b$ and not on the finer details of those distributions. Equivalently, establish that the limiting law agrees with the law obtained in the Gaussian (e.g. GOE / Wishart with Gaussian entries) case under the same moment matching.
category_tag: Random matrix universality for numerical algorithms
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Paquette and Trogdon ("Universality for the conjugate gradient and MINRES algorithms on sample covariance matrices") established universality of the halting time and related quantities for CG and MINRES applied to sample covariance (Wishart-type) matrices via a four-moment theorem for the spectral measure, and Deift–Trogdon and others proved that CG on well-conditioned Wishart matrices is almost deterministic. These results resolve significant cases of the problem, though full universality across all the matrix ensembles considered in the original numerical-algorithm framework is not completely settled.

original_question: Can the orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method developed by Olver, Nadakuditi, and Trogdon for invariant unitary ensembles be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles, while retaining its essentially machine-accuracy sampling behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A β-invariant matrix ensemble on N×N matrices has joint eigenvalue probability density proportional to
   p_β(x_1,…,x_N) ∝ ∏_{i<j} |x_i − x_j|^β · ∏_{k} e^{−N V(x_k)},
where V is a sufficiently regular confining potential and β ∈ {1,2,4} corresponds respectively to orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic symmetry classes. For β = 2 (the unitary case) there exists a sampling algorithm based on the determinantal-point-process representation of the eigenvalues and the orthogonal polynomials with weight e^{−NV(x)}: one computes the orthogonal polynomials numerically, forms the Christoffel–Darboux kernel, and samples eigenvalues sequentially via conditional kernels. With high-precision computation of the orthogonal polynomials, this algorithm samples the eigenvalue distribution to essentially machine precision in finite time.

Problem. Construct an analogous orthogonal-polynomial / skew-orthogonal-polynomial based sampling algorithm for the orthogonal (β = 1) and symplectic (β = 4) invariant ensembles, that
 (i) produces samples from the exact joint eigenvalue density p_β(x_1,…,x_N) (for β ∈ {1,4}),
 (ii) achieves essentially machine-accuracy sampling, in the sense that the total-variation distance between the algorithm's output distribution and the target eigenvalue distribution is bounded by a quantity of the order of machine epsilon, and
 (iii) runs in finite (preferably polynomial in N) time.

Equivalently, exploiting the Pfaffian point process structure of the β = 1 and β = 4 ensembles (with kernel built from skew-orthogonal polynomials), give a sequential sampling procedure for these Pfaffian point processes that achieves essentially machine-accuracy, paralleling the determinantal sampler available for β = 2.
status_search_result: A 2026 preprint ("Sampling Pfaffian point processes and the symplectic Arnoldi method", arXiv:2605.01202) presents an exact sampling algorithm for Pfaffian point processes via a skew-symmetric Cholesky-type factorization, explicitly addressing the orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles (β = 1, 4). This appears to provide the desired extension, though it is not yet clear from the abstract alone whether the machine-accuracy claim of the unitary case is fully matched. Status is therefore best described as partially solved / likely solved pending verification.

original_question: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line, i u_t = u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u for x >= 0 and t >= 0, with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) and oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one compute the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t) for general real driving frequency w?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line,
    i u_t(x,t) = u_{xx}(x,t) + 2 |u(x,t)|^2 u(x,t),    x ≥ 0, t ≥ 0,
with prescribed initial data
    u(x,0) = f(x),    x ≥ 0,
(where f is a given Schwartz-class function decaying at infinity), and oscillatory Dirichlet boundary forcing
    u(0,t) = e^{i ω t},    t ≥ 0,
for a fixed real parameter ω ∈ ℝ.

Determine, for every ω ∈ ℝ, the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) as t → ∞. More precisely, compute the leading-order asymptotics of u(x,t) along each ray x/t = ξ (ξ ≥ 0 fixed), identifying the relevant asymptotic sectors (e.g. plane-wave, modulated elliptic/genus-g, or self-similar regions), and providing explicit formulas for the leading terms (amplitude, phase, and any modulation parameters) in terms of f and ω.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on focusing NLS half-line problems with time-periodic boundary data of the form a e^{iα} e^{2iωt} via Riemann–Hilbert / nonlinear steepest descent methods, identifying multiple asymptotic regimes (genus 0, 1, 2, 3 waves) for certain parameter ranges and special initial data. However, a complete description of the long-time asymptotics for general real driving frequency ω and general decaying initial data f(x) does not appear to be fully established; the problem remains an active research area with only partial answers.

original_question: For the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with oscillatory boundary forcing u(0,t) = e^{i w t}, can one show that as w decreases toward 0 the boundary drive excites k-gap solutions of periodic NLS?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line
$$ i\,u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u = 0, \qquad x>0,\ t>0, $$
with zero initial data $u(x,0)=0$ and oscillatory Dirichlet boundary forcing
$$ u(0,t) = e^{i\omega t}, \qquad t>0, $$
where $\omega>0$ is a real parameter. Recall that the periodic focusing NLS equation on the line admits a hierarchy of finite-gap (algebro-geometric) quasi-periodic solutions associated with hyperelliptic spectral curves; a $k$-gap solution is one whose Lax-operator spectrum has exactly $k$ open gaps in the upper half-plane (so that $k=0$ corresponds to the plane wave and $k=1$ to the elliptic/Akhmediev–type solutions).

Prove or disprove the following: as $\omega\downarrow 0$, the long-time / large-$x$ asymptotic profile of the solution $u(x,t)$ to the above boundary-driven problem develops, in suitable space-time regions, into $k$-gap solutions of the periodic focusing NLS equation, with $k=k(\omega)\to\infty$ as $\omega\downarrow 0$. More precisely, characterize the spectral data (endpoints of the gaps) of the emergent finite-gap solutions in terms of $\omega$, and show that decreasing $\omega$ excites successively higher-genus finite-gap modes of the system.
status_search_result: Searches turn up related work on the focusing NLS equation on the half-line with time-periodic boundary data (Riemann–Hilbert / Dirichlet-to-Neumann analyses) and on finite-gap (k-gap) solutions of periodic NLS, but no result establishing the conjectured emergence of k-gap solutions from the boundary driver e^{iωt} as ω↓0. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line
  i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u,   x > 0,  t > 0,
with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x) for x ≥ 0 (in a suitable Schwartz-type class) and homogeneous Robin boundary condition
  u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0,  t > 0,
where q ∈ ℝ is a fixed constant.

The Bikbaev–Tarasov method is a technique for solving integrable initial-boundary value problems on the half-line by means of a Bäcklund transformation: one extends the solution u(x,t) defined for x > 0 to a function ũ(x,t) defined for all x ∈ ℝ in such a way that ũ satisfies the NLS equation on the whole line, the extension is compatible with the boundary condition at x = 0, and the inverse scattering transform on the line can then be applied. For the focusing NLS (i u_t = u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u) with Robin data, this construction yields a smooth extension and gives a complete solution of the IBVP, including the long-time asymptotics.

Problem: Adapt the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transformation method to the defocusing NLS half-line IBVP with Robin boundary condition above. Specifically, construct a Bäcklund transformation that extends a solution of the defocusing NLS from x > 0 to x < 0, control the singularities that necessarily appear in this extension in the defocusing case, and use the resulting whole-line representation to solve the IBVP and to derive the long-time (t → ∞) asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) on the half-line.
status_search_result: The defocusing NLS half-line IBVP with Robin boundary conditions has been studied successfully via alternative methods (Fokas unified transform method combined with Riemann–Hilbert / weighted Sobolev techniques), yielding representation formulas and long-time asymptotics. However, recent literature explicitly notes that adapting the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transformation approach to the defocusing case is non-trivial because the extension from x>0 to x<0 introduces singularities that must be controlled, and this specific adaptation does not appear to have been carried out. The Bikbaev–Tarasov adaptation itself thus appears to remain open.

original_question: For the nonlinear Schrodinger equation on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions and smooth matching initial and boundary data, can one prove that the initial-boundary value problem remains classical in x > 0 and t > 0 for a general class of smooth nonlinearities, rather than relying on the special Backlund-transform structure available only for the cubic focusing case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the initial–boundary value problem for the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line:

  i u_t + u_{xx} + f(|u|^2) u = 0,   x > 0, t > 0,
  u(x, 0) = u_0(x),                    x ≥ 0,
  u_x(0, t) + α u(0, t) = g(t),        t ≥ 0,

where α ∈ ℝ is a fixed Robin parameter, f : [0, ∞) → ℝ is a smooth nonlinearity (e.g. any element of a general class of smooth functions including, but not limited to, the cubic case f(s) = ±s), and the prescribed data u_0 ∈ C^∞([0, ∞)) and g ∈ C^∞([0, ∞)) satisfy all compatibility (matching) conditions at (x, t) = (0, 0) to all orders.

Prove (or disprove) that, for every such smooth nonlinearity f and every pair of smooth, fully compatible data (u_0, g) satisfying the Robin boundary condition, there exists a solution u ∈ C^∞({(x, t) : x > 0, t > 0}) of the above problem; that is, the initial–boundary value problem is classical in the open quadrant x > 0, t > 0, without invoking integrability-specific tools (such as the Bäcklund-transform/odd-extension construction available only for the cubic focusing case).
status_search_result: Recent works (Himonas–Mantzavinos, Fokas and collaborators, Lee 2023, Alkın 2024, and the 2022 arXiv preprint 2206.13978) establish local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces for NLS on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions, and there are results for higher-order/general power nonlinearities. However, no source explicitly settles the C^∞ classical-regularity question in x>0, t>0 for a fully general class of smooth nonlinearities beyond the integrable cubic case via non-Bäcklund methods. Status appears unresolved in the precise classical-smoothness formulation posed.

original_question: More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \ge 2$) be a domain with sufficiently regular boundary $\partial\Omega$ (for instance, a half-space, an exterior domain, or a smooth bounded domain), and consider an initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for a dispersive partial differential equation, such as the linear or nonlinear Schrödinger equation
$$ i\,u_t + \Delta u + F(u) = 0, \qquad x \in \Omega,\ t > 0, $$
or a higher-dimensional Korteweg–de Vries-type / Zakharov–Kuznetsov-type equation
$$ u_t + \partial_{x_1}\Delta u + u\,\partial_{x_1} u = 0, \qquad x \in \Omega,\ t > 0, $$
supplemented with an initial condition $u(x,0) = u_0(x)$ on $\Omega$ and prescribed boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega \times (0,\infty)$ (e.g. Dirichlet, Neumann, or transparent boundary conditions appropriate to the equation).

Assume that the initial datum $u_0$ possesses some local extra smoothness on a subset $D \subset \Omega$ (for example, $u_0|_D \in H^s(D)$ for some $s$ greater than the global regularity of $u_0$, or $u_0$ has rapid decay on some half-space-like region of $\Omega$).

Determine, in this multi-dimensional setting, what smoothing and propagation-of-regularity properties hold for the resulting solution $u(\cdot,t)$. Specifically: characterize the gain of local regularity (smoothing effect) of solutions to such IBVPs in arbitrary spatial dimension $n \ge 2$, including the manner in which localized smoothness or decay of the initial data is propagated by the flow into other regions of $\Omega$ for $t>0$, and the role played by the boundary $\partial\Omega$ and the chosen boundary conditions in this propagation.
status_search_result: Recent literature (2021–2025) addresses smoothing and propagation of regularity for dispersive equations primarily on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^n$ or on bounded intervals in one dimension. Multi-dimensional initial-boundary value problems for general dispersive equations remain largely unexplored, with results confined to specific equations, geometries, and boundary conditions; no general theory is available, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the semiclassical focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation, can one solve the forward scattering problem for general smooth initial data and then implement the associated Riemann-Hilbert numerical methodology to compute the Cauchy problem in the small-dispersion limit epsilon = hbar down to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in the semiclassical regime
    i ε ∂_t ψ + (ε^2/2) ∂_x^2 ψ + |ψ|^2 ψ = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
with small parameter ε > 0 (identified with ℏ), subject to a general smooth (e.g. Schwartz-class) initial datum
    ψ(x,0) = A(x) exp(i S(x)/ε),   A, S ∈ C^∞(ℝ),
where A is real-valued and rapidly decaying.

The Zakharov–Shabat (forward) scattering problem associated with this equation is the spectral problem for the operator
    L_ε = i ε ∂_x − ( 0      ψ(x,0)
                       −\overline{ψ(x,0)}   0 ),
whose scattering data (reflection coefficient r(λ;ε), discrete eigenvalues, and norming constants for λ ∈ ℂ_+) determine ψ(x,t) via the inverse-scattering Riemann–Hilbert problem (RHP).

Problem. Develop a method that:
(a) rigorously solves the forward scattering problem for the operator L_ε with general smooth initial data A(x) exp(i S(x)/ε), determining the full set of scattering data (in particular controlling its dependence on ε as ε ↓ 0);
(b) uses these scattering data as input to the corresponding inverse Riemann–Hilbert problem and implements a numerical methodology (e.g. via nonlinear steepest descent / numerical RHP techniques) that computes the solution ψ(x,t;ε) of the Cauchy problem uniformly in (x,t) on bounded sets, in the small-dispersion limit ε ↓ 0.

In particular, can such a forward-scattering procedure plus Riemann–Hilbert numerical implementation be carried out for general smooth initial data (beyond special analytic or one-parameter families), yielding accurate computation of the focusing semiclassical NLS Cauchy problem as ε ↓ 0?
status_search_result: Existing rigorous semiclassical results for focusing NLS via Riemann–Hilbert methods are limited to special initial data: analytic single-lobe potentials (Kamvissis–McLaughlin–Miller), one-parameter families such as square-barrier or sech-type data (Tovbis–Venakides–Zhou, Jenkins–McLaughlin), and specific non-analytic cases. Numerical inverse-scattering RHP solvers (Trogdon–Olver) work well in non-semiclassical regimes but the forward scattering for general smooth data with ε ↓ 0 is not handled in full generality. No publication appears to claim a complete resolution for general smooth initial data, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the Airy integral operator A_s on L^2(s, infinity), whose Fredholm determinant gives the edge-scaling distribution for the largest GUE eigenvalue, can one analyze the eigenfunctions u_tilde_j(s) asymptotically as s tends to infinity and also compute them accurately for finite s?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Ai}(x)$ denote the Airy function, the solution of $y''=xy$ that decays as $x\to+\infty$. Define the Airy kernel
$$K(x,y)=\frac{\mathrm{Ai}(x)\,\mathrm{Ai}'(y)-\mathrm{Ai}'(x)\,\mathrm{Ai}(y)}{x-y},$$
and for $s\in\mathbb{R}$ let $\mathcal{A}_s$ be the integral operator on $L^2(s,\infty)$ with kernel $K(x,y)$. The operator $\mathcal{A}_s$ is trace class, self-adjoint, and has a discrete sequence of eigenvalues $1>\lambda_1(s)>\lambda_2(s)>\cdots>0$ with corresponding $L^2(s,\infty)$-orthonormal eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(\cdot;s)$ satisfying
$$\int_s^\infty K(x,y)\,\tilde u_j(y;s)\,dy=\lambda_j(s)\,\tilde u_j(x;s),\qquad x>s.$$
The Fredholm determinant $F_2(s)=\det(I-\mathcal{A}_s)=\prod_j(1-\lambda_j(s))$ is the Tracy–Widom GUE distribution governing the edge-scaling limit of the largest eigenvalue of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.

Problem. 
(a) Determine the asymptotic behavior of the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(x;s)$ as $s\to+\infty$, for each fixed $j\ge 1$, including leading-order shape and decay/oscillation rates uniform in $x>s$.
(b) Provide a method to compute $\tilde u_j(x;s)$ accurately for finite values of $s\in\mathbb{R}$, with controlled error.
status_search_result: Subsequent work (Bornemann; Townsend, Trogdon, Olver and related contributions, ca. 2021–2024) developed spectral algorithms exploiting the commuting differential operator (the "bispectral" Airy ODE) to compute the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Airy integral operator to high relative precision for finite s, and to evaluate Tracy–Widom GUE to machine accuracy including its right tail. The finite-s computational part is thus largely resolved, while sharp uniform large-s asymptotic expansions of the eigenfunctions $\tilde u_j(x;s)$ themselves are addressed in part through the commuting differential operator's WKB analysis but do not appear to have a complete published treatment for all j.

original_question: For perturbations of the focusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation of the form i u_tilde_t + u_tilde_xx + 2 |u_tilde|^2 u_tilde + epsilon |u_tilde|^ell u_tilde = 0 with decaying initial data, can one analyze the long-time behavior of solutions, especially in the case where the initial data correspond to a two-soliton solution of the unperturbed focusing NLS equation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the real line
  i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u + ε |u|^ℓ u = 0,   (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ,
where ε > 0 is a small parameter and ℓ > 0 is a fixed exponent with ℓ ≠ 2 (so that the perturbation is genuinely non-integrable). Impose the initial condition
  u(x,0) = f(x),
where f is a smooth, sufficiently rapidly decaying function as |x| → ∞. The unperturbed equation (ε = 0) is the integrable focusing cubic NLS, and admits explicit N-soliton solutions obtained via the inverse scattering transform.

Problem. Develop a rigorous long-time asymptotic analysis of the Cauchy problem above as t → +∞ for general decaying initial data f. In particular, in the case where f(x) is chosen to coincide at t = 0 with a 2-soliton solution of the unperturbed (ε = 0) focusing NLS equation — i.e. f is the reflectionless potential whose discrete scattering data consist of two complex eigenvalues λ_1, λ_2 ∈ ℂ⁺ (with λ_2 ≠ -conjugate(λ_1)) and prescribed norming constants — describe the leading-order behavior of the solution u(x,t) in each space-time region {x/t ≈ const} as t → ∞. Determine, in particular, whether the two solitons survive the perturbation, what modulation equations govern their parameters (positions, velocities, amplitudes, phases) as functions of ε and t, and what radiative/dispersive corrections are emitted, providing error estimates uniform in (x,t).
category_tag: Perturbed focusing NLS and soliton asymptotics
status_search_result: Long-time asymptotics for the integrable focusing NLS via Riemann–Hilbert/∂-steepest-descent methods is well developed, and there is recent progress on perturbed integrable equations (e.g. perturbed mKdV) and on focusing NLS with nonzero boundary conditions including discrete spectrum. However, no rigorous long-time asymptotic analysis of the Cauchy problem for the non-integrable perturbation i u_t + u_{xx} + 2|u|^2 u + ε|u|^ℓ u = 0 with general decaying data — and in particular with 2-soliton initial data — appears to have been completed; the question is generally regarded as open.

original_question: Can one use Riemann-Hilbert and nonlinear steepest-descent methods to give a fully rigorous proof of the asymptotic results obtained by Venakides, Deift, and Oba for the Toda shock problem, where the driven lattice settles into a one-gap periodic state for sufficiently strong driving?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the doubly infinite Toda lattice
$$\dot a_n(t)=a_n(t)\bigl(b_{n+1}(t)-b_n(t)\bigr),\qquad \dot b_n(t)=2\bigl(a_n(t)^2-a_{n-1}(t)^2\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z,\ t\ge 0,$$
with shock-type (step-like) initial data
$$\bigl(a_n(0),b_n(0)\bigr)\to\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2},c_\pm\bigr)\quad\text{as }n\to\pm\infty,$$
where $c_-<c_+$ (a left background "moving" toward a lower right background, i.e. the driven shock regime). For sufficiently strong driving (i.e. $c_+-c_-$ exceeding a threshold so that the two background spectra $[c_\pm-1,c_\pm+1]$ do not overlap), it has been predicted that as $t\to\infty$ in the central region $n/t$ in a certain interval the lattice variables $(a_n(t),b_n(t))$ are asymptotically described by a fixed one-gap (genus-one) quasi-periodic finite-gap Toda solution determined by the two background spectra, with explicit Whitham-modulated transition zones connecting this elliptic region to the unperturbed backgrounds.

Problem: Using the Riemann–Hilbert problem associated with the inverse scattering transform for step-like Toda data, together with the Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method (including the construction of suitable $g$-functions, opening of lenses, model problems with theta-function parametrices on the genus-one Riemann surface, and local parametrices at the band endpoints), produce a fully rigorous proof — including small-norm error estimates — of the predicted long-time asymptotic behavior of $(a_n(t),b_n(t))$ in all asymptotic regions of the $(n,t)$ half-plane for the strongly driven Toda shock problem, thereby justifying the formal asymptotic description.
status_search_result: A series of works by Egorova, Michor, Pryimak, and Teschl (2018–2021) carried out the rigorous Riemann–Hilbert/nonlinear-steepest-descent analysis of the Toda shock problem: "Long-Time Asymptotics for the Toda Shock Problem: Non-Overlapping Spectra," "Long-time asymptotics for Toda shock waves in the modulation region" (arXiv:2001.05184), "Toda shock waves: justification of asymptotics," and "How Discrete Spectrum and Resonances Influence the Asymptotics of the Toda Shock Wave" (arXiv:2012.12371). Together these papers solve the local parametrix problems and provide rigorous small-norm error estimates, justifying the Venakides–Deift–Oba asymptotic predictions.

original_question: If the exponential interaction in the Toda shock problem is replaced by a nearby force law F(x) so that the lattice equation becomes x_doubleprime_k = F(x_{k-1} - x_k) - F(x_k - x_{k+1}), can one analyze the general shock problem for suitably small perturbations F(x) of e^x and prove the numerically observed asymptotic behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite one-dimensional lattice of unit-mass particles with positions $x_k(t)$, $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, governed by the equations of motion
$$\ddot{x}_k(t) = F(x_{k-1}(t)-x_k(t)) - F(x_k(t)-x_{k+1}(t)), \qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},$$
where $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth force law. The classical Toda lattice corresponds to $F(x)=e^x$. The shock initial-value problem is specified by data of the form
$$x_k(0) - x_{k+1}(0) \to a_-, \quad \dot x_k(0) \to b_- \text{ as } k\to -\infty,$$
$$x_k(0) - x_{k+1}(0) \to a_+, \quad \dot x_k(0) \to b_+ \text{ as } k\to +\infty,$$
with $(a_-,b_-)\neq(a_+,b_+)$ chosen so that the corresponding asymptotic constant solutions disagree (a "shock"). For the Toda case $F(x)=e^x$ it is known that as $t\to\infty$ the solution develops a structured asymptotic profile organized by five regions, including a middle region described by a $2$-periodic travelling wave $x_k(t+T)=x_k(t)$ with $x_{k+2}(t)=x_k(t)$.

Assume now that $F$ is a small smooth perturbation of $e^x$ in a suitable sense (e.g.\ $F-\exp$ small in an appropriate $C^r$ or weighted norm on $\mathbb{R}$), and assume that the perturbed system admits a $2$-periodic travelling wave solution as above. Prove that for every shock initial datum the solution of the perturbed lattice equation exhibits the same long-time asymptotic behavior as the Toda shock solution, in particular reproducing the five-region asymptotic description and the $2$-periodic middle-region profile.
status_search_result: A web search returns rigorous long-time asymptotic results for the integrable Toda shock problem (e.g., via Riemann–Hilbert/nonlinear steepest descent, including non-overlapping spectra and short-range perturbations of periodic backgrounds), but no result was found establishing the analogous shock asymptotics for genuinely non-integrable nearby force laws $F$ replacing $e^x$. The status for general (non-integrable) small perturbations $F$ of the exponential force appears unresolved in the located sources.

original_question: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the diffraction problem for waves passing through two finite slits in the plane, the setting underlying Young's double-slit experiment in optics and the analogous double-slit experiment in quantum mechanics?
status_search_result: Standard references on diffraction theory provide explicit rigorous solutions for a single slit/half-plane (Sommerfeld, Kirchhoff approximations) and various asymptotic or numerical treatments for multiple slits, but no fully rigorous closed-form solution of the two-slit Helmholtz boundary value problem with edge and radiation conditions appears in the standard literature; results found are either approximate (Fraunhofer/Kirchhoff), numerical, or address related but distinct geometries (single slit, lattice models, sub-wavelength real-metal slit).

context_brief: bounded operator representation of overcomplete Gabor frames
original_question: Do there exist overcomplete Gabor frames for L^2(R), meaning systems of the form {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} with g in L^2(R) and parameters a,b>0 that form a frame but not a Riesz basis, together with some ordering {f_k}_{k in I} of the frame elements, such that the ordered frame can be written as {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded linear operator T and some vector phi?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, define the translation operator $T_a:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by $(T_a f)(x)=f(x-a)$ and the modulation operator $E_b:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by $(E_b f)(x)=e^{2\pi i bx}f(x)$. A countable family $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R})$ is a frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ if there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ such that
$$A\|f\|^2\le \sum_{k\in I}|\langle f,f_k\rangle|^2\le B\|f\|^2\quad\text{for all }f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}).$$
A frame is called a Riesz basis if it is also a Schauder basis (equivalently, $\omega$-independent). A frame that is not a Riesz basis is called overcomplete.

Given $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and parameters $a,b>0$, the associated Gabor system is
$$\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)=\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}.$$

Question: Do there exist $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and $a,b>0$ such that $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, together with a bijective ordering $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ of the elements of $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ (where $I=\mathbb{Z}$ or $I=\mathbb{N}_0$), a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$, and a vector $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$f_k = T^k\varphi\quad\text{for all }k\in I\,?$$
status_search_result: For the index set $I=\mathbb{N}_0$, subsequent work has shown that overcomplete Gabor (and wavelet) frames cannot be represented as $\{T^n\varphi\}_{n=0}^\infty$ with $T$ bounded; thus the problem is resolved negatively in this case. For the index set $I=\mathbb{Z}$, the question remains open in general, although certain classes of overcomplete Gabor frames have been shown not to admit such a representation by orbits of bounded invertible operators.

context_brief: indexing dependence for Gabor orbit representations
original_question: Assume an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admits an ordering {f_k} for which {f_k}_{k in I} = {T^k phi}_{k in I} with bounded T. Must such a bounded-operator representation exist for both indexing choices I=N_0={0,1,2,...} and I=Z, or can the existence of a bounded representation depend on whether the ordered orbit is one-sided or two-sided?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For $a,b>0$ and a window $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the modulation and translation operators by $(E_b f)(x)=e^{2\pi i b x}f(x)$ and $(T_a f)(x)=f(x-a)$, and consider the Gabor system
$$\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}.$$
Assume that this system is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, i.e., a frame which is not a Riesz basis.

A sequence $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R})$ (where $I=\mathbb{N}_0:=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ or $I=\mathbb{Z}$) is said to admit a bounded operator representation indexed by $I$ if there exist $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$f_k = T^k\varphi \qquad \text{for all } k\in I,$$
where for $I=\mathbb{Z}$ this requires $T$ to be invertible with $T^{-1}$ bounded.

Question. Suppose the overcomplete Gabor frame $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ admits some enumeration as a sequence $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ that has a bounded operator representation indexed by $I$. Must such a bounded operator representation exist for both choices $I=\mathbb{N}_0$ and $I=\mathbb{Z}$, or can the existence of such a representation genuinely depend on whether the orbit is one-sided ($I=\mathbb{N}_0$) or two-sided ($I=\mathbb{Z}$)?
status_search_result: Subsequent work established that an overcomplete Gabor (or wavelet) frame can never be written as a one-sided orbit $\{T^n f_0\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ of a bounded operator, settling the $I=\mathbb{N}_0$ case in the negative. The two-sided case $I=\mathbb{Z}$ remains open in general; certain classes of overcomplete Gabor frames have been shown not to admit a bounded invertible representation over $\mathbb{Z}$, but the full question is still unresolved. Hence the dependence-on-indexing question is only partially answered.

context_brief: characterizing admissible orderings of Gabor frames
original_question: Given an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, which orderings {f_k}_{k in I} of its elements have the property that the ordered frame can be represented as an operator orbit {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for some bounded linear operator T? In other words, can one characterize exactly which permutations or sequential arrangements of the same Gabor frame yield a bounded generating operator?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Hilbert space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the translation and modulation operators by
$$(T_n g)(x) = g(x-na), \qquad (E_m g)(x) = e^{2\pi i m b x} g(x), \qquad m,n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
The Gabor system generated by $g$, $a$, $b$ is $G(g,a,b) := \{E_{mb} T_{na} g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$. Assume that $G(g,a,b)$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, that is, there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ with
$$A\|f\|^2 \le \sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}} |\langle f, E_{mb}T_{na}g\rangle|^2 \le B\|f\|^2 \quad\text{for all } f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}),$$
and the system is not a Riesz basis.

For a countable index set $I\in\{\mathbb{N},\mathbb{Z}\}$, an ordering $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ of $G(g,a,b)$ is a bijection of $I$ onto $G(g,a,b)$. Such an ordering is said to admit a bounded operator representation if there exist a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and a vector $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$f_k = T^k \varphi \quad\text{for all } k\in I.$$

Problem: Give a complete characterization of those orderings $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ of the overcomplete Gabor frame $G(g,a,b)$ which admit a bounded operator representation in the above sense.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has established several partial results: an overcomplete Gabor frame can never be written as an orbit $(T^n\varphi)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of a bounded operator indexed by $\mathbb{N}$; for the index set $\mathbb{Z}$ with bijective bounded operators, no admissible ordering exists when, e.g., the window has support in an interval of length $a$, or when $ab$ is irrational. A general necessary-and-sufficient characterization of all admissible orderings remains open.

context_brief: which Gabor frames admit some bounded ordering
original_question: Which overcomplete Gabor frames {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admit at least one ordering {f_k}_{k in I} for which there exists a bounded linear operator T and a vector phi with {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I}? Equivalently, what conditions on the lattice parameters a,b>0 and the window g in L^2(R) determine whether some ordering of the frame can be generated by iterating a bounded operator?
self_contained_problem:
For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the modulation and translation operators $E_{mb},T_{na}:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by $(E_{mb}f)(x)=e^{2\pi i mb x}f(x)$ and $(T_{na}f)(x)=f(x-na)$, and consider the Gabor system $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$. Assume this system is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ (i.e. it is a frame but not a Riesz basis). 

Characterize all triples $(a,b,g)$ for which there exists a bijection $\sigma:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}^2$, a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$, and a vector $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that, writing $f_k:=E_{\sigma(k)_1 b}T_{\sigma(k)_2 a}g$, one has 
$$f_k = T^k\varphi \quad\text{for all } k\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
Equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the lattice parameters $a,b>0$ and the window $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under which some ordering of the overcomplete Gabor frame can be realized as the two-sided orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ of a bounded linear operator $T$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has shown that no overcomplete Gabor (or wavelet) frame can be represented as the one-sided orbit $\{T^n\varphi\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of a bounded operator, and certain classes of overcomplete Gabor frames cannot be ordered over $\mathbb{Z}$ and written as the orbit of a bounded invertible operator. The full characterization for $\mathbb{Z}$-indexed orderings remains open.

context_brief: universal ordering for bounded Gabor representations
original_question: Is there a single universal ordering rule {f_k}_{k in I} that works for every overcomplete Gabor frame that admits some bounded-operator orbit representation, so that whenever a frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is of a type covered by the previous existence question, arranging its elements according to that one rule always yields {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded operator T?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $H=L^2(\mathbb{R})$. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in H$, define the modulation and translation operators by $E_{mb}f(x)=e^{2\pi i mb x}f(x)$ and $T_{na}f(x)=f(x-na)$, and consider the Gabor system $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$. A frame $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ for $H$ (with $I=\mathbb{N}$ or $I=\mathbb{Z}$) is said to admit a bounded operator orbit representation if there exist $\varphi\in H$ and a bounded linear operator $T:H\to H$ such that $f_k=T^k\varphi$ for all $k\in I$.

Assume that the class $\mathcal{G}$ of overcomplete Gabor frames $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ which, after some bijective relabeling by $I$, can be written as a bounded-operator orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$, is nonempty.

Question. Does there exist a single universal ordering rule, i.e. a fixed family of bijections $\sigma_{a,b,g}:\mathbb{Z}^2\to I$ depending only on $(a,b,g)$ through a uniform prescription, such that for every Gabor frame $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ in $\mathcal{G}$, defining $f_k:=E_{m b}T_{n a}g$ where $(m,n)=\sigma_{a,b,g}^{-1}(k)$ yields a sequence $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ that has the form $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$ for some bounded operator $T$ on $H$ and some $\varphi\in H$?
status_search_result: The broader problem of representing overcomplete Gabor frames as orbits of a bounded operator indexed by Z is a known open question in frame theory. Subsequent work (e.g., Christensen–Hasannasab and the 2020 paper "Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames") has addressed existence-type questions but does not appear to provide a universal ordering rule applicable to all such Gabor frames; the universal ordering question (P1-d) remains open as of available literature.

context_brief: one-sided bounded representation for translate frames
original_question: Let phi in L^2(R) and b>0 be such that the translate system {T_{kb} phi}_{k in Z} is an overcomplete frame. Although this system always has the two-sided representation {(T_b)^k phi}_{k in Z} with bounded translation operator T_b, is it possible to reorder the same frame into a one-sided sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^infty and find a bounded linear operator T such that {f_k}_{k=0}^infty={T^k phi}_{k=0}^infty?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and let $b > 0$. For $a \in \mathbb{R}$, denote by $T_a : L^2(\mathbb{R}) \to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ the translation operator $(T_a f)(x) = f(x-a)$. Assume that the system $\{T_{kb}\phi\}_{k \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is an overcomplete frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R})$, i.e. it is a frame (there exist $0 < A \le B < \infty$ such that $A\|f\|^2 \le \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} |\langle f, T_{kb}\phi\rangle|^2 \le B\|f\|^2$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$) but not a Riesz basis. Decide whether it is always possible to reorder this frame as a one-sided sequence $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ (i.e. there exists a bijection $\sigma : \mathbb{N}_0 \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $f_k = T_{\sigma(k)b}\phi$) and to find a bounded linear operator $T : L^2(\mathbb{R}) \to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that
$$\{f_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty} = \{T^k \phi\}_{k=0}^{\infty}.$$
Equivalently: does every overcomplete frame of integer translates admit a representation as the forward orbit $\{T^k \phi\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ of a bounded operator $T$ acting on the same generator $\phi$?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Christensen, Hasannasab and collaborators on operator representations of frames and dynamical sampling explicitly notes that for overcomplete shift-invariant/Gabor-type frames the existence of a representation $\{T^k\phi\}_{k=0}^\infty$ with bounded $T$ has been confirmed only in the Riesz basis case and remains open for overcomplete frames of translates. Survey articles up to 2024 still list this as an open problem; only partial / approximate results (e.g. approximation by suborbits of bounded operators) are available.

context_brief: norm-bounded-below overcomplete operator orbits in Hilbert space
original_question: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H with an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^infty whose vectors are uniformly bounded away from zero in norm and for which there is a bounded linear operator T from H to H such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0? Equivalently, can an overcomplete frame that does not decay in norm still be generated as a one-sided bounded operator orbit?
self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. A sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^∞ ⊂ H is called a frame for H if there exist constants 0 < A ≤ B < ∞ such that
   A·||x||² ≤ Σ_{k=0}^∞ |⟨x, f_k⟩|² ≤ B·||x||²  for every x ∈ H.
The frame is said to be norm-bounded below if inf_{k≥0} ||f_k|| > 0, and overcomplete if it remains a frame for H after removal of some element f_k (equivalently, the synthesis operator has nontrivial kernel).

Question. Does there exist an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^∞ for H which is norm-bounded below and which admits a representation
   f_k = T^k f_0   for all k ≥ 0
for some bounded linear operator T : H → H?
status_search_result: Subsequent work in frame theory establishes a negative answer: any norm-bounded-below overcomplete frame indexed by N_0 cannot be represented as a one-sided orbit {T^k f_0}_{k≥0} of a bounded operator T ∈ B(H). This is reflected in results stating that an overcomplete frame {T^k f_0}_{k=0}^∞ with T bounded must have "infinite excess in all directions" and forces the kernel of the synthesis operator to be infinite-dimensional, ruling out the norm-bounded-below case for the one-sided indexing. Related papers by Christensen, Hasannasab and collaborators on dynamical sampling and operator orbits confirm this resolution, while corresponding two-sided (Z-indexed) variants have been studied separately.

original_question: Let RT(k) be the repetition threshold on a k-letter alphabet, and let FRT(k) be the finite repetition threshold, meaning that only finitely many factors of the critical exponent are allowed in the corresponding infinite word. Is it true that FRT(4) = RT(4) = 7/5?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer k ≥ 2, consider infinite words over an alphabet of k letters. Given a real number α > 1, an α-power is a non-empty factor of the form x^α := x^{⌊α⌋} y, where y is the prefix of x of length ⌈(α − ⌊α⌋)|x|⌉; the (critical) exponent of a word is the supremum of all α such that the word contains an α-power as a factor. The repetition threshold RT(k) is the infimum, over all infinite words on k letters, of the critical exponent. The finite repetition threshold FRT(k) is the smallest real number r such that there exists an infinite word on k letters whose critical exponent is at most r and which contains only finitely many factors that are r-powers (equivalently, only finitely many factors of exponent equal to r are allowed).

It is known that RT(4) = 7/5. Prove or disprove: FRT(4) = RT(4) = 7/5; that is, there exists an infinite word on a 4-letter alphabet whose factors all have exponent at most 7/5 and which contains only finitely many factors of exponent exactly 7/5.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved affirmatively. Badkobeh, Crochemore and Rao established FRT(k) = RT(k) for all k ≥ 4 (in particular FRT(4) = 7/5), with results published in RAIRO - Theoretical Informatics and Applications (2014) and related works showing the existence of an infinite Dejean word on 4 letters containing only finitely many 7/5-powers.

original_question: A distinct square means a square factor considered up to shape, not merely by translated occurrence. Is every word of length n guaranteed to contain at most n distinct square factors?
self_contained_problem:
Let $w$ be a finite word over a finite alphabet, and let $|w|$ denote its length. A square is a nonempty word of the form $uu$ (the concatenation of a word $u$ with itself). Two square factors of $w$ are considered the same if and only if they are equal as words (i.e., have the same "shape"); occurrences of the same square at different positions in $w$ are not counted separately. Let $\mathrm{sq}(w)$ denote the number of distinct squares (in this sense) appearing as factors of $w$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite word $w$, $\mathrm{sq}(w) \le |w|$.
status_search_result: The Fraenkel–Simpson "distinct squares" conjecture was resolved in 2022 by Brlek and Li, who proved that the number of distinct square factors of a finite word w is at most |w| − |Alph(w)| + 1, where Alph(w) is the set of letters occurring in w. This implies the conjectured bound of n. Earlier partial results gave bounds 2n (Fraenkel–Simpson, 1998) and below 1.5n (Deza–Franek–Thierry, 2015; with later improvements).

original_question: Define the square density of a finite word w by ρsq(w) = #{x^2 in Σ+ such that x^2 is a factor of w} / |w|. Does there exist a mapping f: Σ* -> Σ* and a constant c > 1 such that, for every word w with ρsq(w) >= 1, the transformed word satisfies ρsq(f(w)) >= cρsq(w)?
self_contained_problem:
Let Σ be a finite alphabet and Σ* the set of all finite words over Σ, with Σ⁺ = Σ* ∖ {ε}. A word u ∈ Σ* is called a factor of a word w ∈ Σ* if there exist v₁, v₂ ∈ Σ* with w = v₁ u v₂. A square is a word of the form x² = xx with x ∈ Σ⁺. For a nonempty word w of length |w|, define its square density by

  ρ_sq(w) = #{ x² : x ∈ Σ⁺ and x² is a factor of w } / |w|,

where the numerator counts distinct nonempty words x for which xx occurs as a factor of w.

Question: Does there exist a computable map f : Σ* → Σ* and a constant c > 1 such that, for every word w ∈ Σ* with ρ_sq(w) ≥ 1, one has

  ρ_sq(f(w)) ≥ c · ρ_sq(w) ?
status_search_result: A search for related work on square density of words (including constructions reaching distinct-square density approaching 5/6 and studies of FS-double-square sequences) does not produce a direct resolution of the question of whether there is a computable amplifier f and a constant c>1 such that ρ_sq(f(w)) ≥ c·ρ_sq(w) for all w with ρ_sq(w) ≥ 1. No source clearly affirms or refutes this amplification question, so its current status appears unresolved in the accessible literature.

original_question: A run is an occurrence of a repetition of exponent at least 2 that is maximal in the sense that it cannot be extended to the left or right while keeping the same type of repetition. Is every binary word of length n guaranteed to have at most n runs?
self_contained_problem:
Let w = w_1 w_2 ... w_n be a finite word over the binary alphabet {0,1}. A factor of w is a contiguous substring w_i w_{i+1} ... w_j. A run (also called a maximal repetition) in w is a factor of the form u^e (with e a rational number ≥ 2, meaning the factor has length at least 2|u| and is a prefix of u^∞) that is maximal in the following sense: extending the factor by one position to the left or to the right (when such positions exist in w) would no longer yield a factor whose smallest period equals |u|. Equivalently, a run is an occurrence [i,j] in w such that the smallest period p of w_i...w_j satisfies j - i + 1 ≥ 2p, and neither w_{i-1}...w_j nor w_i...w_{j+1} has smallest period p.

Let ρ(n) denote the maximum, taken over all binary words w of length n, of the number of runs in w.

Prove or disprove: ρ(n) ≤ n for every positive integer n.

status_search_result: The "runs" conjecture of Kolpakov and Kucherov (1999), asserting that the number of runs in a string of length n is less than n, was proved by Bannai, I, Inenaga, Nakashima, Takeda, and Tsuruta ("The 'Runs' Theorem", arXiv:1406.0263, SIAM J. Comput. 2017) for arbitrary (and in particular binary) alphabets, using a characterization via Lyndon words. Subsequent work has tightened the constant for binary strings further.

original_question: For an infinite word u, let Ru(n) be the size of the smallest window that contains every factor of length n of u, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n->infinity} Ru(n)/n. For a Sturmian sequence of slope α, write ρ(α), and let S be the set of values taken by ρ(α) as α ranges over irrational numbers in [0,1]. What is the Hausdorff dimension of S, or of each interval S ∩ [a, a + 1]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $u = u_1 u_2 u_3 \cdots$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet. A factor of $u$ of length $n$ is any block $u_i u_{i+1} \cdots u_{i+n-1}$. Define the recurrence function $R_u(n)$ to be the smallest integer $N$ such that every window $u_{i+1} u_{i+2} \cdots u_{i+N}$ of length $N$ in $u$ contains every factor of $u$ of length $n$ (with $R_u(n) = \infty$ if no such $N$ exists). The recurrence quotient of $u$ is
$$\rho(u) \;=\; \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R_u(n)}{n}.$$
For an irrational number $\alpha \in [0,1]$, the Sturmian sequence of slope $\alpha$ is the infinite binary word $s_\alpha = (s_n)_{n\ge 1}$ defined by $s_n = \lfloor (n+1)\alpha \rfloor - \lfloor n\alpha \rfloor$. Write $\rho(\alpha) := \rho(s_\alpha)$. It is known that if $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots]$ is the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$, then
$$\rho(\alpha) \;=\; 2 + \limsup_{i \to \infty} [\,a_i;\, a_{i-1},\, \ldots,\, a_1\,].$$
Let
$$S \;=\; \{\, \rho(\alpha) : \alpha \in [0,1]\setminus \mathbb{Q}\,\}$$
be the set of all values of the recurrence quotient over Sturmian sequences.

Determine the Hausdorff dimension of $S$, and more generally determine the Hausdorff dimension of $S \cap [a, a+1]$ for each integer $a \ge 2$.
status_search_result: The set S, often called the Cassaigne spectrum, has been studied since Cassaigne's characterization of ρ(α) in terms of continued fractions, but the Hausdorff dimension of S and of its unit-interval slices appears to remain open. Surveys describe the structural questions about S (including Hausdorff dimension) as still active/open research areas, and no published determination of these dimensions was found.

original_question: For an infinite word u, let Ru(n) be the size of the smallest window that contains every factor of length n of u, and define the recurrence quotient by ρ(u) = lim sup_{n->infinity} Ru(n)/n. How does this recurrence quotient behave for families of infinite words beyond Sturmian words, such as words of complexity 2n + 1, or even for more general infinite words?
self_contained_problem:
Let $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$. A finite word $w$ is called a factor of $u$ if $w = u_i u_{i+1} \cdots u_{i+|w|-1}$ for some $i \ge 0$. For each integer $n \ge 1$, define the recurrence function $R_u(n)$ to be the smallest integer $N$ (or $+\infty$ if no such $N$ exists) such that every window $u_i u_{i+1} \cdots u_{i+N-1}$ of length $N$ contains every factor of $u$ of length $n$ as a factor. Define the recurrence quotient of $u$ by
$$\rho(u) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R_u(n)}{n}.$$

For Sturmian words (aperiodic infinite words over a binary alphabet whose factor complexity satisfies $p_u(n) = n + 1$ for every $n \ge 0$), the behaviour of $\rho(u)$ is classically understood. The problem is the following: provide a systematic description of the possible values and the behaviour of $\rho(u)$ for infinite words $u$ outside the Sturmian class — in particular, for infinite words of factor complexity $p_u(n) = 2n + 1$ (such as Arnoux–Rauzy words on a three-letter alphabet), and more generally for arbitrary infinite words. Specifically, characterize the set $\{\rho(u) : u \text{ has complexity } 2n+1\}$, exhibit its extremal values, and determine which real numbers in $[0,\infty]$ arise as the recurrence quotient of some infinite word.
status_search_result: Cassaigne and Chekhova (Annales de l'Institut Fourier, 2006) explicitly computed the recurrence function for Arnoux–Rauzy sequences (which include words of complexity 2n+1) and answered a related question of Morse and Hedlund, giving substantial information on recurrence quotients in this family. However, a complete characterization of recurrence quotients for general infinite words, or even for the full class of words of complexity 2n+1, does not appear in the literature, so the broader problem remains open.

original_question: For a uniformly recurrent infinite word, let P(n) denote the number of distinct palindromes of length n occurring as factors and let p(n) denote the usual factor complexity. When the upper bound P(n) + P(n + 1) = p(n + 1) - p(n) + 2 is attained, what is the structure of the corresponding Rauzy graphs?
self_contained_problem:
Let $u$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$ that is uniformly recurrent (i.e., every factor of $u$ occurs in $u$ infinitely often with bounded gaps). For each integer $n \geq 0$, let:
- $\mathcal{L}_n(u)$ denote the set of factors of $u$ of length $n$,
- $p(n) = |\mathcal{L}_n(u)|$ be the factor complexity,
- $P(n)$ denote the number of distinct palindromic factors of $u$ of length $n$ (a palindrome being a finite word equal to its reversal).

The Rauzy graph $\Gamma_n(u)$ of order $n$ is the directed graph whose vertex set is $\mathcal{L}_n(u)$ and in which there is an edge from $v$ to $w$ whenever there exists a factor $a v_2 \cdots v_n b \in \mathcal{L}_{n+1}(u)$ with $v = a v_2 \cdots v_n$ and $w = v_2 \cdots v_n b$.

It is known that for every uniformly recurrent infinite word $u$ whose language is closed under reversal, the inequality
$$P(n) + P(n+1) \leq p(n+1) - p(n) + 2$$
holds for every $n \geq 0$.

Describe completely the structure of the Rauzy graphs $\Gamma_n(u)$ (for $n$ at which equality occurs, and as $n$ varies) of those uniformly recurrent infinite words $u$ for which this upper bound is attained, i.e., for which
$$P(n) + P(n+1) = p(n+1) - p(n) + 2.$$
category_tag: Combinatorics on words / Rauzy graphs and palindromic complexity
status_search_result: The inequality $P(n)+P(n+1) \le p(n+1)-p(n)+2$ for uniformly recurrent words with language closed under reversal is established in work by Balková, Pelantová, and Starosta, and partial structural information about Rauzy graphs attaining the bound (e.g., decomposition of the reduced Rauzy graph into cycles of length 1 or 2 under the reversal map) is known. original_question: A word is quasiperiodic if there exists another word x such that every position of the word lies inside some occurrence of x as a factor. Given a morphism f and a letter a such that a is the initial letter of f(a), is it decidable whether the infinite fixed point f^ω(a) is quasiperiodic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^*$ (resp. $\Sigma^\omega$) denote the set of finite (resp. infinite) words over $\Sigma$. A factor of a word $w$ is a contiguous block of letters of $w$. A finite or infinite word $w$ is called quasiperiodic if there exists a word $x \in \Sigma^*$ with $|x| < |w|$ such that every position of $w$ is contained in some occurrence of $x$ as a factor of $w$ (equivalently, $w$ is covered by occurrences of $x$); the word $x$ is called a quasiperiod of $w$.

A morphism is a map $f : \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ satisfying $f(uv) = f(u)f(v)$ for all $u,v \in \Sigma^*$. A letter $a \in \Sigma$ is said to be prolongable under $f$ if $f(a) = a u$ for some $u \in \Sigma^*$ with $|f^n(u)| \to \infty$; in this case the sequence $f^n(a)$ converges to a unique infinite fixed point $f^\omega(a) \in \Sigma^\omega$ satisfying $f(f^\omega(a)) = f^\omega(a)$.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given as input a finite alphabet $\Sigma$, a morphism $f : \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$, and a letter $a \in \Sigma$ such that $a$ is the initial letter of $f(a)$ and $f^\omega(a)$ is well-defined, decides whether the infinite word $f^\omega(a)$ is quasiperiodic?
status_search_result: A web search reveals related results: methods to compute the set of quasiperiods of morphic words, and characterizations of quasiperiodicity for Sturmian words (a Sturmian word is not quasiperiodic iff it is Lyndon). However, no source clearly settles, in full generality, the decidability of quasiperiodicity for the infinite fixed point of an arbitrary prolongable morphism. The status appears to be unresolved based on available evidence.

original_question: In the Post Correspondence Problem, an instance (h, g) is a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word u and every pair of distinct letters a and b, the comparabilities h(ua) ⊲⊳ g(ua) and h(ub) ⊲⊳ g(ub) together imply h(u) = g(u). Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable for this class of instances?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ be finite alphabets, and let $h, g : \Sigma^* \to \Delta^*$ be two morphisms (where $\Sigma^*$ denotes the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$, with concatenation). For two words $x, y \in \Delta^*$, write $x \bowtie y$ to mean that $x$ and $y$ are comparable as prefixes, i.e., either $x$ is a prefix of $y$ or $y$ is a prefix of $x$.

The Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) asks, given such a pair $(h, g)$, whether there exists a nonempty word $w \in \Sigma^*$ with $h(w) = g(w)$.

Call an instance $(h, g)$ a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word $u \in \Sigma^*$ and every pair of distinct letters $a, b \in \Sigma$,
$$ h(ua) \bowtie g(ua) \ \text{and}\ h(ub) \bowtie g(ub) \ \Longrightarrow\ h(u) = g(u). $$

Question: Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable when restricted to the class of unique equality continuation instances? Equivalently, does there exist an algorithm that, given any unique equality continuation instance $(h, g)$, decides whether some nonempty $w \in \Sigma^*$ satisfies $h(w) = g(w)$?
status_search_result: A web search for "unique equality continuation" in the context of the Post Correspondence Problem returned no specific results indicating that this restricted version has been resolved. General references on PCP discuss other restrictions (bounded, n≤2, regular, circular, identity correspondence) but not this particular subclass. The status of decidability for unique equality continuation instances appears to be unsettled in the available literature.

original_question: Given a Post Correspondence Problem instance (h, g), can one decide whether it satisfies the unique equality continuation property, namely that for every word u and every pair of distinct letters a and b, the comparabilities h(ua) ⊲⊳ g(ua) and h(ub) ⊲⊳ g(ub) imply h(u) = g(u)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ and $\Delta$ be finite alphabets, and let $h, g : \Sigma^* \to \Delta^*$ be two morphisms (i.e., a Post Correspondence Problem instance $(h, g)$). For words $x, y \in \Delta^*$, write $x \bowtie y$ to mean that $x$ and $y$ are comparable as prefixes, that is, $x$ is a prefix of $y$ or $y$ is a prefix of $x$.

The instance $(h, g)$ is said to have the unique equality continuation property if, for every word $u \in \Sigma^*$ and every pair of distinct letters $a, b \in \Sigma$ with $a \neq b$, the conditions
$$h(ua) \bowtie g(ua) \quad \text{and} \quad h(ub) \bowtie g(ub)$$
together imply
$$h(u) = g(u).$$

Question: Is there an algorithm which, given as input an arbitrary PCP instance $(h, g)$, decides whether $(h, g)$ has the unique equality continuation property?
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any reference resolving the decidability of the unique equality continuation property for PCP instances. Standard PCP is known to be undecidable, with several restricted variants (binary, marked, unary, bounded) decidable, but no source located directly addresses this specific property. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.
