original_question: Describe all the topological types of singularities that may appear in algebraically inte- grable systems with a small (≤ 3) degree of freedom. Next, describe the symplectic invariants of such singularities.
self_contained_problem:
An algebraically integrable system is a triple $(M^{2n}, \omega, F)$ where $(M,\omega)$ is a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold and $F = (f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon M \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a smooth map whose components Poisson-commute (i.e. $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$) and are functionally independent on a dense open set, such that the regular fibers of $F$ are (compact) Lagrangian tori and the system admits an algebraic structure (its singularities are non-degenerate in the Williamson sense, possibly together with degenerate strata of algebraic type). Two singular points (or singular fibers) of such systems are said to have the same topological type if there is a fiber-preserving homeomorphism between saturated neighborhoods of them, and the same symplectic type if this homeomorphism can be chosen to be a symplectomorphism.

Carry out the following two tasks for $n \le 3$:

(a) Provide a complete classification, up to topological equivalence, of all singularities (singular points and singular fibers, including their saturated neighborhoods) that can occur in algebraically integrable Hamiltonian systems with $n$ degrees of freedom, $n \in \{1,2,3\}$.

(b) For each such topological type, determine a complete set of symplectic invariants that classifies these singularities up to symplectic equivalence in a saturated neighborhood.
status_search_result: The problem is partially solved. Topological and symplectic classifications are known for non-degenerate singularities (elliptic, hyperbolic, focus-focus) in low degrees of freedom (work of Eliasson, Vũ Ngọc, Zung, Bolsinov–Fomenko, and others). For 1 and 2 degrees of freedom, topological classification of non-degenerate singular fibers and several symplectic invariants (e.g. for focus-focus, parabolic/cusp singularities) have been obtained, with recent progress on universal unfoldings of $A_n$ singularities. However, a complete classification covering all degenerate singularities arising in algebraically integrable systems, particularly for 3 degrees of freedom, remains open.

original_question: For integrable systems obtained by toric degeneration, describe the topology and geometry of the resulting singular fibers and of their small neighbourhoods.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ equipped with a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, that is, a smooth map $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are functionally independent and pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$. Suppose that $F$ is obtained by a toric degeneration procedure: there exists a flat family $\pi:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{C}$ of complex projective varieties whose generic fiber is isomorphic to a smooth projective variety $X$ (with a chosen Kähler form pulling back to $\omega$) and whose central fiber $X_0=\pi^{-1}(0)$ is a (possibly singular) toric variety with moment map $\mu_0:X_0\to\Delta\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ for the residual torus action. The map $F:X\to\Delta$ is then constructed by transporting $\mu_0$ via a gradient-Hamiltonian flow associated with the degeneration, yielding a continuous map whose restriction to a dense open subset is a smooth Lagrangian torus fibration over the interior of $\Delta$, but which acquires singular fibers over a codimension-at-least-one subset of $\Delta$ coming from the singularities of $X_0$ and from points where the gradient-Hamiltonian flow fails to be defined.

Problem. Describe the topology and geometry of the singular fibers $F^{-1}(b)$ of such an integrable system $F$ obtained by toric degeneration, and of small open neighbourhoods of these singular fibers in $M$. In particular:

(a) Determine the homeomorphism (and, where possible, diffeomorphism) type of each singular fiber, including whether it is a smooth manifold, an orbifold, or a more general stratified space, and whether it is isotropic or Lagrangian in $(M,\omega)$.

(b) Describe the symplectic germ of $F$ near such a singular fiber: identify normal forms (analogous to the Eliasson–Miranda–Zung normal forms for non-degenerate singularities) and the local monodromy and affine-structure data on the base $\Delta$ near the corresponding singular value.

(c) Classify the singular fibers that arise this way up to fiber-preserving symplectomorphism of a neighbourhood, and relate the classification to the combinatorial/algebraic data of the toric degeneration (e.g. the singularities of $X_0$ and the Newton–Okounkov body $\Delta$).
status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. The degenerate singular fibers arising from toric degenerations form a class of singularities of integrable systems for which almost all standard questions (topology, smooth/symplectic local models, classification) remain unresolved. Recent works (e.g., on hypersemitoric systems and on singular Lagrangian fibrations and symplectic embeddings) study related but more restricted classes of singularities, without giving a general description for the toric-degeneration setting.

original_question: In SYZ-type Lagrangian fibrations on Calabi-Yau 3-folds, describe the special singular fibers that occur at intersections of one-dimensional families of focus-focus singularities.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a smooth Calabi–Yau 3-fold $X$ equipped with a (special) Lagrangian fibration $\pi : X \to B$ of Strominger–Yau–Zaslow type, i.e. a proper map whose generic fibers are special Lagrangian 3-tori. The discriminant locus $\Delta \subset B$ (the set of critical values of $\pi$) is a real codimension-2 graph-like subset of $B$. Along generic edges of $\Delta$ the singular fibers have a single focus–focus (nodal) singularity, so that one obtains one-parameter families of focus–focus singular fibers. At isolated points of $B$ where two or more such one-dimensional families of focus–focus singularities meet (vertices of the discriminant graph), the topology and symplectic local model of the corresponding singular fiber become more intricate.

Problem. Give a complete and explicit description of the singular Lagrangian fibers of $\pi$ that occur over these intersection points of one-dimensional families of focus–focus singularities: describe their topological type, their stratification, and a local symplectic normal form for $\pi$ near such a fiber.

Surveys on the SYZ conjecture and recent work on almost toric/SYZ fibrations describe generic focus-focus fibers and partial models, but the structure of the codimension-2 vertices remains an active research direction without a definitive normal-form description.

original_question: Construct a natural Hamiltonian system with a nonconstant potential on S 2 that admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of degree 5 and does not admit any nontrivial integrals of smaller degrees.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the standard two-dimensional sphere with its round Riemannian metric, and let $T^*S^2$ be its cotangent bundle equipped with the canonical symplectic structure. A natural Hamiltonian system on $S^2$ is one whose Hamiltonian has the form
$$H(q,p) = \tfrac{1}{2}\, g^{ij}(q)\, p_i p_j + V(q),$$
where $g^{ij}$ is the inverse of the round metric and $V \in C^\infty(S^2)$ is a potential. A function $F \in C^\infty(T^*S^2)$ is called a polynomial integral of degree $n$ if $\{H,F\} = 0$ and $F$ is a polynomial in the momenta $p_i$ of degree exactly $n$ with coefficients depending on $q$. An integral is called trivial if it is a polynomial in $H$ (in particular, a constant), and nontrivial otherwise.

Problem. Exhibit a natural Hamiltonian system on $S^2$ with nonconstant potential $V$ that admits a nontrivial polynomial integral of degree $5$ in the momenta, but admits no nontrivial polynomial integral of degree less than $5$. Equivalently, construct such $(S^2, V)$ together with the integral $F$, or prove that no such system exists.
status_search_result: The problem of constructing a natural Hamiltonian system on S^2 with nonconstant potential admitting an irreducible polynomial integral of degree exactly 5 (and no lower-degree nontrivial integral) is listed among open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems. While there are recent results on related obstructions (e.g., for the two-dimensional torus, a 2023 paper shows nonexistence of irreducible degree-5 integrals when certain spectral components are nonconstant), no construction or full nonexistence proof for S^2 has been published, and the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems on higher dimensional mani- folds which are integrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \ge 3$, with cotangent bundle $T^*M$ equipped with its canonical symplectic structure. A natural Hamiltonian system on $M$ is one with Hamiltonian function $H : T^*M 	o \mathbb{R}$ of the form
$$H(q,p) = 	frac{1}{2} g^{ij}(q) p_i p_j + V(q),$$
where $V : M 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth potential and $(q,p)$ are canonical coordinates on $T^*M$. A function $F : T^*M 	o \mathbb{R}$ is called polynomial in momenta of degree $d$ if in canonical coordinates it has the form
$$F(q,p) = \sum_{|\alpha| \le d} a_\alpha(q)\, p^\alpha,$$
with smooth coefficients $a_\alpha$. The system is called integrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta if there exist functions $F_1 = H, F_2, \dots, F_n$ on $T^*M$ that are polynomial in momenta, are functionally independent almost everywhere, and pairwise Poisson commute, $\{F_i, F_j\} = 0$.

Problem. Construct new examples of natural Hamiltonian systems on higher dimensional manifolds (i.e., with $\dim M \ge 3$) that are integrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta, beyond those currently known (such as systems separable in some coordinates, products of lower-dimensional integrable systems, and known superintegrable families).
status_search_result: The construction of new natural Hamiltonian systems on higher-dimensional manifolds integrable via polynomial-in-momenta integrals is a long-standing open research direction. While numerous examples exist in dimension two and many higher-dimensional examples arise via separation of variables or by lifting/products of lower-dimensional integrable systems, producing genuinely new higher-dimensional examples remains an active and unresolved problem.

original_question: Construct stationary axially symmetric 4-dimensional Einstein metrics admitting Killing tensors of higher order.
self_contained_problem:
Construct an explicit example of a 4-dimensional pseudo-Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ with the following properties:

1. $(M,g)$ is an Einstein manifold, i.e. $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \Lambda\, g$ for some constant $\Lambda \in \mathbb{R}$.
2. $(M,g)$ admits two commuting Killing vector fields $\xi$ and $\eta$, where $\xi$ is timelike (generating stationarity) and $\eta$ has closed orbits with a fixed axis (generating axial symmetry); equivalently, $(M,g)$ is stationary and axially symmetric.
3. $(M,g)$ admits a Killing tensor of order (valence) $k \geq 3$, that is, a totally symmetric tensor field $K_{a_1\cdots a_k}$ satisfying $\nabla_{(a_0} K_{a_1\cdots a_k)} = 0$, which is irreducible in the sense that it cannot be expressed as a polynomial in the metric $g$, the Killing vectors $\xi,\eta$, and Killing tensors of lower order.

Either exhibit such a metric explicitly, or prove that no such metric exists.
status_search_result: The problem of constructing stationary axially symmetric 4-dimensional Einstein metrics admitting irreducible higher-order Killing tensors appears to remain open. Recent computer-algebra investigations (Vollmer and others) have established nonexistence of nontrivial Killing tensors up to valence 7 for the Tomimatsu–Sato metric, valence 9 for the C-metric, and valence 11 for the Zipoy–Voorhees metric, suggesting that such examples are rare; no explicit construction has been found in the literature surveyed.

original_question: In a symmetric space, is every Killing tensor a sum of symmetric products of Killing vectors? Equivalently, is it true that the algebra of all polynomial integrals of the geodesic flow in a symmetric space is generated by linear integrals?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian symmetric space. A symmetric tensor field $K$ of valence $r$ on $M$ is called a Killing tensor if its symmetrized covariant derivative vanishes, i.e. $\nabla_{(i_0} K_{i_1\dots i_r)} = 0$. Equivalently, the function $P_K(x,p) = K^{i_1\dots i_r}(x)\, p_{i_1}\cdots p_{i_r}$ on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$ is a polynomial first integral of the geodesic flow. Killing vector fields correspond to valence-1 Killing tensors and yield linear integrals. The set of Killing tensors of all valences forms a graded commutative algebra under the symmetric tensor product.

Question: Is every Killing tensor on a Riemannian symmetric space expressible as a sum of symmetric products of Killing vector fields? Equivalently, is the algebra of all polynomial first integrals of the geodesic flow on a Riemannian symmetric space generated by the linear integrals coming from Killing vector fields?
status_search_result: The question has been answered negatively. While the property holds for spaces of constant curvature and for complex projective spaces, explicit examples of quadratic Killing tensor fields on quaternionic projective spaces and on the Cayley projective plane that cannot be written as quadratic forms (sums of symmetric products) in Killing vector fields have been constructed (see arXiv:2312.16518). Hence the algebra of polynomial integrals of the geodesic flow on a Riemannian symmetric space is not in general generated by linear integrals.

original_question: Construct a natural Hamiltonian system on the 2-sphere with a nonconstant potential which is superintegrable by integrals of degree ≥ 3 and admits no nontrivial integral of degree one and two.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the 2-sphere $S^2$ with a Riemannian metric $g$, and let $H = \frac{1}{2} g^{ij}(q) p_i p_j + V(q)$ be a natural Hamiltonian on the cotangent bundle $T^*S^2$, where $V: S^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth nonconstant potential. A function $F: T^*S^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that is polynomial in the momenta $p_i$ is called an integral of motion of $H$ if its Poisson bracket with $H$ vanishes, $\{F, H\} = 0$; its degree is its degree as a polynomial in the momenta. The system is called superintegrable if it admits, in addition to $H$, two further functionally independent polynomial integrals of motion (so that the total number of functionally independent polynomial integrals is three).

Construct an explicit example of such a natural Hamiltonian system $(S^2, g, V)$ with $V$ nonconstant that is superintegrable, where the two additional functionally independent integrals can be chosen to be polynomial in the momenta of degree $\geq 3$, and which admits no nontrivial polynomial integral of motion of degree one or two (other than those obtained as constants times $H$ or trivially from $H$ itself, in the degree-two case).
status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems on finite-dimensional integrable systems and remains open. Related work has constructed metrics on the 2-sphere with linear and cubic integrals for geodesic flows (V=0), but no example with a nonconstant potential and only higher-degree integrals appears to be known.

original_question: Does there exist a non-conformally flat metric on the sphere S n , n > 2, whose geodesic flow is maximally superintegrable (in the class of integrals which are polynomial in momenta)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n > 2$ and let $S^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional sphere. A Riemannian metric $g$ on $S^n$ is called conformally flat if every point has a neighborhood on which $g = e^{2\varphi} g_0$ for some smooth function $\varphi$ and some flat metric $g_0$. The geodesic flow of $g$ is the Hamiltonian flow on $T^*S^n$ generated by the Hamiltonian $H(x,p) = \tfrac{1}{2} g^{ij}(x) p_i p_j$. A function $F: T^*S^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be polynomial in momenta if, in any local coordinate chart, $F(x,p)$ is a polynomial in the fiber variables $p_i$ with coefficients depending smoothly on $x$. The geodesic flow is called maximally superintegrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta if there exist $2n-1$ functions $F_1 = H, F_2, \dots, F_{2n-1}$ on $T^*S^n$, each polynomial in momenta, that are functionally independent and Poisson-commute with $H$ (i.e., $\{H, F_i\} = 0$ for all $i$).

Question: Does there exist a Riemannian metric on $S^n$ ($n > 2$) which is not conformally flat and whose geodesic flow is maximally superintegrable in the class of integrals polynomial in momenta?
status_search_result: Searches reveal related constructions—non-conformally-flat 4-dimensional superintegrable systems by Kalnins–Kress, self-dual maximally superintegrable metrics, and superintegrable metrics on surfaces with high-degree polynomial integrals—but no result exhibiting a non-conformally-flat metric on $S^n$ ($n > 2$) with maximally superintegrable geodesic flow, nor a proof of nonexistence. The question appears to remain open.

original_question: If a neighbourhood of the boundary of the billiard table Ω ⊂ R2 is foliated by caustics, then the billiard curve γ is an ellipse.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex bounded planar domain with smooth boundary $\gamma = \partial \Omega$. Consider the billiard dynamics inside $\Omega$, in which a point particle moves along straight lines and reflects elastically off $\gamma$ (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). A smooth closed convex curve $\Gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a caustic of the billiard if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\Gamma$ remains tangent to $\Gamma$ after each reflection on $\gamma$. 

Suppose there exists a neighbourhood $U$ of $\gamma$ inside $\Omega$ that is foliated by caustics of the billiard in $\Omega$ (i.e., $U \setminus \gamma$ is the disjoint union of a smooth one-parameter family of caustics accumulating on $\gamma$).

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, $\gamma$ must be an ellipse.
status_search_result: This is a version of the local/Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture. It remains open in full generality, but significant partial results are known: Bialy–Mironov (Annals of Math., 2022) proved the conjecture for centrally-symmetric C²-smooth strictly convex planar billiards, and further results by Kaloshin–Sorrentino and Kaloshin (2023) establish it for domains nearly circular or nearly centrally symmetric. The general case—including for boundaries that are ovals of algebraic curves—is still open.

original_question: Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliated by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed plane curve (of positive curvature), bounding a convex region $K$. The outer (dual) billiard map $T$ is defined on the exterior $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ as follows: for a point $p$ outside $K$, consider the right tangent line from $p$ to $\gamma$ (using a fixed orientation), and let $q$ be the point of tangency; then $T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ in $q$, i.e., $q$ is the midpoint of the segment $[p, T(p)]$.

Suppose the exterior $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ is foliated by a continuous family of closed curves each of which is invariant under $T$ (i.e., the outer billiard around $\gamma$ is totally integrable in this sense).

Prove that $\gamma$ must be an ellipse.
status_search_result: A 2024 result by M. Bialy in the Journal of Modern Dynamics ("Integrable outer billiards and rigidity") proves precisely that if the exterior of a smooth strictly convex plane curve of positive curvature is foliated by continuous curves invariant under the outer billiard map, then the curve must be an ellipse. The proof introduces a new generating function for outer billiards and integral-geometric weights reducing the problem to the Blaschke–Santaló inequality.

original_question: (S. Tabachnikov) Let γ ⊂ RP2 be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let F be a smooth foliation by convex closed curves in its exterior neighbourhood, including γ as a leaf. The intersection of every tangent line to γ with the leaves of F define a local involution on this line, the point of tangency being a fixed point. Suppose that these involutions are projective transformations for all tangent lines of γ. Then γ is an ellipse, and the foliation consists of ellipses that form a pencil.
self_contained_problem:
Work in the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{RP}^2$ be a smooth closed strictly convex curve, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a smooth foliation by smooth closed convex curves of an exterior one-sided neighbourhood of $\gamma$, with $\gamma$ itself being a leaf of $\mathcal{F}$.

For every point $p \in \gamma$, let $\ell_p$ denote the projective tangent line to $\gamma$ at $p$. Each leaf of $\mathcal{F}$ near $\gamma$ meets $\ell_p$ in two points close to $p$, and swapping these two intersection points (with $p$ as a fixed point) defines a germ of an involution $\sigma_p : \ell_p \to \ell_p$ on the tangent line.

Assume that for every $p \in \gamma$, the involution $\sigma_p$ is the restriction of a projective transformation of $\ell_p \cong \mathbb{RP}^1$.

Prove that under these hypotheses $\gamma$ is necessarily an ellipse, and the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$ are ellipses that, together with $\gamma$, belong to a single pencil of conics (a one-parameter family of conics sharing four base points, possibly complex or with multiplicities).
status_search_result: The conjecture is a projective-dual analogue of the Birkhoff conjecture. Glutsyuk has established it under the additional assumption that the curve is $C^4$-smooth and the foliation admits a rational first integral (rational integrability), classifying all such examples (pencils of conics plus a finite list of exotic cases). The general conjecture, without the rational integrability hypothesis, appears still open.

original_question: Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a complete simply connected two-dimensional Riemannian manifold of constant curvature, i.e. either the round sphere $S^2$ or the hyperbolic (Lobachevsky) plane $H^2$. Let $\gamma \subset M$ be a smooth strictly convex closed curve. The outer (dual) billiard map $T_\gamma$ associated with $\gamma$ is defined on the exterior of $\gamma$ as follows: for a point $P$ outside $\gamma$, draw the (oriented) geodesic tangent line from $P$ to $\gamma$ touching $\gamma$ at a point $Q$; then $T_\gamma(P)$ is the point obtained by reflecting $P$ through $Q$ along this geodesic (so that $Q$ is the geodesic midpoint of $P$ and $T_\gamma(P)$).

The map $T_\gamma$ is said to be polynomially (algebraically) integrable if there exists a non-constant function $F$ on the exterior of $\gamma$, polynomial in the natural coordinates inherited from the ambient projective model of $M$, such that $F \circ T_\gamma = F$ on a neighborhood of $\gamma$.

Prove the algebraic version of Birkhoff's conjecture in this setting: if the outer billiard map associated with a smooth strictly convex closed curve $\gamma$ on a non-Euclidean surface of constant curvature ($S^2$ or $H^2$) admits a non-trivial polynomial integral, then $\gamma$ is a conic, i.e. a curve of the form $\{aF^2 + bG^2 + cH^2 = 0\}$ in the standard projective model — equivalently, $\gamma$ is the dual of a confocal-conic boundary on $M$.
status_search_result: The algebraic Birkhoff conjecture for ordinary (inner) Birkhoff billiards on surfaces of constant curvature has been proved by Bialy and Mironov (sphere and hyperbolic plane). Results on dual/outer billiards on $S^2$ and $H^2$ have been obtained giving obstructions to polynomial integrability via the dual curve, but a complete proof of the algebraic Birkhoff conjecture for outer billiards in the non-Euclidean constant-curvature setting does not appear to be definitively established in the sources found; status remains unclear.

original_question: Is it possible to choose the domain so that the dynamics of the corresponding billiard map are locally (near the 2-periodic orbit) conjugated to the dynamics of the rigid rotation through some angle α?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a planar billiard inside a smooth strictly convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ that admits a 2-periodic orbit (a segment hitting the boundary perpendicularly at two points). The billiard map $T$ acts on the space of oriented chords (parametrized, e.g., by an arclength coordinate on $\partial\Omega$ and the angle of reflection), and the 2-periodic orbit corresponds to a fixed point of $T^2$. Assume this fixed point is elliptic, with the linearization of $T^2$ being a rotation by some angle $2\alpha$ (so that $T$ has, at the 2-periodic point, rotation angle $\alpha$).

Question: Does there exist a domain $\Omega$ (other than a disk) such that, in some neighborhood of the 2-periodic orbit, the billiard map $T$ is smoothly (or analytically) conjugate to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha: (x,y)\mapsto (x\cos\alpha - y\sin\alpha,\; x\sin\alpha + y\cos\alpha)$ of the plane by the angle $\alpha$?

Equivalently, does there exist a smooth (resp. analytic) diffeomorphism $h$ from a neighborhood of the fixed point to a neighborhood of the origin in $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $h \circ T = R_\alpha \circ h$ on this neighborhood, for some choice of $\Omega$ and some $\alpha$?
status_search_result: The conjugacy equation for billiard maps near a 2-periodic orbit was introduced by Treschev (Physica D, 2013), who showed that a formal power series solution exists when α is incommensurable with π and provided numerical evidence for convergence. Subsequent work (e.g., Steklov Inst. 2015; "Lazutkin coordinates and the conjugation problem for billiard maps", arXiv 2503.19550, 2025) continues to investigate the analytic conjugacy. As of 2025–2026, the existence of an actual (non-circular) domain with such an analytic/smooth conjugacy to a rigid rotation appears to remain an open problem, with only formal/numerical results known.

original_question: Are there plane billiards, other than ellipses, that possess rational caustics with two different values of the rotation numbers? Same question for outer billiards.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed curve bounding a domain $D$. The (Birkhoff) billiard inside $D$ is the dynamical system on oriented chords of $D$ in which a point moves along straight lines and reflects off $\gamma$ according to the law of equal angles. A smooth convex curve $\Gamma\subset D$ is called a caustic of the billiard if every chord tangent to $\Gamma$ reflects off $\gamma$ to another chord tangent to $\Gamma$. A caustic $\Gamma$ is said to be rational with rotation number $p/q\in\mathbb{Q}$ (in lowest terms, $0<p/q<1/2$) if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\Gamma$ is a closed polygon with $q$ vertices on $\gamma$ that makes $p$ turns around $\Gamma$.

Analogously, for the outer (dual) billiard defined outside a smooth strictly convex closed curve $\gamma$ — where the map $T$ sends a point $x$ outside $\gamma$ to the reflection of $x$ in the point of tangency of the right tangent line from $x$ to $\gamma$ — a smooth closed convex curve $\Gamma$ surrounding $\gamma$ is an invariant caustic if it is invariant under $T$, and it is called rational with rotation number $p/q$ if the restriction of $T$ to $\Gamma$ is conjugate to the rotation by $2\pi p/q$, so that every orbit on $\Gamma$ closes up after $q$ steps and $p$ turns.

It is classical that an ellipse, as the boundary of an inner billiard, possesses a one-parameter family of confocal elliptic caustics, and in particular admits rational caustics for every rational rotation number in $(0,1/2)$; the analogous statement holds for the outer billiard about an ellipse.

Question. Does there exist a smooth strictly convex closed plane curve $\gamma$ that is not an ellipse such that the inner billiard inside $\gamma$ possesses rational caustics with at least two different values of the rotation number? Same question for the outer billiard about $\gamma$.
status_search_result: The question is closely related to the Birkhoff conjecture and to results of Glutsyuk, Bialy–Mironov, and others on rational/algebraic caustics. Recent works (e.g., on complex algebraic caustics in planar and projective billiards, 2025) and surveys still treat the existence of non-elliptic billiards with multiple rational caustics as open; partial results rule it out under additional algebraicity or near-circular hypotheses, but no full resolution was found.

original_question: (V. Kaloshin) A q0 -rationally integrable billiard is elliptic.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain, and consider the Birkhoff billiard inside $\Omega$: a point particle moves in a straight line and reflects off $\partial\Omega$ according to the law of equal angles. A smooth convex curve $\Gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a caustic of the billiard if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\Gamma$ remains tangent to $\Gamma$ after each reflection. To a convex caustic one associates a rotation number $\omega \in (0, 1/2]$.

For coprime integers $0 < p < q$, a caustic $\Gamma$ is called $(p,q)$-rationally integrable if it has rotation number $p/q$ and the billiard map admits an integral whose level sets foliate a neighborhood of the invariant curve associated to $\Gamma$ by invariant curves carrying $(p,q)$-periodic orbits.

Given an integer $q_0 \geq 2$, the billiard in $\Omega$ is said to be $q_0$-rationally integrable if for every rational $p/q \in (0, 1/q_0]$ in lowest terms, $\Omega$ admits a $(p,q)$-rationally integrable convex caustic.

Prove or disprove: if the billiard in $\Omega$ is $q_0$-rationally integrable for some $q_0 \geq 2$, then $\partial\Omega$ is an ellipse.
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in full generality. Substantial partial progress exists: the local Birkhoff conjecture has been established (small smooth perturbations of an ellipse that are rationally integrable must be ellipses), and further results address nearly circular domains and nearly centrally symmetric domains. No complete proof of the global $q_0$-rational integrability conjecture has been published.

original_question: (M. Bialy) Assume that a plane billiard has a family of rotational invariant circles with all the rotation numbers in the interval (0, 1/2). Then the billiard table is an ellipse.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. Consider the Birkhoff billiard inside $\Omega$: a point particle moves along straight lines and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at $\partial\Omega$. The billiard map $T$ acts on the phase cylinder of inward unit vectors based at points of $\partial\Omega$, parametrized by $(s,\varphi)$ where $s$ is arclength on $\partial\Omega$ and $\varphi \in (0,\pi)$ is the angle with the boundary.

A rotational invariant circle is a $T$-invariant curve in the phase cylinder that is homotopically nontrivial (i.e., wraps around the cylinder). Each such invariant curve has a well-defined rotation number $\rho \in (0,1)$ for the restriction of $T$. By time-reversal symmetry one may restrict attention to $\rho \in (0,1/2)$.

Conjecture: If the billiard inside $\Omega$ admits a family of rotational invariant circles whose rotation numbers fill the entire interval $(0,1/2)$, then $\partial\Omega$ is an ellipse.

Prove or disprove this statement.
status_search_result: This is a strong form of the Birkhoff–Poritsky integrability conjecture (Bialy's version, with foliation by invariant curves of all rotation numbers in (0,1/2)). It remains open in full generality. Significant partial results exist: Kaloshin–Sorrentino (Annals 2018) established rigidity near the boundary for rotation numbers in (0,1/4]; Bialy–Mironov (Annals of Math. 2022) proved the conjecture for centrally-symmetric C²-smooth convex tables. Subsequent works (e.g., Bialy–Tsodikovich, 2021; Bialy–Mironov 2024 survey) extend related rigidity results, but the general (non-symmetric) case stated above is not resolved.

original_question: Suppose that a billiard table has a sequence of convex caustics with rotation numbers converging to some number ω ∈ (0, 1/2). Does it imply that the table is an ellipse?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex bounded planar domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$. Consider the Birkhoff billiard inside $\Omega$: a point particle moves along straight lines and reflects off $\partial\Omega$ according to the law of equal angles. A smooth convex curve $\gamma \subset \Omega$ is called a (convex) caustic of the billiard if every billiard trajectory tangent to $\gamma$ remains tangent to $\gamma$ after each reflection at $\partial\Omega$. To each convex caustic $\gamma$ one associates a rotation number $\rho(\gamma) \in (0, 1/2)$, defined as the asymptotic average angular fraction of $\partial\Omega$ traversed per reflection along any trajectory tangent to $\gamma$.

Suppose that there exists a sequence $\{\gamma_n\}_{n \ge 1}$ of convex caustics of the billiard in $\Omega$ whose rotation numbers $\rho(\gamma_n)$ converge to some number $\omega \in (0, 1/2)$. Must $\partial\Omega$ be an ellipse?
status_search_result: The question is a variant of the Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture. Known results include: if a sequence of convex caustics has rotation numbers converging to 1/2, then the table is an ellipse; local versions near ellipses, and a 2022 proof of the Birkhoff conjecture for centrally-symmetric C^2 strictly convex tables (Bialy–Mironov). However, the general case where rotation numbers accumulate at an arbitrary ω ∈ (0, 1/2) does not appear to be resolved in the literature, and recent surveys still list it as open.

original_question: (M. Bialy) Are there multi-dimensional convex billiards, other than ellipsoids, having invariant hypersurfaces in the phase space? Same question for multi-dimensional outer billiards.
self_contained_problem:
Setting (Birkhoff billiards). Let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 3$, be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain with boundary $\partial D$. The Birkhoff billiard map $T: M \to M$ is defined on the phase space
$$M = \{(q,v) : q \in \partial D,\ v \in \mathbb{R}^n,\ \|v\|=1,\ \langle v, \nu(q)\rangle \ge 0\},$$
where $\nu(q)$ denotes the inner unit normal to $\partial D$ at $q$. The map sends $(q,v)$ to $(q', v')$, where $q'$ is the next intersection of the ray $\{q+tv : t>0\}$ with $\partial D$, and $v'$ is obtained from $v$ by reflection in the tangent hyperplane $T_{q'}\partial D$ (so the tangential component of $v$ is preserved and the normal component is reversed). An invariant hypersurface is a smooth codimension-one submanifold $\Sigma \subset M$ with $T(\Sigma) = \Sigma$.

Setting (outer billiards). Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$, $n \ge 2$, be a smooth strictly convex bounded body, and let $\omega$ be the standard symplectic form on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. The outer billiard map $T_K$ is defined outside $K$ as follows: for a point $x$ outside $K$, there is a unique oriented support hyperplane $H$ to $K$ through $x$ (with respect to a chosen rule using $\omega$), tangent to $K$ at a point $z(x)$; then $T_K(x) := 2z(x) - x$. An invariant hypersurface is a smooth codimension-one submanifold of the domain of $T_K$ that is preserved by $T_K$.

It is classical that ellipsoids in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 3$) yield Birkhoff billiards possessing invariant hypersurfaces in phase space (foliated by caustics).

Questions.
(a) Does there exist a smooth strictly convex bounded domain $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 3$, not an ellipsoid, such that the associated Birkhoff billiard map admits an invariant hypersurface in its phase space $M$?
(b) Does there exist a smooth strictly convex bounded body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $n \ge 2$, not an ellipsoid, such that the associated outer billiard map admits an invariant hypersurface?
status_search_result: For multi-dimensional Birkhoff billiards, the question appears to remain open: it is known that only ellipsoids have convex caustics in higher dimensions, but no non-ellipsoidal example of an invariant hypersurface in phase space is known, and recent surveys list this as open. For outer billiards, recent work (2025) on symplectically self-polar convex bodies provides non-trivial examples of invariant hypersurfaces beyond ellipsoids, partially answering the outer-billiard part of the question.

original_question: (A. Glutsyuk, S. Tabachnikov ) Given two nested closed convex hypersurfaces, assume that the billiard transformations on the set of oriented lines that intersect both hypersurfaces commute. Prove that the hypersurfaces are confocal ellipsoids.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ be two closed, smooth, strictly convex hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 2$), with $\Sigma_1$ enclosed in the bounded region bounded by $\Sigma_2$. For each $i \in \{1,2\}$, the billiard reflection $T_i$ is defined on the set of oriented lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that intersect $\Sigma_i$ transversally as follows: given an oriented line $\ell$ meeting $\Sigma_i$, let $p$ be the last point of intersection of $\ell$ (in the direction of $\ell$) with $\Sigma_i$; then $T_i(\ell)$ is the oriented line through $p$ obtained from $\ell$ by reflecting its direction in the tangent hyperplane to $\Sigma_i$ at $p$, oriented away from $p$. Let $\mathcal{U}$ denote the set of oriented lines that intersect both $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ transversally and on which both $T_1, T_2$, and their iterates relevant below, are defined.

Assume that $T_1$ and $T_2$ commute on $\mathcal{U}$, i.e., $T_1 \circ T_2(\ell) = T_2 \circ T_1(\ell)$ for every $\ell \in \mathcal{U}$ for which both sides are defined.

Prove that $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$ are confocal ellipsoids, that is, there exist constants $a_1 > a_2 > \cdots > a_d > 0$ and parameters $\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ (with $\lambda_i < a_d^2$) such that, in suitable Cartesian coordinates,
$$\Sigma_i = \left\{ x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \sum_{k=1}^d \frac{x_k^2}{a_k^2 - \lambda_i} = 1 \right\}, \qquad i=1,2.$$
status_search_result: Glutsyuk proved this commuting-billiards conjecture for nested strictly convex C^2 hypersurfaces in R^d (d ≥ 3), and more generally in spaces of constant curvature, showing the hypersurfaces must be confocal ellipsoids/quadrics. The result appeared in "On commuting billiards in higher-dimensional spaces of constant curvature" (arXiv:1807.10567), published in the Pacific Journal of Mathematics 305 (2020), no. 2.

original_question: For the generalized pentagram maps T_{I,J} on twisted polygons in projective space, is every map T_{I,I} integrable for every multi-index I?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and $n$ with $n$ sufficiently large. A twisted $n$-gon in projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$ is a sequence $\{v_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ of points in general position in $\mathbb{RP}^d$ together with a projective transformation (the monodromy) $M\in\mathrm{PGL}_{d+1}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $v_{k+n}=M(v_k)$ for all $k$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}_n^{\,d}$ the moduli space of such twisted $n$-gons modulo projective equivalence.

Multi-indices and generalized pentagram maps. A multi-index is a tuple $I=(i_1,\dots,i_{d-1})$ of positive integers. To a pair of multi-indices $I=(i_1,\dots,i_{d-1})$ and $J=(j_1,\dots,j_{d-1})$ one associates a generalized pentagram map $T_{I,J}\colon \mathcal{P}_n^{\,d}\dashrightarrow \mathcal{P}_n^{\,d}$ as follows. For each $k$, let
$$P_k \;=\; \overline{v_k\,v_{k+i_1}}\;\cap\;\overline{v_{k+i_1}\,v_{k+i_1+i_2}}\;\cap\;\cdots\;\cap\;\overline{v_{k+i_1+\cdots+i_{d-2}}\,v_{k+i_1+\cdots+i_{d-1}}}^{\,*},$$
that is, $P_k$ is the projective subspace spanned by $d$ consecutive vertices skipping according to $I$; more precisely $P_k$ is the span of $v_k,v_{k+i_1},v_{k+i_1+i_2},\dots,v_{k+i_1+\cdots+i_{d-1}}$, a hyperplane in $\mathbb{RP}^d$. The new vertex $T_{I,J}(v)_k$ is then defined as the intersection of two consecutive such hyperplanes shifted according to $J$; namely the new vertices are obtained by intersecting $d$ consecutive hyperplanes $P_{k},P_{k+j_1},P_{k+j_1+j_2},\dots,P_{k+j_1+\cdots+j_{d-1}}$. (For $d=2$ and $I=J=(2)$ this recovers the classical pentagram map.)

The map $T_{I,J}$ is rational and well defined on a Zariski-open subset of $\mathcal{P}_n^{\,d}$.

Question. Is it true that for every dimension $d\ge 2$ and every multi-index $I=(i_1,\dots,i_{d-1})$, the generalized pentagram map $T_{I,I}$ on twisted $n$-gons in $\mathbb{RP}^d$ is completely integrable, in the sense of admitting an invariant Poisson structure together with a maximal family of functionally independent Poisson-commuting first integrals?
status_search_result: The conjecture that $T_{I,I}$ is integrable for every multi-index $I$ is generally regarded as open in full generality. Integrability has been established in several cases, including the "dented" pentagram maps and special instances such as $T_{(2,2),(1,1)}$, $T_{(2,1),(1,1)}$, $T_{(3,1),(1,1)}$, and integrability frameworks via Poisson–Lie groups of pseudo-difference operators (Izosimov) and refactorization mappings have given Lax representations and invariant Poisson structures for broad subfamilies, but a complete proof for all $I$ does not appear in the literature as of 2026.

original_question: Determine obstructions to the global existence of action-angle coordinates on regular Poisson manifolds.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\pi)$ be a regular Poisson manifold, i.e., a smooth manifold $M$ equipped with a bivector field $\pi \in \Gamma(\wedge^2 TM)$ satisfying $[\pi,\pi]=0$ (Schouten bracket) and such that the rank of $\pi$ is constant on $M$, so that the image of $\pi^\sharp:T^*M\to TM$ defines a regular symplectic foliation $\mathcal{F}$ of $M$. A (non-commutative) integrable system on $(M,\pi)$ is a surjective submersion $F=(f_1,\dots,f_r):M\to B$ onto an $r$-dimensional manifold whose components Poisson-commute with a chosen subset and whose level sets are connected Lagrangian-isotropic submanifolds carrying a free, transitive action of $\mathbb{R}^k$ (with $k$ equal to the rank of the leaves), with compact fibers. Locally near any compact connected fiber there exist action-angle coordinates: a neighborhood of the fiber is Poisson-diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^k\times D^k\times P$ for some Poisson manifold $P$, with $\pi$ given in standard form $\sum_i \partial_{\theta_i}\wedge \partial_{a_i}+\pi_P$.

Problem. Identify and characterize the complete set of cohomological/topological obstructions to the existence of global action-angle coordinates on $(M,\pi)$, that is, to the existence of a global Poisson diffeomorphism (covering $F$) between $M$ and a model of the form $(\mathbb{T}^k\text{-bundle over }B)\times_B P$ with the standard fiberwise action-angle Poisson structure. In particular, determine all obstructions arising from (i) the monodromy and Chern class of the period lattice bundle of $F$, (ii) the action bundle and its lattice, and (iii) the interaction between the action, angle, and transverse foliations of $M$, that go beyond the obstructions known in the symplectic case.
status_search_result: The obstructions to global action-angle coordinates have been classically described by Duistermaat (Liouville case) and Dazord–Delzant (non-commutative case) on symplectic manifolds. For non-commutative integrable systems on regular Poisson manifolds, additional obstructions have been identified and analyzed (e.g., Laurent-Gengoux–Miranda–Vanhaecke, and subsequent work on b-symplectic manifolds), using the action bundle, action lattice bundle, and the action/angle/transverse foliations. A complete classification of obstructions for general regular Poisson manifolds is not fully settled, so the problem is partially solved.

original_question: Which foliations with affine leaves can be described as the image of the moment map?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\pi)$ be a Poisson manifold and let $\mu:M\to B$ be the moment map of an integrable Hamiltonian system (or, more generally, of a Poisson action) on $M$. The connected components of the regular fibers of $\mu$ form a singular foliation of $M$, and the existence of (possibly generalized) action–angle coordinates equips the base $B$ (away from singularities) with an integral affine structure; equivalently, the image of $\mu$ inherits a foliation whose leaves carry affine structures.

Conversely, consider an abstract foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on a manifold $B$ whose leaves are equipped with affine structures (i.e. each leaf carries a torsion-free flat connection, or equivalently an atlas with affine transition maps). 

Characterize intrinsically those foliations $(B,\mathcal{F})$ with affine leaves that can be realized as the image of the moment map of some integrable Hamiltonian system on a Poisson manifold $(M,\pi)$. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on $(B,\mathcal{F})$ for there to exist a Poisson manifold $(M,\pi)$ and a moment map $\mu:M\to B$ such that the induced foliation with affine leaves on $\mu(M)$ coincides with $(B,\mathcal{F})$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys on integrable systems and Poisson action-angle geometry. While related results exist (e.g. integral affine structures on bases of regular Poisson manifolds of compact type, and Liouville–Mineur–Arnold-type theorems), no general characterization of foliations with affine leaves arising as moment-map images appears in the literature.

original_question: Consider a Poisson manifold M of even dimension such that it is symplectic on a dense set U ⊂ M . Assume that M is endowed with a toric action which is Hamiltonian on U . Is there an analog of Delzant theorem for the image of the moment map?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\pi)$ be a Poisson manifold of even dimension $2n$, and assume there is a dense open subset $U\subset M$ on which the Poisson bivector $\pi$ is non-degenerate, so that $(U,\omega)$ is symplectic with $\omega=\pi^{-1}$. Suppose an $n$-dimensional torus $T^n$ acts effectively on $M$ by Poisson diffeomorphisms, and that the restricted action on the symplectic locus $(U,\omega)$ is Hamiltonian, with moment map $\mu:U\to (\mathfrak{t}^n)^*$.

Question: Is there an analog of the Delzant classification theorem in this setting? More precisely, does the image of the moment map (or a suitable extension of it to all of $M$) admit a combinatorial/convex-geometric characterization that classifies such toric Poisson manifolds up to equivariant Poisson isomorphism, in analogy with the bijection between symplectic toric $2n$-manifolds and Delzant polytopes in $(\mathfrak{t}^n)^*$?
category_tag: Poisson toric manifolds and Delzant-type classification
status_search_result: Partial analogs of Delzant's theorem have been established in special cases. In particular, Gualtieri–Li–Pelayo–Ratiu (arXiv:1407.3300) classify compact toric Hamiltonian log-symplectic manifolds — Poisson manifolds that are symplectic away from a normal-crossing degeneracy locus — via decorated log affine polytopes ("tropical momentum map"). Beyond log-symplectic structures (e.g. arbitrary Poisson manifolds symplectic on a dense set, or b^k-Poisson and more general b-symplectic settings), the question is addressed only in further special cases (Guillemin–Miranda–Pires–Scott et al.), and a fully general Delzant analog remains open.

original_question: Problem 6.8 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical mechanics with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern classes.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a connected symplectic manifold equipped with a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, i.e. a smooth map $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are pairwise Poisson-commuting, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$, and are functionally independent on a dense open subset. Let $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the set of regular values of $F$ over which the fibers are compact and connected. By the Liouville–Arnold–Mineur theorem, $F^{-1}(B)\to B$ is locally a Lagrangian torus bundle and admits local action-angle coordinates. The obstructions to globalizing this structure were identified by Duistermaat: the monodromy, the Chern class of the underlying torus bundle (the "Duistermaat–Chern class" $c\in H^2(B;\mathbb{Z}^n)$), and the Lagrangian class. The Duistermaat–Chern class measures the obstruction to the topological torus bundle $F^{-1}(B)\to B$ admitting a global section.

Problem. Exhibit natural examples of completely integrable Hamiltonian systems arising in classical mechanics (e.g. from physically motivated Hamiltonians on cotangent bundles or standard symplectic manifolds) whose Duistermaat–Chern class $c\in H^2(B;\mathbb{Z}^n)$ is non-trivial.
status_search_result: Surveys on monodromy and global invariants of integrable Hamiltonian systems indicate that while non-trivial Hamiltonian monodromy is well-documented in physical examples (spherical pendulum, champagne bottle, hydrogen atom in crossed fields, etc.), no natural classical-mechanical example with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern class is known. Artificial constructions exist via integrable surgery on symplectic 4-manifolds, but the question of finding physically natural examples remains open.

original_question: Assume that a classical integrable system (p1 , . . . , pn ) is given on M . Does there exist a quantum integrable system (P1 , . . . , Pn ) such that pj = σ(Pj )?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold (for instance, the cotangent bundle $T^*X$ of a smooth manifold $X$, or more generally a symplectic manifold) and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algebra of semiclassical pseudodifferential operators (or, more generally, a deformation quantization) acting on a suitable space of functions/half-densities on $X$, equipped with a principal symbol map $\sigma:\mathcal{A}\to C^\infty(M)$ that is a surjective Poisson algebra homomorphism (mapping the commutator bracket, divided by $i\hbar$, to the Poisson bracket on $M$).

Recall:
- A classical integrable system on $M$ of dimension $2n$ is an $n$-tuple $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ of smooth real-valued functions on $M$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{p_i,p_j\}=0$, and that are functionally independent on a dense open subset of $M$.
- A quantum integrable system is an $n$-tuple $(P_1,\dots,P_n)$ of self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{A}$ that pairwise commute, $[P_i,P_j]=0$, and whose principal symbols are functionally independent on a dense open subset of $M$.

Question: Given an arbitrary classical integrable system $(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ on $M$, does there always exist a quantum integrable system $(P_1,\dots,P_n)$ in $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\sigma(P_j)=p_j$ for every $j=1,\dots,n$?
status_search_result: The general problem of whether every classical Liouville integrable system admits a quantization to a quantum integrable system with prescribed principal symbols is widely regarded as open. Obstructions have been identified, and positive results are known under additional hypotheses (e.g., for involutive systems, in the presence of non-degenerate singularities, or in specific algebraic settings), but no general rule is known. Recent surveys and works on classical/quantum integrability state that there is no general procedure guaranteeing the existence of such a quantization.

original_question: Problem 7.3 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin- Toeplitz quantisation.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $(M,\omega,J)$ be a compact prequantizable Kähler manifold of complex dimension two, with prequantum line bundle $(L,h)\to M$ whose Chern curvature equals $-i\omega$. For each integer $k\ge 1$, let $\mathcal H_k = H^0(M,L^{\otimes k})$ be the space of holomorphic sections, with the inner product induced by $h^{\otimes k}$ and the Liouville volume form $\omega^2/2$. For a smooth function $f\in C^\infty(M)$, let $T_k(f):\mathcal H_k\to\mathcal H_k$ denote the Berezin–Toeplitz operator $T_k(f) = \Pi_k\, M_f\,\Pi_k$, where $M_f$ is multiplication by $f$ and $\Pi_k$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_k$. The semiclassical parameter is $\hbar = 1/k$.

Let $F = (f_1,f_2):M\to\mathbb R^2$ be a smooth completely integrable system, i.e. $\{f_1,f_2\}=0$ and $df_1\wedge df_2$ has maximal rank on a dense open set. Assume that $m\in M$ is a non-degenerate singular point of $F$ of focus–focus type: in symplectic Williamson coordinates $(x_1,\xi_1,x_2,\xi_2)$ near $m$ the quadratic part of $(f_1,f_2)$ is conjugate to $(x_1\xi_1+x_2\xi_2,\, x_1\xi_2-x_2\xi_1)$. Let $c_0=F(m)$ be the corresponding focus–focus critical value, and assume $F^{-1}(c_0)$ contains a single pinched torus.

Consider the pair of commuting self-adjoint Berezin–Toeplitz operators $T_k(f_1)$ and $T_k(f_2)$ and their joint spectrum
$$\Sigma_k = \{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb R^2:\ \exists\,\psi\ne 0,\ T_k(f_j)\psi = \lambda_j\psi,\ j=1,2\}.$$

Problem. Derive an explicit asymptotic singular Bohr–Sommerfeld quantisation condition characterising, modulo $O(k^{-\infty})$, the set of joint eigenvalues $(\lambda_1(k),\lambda_2(k))\in\Sigma_k$ that converge to the focus–focus critical value $c_0$ as $k\to\infty$. The condition should:
(i) be expressed in terms of geometric data attached to the focus–focus fibre (action integrals over a vanishing cycle and a transverse cycle, the Eliasson–Vũ Ngọc desingularised actions, and the appropriate sub-principal/Maslov-type corrections specific to Berezin–Toeplitz quantisation);
(ii) recover the analogous singular Bohr–Sommerfeld rules already known for $\hbar$-pseudodifferential quantisation in the limit, with the corrections specific to the Kähler/Toeplitz setting made explicit;
(iii) account for the quantum monodromy of the joint spectrum near $c_0$.
status_search_result: Singular Bohr–Sommerfeld rules at focus–focus singularities are known in the $\hbar$-pseudodifferential setting (Vũ Ngọc, 1998/2003). For Berezin–Toeplitz operators, regular Bohr–Sommerfeld rules (Charles) and singular rules in the elliptic and hyperbolic 1D cases (Le Floch) have been established, and inverse-spectral consequences for focus–focus values have been studied conditional on Bohr–Sommerfeld rules. However, no published derivation of the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld rules for focus–focus singularities specifically in the Berezin–Toeplitz framework appears to be available, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Problem 7.4 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic 4-manifold and let $F=(J,H):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a semitoric integrable system, meaning that $J$ and $H$ Poisson-commute, $F$ is a proper momentum map with only nondegenerate singularities of elliptic-elliptic, elliptic-regular, or focus-focus type (no hyperbolic blocks), and the component $J$ generates an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action on $M$. Such a system carries a well-defined Chern class (e.g. the first Chern class of $TM$ with its almost complex structure compatible with $\omega$, or, in the toric case, the equivariant Chern class associated to the $T^2$-action), which is one of the symplectic invariants attached to $F$.

A quantization of $F$ consists of a pair of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical (e.g. $\hbar$-pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz) operators $(\hat J_\hbar,\hat H_\hbar)$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\hbar$ whose principal symbols are $J$ and $H$ respectively. Its joint spectrum is
$$\Sigma(\hbar)=\{(\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb{R}^2 : \exists\, v\in\mathcal{H}_\hbar\setminus\{0\},\ \hat J_\hbar v=\lambda v,\ \hat H_\hbar v=\mu v\},$$
viewed as a labeled subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ with multiplicities, in the semiclassical limit $\hbar\to 0$.

Problem. Provide an intrinsic definition of a "quantum Chern class" associated to a quantum semitoric system $(\hat J_\hbar,\hat H_\hbar)$, taking values in a suitable cohomological or combinatorial invariant, such that:
(a) (Semiclassical limit / compatibility) In the limit $\hbar\to 0$ the quantum Chern class recovers the classical Chern class of the underlying semitoric system $(M,\omega,F)$.

original_question: Is a semitoric integrable system F = (J, H) uniquely determined up to symplectic equivalence by its semiclassical joint spectrum, and can one explicitly reconstruct the system from that spectrum?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic 4-manifold and let $F=(J,H):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth map whose components Poisson-commute, $\{J,H\}=0$, with $J$ proper and generating an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action, and such that all critical points of $F$ are non-degenerate with no hyperbolic blocks. Such $F$ is called a semitoric integrable system. Two semitoric systems $(M_1,\omega_1,F_1)$ and $(M_2,\omega_2,F_2)$ are symplectically equivalent if there exists a symplectomorphism $\varphi:M_1\to M_2$ and a smooth map $g:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ of the form $g(x,y)=(x,g_2(x,y))$ with $\partial g_2/\partial y>0$ such that $F_2\circ\varphi = g\circ F_1$.

Quantization. Suppose that for each $\hbar\in(0,1]$ one is given a pair of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical $\hbar$-pseudodifferential operators $\hat J_\hbar,\hat H_\hbar$ on a Hilbert space, with principal symbols $J$ and $H$ respectively. The semiclassical joint spectrum of $(\hat J_\hbar,\hat H_\hbar)$ is the family of subsets
$$\Sigma_\hbar := \{(\lambda,\nu)\in\mathbb{R}^2 : \lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue of }\hat J_\hbar,\ \nu\text{ is an eigenvalue of }\hat H_\hbar\restriction_{\ker(\hat J_\hbar-\lambda)}\},$$
considered as $\hbar\to 0$.

Question. Is every semitoric system $F=(J,H)$ uniquely determined, up to symplectic equivalence, by the asymptotic data $\{\Sigma_\hbar\}_{\hbar\to 0}$ of any such quantization? Furthermore, can one give an explicit constructive procedure that, from the semiclassical joint spectrum alone, recovers the semitoric system (i.e., its complete set of symplectic invariants)?
category_tag: inverse spectral theory of semitoric integrable systems
status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved in the affirmative by Le Floch and Vũ Ngọc (arXiv:2104.06704, "The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems"), who give explicit formulas recovering all symplectic invariants of a semitoric system from the semiclassical joint spectrum, combined with the Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc symplectic classification. Earlier partial results had been obtained for the Jaynes–Cummings case (arXiv:1407.5159) and for focus-focus singularities (arXiv:1302.2260).

original_question: Problem 7.7 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Is the singular Bohr-Sommerfeld formal power series in ~ a spectral invariant?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a connected symplectic 4-manifold and let $F=(J,H):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a completely integrable system with two degrees of freedom whose only singularities are non-degenerate, including possibly a focus–focus critical point $m\in M$ with critical value $c=F(m)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $\hat P_1(\hbar),\hat P_2(\hbar)$ be a pair of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical pseudodifferential operators (or Berezin–Toeplitz operators) on $M$ whose joint principal symbol is $(J,H)$, depending on a small parameter $\hbar>0$.

Near the focus–focus value $c$, the joint spectrum of $(\hat P_1,\hat P_2)$ in a small neighborhood of $c$ is described, modulo $O(\hbar^\infty)$, by a singular Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization condition. This condition can be encoded by a formal power series in $\hbar$,
$$ S(x;\hbar)\;=\;\sum_{k\ge 0}\hbar^k\, S_k(x), $$
defined on a punctured neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb{R}^2$, whose coefficients $S_k$ are smooth functions (with prescribed logarithmic behavior of $S_0$ at the origin). Two integrable systems with focus–focus singularities are said to have the same joint semiclassical spectrum (up to $O(\hbar^\infty)$) if there exist commuting semiclassical operators quantizing them whose joint spectra coincide modulo $O(\hbar^\infty)$ on every compact set, after a possible $\hbar$-dependent change of labels.

Question. Is the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series $S(x;\hbar)$ associated with the focus–focus singularity a spectral invariant? Equivalently, is $S(x;\hbar)$ uniquely determined (as a formal power series in $\hbar$, modulo the ambiguities inherent in its definition) by the joint semiclassical spectrum of any commuting self-adjoint semiclassical quantization of $(J,H)$ in a neighborhood of the focus–focus critical value?
status_search_result: Pelayo–Vu Ngoc (Comm. Math. Phys. 2014, "Semiclassical Inverse Spectral Theory for Singularities of Focus–Focus Type") showed that the joint spectrum near a focus–focus value determines the classical symplectic invariants (the Taylor series invariant) of the singularity, and subsequent work has extended this to recover the Lagrangian foliation around the full focus–focus leaf. These results give partial positive answers regarding the spectral-invariance of the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld data, but a complete statement that the full singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series in $\hbar$ is a spectral invariant in all $\hbar$-orders does not appear to be definitively established in the literature surveyed; the problem appears to be at least partially solved with full resolution unclear.

original_question: Problem 7.8 (Á. Pelayo). What information about the principal symbols f1 , . . . , fn of a quantum integrable system T1,~ , . . . , Tn,~ can be detected from their semiclasical joint spectrum? For instance, suppose that we know that a certain object – say, an integer z, or a matrix A – is a symplectic invariant of (M, ω, f1 , . . . , fn ). Can we compute this object from the semiclassical joint spectrum?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic $2n$-dimensional manifold and let $f_1,\dots,f_n\colon M\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth functions whose Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{f_1},\dots,X_{f_n}$ are pointwise linearly independent on a dense open subset of $M$ and pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$. Such $(M,\omega,f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is called a classical integrable system. A semiclassical quantization of it is a family $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ (depending on a parameter $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$) of self-adjoint, pairwise commuting semiclassical operators (pseudodifferential and/or Berezin–Toeplitz) on a Hilbert space, whose principal symbols equal $f_1,\dots,f_n$. The semiclassical joint spectrum is the family of subsets
$$\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})=\{(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,v\neq 0,\ T_{j,\hbar}v=\lambda_j v\ \forall j\},$$
indexed by $\hbar\to 0$.

(a) Determine, in a constructive manner, what information about the principal symbols $f_1,\dots,f_n$ can be recovered from the semiclassical joint spectrum as $\hbar\to 0$.

(b) Suppose $\mathcal{I}$ is a known symplectic invariant of $(M,\omega,f_1,\dots,f_n)$ (for example an integer $z$, or a matrix $A$). Provide an explicit procedure that computes $\mathcal{I}$ from the semiclassical joint spectrum, or show that no such procedure exists.
category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for quantum integrable systems
status_search_result: The general problem remains open, but substantial progress has been made for the class of semitoric systems (n=2 with one $S^1$-action and non-degenerate singularities). Work by Le Floch–Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc and collaborators (2013–2021) gives explicit constructive recovery of all known symplectic invariants of semitoric systems from the semiclassical joint spectrum, proving spectral determinism in that class. The full multidimensional case and recovery of arbitrary symplectic invariants beyond the semitoric setting are not resolved.

original_question: Problem 7.9 (Á. Pelayo). Can one detect from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system T1,~ , . . . , Tn,~ that a singularity is degenerate?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a classical integrable system, i.e. the components $f_i$ are smooth, Poisson-commute ($\{f_i,f_j\}=0$), and have almost-everywhere linearly independent differentials. A point $p\in M$ is a singular point of $F$ if the rank of $dF(p)$ is less than $n$; such a singularity is called non-degenerate (in the Williamson sense) when the Hessians of $f_1,\dots,f_n$ at $p$ span a Cartan subalgebra of the Lie algebra of quadratic forms on $T_pM$ under the Poisson bracket; otherwise the singularity is called degenerate.

A semiclassical quantization of $F$ is a family of commuting self-adjoint operators $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ (e.g. $\hbar$-pseudodifferential operators or Berezin–Toeplitz operators) whose principal symbols are $f_1,\dots,f_n$, depending on a parameter $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$. Their joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of joint eigenvalues, viewed as a family indexed by $\hbar$.

Question: Is there a procedure that, given only the joint spectrum (as $\hbar\to 0$) of a quantum integrable system $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$, decides whether the underlying classical system $F$ has a degenerate singularity?

status_search_result: Recent work by Pelayo, Vũ Ngọc, Le Floch and collaborators has established inverse spectral results for semitoric quantum integrable systems and for non-degenerate (focus–focus, elliptic) singularities, showing that such singularities and their symplectic invariants can be recovered from the joint spectrum. However, no source found explicitly resolves the general detection-of-degeneracy question for arbitrary quantum integrable systems, so the status appears to remain open in full generality.

original_question: Problem 7.10 (Á. Pelayo). Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of µ : M → S 1 ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold equipped with an effective Hamiltonian circle action $S^1 \curvearrowright M$ with momentum map $\mu : M \to \mathbb{R}$ (or, after exponentiation, $\mu : M \to S^1$). Assume $M$ admits a prequantum line bundle $(L,\nabla)$ with curvature $\omega$ and a compatible $S^1$-equivariant structure, so that geometric quantization yields a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ together with a self-adjoint quantum operator $\widehat{\mu}$ obtained as the quantization of $\mu$. The fixed point set $M^{S^1}$ of the action is finite when the action has only isolated fixed points.

Question: Can the number $\#M^{S^1}$ of fixed points of the Hamiltonian $S^1$-action be determined, bounded, or otherwise computed from spectral data of the operator $\widehat{\mu}$ (for instance, from the joint or asymptotic distribution of its eigenvalues, possibly in a semiclassical limit $\hbar \to 0$)? More precisely, find an explicit relation expressing $\#M^{S^1}$ in terms of the spectrum $\mathrm{Spec}(\widehat{\mu})$, or prove that no such relation exists.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. Related work by Pelayo and Vũ Ngọc on inverse spectral results for semitoric systems suggests progress on recovering symplectic invariants from quantum spectra, but no source explicitly settles whether the count of fixed points of a Hamiltonian $S^1$-action can be extracted from the spectrum of the quantized momentum map. Status remains unclear from accessible sources.

original_question: What are necessary and/or sufficient conditions on a metric g such that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian (or pseudo-Riemannian) manifold and let $H:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ be the geodesic Hamiltonian $H(x,p)=\tfrac{1}{2}g^{ij}(x)p_ip_j$. A function $F:T^*M\to\mathbb{R}$ that is polynomial in the fibre coordinates $p$ and Poisson-commutes with $H$ (i.e. $\{H,F\}=0$) is called a polynomial integral of the geodesic flow of $g$.

A polynomial integral $F$ of degree $d$ is said to be quantisable if there exists a differential operator $\widehat{F}$ on $M$ of order $d$, whose principal symbol equals $F$, that commutes with the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ of $g$:
$$[\Delta_g,\widehat{F}]=0.$$

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the metric $g$ under which every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow is quantisable in the above sense.
status_search_result: No published result was located providing general necessary and sufficient conditions on a metric ensuring that every polynomial integral of its geodesic flow admits a commuting differential-operator quantisation. The literature contains case-by-case quantisation results (e.g. for Killing tensors of low degree, superintegrable systems, and specific 2-dimensional examples) and obstruction-type results, but the general characterisation appears to remain open.

original_question: For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) denote the maximum size of a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. Is there a graph parameter alpha_P, analogous to the Gallai identities for ordinary matchings, such that beta_P(G) + alpha_P(G) = |V(G)| for every graph G in the relevant class?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with no isolated vertices. For a matching $M\subseteq E(G)$, let $\langle M\rangle$ denote the subgraph of $G$ induced by the set of endpoints of edges in $M$. Fix a graph property $P$ (a class of graphs closed under isomorphism), and define
$$\beta_P(G)=\max\{|M|:M\text{ is a matching of }G\text{ and }\langle M\rangle\text{ has property }P\}.$$
Recall the classical Gallai identities: if $\alpha_0(G)$ is the vertex-cover number, $\beta_0(G)$ the independence number, $\alpha_1(G)$ the edge-cover number, and $\beta_1(G)$ the maximum-matching number, then for every graph $G$ without isolated vertices,
$$\alpha_0(G)+\beta_0(G)=|V(G)|,\qquad \alpha_1(G)+\beta_1(G)=|V(G)|.$$
Question: Does there exist, for each graph property $P$ (in a suitably broad class), a graph parameter $\alpha_P$ — defined analogously to the Gallai dual parameters $\alpha_0,\alpha_1$ — such that
$$\beta_P(G)+\alpha_P(G)=|V(G)|$$
holds for every graph $G$ (without isolated vertices) in the class for which $\beta_P$ is defined? If so, give an explicit definition of $\alpha_P$ and prove the identity.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published Gallai-type identity of the requested form $\beta_P(G)+\alpha_P(G)=|V(G)|$ for general property-constrained matchings. Existing results on Gallai identities concern the classical matching/covering parameters and chromatic/clique-partition extensions, with no dual parameter $\alpha_P$ found for arbitrary $P$-matchings. The status is therefore inconclusive from the available evidence.

original_question: For a graph G and a graph property P, let beta_P(G) denote the maximum size of a P-matching in G, where a P-matching is a matching M whose induced subgraph <M> has property P. What Nordhaus-Gaddum type bounds can be proved for beta_P over a graph and its complement; specifically, what are the best possible lower and upper bounds for beta_P(G) + beta_P(G_bar) and for beta_P(G) * beta_P(G_bar)?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple graph and let $\bar G$ denote its complement on the same vertex set. A matching of G is a set M ⊆ E of pairwise non-adjacent edges, and the induced subgraph $\langle M\rangle$ is the subgraph of G induced by the set of endpoints of edges in M. Fix a graph property P (a class of graphs closed under isomorphism). A matching M of G is called a P-matching if $\langle M\rangle$ has property P. Define
$$\beta_P(G) = \max\{|M| : M \text{ is a $P$-matching of } G\},$$
with $\beta_P(G)=0$ if G has no P-matching.

For a graph G of order n, determine, in terms of n (and possibly other natural parameters), the best possible (i.e., sharp) constants $f_1(n,P)$, $f_2(n,P)$, $g_1(n,P)$, $g_2(n,P)$ such that for every graph G on n vertices,
$$f_1(n,P) \le \beta_P(G) + \beta_P(\bar G) \le f_2(n,P),$$
$$g_1(n,P) \le \beta_P(G) \cdot \beta_P(\bar G) \le g_2(n,P),$$
and characterize the extremal graphs achieving equality in each bound. In particular, complete this Nordhaus–Gaddum-type program for natural choices of the property P (such as P = "is a disjoint union of edges" giving the induced matching number, P = "is acyclic", P = "is connected", etc.).
status_search_result: A general Nordhaus–Gaddum program for the parameter β_P (over arbitrary graph properties P) does not appear to be resolved in the literature. Nordhaus–Gaddum-type bounds have been established for specific related matching parameters (e.g., dominating induced matchings, induced path number) but no comprehensive sharp bounds for β_P(G)+β_P(\bar G) and β_P(G)·β_P(\bar G) for general P have been found.

self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple graph. A matching in G is a set M ⊆ E of pairwise non-adjacent edges. For a matching M, let ⟨M⟩ denote the subgraph of G induced by the set of endpoints of the edges in M (i.e., the subgraph of G on vertex set V(M) = ⋃_{e∈M} e and containing every edge of G with both endpoints in V(M)).

Fix a graph property P (a class of graphs closed under isomorphism). A matching M is called a P-matching if ⟨M⟩ has property P. Define
   β_P(G) = max{ |M| : M is a matching of G and ⟨M⟩ has property P }.

Special cases include:
 • P = "edgeless graph" (induced matching number),
 • P = "forest" (acyclic matching number),
 • P = "graph in which M is the unique perfect matching" (uniquely restricted matching number),
 • P = "connected graph" (connected matching number),
 • P = "disconnected graph" (disconnected matching number).

Problem. Determine the computational complexity of the decision problem
   INPUT: a graph G and a positive integer k;
   QUESTION: is β_P(G) ≥ k?
for each natural graph property P as above. In particular, characterize the graph classes on which β_P(G) can be computed in polynomial time and the graph classes on which the problem is NP-complete, providing a complete dichotomy.
status_search_result: The complexity of β_P has been studied extensively for specific properties P. Induced matching is NP-complete on bipartite graphs of maximum degree 4, k-regular graphs (k ≥ 4), and planar graphs of maximum degree 4, and is polynomial-time solvable on chordal graphs, chordal bipartite graphs, trapezoid graphs, and cocomparability graphs. Acyclic matching, uniquely restricted matching, and disconnected matching are NP-hard in general; connected matching has the same complexity as ordinary maximum matching. Recent work (e.g., Chaudhary–Zehavi, 2023) studies parameterized complexity by treewidth. A complete classification across all natural P and all graph classes remains open; many specific cases are resolved.

original_question: A disconnected matching is a matching M such that |M| = 1 or the induced subgraph <M> is disconnected, and beta_dc(G) denotes the maximum size of a disconnected matching in G. What is the computational complexity of determining beta_dc(G), especially since the survey notes complexity results for several other matching varieties but leaves beta_dc unresolved?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph. A matching in G is a set M ⊆ E of pairwise non-adjacent edges. Let ⟨M⟩ denote the subgraph of G induced by the set of endpoints of edges in M. Call a matching M disconnected if either |M| = 1, or |M| ≥ 2 and the induced subgraph ⟨M⟩ is disconnected. Define
   β_dc(G) = max{ |M| : M is a disconnected matching of G }.
The Disconnected Matching problem asks, given a graph G and an integer k, whether β_dc(G) ≥ k.

Determine the computational complexity of computing β_dc(G) (equivalently, of the decision problem above): identify the graph classes on which it is NP-hard and those on which it is solvable in polynomial time, and characterize its parameterized complexity with respect to natural parameters such as the solution size k.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has resolved much of the complexity of computing β_dc. Disconnected Matching (the c=2 version corresponding to β_dc) is shown to be NP-complete, including on bipartite graphs of diameter 3, while it is polynomial for bipartite graphs of diameter at most 2 and for interval graphs; it is NP-complete for chordal graphs. Parameterized results have also appeared (e.g., W[1]-hardness in the matching size, paraNP-hardness in c). Thus the original open question on the complexity of β_dc has been substantially answered, though refinements (particular graph classes, kernelization, etc.) continue.

context_brief: Sarwate-Pursley lower bound conjecture in characteristic 2
original_question: Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2 such that the extension degree [F : F_2] is even, and let d be an invertible exponent over F (that is, gcd(d, |F^*|) = 1). Must there always exist a nonzero element a in F such that the Weil sum W_{F,d}(a) has magnitude at least 2*sqrt(|F|)? Equivalently, must there always exist a in F^* such that |W_{F,d}(a) - 1| >= -1 + 2*sqrt(|F|)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a finite field of characteristic $2$ and order $q = |F|$, and assume that the degree $[F:\mathbb{F}_2]$ is even (equivalently, $q$ is an even power of $2$). Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi: F \to \mathbb{C}^\times$, for example $\psi(x) = (-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}_{F/\mathbb{F}_2}(x)}$. For an integer $d$ with $\gcd(d, q-1) = 1$ (an "invertible exponent" over $F$), define the Weil sum
$$W_{F,d}(a) \;=\; \sum_{x \in F} \psi\!\left(a x^d + x\right), \qquad a \in F.$$
Prove or disprove: there always exists a nonzero $a \in F$ such that
$$|W_{F,d}(a)| \;\geq\; 2\sqrt{q},$$
or equivalently, such that
$$|W_{F,d}(a) - 1| \;\geq\; -1 + 2\sqrt{q}.$$
status_search_result: The statement is the Sarwate–Pursley conjecture (1980) on Weil sums in characteristic 2 with even extension degree. A general-form proof has not been located; surveys on Weil sums of binomials describe it as an outstanding conjecture. Direct web verification of full resolution was inconclusive, so it appears to remain open.
