paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find a proof of maximal output p-norm multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel that does not rely on unitary equivalence to channels with negative multipliers.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A qubit channel is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ : M₂(ℂ) → M₂(ℂ). For ρ ∈ M₂(ℂ), the maximal output p-norm of Φ (for p ≥ 1) is

  ν_p(Φ) := sup_{ρ ≥ 0, Tr ρ = 1} ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where ‖A‖_p = (Tr |A|^p)^{1/p}. The channel Φ is said to be multiplicative for p-norms if for every channel Ψ (acting on any finite-dimensional matrix algebra),

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ψ) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ψ).

The two-Pauli qubit channel is the channel

  Φ_{2P}(ρ) = (1 − x) ρ + (x/2) (σ_x ρ σ_x + σ_z ρ σ_z),  x ∈ [0,1],

where σ_x, σ_z are the Pauli matrices. In the Bloch representation it acts as a diagonal map (r_x, r_y, r_z) ↦ (λ_x r_x, λ_y r_y, λ_z r_z) with multipliers (λ_x, λ_y, λ_z) = (1 − x, 1 − 2x, 1 − x); for x > 1/2 the middle multiplier is negative. By a unitary rotation one can conjugate Φ_{2P} into a channel with all multipliers non-negative, and known proofs of p-norm multiplicativity for Φ_{2P} pass through such conjugation.

Problem. Produce a proof, valid for all p ∈ [1, ∞] (in particular for the relevant range establishing additivity-type results), that the two-Pauli qubit channel Φ_{2P} satisfies

  ν_p(Φ_{2P} ⊗ Ψ) = ν_p(Φ_{2P}) · ν_p(Ψ)

for every channel Ψ, without using unitary equivalence to a Pauli-diagonal channel whose Bloch multipliers are all non-negative.
status_search_result: The general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture for quantum channels was disproved (Hastings; Hayden–Winter) for sufficiently large p, but multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel is established via known King-style proofs that do invoke unitary equivalence to a channel with non-negative multipliers. No published work was located that provides a multiplicativity proof for the two-Pauli qubit channel avoiding this reduction, so the specific methodological question appears to remain unresolved, though we could not verify this conclusively.

self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a completely positive trace-preserving (CPT) linear map between finite-dimensional matrix algebras. Recall that $\Phi$ is called extreme if it is an extreme point of the convex set of CPT maps from $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)$ to $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$; equivalently, by Choi's theorem, $\Phi$ has a Kraus representation $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{k=1}^{r} A_k\rho A_k^*$ such that the operators $\{A_j^*A_k\}_{j,k=1}^{r}$ are linearly independent.

Define the minimal output von Neumann entropy of $\Phi$ by
$$S_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}\, S(\Phi(\rho)),\qquad S(\sigma)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma),$$
the infimum being over density matrices on $\mathcal{H}_A$. For $1\le p\le\infty$ define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)=\sup_{\rho}\,\|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,\qquad \|\sigma\|_p=(\operatorname{Tr}|\sigma|^p)^{1/p}.$$

Identify new classes of extreme CPT maps $\Phi$ such that, for every CPT map $\Omega$ (in some natural class, e.g. all CPT maps, or all maps in the same class), one can prove either the additivity relation
$$S_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S_{\min}(\Phi)+S_{\min}(\Omega),$$
or the multiplicativity relation
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega)$$
for some $p>1$.
status_search_result: The general additivity conjecture for minimal output von Neumann entropy was disproved by Hastings (2009) via random channel constructions, with later analyses by Fukuda–King–Moser and Aubrun–Szarek. Multiplicativity of maximal output $p$-norms for $p>1$ was also disproved (Hayden–Winter). However, additivity/multiplicativity is still proved for specific classes of channels (entanglement-breaking, unital qubit, depolarizing, Hadamard, etc.), and the broader task of identifying new classes of extreme CPT maps for which these relations hold remains an active research direction with only partial results.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For random sub-unitary channels, prove maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), at least at p = 2, or determine whether these channels yield additional counterexamples to multiplicativity.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. A quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map Φ: M_d(ℂ) → M_{d'}(ℂ), which can be represented in Kraus form Φ(ρ) = Σ_k A_k ρ A_k^*, with Σ_k A_k^* A_k = I_d. For p ≥ 1, the maximal output p-norm of Φ is defined by

  ν_p(Φ) := sup_{ρ ≥ 0, Tr ρ = 1} ‖Φ(ρ)‖_p,

where ‖X‖_p = (Tr|X|^p)^{1/p} is the Schatten p-norm.

A channel Φ is called a "random sub-unitary channel" if it admits a Kraus representation of the form

  A_k = √{p_k} · U_k P_k,

where {p_k} is a probability distribution (p_k ≥ 0, Σ_k p_k = 1), each U_k is a unitary on ℂ^d, and each P_k is an orthogonal projection on ℂ^d, chosen so that the trace-preserving condition Σ_k p_k P_k U_k^* U_k P_k = Σ_k p_k P_k = I_d holds. (Equivalently, Φ(ρ) = Σ_k p_k U_k P_k ρ P_k U_k^* with Σ_k p_k P_k = I.)

Question. Let Φ be a random sub-unitary channel and let Ω be an arbitrary quantum channel. Prove or disprove the multiplicativity identity

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) · ν_p(Ω),

at least in the case p = 2. If this identity fails, exhibit a pair (Φ, Ω) with Φ random sub-unitary for which strict inequality ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) > ν_p(Φ) ν_p(Ω) occurs.
status_search_result: While the general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture has been disproved for all p > 1 (Hayden–Winter, and for p > 2 by Winter), and weak multiplicativity results for random quantum channels are known (Montanaro and others), no source found directly settles the multiplicativity of ν_p at p = 2 specifically for the class of "random sub-unitary" channels with Kraus operators of the form √{p_k} U_k P_k. The status of this specific question appears unresolved in the literature surveyed.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For any fixed pair of quantum channels Φ and Ω, does there exist a number p* > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds either for every p in an interval (p*,1) with p* < 1 or for every p in an interval (1,p*) with p* > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_A)$ and $\Omega:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_B)$ be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving linear maps between matrix algebras). For $p>0$, $p\neq 1$, the Rényi entropy of order $p$ of a density operator $\rho$ is
$$S^p(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^p),$$
and for $p=1$ it is the von Neumann entropy $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$. The minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy of a channel $\Phi$ is
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}S^p(\Phi(\rho)),$$
where the infimum is over input density operators (equivalently, pure states).

Decide the following statement: for every pair of quantum channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$, there exists $p^*>0$ such that either
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $p^*<1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(p^*,1)$, or
\item[(ii)] $p^*>1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(1,p^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
That is, prove this dichotomy holds for all channel pairs, or exhibit a counterexample.
category_tag: Quantum channels and Rényi entropy additivity
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be refuted. Hastings (2009) produced channels for which additivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy fails at $p=1$; subsequent analyses (Aubrun–Szarek–Werner; Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter; Collins–Fukuda–Nechita and others) show that the same random-subspace constructions yield violations of additivity of the minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy on intervals adjacent to $p=1$ (in particular for $p\in(1-p_0,1)$ with $p_0\approx 0.2855$). Combined with Hayden–Winter / Grudka–Horodecki / recent constructive results showing violations for all $p>1$, there exist fixed pairs $(\Phi,\Omega)$ for which additivity fails on every one-sided neighborhood of $p=1$, contradicting the conjectured dichotomy.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For each fixed dimension bound d, does there exist a number p_d > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds uniformly for all channels Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'} with d' ≤ d either throughout p_d < p < 1 when p_d < 1 or throughout 1 < p < p_d when p_d > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let M_n denote the algebra of n×n complex matrices, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving linear map Φ: M_n → M_n. For p > 0 with p ≠ 1, the minimal output Rényi p-entropy of Φ is defined by
   S^p_min(Φ) = inf_ρ (1/(1−p)) log Tr[(Φ(ρ))^p],
where the infimum runs over all density matrices ρ ∈ M_n (positive semidefinite, trace one); equivalently, S^p_min(Φ) = inf_ρ S_p(Φ(ρ)), where S_p(σ) = (1−p)^{−1} log Tr(σ^p) is the Rényi p-entropy of σ.

For two channels Φ: M_n → M_n and Ω: M_m → M_m, the tensor product channel Φ ⊗ Ω: M_{nm} → M_{nm} is the standard one. Say that the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive if
   S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω).

Prove or disprove: For every positive integer d there exists a real number p_d > 0 such that one of the following holds:
 (i) p_d < 1, and for every pair of integers d', d'' ≤ d, every channel Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'}, every channel Ω: M_{d''} → M_{d''}, and every p with p_d < p < 1, the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive;
 (ii) p_d > 1, and for every pair of integers d', d'' ≤ d, every channel Φ: M_{d'} → M_{d'}, every channel Ω: M_{d''} → M_{d''}, and every p with 1 < p < p_d, the pair (Φ, Ω) is p-additive.
status_search_result: Case (ii) of the conjecture (a neighborhood of 1 from above) has been refuted: counterexamples to additivity of minimum output Rényi p-entropy are now known for every p > 1 (Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter, 2008, and subsequent constructive work). For 0 < p < 1, counterexamples have been constructed for p in intervals (0, p₀) and (1 − p₀, 1) with p₀ ≈ 0.2855, ruling out a uniform p_d for sufficiently large dimensions. The von Neumann (p = 1) additivity itself was disproved by Hastings (2008). Thus a uniform dimension-dependent threshold p_d as conjectured does not survive on the p > 1 side, and is severely constrained on the p < 1 side; the precise dimension-by-dimension version stated remains not fully resolved in the literature.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: Rényi-additivity violations on both sides of p=1
original_question: Does there exist a single channel, or a pair of channels, that violates additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω) both at some p1 > 1 and at some p2 with 0 < p2 < 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A,\mathcal{H}_B$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. A quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map. For $p>0$, $p\neq 1$, the Rényi $p$-entropy of a state $\rho$ is
$$S^p(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\mathrm{Tr}(\rho^p),$$
and the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy of $\Phi$ is
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}S^p(\Phi(\rho)),$$
where the infimum is over input density operators on $\mathcal{H}_A$. One says that channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$ satisfy additivity at exponent $p$ when
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega).$$

Question: Do there exist a quantum channel $\Phi$ (or a pair of quantum channels $\Phi,\Omega$) and exponents $p_1>1$ and $0<p_2<1$ such that additivity of the minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy fails simultaneously at $p=p_1$ and at $p=p_2$ for the same channel (or for the same pair of channels)?
status_search_result: Counterexamples to additivity of the minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy are now known separately for all $p>1$ (constructive examples, e.g., 2025 constructions extending earlier $p>2$ results) and for $p$ close to $0$ (Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter, 2008). However, web searches did not surface a result exhibiting a single channel or fixed pair of channels that simultaneously violates additivity at some $p_1>1$ and at some $p_2\in(0,1)$, so the specific question of joint violation by one channel/pair appears not to be definitively settled in the located literature.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
context_brief: First tensor-power failure of Rényi additivity
original_question: Find a quantum channel Φ, an integer m, and a real p > 0 such that minimal output Rényi entropy is additive for fewer than m tensor powers, S^p_min(Φ^{⊗n}) = n S^p_min(Φ) for n < m, but fails exactly at m copies in the sense S^p_min(Φ^{⊗m}) < m S^p_min(Φ).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a quantum channel, i.e. a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between matrix algebras. For a real number $p>0$, define the minimal output $p$-Rényi entropy of $\Phi$ by
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi) \;=\; \inf_{\rho}\, S_p\bigl(\Phi(\rho)\bigr), \qquad S_p(\sigma)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma^p),$$
where the infimum is over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$. For an integer $n\ge 1$ let $\Phi^{\otimes n}$ denote the $n$-fold tensor power of $\Phi$, acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A^{\otimes n})$. One always has $S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes n})\le n\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi)$.

Exhibit an explicit triple $(\Phi, m, p)$ consisting of a quantum channel $\Phi$, an integer $m\ge 2$, and a real number $p>0$ such that
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes n}) \;=\; n\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi) \quad \text{for every } 1\le n<m,$$
but
$$ S^p_{\min}(\Phi^{\otimes m}) \;<\; m\,S^p_{\min}(\Phi).$$
That is, additivity of the minimal output $p$-Rényi entropy holds for fewer than $m$ tensor copies and fails for the first time at exactly $m$ copies.
status_search_result: Many counterexamples to additivity of minimum output p-Rényi entropy are known (for p>2, p>1, p close to 0, and via random/antisymmetric constructions). However, none of the located references explicitly exhibit a channel where additivity holds for all n<m but breaks exactly at n=m for some finite m≥2; the question of a "first failure at exactly m copies" remains unresolved in the sources found.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For all counterexamples to maximal output p-norm multiplicativity ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ)ν_p(Ω), must the counterexample channels have non-negative completely bounded (CB) entropy and/or zero coherent information?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the bounded operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, and let a quantum channel be a completely positive trace-preserving linear map $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$. For $p\ge 1$, define the maximal output $p$-norm
$$\nu_p(\Phi)=\sup_{\rho}\,\|\Phi(\rho)\|_p,$$
where the supremum runs over density operators $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A$ and $\|X\|_p=(\mathrm{Tr}|X|^p)^{1/p}$. A pair $(\Phi,\Omega)$ of channels is said to be a counterexample to maximal output $p$-norm multiplicativity if
$$\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)>\nu_p(\Phi)\,\nu_p(\Omega).$$

For a channel $\Phi$ with Stinespring isometry $V:\mathcal{H}_A\to\mathcal{H}_B\otimes\mathcal{H}_E$ and complementary channel $\Phi^c(\rho)=\mathrm{Tr}_B(V\rho V^\dagger)$, define:
- the coherent information $I_c(\rho,\Phi)=S(\Phi(\rho))-S(\Phi^c(\rho))$, where $S(\sigma)=-\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma\log\sigma)$ is the von Neumann entropy;
- the completely bounded (CB) entropy $S_{\mathrm{CB}}(\Phi)$, defined as the regularized minimum, over all input states $\rho_{RA}$ on an arbitrary reference system $R$ tensored with the input, of $S(\Phi^c(\rho_A))-S(\Phi(\rho_A))$ optimized in the CB sense (equivalently, $-\inf_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$ in the appropriate completely bounded regularization).

Question: For every $p>1$ and every pair of channels $(\Phi,\Omega)$ that violates maximal output $p$-norm multiplicativity, must at least one of the following hold for the channels involved?
(a) The CB entropy is non-negative;
(b) The maximum coherent information $\max_\rho I_c(\rho,\Phi)$ equals zero.
status_search_result: Hastings (2009) gave random counterexamples disproving the additivity/multiplicativity conjectures for all $p\ge 1$, and the construction was simplified and extended (e.g., via Dvoretzky's theorem). However, no source found explicitly addresses whether all known counterexamples necessarily exhibit non-negative CB entropy and/or zero coherent information; the specific entropy-signature question therefore appears not to have been settled in the literature returned by search.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Prove additivity of minimal output entropy for quantum channels, S_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S_min(Φ) + S_min(Ω), where S_min(Φ) is the infimum of S[Φ(γ)] over density matrices γ, or else find a counterexample to this additivity statement.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the set of density matrices on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. positive semidefinite operators $\gamma$ on $\mathcal{H}$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\gamma = 1$. A quantum channel $\Phi : \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ is a completely positive trace-preserving linear map. The von Neumann entropy of a density matrix $\rho$ is $S(\rho) = -\operatorname{Tr}(\rho \log \rho)$, and the minimal output entropy of a channel $\Phi$ is
$$S_{\min}(\Phi) \;=\; \inf_{\gamma \in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H}_A)} S\bigl(\Phi(\gamma)\bigr).$$
Given two quantum channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$, the tensor product $\Phi \otimes \Omega$ is again a quantum channel acting on density matrices of the joint system.

Determine whether the additivity identity
$$S_{\min}(\Phi \otimes \Omega) \;=\; S_{\min}(\Phi) + S_{\min}(\Omega)$$
holds for all pairs of quantum channels $\Phi, \Omega$. Either prove that the equality always holds, or exhibit a pair of channels for which it fails.
status_search_result: The additivity conjecture for minimal output entropy was disproved by M. B. Subsequent work has refined and simplified the counterexample. Thus the problem is solved in the negative: additivity does not hold in general.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: Find pairs of quantum channels M and N that are mutually degradable, meaning that there exist channels X and Y for which X ∘ M equals the complementary channel N^C and Y ∘ N equals the complementary channel M^C; in particular, find nontrivial examples beyond the known case M = I, such as pairs where both channels have Choi rank d but are not individually degradable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}_A$, $\mathcal{H}_B$, $\mathcal{H}_E$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces. Recall that a quantum channel is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) linear map between spaces of trace-class operators. Every channel $M : B(\mathcal{H}_A) \to B(\mathcal{H}_B)$ admits a Stinespring isometry $V_M : \mathcal{H}_A \to \mathcal{H}_B \otimes \mathcal{H}_E$ such that $M(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_E(V_M \rho V_M^*)$; the complementary channel is defined by $M^C(\rho) = \mathrm{Tr}_B(V_M \rho V_M^*)$. The Choi rank of $M$ is the minimum dimension of $\mathcal{H}_E$ in any Stinespring dilation, equivalently the rank of the Choi matrix of $M$. A channel $M$ is called degradable if there exists a channel $D$ with $D \circ M = M^C$.

Two channels $M$ and $N$ (with appropriately compatible input/output spaces) are said to be mutually degradable if there exist channels $X$ and $Y$ such that
$$ X \circ M = N^C \quad \text{and} \quad Y \circ N = M^C. $$

Note that if $M = I$ is the identity channel, then $M^C$ is (up to isometry) the trace, so the conditions reduce trivially and any channel $N$ pairs with $I$. Exhibit nontrivial pairs $(M, N)$ of mutually degradable channels in which neither channel is the identity. In particular, construct a pair $(M, N)$ such that both $M$ and $N$ act on a $d$-dimensional input system, both have Choi rank equal to $d$, and neither $M$ nor $N$ is individually degradable; or prove that no such pair exists.
status_search_result: A web search for mutually degradable quantum channel pairs and related Choi-rank constructions did not return any work that explicitly constructs nontrivial mutually degradable pairs with both channels of Choi rank d and neither individually degradable, nor a proof that none exist. The literature surveyed focuses on the structure of (individually) degradable channels, complementary channels, and Choi-rank bounds, but does not appear to resolve the mutual degradability problem.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For the N-representability problem, where one seeks necessary and sufficient conditions for a p-particle reduced density matrix to come from an antisymmetric or symmetric N-particle density matrix, find a minimal complete set of local invariants for an antisymmetric or symmetric two-particle density matrix. The local invariants should be parameters invariant under transformations U ⊗ U ⊗ … ⊗ U and rich enough to express the two-particle N-representability conditions.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $U(\mathcal{H})$ denote its unitary group. For an integer $N\ge 2$, consider the $N$-fold tensor power $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}$, and let $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge N}\subset \mathcal{H}^{\otimes N}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee N}$) denote its totally antisymmetric (resp. totally symmetric) subspace. An $N$-fermion (resp. $N$-boson) density matrix is a positive semidefinite trace-one operator $\rho_{1,\dots,N}$ supported on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge N}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee N}$). For $1\le p\le N$, the $p$-particle reduced density matrix is
$$\rho_{1,\dots,p}\;=\;\mathrm{Tr}_{p+1,\dots,N}\,\rho_{1,\dots,N},$$
which acts on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge p}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}^{\vee p}$).

Local unitary action. The unitary group $U(\mathcal{H})$ acts on operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes p}$ via the diagonal representation $U^{\otimes p}$, i.e. by
$$\rho \;\longmapsto\; U^{\otimes p}\,\rho\,(U^{\otimes p})^\dagger,\qquad U\in U(\mathcal{H}).$$
A local invariant of a $p$-particle density matrix is a function of $\rho_{1,\dots,p}$ that is constant on each orbit of this action. A set $\{I_\alpha\}$ of local invariants is called complete if it separates orbits, i.e. two $p$-particle density matrices have the same values of all $I_\alpha$ if and only if they lie in the same $U^{\otimes p}$-orbit. The set is called minimal if no proper subset is complete.

Problem. Take $p=2$. Exhibit, for both the antisymmetric case (operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\wedge 2}$) and the symmetric case (operators on $\mathcal{H}^{\vee 2}$), a minimal complete set of local invariants of a two-particle density matrix under the action $\rho \mapsto (U\otimes U)\rho(U\otimes U)^\dagger$, $U\in U(\mathcal{H})$. The set should be expressive enough that the two-particle $N$-representability conditions (necessary and sufficient conditions on $\rho_{1,2}$ for the existence of an $N$-particle antisymmetric/symmetric density matrix $\rho_{1,\dots,N}$ with $\mathrm{Tr}_{3,\dots,N}\rho_{1,\dots,N}=\rho_{1,2}$) can be formulated in terms of these invariants.
category_tag: N-representability and local invariants of reduced density matrices
status_search_result: The general N-representability problem for the 2-particle reduced density matrix is QMA-hard; while hierarchies of necessary conditions (e.g. Mazziotti's constructive solution via a hierarchy of constraints) and partial parameterizations exist, no explicit minimal complete set of $U\otimes U$-local invariants for the antisymmetric/symmetric 2-RDM that captures full N-representability appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Single-exponential algorithms for all Betti numbers
original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by s polynomial equalities and inequalities whose degrees are bounded by d. Is there an algorithm that computes all Betti numbers of S in time single exponential in k? More concretely, can the currently known single-exponential methods for computing only the first l Betti numbers for fixed l be extended to compute the full Betti sequence of S within a single-exponential running time in the ambient dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set described by a Boolean combination of $s$ polynomial equalities and inequalities, where each defining polynomial has degree at most $d$. For each $i \geq 0$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of $S$. An algorithm is said to run in single-exponential time in $k$ if its complexity is bounded by $(s d)^{k^{O(1)}}$.

It is known that, for every fixed nonnegative integer $\ell$, there is an algorithm running in single-exponential time in $k$ which computes $b_0(S), b_1(S), \ldots, b_\ell(S)$. It is also known that all Betti numbers of $S$ can be computed in doubly-exponential time (e.g., via cylindrical algebraic decomposition).

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given the defining polynomials of $S$, computes the entire sequence $(b_0(S), b_1(S), \ldots, b_k(S))$ of Betti numbers of $S$ in time single-exponential in the ambient dimension $k$?
status_search_result: The problem remains open. Single-exponential algorithms are known for computing the first $\ell$ Betti numbers for any fixed $\ell$ (Basu and collaborators), and recent extensions (e.g., Basu–Karisani 2024) compute homology functors on semi-algebraic maps in low dimensions with single-exponential complexity, but no algorithm is known that computes all Betti numbers of a general semi-algebraic set in single-exponential time. The existing general algorithm has doubly-exponential complexity. This is consistently described as a central open problem in algorithmic semi-algebraic geometry.

original_question: For semi-algebraic sets, are the middle Betti numbers intrinsically harder to compute than the lowest and highest Betti numbers or the Euler-Poincare characteristic? In particular, is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result that explains the apparent algorithmic gap, or an analogue of the phenomenon from smooth projective complex varieties in which the middle Betti numbers contain essentially all the information?
self_contained_problem:
A semi-algebraic set in $\mathbb{R}^k$ is a finite Boolean combination of sets of the form $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^k : P(x) \bowtie 0\}$ for polynomials $P \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$ and $\bowtie \in \{=,>,<,\ge,\le\}$. For such a set $S$, let $b_i(S)$ denote its $i$-th Betti number (rank of the singular homology group $H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$), and let $\chi(S) = \sum_i (-1)^i b_i(S)$ denote its Euler–Poincaré characteristic.

Empirically, in algorithmic real algebraic geometry, computing $\chi(S)$ and the lowest Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_\ell(S)$ for fixed small $\ell$, as well as the highest ones (via Alexander duality), can be done with substantially better complexity bounds than computing the "middle" Betti numbers $b_i(S)$ for $i$ near $\dim(S)/2$.

Question. Establish a complexity-theoretic hardness separation that justifies this gap. Concretely:

(a) Prove (or disprove) that there is a complexity class $\mathcal{C}$ (e.g., $\#\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{PSPACE}$, or a real analogue thereof) such that the problem of computing the middle Betti number $b_{\lfloor \dim(S)/2 \rfloor}(S)$ of a semi-algebraic set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ presented by polynomial inequalities is $\mathcal{C}$-hard, while computing $\chi(S)$ and the individual Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_\ell(S)$ for any fixed $\ell$ lies in a strictly weaker class (under a standard complexity-theoretic assumption).

(b) Identify a complexity-theoretic analogue of the phenomenon, well known for smooth projective complex varieties, that the middle cohomology contains essentially all of the topological information: namely, exhibit a reduction showing that, for semi-algebraic sets, computing all Betti numbers (or some natural complete topological invariant) reduces to computing the middle Betti numbers, thereby explaining why middle Betti numbers concentrate the computational difficulty.
category_tag: complexity of Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets
status_search_result: Partial progress exists: for semi-algebraic sets defined by quadratic inequalities, computing the $\ell$-th Betti number is known to be #P-hard when $\ell = O(\log k)$, while the first/top few Betti numbers and the Euler–Poincaré characteristic admit better (singly exponential or polynomial in restricted cases) algorithms. However, a clean general complexity-theoretic dichotomy proving that middle Betti numbers are intrinsically harder than the extreme ones for arbitrary semi-algebraic sets, and an analogue of the "middle cohomology contains all information" phenomenon from Hodge theory in the complexity setting, do not appear to be fully established.

original_question: Consider a semi-algebraic set in R^k defined by l quadratic inequalities. Can the number of connected components of such a set be computed by an algorithm with complexity k^O(l), or even k^O(l^2), rather than the currently best known k^(2^O(l)) type bound coming from the available all-Betti-number methods? Equivalently, is there a substantially more efficient algorithm for counting connected components in the quadratic case than the general-purpose approach currently provides?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set defined by a Boolean combination (or, in the basic case, a conjunction) of $\ell$ quadratic inequalities
$$P_1(x_1,\dots,x_k) \,\Box_1\, 0,\ \dots,\ P_\ell(x_1,\dots,x_k) \,\Box_\ell\, 0,$$
where each $P_i \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_k]$ has total degree at most $2$ and each $\Box_i \in \{\le, <, =\}$. The number of connected components of $S$ is denoted $b_0(S)$.

Background facts (assumed known):
(a) There exist algorithms that decide whether $S$ is empty and that compute at least one sample point in every connected component of $S$ in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
(b) There exists an algorithm that computes the Euler–Poincaré characteristic $\chi(S)$ in time $k^{O(\ell)}$.
(c) The currently best known algorithm for computing $b_0(S)$ runs in time $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$, obtained as a special case of an algorithm computing all the Betti numbers of $S$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given such an $S$, computes the number of connected components $b_0(S)$ in time $k^{O(\ell)}$, or at least $k^{O(\ell^2)}$, thereby substantially improving on the current $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$ bound?
status_search_result: As of recent surveys on algorithmic real algebraic geometry, polynomial-time (in fact $k^{O(\ell)}$-type) algorithms are known for emptiness, sample points, Euler–Poincaré characteristic, and the top few Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets defined by $\ell$ quadratic inequalities, but the best known complexity for computing $b_0$ (number of connected components) in this setting is still $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$, inherited from the all-Betti-numbers algorithm. No published algorithm appears to achieve $k^{O(\ell)}$ or $k^{O(\ell^2)}$ for $b_0$ specifically, so the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Improve roadmap complexity for general sets
original_question: For a general semi-algebraic set, can the exponent O(k^2) in the complexity of roadmap algorithms be improved to O(k), so that testing connectivity has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness? More broadly, can one design roadmap or connecting-path algorithms whose complexity improvement would also yield sharper effective bounds on the lengths of semi-algebraic connecting paths?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $R$ be a real closed field and let $S \subseteq R^k$ be a semi-algebraic set described by a quantifier-free Boolean combination of $s$ polynomial (in)equalities of degree at most $d$ in $k$ variables. 

- Testing emptiness of $S$ can be done with algebraic complexity $s^{k+1} d^{O(k)}$ (single-exponential, with a linear exponent in $k$).
- A roadmap of $S$ is a semi-algebraic subset $M \subseteq S$ of dimension at most $1$ such that (i) every connected component of $S$ contains a connected component of $M$, and (ii) for every connected component $C$ of $S$, the intersection $M \cap C$ is connected. A roadmap allows one to decide connectivity of $S$ and to construct semi-algebraic paths connecting two given points within the same connected component.
- The known deterministic roadmap algorithms for general semi-algebraic sets have algebraic complexity $s^{k+1} d^{O(k^2)}$, i.e. the exponent in $d$ is quadratic in $k$.

Problems.

(1) Design a roadmap (or, more generally, a connectivity-and-connecting-path) algorithm for an arbitrary semi-algebraic set $S \subseteq R^k$ defined by $s$ polynomials of degree at most $d$ whose algebraic complexity is bounded by $s^{k+1} d^{O(k)}$, so that deciding connectivity of $S$ has asymptotically the same single-exponential complexity (with linear exponent in $k$) as deciding emptiness.

(2) Using such an algorithm, derive a corresponding sharper effective upper bound on the degree (in the sense of complexity of a semi-algebraic description) and combinatorial size of semi-algebraic paths connecting two points lying in the same connected component of $S$, matching the improved roadmap complexity.
category_tag: Roadmap algorithms in real algebraic geometry
status_search_result: The problem remains an active research direction with significant partial progress. For real algebraic sets (a special case), algorithms with complexity $d^{O(k\sqrt{k})}$ have been obtained (Safey El Din–Schost; Basu–Roy baby-step/giant-step roadmaps), improving on the classical $d^{O(k^2)}$, and recent work has extended these to unbounded smooth real algebraic sets. For general semi-algebraic sets, however, no roadmap algorithm with complexity $s^{k+1} d^{O(k)}$ matching the emptiness-testing exponent is known; the best general bounds still have a superlinear exponent in $k$. Thus the problem is partially solved (algebraic case improved to $d^{O(k\sqrt{k})}$) but in the form posed (linear exponent $O(k)$ for general semi-algebraic sets) it appears open.

original_question: Let Ω be an open connected subset of C^n, and let Γ: Ω -> C^n be a holomorphic mapping such that the maximal rank of its Jacobian DΓ is an integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1. For each point ξ in the maximal-rank set Ω^(k) = {ξ in Ω : rank DΓ(ξ) = k}, assume the level set Γ^{-1}(Γ(ξ)) is an affine (n-k)-dimensional space through ξ, equivalently of the form ξ + κ(ξ) where κ(ξ) = ker DΓ(ξ). Under these hypotheses, when does the resulting affine fibration extend analytically from Ω^(k) to all of Ω?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be an open connected set and let $\Gamma : \Omega \to \mathbb{C}^n$ be a holomorphic mapping. Set
$$ k := \max_{\xi \in \Omega} \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi), $$
and assume $1 \le k \le n-1$. Let
$$ \Omega^{(k)} := \{\xi \in \Omega : \operatorname{rank} D\Gamma(\xi) = k\}, $$
which is open and dense in $\Omega$. For $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$ write $\kappa(\xi) := \ker D\Gamma(\xi) \subset \mathbb{C}^n$, an $(n-k)$-dimensional linear subspace depending holomorphically on $\xi$ on $\Omega^{(k)}$. Assume further that for every $\xi \in \Omega^{(k)}$ the level set
$$ \Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) = \{\eta \in \Omega : \Gamma(\eta) = \Gamma(\xi)\} $$
is an affine $(n-k)$-dimensional plane through $\xi$, so that
$$ \Gamma^{-1}(\Gamma(\xi)) = (\xi + \kappa(\xi)) \cap \Omega. $$

In this way, on $\Omega^{(k)}$ one obtains an analytic affine fibration $\xi \mapsto \xi + \kappa(\xi)$ by $(n-k)$-dimensional affine subspaces. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which this affine fibration extends analytically from $\Omega^{(k)}$ to all of $\Omega$; equivalently, characterize when the holomorphic family $\xi \mapsto \kappa(\xi)$ of kernels (viewed as a holomorphic map from $\Omega^{(k)}$ into the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(n-k, n)$) admits a holomorphic extension to $\Omega$ giving an affine fibration of $\Omega$ whose fibers contain those of $\Gamma$ on $\Omega^{(k)}$.
category_tag: Several complex variables: analytic extension of foliations
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return clear authoritative information about the resolution status of this extension problem for affine fibrations arising from holomorphic maps with affine level sets. Without reliable evidence, the current status is reported as unknown.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
context_brief: A-local reflexivity for maximal Banach ideals
original_question: Let (A, A) be an arbitrary maximal Banach ideal. Must the principle of A-local reflexivity always hold? Concretely, for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every finite-dimensional subspace F of Y', every operator T in L(E, Y''), and every epsilon > 0, does there always exist an operator S in L(E, Y) such that A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T), the pairing identity <Sx, y'> = <y', Tx> holds for all (x, y') in E x F, and j_Y Sx = Tx for every x in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y))? Equivalently, is there any maximal Banach ideal for which this A-LRP factorization property fails?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ be a maximal Banach operator ideal. Recall that an operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ assigns to every pair of Banach spaces $X, Y$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y) \subseteq L(X,Y)$ together with an ideal norm $A(\cdot)$, and is called maximal if for every $T \in L(X,Y)$ one has $A(T) = \sup\{ A(Q_F T J_E) : E \subseteq X \text{ finite-dimensional}, F \subseteq Y \text{ finite-codimensional}\}$, where $J_E : E \hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion and $Q_F : Y \to Y/F$ is the quotient map (so $A$ is determined by its values on finite-rank operators between finite-dimensional spaces and extended by this supremum formula).

For a Banach space $Y$, let $j_Y : Y \hookrightarrow Y''$ denote the canonical embedding into the bidual.

Definition (principle of $A$-local reflexivity, $A$-LRP). The ideal $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ is said to satisfy the principle of $A$-local reflexivity if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F \subseteq Y'$, every operator $T \in L(E, Y'')$, and every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists an operator $S \in L(E, Y)$ such that:
  (i) $A(S) \le (1 + \varepsilon)\, A(T)$;
  (ii) $\langle Sx, y' \rangle = \langle y', Tx \rangle$ for all $(x, y') \in E \times F$;
  (iii) $j_Y(Sx) = Tx$ for every $x \in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y))$.

Question. Does every maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ satisfy the principle of $A$-local reflexivity? Equivalently, does there exist a maximal Banach ideal for which the above factorization property fails?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the A-local reflexivity question for arbitrary maximal Banach ideals. The problem is closely tied to the long-standing question of whether every maximal Banach ideal is accessible, which remains open in the literature on operator ideals. No source found establishes either a positive answer for all maximal ideals or an explicit counterexample.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two conditions equivalent: first, that (A, A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every operator T in L(E, Y), and every epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and an operator S in L(E, N) with T = J_N^Y S and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T); and second, that (A, A) satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle described in Definition 1.1?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A pair $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ is called a Banach operator ideal if $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq \mathfrak{L}$ is an operator ideal in the sense of Pietsch and $A$ is a complete ideal norm on $\mathfrak{A}$. For Banach spaces $E,F$, write $\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ for the component of the ideal and $A(\cdot)$ for its norm. The maximal hull $(\mathfrak{A}^{\max}, A^{\max})$ of $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is defined by
$$A^{\max}(T) := \sup\{ A(Q_L^F T J_M^E) : M\subseteq E\text{ finite-dimensional},\ L\subseteq F\text{ finite-codimensional}\},$$
where $J_M^E:M\hookrightarrow E$ is the inclusion and $Q_L^F:F\twoheadrightarrow F/L$ the quotient map; $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called maximal if $(\mathfrak{A},A)=(\mathfrak{A}^{\max},A^{\max})$.

For a Banach space $Y$ and a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$, let $J_N^Y:N\hookrightarrow Y$ be the canonical inclusion.

Right-accessibility. A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called right-accessible if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,Y)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$ and an operator $S\in\mathfrak{L}(E,N)$ such that
$$T = J_N^Y\, S \qquad\text{and}\qquad A(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)\, A(T).$$

The $A$-local reflexivity principle ($A$-LRP). A maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is said to satisfy the $A$-local reflexivity principle if for every Banach space $X$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq X^{**}$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subseteq X^*$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an operator $R:M\to X$ such that:
(a) $\langle R x^{**},\,x^*\rangle = \langle x^{**},\,x^*\rangle$ for all $x^{**}\in M$ and all $x^*\in F$;
(b) $R x^{**}=x^{**}$ for every $x^{**}\in M\cap X$ (under the canonical embedding $X\hookrightarrow X^{**}$);
(c) for every Banach space $Z$ and every $T\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,X^{**})$ with $T(Z)\subseteq M$, the operator $R\circ T\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,X)$ satisfies $A(R\circ T)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,A(T)$.

It is known that every right-accessible maximal Banach ideal satisfies the $A$-LRP.

Question.

Let $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(i) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible.
(ii) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the $A$-local reflexivity principle.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or counterexample establishing the equivalence between right-accessibility and the A-local reflexivity principle for maximal Banach ideals. Related work by Oertel and others addresses accessibility properties and extensions of finite-rank operators, but the specific equivalence appears not to have been resolved in the sources retrieved. Status is therefore unverified.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (A_P, A_P) be Pisier's explicitly constructed maximal Banach ideal that is known not to be right-accessible. Does this specific ideal nevertheless satisfy the A_P-local reflexivity principle? That is, does the A-LRP from Definition 1.1 hold when A is specialized to A_P?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is a subclass $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ together with an ideal norm $\mathbf{A}$ such that, for every pair of Banach spaces $E,F$, the component $\mathfrak{A}(E,F):=\mathfrak{A}\cap\mathfrak{L}(E,F)$ is a Banach space under $\mathbf{A}$, satisfies the ideal property $\mathbf{A}(BTC)\le\|B\|\,\mathbf{A}(T)\,\|C\|$ for all composable bounded operators $B,C$ and all $T\in\mathfrak{A}$, and contains all finite rank operators with $\mathbf{A}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\,\|y\|$.

A Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is called maximal if for every operator $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,F)$ one has $T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ with $\mathbf{A}(T)=\sup\mathbf{A}(Q_LTJ_M)$, where the supremum is over all finite-codimensional closed subspaces $L\subseteq F$ and finite-dimensional subspaces $M\subseteq E$, $J_M$ is the inclusion and $Q_L$ the quotient map.

The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ is called right-accessible if for every operator $T:E\to F$ between Banach spaces with $E$ finite-dimensional, every $S\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional Banach space $G$, an operator $S_0\in\mathfrak{A}(E,G)$, and an operator $R\in\mathfrak{L}(G,F)$ with $\|R\|\le 1$ such that $S=R S_0$ and $\mathbf{A}(S_0)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(S)$.

For a Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},\mathbf{A})$ we say the $\mathfrak{A}$-local reflexivity principle ($\mathfrak{A}$-LRP) holds if for every Banach space $E$, every Banach space $F$, every $T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F^{**})$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq E$, every finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq F^{*}$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\widetilde T\in\mathfrak{A}(E,F)$ with $\mathbf{A}(\widetilde T)\le(1+\varepsilon)\mathbf{A}(T)$ such that $\widetilde T x=Tx$ on the weak-$*$ closure-sense for $x\in M$ in the duality with $N$, i.e. $\langle \widetilde T x, y'\rangle=\langle Tx,y'\rangle$ for all $x\in M$ and $y'\in N$.

In 1993 G. Pisier constructed an explicit maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P)$ which is not right-accessible.

Question. Does the maximal Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A}_P,\mathbf{A}_P)$ satisfy the $\mathfrak{A}_P$-LRP?

The question appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible via search, but no authoritative confirmation of its current status was found.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
context_brief: Normed product ideal with L2 factor
original_question: Does the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 admit an ideal norm? Equivalently, is the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 normed?
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Work in the category of operators between Banach spaces. For Banach spaces $E,F$ let $\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ denote the Banach space of all bounded linear operators from $E$ into $F$. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ (in the sense of Pietsch) assigns to every pair $(E,F)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(E,F)\subseteq \mathcal{L}(E,F)$ containing all finite-rank operators and stable under composition with bounded operators on either side. A quasi-norm $A$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ making $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ a quasi-Banach ideal is called an ideal quasi-norm; if it is a norm satisfying $A(SRT)\le \|S\|\,A(R)\,\|T\|$ and $A(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{K}})=1$, then $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is a Banach (or normed) operator ideal.

Given two quasi-Banach operator ideals $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ and $(\mathfrak{B},B)$, their product $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ consists of all operators $T\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ that admit a factorization $T=RS$ with $S\in\mathfrak{B}(E,G)$ and $R\in\mathfrak{A}(G,F)$ for some Banach space $G$. The natural quasi-norm on $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ is
$$ (A\circ B)(T) \;=\; \inf\{A(R)\,B(S) : T=RS\}, $$
which is in general only a quasi-norm. One says that the product ideal $\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}$ is normed (admits an ideal norm) if there exists an ideal norm on it equivalent to $A\circ B$ turning it into a Banach operator ideal.

Let $\mathfrak{L}_1$ denote the Banach ideal of absolutely $1$-summing operators, $\mathfrak{L}_2$ the Banach ideal of absolutely $2$-summing operators, and $\mathfrak{L}_\infty$ the Banach ideal of all bounded linear operators. For a quasi-Banach ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$, write $(\mathfrak{A}^{**},A^{**})$ for its bidual ideal in the sense of Pietsch.

Question. Set $\mathfrak{A} := (\mathfrak{L}_1\circ \mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}$. Does the product operator ideal
$$ \mathfrak{A}\circ \mathfrak{L}_2 \;=\; (\mathfrak{L}_1\circ \mathfrak{L}_\infty)^{**}\circ\mathfrak{L}_2 $$
admit an ideal norm; equivalently, is this product ideal normed?
status_search_result: A 2001 preprint by Oertel ("On normed products of operator ideals which contain L_2 as a factor") raises and studies precisely this type of question, and a 2007 note by the same author lists Problem 2.4 (the question above) as still open, noting that no known criteria suffice to establish such an ideal norm on a product of quasi-Banach ideals. No subsequent published resolution was located.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does the product ideal C2* ◦ L∞ have property (I), meaning that for every epsilon > 0 and every finite-rank operator L in C2* ◦ L∞, one can factor L = AB so that A(A) B(B) <= (1 + epsilon) (C2* ◦ L∞)(L) and one of the factors has finite-dimensional range?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach operator ideal is a pair (A, A(·)) consisting of a class A of bounded linear operators between arbitrary Banach spaces, together with a complete ideal norm A(·), in the sense of Pietsch.

For Banach operator ideals (A, A(·)) and (B, B(·)), the product ideal A ∘ B is defined by L ∈ A ∘ B if and only if L admits a factorization L = AB with B ∈ B and A ∈ A; the product ideal norm is
   (A ∘ B)(L) := inf { A(A) · B(B) : L = AB, A ∈ A, B ∈ B }.

Definition (property (I)). The product ideal A ∘ B is said to have property (I) if for every ε > 0 and every finite-rank operator L ∈ A ∘ B there exists a factorization L = AB with A ∈ A, B ∈ B such that
   A(A) · B(B) ≤ (1 + ε) · (A ∘ B)(L)
and such that the operator A has finite-dimensional range.

Let (C₂, C₂(·)) denote the maximal injective Banach operator ideal of all cotype-2 operators (the operator-ideal analogue of the Banach-space class of cotype 2), and let C₂* denote its adjoint (dual) Banach operator ideal. Let (L∞, L∞(·)) denote the maximal Banach operator ideal of all L∞-factorable operators.

Question. Does the product ideal C₂* ∘ L∞ have property (I)?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of whether C₂* ∘ L∞ has property (I). Related work establishes property (I) and (S) for product ideals containing L₂ as a factor, but the specific case C₂* ∘ L∞ does not appear to have been settled in the accessible literature.

paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
original_question: Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal, and let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B*(X0, Y0) is not contained in L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ has property (I), does it already follow that the B-LRP is not satisfied, even without assuming that B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible? In other words, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on B ◦ L∞ be removed from this implication?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Work in the category of Banach spaces and bounded linear operators. For Banach spaces $X,Y$, let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the Banach space of bounded linear operators $X\to Y$, and let $\mathcal{F}(X,Y)$ denote the finite-rank operators. A Banach (operator) ideal $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ assigns to each pair $(X,Y)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ containing $\mathcal{F}(X,Y)$, equipped with a norm $\mathbf{B}$ such that $(\mathfrak{B}(X,Y),\mathbf{B})$ is a Banach space, $\mathbf{B}(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\,\|y\|$, and the two-sided ideal property holds with respect to bounded operators. The adjoint ideal is $(\mathfrak{B}^*,\mathbf{B}^*)$, and $\mathfrak{B}$ is called maximal if it coincides isometrically with its bidual ideal in the sense of Pietsch. Let $\mathcal{L}_2$ denote the ideal of operators factoring through a Hilbert space (the $\gamma_2$-ideal), and $\mathcal{L}_\infty$ the maximal Banach ideal of $\mathcal{L}_\infty$-factorable operators. The composition ideal $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ is the Banach ideal whose component on $(X,Y)$ consists of operators that factor as $T=B\circ S$ with $S\in\mathcal{L}_\infty(X,Z)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{B}(Z,Y)$ for some Banach space $Z$, equipped with the natural infimum norm.

Recall that a Banach space $X$ has cotype $2$ if there exists $C>0$ such that $\big(\sum_i \|x_i\|^2\big)^{1/2}\le C\,\big(\mathbb{E}\|\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_i\|^2\big)^{1/2}$ for all finite families $(x_i)$ in $X$, where $(\varepsilon_i)$ are independent Rademacher variables. A Banach ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is right-accessible if for every finite-rank operator $L\in\mathcal{F}(M,Y)$ from a finite-dimensional space $M$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional space $N$, an operator $A\in\mathcal{L}(M,N)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{A}(N,Y)$ with $L=B\circ A$ and $\|A\|\,\mathbf{A}(B)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,\mathbf{A}(L)$. The ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to have property (I) if for all Banach spaces $X,Y$ the natural inclusion $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)\hookrightarrow\mathfrak{A}^{**}(X,Y)$ is an isometric embedding into the maximal hull. The Banach ideal $\mathfrak{B}$ is said to satisfy the $\mathfrak{B}$-Limit Order Right Property ($\mathfrak{B}$-LRP) if a certain right-sided factorization/limit-order condition holds (the precise definition being the standard one used in the geometry of maximal Banach ideals).

Problem. Let $(\mathfrak{B},\mathbf{B})$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Let $X_0$ and $Y_0$ be Banach spaces such that $X_0'$ and $Y_0$ are of cotype $2$ and $\mathfrak{B}^*(X_0,Y_0)\not\subseteq \mathcal{L}_2(X_0,Y_0)$. Suppose that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ has property (I). Does it follow that the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP fails, without assuming that $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ is right-accessible? Equivalently, can the hypothesis of right-accessibility of $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$ be removed from the known implication that, under the above hypotheses together with right-accessibility of $\mathfrak{B}\circ\mathcal{L}_\infty$, the $\mathfrak{B}$-LRP is not satisfied?
status_search_result: No follow-up resolution was located. The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the literature on the geometry of operator ideals, and no subsequent published work could be verified to remove the right-accessibility hypothesis. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on the real line with initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x), where u_0 is almost periodic in x. McKean and Trubowitz proved that periodic initial data produce solutions that are almost periodic in time. Does the same conclusion hold for almost periodic initial data, and more fundamentally can one establish short-time existence and then understand the associated spectral theory of the Schrödinger operator H(t) = -d^2/dx^2 + u(x,t) for general almost periodic potentials well enough to analyze the KdV evolution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation
  u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t ∈ ℝ,
with initial condition u(x,0) = u_0(x), where u_0 : ℝ → ℝ is an almost periodic function (i.e., u_0 lies in the closure, in the uniform norm on ℝ, of the set of trigonometric polynomials Σ c_j e^{i ξ_j x}).

It is known (McKean–Trubowitz) that when u_0 is periodic, the resulting KdV solution exists globally and is almost periodic in time, with the spectrum of the Schrödinger operator H(t) = −d^2/dx^2 + u(·,t) being preserved under the flow.

Address the following for general almost periodic initial data u_0:

(a) Prove short-time existence of a classical solution u(x,t) of the above Cauchy problem in the class of functions that are almost periodic in x for each t in some interval (−T, T), T > 0.

(b) Develop the spectral theory of the family of Schrödinger operators H(t) = −d^2/dx^2 + u(·,t), acting on L^2(ℝ), for almost periodic potentials u(·,t), to a degree sufficient to track the KdV evolution (in particular, isospectrality of H(t)).

(c) Show that the resulting solution u(x,t) is almost periodic in t, thereby extending the McKean–Trubowitz periodic-in-time result from periodic to almost periodic initial data.
category_tag: KdV with almost periodic initial data
status_search_result: The problem (often called the Deift conjecture) has been settled in important cases but not in full generality. Damanik–Goldstein (2014) established short-time existence and uniqueness for quasi-periodic initial data with exponentially decaying Fourier coefficients, and global existence/uniqueness for small analytic quasi-periodic data with Diophantine frequency. Binder–Damanik–Goldstein–Lukic (Duke Math. J., 2018) proved almost periodicity in time of KdV solutions for a class of almost periodic initial data whose associated Schrödinger operators have absolutely continuous, not-too-thin spectrum, including all small analytic quasi-periodic data with Diophantine frequency. The full conjecture for general almost periodic initial data remains open.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For random matrix ensembles with symmetry classes β=1 and β=4, prove bulk and edge universality for general potentials of the form Q(x)=N V(x), especially when the associated equilibrium measure is supported on several disjoint intervals, rather than only for the already understood polynomial-potential cases with one-cut support. More broadly, determine whether the newer methods developed for unitary ensembles can be adapted to these orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, and resolve the long-standing conjecture that Wigner matrices also exhibit bulk universality.
self_contained_problem:
Consider invariant random matrix ensembles on the spaces of N×N real symmetric (β=1), complex Hermitian (β=2), or quaternion self-dual (β=4) matrices, with joint eigenvalue density proportional to

  ∏_{i<j} |x_i − x_j|^β · exp(−∑_{k=1}^N Q(x_k)),

where Q(x) = N V(x) and V : ℝ → ℝ is a sufficiently regular (e.g. real-analytic or polynomial) confining potential. Let μ_V denote the associated equilibrium measure, i.e. the unique minimizer of

  I[μ] = ∫∫ log(1/|x−y|) dμ(x) dμ(y) + ∫ V(x) dμ(x)

over Borel probability measures on ℝ. Assume the support of μ_V consists of finitely many disjoint intervals (the multi-cut regime).

(a) For β = 1 and β = 4, prove bulk universality: after appropriate rescaling around any point in the interior of the support of μ_V, the local k-point correlation functions of the eigenvalues converge, as N → ∞, to the universal limits given by the standard β=1 and β=4 sine kernels (respectively the Pfaffian sine kernels of the GOE and GSE).

(b) For β = 1 and β = 4, prove edge universality: after appropriate rescaling around any soft edge of the support of μ_V, the local correlation functions converge to the universal β=1 and β=4 Airy (Pfaffian Airy) kernels.

(c) Determine whether the techniques developed for unitary (β=2) ensembles—in particular Riemann–Hilbert methods—can be adapted so as to establish (a) and (b) in this multi-cut, general-potential setting.

(d) (Wigner bulk universality.) Let H = (H_{ij}) be an N×N real symmetric or Hermitian Wigner matrix whose entries above the diagonal are i.i.d. (with appropriate symmetry) random variables of mean zero, variance 1/N, and suitable moment conditions. Prove that the bulk local eigenvalue statistics of H, in the limit N → ∞, coincide with those of the GOE (resp. GUE).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. Wigner bulk universality (part d) has been resolved by Erdős–Schlein–Yau and independently Tao–Vu (around 2010–2012). For invariant β=1, 4 ensembles, bulk and edge universality have been established for one-cut regular potentials of class C⁴ or analytic (Shcherbina; Bourgade–Erdős–Yau; Krishnapur–Rider–Virág; Deift–Gioev and others), and Laguerre-type analogues are known. The full multi-cut case for general (non-polynomial) potentials in β=1, 4 is partially understood but not completely resolved in the generality stated.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Extend the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems with oscillatory data of the form e^{i n φ(z)} r(z) as n→∞ to the case where the phase function φ is not analytic but has only finite smoothness. The goal is to recover asymptotic control of the associated equilibrium measure and contour deformations without the analyticity assumption that current theory relies on.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{C}$ be an oriented contour and consider a family of $2\times 2$ matrix-valued Riemann–Hilbert problems indexed by $n\in\mathbb{N}$: find $M_n:\mathbb{C}\setminus\Sigma\to GL_2(\mathbb{C})$ such that
\[ M_{n,+}(z) = M_{n,-}(z)\,J_n(z),\quad z\in\Sigma,\qquad M_n(z)\to I\ \text{as}\ z\to\infty, \]
where the jump matrix has the oscillatory form
\[ J_n(z) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \overline{r(z)}\,e^{-in\varphi(z)} \\ r(z)\,e^{in\varphi(z)} & 1+|r(z)|^2 \end{pmatrix} \]
(or a closely related factorized form), with reflection coefficient $r$ and real-valued phase $\varphi$.

The Deift–Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method provides, as $n\to\infty$, asymptotics for $M_n$ via:
(i) the construction of a $g$-function and an associated equilibrium measure determining the relevant signature regions of $\operatorname{Re}(i\varphi)$;
(ii) lensing/contour deformations of $\Sigma$ into steepest-descent contours where the off-diagonal entries decay; and
(iii) local parametrices at stationary/critical points matched to a global parametrix.

All standard implementations of this scheme assume that $\varphi$ is real-analytic in a neighborhood of $\Sigma$, so that the deformations and analytic continuations in (ii) are available.

Problem. Develop a version of the nonlinear steepest descent method that yields the same asymptotic control of $M_n$ — including a workable analogue of the equilibrium measure, the $g$-function transformations, the contour deformations, and the local parametrix construction — under the weaker hypothesis that the phase $\varphi$ has only a finite number of derivatives (i.e. $\varphi\in C^k$ for some finite $k$, with $r$ likewise of finite smoothness) rather than being analytic. In particular, identify the minimal smoothness on $\varphi$ and $r$ under which leading-order (and subleading) large-$n$ asymptotics for $M_n$ can be rigorously established.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made on relaxing the analyticity hypothesis. Varzugin extended Deift–Zhou to a restricted class of non-analytic phases, and the $\bar\partial$-steepest descent method (McLaughlin–Miller and later authors) handles substantially broader non-analytic settings by replacing analytic continuation with $\bar\partial$-extensions. However, sharp characterizations of the minimal finite smoothness required for full asymptotic control remain incomplete, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory for the six Painlevé equations, analogous in spirit to the Bateman project or Abramowitz-Stegun for classical special functions. In particular, build dependable software and accompanying asymptotic and algebraic infrastructure for computing Painlevé transcendents, such as determining features like the pole locations in the complex plane for the Painlevé II solution asymptotic to the Airy function as x→+∞.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic and computationally reliable theory of the six Painlevé equations P_I, P_II, P_III, P_IV, P_V, P_VI, comparable in scope and dependability to classical handbooks of special functions (such as the Bateman manuscript project or the Abramowitz–Stegun Handbook). The theory should provide:

1. A unified algebraic and analytic infrastructure (Hamiltonian forms, Bäcklund transformations, isomonodromic representations, connection formulas, Riemann–Hilbert problems, classical and rational solutions, parameter symmetries) sufficient to characterize and tabulate the Painlevé transcendents.
2. Reliable asymptotic expansions of solutions in all directions of the complex plane, including the connection problem relating asymptotic data at different critical points.
3. Robust numerical software that, given initial/asymptotic data identifying a particular Painlevé transcendent, computes its values throughout the complex plane to controlled accuracy and locates its singularities.

As a concrete benchmark within this program, consider the Hastings–McLeod-type setting for the second Painlevé equation
   u''(x) = 2 u(x)^3 + x u(x),
and let u(x) be the unique real solution satisfying u(x) ~ Ai(x) as x → +∞, where Ai is the Airy function. Determine, by means of the developed theory and software, the locations in the complex x-plane of the poles of this solution u(x) (each of which is a simple pole with residue ±1), including their distribution and asymptotic pattern.
status_search_result: The Painlevé Project was launched (NIST e-site, DLMF Chapter 32) and substantial progress has been made: numerical Riemann–Hilbert based algorithms (Olver, Bornemann, Trogdon) compute Painlevé transcendents reliably in the complex plane, and pole distributions for the Hastings–McLeod and tronquée solutions of P_II have been studied (Fornberg–Weideman, Costin–Huang–Tanveer, Bertola–Bothner). However, a complete, comprehensive Bateman/Abramowitz–Stegun-style infrastructure with universally validated software for all six Painlevé equations is still an ongoing community effort rather than a finished project.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Let M be a p×n data matrix with p,n→∞ and p/n→γ∈(0,∞), and let S=(1/n) M̂ M̂^T be the centered sample covariance matrix whose ordered eigenvalues are l_1≥⋯≥l_p. For real Gaussian spiked covariance models, where the population covariance has eigenvalues η_1≥⋯≥η_k>η_{k+1}=⋯=η_p=1, determine the asymptotic distributions of the leading sample eigenvalues and describe the phase transitions analogous to the complex case, despite the absence of a real analogue of the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber formula.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a real Gaussian spiked covariance model in the following setting. For each pair $(p,n)$ with $p,n\to\infty$ and $p/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, let $X$ be a $p\times n$ matrix whose columns are i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$, where the population covariance $\Sigma$ has ordered eigenvalues
$$\eta_1\ge\eta_2\ge\cdots\ge\eta_k>\eta_{k+1}=\cdots=\eta_p=1$$
for some fixed $k\ge 1$ and fixed spike values $\eta_1,\dots,\eta_k$. Let $\hat X$ denote the column-centered version of $X$ and define the sample covariance matrix
$$S=\tfrac{1}{n}\hat X\hat X^{T},$$
with ordered eigenvalues $\ell_1\ge\ell_2\ge\cdots\ge\ell_p$.

Determine, for each fixed $i\le k$, the limiting distribution (after suitable centering and scaling) of the leading sample eigenvalue $\ell_i$ as $p,n\to\infty$ with $p/n\to\gamma$. In particular, identify the critical threshold $\eta_c(\gamma)$ governing the phase transition between the regime in which $\ell_i$ converges to the bulk edge with Tracy–Widom-type fluctuations and the regime in which $\ell_i$ separates from the bulk with Gaussian-type fluctuations, and describe the limiting laws on each side of the transition. The problem is to obtain such a complete real-case analogue of the known results for the complex Gaussian spiked model, despite the lack of a real analogue of the Harish-Chandra–Itzykson–Zuber integral formula.
status_search_result: The problem of asymptotic distributions and phase transitions for the leading eigenvalues of real Gaussian spiked sample covariance matrices has been substantially resolved in subsequent work. Bai–Yao, Paul, and Benaych-Georges–Nadakuditi established Gaussian fluctuations for supercritical spikes, while Bloemendal–Virág ("Limits of spiked random matrices I/II") and Mo determined Tracy–Widom-type laws at and below the BBP threshold $1+\sqrt{\gamma}$ in the real case, providing real analogues of the complex results.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For general β-ensembles, equivalently log gases at inverse temperature β>0, use the stochastic Schrödinger operator H_β = d^2/dx^2 - x - √(2/β) dB(x)/dx on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0 to obtain structural information about the edge statistics of the ensemble. In particular, derive the Tracy-Widom distribution for the top eigenvalue in the case β=2 directly from H_β.
self_contained_problem:
For each inverse temperature parameter β>0, consider the log-gas (general β-ensemble) on the real line with joint density proportional to ∏_{i<j}|x_i−x_j|^β exp(−(β/4)∑_i x_i^2), and let λ_1(N;β) denote the largest particle in the N-particle ensemble (suitably centered and rescaled at the soft edge by 2√N + N^{−1/6}·).

Define the stochastic Airy (Schrödinger) operator
   H_β = −d^2/dx^2 + x + (2/√β) dB(x)/dx,
acting on L^2((0,∞)) with Dirichlet boundary condition at x=0, where dB/dx is standard one-dimensional white noise. Let Λ_1(β) ≤ Λ_2(β) ≤ … denote the (almost surely well-defined, discrete, simple) spectrum of H_β, and define the Tracy–Widom_β distribution by TW_β(t) = P(−Λ_1(β) ≤ t).

(a) Use the operator H_β to extract structural information about the edge statistics of the β-ensemble; in particular, show that the rescaled top eigenvalue of the β-ensemble converges in distribution to −Λ_1(β).

(b) In the case β=2, derive the classical Tracy–Widom GUE formula
   F_2(t) = exp(−∫_t^∞ (s−t) q(s)^2 ds),
where q solves the Painlevé II equation q''(s) = s q(s) + 2 q(s)^3 with q(s) ~ Ai(s) as s→∞, directly from the stochastic operator H_2 (rather than via determinantal/Hermitian-matrix kernel techniques).
status_search_result: Ramírez–Rider–Virág (J. Amer. Math. Soc., 2011) proved that the rescaled top eigenvalues of general β-ensembles converge to the low eigenvalues of the stochastic Airy operator H_β, and characterized the resulting Tracy–Widom_β laws via a one-dimensional diffusion (explosion probability). This resolves part (a) and gives a stochastic-operator characterization of TW_β for all β>0. However, a direct derivation of the classical Fredholm-determinant / Painlevé II Tracy–Widom formula F_2 specifically from H_2 (without invoking determinantal/Hermite kernel methods) does not appear to be established; subsequent works (e.g., right-tail asymptotics by Ramírez–Rider–Virág and tail analyses) give partial information but not the full explicit β=2 formula directly from H_β. The problem is therefore partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop theoretical and numerical methods that can determine where, and at what rate, the eigenvalues of important non-self-adjoint operators accumulate in the complex plane. A central example is the AKNS operator arising in the semiclassical focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation, where the spectrum off the real axis is discrete but the numerical range is open and the relevant spectral computation is unstable beyond all algebraic orders in the semiclassical parameter h.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the semiclassical regime
$$ i h\, \partial_t \psi + \tfrac{h^2}{2}\, \partial_x^2 \psi + |\psi|^2 \psi = 0, \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},\ t\ge 0, $$
with small parameter $h>0$ and initial data $\psi(x,0)=A(x)\exp\!\big(\tfrac{i}{h} S(x)\big)$ for smooth real-valued functions $A,S$ with $A$ rapidly decaying. The associated AKNS (Zakharov–Shabat) scattering operator is the non-self-adjoint first-order system
$$ \mathcal{L}_h \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix} = \lambda \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal{L}_h := \begin{pmatrix} -i h\,\partial_x & i\, q(x) \\ i\,\overline{q(x)} & i h\,\partial_x \end{pmatrix}, $$
where $q(x) = A(x) e^{i S(x)/h}$. For generic such potentials the spectrum of $\mathcal{L}_h$ off the real axis consists of discrete eigenvalues $\{\lambda_j(h)\}\subset\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}$, while the numerical range of $\mathcal{L}_h$ is an open subset of the complex plane, and the standard numerical computation of these eigenvalues is unstable beyond all algebraic orders in $h$ (errors decay no faster than any power of $h$ but are dominated by exponentially small terms).

Develop theoretical and/or numerical methods to determine, in the limit $h\to 0^+$:

1. The asymptotic locus (curve, set, or measure) in $\mathbb{C}$ on which the eigenvalues $\lambda_j(h)$ of $\mathcal{L}_h$ accumulate, as a function of the data $(A,S)$.
2. The asymptotic rate (density) at which the eigenvalues populate this locus, including a quantitative description of the counting measure $\sum_j \delta_{\lambda_j(h)}$ as $h\to 0^+$.

The methods should be applicable to general (not necessarily analytic or exactly solvable) initial data $(A,S)$ and should overcome the instability of direct spectral computation for such non-self-adjoint operators.
status_search_result: The problem of locating and quantifying the accumulation of complex eigenvalues of the non-self-adjoint Zakharov–Shabat (AKNS) operator in the semiclassical focusing NLS limit remains an active area of research. Partial results exist for special classes of analytic potentials (e.g. WKB / Bohr–Sommerfeld-type quantization yielding accumulation along Stokes curves and "Y-shaped" sets, with $O(1/h)$ density), via works of Bronski, Klaus–Shaw, Fujiié–Kamvissis and others, but a general theory for arbitrary smooth data and stable numerical algorithms beyond all algebraic orders in $h$ has not been established.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Determine the long-time behavior of integrable systems when the initial data are non-generic and the associated Lax operator has singular spectral features not covered by the standard generic theory. In particular, for focusing nonlinear Schrödinger evolution, understand how spectra that accumulate on the real line at essentially arbitrary rates affect long-time asymptotics, and similarly clarify the situation for higher-order self-adjoint Lax operators such as those for the Boussinesq equation.
self_contained_problem:
Consider integrable nonlinear evolution equations whose Cauchy problems are solved via inverse scattering using a Lax pair, focusing on two cases.

(a) Focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Let q(x,t) satisfy
   i q_t + q_{xx} + 2|q|^2 q = 0,  x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
with initial data q(x,0) = q_0(x) decaying as |x| → ∞. The associated Lax operator is the Zakharov–Shabat operator
   L = i σ_3 ∂_x + ( 0, q_0(x); -\bar q_0(x), 0 ).
For "generic" initial data, the discrete spectrum of L consists of finitely many simple eigenvalues lying off the real axis, and the reflection coefficient is smooth on ℝ; in this case the long-time asymptotics of q(x,t) are known via nonlinear steepest descent. Consider instead non-generic initial data for which the spectrum exhibits singular features, in particular sequences of (possibly higher-order) eigenvalues accumulating on the real axis at arbitrary prescribed rates, and/or spectral singularities (poles of the scattering data on ℝ). Determine, as t → ∞, the leading-order asymptotic behavior of q(x,t) along all rays x/t = ξ ∈ ℝ in this non-generic regime, and identify how the rate of accumulation of eigenvalues on ℝ enters the asymptotic formulas and error terms.

(b) Boussinesq equation. Let u(x,t) satisfy the (good) Boussinesq equation
   u_{tt} = u_{xx} + (u^2)_{xx} + u_{xxxx},  x ∈ ℝ, t > 0,
with general decaying initial data (u(x,0), u_t(x,0)). The associated Lax operator is a third-order self-adjoint differential operator
   L = ∂_x^3 + ∂_x q(x,t) + q(x,t) ∂_x + p(x,t),
whose spectral theory is significantly more involved than that of second-order operators, with continuous spectrum on ℝ and possible embedded singularities. Determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of u(x,t) for general (not merely Schwartz-class or generic) initial data.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Using ∂̄-steepest descent, long-time asymptotics for focusing NLS have been extended to non-generic initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces, including the presence of high-order discrete spectrum (e.g., arXiv:2104.07301). Long-time asymptotics for the Boussinesq equation with Schwartz-class data have been obtained via nonlinear steepest descent methods. However, the fully general non-generic regime—covering eigenvalue sequences accumulating on the real axis at arbitrary rates, general spectral singularities for NLS, and general (non-Schwartz) initial data for Boussinesq—has not been completely resolved, so the problem remains only partially solved.
