paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Construct a microscopic mathematical model for parked-car spacing statistics on long streets that explains why empirical data exhibit random-matrix behavior and why two-way streets appear to show GUE statistics whereas left-side parking on one-way streets appears to show GOE statistics. The goal is an analogue, for parking, of the microscopic random-matrix explanation previously developed for the Cuernavaca bus problem.
self_contained_problem:
Empirical observations of parked-car positions along long urban streets indicate that, after appropriate normalization, the gaps between consecutive parked cars exhibit spacing statistics characteristic of random matrix ensembles: on two-way streets the empirical spacing distribution matches that of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE), while for left-side parking on one-way streets it matches that of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE).

Recall that for an N×N Hermitian matrix drawn from the GUE (respectively, real symmetric from the GOE), with eigenvalues λ_1 ≤ … ≤ λ_N rescaled so that the mean nearest-neighbor spacing in the bulk equals 1, the limiting nearest-neighbor spacing distribution p_β(s) (β=2 for GUE, β=1 for GOE) is well-approximated by the Wigner surmise p_β(s) = a_β s^β exp(−b_β s^2) with constants a_β, b_β fixed by normalization.

Recall also the Cuernavaca bus problem: for a bus line in Cuernavaca, Mexico, the spacings between consecutive buses passing a fixed checkpoint were observed to follow GUE statistics, and a microscopic stochastic model (in which independent drivers adjust their speeds to avoid being too close to the bus ahead, leading via a hard-core interaction to a determinantal point process with the sine-kernel correlations of GUE) was constructed which provably reproduces these statistics in an appropriate scaling limit.

Problem. Construct an analogous microscopic stochastic model for the positions of parked cars along a long street, based on plausible local rules describing how drivers choose parking spots given the positions of already-parked cars, with the following properties:

(a) The model is defined for both a "two-way street" variant and a "one-way street, left-side parking" variant, the only difference being the local rules / symmetry constraints reflecting the directional structure of the street.

(b) In an appropriate thermodynamic / large-street scaling limit, the rescaled point process of parked-car positions converges to a translation-invariant point process on ℝ whose nearest-neighbor spacing distribution coincides with the bulk GUE spacing distribution p_2(s) in the two-way case and with the bulk GOE spacing distribution p_1(s) in the one-way left-side case.

(c) The mechanism producing the change from β=2 to β=1 statistics is identified explicitly in terms of the symmetry of the underlying interaction (e.g. a time-reversal or reflection symmetry that is present in the one-way left-side rules but broken in the two-way rules).

Either exhibit such a model with proofs of the convergence claims in (b)–(c), or prove that no model in a specified natural class can reproduce both ensembles by symmetry breaking alone.

The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Find a probabilistic operation X on an i.i.d. sequence (a_1,a_2,...) that plays a role for random-matrix statistics analogous to summation in the classical central limit theorem: after applying X to the first n inputs, the resulting random variables should converge, as n→∞, to the Gaudin distribution or to a Tracy-Widom distribution. In other words, characterize random-matrix universality in purely probabilistic terms.
self_contained_problem:
Background. In classical probability, the central limit theorem identifies summation as the canonical probabilistic operation that, applied to an i.i.d. sequence with finite variance, produces (after centering and scaling) Gaussian limits in the large-n limit. In random matrix theory, the Gaudin distribution governs spacings between consecutive eigenvalues in the bulk of the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (or, more generally, of large Hermitian random matrices), and the Tracy–Widom distributions F_1, F_2, F_4 govern the fluctuations of the largest eigenvalue of GOE/GUE/GSE random matrices. Both Gaudin and Tracy–Widom limits are known to be universal: they arise in a wide variety of models (random matrices, longest increasing subsequences of random permutations, last-passage percolation, growth processes, etc.).

Problem. Exhibit a probabilistic operation X — a measurable map taking an i.i.d. sequence (a_1, a_2, …) of real-valued random variables (under some natural moment hypothesis, e.g. finite variance or finite fourth moment) and the integer n to a random variable X_n(a_1, …, a_n), or to a finite collection of such variables — with the following property: for every law of a_1 in the prescribed class, after suitable centering and scaling the random variables X_n(a_1, …, a_n) converge in distribution as n → ∞ to either the Gaudin spacing distribution or one of the Tracy–Widom distributions F_1, F_2, F_4. The operation X should be a genuine analogue of summation: it must be defined directly in probabilistic/combinatorial terms (without reference to a specific underlying random matrix model) and must produce the prescribed random-matrix limit universally over the class of input distributions. In other words, give a purely probabilistic characterization of random-matrix universality of Gaudin/Tracy–Widom type, parallel to the way summation characterizes Gaussian universality in the classical CLT.
status_search_result: The full problem of identifying a universal probabilistic operation X analogous to summation that produces Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits from arbitrary i.i.d. inputs is generally regarded as open. Important partial progress has been made: Baik–Suidan (2005) and Bodineau–Martin (2005) independently established GUE/Tracy–Widom universality for directed last-passage site percolation in thin rectangles under finite-moment assumptions, and a substantial subsequent literature (KPZ universality, invariance principles for last-passage percolation, etc.) has extended such results to wider classes. However, no fully general probabilistic operation X analogous to summation has been singled out that yields Tracy–Widom or Gaudin limits universally on all i.i.d. inputs.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Given a tridiagonal TE1 random matrix, equivalently Toda lattice initial data whose diagonal entries are independent Gaussians and whose off-diagonal entries have the corresponding χ-distributions, determine the average time required for the Toda flow to diagonalize the matrix to a prescribed accuracy ε. Equivalently, estimate the average time until the interacting Toda particles become asymptotically free, which in the algorithmic formulation can be taken as the time when the last off-diagonal entry b_{n-1}(t) drops below ε.
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let T = (T_{ij}) be a random real symmetric tridiagonal n×n matrix sampled from the following ensemble (the tridiagonal β=1 / TE1 ensemble): the diagonal entries T_{ii} (1 ≤ i ≤ n) are independent Gaussian random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and the off-diagonal entries b_i := T_{i,i+1} = T_{i+1,i} (1 ≤ i ≤ n−1) are independent (and independent of the diagonal) with b_i distributed as (1/√2) χ_{n−i}, where χ_k denotes the chi distribution with k degrees of freedom.

Let X(t) be the solution of the Toda lattice flow with initial condition X(0) = T, i.e. X(t) is the symmetric tridiagonal n×n matrix evolving according to
   dX/dt = [B(X), X],
where B(X) is the skew-symmetric matrix obtained from X by taking its strictly lower-triangular part minus its strictly upper-triangular part. Let b_i(t) denote the (i, i+1) entry of X(t).

For ε > 0 (the prescribed accuracy), define the halting time
   τ_n(ε) := inf{ t ≥ 0 : b_{n−1}(t) < ε }.

Determine the asymptotic behavior, as n → ∞ (and as a function of ε), of the expected halting time E[τ_n(ε)]. Equivalently, determine the average time required for the Toda flow with TE1 initial data to drive its last off-diagonal entry below the threshold ε, i.e. for the interacting Toda particles to become asymptotically free to within accuracy ε.
status_search_result: Empirical and theoretical work by Pfrang–Deift–Menon and Deift–Trogdon established universality for the (suitably normalized) deflation/halting time of the Toda algorithm on Wigner-class random matrices, showing that the limiting distribution depends only on the algorithm and not on the underlying ensemble or matrix size. However, a full rigorous determination of the average halting time E[τ_n(ε)] as a function of n and ε for the TE1 ensemble is described in the literature as still far from resolved, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Develop perturbation theory for infinite-dimensional integrable systems in settings where solitons are present and the perturbation no longer becomes asymptotically negligible. A central instance is the focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with an added perturbation term ε V(|u|)u, especially for solutions lying near k-soliton states with k≥2, together with a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics; related questions include the persistence of Toda shocks and rarefactions under perturbations and perturbations of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam problem.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the perturbed focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the real line,

  i u_t + u_{xx} + 2 |u|^2 u + ε V(|u|) u = 0,   x ∈ ℝ, t ≥ 0,

where ε > 0 is a small parameter and V: [0,∞) → ℝ is a smooth real-valued function such that the perturbation does not become asymptotically negligible as t → ∞ (i.e. solitonic structures of the unperturbed equation persist and interact with the perturbation). Recall that the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS (ε = 0) is completely integrable via inverse scattering and admits k-soliton solutions for every integer k ≥ 1.

Develop a perturbation theory for this equation in the regime where the initial data lie in a neighborhood of a k-soliton solution (k ≥ 2) of the unperturbed focusing cubic NLS. Specifically:

(a) Construct, for sufficiently small ε, the global solution u(x,t) of the perturbed equation with initial data near a prescribed k-soliton.

(b) Provide a detailed description of the long-time asymptotics of u(x,t) as t → ∞, including the modulation of soliton parameters (positions, velocities, amplitudes, phases), the interaction between solitons induced by the perturbation, the radiation component, and explicit error estimates.

In parallel, address the analogous problems of: (i) the persistence (or breakdown) of Toda shock and Toda rarefaction wave solutions of the Toda lattice under small Hamiltonian perturbations, and (ii) the perturbation theory of the sine-Gordon equation relevant to the Fermi–Pasta–Ulam problem, again with a description of long-time asymptotics in the presence of solitons.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., Borghese–Jenkins–McLaughlin and Cuccagna–Jenkins, and more recent ∂̄-steepest descent analyses) has produced detailed long-time asymptotics for the unperturbed focusing NLS in soliton regions and partial results for certain perturbations and for the defocusing N-soliton case. However, a complete perturbation theory for the focusing cubic NLS near a k-soliton state (k ≥ 2) with non-negligible perturbation εV(|u|)u, together with the analogous Toda shock/rarefaction persistence and sine-Gordon/FPU problems, does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature; the program is still considered open in its general form.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Create an effective perturbation theory for exactly solvable combinatorial models whose asymptotic random-matrix behavior is currently proved only for very rigid input distributions. For example, in last-passage percolation the exact analysis uses geometric or exponential waiting times; determine what happens under small perturbations of those distributions and prove whether the same random-matrix fluctuation laws persist.
self_contained_problem:
Consider last-passage percolation on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2$: assign i.i.d. nonnegative random weights $\{w(i,j)\}_{(i,j)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2}$ with common distribution $\mu$, and define
$$L_\mu(N,N) = \max_{\pi}\sum_{(i,j)\in\pi} w(i,j),$$
where the maximum is over all up-right lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(N,N)$. When $\mu$ is the geometric distribution with parameter $q\in(0,1)$ (or, in a related model, the exponential distribution), it is known that
$$\frac{L_\mu(N,N) - c_1(\mu)\,N}{c_2(\mu)\,N^{1/3}} \xrightarrow{d} F_2 \qquad (N\to\infty),$$
where $F_2$ is the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution and $c_1(\mu),c_2(\mu)>0$ are explicit model-dependent constants.

Develop an effective perturbation theory for this exactly solvable model under perturbations of the input weight distribution. Specifically, prove or disprove the following: for every distribution $\nu$ in a suitable neighborhood of the geometric distribution $\mu_q$ (for example, distributions of the form $\nu_\epsilon = (1-\epsilon)\mu_q + \epsilon\rho$ for an arbitrary probability measure $\rho$ on $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ with sufficient moments and $\epsilon$ small), there exist constants $c_1(\nu),c_2(\nu)>0$ such that
$$\frac{L_\nu(N,N) - c_1(\nu)\,N}{c_2(\nu)\,N^{1/3}} \xrightarrow{d} F_2.$$
Equivalently, establish quantitative stability of the $N^{1/3}$ scaling and the GUE Tracy–Widom limit law under small perturbations of the underlying i.i.d. weight distribution away from the integrable (geometric or exponential) case.
status_search_result: Full KPZ-class universality of one-point Tracy–Widom fluctuations for last-passage percolation with general i.i.d. weights remains an outstanding open problem. Partial progress exists: universality has been established in special regimes such as paths close to the axis (Bodineau–Martin 2005 and recent 2025 work), and for TASEP-type models with arbitrary particle density (Ferrari–Nejjar 2017), and there are recent extensions via KMT coupling toward the directed landscape. However, no general perturbation theory establishing Tracy–Widom limits for arbitrary small perturbations of the geometric/exponential distributions is currently available.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For integrable equations on a half-line, resolve the mismatch between the well-posed initial-boundary data and the additional dependent boundary quantities required by the Fokas method. In particular, for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on x≥0,t≥0 with smooth compactly supported initial data u(x,0)=u_0(x) and periodic boundary forcing u(0,t)=sin(ω t) with ω≠0, determine the long-time behavior of the solution and decide whether a fully explicit description is possible for general data.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the quarter-plane
  i u_t + u_{xx} - 2|u|^2 u = 0,   x ≥ 0,  t ≥ 0,
with initial data
  u(x, 0) = u_0(x),  x ≥ 0,
where u_0 is smooth and compactly supported, and with the time-periodic Dirichlet boundary condition
  u(0, t) = sin(ω t),  t ≥ 0,
for some fixed real ω ≠ 0.

The Fokas (unified transform) method represents the solution via a matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem whose jump data depend on four spectral functions determined by both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary values at x = 0. Although the Dirichlet datum is prescribed, the corresponding Neumann datum u_x(0, t) is not free and must be determined consistently with the initial data and the boundary forcing (the "generalized Dirichlet-to-Neumann problem").

Determine the long-time behavior of u(x, t) as t → ∞ in different regions of the (x, t) quarter-plane (e.g., along rays x/t = const), and decide whether a fully explicit asymptotic description of u(x, t) can be obtained for general smooth compactly supported initial data u_0.
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Boutet de Monvel–Its–Kotlyarov and by Lenells–Fokas (the "Unified Method II" series) treats NLS on the half-line with t-periodic boundary data, in particular single-exponential forcing a e^{2iωt}, and obtains long-time asymptotics and an asymptotically periodic Neumann value via Riemann–Hilbert analysis. The case of strictly real sinusoidal forcing sin(ωt) and the construction of fully explicit solutions for general smooth compactly supported initial data have been only partially resolved; rigorous treatments (e.g., for the linearized/inhomogeneous Schrödinger case) appeared as recently as 2023, indicating the original problem is partially solved rather than fully closed.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: Extend the Riemann-Hilbert/steepest-descent method beyond the currently tractable 3×3 problems so that it applies to generic n×n Riemann-Hilbert problems arising in multi-matrix random matrix models and matrix models with an external field. Such an extension should also have consequences for multiple orthogonal polynomials, Padé-Hermite approximation, and irrationality problems for special real numbers.
status_search_result: The general program of extending nonlinear steepest descent to arbitrary n×n Riemann-Hilbert problems remains open. Significant partial progress has been made for specific 3×3 and 4×4 cases: e.g., steepest-descent analyses of 4×4 RH problems for biorthogonal polynomials in the two-matrix model (one-cut regular case) and Gaussian matrices with external source, and corresponding multi-sheeted-Riemann-surface global parametrix constructions. A fully general n×n framework with universal local parametrices and arithmetic applications has not been achieved.

paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
original_question: For symmetric random band matrices whose bandwidth W ranges from 1 to N-1 in dimension N, determine the transition from Poisson bulk eigenvalue statistics to Gaudin-Mehta statistics and locate the sharp threshold. The conjecture highlighted in the source predicts a narrow transition region around W≈√N.
status_search_result: The conjectured sharp transition at $W \asymp \sqrt{N}$ for one-dimensional symmetric random band matrices remains open in full strength. Substantial partial progress has been made: delocalization has been proved for bandwidths well above $\sqrt{N}$ (work of Bourgade, Yang, Yau, Yin, Erdős–Riabov and others establishing GOE/GUE bulk statistics for sufficiently large $W$), and recent localization results push the localized/Poisson regime closer to $\sqrt{N}$ from below, but the optimal threshold $W \sim \sqrt{N}$ has not been reached from either side as of 2025–2026.

original_question: Does every subgroup H of an infinite-dimensional Lie group G admit a smooth manifold structure making H an initial Lie subgroup of G? Here this means that, for every k in N union {infinity}, H is C^k-initial in G in the sense that the inclusion map lambda: H -> G is C^k and every map f: X -> H from a C^k-manifold X is C^k whenever lambda o f is C^k, and moreover the induced tangent map L(lambda): L(H) -> L(G) is injective.
self_contained_problem:
Let G be an infinite-dimensional Lie group modeled on a locally convex space, with Lie algebra L(G) = T_1(G). For k ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}, a subset H ⊆ G equipped with a smooth manifold (Lie group) structure is called C^k-initial in G if:

(i) the inclusion map λ: H → G is C^k, and
(ii) for every C^k-manifold X and every map f: X → H, if λ ∘ f: X → G is C^k, then f: X → H is C^k.

A subgroup H ⊆ G is called an initial Lie subgroup of G if it admits a smooth manifold structure making it a Lie group such that H is C^k-initial in G for every k ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}, and such that the induced tangent map L(λ) := T_1(λ): L(H) → L(G) is injective.

Question: Does every subgroup H of every infinite-dimensional Lie group G admit such a smooth manifold structure making it an initial Lie subgroup of G?

Equivalently: must every subgroup of an infinite-dimensional Lie group be an initial Lie subgroup?
status_search_result: The problem is resolved in the negative. A counterexample shows that the additive subgroup ℓ^∞ of bounded sequences inside the Lie group ℝ^ℕ (with product topology) is not a C^k-initial submanifold for any k ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}, hence not an initial Lie subgroup.

context_brief: Subgroups of direct limit Lie groups
original_question: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence G1 subseteq G2 subseteq ... of finite-dimensional real Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, must every subgroup H of G be an initial Lie subgroup of G? Equivalently, can H be equipped with the direct-limit Lie group structure coming from Hn := Gn intersection H so that the inclusion H -> G is strongly C^k-initial for every k in N union {infinity}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G_1 \subseteq G_2 \subseteq \cdots$ be an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional real Lie groups such that for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the inclusion map $G_n \hookrightarrow G_{n+1}$ is a smooth homomorphism. Let $G = \varinjlim G_n$ be the direct limit Lie group (a possibly infinite-dimensional Lie group modeled on a locally convex space, obtained as the direct limit in the category of Lie groups).

Given a smooth map $f: M 	o N$ between (possibly infinite-dimensional) manifolds, recall that an injective immersion $\iota: H 	o G$ endows $H$ with a manifold structure called \emph{strongly $C^k$-initial} in $G$ if, for every $C^k$-manifold $M$ and every map $f: M 	o H$, the composite $\iota \circ f: M 	o G$ is $C^k$ if and only if $f$ is $C^k$. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ equipped with a Lie group structure for which the inclusion is strongly $C^k$-initial for all $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is called an \emph{initial Lie subgroup} of $G$.

Let $H \subseteq G$ be an arbitrary subgroup. For each $n$, set $H_n := G_n \cap H$ and equip $H_n$ with its (uniquely determined) finite-dimensional real Lie group structure as a subgroup of $G_n$. Equip $H$ with the direct limit Lie group structure $H = \varinjlim H_n$.

Prove or disprove: With this Lie group structure, $H$ is an initial Lie subgroup of $G$; that is, the inclusion $H \hookrightarrow G$ is strongly $C^k$-initial for every $k \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
status_search_result: The problem is resolved affirmatively: every subgroup $H$ of a direct limit $G=\varinjlim G_n$ of finite-dimensional Lie groups, equipped with the direct limit Lie group structure from $H_n=G_n\cap H$, is an initial Lie subgroup of $G$, with strongly $C^k$-initial inclusion for all $k\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$. This answers Problem VII.3 of Glöckner–Neeb's problem list on infinite-dimensional Lie groups.

This answers Problem VII.3 in the affirmative.", "claim": "The problem is solved positively by Theorem 2.1."}]

context_brief: Direct limits as topological groups with Lie algebra
original_question: If G = lim-> Gn is the direct limit of an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional Lie groups with smooth inclusion homomorphisms, is G a topological group with Lie algebra in the sense of Hofmann and Morris? That is, do the continuous one-parameter subgroups Hom_c(R, G) carry the vector-space and Lie-bracket operations specified by Definition 3.1, with addition given by the Trotter-type limit of (gamma(t/n) eta(t/n))^n and bracket given by the commutator limit, so that Hom_c(R, G) becomes a topological Lie algebra naturally identified with L(G)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(G_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an ascending sequence of finite-dimensional real Lie groups, with smooth inclusion homomorphisms $G_n \hookrightarrow G_{n+1}$, and let $G = \varinjlim G_n$ denote its direct limit, equipped with the finest topology making all canonical maps $G_n \to G$ continuous (so that $G$ is a topological group).

Let $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ denote the set of continuous one-parameter subgroups of $G$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

Call a topological group $G$ a topological group with Lie algebra if the following hold:
(a) For all $\gamma, \eta \in \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$, the limit
$$(\gamma+\eta)(t) := \lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(\gamma(t/n)\,\eta(t/n)\bigr)^n$$
exists for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and defines a continuous homomorphism $\gamma+\eta:\mathbb{R}\to G$;
(b) Together with the scalar multiplication $(r\cdot \gamma)(t) := \gamma(rt)$, this addition makes $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ into a topological vector space;
(c) There exists a continuous bilinear map $[\cdot,\cdot]:\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)\times\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)\to\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ making $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ a Lie algebra (typically realized as a commutator-type limit).

Question: Is every such direct limit $G = \varinjlim G_n$ of finite-dimensional Lie groups a topological group with Lie algebra in the above sense, with $\mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ naturally isomorphic, as a topological Lie algebra, to the direct limit Lie algebra $L(G) = \varinjlim L(G_n)$?
status_search_result: The paper itself proves the result affirmatively: for every direct limit $G=\varinjlim G_n$ of finite-dimensional Lie groups, the natural map $L(G)\to \mathrm{Hom}_c(\mathbb{R},G)$ is a homeomorphism, so $G$ is a topological group with Lie algebra in the Hofmann–Morris sense. This resolves the cited problem positively.

original_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $\sigma$-compact smooth manifold of finite dimension $n \geq 1$, and fix a point $p \in M$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$ denote the group of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms of $M$, and define
$$\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0} := \{\gamma \in \mathrm{Diff}_c(M) : \gamma(p) = p 	ext{ and } \det(d\gamma_p) > 0\}.$$
Let $G^n_f(\mathbb{R})$ denote the group of formal power series diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin, i.e. the group (under formal composition) of formal power series maps $F = (F_1,\dots,F_n) \in \mathbb{R}[[x_1,\dots,x_n]]^n$ with $F(0) = 0$ and invertible linear part, and let $G^n_f(\mathbb{R})_0$ be the subgroup of those whose linear part has positive determinant.

Choose a smooth chart $\varphi$ around $p$ with $\varphi(p) = 0$, and for $\gamma \in \mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$ let $T^\infty_p(\gamma)$ denote the Taylor series at $0$ of $\varphi \circ \gamma \circ \varphi^{-1}$, viewed as an element of $G^n_f(\mathbb{R})_0$.

Question: Is the Taylor-series map
$$T^\infty_p : \mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0} \longrightarrow G^n_f(\mathbb{R})_0$$
a surjective homomorphism of groups? Equivalently, is every formal diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^n$ at the origin with positive-determinant linear part realized as the Taylor series at $p$ of a compactly supported smooth diffeomorphism of $M$ fixing $p$ and preserving orientation at $p$?
status_search_result: The provided source evidence states and proves a "Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms" establishing that $T^\infty_p$ is a surjective group homomorphism, with the surjectivity for $M = \mathbb{R}^n$ shown via a lemma and the general case reduced to it through a chart. The problem is therefore solved (affirmatively).

paper_title: Vectored route-length minimization – a heuristic and an open conjecture
original_question: Given a finite partially connected network of N nodes embedded in a strictly Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, with a pre-specified source node S0 and sink node SN, does Vectored Route-length Minimization Search (VeRMinS) necessarily and sufficiently identify a route from S0 to SN whose total Euclidean route length is minimum? In VeRMinS, a connectivity matrix encodes the available edges, route vectors indicate which nodes lie on each source-to-sink route, an ideal route is the straight line from source to sink, a weight vector records each node's Euclidean distance from that ideal route with source and sink weights equal to zero, Euclidean-dominance filtering removes any route vector that differs from another only by including an extra intermediate node, and the selected route is the remaining route minimizing the route-vector/weight-vector product. Can this procedure be proved correct for every such finite Euclidean network, or can one construct a counterexample in which a shorter route exists but is not selected by VeRMinS?
self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite undirected graph with vertex set V = {S_0, S_1, ..., S_N} embedded in a Euclidean space R^d (d ≥ 1) so that each vertex S_i has a position x_i ∈ R^d, and each edge {S_i, S_j} ∈ E has length ‖x_i − x_j‖_2. Designate S_0 as a source and S_N as a sink. Define an admissible route from S_0 to S_N as a simple path in G starting at S_0 and ending at S_N; encode such a path as a 0/1 incidence vector P = (k_0, k_1, ..., k_N) over V, where k_j = 1 iff S_j lies on the path. Let the ideal route be the straight line segment L from x_0 to x_N in R^d, and define the weight vector W = (w_0, w_1, ..., w_N) by w_j = dist(x_j, L) (the Euclidean distance from S_j to L), with the convention w_0 = w_N = 0.

Define the following heuristic procedure (VeRMinS) to choose a route:
(1) Enumerate every simple path from S_0 to S_N as a vector P_t = (k_{t,0}, ..., k_{t,N}).
(2) Apply Euclidean-dominance filtering: discard any route vector P_t whenever there exists another route vector P_s such that P_t and P_s differ in exactly one coordinate j ∉ {0, N} with k_{t,j} = 1 and k_{s,j} = 0 (i.e., P_t is obtained from P_s by inserting one extra intermediate vertex while keeping all other vertices the same).
(3) Among the surviving route vectors, select the one minimizing the dot product P_t · W = Σ_j k_{t,j} w_j.

Question: Is it true that for every finite graph G with Euclidean vertex positions and every choice of source S_0 and sink S_N, the route selected by VeRMinS is necessarily and sufficiently a route of minimum total Euclidean length from S_0 to S_N? Equivalently, prove that VeRMinS always returns an actual shortest path, or exhibit a finite Euclidean network on which VeRMinS fails to identify a path of minimum total Euclidean length.
status_search_result: The conjecture was posed as an open problem in 2008, with the authors explicitly stating only a heuristic was provided. A web search reveals no subsequent published proof or counterexample, and no follow-up literature addressing the VeRMinS conjecture beyond the original posting. Its current status therefore could not be verified from available sources.

paper_title: An open question: Are topological arguments helpful in setting initial conditions for transport problems and quantization criteria/ quantum computing for Density Wave physics?
original_question: For charge-density-wave transport modeled by a generalized tunneling Hamiltonian in a driven sine-Gordon system, with tunneling between Gaussian wavefunctionals of a scalar quantum field, should the coefficients in the wavefunctionals and the coefficients in the driven sine-Gordon physical system be chosen by topological-charge arguments tied to Coleman's false-vacuum hypothesis, and can that topological choice help explain the observed current-versus-electric-field behavior as evidence for a first-order phase transition and quantum switching relevant to quantum computing via quantum-coherent phase evolution?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional driven sine-Gordon model for charge-density-wave (CDW) transport, with Lagrangian density of the form

  L[φ] = (1/2)(∂_t φ)^2 − (1/2)v^2(∂_x φ)^2 − V_0[1 − cos(βφ)] + Jφ,

where φ(x,t) is a real scalar field, β, V_0, v are real parameters, and J is a driving term proportional to an applied electric field E. Model CDW tunneling between two metastable configurations of φ by a generalized tunneling Hamiltonian whose matrix elements are taken between Gaussian wavefunctionals

  Ψ_i[φ] = N_i exp{ −(1/2) ∫ dx dy [φ(x) − φ_i(x)] K_i(x,y) [φ(y) − φ_i(y)] },  i = 1,2,

centered on classical false- and true-vacuum field configurations φ_1, φ_2 of the tilted washboard potential, with positive-definite kernels K_i and normalization N_i.

Questions:

(a) Determine whether the parameters {φ_i, K_i, N_i} of the Gaussian wavefunctionals, together with the coefficients (β, V_0, v, J) of the driven sine-Gordon system, can be selected canonically by topological-charge arguments — i.e. by requiring that φ_1 and φ_2 lie in distinct topological sectors of the sine-Gordon vacuum manifold and that the tunneling amplitude correspond to a kink/anti-kink (false-vacuum decay) configuration in the sense of Coleman's bounce solution.

(b) Show whether such a topological-charge prescription forces the tunneling current I, computed from the resulting Hamiltonian as a function of the drive E, to exhibit a threshold-type, first-order-transition I–E characteristic with a sharp onset above a critical field E_T.

(c) Decide whether the resulting two-state tunneling dynamics admit a quantum-coherent phase evolution between the Gaussian wavefunctionals (a Josephson-like oscillation of the CDW phase φ) suitable as a qubit-like quantum switching mechanism, and quantify the decoherence conditions under which such coherent evolution persists.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open conceptual/physical question about whether topological-charge arguments à la Coleman's false-vacuum decay provide the correct way to fix wavefunctional and sine-Gordon coefficients for CDW tunneling. No subsequent work definitively resolving this specific prescription was identified; the status appears unresolved.

paper_title: An open question: Are topological arguments helpful in setting initial conditions for transport problems and quantization criteria/ quantum computing for Density Wave physics?
original_question: In the paper's charge-density-wave false-vacuum model, where the Gaussian parameter α is identified with the inverse soliton-pair separation L⁻¹ and with the energy-gap difference ΔE_gap = V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) between false-vacuum phase φ_F and true-vacuum phase φ_T, can the change from a false vacuum to a real vacuum be described by a topological model of phase transitions rather than only by an analytical current derivation, especially when one compares the derived current-versus-electric-field curve with the low-dimensional electron-positron pair-production curve?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional charge-density-wave system modeled as a scalar field theory with a tilted double-well (Euclidean) potential V_E(φ) having a metastable false-vacuum minimum at φ = φ_F and a stable true-vacuum minimum at φ = φ_T, separated by an energy-gap difference ΔE_gap := V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) > 0. Suppose the decay of the false vacuum proceeds through nucleation of soliton–antisoliton pairs of mean separation L, and that the instanton/bounce profile is approximated by a Gaussian of width parameter α satisfying the identification α ≈ L^{-1} ≈ ΔE_gap.

Let I(E) denote the analytically derived tunneling current as a function of an applied electric field E obtained via a WKB/instanton calculation in this false-vacuum model (call this curve C₁), and let Ĩ(E) denote the corresponding current–field curve produced by the Schwinger-type low-dimensional electron–positron pair-production formula (call this curve C₂).

Question: Construct a topological model of the false-vacuum-to-true-vacuum phase transition in this setting — for instance, by realizing the soliton–antisoliton nucleation as a topological soliton sector and applying a Bogomolnyi-type inequality saturated by BPS configurations — that reproduces the I–E curve C₁ in the regime where C₁ and C₂ fail to coincide. More precisely:

(a) Determine whether there exists a topological (Bogomolnyi-bound) description of the transition φ_F → φ_T, compatible with the identification α ≈ L^{-1} ≈ ΔE_gap, whose predicted current–field relation agrees with C₁.

(b) Identify a quantitative criterion (e.g., a bound on ‖C₁ − C₂‖ over a specified field range) under which the analytic derivation suffices and the topological description becomes redundant, versus the regime in which the topological/Bogomolnyi description is strictly necessary.
category_tag: topological phase transitions in density wave models
status_search_result: No publication was located that resolves this specific question of constructing a topological/Bogomolnyi model for the false-vacuum to true-vacuum transition in the charge-density-wave setting and matching it to the analytic I–E curve. The question appears to remain open, though confirmation in the literature is inconclusive.

paper_title: An open question: Are topological arguments helpful in setting initial conditions for transport problems and quantization criteria/ quantum computing for Density Wave physics?
original_question: Does the abrupt turn-on of the current-versus-electric-field curve imply a phase transition that could be exploited for quantum switching devices and ultra-fast data transitions, specifically if the Bogomolnyi inequality can be used to derive the identification α ≈ L⁻¹ ≡ ΔE_gap ≡ V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) and thereby connect 1+1-dimensional φ⁴ field theory to Gaussian wavefunctionals in the charge-density-wave setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional charge-density-wave (CDW) condensate modeled by a real scalar field φ(x,t) in 1+1 spacetime dimensions whose dynamics, after appropriate rescaling, is governed by a φ^4 (double-well) effective potential V_E(φ) with two distinct extrema φ_T (a "true" or false vacuum) and φ_F such that ΔE_gap := V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T) > 0. Static finite-energy solutions interpolating between the two minima saturate the Bogomolnyi bound: for any field configuration with appropriate boundary conditions, the static energy obeys E[φ] ≥ |∫ dφ √(2 V_E(φ))|, with equality on BPS (kink/instanton) configurations satisfying dφ/dx = ±√(2 V_E(φ)). Let L denote the characteristic spatial width of such a soliton and let α denote the inverse correlation length governing the exponential turn-on of the tunneling/pinning current J as a function of applied electric field E in the CDW system, so that J(E) is sharply switched on at a threshold field E_T.

Question: Does the abrupt turn-on of the current–field characteristic J(E) at E_T correspond to a genuine phase transition of the underlying 1+1-dimensional φ^4 field theory? More precisely, can the Bogomolnyi (BPS) inequality applied to this φ^4 model be used to rigorously establish the identification
   α ≈ L^{-1} ≡ ΔE_gap ≡ V_E(φ_F) − V_E(φ_T),
and to construct an exact bridge between the soliton sector of the 1+1-dimensional φ^4 field theory and a Gaussian wavefunctional description of the CDW ground state, thereby providing a field-theoretic mechanism for quantum switching and ultrafast transitions in CDW devices?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open conjecture about whether a Bogomolnyi-type bound in 1+1-dimensional φ^4 theory can be used to identify the inverse soliton width with the CDW gap and thereby establish a phase transition underlying CDW current switching. No subsequent literature was located that rigorously establishes this identification or the claimed bridge to Gaussian wavefunctionals; the status appears to remain open.

original_question: Can a 1+1-dimensional φ⁴ field theory be solved exactly in real time without invoking the Bogomolnyi inequality by evolving initial and final Gaussian wavefunctionals that represent a kink-antikink configuration, and by using the symplectic evolution equations given for the discretized field dynamics?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a (1+1)-dimensional real scalar field theory with Lagrangian density
  L = (1/2)(∂_t φ)² − (1/2)(∂_x φ)² − (λ/4)(φ² − v²)²,
whose static finite-energy solutions include the kink φ_K(x) = v tanh(√(λ/2)·v·x) and the antikink φ_{\bar K}(x) = −v tanh(√(λ/2)·v·(x − a)) separated by a distance a > 0. Discretize the spatial line into a lattice {x_n}_{n∈ℤ} of spacing Δx, denote the canonical fields and momenta by (φ_n, π_n), and let H_lat be the lattice Hamiltonian obtained from L. Define a Gaussian wavefunctional centred on a classical configuration φ̄_n with width kernel K_{nm} > 0:
  Ψ[φ; φ̄, K] = N · exp(−(1/2) Σ_{n,m}(φ_n − φ̄_n) K_{nm} (φ_m − φ̄_m)).
Take an initial Gaussian wavefunctional Ψ_i centred on a kink–antikink configuration with separation a_i and a final Gaussian wavefunctional Ψ_f centred on a kink–antikink configuration with separation a_f, with prescribed width kernels K_i, K_f.

Question: Is it possible to compute exactly, in closed form, the real-time amplitude
  A(t) = ⟨Ψ_f | exp(−i t H_lat) | Ψ_i⟩
(equivalently, to determine exactly the symplectic Hamiltonian flow on the phase-space variables (φ_n, π_n) connecting these two Gaussian wavefunctionals) without invoking the Bogomolnyi inequality / BPS bound, using only the symplectic evolution equations
  dφ_n/dt = ∂H_lat/∂π_n,  dπ_n/dt = −∂H_lat/∂φ_n
to evolve the centres and covariances of the Gaussian wavefunctionals? If so, exhibit such an exact solution; if not, prove an obstruction.
category_tag: Real-time evolution of φ⁴ kink-antikink wavefunctionals
status_search_result: A web search for exact real-time Gaussian-wavefunctional evolution of (1+1)-d φ⁴ kink–antikink configurations without invoking the Bogomolnyi/BPS inequality returns work on kink–antikink scattering, oscillon decay, and semiclassical or numerical treatments, but no construction of an exact closed-form real-time evolution between Gaussian wavefunctionals representing kink–antikink states. The φ⁴ theory is non-integrable (kink–antikink collisions exhibit chaotic n-bounce resonances), and standard exact treatments of the kink sector rely on BPS/Bogomolnyi bounds, so the question appears still open.

original_question: In the appendix's adjacent-chain charge-density-wave model, what role does the multi-chain interaction and the added Peierls-gap term Δ′ play in forming a soliton-instanton configuration, and is that term necessary in order to obtain a sine-Gordon equation and therefore an instanton formulation?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional charge-density-wave (CDW) system modeled by two adjacent coupled chains, with a complex order parameter whose phase field φ(x,t) describes the collective mode. The Lagrangian density contains the usual kinetic and gradient terms for φ together with an inter-chain coupling and an added Peierls-gap pinning term of the form −Δ′ cos(φ) (with Δ′ > 0) that arises from the single-particle gap of the underlying Peierls instability.

(a) Derive the Euler–Lagrange equation of motion for φ in the presence of both the multi-chain (inter-chain) interaction and the Peierls-gap term Δ′, and show whether it reduces to a sine-Gordon equation
   ∂_t² φ − c² ∂_x² φ + (Δ′/α) sin(φ) = 0
for some effective constants c, α determined by the model parameters.

(b) Determine whether removing the Peierls-gap term (Δ′ = 0) still permits a sine-Gordon reduction, and consequently whether soliton/instanton solutions of the standard sine-Gordon type exist in that case.

(c) Conclude precisely what role the multi-chain coupling plays versus the role of the Peierls-gap term Δ′ in producing a soliton–instanton configuration: which of these two ingredients is necessary, and which is merely auxiliary, for obtaining the sine-Gordon equation and the associated instanton formulation?
status_search_result: The question is internally answered within the same source: without the added Peierls-gap term Δ′, the equation of motion does not reduce to a sine-Gordon equation, and hence no instanton formulation is obtained; the multi-chain coupling alone is insufficient. The Peierls term is therefore a necessary ingredient. This is a well-known feature of standard sine-Gordon reductions of CDW models (e.g., Brazovskii–Kirova, Su–Schrieffer–Heeger style treatments).

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Generic Weyl remainder in negative curvature
original_question: For a compact unit-area Riemannian surface of negative curvature with quantum Hamiltonian P = sqrt(-Δ), eigenvalues λ_k, and counting function N(λ) = #{k: λ_k ≤ λ} = λ^2/(4π) + R(λ), can one prove that a generic negatively curved surface has Weyl remainder R(λ) = O(λ^ε) for every ε > 0? More broadly, which refined dynamical quantities of the geodesic flow determine the sharp high-energy spectral remainder beyond the known O(λ/log λ) bound?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface of unit area and everywhere negative Gaussian curvature, with Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$. Set $P = \sqrt{-\Delta_g}$, and let $0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots$ denote its eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity). Define the spectral counting function
$$N(\lambda) = \#\{k : \lambda_k \le \lambda\}, \qquad \lambda \ge 0,$$
and write Weyl's law in the form
$$N(\lambda) = \frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi} + R(\lambda).$$
It is known that $R(\lambda) = O(\lambda/\log\lambda)$ as $\lambda \to \infty$ for any such surface.

(a) Prove or disprove: for a generic compact unit-area negatively curved Riemannian surface (in a suitable Baire-category or measure-theoretic sense on the space of negatively curved metrics), one has
$$R(\lambda) = O_\varepsilon(\lambda^\varepsilon) \quad \text{for every } \varepsilon > 0.$$

(b) Identify and characterize the refined dynamical invariants of the geodesic flow on $(M,g)$ — such as the topological entropy, topological pressure, or the Ruelle–Pollicott resonance spectrum — that govern the precise high-energy asymptotics of the remainder $R(\lambda)$ beyond the bound $O(\lambda/\log\lambda)$.
category_tag: Weyl remainder on negatively curved surfaces
status_search_result: The best known general upper bound for the Weyl remainder on a compact negatively curved surface remains $O(\lambda/\log\lambda)$ (Bérard, 1977). Lower-bound results (e.g. Jakobson–Polterovich–Toth) show $R(\lambda)$ cannot be too small, but the conjectured generic bound $R(\lambda)=O(\lambda^\varepsilon)$ has not been proved. Surveys such as Ivrii's "100 years of Weyl's law" (2016) list this as open. No published resolution was found.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Gutzwiller trace formula beyond Ehrenfest time
original_question: For chaotic quantum systems, can the Gutzwiller trace formula and related semiclassical propagator approximations be justified for times substantially larger than the Ehrenfest time T_E ≈ log(λ)/χ_Lya, and in particular on time scales relevant for sharp spectral statistics? The problem asks how to control the quantum evolution after exponential separation of classical trajectories causes the usual semiclassical approximation to break down.
self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a quantum Hamiltonian on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (or on a compact Riemannian manifold) whose underlying classical Hamiltonian flow on phase space is uniformly hyperbolic (chaotic), with largest Lyapunov exponent $\chi_{\mathrm{Lya}}>0$. Let $\hbar>0$ be the semiclassical parameter and define the Ehrenfest time $T_E(\hbar) = \frac{|\log \hbar|}{\chi_{\mathrm{Lya}}}$. The Gutzwiller trace formula provides a semiclassical asymptotic expansion of $\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\varphi(H)\, e^{-itH/\hbar}\bigr)$ (for a smooth energy localizer $\varphi$) as a sum over classical periodic orbits, and is rigorously known to be valid for times $|t|$ bounded, and more generally for $|t| \le c\, T_E(\hbar)$ with $c<1$.

Problem: Develop a rigorous semiclassical control of the propagator $e^{-itH/\hbar}$, and a corresponding extension of the Gutzwiller trace formula (or related semiclassical trace expansions), valid for time scales $t$ substantially exceeding the Ehrenfest time $T_E(\hbar)$ — ideally up to the Heisenberg time scale relevant to resolving individual eigenvalues — with explicit error estimates that vanish as $\hbar \to 0$. In particular, determine to what extent such extended trace formulas can be used to derive sharp spectral statistics (e.g. pair correlation, level spacing distributions) for chaotic quantum systems.
status_search_result: Partial progress exists. Faure (Ann. Inst. Fourier 2007) established a semi-classical trace formula beyond the Ehrenfest time using normal form methods, extending validity by arbitrarily small factors. Subsequent work (e.g., Anantharaman, Nonnenmacher, and the many-body semiclassical program reviewed by Richter et al., 2022) has pushed semiclassical control past $T_E$ in specific settings, but a general justification up to the Heisenberg time yielding sharp spectral statistics remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
original_question: Can the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit, or random matrix theory, conjecture be proved rigorously for generic chaotic quantum Hamiltonians, so that the local high-energy spectrum at the mean level spacing scale δλ ∼ 2π/λ has the same statistics as the appropriate Gaussian random matrix ensemble such as the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble? A proof would need to justify the periodic-orbit expansion at times comparable to the Heisenberg time T_H ∼ λ and show that the sum over non-correlated pairs of periodic orbits is negligible relative to the correlated pairs.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) whose geodesic flow is chaotic in a generic sense (for example, ergodic and hyperbolic, with isolated and unstable periodic orbits, and non-degenerate Lyapunov spectrum). Let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$ (with Dirichlet boundary conditions if $\partial M\neq\emptyset$), and let $0\le \lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le \cdots$ denote the square roots of its eigenvalues. Around a large energy $\lambda$, unfold the spectrum so that the mean level spacing equals $1$ on the scale $\delta\lambda\sim 2\pi/\lambda$, and consider the local statistics (e.g. the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution, the two-level correlation function $R_2(s)$, the number variance, and higher $n$-point correlation functions) of the unfolded eigenvalues in a window centered at $\lambda$.

Prove (or disprove) the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture in this setting: that for generic such systems with time-reversal symmetry, the local spectral statistics at energy $\lambda\to\infty$ converge to those of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (real symmetric $N\times N$ matrices with independent Gaussian entries, $N\to\infty$); and analogously to the Gaussian Unitary or Symplectic ensembles when time-reversal symmetry is broken or in the presence of half-integer spin.

A rigorous proof should in particular justify the use of the Gutzwiller periodic-orbit trace formula at times comparable to the Heisenberg time $T_H\sim\lambda$ (far beyond the Ehrenfest time $T_E\sim \log\lambda$), and establish that the contribution to the spectral form factor from sums over pairs of periodic orbits whose actions are not correlated is negligible compared to the contribution from correlated pairs (such as the diagonal pairs and the Sieber–Richter pairs and their higher-order generalizations).
status_search_result: The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture remains a major open problem in quantum chaos. Semiclassical work by Sieber–Richter, Müller–Heusler–Braun–Haake–Altland, and others reproduces the GOE/GUE/GSE form factor to all orders in perturbation theory via periodic-orbit pair contributions, but a rigorous proof for generic chaotic Hamiltonians is not available, and recent surveys still list it as open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Poisson statistics for arithmetic quantum chaos
original_question: For arithmetic negatively curved surfaces, or analogous systems such as the quantum cat map, can one give a full rigorous proof that the two-point correlation function of the high-energy quantum spectrum converges to the correlation function of Poisson-distributed points rather than to random matrix statistics? The issue is to control the additional periodic-orbit correlations caused by large degeneracies of the length spectrum.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact arithmetic hyperbolic surface (a quotient $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ where $\Gamma$ is a congruence arithmetic Fuchsian group), and let $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ be the eigenvalues of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Unfold the spectrum by setting $x_n = N(\lambda_n)$, where $N(\lambda)\sim\frac{\mathrm{Area}(M)}{4\pi}\lambda$ is the Weyl counting function, so that the sequence $\{x_n\}$ has unit mean spacing. Define the (smoothed) two-point correlation function
$$R_2(s) = \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{1}{X}\#\{(m,n): m\ne n,\ x_m,x_n\in[0,X],\ |x_m-x_n|\le s\},$$
and similarly define the analogous spectral two-point statistic for the quantization of a hyperbolic toral automorphism (the "quantum cat map") on $\mathbb{T}^2$ along a sequence of Planck constants $\hbar = 1/N$, $N\to\infty$.

Prove rigorously that, for almost every such system (or at least for a generic sequence of moduli/Planck constants in the cat map case), the limiting two-point correlation function coincides with that of a Poisson point process on the real line of unit intensity, namely
$$R_2^{\mathrm{Poisson}}(s) = s,$$
rather than with the GOE/GUE random-matrix two-point correlation function. The principal difficulty to be overcome is to control, via the Selberg / Gutzwiller trace formula, the contribution of correlated pairs of periodic orbits arising from the high multiplicities in the length spectrum (lengths being essentially logarithms of integers or determined by integer traces), which produce diagonal-type contributions far in excess of those occurring for generic chaotic systems.
status_search_result: The conjecture that the high-energy spectrum of arithmetic surfaces and quantum cat maps obeys Poisson rather than random-matrix two-point statistics has been supported by heuristic semiclassical arguments and by numerical evidence. Partial rigorous results exist (e.g., Luo–Sarnak's theorem on the non-rigidity of the number variance for arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces, showing behavior close to Poissonian in part of the universal range, and Rudnick and others on related pair-correlation moments for cat maps), but a full proof that the two-point correlation function converges to the Poisson form is not known. The problem appears still open as of available literature.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Dynamical criterion for generic spectral universality
original_question: What refined dynamical property separates exceptional arithmetic chaotic systems from generic chaotic systems for purposes of spectral universality, and how generic is that property among all negatively curved surfaces? The candidate property should go beyond global chaoticity, should likely restrict large degeneracies and near-degeneracies in the length spectrum {ℓ_γ}, and may require a Diophantine condition on the differences ℓ_γ − ℓ_γ′.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(X,g)$ be a smooth closed surface equipped with a Riemannian metric $g$ of negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta_g$ be the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, with eigenvalues $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots\to\infty$. The geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle is then Anosov; let $\{\ell_\gamma\}_{\gamma}$ denote the length spectrum, i.e. the multiset of lengths of primitive closed geodesics on $(X,g)$.

The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit (BGS) universality hypothesis predicts that, for "generic" such $(X,g)$, the local statistics of the high-lying Laplace eigenvalues (e.g. nearest-neighbor spacing distributions, two-point correlation functions on scales of the mean spacing) coincide in the semiclassical limit $\lambda\to\infty$ with those of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble of random matrix theory. It is known that arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces (compact quotients $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H^2$ with $\Gamma$ a congruence subgroup of an arithmetic Fuchsian group) are exceptional: their length spectra exhibit unbounded multiplicities, leading to Poissonian rather than GOE-type level statistics.

Problem. Identify a refined dynamical/geometric property $\mathcal P$ of the geodesic flow on $(X,g)$, formulated in terms of the length spectrum $\{\ell_\gamma\}$ (going beyond mere global chaoticity / Anosov-ness), such that:

(a) Property $\mathcal P$ rules out the exceptional behavior of arithmetic surfaces — in particular it forbids large degeneracies $\#\{\gamma:\ell_\gamma=L\}$ growing too rapidly as $L\to\infty$, and also controls almost-degeneracies, e.g. through a Diophantine-type lower bound on the nonzero differences $|\ell_\gamma-\ell_{\gamma'}|$ as a function of $\ell_\gamma+\ell_{\gamma'}$;

(b) Whenever $(X,g)$ satisfies $\mathcal P$, the eigenvalues of $\Delta_g$ obey GOE local statistics in the high-energy limit (i.e. $\mathcal P$ implies the BGS universality);

(c) The set of metrics $g$ of negative curvature on $X$ satisfying $\mathcal P$ is generic, in a sense to be made precise (e.g. residual, of full measure, or open and dense) within the space of all smooth negatively curved Riemannian metrics on $X$.

Determine such a property $\mathcal P$ and quantify the genericity in (c) among all negatively curved metrics on closed surfaces.
status_search_result: The BGS conjecture for negatively curved surfaces remains open. Partial semiclassical evidence (form-factor expansions in the Sieber–Richter and Müller–Heusler–Braun–Haake–Altland diagonal-correction program) supports it, and small-gap results on the length spectrum exist, but no refined dynamical criterion separating arithmetic from generic chaotic systems has been established, and no proof of GOE statistics for any individual variable-curvature surface is known.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
original_question: If the Laplace-Beltrami operator on an arithmetic surface is perturbed by generic selfadjoint lower-order terms, or if one changes the quantization scheme attached to the same classical geodesic flow, does the resulting quantum spectrum become universal in the random-matrix sense? If universality can be restored this way, how large must the lower-order perturbing terms be?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be an arithmetic hyperbolic surface, i.e. a compact (or finite-area) quotient $\Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ where $\Gamma$ is a congruence arithmetic lattice in $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, and let $\Delta_g$ denote its Laplace–Beltrami operator. The eigenvalue statistics of $\Delta_g$ on such surfaces are known to deviate from the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) predictions of random matrix theory (a phenomenon called "arithmetic chaos"), exhibiting in particular Poisson-like behavior of level spacings due to large multiplicities/Hecke symmetries.

Consider self-adjoint perturbations of the form $P_\varepsilon = \Delta_g + \varepsilon Q$, where $Q$ is a self-adjoint differential (or pseudodifferential) operator on $M$ of order strictly less than $2$, drawn "generically" from a suitable family. More generally, consider any self-adjoint quantization $\mathrm{Op}(H)$ of the classical Hamiltonian $H = \tfrac12|\xi|_g^2$ generating the geodesic flow on $T^*M$, varying over the family of admissible quantization schemes attached to this same classical flow.

Questions:
(a) For a generic choice of lower-order self-adjoint perturbation $Q$, do the high-energy eigenvalue statistics (e.g. nearest-neighbour spacing distribution, number variance) of $P_\varepsilon$ converge, in the semiclassical/high-energy limit, to those predicted by GOE random matrix theory?

(b) If such universality is restored, determine the minimal order/size threshold of the perturbation $\varepsilon Q$ (as a function of the spectral parameter $\lambda \to \infty$) needed to drive the statistics from arithmetic (Poisson-type) to GOE behavior.

(c) Equivalently, does varying the quantization scheme attached to the geodesic flow on $M$ over a generic family produce GOE statistics for the resulting quantum spectra?
status_search_result: No search result indicates a resolution of this question. The eigenvalue statistics of arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces remain a central open problem in quantum chaos, and the question of whether generic lower-order self-adjoint perturbations of the Laplacian (or a generic choice of quantization of the geodesic flow) restores GOE universality—and at what threshold size—appears to remain open as of recent surveys and conferences on random and arithmetic models in spectral theory.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Rates and distributions in quantum ergodicity
original_question: For Laplacian eigenfunctions ψ_k on a negatively curved compact surface and their phase-space semiclassical measures μ_k, what is the rate and limiting distribution of the quantum averages μ_k(f) for a fixed phase-space observable f as λ_k grows? In particular, for a generic chaotic system, is the distribution Gaussian with variance asymptotic to Var(f)/λ, as predicted by Feingold and Peres, and can the current gap between the expected O(λ^−1) variance and the proven O(1/log λ) upper bound be closed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface of negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta_g$ denote the (nonpositive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Let $\{\psi_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(M)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of $-\Delta_g$ with eigenvalues $0\le \lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le \cdots \to \infty$. To each $\psi_k$ associate a semiclassical (Wigner) distribution $\mu_k$ on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$, characterized by
$$\mu_k(f) = \langle \mathrm{Op}_{\hbar_k}(f)\psi_k, \psi_k\rangle_{L^2(M)} \quad \text{for } f\in C^\infty_c(T^*M),$$
with $\hbar_k=\lambda_k^{-1/2}$ and $\mathrm{Op}_\hbar$ a fixed semiclassical quantization. Let $\mu_L$ denote the normalized Liouville measure on $S^*M$, and let $g^t$ be the geodesic flow on $S^*M$. The quantum ergodicity theorem implies that $\mu_k(f)\to \mu_L(f)$ along a density-one subsequence for every $f\in C^\infty(S^*M)$.

Address the following:

(a) Determine the rate of convergence: for a fixed observable $f\in C^\infty(S^*M)$, find the optimal exponent $\alpha>0$ (and constant) such that
$$\frac{1}{N(\lambda)}\sum_{\lambda_k\le \lambda}\bigl|\mu_k(f)-\mu_L(f)\bigr|^2 \asymp \lambda^{-\alpha}\quad\text{as } \lambda\to\infty,$$
where $N(\lambda)=\#\{k:\lambda_k\le \lambda\}$.

(b) Determine the limiting distribution of the rescaled values $\{\mu_k(f)-\mu_L(f):\lambda_k\le \lambda\}$ as $\lambda\to\infty$. Specifically, prove or disprove the prediction that, for a generic chaotic system, this distribution (after rescaling) is Gaussian with variance asymptotic to $\mathrm{Var}(f)/\lambda$, where
$$\mathrm{Var}(f)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\!\int_{S^*M}\bigl(f\circ g^t - \mu_L(f)\bigr)\bigl(f-\mu_L(f)\bigr)\,d\mu_L\,dt$$
is the variance from the classical central limit theorem for the geodesic flow.

(c) Close the gap between the conjectured variance bound $O(\lambda^{-1})$ and the currently established upper bound $O(1/\log\lambda)$, i.e., establish that the average quantum variance decays like $\lambda^{-1}$ rather than only $1/\log\lambda$.
status_search_result: For generic negatively curved compact surfaces the problem remains open. Sharp variance asymptotics and Gaussian fluctuations matching the Feingold–Peres prediction (variance ~ Var(f)/λ) have been established only in arithmetic settings — most notably the modular surface / Hecke–Maass eigenforms (Luo–Sarnak, Sarnak–Zhao) and for quantum cat maps (Kurlberg–Rudnick, Schubert) — where arithmetic L-value twists appear. For general negatively curved surfaces the best known average upper bound on the quantum variance is still of order $1/\log\lambda$, controlled by the Ehrenfest time, and no proof of the conjectured polynomial rate or of Gaussianity is known.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: QUE for non-arithmetic negatively curved manifolds
original_question: Can Quantum Unique Ergodicity be proved for non-arithmetic negatively curved surfaces and higher-dimensional negatively curved manifolds, meaning that every high-energy semiclassical measure μ_k of Laplacian eigenfunctions converges to the Liouville measure μ_L rather than only a full-density subsequence? If a full proof is unavailable, what restrictions can be proved on all possible invariant limit measures?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact connected Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature (in particular, the geodesic flow on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$ is Anosov), and let $\Delta_g$ be the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Let $(\psi_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(M)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of $-\Delta_g$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_k\to\infty$. To each $\psi_k$ associate its semiclassical (microlocal) lift $\mu_k$, a probability measure on $S^*M$, defined so that for every classical symbol $a\in C_c^\infty(T^*M)$ one has $\langle \psi_k, \mathrm{Op}_{\hbar_k}(a)\psi_k\rangle \to \int a\,d\mu$ along any weak-$*$ limit, with $\hbar_k=\lambda_k^{-1/2}$. Any weak-$*$ limit $\mu$ of the sequence $(\mu_k)$ is invariant under the geodesic flow and is called a semiclassical (or quantum) limit measure. Let $\mu_L$ denote the normalized Liouville measure on $S^*M$.

The Quantum Unique Ergodicity (QUE) question asks: 

(a) Suppose $M$ is not assumed to carry any arithmetic/Hecke structure (in particular $M$ may be a non-arithmetic negatively curved surface, or a higher-dimensional negatively curved manifold). Is it true that the entire sequence of semiclassical lifts converges, $\mu_k \rightharpoonup \mu_L$ as $k\to\infty$? Equivalently, is $\mu_L$ the unique semiclassical limit measure?

(b) If a full proof of (a) is not available, determine the strongest possible restrictions on the set of geodesic-flow-invariant probability measures on $S^*M$ that can arise as semiclassical limit measures $\mu$ of sequences of Laplacian eigenfunctions. For example, give nontrivial lower bounds on the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy $h_{KS}(\mu)$ of any such $\mu$, or rule out concentration on lower-dimensional invariant subsets of $S^*M$.
status_search_result: The full QUE conjecture for non-arithmetic negatively curved surfaces and higher-dimensional negatively curved manifolds remains open. Significant partial results restrict the possible semiclassical limit measures: Anantharaman (2008) proved that any semiclassical limit measure has positive Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, and Anantharaman–Nonnenmacher established quantitative entropy lower bounds (e.g., at least half the maximal entropy on constant negatively curved surfaces) for Anosov geodesic flows. The arithmetic case on congruence hyperbolic surfaces was resolved by Lindenstrauss (with Soundararajan handling the non-compact modular surface), but these methods do not extend to the general non-arithmetic setting.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
original_question: For eigenfunctions on manifolds of constant negative curvature, can entropy lower bounds for possible semiclassical limit measures be strengthened from at least one half of maximal Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy to maximal entropy, thereby proving Quantum Unique Ergodicity by ruling out partially localized limit measures?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of constant negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Consider an orthonormal basis $(\psi_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of $L^2(M)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of $-\Delta$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_n\to\infty$. To each $\psi_n$ associate its Wigner distribution on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$; any weak-* accumulation point (as $\lambda_n\to\infty$) of these distributions is a probability measure on $S^*M$ that is invariant under the geodesic flow $(\varphi_t)$. Such a limit is called a semiclassical (quantum) limit measure. For an invariant probability measure $\mu$, let $h_{KS}(\mu)$ denote its Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy with respect to the geodesic flow, and let $h_{\max}$ denote the topological entropy of the geodesic flow on $S^*M$ (which equals $(\dim M-1)$ times the curvature constant for constant negative curvature, and is the maximum of $h_{KS}$ over invariant probability measures, attained by the Liouville measure).

It is known that every semiclassical limit measure $\mu$ satisfies $h_{KS}(\mu)\ge \tfrac{1}{2}\,h_{\max}$. Question: Can this lower bound be strengthened to $h_{KS}(\mu)=h_{\max}$ for every semiclassical limit measure $\mu$? Equivalently, does ruling out semiclassical limit measures of submaximal entropy hold, thereby establishing Quantum Unique Ergodicity (i.e., the unique semiclassical limit measure being the normalized Liouville measure) on every compact manifold of constant negative curvature?
category_tag: Quantum unique ergodicity and entropy of eigenfunctions
status_search_result: The Anantharaman–Nonnenmacher half-delocalization theorem (entropy ≥ ½ h_max on constant-curvature manifolds) remains the state of the art in this approach. No published result is known to remove the factor 1/2 to obtain QUE via the entropy method on general compact constant negative curvature manifolds; QUE in this setting is established only for arithmetic congruence surfaces by Lindenstrauss/Soundararajan via different (Hecke) methods. The entropy-route strengthening therefore appears still open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Exceptional eigenstates and genericity of QUE
original_question: Can Quantum Unique Ergodicity be disproved by constructing a negatively curved manifold and a sequence of exceptional high-energy eigenstates of the Laplacian, or of a lower-order perturbation of the Laplacian, whose semiclassical measures do not converge to Liouville measure? More generally, does QUE hold only for generic negatively curved surfaces or generic lower-order perturbations rather than for every negatively curved system?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold of strictly negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta_g$ be the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Let $\{\varphi_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(M)$ consisting of eigenfunctions, $\Delta_g\varphi_n=\lambda_n\varphi_n$ with $\lambda_n\to\infty$. To each $\varphi_n$ one associates a microlocal lift, a probability measure $\mu_n$ on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$, defined by $\int a\,d\mu_n=\langle\mathrm{Op}(a)\varphi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$ for symbols $a\in C_c^\infty(T^*M)$ via a standard semiclassical quantization $\mathrm{Op}$ at scale $h_n=\lambda_n^{-1/2}$. Any weak-$*$ limit of $\{\mu_n\}$ is called a semiclassical (or quantum) limit measure; every such limit is invariant under the geodesic flow on $S^*M$. The Liouville measure $\mu_L$ is the normalized Riemannian volume on $S^*M$.

The Quantum Unique Ergodicity (QUE) conjecture asserts: for every such $(M,g)$ and every orthonormal eigenbasis, the only quantum limit is $\mu_L$.

(a) Determine whether QUE can be disproved, in the sense of exhibiting a compact negatively curved Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$, possibly replacing $\Delta_g$ by a self-adjoint perturbation $\Delta_g+V$ where $V$ is a lower-order (e.g.\ pseudodifferential of order $<2$) operator, together with an orthonormal sequence of eigenfunctions $\varphi_{n_k}$ with eigenvalues tending to infinity such that the associated semiclassical measures $\mu_{n_k}$ converge weakly-$*$ to a probability measure on $S^*M$ different from $\mu_L$.

(b) More generally, decide whether QUE holds for every compact negatively curved manifold and every choice of eigenbasis, or whether it holds only generically: that is, whether there exists a residual (Baire-generic) or full-measure subset of negatively curved metrics $g$ on a fixed manifold $M$ (or of lower-order perturbations $V$) for which QUE holds, while failing for some non-generic choices.
status_search_result: QUE for general compact negatively curved manifolds remains open. Lindenstrauss (2006) proved arithmetic QUE for Hecke–Maass forms on the modular surface, and partial entropy-bound results (Anantharaman, Anantharaman–Nonnenmacher, Dyatlov–Jin) constrain possible exceptional quantum limits, but no construction of exceptional eigenstates with non-Liouville semiclassical measure on a negatively curved manifold is known, and no proof of QUE in the general (non-arithmetic) negatively curved setting is known. The genericity version is also open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
context_brief: Amount of chaos needed for QUE
original_question: How much classical chaos is required for Quantum Unique Ergodicity: must the classical dynamics be uniformly hyperbolic, or Anosov, as in geodesic flows on negatively curved manifolds, or can systems with flat parts support exceptional eigenstates such as bouncing-ball modes?
self_contained_problem:
Quantum Unique Ergodicity (QUE) for a compact Riemannian manifold (M,g), possibly with boundary, asserts that for every orthonormal basis {ψ_n} of L²(M) consisting of Laplace–Beltrami eigenfunctions (with Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions if ∂M ≠ ∅), the probability measures |ψ_n(x)|² dvol_g converge weak-* to the normalized Riemannian volume as the eigenvalue tends to infinity (more strongly, all microlocal lifts of the ψ_n converge to Liouville measure on the unit cotangent bundle).

A classical flow is called Anosov (uniformly hyperbolic) if the tangent bundle of the phase space splits continuously into stable, unstable, and flow directions with uniform exponential contraction/expansion. The geodesic flow on a closed Riemannian manifold of strictly negative sectional curvature is Anosov. By contrast, the Bunimovich stadium (a planar billiard formed by a rectangle capped with two semicircular ends) is ergodic but not uniformly hyperbolic: it admits a one-parameter family of marginally unstable "bouncing-ball" trajectories that bounce vertically between the two parallel flat segments.

Determine how much classical chaos is required for QUE to hold. Specifically:

(a) Identify the minimal dynamical assumption on the geodesic (or billiard) flow under which QUE necessarily holds for the Laplace eigenfunctions. In particular, can QUE fail when the flow is ergodic but not uniformly hyperbolic, due to the presence of "flat parts" (regions where the flow has a family of neutrally stable trajectories)?

(b) For Riemannian manifolds or billiards whose phase space contains an invariant set of flat/marginally stable trajectories (such as bouncing-ball trajectories in the Bunimovich stadium), determine whether there exists a positive-density subsequence of eigenfunctions whose mass concentrates on the projection of these trajectories, thereby providing exceptional (non-equidistributed) quantum limits.
status_search_result: Part (b), the existence of exceptional non-equidistributed quantum limits in the Bunimovich stadium, has been resolved: Hassell (Annals of Mathematics, 2010, "Ergodic billiards that are not quantum unique ergodic," with appendix by Hassell–Hillairet) proved that for almost every aspect ratio in a certain range the stadium is ergodic but not QUE, with bouncing-ball quasimodes producing exceptional quantum limits. This shows QUE does not follow from mere ergodicity and that "flat parts" can support exceptional eigenstates. However, the broader question (a) — identifying the precise minimal amount of hyperbolicity/chaos required to guarantee QUE — remains open in general; QUE itself is known for arithmetic surfaces (Lindenstrauss, Soundararajan) but is not established for general negatively curved (Anosov) manifolds.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
original_question: Can the random-wave or random-state conjecture for chaotic eigenfunctions be made into a rigorous theorem at microscopic scales, or at intermediate scales between macroscopic size and the wavelength λ^−1? The question asks whether high-energy eigenfunctions ψ_k(x) of chaotic quantum systems have the same statistics as an appropriate random-state ensemble, including value distributions, wavelength-scale correlation functions, nodal sets, and nodal components.
status_search_result: Berry's random wave conjecture for eigenfunctions of chaotic systems remains a central open problem. Rigorous random-wave behavior has been established only in special settings: certain arithmetic cases (e.g. partial results for dihedral Maass forms, including planck-scale mass equidistribution and fourth-moment asymptotics), and Benjamini–Schramm limit results on hyperbolic surfaces.
