context_brief: Initial homogeneity and the Weyl tensor condition
original_question: Is the relevant low-entropy condition of the early universe best understood as primordial homogeneity, as Penrose’s vanishing-Weyl-tensor condition on past singularities, or as some closely related condition; and if the Weyl condition cannot be explained by absorptive matter in the way electromagnetic retardation can, must it instead be taken as the law-like ingredient that establishes the causal asymmetry of the universe by excluding future-relevant initial correlations?
self_contained_problem:

One proposal identifies this initial low-entropy condition with the spatial homogeneity of the early universe; a sharper formulation, due to Penrose, postulates that the Weyl curvature tensor vanishes on all past (initial) singularities, while no analogous restriction is imposed on future singularities.

(b) In the analogy with electromagnetism, the use of purely retarded radiation (excluding incoming free fields) can be derived from the presence of a sufficient distribution of absorbing matter (the Sommerfeld/Wheeler–Feynman absorber argument). context_brief: Black holes, singularities, and information loss
original_question: In the quantum-gravitational treatment of black holes, should one impose a time-symmetric Weyl-tensor condition on all spacelike singularities, and would doing so eliminate genuine black-hole interiors, horizons, or information loss? Because the black-hole interior is causally inaccessible and quantum gravity no longer sharply distinguishes past from future singularities, the unresolved issue is whether a symmetric singularity condition is the correct way to understand black-hole entropy and avoid the information-loss paradox.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In a Lorentzian 4-manifold (M,g) modelling a spacetime in a quantum-gravitational regime, let C_{abcd} denote the Weyl conformal curvature tensor of g. A "Weyl curvature condition" at a spacelike singularity Σ ⊂ ∂M is the requirement that, in a suitable limit toward Σ, an appropriate scalar invariant of the Weyl tensor (e.g. C_{abcd}C^{abcd} relative to the Ricci scalar squared, or a similar measure of Weyl anisotropy) vanishes, so that Σ is conformally regular. The classical Weyl curvature hypothesis imposes this only on initial (past) spacelike singularities, thereby providing a low-entropy past boundary condition while permitting generic high-Weyl future singularities inside black holes.

Consider instead the time-symmetric Weyl curvature condition: require that C_{abcd} satisfies the same vanishing/regularity condition on every spacelike singularity of M, both past and future, on the grounds that in quantum gravity past and future singularities cannot be sharply distinguished and that the interior of a black hole is causally inaccessible to external observers.

Problems.
(a) Determine whether the time-symmetric Weyl curvature condition is mathematically consistent with the known classical and semiclassical observational constraints on cosmological and astrophysical spacetimes (in particular, with the existence of the observed CMB low-entropy initial state and with the exterior geometry of astrophysical black holes).

(b) Determine whether imposing this time-symmetric condition forces, at the level of the allowed quantum-gravitational spacetimes, the absence of genuine event horizons and trapped black-hole interiors — i.e. whether all apparent black-hole-like regions must be replaced by horizonless, information-preserving configurations.

(c) Decide whether such a condition provides a consistent statistical-mechanical account of black-hole entropy (e.g. reproducing the Bekenstein–Hawking area law as a coarse-grained entropy) while avoiding any genuine information-loss paradox in the global evolution.

State and prove (or disprove) the precise theorems answering (a), (b), and (c) within a chosen rigorous framework for semiclassical or quantum gravity.

context_brief: Emergence of time in Wheeler-DeWitt quantum gravity
original_question: How do physical time and its arrow emerge in quantum gravity when the fundamental Wheeler-DeWitt equation has no external time parameter? More specifically, if the quantum-gravitational wave functional satisfies HΨ = 0 and there is no external variable t with respect to which a time direction can be defined, under what assumptions and through what mechanism can one recover an effective physical time and a corresponding arrow of time from intrinsic variables and semiclassical structure?

Consider canonical quantum gravity in the Wheeler–DeWitt formulation. Let configuration space be superspace, the space of Riemannian 3-metrics h_{ab} on a spatial slice (together with non-gravitational matter fields φ), modulo spatial diffeomorphisms. A physical state is described by a wave functional Ψ[h_{ab}, φ] satisfying the Wheeler–DeWitt constraint

   H Ψ[h_{ab}, φ] = 0,

where H is the Hamiltonian constraint operator (a hyperbolic second-order functional differential operator on superspace whose kinetic term involves the DeWitt supermetric, which has indefinite signature with one negative direction associated with the local scale of h_{ab}). Because Ψ has no explicit dependence on any external parameter t, the equation contains no a priori notion of time evolution and no a priori arrow of time.

Problem. Formulate precise assumptions on (i) the structure of Ψ (for example, a WKB/semiclassical ansatz Ψ ≈ C[h] exp(i S[h]/ℏ) χ[h, φ] with respect to a suitable expansion parameter, such as an inverse power of the Planck mass), (ii) boundary conditions on Ψ in superspace (for instance, conditions imposed in the limit of vanishing three-volume), and (iii) the decomposition of degrees of freedom into "heavy/geometric" and "light/matter" sectors, under which one can:

(a) derive an effective Schrödinger-type equation iℏ ∂_τ χ = H_matter χ for the light sector, where τ is an intrinsic parameter constructed from the heavy variables (e.g. along integral curves of ∇S on superspace), so that τ plays the role of a physical, emergent time;

(b) identify a mechanism — for example, a low-entropy/simplicity condition on Ψ at the boundary corresponding to small three-volume together with decoherence between semiclassical branches — that singles out a preferred direction along τ, thereby producing an arrow of time correlated with the growth of suitable entropy functionals.

State explicitly the minimal set of assumptions on H, on Ψ, and on the boundary behaviour in superspace, and exhibit the construction of τ and of the asymmetry of correlations along τ that yields both an effective physical time and its arrow from a fundamentally timeless equation HΨ = 0.

context_brief: Initial conditions for partial Schrödinger waves
original_question: Can the global intrinsic dynamics of the Wheeler-DeWitt framework determine the initial conditions of the partial Schrödinger waves that appear in the semiclassical WKB regime? Since the WKB approximation yields approximately autonomous matter-wave evolution along quasi-classical geometries but does not by itself justify an ensemble of trajectories, the unresolved problem is how the full, timeless quantum state fixes the initial data for the branch-dependent partial waves observed as evolving quasi-classical worlds.
self_contained_problem:
Consider canonical quantum gravity coupled to matter, in which physical states $|\Psi\rangle$ are annihilated by the Hamiltonian constraint, yielding the timeless Wheeler–DeWitt equation
$$\hat{\mathcal{H}}\,\Psi[h_{ij},\phi] = 0,$$
where $h_{ij}$ denotes a spatial 3-metric on a closed 3-manifold and $\phi$ collectively denotes matter fields. In a semiclassical (WKB) regime far from a putative initial singularity, one expands
$$\Psi[h,\phi] \approx \sum_{\alpha} A_{\alpha}[h]\, e^{i S_{\alpha}[h]/\hbar}\, \chi_{\alpha}[h,\phi],$$
where each phase $S_\alpha$ satisfies the gravitational Hamilton–Jacobi equation, defining a congruence of quasi-classical 4-geometries, and the matter wave functional $\chi_\alpha[h,\phi]$ obeys, to leading order in $\hbar$, an effective Schrödinger equation
$$i\hbar\, \nabla S_\alpha \cdot \delta_{h}\chi_\alpha = \hat{H}_{\text{matter}}[h,\phi]\,\chi_\alpha$$
along the integral curves of $\nabla S_\alpha$. Each $\chi_\alpha$ is a "partial Schrödinger wave" associated with one branch of the global superposition.

Problem: Determine whether the intrinsic global dynamics encoded by the Wheeler–DeWitt equation, together with any natural boundary condition on $\Psi$ at small 3-geometries (the "big-bang" boundary of superspace), uniquely fixes the initial data $\chi_\alpha[h_0,\phi]$ for every partial Schrödinger wave $\chi_\alpha$ on a hypersurface of constant $S_\alpha$ in the WKB region. Equivalently, give a derivation that selects, from the timeless quantum state $\Psi$, a canonical assignment of initial conditions for each branch-dependent matter wave $\chi_\alpha$, or prove that no such derivation exists within the framework, so that additional postulates beyond the Wheeler–DeWitt dynamics are required.
status_search_result: No published derivation appears to extract canonical initial data for the branch-dependent partial Schrödinger waves of the WKB expansion directly from the timeless Wheeler–DeWitt state. Standard references on the Wheeler–DeWitt equation and its semiclassical (WKB) limit treat such initial conditions as additional input (e.g., via Hartle–Hawking or tunneling proposals), and the issue of justifying an ensemble of WKB branches and their matter initial states remains a recognized foundational problem in quantum cosmology.

If negative a is interpreted as a pre-big-bang phase, one must explain how WKB time could continue through a = 0 and how a low-entropy state at a = 0 could have been preceded by an even lower-entropy state at a < 0 without forcing a reversal of the thermodynamic arrow in an oscillating-universe picture.
self_contained_problem:
In the Wheeler–DeWitt formulation of quantum cosmology for a homogeneous and isotropic universe with scale factor a, the wavefunction Ψ(a, φ) (with φ a matter field) is governed by a hyperbolic-type constraint equation that admits, in suitable regimes, a WKB form Ψ ≈ A(a, φ) exp(iS(a, φ)/ℏ) from which a notion of classical "WKB time" emerges via the gradient of S. The classical configuration variable a is taken to be nonnegative, but the Wheeler–DeWitt equation is naturally defined for all real a, and one may attempt to extend solutions and the dynamics through a = 0 to negative values of a.

Loop quantum cosmology refines this picture by replacing the differential operator in a by a difference operator on a discrete lattice in a (or in volume), and the resulting quantum dynamics is also formally defined for negative values of a.

Address the following questions in this setting:

(a) Determine whether negative values of the scale factor a admit a consistent physical interpretation after extending the (Wheeler–DeWitt or loop quantum cosmology) dynamics through a = 0, and in particular whether they can represent a "pre-big-bang" epoch.

(b) Establish whether, and in what precise sense, the WKB time function S can be continued through the locus a = 0 so as to provide a classical-time interpretation on both sides.

(c) In an oscillating-universe interpretation in which a < 0 is identified with a pre-big-bang phase, decide whether it is possible to have a low-entropy state at a = 0 preceded by an even lower-entropy state at a < 0 without forcing a reversal of the thermodynamic arrow of time, and reconcile this with the second law of thermodynamics.

Provide a precise mathematical and physical resolution, or demonstrate that no consistent extension is possible.

While LQC generically replaces the singularity by a bounce, the physical status of the pre-bounce branch and its compatibility with a single thermodynamic arrow remain unresolved, with multiple competing proposals (Janus-point, two-sided arrows, low-entropy initial conditions). No consensus resolution to the questions posed has been established.

original_question: Let K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, and G be the classes of groups considered in the paper, and recall that Theorem 1.1 proves the following statement whenever A and B are members of this collection with B properly contained in A and A containing K_3: there is no algorithm that decides, given a finite presentation of a group known to lie in A, whether that group lies in B. Does the same undecidability statement remain true in the case A = K_2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following classes of finitely presentable groups arising from codimension‑2 embeddings:

- $\mathcal{K}_n$ ($n=0,1,2,3$): the class of fundamental groups $\pi_1(S^{n+2}\setminus \Sigma)$, where $\Sigma\subset S^{n+2}$ ranges over locally flat embedded $n$‑spheres (so $\mathcal{K}_0=\{\mathbb{Z}\}$, and $\mathcal{K}_n$ is the class of classical knot groups, 2‑knot groups, 3‑knot groups for $n=1,2,3$).
- $\mathcal{S}$: the class of fundamental groups of complements of orientable closed surfaces locally flatly embedded in $S^4$.
- $\mathcal{M}$: the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flatly embedded simply connected closed 4‑manifolds in $S^6$.
- $\mathcal{G}$: the class of all finitely presentable groups.

These satisfy the strict inclusions $\{\mathbb{Z}\}=\mathcal{K}_0\subsetneq\mathcal{K}_1\subsetneq\mathcal{K}_2\subsetneq\mathcal{K}_3\subsetneq\mathcal{S}\subsetneq\mathcal{M}\subsetneq\mathcal{G}$.

It is known that for every choice of $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\in\{\mathcal{K}_0,\mathcal{K}_1,\mathcal{K}_2,\mathcal{K}_3,\mathcal{S},\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G}\}$ with $\mathcal{B}\subsetneq\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{A}\supseteq\mathcal{K}_3$, there is no algorithm that, given a finite presentation of a group $G\in\mathcal{A}$, decides whether $G\in\mathcal{B}$.

Question: Does the same undecidability statement hold when $\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{K}_2$? That is, for every $\mathcal{B}\in\{\mathcal{K}_0,\mathcal{K}_1\}$ (the proper subclasses of $\mathcal{K}_2$ in this list), is it true that no algorithm exists which, given a finite presentation of a group $G$ that is known to lie in $\mathcal{K}_2$, decides whether $G\in\mathcal{B}$?

Equivalently, does there exist a group in $\mathcal{K}_2$ (i.e., a 2‑knot group) with unsolvable word problem?
status_search_result: Available sources indicate the question reduces to whether some 2‑knot group has unsolvable word problem, which is widely cited as an open problem. No published resolution was located.

original_question: Is the isomorphism problem for 2-knot groups algorithmically unsolvable? In other words, is there no algorithm that takes finite presentations of two groups known to belong to K_2, the class of groups of 2-knots, and always decides whether the two groups are isomorphic?
self_contained_problem:
A 2-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding of the 2-sphere $S^2$ into the 4-sphere $S^4$. The group of a 2-knot $K \subset S^4$ is the fundamental group $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K)$ of its complement. Let $\mathcal{K}_2$ denote the class of all groups that arise as groups of 2-knots; each such group admits a finite presentation.

Question: Is the isomorphism problem for $\mathcal{K}_2$ algorithmically unsolvable? Equivalently, prove or disprove that there is no algorithm which, given two finite presentations of groups both known to lie in $\mathcal{K}_2$, always halts and correctly decides whether the two presented groups are isomorphic.
status_search_result: The unsolvability of the isomorphism problem is established for 3-knot groups (and larger classes containing them), since every finitely presented group embeds in a 3-knot group. For 2-knot groups the question is conjectured but unresolved; it would follow if a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem could be exhibited, which is currently not known. No subsequent resolution was found in the search.

original_question: Does there exist a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem? Here K_2 is the class of groups of 2-knots, so the question asks whether some group of a 2-knot has no algorithm deciding, for an arbitrary word in its generators, whether that word represents the identity element.
self_contained_problem:
A 2-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding of the 2-sphere $S^2$ into the 4-sphere $S^4$. The group of a 2-knot $K\subset S^4$ is the fundamental group $\pi_1(S^4\setminus K)$ of its complement. A finitely presented group $G=\langle x_1,\dots,x_n \mid r_1,\dots,r_m\rangle$ is said to have solvable word problem if there exists an algorithm that, given any word $w$ in the generators $x_1^{\pm 1},\dots,x_n^{\pm 1}$, decides whether $w$ represents the identity element of $G$; otherwise $G$ has unsolvable word problem.

Question: Does there exist a 2-knot $K\subset S^4$ such that the 2-knot group $\pi_1(S^4\setminus K)$ has unsolvable word problem?

original_question: Does every finitely presented group embed in a 2-knot group? That is, for each finitely presented group G, must there exist a group in K_2, the class of groups of 2-knots, that contains an isomorphic copy of G as a subgroup?
self_contained_problem:
A 2-knot is a smooth (or locally flat topological) embedding $K\colon S^2 \hookrightarrow S^4$ of the 2-sphere into the 4-sphere. The group of the 2-knot $K$ is $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K(S^2))$. Let $\mathcal{K}_2$ denote the class of all groups that arise as the group of some 2-knot.

Question: Does every finitely presented group embed as a subgroup of some group in $\mathcal{K}_2$? Equivalently, for every finitely presented group $G$, must there exist a 2-knot $K \subset S^4$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\pi_1(S^4 \setminus K(S^2))$?
status_search_result: No published resolution of the question was found in the search. The question is posed as a conjecture (with the conjectured answer "yes") in survey-style writings on 2-knot groups, and recent literature on 2-knot groups (e.g., work on ribbon 2-knot groups) does not report a proof or disproof. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: In the setting of Theorem 5.1, let C be a class of infinite sequences of abelian groups, closed under isomorphism, such that there exist finitely presented groups G_1 and G_2 with the same first homology H_1(G_1) isomorphic to H_1(G_2), with H_*(G_1) in C and H_*(G_2) not in C. Theorem 5.1 proves that the set of finite presentations P for which the integral homology sequence H_*(P) belongs to C is not recursive. Under what additional hypotheses on C can this conclusion be strengthened by replacing 'not recursive' with 'not recursively enumerable'?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite presentation $P = \langle x_1,\dots,x_n \mid r_1,\dots,r_m\rangle$ of a group $G_P$, let $H_*(P) = (H_1(G_P), H_2(G_P), H_3(G_P), \dots)$ denote the sequence of integral homology groups of $G_P$ (equivalently, of the Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G_P,1)$). Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of infinite sequences $(A_1, A_2, A_3, \dots)$ of abelian groups which is closed under isomorphism (i.e., if $(A_i) \in \mathcal{C}$ and $A_i \cong B_i$ for all $i$, then $(B_i) \in \mathcal{C}$). Assume there exist finitely presented groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with $H_1(G_1) \cong H_1(G_2)$, $H_*(G_1) \in \mathcal{C}$, and $H_*(G_2) \notin \mathcal{C}$. It is known that under these hypotheses the set
$$ \{ P : P \text{ is a finite presentation with } H_*(P) \in \mathcal{C} \} $$
is not recursive. Determine additional hypotheses on the class $\mathcal{C}$ under which this set can be shown to be not recursively enumerable.

context_brief: Unknot recognition for surfaces in S4
original_question: If g is a non-negative integer, is there an algorithm to decide whether or not a given locally flat PL-embedded surface of genus g in S^4 is unknotted?
self_contained_problem:
Let $g$ be a non-negative integer. Consider closed surfaces of genus $g$ that are locally flatly PL-embedded in the 4-sphere $S^4$. Such a surface $\Sigma \subset S^4$ is said to be unknotted if it bounds a locally flat PL-embedded 3-dimensional handlebody in $S^4$ (equivalently, it is ambient isotopic to the standard genus-$g$ surface). 

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a finite combinatorial description (e.g., a triangulation) of a locally flat PL-embedded genus-$g$ surface $\Sigma \subset S^4$, decides whether or not $\Sigma$ is unknotted?
status_search_result: No algorithm is known for deciding whether a locally flat PL-embedded surface of genus g in S^4 is unknotted. While topological characterizations of unknottedness (via fundamental group of the complement) have been established by Freedman–Quinn (g=0), Hillman–Kawauchi, and more recent work for higher genus, these characterizations are not known to give a decision algorithm, and the algorithmic problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: TV convergence in stationary ergodic G/G/m FCFS
original_question: Consider the multi-server first-come-first-served queue G/G/m with interarrival times {(t_n)} and service times {(sigma_n)} such that the two-dimensional sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, the stability condition E sigma_1 < m E t_1 holds, and the Kiefer-Wolfowitz workload vector starts from the zero initial value. Is it true that, under these assumptions alone and without any further mixing or regenerative condition, the distribution of the workload vector converges in total variation to a stationary distribution as n tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-server first-come-first-served queue with $m\ge 2$ identical servers. Let $\{(\sigma_n, t_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary ergodic sequence of nonnegative random variables, where $\sigma_n$ is the service time of the $n$th customer and $t_n$ is the interarrival time between customers $n$ and $n+1$. Assume the stability condition
$$ \mathbb{E}\,\sigma_1 < m\,\mathbb{E}\,t_1, \qquad 0<\mathbb{E}\,t_1<\infty. $$
Let $W_n=(W_n^{(1)},\dots,W_n^{(m)})\in\mathbb{R}_+^m$ denote the Kiefer–Wolfowitz workload vector at the arrival epoch of customer $n$ (with components arranged in nondecreasing order), defined by the recursion
$$ W_{n+1} = R\big( (W_n + \sigma_n e_1 - t_n \mathbf{1})^+ \big), $$
where $e_1=(1,0,\dots,0)$, $\mathbf{1}=(1,1,\dots,1)$, $(\cdot)^+$ is taken componentwise, and $R$ rearranges its argument in nondecreasing order. Suppose the recursion is started from the deterministic initial condition $W_0=0$.

It is known that there exists a stationary distribution $\pi$ for $\{W_n\}$ on $\mathbb{R}_+^m$. Prove or disprove the following statement: under the above assumptions alone (stationarity, ergodicity, stability, and zero initial value), and without any additional mixing, regenerative, or distributional assumptions on $\{(\sigma_n,t_n)\}$, the law of $W_n$ converges to $\pi$ in total variation, i.e.
$$ \sup_{A\subset\mathbb{R}_+^m}\big| \mathbb{P}(W_n\in A) - \pi(A) \big| \;\longrightarrow\; 0 \quad\text{as } n\to\infty. $$

Foss in Queueing Systems (vol. 100, pp. 293–295), titled "Convergence in the total variation norm in multiserver queues," revisits this conjecture; available evidence indicates the conjecture in its full generality (stationary ergodic input with no extra mixing or regenerative assumption) remains an open problem, with positive results known only under additional structural assumptions.

context_brief: Moments of stationary delay at integer load
original_question: Let D be the stationary waiting time in an i.i.d. G/G/m first-come-first-served queue where the service-time sequence {(sigma_n)} and interarrival-time sequence {(t_n)} are independent, identically distributed, and satisfy rho := E sigma_1 / E t_1 < m. When rho is an integer, what conditions are necessary and sufficient for the power moment E D^gamma to be finite?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a first-come-first-served multi-server queue with $m \ge 2$ identical servers fed by a single arrival stream. Let $\{\sigma_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be the i.i.d. sequence of service times and $\{t_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ the i.i.d. sequence of interarrival times, and assume the two sequences are mutually independent. Define the traffic intensity
$$\rho := \frac{\mathbb{E}\sigma_1}{\mathbb{E} t_1},$$
and assume the stability condition $\rho < m$, so that the stationary distribution of the waiting time is unique. Let $D$ denote the stationary waiting time (the delay before service begins) of a typical customer in this queue.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the distributions of $\sigma_1$ and $t_1$ for the power moment $\mathbb{E}[D^{\gamma}]$ to be finite, in the boundary regime where $\rho$ is a positive integer (i.e., $\rho \in \{1, 2, \dots, m-1\}$), as a function of the exponent $\gamma > 0$.
status_search_result: Scheller-Wolf and Vesilo (2003, 2006) and Foss–Korshunov (2012, "On Large Delays in Multi-Server Queues with Heavy Tails") provide matching necessary and sufficient moment conditions for non-integer ρ via a "principle of (s−⌊ρ⌋) big jumps." The integer ρ case remains a known boundary gap in these results, where existing upper and lower bounds do not match; no source found that fully resolves the integer-ρ case.

context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue at rho=1
original_question: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho = 1 and the service-time distribution is subexponential (for example regularly varying), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a GI/GI/2 first-come-first-served queue with two identical servers. Customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean $1/\lambda$, and require i.i.d. service times $\{S_n\}$, independent of the arrivals, with common distribution function $F$ having mean $\mathbb{E} S < \infty$. Define the traffic intensity $ho = \lambda \mathbb{E} S / 2$, and assume that under $ho < 1$ the system possesses a unique stationary distribution; let $D$ denote a random variable with the stationary waiting-time distribution.

Assume that the service-time distribution $F$ is subexponential, i.e., $\overline{F}(x) := 1 - F(x) > 0$ for all $x$ and $\overline{F*F}(x)/\overline{F}(x) 	o 2$ as $x 	o \infty$. As a concrete representative case, one may take $F$ to be regularly varying at infinity with index $-\alpha$, $\alpha > 1$, meaning $\overline{F}(x) = x^{-\alpha} L(x)$ for some slowly varying function $L$.

In the critical regime $ho = 1$ (taken as a limiting/boundary case in which a stationary waiting time can still be defined, e.g., via appropriate scaling or via a suitable taboo / time-stationary version), determine the asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb{P}(D > x)$ as $x 	o \infty$. Specifically, provide an explicit asymptotic equivalent (with constant) of $\mathbb{P}(D > x)$ for at least one such subexponential family of service-time distributions, and identify the typical sample-path behavior (the dominant trajectories of arrivals and services) that produces a large stationary waiting time.

Sharp asymptotics with explicit constant are established in some sub-cases, while general subexponential service-time distributions are not fully covered, so the problem is partially solved.

context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue with finite moments
original_question: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho in (1, 2) and the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) for some beta in (0, 1), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a stable FCFS GI/GI/2 queue with two identical servers. Customers arrive at the epochs of a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times $\{\tau_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ having mean $1/\lambda$, and require i.i.d. service times $\{\sigma_n\}_{n\ge 1}$, independent of the arrivals, with mean $\mathbb{E}\sigma_1 < \infty$. Define the traffic intensity $\rho = \lambda\, \mathbb{E}\sigma_1$, and assume $\rho < 2$ (so a stationary regime exists). Let $D$ denote the stationary waiting time of a typical customer.

Assume that the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed (i.e.\ $\mathbb{E}\,e^{\varepsilon \sigma_1} = \infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$) but has all power moments finite; as a concrete representative case, assume the Weibull-type tail
$$\mathbb{P}(\sigma_1 > x) = \exp(-x^\beta), \qquad x \ge 0,$$
for some fixed $\beta \in (0,1)$.

Suppose moreover that $\rho \in (1,2)$, i.e.\ the system is stable but each individual server is overloaded.

Determine the exact asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb{P}(D > x)$ as $x \to \infty$ in this regime. In particular, find a function $f(x)$ such that
$$\mathbb{P}(D > x) \sim f(x) \quad \text{as } x \to \infty,$$
or otherwise identify the logarithmic asymptotics $\log \mathbb{P}(D > x)$ to leading order.
status_search_result: The exact tail asymptotics of the stationary waiting time in the GI/GI/2 queue with Weibull-type service times in the regime $\rho\in(1,2)$ appear to remain open. Related work (Foss–Korshunov on large delays in multi-server queues, and Bazhba–Blanchet–Rhee–Zwart 2019 on Weibull queue-length asymptotics) gives logarithmic/sample-path large-deviations results for related quantities, but a complete sharp tail for $\mathbb{P}(D>x)$ in the overloaded-per-server regime $\rho\in(1,2)$ has not been established; existing arguments for $\rho<1$ do not extend, and steady-state results in the Weibull case have been obtained mainly for queue length in transient settings.

context_brief: Typical paths producing large stationary delays
original_question: For the two-server queue regimes just described, namely the case rho = 1 with a subexponential service-time distribution and the case rho in (1, 2) with a heavy-tailed service-time distribution having all power moments finite, what are the typical sample paths that lead to large values of the stationary waiting time D?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a FCFS GI/GI/2 queue with two identical servers. Customers arrive at epochs of a renewal process with i.i.d. interarrival times having mean 1/λ, and require i.i.d. service times {σ_n} with common distribution F, independent of the interarrival process. Let ρ = λ E[σ]/2 denote the traffic intensity per server (so ρ < 1 ensures stability), and let D denote the stationary waiting time (time spent waiting in queue, not in service) in steady state, assumed to exist in distribution.

Two regimes are of interest:

(a) Critical load with subexponential service: ρ = 1 and F is subexponential, i.e. F has support on [0,∞), F̄(x) := 1 − F(x) > 0 for all x, and the convolution F*F satisfies F*F(x)/F̄(x) → 2 as x → ∞.

(b) Overloaded regime with light power tails: ρ ∈ (1,2), and the service-time distribution F is heavy-tailed (not exponentially bounded) yet has all power moments finite, i.e. ∫₀^∞ x^k dF(x) < ∞ for every integer k ≥ 0.

Identify, in each of regimes (a) and (b), the typical sample paths of the arrival and service processes that produce a large value of the stationary waiting time D. Specifically, describe (in a precise large-deviations or "principle of big jumps" sense) the dominant scenario by which the event {D > x} occurs as x → ∞, including how many and which customers experience large service times, the orders of magnitude of those services, and the structure of the surrounding interarrival pattern.
status_search_result: For the standard stable regime ρ ∈ (0,1) with subexponential service, Foss–Korshunov established a "principle of s−k big jumps" identifying the typical sample paths producing large D. Subsequent work (e.g., Foss–Korshunov 2012; the half-loaded GI/GI/2 paper by Boxma–Foss–Korshunov, 2015) addressed tail asymptotics in the critical case ρ = 1 with heavy-tailed services and partial results in overloaded regimes, but a complete description of typical sample paths in the regimes ρ = 1 (subexponential) and ρ ∈ (1,2) (heavy-tailed with all power moments) does not appear to be settled in the literature accessible to this search. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

context_brief: Number of stationary regimes for join-the-shortest-queue
original_question: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and the join-the-shortest-queue discipline, meaning each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest of the individual queues. Assuming only the obvious stability condition and no extra hypotheses, how many stationary regimes can this model have?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-server queueing system operating in continuous time. Customers arrive according to a marked point process {(t_n, σ_n) : n ∈ Z} that is jointly stationary and ergodic on some probability space, where t_n is the arrival epoch of customer n (with t_n < t_{n+1} and Et_1 - Et_0 = 1/λ for some 0 < λ < ∞) and σ_n ≥ 0 is the service requirement of customer n (with Eσ_0 = 1/μ for some 0 < μ < ∞). There are two servers, each having its own individual FIFO queue. The dispatching discipline is "Join the Shortest Queue" (JSQ): upon arrival, customer n is routed to the queue with the smallest current number of customers; ties are broken uniformly at random. Each server works at unit speed and is non-idling, processing the customers assigned to its queue in order of arrival.

Assume only the natural stability condition λ < 2μ (i.e. ρ := λ/(2μ) < 1), and impose no further structural hypothesis on the joint law of {(t_n, σ_n)} (in particular, no independence, no renewal, and no light-tail assumption beyond the integrability already stated).

Determine, under these assumptions, the number of distinct stationary regimes (i.e. jointly stationary and ergodic solutions, on a possibly enlarged probability space, of the dynamical recursion describing the workload/queue-length process driven by the input) that the system can admit. In particular: must the stationary regime be unique, can there be finitely many, or can there be infinitely many?
status_search_result: Web search did not surface a result settling the number of stationary regimes for the two-server JSQ queue with general stationary-ergodic input under only the natural stability condition. Existing literature (e.g. Bramson–Lu–Prabhakar on stability of JSQ networks, and subsequent works on stationary analysis and Halfin–Whitt diffusion limits) treats stability and convergence under additional independence/renewal assumptions, but does not resolve uniqueness vs. multiplicity of stationary regimes in the general stationary-ergodic setting. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For the same join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input, what are the minimal assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with two identical servers fed by a single arrival stream. Customer $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ arrives at time $T_n=\sum_{k<n}t_k$ (with $t_n>0$ the inter-arrival times) and brings a service requirement $\sigma_n\ge 0$. Assume that $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is a stationary ergodic sequence on some probability space equipped with a measure-preserving shift, with finite means $\mathbb{E}[t_0]=1/\lambda$ and $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0]=1/\mu$, satisfying the natural stability condition $\lambda<2\mu$. Customers are routed under the join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) discipline: upon arrival, customer $n$ is sent to the server whose current workload (sum of remaining service times of customers already there) is the smaller of the two, with ties broken by a fixed deterministic rule. Each server processes its queue in first-in-first-out order at unit speed.

Let $W_n=(W_n^{(1)},W_n^{(2)})$ denote the pair of workloads seen by customer $n$ at arrival. A stationary regime is a stationary distribution for the workload process $\{W_n\}$ on the underlying ergodic dynamical system (equivalently, a finite random vector $W$ jointly stationary with the input sequence and satisfying the JSQ recursion).

Determine minimal assumptions on the joint distribution of the stationary ergodic input $\{(t_n,\sigma_n)\}$ (beyond the stability condition $\lambda<2\mu$) which guarantee that the stationary regime of the workload process under JSQ is unique.
status_search_result: Recent work on JSQ focuses on many-server asymptotics, Halfin–Whitt diffusion limits, and stability under i.i.d. or Markovian inputs, but no source establishes minimal conditions for uniqueness of the stationary regime under general stationary ergodic input. The question of minimal assumptions for uniqueness in the stationary ergodic JSQ setting appears to remain open.

original_question: For the join-the-shortest-queue model with stationary ergodic input and only the obvious stability condition, under what conditions, if any, do the queue-length or workload distributions converge weakly or in total variation to stationarity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a join-the-shortest-queue (JSQ) system with $K \geq 2$ parallel single-server queues. Customers arrive at epochs $\{T_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ and the $n$-th customer brings a service requirement $\sigma_n$. Assume that the marked point process $\{(T_n,\sigma_n)\}$ is stationary and ergodic on some probability space, with finite intensity $\lambda$ and mean service requirement $\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0]$. Each arriving customer is routed to a queue with the shortest current workload (or, in a parallel formulation, the shortest queue length), with ties broken by a fixed measurable rule; each server works at unit speed and serves its queue in FIFO order. Assume the natural (and necessary) stability condition $\lambda\,\mathbb{E}[\sigma_0] < K$.

Let $Q(t) = (Q_1(t),\dots,Q_K(t))$ denote the vector of queue lengths and $W(t) = (W_1(t),\dots,W_K(t))$ the vector of workloads at time $t$.

Determine conditions on the input process $\{(T_n,\sigma_n)\}$ (beyond stationarity, ergodicity and the stability condition above) under which the laws of $Q(t)$ and/or $W(t)$ converge, as $t\to\infty$, weakly (and/or in total variation) to a stationary distribution. In particular, decide whether such convergence holds under stationary ergodic input alone, or exhibit a minimal additional hypothesis that guarantees it.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a resolution of the JSQ convergence-to-stationarity question under general stationary ergodic input. Existing literature treats either Markovian (Poisson/exponential) inputs (where exponential ergodicity and convergence in total variation are established, e.g., in the Halfin–Whitt regime), heavy-traffic diffusion limits, two-queue or orbit-queue special cases, or stability/large-deviations results. The lack of monotonicity of JSQ obstructs Loynes-type constructions, and no general weak/total-variation convergence theorem for JSQ with arbitrary stationary ergodic input appears to have been published, so the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Stability of a greedy server on a circle
original_question: A single server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda and are placed uniformly on the circle. Serving a particle takes one unit of time, and after each service the server moves at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server model stable for every lambda < 1?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following continuous-time stochastic service system on the unit circle. A single server is located on the circle and moves along it at a fixed positive finite speed. Particles (customers) arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda > 0$ in time, and each arriving particle is placed at a position drawn independently and uniformly on the circle, independently of everything else. Service of any particle takes exactly one unit of time, during which the server remains at the particle's location. Immediately after completing a service, the particle disappears and the server selects the waiting particle whose arc-distance to its current position is smallest, then travels to that particle along the circle at the fixed speed (ties broken arbitrarily); during this travel the server does not respond to any newly arriving particles. Once it reaches the chosen particle, service begins, and the procedure repeats.

Let $Q(t)$ denote the number of particles waiting (including any in service) at time $t$. Prove or disprove the following: for every $\lambda < 1$ and every fixed positive finite server speed, the system is stable, in the sense that the underlying Markov process describing the configuration of waiting particles and the server is positive recurrent.
category_tag: Stability of greedy server queueing systems
status_search_result: The conjecture, originally due to Coffman and Gilbert (1987), was resolved affirmatively by Rojas-Nandayapa, Foss, and Kroese in "Stability of the Greedy Algorithm on the Circle" (arXiv:1112.2389), which proves positive recurrence for any arrival rate strictly less than the service rate, at any positive finite server speed.

context_brief: Stability of black-white particle circle model
original_question: On a circle, black particles arrive according to a Poisson stream of rate lambda and remain there, while white particles arrive according to an independent Poisson stream of rate 1 and immediately disappear after, if possible, deleting the nearest black particle within distance epsilon of their arrival location. Is this model stable whenever lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and of epsilon?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a circle of length $L>0$ and a parameter $\varepsilon>0$. Consider two independent Poisson processes in time on the circle:

- Black particles arrive in space-time according to a Poisson process of intensity $\lambda$ per unit length per unit time. Upon arrival, a black particle is placed at its arrival location on the circle and remains there forever (unless deleted).
- White particles arrive in space-time according to an independent Poisson process of intensity $1$ per unit length per unit time. When a white particle arrives at a point $x$ on the circle, it inspects the set of currently present black particles within (geodesic) distance $\varepsilon$ from $x$. If this set is non-empty, the white particle deletes the black particle nearest to $x$ (with ties broken arbitrarily), and then disappears immediately. If no black particle lies within distance $\varepsilon$ of $x$, the white particle disappears without effect.

Let $N_t$ denote the number of black particles present on the circle at time $t\ge 0$, starting from any initial configuration with finitely many black particles.

Question: Is it true that whenever $\lambda<1$, the process $(N_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is stable (i.e. positive recurrent, with a unique stationary distribution to which it converges from any initial condition), for every choice of circle length $L>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$?
category_tag: Interacting particle systems on a circle
status_search_result: Web searches did not turn up a published resolution of this conjecture. The problem appears to remain open in the literature on stability of greedy/matching particle systems on the circle, but no definitive recent reference confirming or refuting it was located.

original_question: Consider the following queueing system. There are three servers and a Poisson arrival process of rate lambda. Each arrival becomes class 1, 2, or 3 with probability 1/3. Class 1 customers may be served by servers 1 and 2, class 2 customers by servers 2 and 3, and class 3 customers by servers 3 and 1. Upon arrival, a customer chooses the accessible server with the shorter workload. If served by its left server, the service time has distribution F_l; if served by its right server, the service time has distribution F_r. In this model, can stability depend on both the initial state and the full service-time distributions F_l and F_r rather than only on coarse summary parameters?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following queueing system. Three servers, labeled 1, 2, and 3, are arranged cyclically. Customers arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda > 0$. Independently, each arrival is labeled class $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ with probability $1/3$. Class 1 customers may be served only by servers 1 or 2; class 2 customers only by servers 2 or 3; class 3 customers only by servers 3 or 1. For each class, designate one of its two accessible servers as "left" and the other as "right" (in the cyclic order). Upon arrival, a customer joins the accessible server whose current workload is smaller (with some fixed tie-breaking rule). The customer's service time is drawn independently from a distribution $F_l$ if it is served by its left server, and from a distribution $F_r$ if served by its right server. Servers process work at unit rate in FIFO fashion.

Question: Do there exist a rate $\lambda$, distributions $F_l$ and $F_r$, and two initial workload configurations such that, with the same $\lambda$, $F_l$, $F_r$, the system started from one configuration is stable (positive recurrent in the appropriate Markovian description) while the system started from the other configuration is unstable? More generally, can the stability of this system depend on the full distributions $F_l, F_r$ (and not merely on summary parameters such as their means) and on the initial workload state?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a clear resolution of this specific conjecture about a three-server cyclic Join-the-Shortest-Workload system whose stability may depend on the initial state and the full service-time distributions $F_l, F_r$. Related work on stability of JSQ/JSW networks exists (e.g., Bramson and others), but no source explicitly confirming or refuting this exact three-server conjecture was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

context_brief: Positive-measure null recurrence in polling system
original_question: Consider an open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers. Each station has Poisson input of rate 1. For i, j in {1, 2}, service times of server j at station i are i.i.d. exponential with rate mu_i^(j). Both servers use the exhaustive service policy, switch-over times are zero, and a server becomes passive if neither station has a free customer. In the positive four-dimensional parameter cube for {(mu_i^(j))}, does the subset of parameter values for which the system is null recurrent have positive Lebesgue measure?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open polling system with two stations, labeled $i=1,2$, and two heterogeneous servers, labeled $j=1,2$. Customers arrive at station $i$ according to independent Poisson processes of rate $\lambda_i = 1$. When server $j$ serves a customer at station $i$, the service time is exponentially distributed with rate $\mu_i^{(j)} > 0$, independent of all other service and arrival times. Each server follows the exhaustive service policy: upon arriving at a station, the server keeps serving customers there until that station is empty, then switches to the other station. Switch-over times are zero. If, upon completing service or switching, a server finds that neither station has a customer waiting, the server becomes passive (idle) and resumes service as soon as a customer arrives.

The system's dynamics are characterized by the four positive parameters $\{\mu_i^{(j)} : i,j\in\{1,2\}\}\in (0,\infty)^4$. For each parameter vector, the underlying Markov process describing the system is either positive recurrent, null recurrent, or transient.

Question: Does the set 
$$ N \;=\; \bigl\{(\mu_1^{(1)},\mu_2^{(1)},\mu_1^{(2)},\mu_2^{(2)})\in(0,\infty)^4 : \text{the system is null recurrent}\bigr\} $$
have strictly positive four-dimensional Lebesgue measure?
category_tag: Polling systems and stability of queueing networks
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the conjecture that the set of parameters yielding null recurrence in this two-station, two-heterogeneous-server exhaustive polling system has positive Lebesgue measure. Related literature on multi-server polling stability discusses other open conjectures but does not appear to settle this specific question, so the status is taken as unknown.

original_question: Consider a slotted multi-access channel in which packets have unit service time, arrivals during each slot are Poisson with parameter lambda, W_n is the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n, and each packet attempts transmission in slot n with probability p_n. A transmission succeeds if exactly one packet transmits, collides if two or more transmit, and is empty if none transmits. Suppose p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Does there exist a protocol of this form for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a slotted multi-access communication channel operating in discrete time slots $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. All packets have unit service time equal to one slot. The number of new packets arriving during each slot is Poisson distributed with parameter $\lambda > 0$, independently across slots. Let $W_n$ denote the number of packets present in the system at the beginning of slot $n$.

At the beginning of slot $n$, each of the $W_n$ packets independently attempts transmission with probability $p_n \in (0,1]$. The slot outcome is:
- successful if exactly one packet attempts transmission (in which case that packet leaves the system),
- a collision if two or more packets attempt transmission (all packets remain),
- empty if no packet attempts transmission.

Assume the transmission probabilities are defined inductively so that $p_{n+1}$ is a (deterministic) function only of $p_n$ and of the binary feedback $S_n \in \{0,1\}$ indicating whether slot $n$ contained a successful transmission ($S_n = 1$) or not ($S_n = 0$). Under this rule, $(W_n, p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain.

Question: Does there exist a protocol of this form (i.e., a choice of the update map $(p_n, S_n) \mapsto p_{n+1}$) and some $\lambda > 0$ for which the Markov chain $(W_n, p_n)$ is positive recurrent (ergodic)?
category_tag: Random access protocols and Markov chain stability

The status with respect to a definitive proof or disproof in the open literature could not be verified.

context_brief: Keller maps determined by agreement on xy=0
original_question: Let F and G be Keller maps, meaning polynomial endomorphisms such that det(Jac(F)) = det(Jac(G)) = 1. If the restrictions of F and G agree on the subset defined by xy = 0, must F and G be equal everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and consider polynomial maps $F, G : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^n$. Recall that a polynomial map $H = (H_1, \dots, H_n) : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^n$ is called a Keller map if its Jacobian determinant $\det\bigl(\partial H_i / \partial x_j\bigr)$ is a nonzero constant; equivalently (after rescaling) $\det(\mathrm{Jac}(H)) = 1$. Fix coordinates $x = x_1$ and $y = x_2$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and let $V = \{(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n : x_1 x_2 = 0\}$ be the union of the two coordinate hyperplanes $\{x_1 = 0\}$ and $\{x_2 = 0\}$.

Suppose that $F$ and $G$ are Keller maps satisfying $\det(\mathrm{Jac}(F)) = \det(\mathrm{Jac}(G)) = 1$, and that
$$F\big|_{V} \;=\; G\big|_{V},$$
i.e., $F(p) = G(p)$ for every point $p \in \mathbb{C}^n$ with $x_1 x_2 = 0$.

original_question: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. Is the group GAn(k) generated by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups of automorphisms?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k) := \mathrm{Aut}_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n])$ denote the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of the polynomial ring in $n$ variables. The subgroup $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ of tame automorphisms is the subgroup generated by:
\begin{itemize}
\item the affine automorphisms $\mathrm{Aff}_n(k) = \mathrm{GL}_n(k) \ltimes k^n$, and
\item the elementary (triangular) automorphisms of the form $(x_1,\dots,x_n) \mapsto (x_1,\dots,x_{i-1},\, x_i + f(x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n),\, x_{i+1},\dots,x_n)$, where $f \in k[x_1,\dots,\hat{x_i},\dots,x_n]$.
\end{itemize}
A one-parameter subgroup of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is a homomorphism $\varphi : (k,+) \to \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$, equivalently the exponential flow $\exp(tD)$ associated to a locally nilpotent $k$-derivation $D$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.

Question: Does there exist a finite collection of one-parameter subgroups $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_N$ of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ such that $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ is generated, as a group, by $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ together with the images of $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_N$?
status_search_result: No source verifying a resolution of this question was found. The structure of $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ for $n \geq 3$ remains poorly understood: Shestakov–Umirbaev showed in 2004 that the Nagata automorphism is non-tame for $n=3$, but no finite generating set involving tame automorphisms plus finitely many one-parameter subgroups is known. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Find an intrinsic algebraic invariant of normal finitely generated k-algebras that captures the algebraic rigidity of the tubular neighborhood of infinity and can be viewed as adding a continuous dimension to the homotopy type at infinity. $$A_{n,f} \;=\; k[x,y,z]\big/\bigl(x^{n}z - y^{2} - f(x)y\bigr).$$

Construct an intrinsic algebraic invariant $\Phi(A)$ defined on the class of all normal finitely generated $k$-algebras with the following properties:

1. $\Phi$ captures the algebraic rigidity of a "tubular neighborhood of infinity" of $\operatorname{Spec} A$, in the sense that it refines the homotopy type at infinity by an additional continuous parameter.
2. $\Phi$ is intrinsic (depends only on the isomorphism class of $A$ as a $k$-algebra) and can be computed in a direct (though possibly involved) manner.

Provide such an invariant $\Phi$ and prove that it distinguishes the isomorphism classes within the family $\{A_{n,f}\}$.

context_brief: Kernels of triangular locally nilpotent derivations
original_question: Let R = C[a, b]. Let D : R[x, y, z] -> R[x, y, z] be a triangular locally nilpotent R-derivation, meaning that D(x) belongs to R, D(y) belongs to R[x], and D(z) belongs to R[x, y]. If D has a slice, does it follow that ker(D) = R[2]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}$ denote the field of complex numbers, and set $R = \mathbb{C}[a,b]$, the polynomial ring in two variables over $\mathbb{C}$. Consider the polynomial ring $R[x,y,z]$ in three further indeterminates over $R$. Let $D : R[x,y,z] 	o R[x,y,z]$ be an $R$-derivation (i.e., $\mathbb{C}$-linear, satisfying the Leibniz rule, and vanishing on $R$) which is:

(i) locally nilpotent: for every $f \in R[x,y,z]$ there exists $n \geq 1$ with $D^n(f) = 0$;

(ii) triangular: $D(x) \in R$, $D(y) \in R[x]$, and $D(z) \in R[x,y]$.

Assume further that $D$ admits a slice, i.e., there exists $s \in R[x,y,z]$ with $D(s) = 1$. Let $\ker(D) = \{f \in R[x,y,z] : D(f) = 0\}$.

Does it follow that $\ker(D)$ is isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra, to a polynomial ring in two variables over $R$ (i.e., $\ker(D) \cong R^{[2]} = \mathbb{C}[a,b][t_1,t_2]$)?
status_search_result: A literature search on triangular locally nilpotent derivations of $R[x,y,z]$ with $R=\mathbb{C}[a,b]$ admitting a slice did not turn up an explicit resolution of this specific question. Related results (Bhatwadekar–Dutta, Daigle–Freudenburg, Berson–van den Essen–Maubach) treat fixed-point-free LNDs and $\mathbb{A}^2$-fibrations, and the kernel is known to be an $\mathbb{A}^2$-fibration over $\mathbb{A}^2$, but whether it must be a polynomial ring in this triangular-with-slice setting appears not to have been settled in the sources found.

context_brief: Generation and amalgam structure from stabilizer subgroups
original_question: For each i, let Gi be the subgroup of GAn(k) that stabilizes k ⊕ kx1 ⊕ ... ⊕ kxi, so that Gn = Aff_n(k), G2 = Aff_2(k) when n = 2, and G1 is the set of triangular automorphisms. Is GAn(k) generated by G1, ..., Gn? If so, is the group described in the source as an amalgamated product of the Gi along pairwise intersections?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ denote the group of polynomial automorphisms of the affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k = \mathrm{Spec}\, k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, i.e. the group of $k$-algebra automorphisms of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. For each $i \in \{1,2,\dots,n\}$, let
$$G_i = \{\,\varphi \in \mathrm{GA}_n(k) : \varphi(k \oplus k x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus k x_i) = k \oplus k x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus k x_i\,\}$$
be the subgroup of automorphisms stabilising the $k$-linear subspace $k \oplus k x_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus k x_i$ of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. Note that $G_n = \mathrm{Aff}_n(k)$, the affine subgroup, and $G_1$ is the subgroup of triangular (Jonquières) automorphisms. Let $\mathrm{TA}_n(k) \le \mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ denote the tame subgroup, generated by $\mathrm{Aff}_n(k)$ and the triangular subgroup. By the Jung–van der Kulk theorem, when $n = 2$ one has $\mathrm{GA}_2(k) = G_1 *_{G_1 \cap G_2} G_2$.

Answer the following two questions:
(a) Is $\mathrm{GA}_n(k) = \langle G_1, G_2, \dots, G_n \rangle$?
(b) If the answer to (a) is affirmative, is $\mathrm{TA}_n(k)$ isomorphic to the amalgamated product of the groups $G_1,\dots,G_n$ along their pairwise intersections (in the sense of a generalised amalgamated product / colimit of the diagram of subgroups $G_i$ and $G_i \cap G_j$)?
status_search_result: For $n=2$ the result is the classical Jung–van der Kulk theorem. For $n=3$ over a field of characteristic zero, Wright (2013/2015) established that the tame automorphism group $\mathrm{TA}_3(k)$ is the generalised amalgamated product of the three subgroups $G_1, G_2, G_3$ along their pairwise intersections, using Umirbaev's defining relations; however, since $\mathrm{TA}_3(k) \ne \mathrm{GA}_3(k)$ by Shestakov–Umirbaev, the question of whether $G_1,\dots,G_n$ generate the full $\mathrm{GA}_n(k)$ in dimensions $n \ge 3$ remains open. Thus the problem is partially solved (tame case in dimension 3 done; full group in dimensions $\ge 3$ open).

context_brief: Vanishing moments on the unit cube
original_question: Let x = (x1, x2, ..., xn) and let Cn = [0, 1]^n be the n-cube in R^n. Suppose f(x) belongs to C[x] and every moment integral over the cube vanishes, meaning that integral over Cn of f(x)^m dx equals 0 for every integer m >= 1. Does this force f to be the zero polynomial?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 1$ be an integer and let $C_n=[0,1]^n\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the unit $n$-cube. Let $f\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with complex coefficients, and suppose that
$$\int_{C_n} f(x_1,\dots,x_n)^m\,dx_1\cdots dx_n = 0\qquad\text{for every integer } m\geq 1.$$
(The integral is the ordinary Lebesgue integral of the complex-valued polynomial $f^m$ over the cube.) Determine whether these conditions force $f$ to be the zero polynomial. It is known that the implication holds when $n=1$; the question is whether it holds for all $n\geq 2$.
status_search_result: The question is a variant of the "Moment Vanishing / Integral Conjecture" associated with work surrounding the Jacobian Conjecture. The one-dimensional case is classical. In higher dimensions, related general moment-vanishing conjectures are known to admit counterexamples in more than two variables in some formulations (e.g., over Gaussian measures or general domains), while the Gaussian Moments Conjecture is known to imply the Jacobian Conjecture. No definitive published resolution of this exact cube version was located, so the status is taken as unknown/open.

original_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?

Let $\mathbb{C}[x] = \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n]$ denote the polynomial algebra in $n$ variables over the complex numbers, and let $C^n = [0,1]^n$ denote the closed unit $n$-cube in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Recall the following definition. Given a commutative ring $R$ and a commutative $R$-algebra $A$, an $R$-subspace $M \subseteq A$ is called a Mathieu subspace of $A$ if it has the following property: for any $a, b \in A$, if $a^m \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$, then $a^m b \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$.

Define
$$M \;=\; \Bigl\{\, f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n] \;:\; \int_{C^n} f(x)\,dx \;=\; 0 \,\Bigr\},$$
where the integral is the standard Lebesgue integral over the unit cube $C^n \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (extended $\mathbb{C}$-linearly to complex-valued polynomials).

Determine whether $M$ is a Mathieu subspace of the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.

context_brief: Closure of Mathieu subspaces under addition
original_question: Let A be a finitely generated k-algebra over a field k. If M1 and M2 are Mathieu subspaces of A, must their sum M1 + M2 also be a Mathieu subspace of A?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finitely generated associative (commutative or noncommutative) $k$-algebra. A $k$-subspace $M \subseteq A$ is called a Mathieu subspace (also known as a Mathieu–Zhao subspace) of $A$ if it has the following property: for every $a \in A$ such that $a^m \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$, and for every $b \in A$, one has $b\, a^m \in M$ for all sufficiently large positive integers $m$ (equivalently, the analogous condition with $a^m b$ also holds).

Suppose $M_1$ and $M_2$ are two Mathieu subspaces of $A$. Determine whether the sum
$$M_1 + M_2 = \{x_1 + x_2 : x_1 \in M_1,\ x_2 \in M_2\}$$

context_brief: Spectrum and geometry of Γ-commutative algebras
original_question: How can one define and develop a geometry for Γ-commutative algebras by introducing an appropriate notion of the spectrum of a Γ-commutative algebra, in a way that extends the well-developed Z2-commutative (supercommutative) case and could provide a new viewpoint on Clifford analysis?

Let Γ be an abelian group equipped with a symmetric bicharacter β : Γ × Γ → k× (where k is a fixed ground field of characteristic 0). A Γ-graded associative unital k-algebra A = ⊕_{γ∈Γ} A_γ is called Γ-commutative (with respect to β) if for all homogeneous elements a ∈ A_γ and b ∈ A_δ one has

   a · b = β(γ, δ) · b · a.

The case Γ = Z/2Z with β(1,1) = −1 recovers the notion of supercommutative (Z₂-commutative) algebra, for which the standard theory of superschemes provides a fully developed algebraic geometry: a structure sheaf on a topological space Spec(A) built from homogeneous prime ideals, an associated category of (super)schemes, and a duality between geometric and algebraic objects extending the classical Spec construction for commutative rings.

Problem. Develop an algebraic geometry for general Γ-commutative algebras. Concretely:

(a) Introduce a workable notion of "spectrum" Spec_Γ(A) of an arbitrary Γ-commutative algebra A, generalizing the prime/ homogeneous-prime-ideal spectrum used in the commutative and supercommutative cases, and equip it with a topology and a structure sheaf of Γ-commutative algebras so that A can be recovered (up to suitable equivalence) as global sections.

(b) Define the resulting category of "Γ-schemes" obtained by gluing such spectra, prove a contravariant adjunction/equivalence between Γ-commutative algebras (or a localized subcategory thereof) and affine Γ-schemes that specializes to the classical Spec ⊣ Γ(−,O) adjunction when Γ is trivial and to the superscheme adjunction when Γ = Z/2Z with the sign bicharacter.

(c) Apply this framework to Clifford algebras (which carry natural Γ-commutative gradings for suitable Γ and β) so as to provide a geometric, scheme-theoretic viewpoint on Clifford analysis.

Give such a construction, or prove that no such extension with the listed properties can exist.

The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Mass-loss law for RGB and AGB stars

paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
original_question: For red-giant-branch stars, is mass loss a continuous process or an episodic one, and how strongly, if at all, is the mass-loss behavior correlated with cluster metallicity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider stars evolving along the red giant branch (RGB) phase, during which they lose mass through stellar winds before reaching the horizontal branch. Two questions concerning RGB mass loss in stellar (in particular globular) clusters are posed:

(1) Is RGB mass loss a continuous process operating throughout the ascent of the giant branch, or is it instead an episodic phenomenon concentrated in discrete events?

(2) Is the integrated RGB mass loss (or its efficiency) significantly correlated with the metallicity [Fe/H] of the host cluster, and if so, what is the sign and strength of this correlation?

Provide a quantitative characterization of the temporal nature of RGB mass loss and of its dependence (or lack thereof) on cluster metallicity.
status_search_result: The questions remain active research topics. Recent studies (e.g., MNRAS 2015, 448, 502; MNRAS 2020, 498, 5745; arXiv:2505.12794) provide partial answers: mass loss appears not to be uniformly continuous along the RGB and shows differences between first- and second-generation populations, while the metallicity dependence is debated — some works find weak/no dependence, others find a positive correlation in metal-poor clusters and a negative one near solar metallicity. No consensus closed-form law is established.

paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
context_brief: C-rich opacity effects in AGB models
original_question: What quantitative changes do improved opacity tables for carbon-rich Asymptotic Giant Branch envelopes produce in the effective-temperature scale of AGB models, and how do those changes propagate into stellar-population-synthesis predictions that depend on AGB stars?
self_contained_problem:
Consider stellar evolution models of the thermally pulsing Asymptotic Giant Branch (TP-AGB) phase, in which a low- or intermediate-mass star develops a degenerate carbon–oxygen core surrounded by helium- and hydrogen-burning shells and an extended convective envelope. During this phase, repeated third dredge-up episodes can transport carbon to the surface, so that the surface number ratio C/O exceeds unity and the envelope becomes carbon-rich. The structure of such an envelope, and in particular its photospheric effective temperature T_eff, is highly sensitive to the low-temperature (T ≲ 5000 K) Rosseland mean opacity κ_R(ρ,T;X_i), which depends on the detailed molecular chemistry (CN, C2, HCN, C2H2, etc.) set by the elemental abundances X_i.

(a) Quantify how replacing a fixed-composition (scaled-solar) low-temperature opacity table with a table that consistently accounts for the variable C/O ratio in carbon-rich envelopes shifts the effective-temperature track T_eff(t) of TP-AGB models as a function of initial mass M (1 M_⊙ ≤ M ≤ 5 M_⊙) and metallicity Z (0.0001 ≤ Z ≤ 0.02). Specifically, determine the magnitude (in K) and sign of ΔT_eff at the moment C/O first exceeds 1, and along the subsequent C-star evolution, and characterize how ΔT_eff scales with Z and with the surface carbon excess (C − O).

(b) Propagate these revised T_eff tracks through a stellar population synthesis (SPS) framework that integrates isochrones weighted by an initial mass function and a star-formation history. Determine the resulting changes in: (i) the integrated bolometric and near-infrared (J, H, K) luminosities contributed by the TP-AGB component, (ii) broad-band colours such as V−K and J−K of single-burst stellar populations of ages 0.1–2 Gyr, and (iii) the inferred mass-to-light ratios at fixed observed colours.

Provide explicit quantitative predictions and identify the regimes (in age, metallicity, and mass) where the use of carbon-consistent opacities produces the largest deviations from models employing scaled-solar opacities.
category_tag: Stellar evolution and population synthesis modeling
status_search_result: Subsequent work (Marigo & Aringer 2009; Marigo et al. 2013, 2017 COLIBRI/PARSEC; Ventura et al.) implemented variable-composition low-temperature opacities in TP-AGB models and quantified that C-rich opacities lower T_eff by several hundred K (more strongly at higher Z, nearly vanishing for Z ≲ 0.0004), enhance mass loss, and shift integrated near-IR colours and TP-AGB contributions in SPS predictions. Hence the qualitative question is largely addressed, although precise quantitative SPS predictions continue to be refined and calibrated against resolved-population data.

paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
context_brief: Predictive power of synthetic AGB models
original_question: What is the predictive power of synthetic Asymptotic Giant Branch models outside the parameter space covered by the populations used to calibrate them, given that these simulations still inherit the same unresolved physical problems as full evolutionary AGB models and require multiple parameters to be tuned by hand to match selected observations?
self_contained_problem:
Synthetic Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) models are simplified, parametric prescriptions of the late evolutionary phase of low- and intermediate-mass stars (roughly 0.8–8 solar masses) in which key uncertain physical processes—third dredge-up efficiency, hot bottom burning, mass-loss rates, the treatment of convective boundaries, and nucleosynthetic yields—are encoded by a finite set of free parameters. These parameters are typically calibrated by tuning their values so that the resulting synthetic stellar populations reproduce selected observational constraints (for example, the carbon-star luminosity functions of the Magellanic Clouds, AGB lifetimes, or initial–final mass relations) for stellar populations of given metallicity, age, and mass distribution.

Assess the predictive power of such calibrated synthetic AGB models when they are applied outside the region of parameter space (in metallicity, initial mass, age, and environment) covered by the calibrating populations. Specifically:

(a) Quantify the extent to which observables predicted by a synthetic AGB model calibrated on one stellar population (e.g., Magellanic Cloud C-star luminosity functions) remain reliable when the model is extrapolated to populations with substantially different metallicities, ages, or mass ranges.

(b) Determine whether, given that synthetic models inherit the same unresolved physical uncertainties as full evolutionary AGB calculations and require multiple hand-tuned parameters, their extrapolations can be expected to be predictive in any rigorous sense, or whether they should be regarded as interpolating descriptions valid only within their calibration domain.
status_search_result: The predictive power of extrapolated synthetic AGB models remains an open issue in stellar astrophysics. Recent reviews and modeling papers continue to emphasize that synthetic AGB prescriptions depend on hand-tuned parameters calibrated to specific populations (notably the Magellanic Clouds), and that their reliability outside the calibration domain has not been established. No definitive resolution is reported.

paper_title: Stellar models: firm evidence, open questions and future developments
original_question: Is a solar-calibrated mixing-length parameter suitable for modeling Red Giant Branch stars across different metallicities, or do differences in input physics such as the equation of state and outer boundary conditions require a different calibration in order to reproduce empirical Red Giant Branch effective-temperature scales consistently?
self_contained_problem:
In one-dimensional stellar evolution modeling, convective energy transport in the outer envelope of a star is commonly described by mixing-length theory (MLT), in which the characteristic length scale of convective elements is parametrized as ℓ = α_MLT · H_p, where H_p is the local pressure scale height and α_MLT > 0 is a free parameter. The standard practice is to fix α_MLT by "solar calibration": one chooses α_MLT so that a stellar model of one solar mass and chemical composition equal to that of the present Sun reproduces, at the solar age, the observed solar radius (and luminosity and effective temperature). The value obtained depends on the other input physics adopted in the code, in particular the equation of state, the low-temperature opacities, the surface boundary conditions (for instance gray Eddington atmosphere versus integration of a detailed atmosphere model), and the assumed initial helium and metal abundances.

Consider stars on the Red Giant Branch (RGB) — low-mass stars (≈ 0.7–1.0 solar masses) after central hydrogen exhaustion, ascending the giant branch with deep convective envelopes — across a range of metallicities [Fe/H] from roughly −2.3 to solar. For such stars, the predicted effective temperature T_eff at fixed luminosity along the RGB depends sensitively on α_MLT.

Question: Is it the case that, for every reasonable choice of input physics (equation of state, low-T opacities, outer boundary conditions, heavy-element mixture, treatment of atomic diffusion), the solar-calibrated α_MLT obtained with that same input physics, when used unchanged to compute RGB tracks of low-mass stars at all metallicities in the above range, yields RGB effective-temperature predictions consistent with empirical RGB T_eff scales derived from observations of Galactic globular clusters and field giants? Equivalently: does there exist an empirical RGB T_eff scale that all internally consistent, solar-calibrated stellar codes reproduce simultaneously, or must α_MLT on the RGB be recalibrated separately (and possibly metallicity-dependently) for at least some choices of input physics?
status_search_result: Recent literature indicates that the adequacy of a solar-calibrated α_MLT for RGB stars across metallicities remains unsettled. Calibrations against 3D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations (e.g. CO5BOLD) and against asteroseismic field-star samples produce conflicting conclusions: some studies find a metallicity dependence of α_MLT (e.g. an increase of ~0.4 per dex in [Fe/H]), while others (e.g. Vázquez Ramió et al. 2019) argue that such trends are largely spurious and statistically unreliable, and that, with appropriate solar reference, a single α reproduces both the Sun and Population II RGB temperatures. The consensus is that the answer depends sensitively on the input physics (EOS, boundary conditions, opacities, mixture), so the question is best regarded as still open.

paper_title: A review of results and open problems on mathematical models of motion of viscoelastic media of Jeffreys' type
original_question: For the boundary-value problem for an incompressible Jeffreys-type viscoelastic medium governed by equations (0.2), (0.4), (0.5), and the objective-derivative constitutive law (2.18), does the initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution in dimensions n ≥ 2 without imposing any restrictions on the coefficients, the external force, or the initial data?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $T>0$. Consider the initial-boundary value problem for an incompressible viscoelastic medium of Jeffreys' type with an objective (frame-indifferent) constitutive law:

(i) Momentum balance and incompressibility:
$$\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v - \mathrm{Div}\,\sigma = f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\,v = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega\times(0,T),$$
where $v:\Omega\times(0,T)\to\mathbb{R}^n$ is the velocity field, $f$ is a given external body force, and $\sigma$ is the stress tensor of the form
$$\sigma = -p\,I + 2\mu_0\, E(v) + 2\mu_1\, \tau,$$
with pressure $p$, deformation-rate tensor $E(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v + (\nabla v)^\top)$, and $\mu_0,\mu_1>0$.

(ii) Constitutive law of Jeffreys' type with an objective derivative: the extra-stress $\tau$ satisfies
$$\tau + \lambda\, \frac{\mathcal{D}\tau}{\mathcal{D}t} = E(v),$$
where $\lambda>0$ is a relaxation time and $\frac{\mathcal{D}}{\mathcal{D}t}$ denotes an objective tensor derivative of the form
$$\frac{\mathcal{D}\tau}{\mathcal{D}t} = \partial_t \tau + (v\cdot\nabla)\tau + \tau\, W(v) - W(v)\,\tau + a\,(\tau\, E(v) + E(v)\,\tau),$$
with vorticity tensor $W(v) = \tfrac12(\nabla v - (\nabla v)^\top)$ and parameter $a\in[-1,1]$.

(iii) Boundary and initial conditions: $v=0$ on $\partial\Omega\times(0,T)$, $v(\cdot,0)=v_0$ in $\Omega$, and $\tau(\cdot,0)=\tau_0$ in $\Omega$.

Question. Does this initial-boundary value problem admit a global strong solution $(v,\tau,p)$ on $\Omega\times(0,T)$ for every $T>0$, in every dimension $n\ge 2$, without imposing any smallness or structural restrictions on the coefficients $\mu_0,\mu_1,\lambda,a$, on the external force $f$, or on the initial data $(v_0,\tau_0)$?
status_search_result: Recent literature indicates that for differential viscoelastic models of Jeffreys type with an objective derivative in the constitutive law, no global strong solvability results in arbitrary dimension $n\ge 2$ without restrictions on data and coefficients are known; partial results require regularization (e.g. averaging the vorticity tensor) or smallness assumptions. Global existence of large-data strong solutions for related viscoelastic systems is described as a longstanding open problem even in 2D.
