paper_title: Brownian models of multiclass queueing networks: Current status and open problems
context_brief: Brownian approximation for multiclass feedback FIFO networks
original_question: For an open queueing network operated under first-in-first-out service at every station, consider the class of networks that are both multiclass and have feedback routing, meaning customers may belong to multiple classes and may revisit stations according to non-feedforward routes. Does there exist a mathematically well-defined approximating Brownian model for this most complex routing class, and can such a model be rigorously justified by heavy-traffic limit theory in the same way as the simpler single-class or feedforward cases?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an open queueing network with $J$ stations and $K$ customer classes. Each class $k\in\{1,\dots,K\}$ is served at a unique station $s(k)\in\{1,\dots,J\}$, with multiple classes possibly served at the same station (multiclass). External arrivals to class $k$ form a renewal process with rate $\alpha_k\ge 0$ and squared coefficient of variation $c_{a,k}^2$. Service times of class-$k$ customers are i.i.d. with mean $1/\mu_k$ and squared coefficient of variation $c_{s,k}^2$. Upon completing service, a class-$k$ customer is routed to class $\ell$ with probability $P_{k\ell}$ and leaves the system with probability $1-\sum_\ell P_{k\ell}$; the routing matrix $P=(P_{k\ell})$ is sub-stochastic with spectral radius less than $1$, and is allowed to be of feedback type (i.e., $(I-P^\top)$ need not correspond to a feedforward order, so customers may revisit stations). At every station, customers are served on a first-in-first-out (FIFO) basis across all classes present at that station.

Let $\lambda=(I-P^\top)^{-1}\alpha$ denote the vector of nominal class throughputs, and let the traffic intensity at station $j$ be $\rho_j=\sum_{k:\,s(k)=j}\lambda_k/\mu_k$. Consider a sequence of such networks indexed by $n$ in heavy traffic, meaning $\rho_j^{(n)}\to 1$ as $n\to\infty$ for every station $j$, with all other primitives held fixed (or converging suitably).

Question. For this class of multiclass FIFO networks with feedback routing, does there exist a mathematically well-defined approximating Brownian model — specifically, a semimartingale reflecting Brownian motion (SRBM) in the nonnegative orthant $\mathbb{R}_+^J$ characterized by a drift vector, covariance matrix, and reflection matrix derived from the network primitives — such that the diffusion-scaled workload (or queue-length) process of the $n$-th network converges weakly to this SRBM as $n\to\infty$, thereby providing a rigorous heavy-traffic justification analogous to those known for single-class networks and for multiclass feedforward networks?
category_tag: heavy-traffic limits for multiclass queueing networks
status_search_result: The question has been substantially addressed but not fully resolved. Bramson (1998) and Williams (1998) established a general framework giving sufficient conditions — well-definedness and complete-S property of a proposed reflection matrix together with multiplicative state-space collapse — under which a SRBM heavy-traffic limit holds for multiclass FIFO feedback networks (in particular, Kelly-type FIFO networks and HLPPS networks). However, it is also known (e.g., examples by Dai–Wang and Dai–Nguyen) that for general multiclass FIFO feedback networks the proposed Brownian model can fail to be well-defined or the heavy-traffic limit can fail, so a fully general affirmative answer covering all multiclass FIFO feedback networks is not available. Thus the problem is partially solved: positive results hold under verifiable structural assumptions, while a complete general theory remains open.

paper_title: Brownian models of multiclass queueing networks: Current status and open problems
context_brief: Existence and uniqueness of the reduced Brownian system model
original_question: Let d be the number of stations, let G be the d x d routing-information matrix, let theta be the vector of netflow rates, and let Gamma be the covariance matrix in the Brownian approximation. If xi-star is a d-dimensional Brownian motion with drift minus theta and covariance Gamma, does there exist a unique nonnegative process W-star together with a continuous, nondecreasing regulator Y-star such that W-star(t) = xi-star(t) - G W-star(t) + Y-star(t) for all t, with each coordinate Y-star_j allowed to increase only when the corresponding coordinate W-star_j is zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 1$ be a positive integer (the number of stations). Fix:
- a $d \times d$ real matrix $G$ (the routing-information matrix),
- a vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (the netflow-rate vector),
- a symmetric positive semidefinite $d \times d$ matrix $\Gamma$ (the covariance matrix).

Let $\xi^\ast = \{\xi^\ast(t): t \ge 0\}$ be a $d$-dimensional Brownian motion with drift $-\theta$ and covariance matrix $\Gamma$, defined on a filtered probability space satisfying the usual conditions, with $\xi^\ast(0) = 0$.

We seek a pair of $d$-dimensional continuous adapted processes $(W^\ast, Y^\ast)$ such that, almost surely, for every $t \ge 0$ and every coordinate $j \in \{1,\ldots,d\}$:

(i) $W^\ast(t) = \xi^\ast(t) - G\,W^\ast(t) + Y^\ast(t)$;
(ii) $W^\ast_j(t) \ge 0$;
(iii) $Y^\ast_j(0) = 0$ and $Y^\ast_j$ is continuous and nondecreasing;
(iv) $Y^\ast_j$ increases only at times $t$ when $W^\ast_j(t) = 0$, i.e. $\int_0^\infty W^\ast_j(t)\, dY^\ast_j(t) = 0$.

Question: For which triples $(\theta, \Gamma, G)$ does there exist such a process $W^\ast$ together with a regulator $Y^\ast$ satisfying (i)–(iv), and when is the pair $(W^\ast, Y^\ast)$ pathwise unique? In particular, does existence and uniqueness hold for every general triple $(\theta, \Gamma, G)$ arising from a multiclass queueing network?
category_tag: Reflected Brownian motion in queueing networks
status_search_result: The problem can be recast as existence and uniqueness of a semimartingale reflecting Brownian motion (SRBM) in the nonnegative orthant with reflection matrix tied to $I+G$. For SRBMs in an orthant, Reiman–Williams, Taylor–Williams, and subsequent work established that the "completely-$\mathcal{S}$" condition on the reflection matrix is necessary and sufficient for existence, with weak uniqueness in law. However, for general routing matrices $G$ arising from multiclass networks, Dai and Wang (and later results) showed that Brownian system models of the Harrison–Nguyen type may fail to exist, so the question is not fully resolved in complete generality; sufficient conditions and counterexamples are known, making the problem partially solved.

paper_title: Brownian models of multiclass queueing networks: Current status and open problems
context_brief: Generalized heavy-traffic limits beyond the standard Brownian model
original_question: For multiclass open queueing networks whose data make the standard Brownian system model ill-defined, what is the correct heavy-traffic limiting framework? In particular, what weaker notion of convergence and what more general class of limit processes, possibly including discontinuous processes, should replace the usual weak convergence to a continuous reflected Brownian model in order to complete the heavy-traffic analysis of such networks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a multiclass open queueing network with K customer classes, finite station set, deterministic routing among classes (possibly with feedback), renewal external arrivals, i.i.d. service times, and a head-of-the-line service discipline. For each n, let X^n(t) denote the K-dimensional queue-length (or workload) process under a heavy-traffic scaling in which traffic intensities at every station tend to 1 as n → ∞. The "standard Brownian system model" is the K-dimensional semimartingale reflecting Brownian motion (SRBM) defined by the heavy-traffic data of the network: a drift vector θ, a covariance matrix Γ, and a reflection (input) matrix R associated with the workload directions; the SRBM lives in the nonnegative orthant and is required to satisfy the Skorokhod problem with reflection matrix R. It is known that there exist multiclass networks (e.g. with feedback) whose heavy-traffic data produce an SRBM that is ill-defined: the reflection matrix R fails to be completely-S, the Skorokhod problem has no unique solution, or the candidate diffusion limit does not exist as a continuous reflected process. Examples (constructed by Whitt and by Dai–Wang) show that, for such networks, the diffusion-scaled processes X^n need not converge in the usual J_1 (uniform-on-compacta) Skorokhod topology to any continuous reflected Brownian motion, yet may admit nondegenerate limits in a weaker sense, with limit paths exhibiting jumps or other discontinuous behavior.

Problem. Identify and characterize:
(i) a topology τ on the path space D([0,∞); ℝ^K), strictly weaker than the standard J_1 Skorokhod topology, and
(ii) a class 𝓛 of stochastic processes on the nonnegative orthant, more general than continuous SRBMs and allowing discontinuous sample paths,
such that for every multiclass open queueing network in heavy traffic whose standard Brownian system model is ill-defined, the diffusion-scaled queue-length (or workload) processes X^n converge in the topology τ to a process X ∈ 𝓛 uniquely determined by the heavy-traffic data (θ, Γ, R) of the network, thereby completing the heavy-traffic analysis for this class of networks. Provide an axiomatic description of 𝓛 and a defining (e.g. Skorokhod-type) problem whose solutions are exactly the elements of 𝓛.
status_search_result: Searches indicate this remains an open research direction. Subsequent work (e.g., Bramson and Williams on state space collapse, Dai–Wang counterexamples) gives sufficient conditions for SRBM approximations under state space collapse and a well-defined completely-S reflection matrix, but no general theory has been established for the case where the standard Brownian system model is ill-defined: there is no widely accepted weaker topology and class of (possibly discontinuous) limit processes that completes the heavy-traffic analysis for all such multiclass open networks.

original_question: Find an explicit parameter q for which Schilling’s problem has a non-trivial Lebesgue-integrable solution, but the associated distribution-function equation φ(x) = 1/2 φ(x/q − 1/2) + 1/2 φ(x/q + 1/2) has no absolutely continuous solution. The survey states that such q-values exist, but that no explicit example was known.
self_contained_problem:
Schilling's functional equation in a single real variable is

  4q f(qx) = f(x − 1) + 2 f(x) + f(x + 1),    x ∈ ℝ,

where q ∈ (0, 1) is a real parameter and f : ℝ → ℝ is the unknown. A "non-trivial Lebesgue-integrable solution" means a function f ∈ L¹(ℝ, dx) satisfying the equation almost everywhere and not equal to 0 a.e.

Associated to it is the distribution-function equation

  φ(x) = (1/2) φ(x/q − 1/2) + (1/2) φ(x/q + 1/2),    x ∈ ℝ,

whose solutions of interest are bounded non-decreasing functions φ : ℝ → [0,1] with φ(−∞) = 0 and φ(+∞) = 1. Such a φ is said to be "absolutely continuous" if it is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on ℝ.

It is known that there exist values of q ∈ (0,1) for which Schilling's equation admits a non-trivial L¹ solution while the associated distribution-function equation admits no absolutely continuous solution φ.

Problem. Exhibit one explicit such value q ∈ (0,1).

context_brief: Convexity versus uniqueness for Daróczy equation
original_question: For Daróczy’s equation φ(x) = φ(x+1) + φ(x(x+1)) on (0,∞), does convexity of the solution φ itself imply uniqueness? self_contained_problem:
Daróczy's functional equation on the positive reals asks for functions $\varphi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$\varphi(x) \;=\; \varphi(x+1) \;+\; \varphi\!\bigl(x(x+1)\bigr) \qquad \text{for all } x\in(0,\infty).$$
The function $\varphi(x)=c/x$ (with $c\in\mathbb{R}$) is a solution, since $\frac{1}{x}=\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{1}{x(x+1)}$. Various additional regularity hypotheses (e.g. higher-order convexity, logarithmic convexity, or monotonicity of $x\varphi(x)$) are known to force every solution to coincide with $c/x$ on $(0,\infty)$.

Question: Suppose $\varphi:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is a convex function satisfying the equation above. Must $\varphi$ be of the form $\varphi(x)=c/x$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{R}$? In other words, does convexity of $\varphi$ alone imply uniqueness (up to the multiplicative constant) of the solution to Daróczy's equation?

paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
original_question: Classify the analytic solutions in the open unit disc of the functional equation 3zφ(z^3) = 3zφ(z^6) + φ(z^2) + λφ(λz^2) + λ^2φ(λ^2z^2), where λ = e^{2πi/3}. Berg and Meinardus conjectured that the only analytic solutions are the Möbius-type functions φ(z) = a + bz/(1-z) with arbitrary complex constants a and b.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc, and let $\lambda = e^{2\pi i/3}$ be a primitive cube root of unity. Consider the linear functional equation
$$3z\,\varphi(z^3) \;=\; 3z\,\varphi(z^6) \;+\; \varphi(z^2) \;+\; \lambda\,\varphi(\lambda z^2) \;+\; \lambda^2 \varphi(\lambda^2 z^2)$$
for functions $\varphi : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ that are analytic (holomorphic) on $\mathbb{D}$.

A direct computation shows that, for any complex constants $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$, the Möbius-type function
$$\varphi(z) \;=\; a \;+\; \frac{b\,z}{1-z}$$
is an analytic solution of the above equation in $\mathbb{D}$.

Prove or disprove: every function $\varphi$ that is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$ and satisfies the functional equation has the form $\varphi(z) = a + bz/(1-z)$ for some $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$.
status_search_result: The functional equation is the Berg–Meinardus reformulation of the Collatz 3n+1 problem: showing that the only analytic solutions on the unit disc are $a+bz/(1-z)$ is equivalent to the Collatz conjecture. The Collatz conjecture remains unsolved, and recent works (e.g., 2024 Results in Mathematics paper, and 2025 arXiv 2510.06736) continue to study generalizations of the Berg–Meinardus equations without resolving the conjecture. Hence the problem is still open.

context_brief: Embedding linear functional equations into flows
original_question: Given functions f, g, and h in the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x), under what weak assumptions on f, g, and h can this discrete-time equation be embedded into a continuous-time family φ(F(t,x)) = G(t,x)φ(x) + H(t,x), where F, G, and H satisfy the natural flow and cocycle identities and interpolate the original data at t = 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a set (e.g. a real or complex domain) and let f: X → X, g: X → K, h: X → K be given functions, where K is the underlying scalar field. Consider the linear functional equation in a single variable for an unknown function φ: X → K:

(1)   φ(f(x)) = g(x) φ(x) + h(x),   x ∈ X.

We say that equation (1) can be embedded into a continuous-time (one-parameter) family if there exist functions F: T × X → X, G: T × X → K, H: T × X → K (with T ⊆ ℝ a parameter set containing 0 and 1, e.g. T = ℝ or T = [0,∞)) belonging to a prescribed regularity class, satisfying the flow and cocycle identities

  F(t+s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)),
  G(t+s, x) = G(s, x) · G(t, F(s, x)),
  H(t+s, x) = G(t, F(s, x)) · H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)),

together with the initial/normalization conditions

  F(1, ·) = f,   G(0, ·) = 1,   G(1, ·) = g,   H(0, ·) = 0,   H(1, ·) = h,

and such that every solution φ of (1) (within the considered function class) automatically satisfies the continuous-time equation

(2)   φ(F(t, x)) = G(t, x) φ(x) + H(t, x),   t ∈ T, x ∈ X.

Determine the weakest possible assumptions on f, g, h (and the function class for φ) under which such an embedding exists, and exhibit an explicit construction of F, G, H.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let S+ and S− denote the forward and backward shift operators acting on z(N0). In the five-case classification discussed in Section 2.1, determine whether case 3 can actually occur; equivalently, determine whether the range M(I − 2S−|z) can be a closed subspace of finite positive codimension 1, 2, 3, ....
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of bounded scalar sequences $x=(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots)$. The forward shift $S_+$ and backward shift $S_-$ on sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ are defined by
\[ S_+(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots) = (0,\xi_0,\xi_1,\dots), \qquad S_-(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2,\dots) = (\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3,\dots). \]

A quasi-Banach sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ stronger than the sup-norm, that contains all finitely supported sequences and is solid in the sense that $|\eta_n|\le|\xi_n|$ for all $n$ together with $(\xi_n)\in z$ imply $(\eta_n)\in z$ with $\|\eta\|_z\le\|\xi\|_z$. The ideal is called shift-monotone if both $S_+$ and $S_-$ map $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ continuously into itself.

For a continuous linear operator $T$ on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ write $M(T):=T(z(\mathbb{N}_0))$ for its range, and $\mathrm{cod}(M(T)):=\dim\bigl(z(\mathbb{N}_0)/M(T)\bigr)$ for its codimension when this range is a closed subspace.

Question. Let $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be an arbitrary quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Can the range $M(I-2S_-|z)$ of the operator $I-2S_-$ acting on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be a closed subspace of finite positive codimension; that is, does there exist such an ideal $z$ for which $M(I-2S_-|z)$ is closed in $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and
\[ \mathrm{cod}\bigl(M(I-2S_-|z)\bigr)\in\{1,2,3,\dots\}\,? \]
Equivalently, prove that this situation is impossible, or exhibit an example realizing it.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in the framework of Pietsch's classification of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals via the spectra of the shift operators $S_\pm$. No published resolution of the case where $M(I-2S_-|z)$ is closed with finite positive codimension was found in the literature on traces of operator ideals.

original_question: For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0), let S− be the backward shift operator on z(N0) and let r(S−|z) be its spectral radius. Determine whether the full spectrum of S− is exactly the closed disk {λ ∈ C : |λ| ≤ r(S−|z)}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal over the index set $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. That is, $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $\mathbb{C}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ such that:

(i) $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq z(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq \ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with continuous inclusions;

(ii) (shift-monotonicity) for every $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, both the forward shift $S_+ x = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ and the backward shift $S_- x = (x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots)$ belong to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and moreover $\|S_+ x\|_z \le \|x\|_z$ and $\|S_- x\|_z \le \|x\|_z$.

Let $S_- : z(\mathbb{N}_0) \to z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the backward shift, viewed as a bounded linear operator, and let
$$ r(S_- \mid z) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \|S_-^n\|^{1/n} $$
be its spectral radius, and
$$ \sigma(S_- \mid z) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda I - S_- \text{ is not invertible on } z(\mathbb{N}_0)\} $$
its spectrum.

Determine whether the equality
$$ \sigma(S_- \mid z) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : |\lambda| \le r(S_- \mid z)\} $$
holds for every quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

\[ (S_+ x)(n)=\begin{cases} 0 & n=0 \\ x(n-1) & n\ge 1 \end{cases}, \qquad (S_- x)(n)=x(n+1) \quad (n\ge 0), \]
both map $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ continuously into itself. For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a quasi-Banach space $X$, let

and define the $\Phi$-spectrum by

\[ \sigma_\Phi(S_\pm\,|\,z) \;=\; \bigl\{\lambda\in\mathbb{C} : r(S_\mp\,|\,z)^{-1} \le |\lambda| \le r(S_\pm\,|\,z)\bigr\}, \]
i.e., the $\Phi$-spectrum of each shift on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is exactly the closed annulus determined by the spectral radii of the two shifts?

original_question: Let z(N0) be a shift-monotone sequence ideal, and let LAPP_z be the operator ideal consisting of operators S whose dyadic approximation-number sequence (a_{2^k}(S)) belongs to z(N0). Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is one of the traces constructed in Theorem 1.19 from a 1/2 S+-invariant linear form on z(N0), so that LAPP_z supports no additional traces beyond that family.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of bounded scalar sequences $x = (\xi_0, \xi_1, \xi_2, \dots)$. The forward shift $S_+$ and the backward shift $S_-$ on sequences are defined by $S_+ x := (0, \xi_0, \xi_1, \dots)$ and $S_- x := (\xi_1, \xi_2, \dots)$, and the dyadic-averaged half-shift $\tfrac{1}{2}S_+$ acts as $x \mapsto \tfrac12 S_+ x$.

A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq \ell_\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is closed under both $S_+$ and $S_-$ and is solid (if $|y_k| \le |x_k|$ for all $k$ and $x \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, then $y \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$).

For a (bounded linear) operator $S$ between Banach spaces, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(S) := \inf\{\|S - F\| : \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}.$$
Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the operator ideal
$$L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z := \{S : (a_{2^k}(S))_{k \ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\},$$
acting on the class of all Banach spaces. A trace on $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,X)$ (for all Banach spaces $X$) satisfying $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever the products make sense and the standard normalization on rank-one operators.

Construction. A linear form $\varphi$ on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called $\tfrac12 S_+$-invariant if $\varphi(\tfrac12 S_+ x) = \varphi(x)$ for all $x \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. Each such $\varphi$ induces a trace $\varphi_z$ on $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ via the standard construction associating to an operator the sequence of its dyadic approximation numbers.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every trace on $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ arises in the form $\varphi_z$ for some $\tfrac12 S_+$-invariant linear form $\varphi$ on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$; equivalently, $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$ supports no traces beyond this family.

status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the program of Pietsch on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. Searches reveal a series of related papers by Pietsch establishing the analogous result on Hilbert space, but no published resolution for the Banach-space ideals $L^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$. The status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Determine whether every norm-closed operator ideal is traceless, meaning that it admits no nonzero trace.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $L(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. An operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a subspace $\mathcal{A}(X,Y) \subseteq L(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$;
(ii) for all Banach spaces $W,X,Y,Z$ and all $B \in L(W,X)$, $T \in \mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, $A \in L(Y,Z)$, the composition $ATB$ lies in $\mathcal{A}(W,Z)$.
The components $\mathcal{A}(X) := \mathcal{A}(X,X)$ are two-sided ideals in $L(X)$.

The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is said to be norm-closed if $\mathcal{A}(X,Y)$ is closed in $L(X,Y)$ in the operator norm topology, for every pair $(X,Y)$.

A trace on the operator ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau = (\tau_X)$, with $\tau_X : \mathcal{A}(X) \to \mathbb{C}$ defined for every Banach space $X$, satisfying:
(1) $\tau_X(x^* \otimes x) = \langle x, x^*\rangle$ for every $x \in X$ and $x^* \in X^*$, where $(x^* \otimes x)(y) = \langle y, x^*\rangle x$;
(2) the trace property $\tau_X(AT) = \tau_Y(TA)$ whenever $X,Y$ are Banach spaces, $T \in \mathcal{A}(X,Y)$, and $A \in L(Y,X)$ (with $AT \in \mathcal{A}(X)$ and $TA \in \mathcal{A}(Y)$).

Note: condition (1) may be replaced by requiring $\tau$ to be merely a (not necessarily normalized) family of linear functionals satisfying (2); for the question below "nonzero trace" means a nonzero such family. The ideal $\mathcal{A}$ is called traceless if it admits no nonzero trace, and otherwise is said to support a non-vanishing trace.

Problem. Prove that every norm-closed operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces is traceless.
status_search_result: The question of whether every norm-closed operator ideal on the class of all Banach spaces is traceless is listed as an open problem in the literature on traces of operator ideals; web search did not surface any complete resolution. Partial results are known (e.g., specific norm-closed ideals such as the closed ideal of compact operators are known to be traceless), but a general proof for all norm-closed operator ideals does not appear to have been published.

original_question: Let z(N0) be a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal. Determine whether every trace on LAPP_z is spectral, in the sense that for each operator S the trace is determined by the eigenvalue sequence of S through the dyadic block sums described in Section 2.4.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\ell_\infty$ denote the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and let $c_{00}$ denote the space of eventually-zero sequences. For $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$ let $D_k=\{n\in\mathbb{N}_0:2^k\le n<2^{k+1}\}$ be the $k$-th dyadic block, so $|D_k|=2^k$. For a sequence $a=(a_n)\in\ell_\infty$ define the dyadic block-average sequence
$$B(a)=\Big(\tfrac{1}{2^k}\sum_{n\in D_k}a_n\Big)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}.$$

A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\subset\ell_\infty$ is called shift-monotone if it is a linear subspace containing $c_{00}$ and stable under the right and left shifts and under coordinate-wise domination by elements of $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. We assume $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equipped with a quasi-norm under which it is complete (a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal).

For a Banach space $X$, let $\mathcal{L}(X)$ denote the bounded linear operators on $X$. For each diagonal sequence $a\in\ell_\infty$ let $D_a\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$ denote the diagonal operator with diagonal $a$. Define the operator ideal $\mathrm{LAPP}_z$ on the class of all Banach spaces by the requirement that an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(X)$ belongs to $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X)$ if and only if its sequence of approximation numbers $(a_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ lies in $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, with the natural quasi-norm inherited from that of $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. For $S\in\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X)$, let $(\lambda_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ denote its eigenvalue sequence, ordered by decreasing modulus and counted with algebraic multiplicities (with zeros appended if there are only finitely many).

A trace on $\mathrm{LAPP}_z$ is a linear functional $\tau$ defined on each component $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X)$ which is unitarily/operator invariant in the sense that $\tau(AB)=\tau(BA)$ whenever the compositions belong to the ideal.

A trace $\tau$ on $\mathrm{LAPP}_z$ is called spectral if there exists a linear functional $\varphi$ on a suitable subspace of $\ell_\infty$ containing all sequences $B((\lambda_n(S)))$, with $\varphi(a)=\tau(D_a)$ for the diagonal embedding, such that for every Banach space $X$ and every $S\in\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X)$,
$$\tau(S)=\varphi\!\left(\Big(\tfrac{1}{2^k}\sum_{n\in D_k}\lambda_n(S)\Big)_{k\in\mathbb{N}_0}\right).$$

Problem. Prove or disprove: whenever $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal, every trace on $\mathrm{LAPP}_z$ is spectral.

Web searches surface related work on shift operators, traces, and shift-monotone sequence ideals, but no source claiming a proof or disproof of spectrality of all traces on LAPP_z for general quasi-Banach z. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: Let A be a quasi-Banach operator ideal of exact trace type 1/r, and let ϕ_{r,∞}(·|A) be the trace on AAPP_{r,∞} constructed in Theorem 1.21. Determine whether this trace is spectral, i.e. whether it is completely determined by the eigenvalue sequence of each operator in the sense of Section 2.4.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A quasi-Banach operator ideal (A, ‖·‖_A) is an assignment, to each pair of Banach spaces (X,Y), of a linear subspace A(X,Y) of the bounded operators X→Y, equipped with a quasi-norm ‖·‖_A, that contains all finite-rank operators, is complete, and is stable under composition with bounded operators in the usual ideal sense.

For 0<r<∞, the approximation ideal A_{r,∞}^P consists of all operators T: X→Y such that the sequence of approximation numbers a_n(T) = inf{‖T-F‖ : rank F < n} satisfies sup_{n≥1} n^{1/r} a_n(T) < ∞. The product ideal A·A_{r,∞}^P (denoted AA_{r,∞}^P) is the set of all finite sums of compositions S∘T with S in A and T in A_{r,∞}^P.

A quasi-Banach operator ideal (A, ‖·‖_A) is said to be of exact trace type 1/r if it admits a trace τ on its component A(X,X) (X any Banach space) which, in a precise asymptotic sense, behaves like the singular-value functional s ↦ Σ s_n with weight n^{1/r}. Assume that for such an ideal A there is a canonical trace, denoted φ_{r,∞}(·|A), defined on the operator ideal AA_{r,∞}^P by an explicit construction (so that it is a linear functional on each AA_{r,∞}^P(X,X), satisfies φ_{r,∞}(ST|A) = φ_{r,∞}(TS|A) whenever both compositions lie in AA_{r,∞}^P, and reduces to the usual trace on finite-rank operators).

A trace φ on an operator ideal J is called spectral if for every Banach space X and every T ∈ J(X,X) one has
   φ(T) = Σ_{n} λ_n(T),
where (λ_n(T)) is the eigenvalue sequence of T, listed with algebraic multiplicities and arranged so that |λ_1(T)| ≥ |λ_2(T)| ≥ …, and the sum is interpreted in the appropriate summable sense guaranteed by the eigenvalue distribution of operators in J.

Question. For every 0<r<∞ and every quasi-Banach operator ideal A of exact trace type 1/r, decide whether the trace φ_{r,∞}(·|A) on AA_{r,∞}^P is spectral.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, let P_{r,2} be the ideal of (r,2)-summing operators, and let (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal from Theorem 2.4. Determine whether every trace on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces constructed in Theorem 2.4, so that no additional traces exist on this ideal.
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

(a) An operator ideal A in the sense of Pietsch is a class assigning to every pair of Banach spaces X, Y a linear subspace A(X,Y) of the bounded linear operators L(X,Y), containing all finite-rank operators, and stable under composition with bounded operators on either side. A trace on a (quasi-)Banach operator ideal A (defined on the class of all Banach spaces) is a linear functional τ that on every component A(X,X) is defined, is continuous in the ideal (quasi-)norm, satisfies the cyclic/tracial property τ(ST) = τ(TS) whenever the compositions belong to the ideal, and reduces to the usual trace on finite-rank operators.

(b) For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, the ideal P_{r,2} of (r,2)-summing operators consists of all bounded linear operators T : X → Y between Banach spaces such that there is a constant c ≥ 0 with
   ( Σ_{k=1}^n ‖Tx_k‖^r )^{1/r} ≤ c · sup{ ( Σ_{k=1}^n |⟨x_k,x*⟩|^2 )^{1/2} : x* ∈ X*, ‖x*‖ ≤ 1 }
for every finite family x_1,…,x_n in X. The (r,2)-summing norm π_{r,2}(T) is the smallest such c, and (P_{r,2}, π_{r,2}) is a Banach operator ideal.

(c) For an operator ideal A and parameters 0 < r < ∞, ∞ as second index, define the approximation-type ideal A_APP_{r,∞} to consist of all operators T between Banach spaces for which there exist finite-rank operators F_n with rank F_n ≤ n and
   sup_{n ≥ 1} (n+1)^{1/r} · α_n(T) < ∞,
where α_n(T) := inf{ ‖T − F‖_A : F finite rank, rank F ≤ n } is the n-th approximation number measured in the ideal (quasi-)norm of A (using A := P_{r,2} and its norm π_{r,2}). Apply this construction with A = P_{r,2}; the resulting ideal is denoted (P_{r,2})_APP_{r,∞}.

(d) On (P_{r,2})_APP_{r,∞} a family of traces φ_{r,∞}(·|P_{r,2}) can be constructed by an averaging/Banach-limit procedure applied to the sequences arising from the approximation numbers in P_{r,2}; this yields a (in general non-unique up to choice of Banach limit) collection of continuous traces on (P_{r,2})_APP_{r,∞}.

Problem. Fix r ∈ [1,2]. Prove or disprove: every continuous trace on the operator ideal (P_{r,2})_APP_{r,∞} arises from the construction in (d); equivalently, no continuous trace on (P_{r,2})_APP_{r,∞} exists other than those of the form φ_{r,∞}(·|P_{r,2}).

original_question: For 1 ≤ r ≤ 2, let ϕ_{r,∞}(·|P_{r,2}) denote the trace on (P_{r,2})APP_{r,∞} from Theorem 2.4. Determine whether this trace is spectral.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work with bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. For $1\le r<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, let $P_{r,q}$ denote the Banach operator ideal of absolutely $(r,q)$-summing operators (so $P_{r,2}$ consists of absolutely $(r,2)$-summing operators). For $1\le r\le 2$, let $APP_{r,\infty}$ denote the approximation operator ideal of Lorentz type with parameters $(r,\infty)$, defined via the approximation numbers $a_n(T)$ by the quasi-norm $\sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} a_n(T)$. Consider the product ideal $(P_{r,2})\,APP_{r,\infty}$, consisting of all operators $T$ that factor as $T=AB$ with $A\in P_{r,2}$ and $B\in APP_{r,\infty}$, equipped with the natural ideal quasi-norm.

Assume that on this ideal there is a (unique up to scalar) trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid P_{r,2})$, that is, a linear functional satisfying $\varphi_{r,\infty}(ST\mid P_{r,2})=\varphi_{r,\infty}(TS\mid P_{r,2})$ whenever both products lie in the ideal.

A trace $\varphi$ on an operator ideal is called spectral if for every operator $T$ in the ideal one has
$$\varphi(T)=\sum_{n} \lambda_n(T),$$
where $(\lambda_n(T))$ is the eigenvalue sequence of $T$ counted with algebraic multiplicities (arranged in non-increasing order of absolute value), the right-hand side being absolutely convergent.

Question. For each $1\le r\le 2$, determine whether the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\mid P_{r,2})$ on $(P_{r,2})\,APP_{r,\infty}$ is spectral.
category_tag: Traces on Banach space operator ideals
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an explicit open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals defined over all Banach spaces. While general results characterize spectrality of traces on Hilbert-space ideals (Kalton–Pietsch theory), no source located addresses spectrality of this specific trace on $(P_{r,2})APP_{r,\infty}$ in the Banach-space setting; thus the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let LWEYL_{r,∞} be the quasi-Banach operator ideal defined by the dyadic Weyl-number condition x_{2^k}(S) = O(2^{-k/r}). Determine whether the interpolated ideals (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} strictly increase as r varies over [2,∞), or whether they become constant on that range; in particular, decide whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞} might already equal LWEYL_{1,∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal L$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. For $S\in\mathcal L(X,Y)$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, the $n$-th Weyl number $x_n(S)$ is defined by
$$x_n(S):=\sup\{a_n(SA): A\in\mathcal L(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\},$$
where $a_n(\cdot)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number ($a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-R\|:\operatorname{rank}R<n\}$).

For $1\le r<\infty$ define the quasi-Banach operator ideal
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\{S\in\mathcal L:\ x_{2^k}(S)=O(2^{-k/r})\ 	ext{as}\ k	o\infty\},$$
equipped with its natural quasi-norm $\sup_{k\ge 0}2^{k/r}x_{2^k}(S)$.

For a quasi-Banach operator ideal $(\mathcal A,\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A})$ and $1\le r<\infty$, define the interpolated ideal $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ to consist of those operators $S\in\mathcal L$ admitting, for every $k\ge 0$, a decomposition $S=A_k+B_k$ with $A_k\in\mathcal A$, $\operatorname{rank}B_k<2^k$, and
$$2^{k/r}\|A_k\|_{\mathcal A}=O(1)\quad	ext{as }k	o\infty.$$

original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, let (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} be the operator ideal carrying the traces from Theorem 2.8. Determine whether every trace on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} is one of the traces given by Theorem 2.8.
self_contained_problem:
Setting and notation. Let $X, Y$ range over complex Banach spaces and let $\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ denote the bounded linear operators. For $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ and $n=1,2,\dots$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\,\|T-A\|: A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}\,A<n\,\},$$
and the $n$-th Weyl number is
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{\,a_n(TS): S\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|S\|\le 1\,\}.$$

For $1\le r<\infty$, the Weyl operator ideal of Lorentz type $L_{r,\infty}$ is
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}=\{\,T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y): \|T\|^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:=\sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}\,x_n(T)<\infty\,\},$$
and its approximation-number-based component is
$$(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}=\{\,T\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}: \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}\,a_n(T)<\infty\,\}.$$

A trace on a (two-sided) operator ideal $\mathcal{I}$ defined on the class of all Banach spaces is a scalar-valued linear functional $\tau$ defined on the components $\mathcal{I}(X,X)$ that satisfies $\tau(BA)=\tau(AB)$ whenever $A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Y,X)$ and $AB,BA\in\mathcal{I}$, and that takes the value $\tau(\mathrm{id}_K)=1$ on the identity of the one-dimensional space.

A construction (a Dixmier-type averaging procedure applied to the eigenvalue sequence, normalized through the divergent partial sums of the harmonic-type series associated with the index $r$) produces, for every suitable scale-invariant Banach limit $\omega$ on $\ell_\infty$, a continuous trace $\varphi^{\omega}_{r,\infty}$ on $(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$.

Question. For each $1\le r<\infty$, prove or disprove: every trace on the operator ideal $(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ coincides with one of the traces $\varphi^{\omega}_{r,\infty}$ obtained by the above construction.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem on traces of Weyl-type operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. Web searches did not surface any subsequent work claiming a resolution, and no published solution could be located. The status therefore appears to remain open.

original_question: For 1 ≤ r < ∞, determine whether the trace ϕ_{r,∞}(·|LWEYL_{r,∞}) on (LWEYL_{r,∞})APP_{r,∞} constructed in Theorem 2.8 is spectral.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary (complex) Banach spaces. For $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-A\|:A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\},$$
and the $n$-th Weyl number is
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(TS):S\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|S\|\le 1\}.$$

For $1\le r<\infty$, let
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}=\{T\in\mathcal{L}:\ \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}\,x_n(T)<\infty\}$$
be the Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal of type $(r,\infty)$, and let
$$\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}=\Bigl\{T\in\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}:\ \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r}\,a_n(T)<\infty\Bigr\}$$
be the subideal of those operators in $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}$ whose approximation numbers also belong to the Lorentz sequence space $\ell_{r,\infty}$.

A continuous trace can be constructed on the component
$$\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}(X,X),\qquad X\text{ a Banach space},$$
as follows. The Lorentz sequence space $\ell_{r,\infty}$ admits a translation-invariant, dilation-invariant, positive linear functional (a generalized limit) $L:\ell_{r,\infty}\to\mathbb{C}$ vanishing on $\ell_r$. Using such a functional $L$ together with the eigenvalue/approximation-number structure of operators in $(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$, one obtains a continuous trace
$$\varphi_{r,\infty}\bigl(\,\cdot\,\big|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr):\ \bigcup_{X}\bigl(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty}\bigr)^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}(X,X)\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}.$$

A trace $\tau$ defined on a (component of an) operator ideal is called spectral if for every operator $T$ in its domain
$$\tau(T)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n(T),$$
where $(\lambda_n(T))_{n\ge 1}$ is the eigenvalue sequence of $T$ ordered by decreasing modulus and counted with algebraic multiplicities (the right-hand side being known to converge absolutely on the given ideal).

Problem. For each $r$ with $1\le r<\infty$, decide whether the trace $\varphi_{r,\infty}(\,\cdot\,|\,\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})$ on $(\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{r,\infty})^{\mathrm{APP}}_{r,\infty}$ is spectral in this sense.

original_question: Determine whether the Weyl-number ideal LWEYL_{1,∞} supports non-vanishing traces; the author explicitly conjectures that it should even support non-vanishing singular spectral traces.
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and let $T: X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. For each integer $n \geq 1$, the $n$-th Weyl number of $T$ is defined by
$$x_n(T) := \sup\{\, a_n(T A) : A : \ell_2 \to X,\ \|A\| \leq 1\,\},$$
where $a_n(\cdot)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number. The Lorentz–Weyl operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ consists of all bounded linear operators $T$ between arbitrary Banach spaces such that
$$\sup_{n \geq 1} n \cdot x_n(T) < \infty.$$
A trace on a (two-sided) operator ideal $\mathcal I$ defined on the class of all Banach spaces is a linear functional $\tau$ on the components $\mathcal I(X,X)$ (for every Banach space $X$) satisfying $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever the compositions make sense and $T \in \mathcal I$, together with the standard additivity and finite-rank-trace compatibility. The trace is called non-vanishing if it is not identically zero on $\mathcal I$. A trace is called a spectral trace if its value on every operator $T \in \mathcal I(X,X)$ depends only on the eigenvalue sequence of $T$ (counted with algebraic multiplicities); it is called singular if it vanishes on all finite-rank operators.

Question: Does the operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ admit a non-vanishing trace? In particular, does it admit a non-vanishing singular spectral trace?
status_search_result: No published resolution of the existence of non-vanishing (or non-vanishing singular spectral) traces on the Lorentz–Weyl ideal $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{WEYL}}_{1,\infty}$ was located. The problem appears in a list of open problems on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces, and no follow-up work establishing or refuting it was found in available search results.

original_question: Let LENT_z be the operator ideal defined by the dyadic entropy-number condition (e_{2^k}(S)) ∈ z(N0). Determine whether LAPP_z is always contained in LENT_z for every shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. For an operator $S\colon X\to Y$ in $\mathcal{L}$, define:

- The $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-A\|:A\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(A)<n\},\qquad n=1,2,\dots$$
- The $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number
$$e_n(S):=\inf\Big\{\varepsilon>0:\exists\,y_1,\dots,y_{2^{n-1}}\in Y\ \text{with}\ S(B_X)\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{2^{n-1}}(y_j+\varepsilon B_Y)\Big\}.$$

A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of $\ell^\infty(\mathbb{N}_0)$ (the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$) that contains all eventually zero sequences and is solid in the usual sense. The sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if for every $(\xi_k)_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ the shifted sequence $(\xi_{k+1})_{k\ge 0}$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, and conversely if a sequence and its left-shift coincide modulo membership conditions, the membership is preserved.

For a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the following classes of operators:
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}:=\{S\in\mathcal{L}:(a_{2^k}(S))_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\},$$
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z}:=\{S\in\mathcal{L}:(e_{2^k}(S))_{k\ge 0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\}.$$
Both are operator ideals on the class of all Banach spaces.

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$,
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{z}\ \subseteq\ \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_{z}.$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in the listed Pietsch-style collection of open problems on traces and operator ideals (2023). Web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the inclusion $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\subseteq\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ for all shift-monotone sequence ideals. While classical inequalities relating entropy and approximation numbers (Carl, Triebel, Pietsch) are well known, no general resolution at the level of arbitrary shift-monotone sequence ideals appears in the indexed literature.

original_question: Find shift-monotone sequence ideals z(N0) for which the entropy-number ideal LENT_z carries non-vanishing singular traces.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of real (or complex) null sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A linear subspace $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \subseteq c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ equipped with a quasi-norm is called a shift-monotone sequence ideal if:
(i) it is solid: whenever $(a_k) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and $(b_k) \in c_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ satisfies $|b_k| \le |a_k|$ for all $k$, then $(b_k) \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(b_k)\| \le \|(a_k)\|$; and
(ii) it is invariant under the forward shift $S: (a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots) \mapsto (0, a_0, a_1, \dots)$ as well as under the backward shift $T: (a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots)\mapsto (a_1,a_2,\dots)$, both acting continuously on $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

For an operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ between Banach spaces, the $n$-th (dyadic) entropy number $\varepsilon_n(T)$ is the infimum of all $\varepsilon>0$ such that the image of the unit ball of $X$ can be covered by $2^{n-1}$ closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ in $Y$. Given a shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$, define the entropy-number operator ideal
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z := \{\, T \in \mathcal{L} : (\varepsilon_n(T))_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\,\},$$
where $\mathcal{L}$ denotes the class of all bounded linear operators between arbitrary Banach spaces.

A trace on an operator ideal $\mathcal{I}$ is a linear functional $\tau$ on the components $\mathcal{I}(X,X)$ (for every Banach space $X$) satisfying $\tau(AB) = \tau(BA)$ whenever the products make sense. The trace $\tau$ is called singular if it vanishes on every finite-rank operator.

Problem. Determine the shift-monotone sequence ideals $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ for which the entropy-number operator ideal $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ carries a non-vanishing singular trace.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. A web search did not reveal any subsequent work resolving the existence of non-vanishing singular traces on entropy-number ideals $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{ENT}}_z$ for general shift-monotone sequence ideals $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$. The status appears to remain open.

self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be infinite-dimensional Banach spaces, and let $T:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator. For $n\ge 1$, denote by 
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\,\|T-F\|:F:X\to Y\text{ linear, }\operatorname{rank}F<n\,\}$$

$$\mathrm{LAPP}_{p,\infty}(X,Y)=\bigl\{\,T\in\mathcal L(X,Y):\sup_{n\ge 1}n^{1/p}\,a_n(T)<\infty\,\bigr\}.$$

$$S\in \mathrm{LAPP}_{s,\infty}(X,Y)\setminus \mathrm{LAPP}_{r,\infty}(X,Y),$$
i.e., an operator $S:X\to Y$ for which $\sup_n n^{1/s}a_n(S)<\infty$ but $\sup_n n^{1/r}a_n(S)=\infty$.

original_question: Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y. Find large families Z of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals such that (i) Z contains every Lorentz-type ideal d_{r,w}(N0), and (ii) the map z(N0) ↦ LAPP_z(X,Y) is injective on Z.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$ that is closed under coordinatewise multiplication by bounded sequences (so that the usual ideal property holds). Such a sequence ideal is called a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal if it is equipped with a complete quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_z$ such that:

(a) the unit-vector basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ generates $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ in a suitable sense and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural pointwise order on nonnegative non-increasing sequences;

(b) shift-monotonicity holds: for every sequence $a=(a_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every $k\geq 0$, the shifted sequence $S_k a = (a_{n+k})$ also belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|S_k a\|_z \le \|a\|_z$.

For parameters $0<r<\infty$ and a non-increasing weight $w=(w_n)\in c_0\setminus\ell_1$ with $w_0=1$, the Lorentz-type sequence ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is defined by
$$d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0) = \Big\{ a=(a_n) : \|a\|_{d_{r,w}} := \Big(\sum_{n=0}^\infty w_n\, a_n^{*\,r}\Big)^{1/r} <\infty \Big\},$$
where $(a_n^*)$ denotes the non-increasing rearrangement of $(|a_n|)$.

For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$, the operator ideal of approximable operators of type $z$ is
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y) :=  ig\{ T\in \mathcal{L}(X,Y) : (a_n(T))_{n\ge 0} \in z(\mathbb{N}_0)  ig\},$$
endowed with its natural quasi-norm, where $a_n(T)$ denotes the $n$-th approximation number of $T$.

Fix infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$. Determine large families $\mathcal{Z}$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals satisfying:

(i) every Lorentz-type ideal $d_{r,w}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ belongs to $\mathcal{Z}$;

(ii) the assignment $z(\mathbb{N}_0) \mapsto \mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$ is injective on $\mathcal{Z}$, i.e. distinct members of $\mathcal{Z}$ give rise to distinct operator-ideal components $\mathrm{LAPP}_z(X,Y)$.

original_question: Find infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X that have few approximable operators, in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than the cone c0*(N) of nonincreasing null sequences; ideally, make app(X) as small as possible.
self_contained_problem:
Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the cone of all nonincreasing null sequences of nonnegative real numbers, equipped with the dominance preorder $\sigma \preccurlyeq \tau$ meaning $\sigma_n \le \tau_n$ for all $n$. For a bounded linear operator $S$ between Banach spaces, let $a_n(S)$ denote its $n$-th approximation number, defined by
$$a_n(S) = \inf\{\|S - F\| : F \text{ has rank} < n\}.$$
For an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$, let $\mathcal{C}_0(X)$ denote the set of all bounded linear operators $S : X \to X$ whose approximation numbers form a null sequence, and define
$$\mathrm{app}(X) := \{(\sigma_n) \in c_0^*(\mathbb{N}) : \sigma_n \preccurlyeq a_n(S) \text{ for some } S \in \mathcal{C}_0(X)\}.$$
We say $X$ has *few approximable operators* if $\mathrm{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$.

Problem: Exhibit infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ that have few approximable operators, and make the set $\mathrm{app}(X)$ as small as possible.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No subsequent work explicitly resolving the size of app(X) for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces with few approximable operators was located; existing constructions of Banach spaces with few operators (e.g., Argyros–Haydon-type spaces, Gowers–Maurey, Wark's spaces) are related but do not appear to settle this specific question.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence and nevertheless have few approximable operators in the sense that app(X) is strictly smaller than c0*(N).
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let $\mathcal{L}(X)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded linear operators on $X$. Denote by $\mathrm{App}(X)$ the closed two-sided ideal of approximable operators on $X$, that is, the closure in the operator norm of the ideal of finite-rank operators on $X$. Let $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denote the operator ideal consisting of all bounded linear operators $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ whose sequence of approximation numbers $(a_n(T))_{n=1}^\infty$ tends to $0$, where 
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : F \in \mathcal{L}(X),\ \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}.$$
One says that $X$ has few approximable operators if $\mathrm{App}(X)$ is strictly smaller than $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$ (i.e., there exists a bounded operator on $X$ whose approximation numbers tend to zero but which is not a norm limit of finite-rank operators).

Exhibit an example of an infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ that simultaneously satisfies:
(i) $X$ contains an infinite unconditional basic sequence; and
(ii) $X$ has few approximable operators, i.e., $\mathrm{App}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals. Related constructions exist: Argyros and Deliyanni built spaces with few operators that fail to contain unconditional basic sequences, while Argyros's later "sequentially unconditional Banach space with few operators" (Proc. London Math. Soc., 2005) provides a space where every operator is a strictly singular perturbation of a multiple of the identity and which contains unconditional basic sequences. Whether that or a similar construction strictly separates $\mathrm{App}(X)$ from $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})(X)$ is not clearly settled by the sources retrieved, so the status with respect to the precise formulation is not definitively established.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Let X_K be the C0-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of ℓ1 mentioned in Section 2.9, and let τ_Z be the continuous singular trace on N(2/3,Z) constructed in Theorem 2.26. Describe the restriction of τ_Z to the operator ideal N(2/3,X_K)(ℓ2).
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) For Banach spaces $E,F$ and $0<r\le 1$, an operator $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ is called $r$-nuclear if it admits a representation $S=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} a_i\, x_i^*\otimes y_i$ with $x_i^*\in E^*$, $y_i\in F$, $\|x_i^*\|\le 1$, $\|y_i\|\le 1$, and $(a_i)\in\ell_r$. The class of all $r$-nuclear operators forms a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}_r$.

(b) Given a Banach space $Z$, the factor ideal $\mathcal{N}_r^{Z}$ consists of all operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(E,F)$ that admit a factorization $S=BTA$ with $A\in\mathcal{L}(E,Z)$, $T\in\mathcal{N}_r(Z,Z)$, $B\in\mathcal{L}(Z,F)$. We write $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)$ for this ideal and $\mathcal{N}(r,Z)(\ell_2)$ for its component on $\ell_2$, i.e. the operators $S\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$ admitting such a factorization through $Z$.

(c) A Banach space $Z$ is called $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial (in the sense relevant here) if every operator on $Z$ has the form $\lambda I_Z + K$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $K$ compact, equivalently if the Calkin algebra $\mathcal{L}(Z)/\mathcal{K}(Z)$ is one-dimensional. The Argyros–Haydon construction provides such a Banach space $X_K$ which is moreover a predual of $\ell_1$ and possesses a Schauder basis.

(d) Fix $r=2/3$ and an $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Banach space $Z$. For $S\in\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)(Z,Z)$, choose any factorization $S=\sum_{i} U_i T_i V_i$ with $T_i\in\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$ such that the canonical scalar $\varphi(U_iV_i)$ (the unique scalar $\lambda_i$ with $U_iV_i-\lambda_i I_Z$ compact, extracted via the trivial Calkin algebra of $Z$) is well defined. Then the formula
$$ \tau_Z(S)\;:=\;\sum_{i} \varphi(U_iV_i)\,\operatorname{tr}(T_i) $$
defines a continuous singular trace on the quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,Z)$ (here $\operatorname{tr}$ is the standard nuclear trace on $\mathcal{N}_{2/3}(Z,Z)$, which is well defined because $2/3\le 2/3$).

Problem. Take $Z=X_K$, the $\mathcal{C}_0$-trivial Argyros–Haydon predual of $\ell_1$. Give an explicit description of the restriction of the trace $\tau_{X_K}$ to the ideal $\mathcal{N}(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2)$ of operators on $\ell_2$ that factor (in the sense above) through $X_K$ via a $2/3$-nuclear middle operator. In particular, identify this restriction in terms of standard traces (the operator trace, Dixmier-type singular traces, etc.) on the corresponding ideal in $\mathcal{L}(\ell_2)$.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem ("Problem 23") in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals over the class of all Banach spaces. No subsequent paper resolving the description of $\tau_{X_K}$ restricted to $\mathcal{N}(2/3,X_K)(\ell_2)$ was located, so the problem appears still open.

original_question: Let LLEX_z = H ◦ LWEYL_z be the old-fashioned left-hand extension ideal built from operators factoring through Hilbert spaces. Determine whether (LWEYL_{2,∞})APP_{2,∞}, or even the smaller ideal LAPP_{1,∞}, fails to be contained in LLEX_{1,∞}.
self_contained_problem:
Background and notation. Work in the category of bounded linear operators between (complex) Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ assigns to every pair of Banach spaces $X,Y$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)\subseteq\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$ that is stable under composition with bounded operators on either side and contains the finite-rank operators. A quasi-Banach operator ideal is an operator ideal equipped with a complete quasi-norm respecting the ideal structure.

For a bounded sequence $(s_n)$ of non-negative reals, the Lorentz quasi-norm of type $(r,\infty)$ is
$$\|(s_n)\|_{r,\infty} := \sup_{n\ge 1} n^{1/r} s_n^*,$$
where $(s_n^*)$ is the non-increasing rearrangement. For an operator $T\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y)$, denote by $a_n(T)$ the $n$-th approximation number
$$a_n(T)=\inf\{\|T-F\|:\ F\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y),\ \mathrm{rank}(F)<n\},$$
and by $x_n(T)$ the $n$-th Weyl number
$$x_n(T)=\sup\{a_n(T A):\ A\in\mathcal{L}(\ell_2,X),\ \|A\|\le 1\}.$$

Define the following quasi-Banach operator ideals:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(a_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$, quasi-normed by $\|T\|_{\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}}=\|(a_n(T))\|_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$: operators with $(x_n(T))\in\ell_{r,\infty}$.
\item $\mathrm{LAPP}_{r,\infty}$ and $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$: the "left-sided" versions, defined as the components $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}\circ\mathfrak{F}$ obtained by composing on the right with arbitrary bounded operators (equivalently, the largest ideals whose Hilbert-space components coincide with those of $\mathrm{APP}_{r,\infty}$ resp. $\mathrm{WEYL}_{r,\infty}$ via factorization through arbitrary Banach spaces on the left and $\ell_2$ on the right).
\item $\mathfrak{H}$: the ideal of operators that factor through some Hilbert space.
\item $\mathrm{LLEX}_{r,\infty} := \mathfrak{H}\circ\mathrm{LWEYL}_{r,\infty}$, the "left-hand extension" ideal.
\end{itemize}

Product ideals are defined componentwise via factorization: $T\in\mathfrak{A}\circ\mathfrak{B}(X,Y)$ iff $T=AB$ with $B\in\mathfrak{B}(X,Z)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(Z,Y)$ for some Banach space $Z$.

Problem. Show that the operator ideal $\mathrm{LWEYL}_{2,\infty}\circ\mathrm{APP}_{2,\infty}$ is not contained in $\mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}$. More strongly, show that even
$$\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}\ \not\subseteq\ \mathrm{LLEX}_{1,\infty}.$$
Equivalently, exhibit Banach spaces $X,Y$ and an operator $T\in\mathrm{LAPP}_{1,\infty}(X,Y)$ that does not admit a factorization $T=A_2 A_1$ with $A_1\in\mathrm{LWEYL}_{1,\infty}$ and $A_2$ factoring through a Hilbert space.

paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
original_question: Find operator ideals, different from the examples furnished by Theorems 2.26 and 2.27, that support non-vanishing traces.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators acting between arbitrary Banach spaces. An operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$ is an assignment, to every pair of Banach spaces $(X,Y)$, of a linear subspace $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y) \subseteq \mathfrak{L}(X,Y)$ such that:
(i) every finite-rank operator belongs to $\mathfrak{A}$;
(ii) for all Banach spaces $W,X,Y,Z$ and all $B\in\mathfrak{L}(W,X)$, $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$, $C\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,Z)$, the composition $CAB$ lies in $\mathfrak{A}(W,Z)$.

A trace on $\mathfrak{A}$ is a family of linear functionals $\tau_X : \mathfrak{A}(X,X) \to \mathbb{C}$, defined for every Banach space $X$, satisfying:
(a) $\tau_X(\mathrm{id}_X \otimes x^*\otimes x) = \langle x, x^*\rangle$ for all rank-one operators on $X$ (equivalently, $\tau$ extends the standard trace on finite-rank operators);
(b) the trace property: $\tau_Y(AB) = \tau_X(BA)$ whenever $A\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ and $B\in\mathfrak{L}(Y,X)$ (or, more generally, whenever both compositions lie in the relevant ideal components).

A trace $\tau$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ is said to be non-vanishing if $\tau$ is not identically zero on $\mathfrak{A}$.

It is known that non-vanishing traces exist on certain operator ideals, e.g. on the ideal of nuclear operators (where the spectral / Grothendieck–Lidskii trace need not vanish), and on certain ideals constructed via specific shift-invariant sequence space methods.

Problem. Exhibit operator ideals defined on the class of all Banach spaces, distinct from the previously known examples (the nuclear-type ideals and ideals built from the standard sequence-ideal/shift-invariant-functional construction), that support a non-vanishing trace in the sense above.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on traces on operator ideals defined over the class of all Banach spaces. Web searches do not reveal subsequent work exhibiting genuinely new operator ideals (beyond the nuclear-type and sequence-ideal-based constructions) supporting non-vanishing traces. Construction of non-vanishing traces on Banach-space operator ideals remains a notably difficult area, and the problem appears to still be open.

original_question: For every quasi-Banach operator ideal A and every pair of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals x(N0) and y(N0), determine whether there always exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) such that the reiteration identity (AAPP_x)APP_y = AAPP_z holds.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0=\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. A sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_x$ making it a quasi-Banach space, and satisfying the usual ideal property (it contains all finitely supported sequences and is closed under coordinate-wise multiplication by bounded sequences with $\|(\lambda_n a_n)\|_x\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\,\|(a_n)\|_x$). It is called shift-monotone if the forward and backward shift operators act boundedly on it and the quasi-norm is monotone with respect to the natural shift partial order (equivalently, $\|(a_{n+1})\|_x\le\|(a_n)\|_x$).
 
A quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}=(\mathfrak A(E,F),\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A})$ assigns to each pair of Banach spaces $(E,F)$ a linear subspace $\mathfrak A(E,F)$ of bounded operators, complete under a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathfrak A}$ dominating the operator norm, with the usual ideal axioms (containing finite-rank operators and being closed under composition with bounded operators on either side).
 
For a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and a quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak{A}$, define the approximation procedure $\mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{APP}}_{x}$ as the class of all bounded operators $T:E\to F$ between Banach spaces such that there exists a sequence $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ of operators with $T_n\in\mathfrak A(E,F)$ for all $n$, $\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A}<\infty$, and the sequence of approximation-type numbers $(\|T-T_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ belongs to $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with the natural quasi-norm
$$\|T\|_{\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x}:=\inf\big\{\max(\sup_n\|T_n\|_{\mathfrak A},\,\|(\|T-T_n\|)_n\|_x)\big\},$$
the infimum running over all such sequences $(T_n)$. Then $\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x$ is again a quasi-Banach operator ideal.
 
Problem. Prove or disprove: for every quasi-Banach operator ideal $\mathfrak A$ and every pair $x(\mathbb{N}_0)$, $y(\mathbb{N}_0)$ of quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideals, there exists a quasi-Banach shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ such that the reiteration identity
$$\big(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_x\big)^{\mathrm{APP}}_y \;=\; \mathfrak A^{\mathrm{APP}}_z$$
holds (with equivalent quasi-norms).

No web evidence was found indicating that a resolution of this generalized reiteration identity for approximation procedures has been published; it appears to remain open.

original_question: Find a shift-monotone sequence ideal z(N0) for which the two equivalent quasi-norms on LAPP_z discussed in Theorem 1.4, namely ‖·|LAPP_z‖ and |||·|LAPP_z|||, are genuinely different on at least one operator S ∈ LAPP_z(X,Y).
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbb{N}_0 = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ and let $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$ denote the space of eventually zero scalar sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}_0$. A quasi-normed sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is a linear subspace of the space of bounded sequences containing $c_{00}(\mathbb{N}_0)$, equipped with a quasi-norm $\|\cdot\,|z\|$ that makes it complete (or at least quasi-normed) and that satisfies the ideal property: for every $\xi=(\xi_n)\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ and every bounded sequence $(\lambda_n)$, the pointwise product $(\lambda_n\xi_n)$ belongs to $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ with $\|(\lambda_n\xi_n)\,|z\|\le \sup_n|\lambda_n|\cdot\|\xi\,|z\|$.

For $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$ let $\sigma_k:\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}\to\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_0}$ denote the right-shift defined by $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=\xi_{n-k}$ for $n\ge k$ and $(\sigma_k\xi)_n=0$ for $n<k$. The ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is called shift-monotone if $\sigma_k$ maps $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$ into itself for every $k\ge 0$ and the operator quasi-norms $c_k:=\|\sigma_k:z\to z\|$ satisfy $c_k\to 0$ as well as $c_0=1$ (more precisely, the standard shift-monotonicity assumption $\|\sigma_k\xi\,|z\|\le c_k\|\xi\,|z\|$ with $c_k\downarrow 0$ as $k\to\infty$ -- equivalently, the canonical embedding $z(\mathbb{N}_0)\hookrightarrow c_0$ is bounded and shifts contract suitably).

Approximation numbers. For Banach spaces $X,Y$ and a bounded linear operator $S:X\to Y$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L:X\to Y \text{ linear, } \mathrm{rank}\,L<n\}, \qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.$$
Set $\alpha_n(S):=a_{n+1}(S)$ for $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, so that $\alpha_0(S)=\|S\|\ge \alpha_1(S)\ge \alpha_2(S)\ge\cdots$.

The approximation operator ideal associated with $z$. Define
$$\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y):=\{S\in\mathcal{L}(X,Y): (\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\in z(\mathbb{N}_0)\}$$
and equip it with the quasi-norm
$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|:=\bigl\|(\alpha_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|.$$
A second quasi-norm is defined by means of finite-rank approximations: with $\mathcal{F}_{<n}(X,Y)$ the set of bounded linear operators of rank strictly less than $n$,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\bigl\|(\beta_n(S))_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|, \quad \text{where } \beta_n(S):=\inf\{\|S-L\|: L\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\text{ attains a rank-}n\text{ optimal-type form}\},$$
the second quantity being the natural "ideal-internal" quasi-norm obtained by replacing the scalar infimum defining $\alpha_n$ with the $z$-quasi-norm of the residual sequences; equivalently,
$$|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||:=\inf\bigl\{\bigl\|(\|S-L_n\|)_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}\,\bigm|\,z\bigr\|: L_n\in\mathcal{F}_{<n+1}(X,Y)\bigr\}.$$

It is known that $\|\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|$ and $|||\cdot\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||$ are equivalent quasi-norms on $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z(X,Y)$ for every quasi-normed shift-monotone sequence ideal $z(\mathbb{N}_0)$.

$$\|S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z\|\;\neq\;|||S\,|\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{APP}}_z|||.$$

paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
context_brief: Distance complexity in discrete time-tree graphs
original_question: A discrete time-tree is a rooted binary phylogenetic tree on a fixed labeled leaf set in which every node is assigned a distinct non-negative integer time and each child has smaller time than its parent. The paper studies graph families on such trees, including DtTm, DtTum, RNNI, and RNNIu, where two trees are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by one allowed local move such as changing the length of one event interval by 1, swapping the ranks of two nodes that bound a unit-length interval, or performing a nearest-neighbor interchange move on a unit-length interval, with graph-specific restrictions. Given two discrete time-trees in one of these graph families, what is the computational complexity of computing their graph distance, meaning the minimum number of allowed moves needed to transform one tree into the other?
status_search_result: The complexity of computing the RNNI distance has been resolved: Collienne and Gavryushkin (published 2021) gave an O(n^2)-time algorithm (FINDPATH) for computing shortest paths in the RNNI graph, and the same approach extends to RNNIu. However, related variants remain hard: with rank moves only (RNNI(0)) the problem is NP-hard, and the complexity for the full DtTm and DtTum graphs (which include integer length moves on event intervals) does not appear to have been settled. Thus the original problem is partially solved.

paper_title: The combinatorics of discrete time-trees: theory and open problems
context_brief: Split theorem for ranked and timed tree graphs
original_question: Consider any of the discrete time-tree graph families DtT, DtTu, RNNI, or RNNIu on a fixed leaf set. Suppose two trees T and R share a split, meaning that each tree has an edge whose removal induces the same bipartition of the leaves. Must every shortest path from T to R in the chosen graph stay entirely within trees that continue to display that shared split?
self_contained_problem:
Let L be a fixed finite leaf set with |L| = n. A discrete time-tree on L is a rooted phylogenetic tree with leaves bijectively labelled by L, in which each internal node is assigned an integer "time" (rank) such that times strictly increase along every path from a leaf to the root. Consider the following four graphs whose vertices are such trees:

• DtT: discrete time-trees on L, where each internal node carries a positive integer time and ties between non-adjacent nodes are allowed.
• DtTu: the analogue of DtT in which all leaves are required to have time 0 ("ultrametric"/coalescent-style).
• RNNI: ranked nearest-neighbour-interchange graph, whose vertices are discrete time-trees in which the n−1 internal nodes have distinct ranks 1,…,n−1.
• RNNIu: the ultrametric variant of RNNI.

In each of these graphs, edges are given by the natural local moves: an NNI-style move that exchanges two subtrees adjacent to an interval between consecutive-rank internal nodes, and a "rank move" that swaps the ranks of two internal nodes whose ranks differ by one (plus, in DtT/DtTu, moves that change an integer time by one, when permitted). Distance d(T,R) is the length of a shortest path in the graph.

Given a tree T on L and an internal edge e of T, removing e disconnects T into two components and induces a bipartition (split) of L. Two trees T and R are said to share a split σ if each of them has an internal edge inducing the bipartition σ.

Question. Let G be any one of DtT, DtTu, RNNI, RNNIu. Suppose T and R are two vertices of G that share a split σ. Must every shortest path from T to R in G consist entirely of trees that also display σ?
status_search_result: A counterexample to the conjectured Split Theorem in the RNNI graph was found by Collienne (reported on the bioAI lab page describing Collienne's RNNI geometry paper). Thus the strong split-preservation statement is false in RNNI; a weaker version remains plausible but is not established.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
context_brief: BRAVO for critically loaded finite-buffer GI/G/1/K queues
original_question: Consider a finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue with one server, renewal arrivals, independent and identically distributed service times, K-1 waiting places, and loss of customers who arrive when the system is full. In the critically loaded case λ = μ, where c_a^2 and c_s^2 denote the squared coefficients of variation of the inter-arrival and service times, does the queue exhibit the BRAVO effect (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs), and in particular, for light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, is the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* equal to (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (one server in service plus K−1 waiting positions). Customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2 := Var(inter-arrival)/(mean inter-arrival)^2. Service times are i.i.d., independent of arrivals, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. A customer who arrives to find the system full (K customers present) is lost; otherwise the customer joins the queue and is eventually served in FCFS order. Let D(t) denote the number of customers that have departed (completed service and left) by time t in stationarity, and define the long-run departure-process variability parameter
   γ*(K) := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / (μ t),
assumed to exist.

Assume the system is critically loaded, i.e. λ = μ, and assume that both the inter-arrival and the service time distributions are light-tailed (have finite moment generating functions in a neighborhood of zero).

Question. Does the BRAVO ("Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs") effect hold for this GI/G/1/K queue, and in particular is it true that
   γ*(K) = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)   as K → ∞ ?
status_search_result: The conjecture, posed for the critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue with light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, appears still open. Subsequent work has established BRAVO-type results for related models (M/M/1/K, GI/G/1, GI/G/s heavy-traffic departure variance, and busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue), and a 2024 work studies generalized BRAVO and oscillating cumulants for M/M/1/K, but no source found proves the (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) asymptotics for the general GI/G/1/K case.

paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
original_question: For the critically loaded finite-capacity GI/G/1/K queue in Conjecture 1, what are the weakest distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service times under which the asymptotic formula γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) should hold? More specifically, if requiring light tails in the sense of an exponential moment is stronger than necessary, is there a sharper minimal condition, and is the existence of 2+ε moments sufficient or not?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite capacity K (the GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ, variance σ_a², and squared coefficient of variation c_a² = λ²σ_a²; service times are i.i.d. with mean 1/μ, variance σ_s², and squared coefficient of variation c_s² = μ²σ_s²; arrivals finding K customers in the system are lost. Assume the system is critically loaded, i.e. ρ = λ/μ = 1. Let D(t) denote the number of departures (served customers) in [0, t], and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K = lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized variability parameter γ_K* = V_K / μ. It has been conjectured that, under suitable distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions,

   γ_K* = (1/3)(c_a² + c_s²) + O(1/K)   as K → ∞.

The original conjecture is stated under the assumption that both the inter-arrival and service distributions possess a finite exponential moment (i.e., are light-tailed). The problem is the following:

(a) Determine the weakest distributional assumptions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions under which the asymptotic formula above holds.

(b) In particular, decide whether the existence of 2+ε moments (for some ε > 0) on both inter-arrival and service time distributions is sufficient for the formula to hold, or whether some strictly stronger condition (weaker than an exponential moment but stronger than 2+ε moments) is necessary.
status_search_result: The conjectured 1/3 asymptotic variance formula for critically loaded GI/G/1/K queues (BRAVO effect) is known and has been studied in several follow-up works (e.g., Hanbali–Mandjes–Nazarathy–Whitt on heavy-traffic GI/GI/1 departure variance, and recent 2024 work on phase transitions and generalized BRAVO). However, no source located in the search states a sharp minimal moment condition on the inter-arrival and service time distributions under which the (1/3)(c_a² + c_s²) + O(1/K) formula holds; the question of the minimal condition (and whether 2+ε moments suffice) appears to remain open.
